dialoguetext: Try to unlock the door.
Your key no longer turns in the lock.
"It must be an electronic lock. You will have to get Garte, the cafeteria manager, to open it first -- after you've paid for the night."
You feel uncertain, like a child who's lost his mother in the crowd.
Why would I want to stay in such a place?
Still sounds better than sleeping outside.
Because it's your last lifeline to being a police officer instead of a hobo.
Yes, and it's not just a matter of comfort, but also of principle. This may be your last lifeline to being a police officer instead of a hobo.
Just punch the damned door. No *locks* are going to keep you out.
"Nah, I'll get by somehow. Didn't like that room very much anyway."
"Actually, I don't need to pay -- I will brave the streets. Go undercover as a hobocop."
"Right, I should go pay my debts before I can go to sleep."
[Leave.]
"Our investigation does not at present require for anyone to go undercover. Let's drop this discussion and go settle your debt with the manager."
"I would advise against that. It's already late, and you won't find cheaper accommodation in the vicinity."
He nods. "Yes, we both need to get proper rest tonight."
He's asserting his leadership talents because he is concerned about you.
Observe the damage to your knuckles. Is this really worth it?
The lieutenant looks on impassively. "Even if you could break down the door, all you would get is another bill."
*Even if you could*? Don't let him talk you down, son!
Try one more time. This time with both fists, one after the other.
(His voice echoes from downstairs.) "What's going on up there?"
The lieutenant purses his lips. "Admirable form. Now come on, let's go down."
(His voice echoes from downstairs.) "What the hell is going on up there?"
The lieutenant looks at you with a mixture of pity and weariness. "Come on, let's go down."
Blubber. And keep blubbering.
Something about it has changed.
This is the door to your room.
Punch the door.
The door rings from the impact, but does not budge.
Your fist bounces off the door and comes back to you on a wave of agony that surges up your arm.
"Aaaaa! It huuurts!"
Keep it in. Cradle your arm.
The tears bring some relief, but not much.
Your angry voice carries through the Whirling, but you still can't stop the tears from welling up in your eyes...
Try to stay cool.
Nice try. The tears come streaming down your face as you crumble to the ground.
It hurts, but keep your cool. You've got this.
(His voice echoes from downstairs.) "What's going on up there?"
Pow-pow! That was impressive.
"This door will fall prostrate before The Law!" (Punch the door again.)
The door shudders, but appears undamaged.
The door appears undamaged, and even more impassive than the lieutenant.
You've got this. Men like you don't cry unless it serves their purposes.
Confront the door with a stoical expression. You are still The Law.
He nods toward the staircase. "Come on, let's go down."
"Good night, lieutenant."
"Alright, let's go."
(His voice echoes from downstairs.) "What the hell is going on up there?"
The lieutenant looks at you with a mixture of pity and weariness. "Come on, let's go down."
"Just a moment. You had some questions earlier, I believe, and, besides, we should discuss our progress on the investigation. Let's go out to the balcony."
"Just a moment. We should talk about our progress on the investigation. Let's go out to the balcony."
The door to your room locks every night at 21.00 if you haven't paid for the room. You can pay downstairs when speaking to Garte, the cafeteria manager.
You could try climbing into that trash bin in the yard, hobocop style...
You could try climbing into that trash bin in the yard, hobocop style... after you've gotten open the lid.
Hey, remember that trash bin idea...? Time to get climbing!
The door has seen better days -- the layer of paint has started to peel off due to the salt and wind from the sea. Even the lock looks slightly rusted.
Unlock the shack door with the key.
Never mind. [Leave.]
The key turns with a satisfying click. You can enter the shack now.
"I'll be sleeping in my room in the Whirling. We'll meet in front of the shack in the morning."
"I'm afraid we don't have time for rest stops right now, officer. We should really get back to the Whirling."
"Right." [Leave.]
"I'll sleep here then. See you in the morning." (Keep turning the key.)
"Good night." He smiles: "And try not to break the case without me."
"I'll wait outside to give you some time and privacy to check out your new living arrangement. But just so you know..."
"After we're done with the day, I'll still be staying in the Whirling-in-Rags for the night. We'll meet in front of the shack in the morning."
It's getting cold this late in the night. Time to call it a day.
"Good night, Kim." (Send him away for the night.)
Not yet. [Leave.]
"Good night, officer. We'll meet in front of the shack in the morning."
Enter the shack.
Enter the shack.
The door is locked. Lieutenant Kitsuragi resides inside.
Wow, you work *hard*.
I do?
(Discard thought.)
I know you're in a hurry, sir -- off to work really hard, as always -- I just need *one* moment of your time to discuss how hard you hustle.
Oh, yes. You hustle. You're a provider. It's tough out there, but you keep it real and provide...
I guess I do, yeah.
What hard work do I do exactly?
Oh yeah! Like a horse. A work horse. For hard work.
Look at yourself, you're a human pedometer! You must have walked 200,000 steps down cracked asphalt, mosaic, sand, and linoleum after you re-emerged.
That is the sign of a hustler who never gives up. The world is harsh and people are evil -- you didn't make it that way. And you won't let it break you. You *ride*.
Yeah, I ride. A little.
I fuckin' ride till I die, bitch.
I'm not sure I *ride*...
Oh, you do. You *make* money. You got gills, baby, meaning those black papers with the faces of the innocences on them. You bring in the Franconegros and the Solas.
A little? You *make* money. You got gills, baby, got those black papers with the faces of the innocences on them. You bring in the Franconegros and the Solas.
It ain't easy, but you *do* it. Day in and day out. You didn't make the rules but you won't lose! You're a cop and a sprinter and a money printer.
I mean yeah, I *did* take that bribe from that Joyce woman.
I guess I've made *some* gills, sure.
Can't say I didn't make that Siileng guy give some of his money either.
Sure, and I got that giant novelty cheque from Evrart...
Oh yeah, you took that bribe *hard*. You're a killa'.
Can't say that -- you *shook* him. You're a killer. A shark.
Wasn't *easy* getting that giant novelty cheque from Evrart. Took some ingenuity to get into the harbour, but you got in -- and you *took* that bribe as hard as any cop's taken it.
You could say I took some money from that Mañana guy too.
You didn't log that in as a donation either -- you don't log any of that shit in, you're a straight rider.

Sure, sure. And has it been easy? Is life easy? Have you *not* gone into cardiac arrest? Are you *not* about to have an anxiety attack or shoot yourself in the mouth? But you still hustle 24/7, ride or die. Now, ask yourself...
...are you *rich*?
That's just what it's like -- life and death. But you got *gills* on your side, baby, got those black papers with the faces of the innocences on them -- you bring in the Franconegros and the Solas.
Oh, and then there's pawning stuff off to that suspicious Roy guy.
Yeah, you're in the sales business. Shake 'em for shit and then pawn it off, *law officer*-style.
Yes. Quite.
No, I'm actually *not*.
Get outta here! You're a pauper! You work harder than *anyone*, almost rode yourself to the grave and you're still practically a *hobo* -- why is that?
That's right. You work harder than *anyone*, you almost rode yourself to the grave and you're still practically a *hobo* -- why is that?
It's because of that Garte guy riding my ass!
The system is broken!
There's a market for corrupt cops out there, but the immigrant cops have price dumped it.
I don't know. Why *am* I so poor?
Boohoo, *the system is broken*. *The establishment is keeping me down...* That's not the fuck-yeah attitude you're used to, what is this? Why are you so poor?
Look, the immigrants are cool. The immigrants play *cool* music. Everyone likes them. Especially the women. Don't hate on the immigrants. They've got nothing to do with you living under a boat.
The Garte-man has set himself up one of those self replicating money-structures. You should *learn* from it. Don't play the victim. Think, hustler. Think with your head.
Because of the TAXES. G-man's got his jam-covered sticky-fingers in your pocket, stealing from you every time you buy, sell, walk, talk, fart, so much as sneeze!
That's right! One-hundred percent. Fucking G-man's got his jam-covered sticky-fingers in your pocket, stealing from you every time you buy, sell, walk, talk, fart, so much as sneeze!
Fucking taxes, man.
What are you not sure about?! They're *milking* your nipples till they bleed. Can't you see? Aren't you *sick and tired* of having bloody nipples?
Aren't taxes almost non-existent in the Gossamer State that is Revachol?
I thought there *were* no taxes.
Really? Every time I sneeze?

You and I both, but they got those *indirect modes of taxation*. Sales tax, excise duty, extraction tax, this tax that doesn't even have a name -- plus there's the stuff *people in other countries* pay for, that makes them ask for more money from *you* here! The Gossamer State's a myth. In total the Coalition Government is taking...
NINETY-EIGHT PERCENT OF ALL YOUR MONEY.

Every time you wipe your ass! They got their direct and their *indirect modes of taxation*: sales tax, excise duty, extraction tax, alimony, one tax that doesn't even have a name! Plus there's the stuff *people in other countries* pay for, that makes them ask for more money from *you* here. Total tax duties add up to...
NO FUCKING WAY. I guess I'm a free market fundamentalist now. (Opt in.)
Are you sure? That seems like a pretty big number...
This isn't helping me solve my money problem, it's only making me into a free-market type. (Opt out.)
Here you go, hustler, fight the righteous fight! Free the people. Keep it real. Keep it street. Keep foaming at the mouth *furiously* on the tax issue!
Bleeding nipples are kind of a pain, but how will deregulation help with that? (Opt in, but only a little.)
It's *all* about the tax issue, hustler. No other problem in the world is as pressing as top-marginal tax rates, and don't you fucking forget it.
What are you, a racist? Don't be a racist! Be a cool immigrant ultraliberal free market advocate! Ride or die, keep it street!
Well... if *not* being an ultraliberal makes me a racist then I guess I should be an ultraliberal? (Opt in.)
Go away! [Discard thought.]
Here you go, hustler, fight the righteous fight! Free the people. Keep it real. Keep it street. Keep foaming at the mouth *furiously* on the tax issue!
This guy's appropriating the emerging Boogie Street lingo as part of his sales pitch for the free market economy.
You're trying to sound like a Boogie Street youth to peddle me this stuff, aren't you?
Yeah, ain't it cool, rider?! Ain't it street?
It's not. (Opt out.)
He did, yes he did. And you took it. Took it and put in in your pocket. Ka-ching, baby doll. Officer Hustle riding shotgun.
Yeah, and Evrart gave me that fiver."
Hey, psst...
Who -- me?
Yes, you. Word on the street is you're ready to start building *communism* again!
Look around.
Psst, hey, you!

Yes -- you're ready to start building communism *again*. You've built it before, *they've* built it before. Hasn't really worked out yet, but neither has *love* -- should we just stop building love, too?
'Again'?
How come there's *word on the street*?
Can't argue with that.
Yes, we should all stop building love.
Love has worked out really well for me. I'm a love winner.

Good. We need tender men like you building gargantuan communism. Word on the street is it's going to be ten thousand times larger than any communism previously attempted by human beings. Is that right?

This conversation isn't really about love. Try to keep up, okay? This is about the communism you've *promised* to build. Word on the street is it's going to be ten thousand times larger than any communism previously attempted. Is that true?

You keep saying things like *down with the bourgeoisie*, *eat the rich*, *sodomize the land-owners*, *impale all people who have more than 25 reál in their pocket*, *literally murder all human beings regardless of their political beliefs* -- that kind of stuff.
Oh, right. That sounds like me.
I haven't said anything like that.

Okay, not in so many words. But don't deny it. You're about to rip off that mask of social democracy and reveal the monstrous seven-eyed lamb of global communism that will devour and masticate mankind.
Everyone can see that. So tell me, do you have any questions before we fire up the Big Communism Builder, or do we get *right down to it*?

So, what about all that communism you've promised to build? Word on the street is you've woken up from a thousand years of slumber, promising to erect a version of communism many times greater than any attempted before. Is that true?
Funky-style. Very funky. So tell me. Do you have any questions before we fire up the Big Communism Builder, or do we get right down to it?
Wait, first -- what's this *communism* even about?
It's too tiring. I don't have it in me. I'm beat down and broken. (Opt out.)
Roll up your sleeves and start building Communism. (Opt in.)
Failure. It's about failure.
Failure?
I don't *do* failure.

You alone, against every living thing, against every human alive: eight hundred trillion reál in the hands of an *impossibly* well organized ruling class; towering city blocks of bank-men who have the ears of prime ministers; million-headed armies of nations and the love of your own mother!

Yes! Abject failure. Total, irreversible defeat on all fronts! Absolutely vanquished, beaten, curb-stomped and pissed on -- until *you* came along! *You* will reverse the fortune of the workers of the world.

You -- against the atom, the charm and the spin. Where the whole world failed -- matter failed to bend to human will; human will failed to get out of bed and tie its laces -- you alone, single-handedly, will rebuild the dreams of the working class. You are The Last Communist.
Now get to work, comrade.

Of course you do! You *are* failure, you *are* Communism. Absolutely vanquished, beaten, curb-stomped, shat on. While everyone else is out partying, having a callous laugh, *you* will reverse the fortune of the workers of the world.
Very well. I guess no one will build Communism then. Tell the working man it's over. Unless anyone has... objections?
No objections. It's mathematically impossible to achieve a classless society. Everyone knows this.
Let not failure ensnare you any further, beautiful pixie girl! Be an acrobat! A prancing faerie queen!
Did someone mention cocaine? Are we doing cocaine? No? I'm sure I heard someone say Cocainimism...
Anyone? Anyone else? There's no one?
There's one.
Oh yeah! Get the firing squads and the animal wagons ready!
What should I do?
No. Shut up. I want to lie down and let the water carry me downstream. [Discard thought.]
You should build Communism -- precisely *because* it's impossible.
There's no one. Okay then. Lie down and let the water carry you downstream...
Good bye, Communism. [Finish thought.]
Wait, what? Firing squads? You didn't say anything about those.
Roll your sleeves up further and breathe in the pristine air. [Finish thought.]
Too late to back out now. You can't make an omelet without breaking a few million eggs!
I've said *some* mildly left wing things but none of those.
Oh yes, the *mask of ambivalence*. Don't deny it. You're about to rip it off and reveal the monstrous seven-eyed lamb of global communism that will devour and masticate mankind.
Get the fuck outta here! No. [Finish thought.]
Wow, so someone's been a little... *boring*?
No, I'm not. Get outta here! [Finish thought.]
What?
Yes, my *standard* liege. Someone's seen all sorts of wild ideas pop off and thought -- 'I'll take the *boring* one. The regular, please. The brown.'
I like brown.
I like standards.
Look, I'm just trying to do my job, no need for extravagance.
What is this? Picking on me for not being *crazy* enough? That's the LEAST of my concerns.
"Kim. Am I boring?"
"You?" He looks at you. "I wouldn't worry about that."
See? You're so *regular* and vinyl-brown, he doesn't even want to talk to you about it.
Of course you do. And maybe some black shoes or a pristine white shirt to go with that. It's official: My lord's *copotype* is Regular Cop. I'll let everyone know. I'll send out a telefax.
Of course you do. Maybe some *regulations* and a *usual* pistol to go with them? It's official: My lord's *copotype* is Regular Cop. I'll let everyone know. I'll send out a telefax.
Of course you do. Let's get right to it. My lord's *copotype* is Regular Cop. I'll let everyone know. I'll send out a telefax.
Wait, wait -- this will be my *copotype* now?
Why not. Send out the telefax then. I'm not ashamed. (Opt in.)
Yeah, no need. Let's keep that announcement on standby for now. (Opt out.)
Yes, the type of cop you are, sire. Think of it as a caste, a *class*, even. A nation of Regular Law Officials that you belong to. It comes, of course, with the *usual* benefits.
No need to be defensive. The regularity, the brownness, the *cut-and-dry* have their appeal -- a very *standard* appeal.
Done and done. No actual *communiques* will be sent, of course. That would be too dramatic.
Good, good. Of course. To outright declare yourself something does seem a bit too... *interesting* now, doesn't it? I won't trouble you any further.
As you turn, a bright light catches your eye, making you squint.
Where's it coming from?
[Discard thought.]
"Yes." [*Really* discard it.]
From a distant sunset? A stage light? Flash photography? Nowhere in particular? It's just what *superstar law-officers* do -- they squint at lights. And they solve shit.
Actually, now that I hear *superstar* and *law official* in a sentence they sound weird together.
Yeah, that's me -- I've been *establishing* my superstardom hard lately.
Yeah, you have! You're a big dick cop. Dick Mullen. Salaam Rocky Bhai. Bad-ass, on-the-edge disco cop. Time to recede into a ludicrous fantasy world, HERE WE GO! Camera, lights...
What are you, deaf? They're perfect! Like 'rockstar politician' and 'drug-addict teacher'. Embrace the superstardom you've worked so hard to establish.
You sure? The light is *important*. The light is life. And destiny.
You've got the wrong impression. I'm no superstar. I'm trash.
Yeah, a cool *trash* superstar. Big dick cop down on his luck. Salaam Rocky Bhai. Bad-ass, on the edge disco cop. Time to recede into a ludicrous fantasy world, HERE WE GO! Camera, lights...
ACTION!
Wait, what's that about a ludicrous fantasy world?

Yeah. You know, beneath it is just heartbreak, a pulmonary tract infection, atherosclerotic disease. This is where you say *action* and re-conceptualize all that. Re-invent it as the world's first celebrity police officer!
Cool.
Sooooo cool.
This is the beginning of your *legend*.
No. I'm too down beat. I won't say those things anymore. [Wave off the thought.]
Fuck it -- ACTION!
With a sudden flash the world freezes around you -- and you along with it. In an iconic monochrome solution, a black silhouette against a rasterized orange world. It's *on*.
No. Fuck you! [Finish thought]
What's this? We're getting reports of *normal*, *reasonable*, *temperate* political opinions somewhere in Martinaise...
You must be mistaken: I'm a real radical.
That's me, Mr. Reasonable. Someone's got to keep it sane around here.
[Discard thought.]
Of course, a *radical centrist*. In these bright and loud times where a thousand frequencies drown one another out, sober thinking is a radical act...
The air suddenly feels calmer. More transparent in a strangely tender way. Perhaps it's the hangover, perhaps it's a temporary surge of serotonin, but something tells you...
It's time... to become a citizen of the *Kingdom of Conscience*.
First, where is this Kingdom of Conscience?
No more talk -- Sign me up for a passport! (Opt in.)
No, I'm too fiery for this watercolour ideology. I'm trying to develop more *extreme* and *interesting* opinions... (Opt out.)
It is not a place, it is a *moment* in time that can only arise in the right circumstances. In all of human history, it's only been achieved a handful of times...
I knew we could trust you. Remember -- *real democracy* is just around the corner for Revachol. When that real democracy kicks in we are all going to be so much happier.
That's a pity. *Real democracy* was just around the corner for Revachol. All the leading citizens are waiting there -- without you.
Must have been a false alarm, then.
There you have it. Sometimes holding the line *is* progress.
Speaking of, when are you going to get on that, bub?
Oh, right. Then let's get there... eventually?
How do you bring about those *circumstances*?
Sometimes, in the face of great disaster, defending the status quo *is* progress.
That's a stupid goal. (Shake your head dismissively.)
Then you've never lived through *real* chaos...
That's an honourable goal. (Nod your head approvingly.)
*Incrementally*.
Yes.
Is it?
History's greatest catastrophes have been brought about by people trying to make the world a better place *too quickly*...
It is, isn't it?
No.
What a fucking joke!
YAWN. You'd get there faster with a little *speed*.

dialoguetext: Do you believe the status quo is preferable to chaos and bloodshed?
*Tsk, tsk*. Just because you live in the *present* doesn't mean you have the right to place your needs above the needs of the *future*...
It's also post-industrial, post-ideological, and even *post-sexual*.
What sangfroid...
But what about all the things that are wrong *now*?
What benevolence...
You may never live to see the Kingdom of Conscience. Your children may not. Even your *grandchildren* might not. But that's no excuse not to keep working...
Partly because humanity will need to discard many of the categories that define and limit it today. The Kingdom of Conscience is post-capitalist, post-national...

That's the genius of *Dolores Dei*. She recognized that progress is meaningless if its gains are lost because of instability. *Real*, lasting change can only come about gradually. Increment by increment.
Sounds incredible. Allons-y! Let's go there right now. (Opt in.)
Okay, but what's the Kingdom of Conscience actually *like*?
What you *want* is immaterial. The Kingdom of Conscience is coming... WHETHER YOU LIKE IT OR NOT. (Only very slowly.)
Man, that sounds kind of terrible. I don't think I want to be a moralist anymore. (Opt out.)
The Kingdom is difficult to comprehend and even more difficult to describe...
Slow down, Mr. Reasonable! Did you miss the part about compromising and taking things slow?
This sounds mega boring. Count me out. (Opt out.)
Wait, is the Kingdom of Conscience really about doing things, or just preserving the status quo?
That seems fine. I still want to live for the present, though. (Opt out.)
What rationality...
That's right. Remember -- *real democracy* is just around the corner for Revachol. When that real democracy kicks in -- a long time from now -- we are all going to be so much happier.
This is because I keep saying *none of the above* to political stuff, isn't it?"
It's *also* about that. But it's *also* more! Perhaps it's the hangover, perhaps it's a temporary surge of serotonin, but something tells you...
Tremble. THE TIME IS NOW. τὰ ὅλα.
What time?
Am I sure it's not just a joke, or some kind of coping mechanism?
This is because of the insane world-ending I've been saying isn't it? (Proceed.)

Time for THE SHOW. For τὰ ὅλα. The hallowed time of fear and disintegration. A countdown has begun. All will collapse on itself. The world will disappear into a single grain of blackness. All sound will be muted. All life will scream.
Yes. You spoke the words of the παλίντροπος, and the houses of Perikarnassis. Items, people, even WORDS will tumble, all will lose its meaning in the coming years. That is why you marked yourself.
It's *totally* also a coping mechanism.
Wait, wait -- when did this *countdown* begin?
Monday morning. The moment you arrived in this reality. You are the first crack in the sheer face of god. From you it will spread.
I *do* think the world might end soon. (Opt in.)
Uhm... yeah, I'm going to opt out of the 'παλίντροπος' whatever it is. This was a mistake. (Opt out.)
Yeah... I don't think the time is *now*. Later maybe. [Leave.]
No. You cannot *leave*. The countdown has not yet reached XERO.
τὰ ὅλα? What's that?
οῦ λόγου δ' ἐόντος ξυνοῦ ζώουσιν οἱ πολλοὶ ὡς ἰδίαν ἔχοντες φρόνησιν.
The face of the woman fractures. There will be herd killing. We all become vapour.
Okay, yes. Maybe it *is* just the hangover talking. Or some kind of joke you're playing on yourself instead of working on the case...
I'm... a little afraid.
So you should be. The world island crumbles at your feet and in the far plain -- παλίντροπος.
Perhaps -- just a thought -- this has something to do with the hangover?
Hey, so we've been monitoring you internally, and now we know your *copotype*.
Wait, there are *copotypes*?
Okay. What am I?
[Discard thought.]
Yes. Guess what's yours?
Guess.
Sorry cop? I'm sorry, I'm not sure...
Cool cop?
Some kind of... weapon-cop?
I'm sorry you had to monitor me.

dialoguetext: Okay, just for the length of this short demonstration, please say something that isn't *I'm sorry*. Guess. What is it?
Yes. Sorry Cop. The cop who's sorriest. Let's make it official, then, shall we?
No, you're the *Sorry Cop*. The cop who's sorriest. Let's make it official, then, shall we?
Okay, okay, but what are the *other* copotypes?
conditionstring: IsTHCPresent("apocalypse_cop") == false  and  IsTHCPresent("superstar_cop") == false  and  IsTHCPresent("boring_cop") == false

dialoguetext: Uhm, won't the other copotypes be jealous?
I'm sorry. (Opt in.)
Oh, you know. Apocalypse, Superstellar, The Advanced Interesting Cop. Liquid Shadow Cop. But you're too sorry to say those things, so -- here we go?
What? Jealous of the *Sorry Cop*? I think they'll be fine. Don't worry.
Of course you are. It's okay. See if you can get something out of this. Like... info, or... maybe every time you say you're sorry you get a million bucks?
Huge lack of enthusiasm going on in here.
You know, actually I'm *not* sorry. I change my mind.
Fuckin'... *they* should be sorry!
Yes-yes, impotent rage and lamentation. Let's wrap it up?
They'll be super, super fine. It'll be totally *okay*. You can dual-copotype from sorry to anything.
No, you don't. C'mon. You'll be back to saying sorry in two minutes. Stop wasting time and begin The Repentance.
No. I'm *really* not sorry. Fuck off! (Opt out.)
Wow. Okay. *Fuck off*? Maybe we were wrong about you then...
Check out the big balls on Fire Cop...
That won't happen.
I was kinda hoping I'm the Apocalypse Cop.
I was kinda hoping I'm the Superstar Cop.
I was kinda thinking I'm the Regular Cop.
That is only a ludicrous daydream. Guess again. You're the...
I don't want this. I really don't care about honour... at all.
No! You're not a snivelling shit-heel chasing imaginary karma-coupons! Not for this, nor the afterlife! Fuck this honour shit!
Ah... ahhh. You continue to display such humility. This is to be admired! Refusing praise for your personal integrity is most honourable indeed.
You brought much shame on your family today. Your name will forever be tarnished by this most shameful of deeds. Be forever banished, Shameful One!
Good. You feel its presence. Now you are ready for the *Rite of Honour*.
Honourable One, you have accumulated a substantial amount of honour points on your life-path. You are a man most virtuous.
Go forth and commit even more honourable deeds. And should your resolve ever waiver, remember The Rite of Honour. It will always cleanse a man's soul...
You're not hearing me. I'm not some creepy honour-lover. Period.
This honour thing feels overwhelming. Maybe I should open my heart to it?
Wait, there were honour points?
My honour is my life.
Isn't honour sort of an archaic concept?
Of course there were honour points. Did you think no one was paying attention to all of your honourable deeds, Honourable One?
Living in the name of virtue and doing noble deeds while expecting nothing in return is not *archaic*. How can you even think that?
Selflessness forms the basis for the warrior code. An ageless code, as fit for nomadic Iilmaraan tribes traversing the vast Red Plateau in Provincia Gurdi as it is for your neighbourhood postman.
Yes. Your deeds have spoken for you, Honourable One, but to fully drape one's self in an eternal cloak of honour a ritual must be completed. A *Rite of Honour*...
I only try my best. It's the most any of us can do.
Oh, the modesty on this one. Another 10 honour points for you, sir!
A warrior code, you say... I do feel like a warrior. This whole thing is beginning to sound very *me*.
It sounds rather arrogant, a secretive self-regard.
No, no, no! You see, you're putting the needs of *others* above *yours*. *You* get nothing in return -- not even praise. You always get the short, *noble* end of the stick...
Don't think about it too much! Just say it -- are you ready to get knee-deep in honour?
Hold your horses! This is a mistake. Honour is meaningless to me. [Discard thought.]
You are on the fast track to becoming one of the rarest, most revered of all police officers -- an honour cop.
Most dishonourable are those who have known honour, carried honour in their hearts, and then disowned honour. They are the *honourfallen*...
Even among the honourable only the most dignified are deemed worthy -- but you, oh honourable one, have excelled... in honour.
Honour comes from deep within you and to truly know oneself, to *know* one's honour, one must reach deep within oneself and *touch* one's honour...
You need to bring the thumb of your right hand -- your sword hand -- to your rectum and stick it in there to form the Arch of Honours.
All I ever wanted was to live with dignity -- to die with honour. (Stick your thumb in your ass.)
You're crazy if you think I'm just going to stick a finger in my ass! NO WAY!
What? I don't know... just like that? Outside? What about people?
What? What if someone comes and *sees* me?
People will be in awe, admiring a police officer most honourable in a sacred ritual of uttermost righteousness.
Then they will witness honour so great it seems nigh impossible a single man can contain it. They will admire you, Honourable One.
"WHAT ARE YOU DOING?!" The lieutenant jumps away from you.
Congratulations, Honourable One! You have become a member of a noble faculty. A man kneels, an Honour Cop rises...
"I am honouring myself, lieutenant."
"Nothing, you wouldn't understand. It's an honour thing."
"Who, me? Nothing. I'm doing nothing, Kim."
"Scratching my ass. What's the big deal?"
"The big deal?" The lieutenant rolls his eyes. "I guess we really do come from different upbringings..."
Good. That was a lie most honourable. Sometimes we must hide the truth from those who wouldn't understand it. The Less-Honoured Ones.
It is an honour to serve with you, Honour Cop!
"Then why are you elbow deep in your pants like..." He suddenly stops as if realizing he doesn't want to hear the answer. "Never mind, officer. Carry on."
"Really? It seems more like a personal hygiene thing." He leans even more away from you. "But let's not delve deeper."
You're right. The lieutenant, although a noble man, does not understand honour like you do. Best not to waste time trying to explain. Lead by example.
"I can see that, but do you have to do it where everyone can see you?" He looks shocked.
"Have you no self control?" Then realizing the naivete of the question he looks at the ground. "Please spare me this sight."
"Well... uh... don't!" The lieutenant looks truly shocked.
The lieutenant is a noble man, but he does not *know* honour like you and I do. Best not to waste time trying to explain. Lead by example.
Mhmh-mhmh, you are like a wondering knight-monk setting right the wrongs of the world you come upon.
Are you ready to drink deep from the cup of honour?
Meaningless?! Vulgar knave, how dare you besmirch the honour of honour points... It hurts the eyes to look upon filth like you. Begone.
My honour is my life. It's what separates me from the treacherous wömen.
Okay...
It's clear you like the hard stuff, bröther.
The what? Sounds like my stomach is growling...
What is my lower intestine going on about?
[Discard thought.]
Evening falls. The time has come to take the vows.
Vows?
The Vows of Blööd and Flesh.
Lower intestine? The term is METABOLIC AND CIRCULATORY SYSTEM.
Okay, but... what's *the hard stuff*?
*Fascism*, bröther.
No, no. When the blööd and the flesh call, there is no discarding them. Speak true, do you like *the hard stuff*?
What is *the hard stuff*?
What *is* fascism, though?
Am I having some kind of stomach seizure?
*Fascism* sounds so bad, though. What if we called it something else? Like, uh, *traditionalism*?
Many things, but it's möstly about trusting your gut. Who does your gut tell you is the source of Revachol's problems?
Foreigners?
Yes, them, but also...
Financiers?
Leftist academicians?
Liberals?
...wömen.
Wömen?
Wö-Men. Men of Wö. You don't like them. They're insane. Their idiocy needs to be scrubbed off this world with rubbing alcohol. Wömen need to go back to the fucking kitchen.
That's what fascism boils down to. The rest is also important, but the *main thing* is that wömen need to *know their place*.
Stomach truth. You're having a stomach *truth*.
Ökay. Yes. Let's call it that. Good thinking.
That sounds much better. Traditionalism. You like the sound of that.
Okay, stomach. I've made up my mind about fascism. (Proceed to the Jüdgement.)
You're going to keep your vöws, right? Keep your vöws, bröther!
Absolutely not. I'm not going to be played by an upset stomach. (Opt out.)
I will keeps my vöws... for the glory of the Revacholian nation. (Opt in.)
Why am I getting this?
Because you've said the hard things, that others won't say. The gööd things. You've said them many times.
I thought you were my circulatory system?
Quit stalling, bröther! We were talking about the weakest, worst, most insane thing. The weak link!
There's a slow, painful growl somewhere in your intestines, knocking on your alcohol-engorged liver...
For the nation... smart. Best not to mention *the wömen* too often. That's why you're the head and I am the stomach.
Pat your stomach. [Finish thought.]
It is one of betrayal and disappointment.
No, fascism is about industry and politics and nationhood, not wömen. I'm absolutely okay with women.
Of course you are, bröther. Of course. (A wink-shaped growl sounds from your ass.)
For the nation... smart. Best not to mention *the wömen issue* too often. People are not ready.
But I'm a feminist!
Föminist? No! It can't be. Not you. No one believes this.
Did you know you can FORGET Thoughts? Go to your THOUGHT CABINET and FORGET all about föminism.
You are *The Destroyer*, the bane of inanimate matter.
Gaze upon me, stuff, and despair!
No, I'm just a disempowered individual trying to take my disempowerment out on everyday objects.
Yeah, I rip shit apart.
Kudos.
Look! There's a discarded milk carton on the floor. Why don't you destroy that, too?
No, I actually feel sorry for the things I've destroyed. (I'm sorry, milk carton.)
Good idea. Fuck you, milk carton, this is all *your* fault!
You're right, that's definitely not the behaviour of a destroyer at all. That's just severe anger-management problems and a disregard for property rights.
Bent metal, broken glass... your path lies strewn with the broken forms of everyday objects...
The hardened vitreous enamel, at once sleek and light, adds a glow to your cheeks and a spring to your step. Just imagine what a full suit of this stuff could do for you!
The white ceramic cuirass hugs your torso, shielding your vitals without adding much bulk to your form...
You look down at the white ceramic sabatons hugging your arches and calves, surprised at how well they fit.
As you fold your fingers into a fist, you realize you could knock anyone out with one punch... the white ceramic gloves wrap around your digits comfortably.
I remember a feeling -- being worried about crossing paths with someone in this armour.
This is the long sought after *enemy technology*. I can't just enjoy it -- I must *study* it.
Yeah, I *want* the full suit!
This gear could line my pockets with cash. I could probably sell it to some other cops.
Then you should prepare -- analyse this armour, figure out its vulnerabilities.
Yes. You should analyse the armour, figure out its vulnerabilities.
It may be a while before you have all the pieces. In the meantime, you should analyse the armour, figure out its vulnerabilities.
Certainly, but you may want to hold on to the armour you have for long enough to properly analyse it, figure out its vulnerabilities.
Remember, this is a highly specialized kinetic re-distributor meant to stop bullets. Wear it, observe its properties. See if there's a *weakness* in the design.
Remember, the vitreous enamel material acts as a kinetic re-distributor. It's meant to stop bullets. Wear it, observe its properties. See if there's a *weakness* in the design.
You really do feel more confident. Invulnerability does that. Even partial invulnerability.
Your movements cause tiny little clicks, like dice rolling somewhere far away, as the plates reorient to your motions.
I will be responsible with this. This is just to protect me from harm, not to show off.
Decked out in future-armour. Like a cop ought to be.
[Discard thought.]
The hardened vitreous enamel, at once sleek and voluptuous, adds a glow to your cheeks and a spring to your step. Just imagine what a full suit of this stuff could do for you!
You really do feel more confident. Invulnerability does that. Even partial invulnerability.
Well, you found that one piece you were after, anyway. Don't forget to enjoy it!
One down -- two pieces to go. Here I come.

dialoguetext: Two? Are you sure you're correct there? There was a helmet too. Three pieces more like. You were *ambitious*.
This is the long sought after *enemy technology*. I can't just enjoy it -- I must *study* it.
As your head is ensconced in the ceramic helm, you realize --
Well, it's a bit late to think about all this now, isn't it?
Better late than never, huh?
I guess so.
Vulnerabilities?
For the day you have to *fight* someone covered in the same material.
It is good to be an unstoppable ceramic man.
Son, you've really let yourself go -- it's a disgrace. But Coach Physical Instrument is going to get you back in prime condition. Even if it takes a million push-ups!
Yes sir! Forge me into organic steel, coach!
Does a master swordsman insult his own blade? No! I'm going to turn you into an athletic bench-mark, you big pussy!
Wait, why piss?
Let's do this, coach, I'm with you! (Opt in.)
Too much abuse for my taste. I'm more of an intellectual. (Opt out.)
When a man sets his mind and body on something and gives his hundred and ten percent, he is sometimes going to piss himself. It just happens. No shame in that.
Attention, attention! An old has-been giving up! Come see the has-been quitting again, everyone!
Behold, world -- here walks a sportsman, hands chalked and hair kept back with a bandana. The *homo athleticus!*.
I'm really, *really* not interested. [Discard thought.]
Coach Physical Instrument? Does that mean you'll call me a maggot and a nancy-boy to motivate me?
It's going to take blood, sweat, piss, and tears, but when I'm done with you, boy, you will be a Master Athlete!
Now that you've acquired some stimulants, it's time for a little pick-me-up. Time to *detect*.
What... but right *here*? Now?
Okay, my body is ready. Let's do this. (Try some speed.)
This is gonna be really bad for my health, isn't it?
See, that's your problem -- a lack of confidence. Speed can help you with that. It can help you with EVERYTHING.
I'm not doing this now. [Ignore thought.]
It's not ideal, no... But you need the zeal. Let's face it, you're never going to finish this case without cheating.
You raise the bottle, close a nostril and inhale *furiously*. The rush is almost immediate. It tastes bitter and caustic, and stings a bit inside your nose.
Mamma mia!
Good to have you back, Officer Supercop. The world has been waiting.
Now the taste is slowly receding into your throat... The rush is growing in intensity, your little heart pounding like a bird in a cage. A sweat breaks out across your brow, your jaw clenches...
And, let's be honest, there's a little chest pain -- the *good* kind, of course. You may wanna blast a Nosaphed or something.
This is so unprofessional of you. Think you can ignore this -- your *moral compass* telling you to sniff it? Guess again -- you'll be back here soon. You'll get the chance to choose more wisely.
You raise the Preptide bottle, press one nostril closed, and inhale *furiously* with the other. The rush is almost immediate. It tastes bitter and caustic, and stings a bit inside your nose.
Will it make me into a Supercop?
It will make you into *more* than that -- a Megacop! This is your modus operandi. This is how you've done it for *years*. Let's go!
"Hngfff..."

Hmmm, you could work with this high... Like, literally *work*: Solve the case, file some papers. Maybe clean up your hostel room, then solve *another* case, then start a side investigation into the para-natural, then build a radiocomputer...
Whooh, this shit is strong. This shit is disco.
"Kim, I did a little speed. I hope you don't mind. It was for professional reasons."
Feels great. Are there *any* downsides to this at all?
Cool, cool, let's boogie. [Finish thought and spring to action.]
"I'm not your mother." He avoids your gaze. "I don't care. Do what you have to do."
As long as you remain functional, he thinks. Now let's get back to work.
To *this*? You kidding?! There are downsides to *not* being on it.
There are *massive* downsides. It's a potent neurotoxin. You're turning yourself into a frayed idiot.
Time for a little truth. Tell the lieutenant you did some, clear the air.
Spring-spring! Everything is clear around you. You're ready to concentrate on the next task in the task chain.

In the bottom right corner of the screen there's a SPEED button! SPEED gives +1 to MOTORIC skills: Perception, Reaction Speed, Hand/Eye Coordination, Savoir Faire, Interfacing, and Composure. This is good before a White Check -- but damages your Morale.
You raise the Preptide bottle, press one nostril closed, and inhale *furiously* with the other. The rush is almost immediate. It tastes bitter and caustic, and stings a bit inside your nose.
You raise the bottle, close a nostril and inhale *furiously*. The rush is almost immediate. It tastes bitter and caustic, and stings a bit inside your nose.
You've passed up your chance to start using SPEED for now, but don't worry! The option to use it becomes available again in 1 hour.
Open the bottle.
No. No. I'm not doing it. [Ignore thought.]
There's a satisfying pop as the cap comes off, and the hair on your back rises like an army at attention. You've been here before. Welcome back, detective. You're home now...
Should I though? I may have a teeny-weeny heart attack problem.
Oh, yes. The chest pain and the dizziness. You've *suffered* long enough -- now it's time to drink, to live.
Why is it always about *you*? *Your* heart problem? *Your* coronary artery? Think about *us*. We're in this together. You and your wacky tie of substance abuse! Do it for *us*! Pop it open.
Fine. We're not worried... you'll crawl back to this bottle soon enough. We'll give you another chance. Booze *always* gives you *another* chance.

A golden sun melts down your throat, its rays filling your nostrils with sunshine. Your stomach melts from it -- into a happy gooey mess! So does your mind, all the bad things are melting. You're you again. A *real* cop. A real detective. *Incredibly* well done.
Well, hello. Someone seems to have found himself a bottle of *alcohol*. Here's where the *magic* happens.
Light reflects off the green glass of the Commodore Red. The gods have been generous. Better pop it open before they change their minds...
Light reflects off the thermal cup. The borscht may not look like much, but doubtless it'll get the job done. Better pop it open before it gets cold...
Pale-aged vodka? This is rare game indeed. The gods have been generous. Better pop it open before they change their minds...
What a *solid* can of mass-produced piss water. Well over 10% alcohol in this so-called *beer*. Pop it open before it gets too warm...
The light reflects off this bottle of sweet, sweet liquor -- a gift from above. The gods have been generous. Pop it open before they change their minds...
There's a satisfying pop as the cork jumps out, and the hair on your back rises like an army at attention. You've been here before. Welcome back, detective. You're home now...
There's a satisfying crack as the cap comes off, and the hair on your back rises like an army at attention. You've been here before. Welcome back, detective. You're home now...
There's a satisfying pop as the cap comes off, and the hair on your back rises like an army at attention. You've been here before. Welcome back, detective. You're home now...
Look at the bottle.
[Discard thought.]
Oh, no, you don't -- not this one. That's not *you*. You...
Wow, the gods of mass production have made this alcohol container *laughably* easy to open. A child could have done it.
I don't know about this...
Fine. We're not worried... you'll crawl back to this bottle soon enough. We'll give you another chance. Booze *always* gives you *another* chance.
Yes, it's *merciful* that way. It's your friend. Come back to it, we're all rooting for you to.
Not *all* of us...
What will be the repercussions if I take that sip?
Take a sip.
You see a flash of teeth -- a young woman smiling at you, near some railway overpass in your ruined past. She is gorgeous. And she is *yours*.
Nothing. Some *mental* stuff. Nothing to be worried about. Physically you'll be strong as an ox!

In the bottom right corner of the screen there's an ALCOHOL button! ALCOHOL gives +1 to PHYSIQUE skills: Physical Instrument, Half Light, Electrochemistry, Endurance, Pain Threshold, and Shivers. This is good before rolling a White Check -- but damages your Morale. And remember...
From the void we came. And to the void we must return!

A golden sun melts down your throat, its rays filling your nostrils with sunshine. Your stomach melts from it -- into a happy gooey mess! So does your mind, all the bad things are melting. You're you again. A *real* cop. A real detective. *Incredibly* well done.
You've passed up your chance to start drinking ALCOHOL for now, but don't worry! The option to start drinking becomes available again in 2 hours.
No. No. I'm not doing it. [Ignore thought.]
Whoa! In your hand: *pyrholidon* -- the double rainbow of synthetic hallucinogens. Rare and gritty, a product of the age of atomic power.
Look at the little puck of liquid.
Atomic power? Too scary. [Ignore thought.]
What a funny little cap! Don't let the *scary* medical warnings throw you off. It's an inadequate antidote to radiation poisoning, but a *potent* antidote to *boredom*.
It's not gonna *give* you radiation poisoning, stupid. Pyrholidon is a perfect match for a bad-ass junkie cop who's looking for a little *heat*.
Wait -- radiation poisoning sounds scary.
You need to lower the radiation levels, your stomach thinks. Slurp it.

No problem. This one's for the brave and sensitive ones anyway. It could improve your human interactions. But -- you threw that chance away. No matter, in a few hours you'll get the urge again. Maybe then you'll choose more courageously?
That's really not what I'm looking for. [Ignore thought.]
Hmm... open the cap.
The container is warm to the touch -- or is that just the anticipation? You screw the lid open and look. A little slit on the side lets you just *slurp* it up, like an oyster! C'mon! Slurp it!
Slurp it *aggressively*.
Slurp it, but only a little.
I'm not going to slurp it. [Ignore thought.]
Wait, won't Kim see me slurp it?
What is he, your mother? Is Kim your *au pair*? Slurp it, slurp the morsel of danger-joy!
You suck a manly dose of the extremely chemical-smelling liquid into your mouth. There it seeps into your tongue. When you swallow it's already almost all gone.
You suck a minuscule drop of extremely chemical-smelling liquid into your mouth. There it seeps into your tongue. When you swallow it's already almost all gone.
Tastes like fire.
Tastes like gasoline.
Tastes like... an anti-radiation drug.

It tastes like *many* things, all melting into one conflagration in the back of your throat. As you look around, the world slowly *exists*. As it did before. Only now gentle flames lick at its edges, as though it were a photo burning.
Tastes like a kiss.
Really?
No. Of course not really. It's just a metaphor. The effect of that otherworldly drop of liquid is slower, more subtle than that of real flames -- yet just as warm.
Oh god, on *fire*?
Not *really*. It's just a metaphor. The effect of that otherworldly drop of liquid is slower, more subtle than that of real flames -- yet just as warm.
This warmth. It makes you want to share your *discovery* with Kim!
No. I can't see it.
Of course, it's just a metaphor. It's just a metaphor. The effect of that otherworldly drop of liquid is slower, more subtle than that of real flames -- yet just as warm.
"Kim, I just did a drop of that anti-radiation drug. It's great."
This is going to be *so* useful in my line of work. [Finish thought.]
Will I be able to stand straight and walk?
"I'm happy for you," he answers.
His glasses turn golden as the fire reflects off the lenses. You feel this man is your brother.
Just don't *mix* it with anything, he thinks, looking you over. Thankfully his sense of balance seems okay. Whatever. I'm not getting involved.
Wow, Kim's bad ass. *Or* he's had a druggie partner? Whoa. That's probably it! He's seen it before.
Look at all these guys go off like fireworks as information pours into you -- about the lieutenant's simple remark: *I'm happy for you*. This stuff is great.
Why not? This government-developed substance seems very non-intrusive. You could even operate heavy machinery! Fire-machinery!
Please don't actually operate any fire-machines.
Already you can tell you're going to be slurping a *lot* more pyrholidon! This stuff is going to give you insight into that little flickering light hidden in all human beings.
If you can keep the vomit in. Because it sort of also makes you want to throw up.

In the bottom right corner of the screen there's a PYRHOLIDON button! It gives +1 to PSYCHE skills: Empathy, Suggestion, Authority, Inland Empire, Esprit de Corps, and Volition. This is good before rolling a White Check -- but damages your Health.
His glasses turn golden as the fire reflects off the lenses. Once again, you are filled with the certainty: this man is your brother.
You suck a minuscule drop of extremely chemical-smelling liquid into your mouth. There it seeps into your tongue. When you swallow it's already almost all gone.
You suck a manly dose of the extremely chemical-smelling liquid into your mouth. There it seeps into your tongue. When you swallow it's already almost all gone.
You've passed up your chance to start using PYRHOLIDON for now, but don't worry! The option to use it becomes available again in 4 hours.
You picked the best one! This soldier is fat and succulent. What are you waiting for? Light up -- re-become yourself!
Oh yes, *bratan*! (The tie is shaking around your neck excitedly.) Please light up. You *need* a trooper between your lips right now! Calm your shit down. Go to Pleasureland. Become a *genius*!
I don't wanna light it right *now*, people are watching.
People are watching. What a pussy! People are *always* watching -- that's what makes it *cool*, now come on!
Shut up and light that shit! You wanna be an idiot for the rest of your life? This shit will give you the cool edge you need.
There it is, a brave little army in your pocket. The First Smokes Platoon. Twenty brave souls standing in salute, ready to step into the fire for you, sir...
Light it up!
Get a load of this rock and roll cop here, people! Johnny Thundercop fishes a cheap lighter out of his pants. With a flick of the thumb there's fire, a primal satisfaction. Here we go...
I already had a heart attack. Maybe smokes are harmful?
Put it back in the pack. [Ignore thought.]
The lighter's dark green, disposable plastic. Safety's off -- in your case, the safety is *always* off.
No, what's *harmful* is fretting and worrying. It's the *stress* that's wearing your ticker down. The smokes will soothe it. They're medicinal.
Step into the light and be reborn in the cleansing flame, *bratan*!
Will they *always* be looking, though? Because they might go to the toilet or you might be in a different...
"Hey, you can't smoke in here." The girl's voice betrays little interest or enthusiasm. She doesn't even look up when as she continues: "Please don't fuck with Frittte."
The man in the stinking tracksuit nods solemnly. "Having a well-deserved break from your adventures. It's what we all need sometimes."
...bla bla bla. Boring. Light it up!
Already you regret it -- looking at the pack... But don't worry. You can come back to this later. The army of smokes is honourable and faithful to you. You have your entire *life* to return to it.
Pull one out of the pack.
I'm not going to do it. [Ignore thought.]
Shut up. It's already happening...
What are the repercussions if I do this?
Dip that bad boy in the flame and breathe in.
No. Throw it away at the last second. [Ignore thought.]
Repercussions? There's a high risk of GLORY? With a mild chance COOL *GENIUS*. Smoking makes you into an INTELLECTUAL, everybody knows that.

Thick, warm smoke gets sucked down into your lungs. Immediately you feel a warm nostalgia fill your head, body *and* soul. A nostalgia for *yourself*, the man you were in your youth. Johnny Thundercop is back. And he's chill as balls.

In the bottom right corner of the screen there's a CIGARETTES button! CIGARETTES give +1 to INTELLECT skills: Logic, Rhetoric, Conceptualization, Visual Calculus, Encyclopedia, and Drama. This is good before a White Check -- but damages your Health.
Get a load of this rock and roll cop here, people! Johnny Thundercop fishes a cheap lighter out of his pants. With a flick of the thumb there's fire, a primal satisfaction. Here we go...
It *will* help you concentrate a bit, that much is true.
It only lets you concentrate because you're in *nicotine withdrawal*. It only mitigates it's own...

Thick, warm smoke gets sucked down into your lungs. Immediately you feel a warm nostalgia fill your head, body *and* soul. A nostalgia for *yourself*, the man you were in your youth. Johnny Thundercop is back. And he's chill as balls.
You've passed up your chance to start smoking CIGARETTES for now, but don't worry! The option to start smoking becomes available again in 3 hours.
Why does art inspire you so much?
It does, yes -- but what *is* art?
No, art is for arrogant blowhards. Why am I getting this?

Excellent question. Art is a diverse range of visual, literary, auditory, and performative creativity! It's an expression of imagination and technical skill. Additionally, it's history, criticism and pure enjoyment...
Is it? Yet your eye constantly seeks out the most critical side of any aesthetic confrontation. You follow the expressions of imagination and technical skill with curiosity...

Yes! You seek substance. No vapid representations and reproductions of social mores, as made manifest in stuffy biennials, we're talking real *living art* here. Become the Art Cop. Half art critic -- half cop.

Have you looked in the mirror lately? You have the exact features of a savage art critic, with that beard and those clothes! Dishevelled and *prophetic*. Perhaps you should try to critique architecture too!

Of course not, it's autism. Box-drawing. Masturbation with a ruler and a sextant or whatever they use. You should demean and criticize the genteel institution of architecture. While extolling the virtues of the *pure* arts.
In short, art is the highest form of human communication -- representation, narrative, emotion and agency intertwined.
Hold on, is architecture also art?
Would I fit into the art world? I mean...
I guess I *have* been feeling critical lately.
That's stupid. Architecture is stupid.

Such vigour! Already you express a sharp descriptive mind, ready to slice through the empty and superficial in favour of the *sublime* and the *beautiful*... Do it. Become the Art Cop. Half art critic -- half cop.
[Discard thought.]
Wait, but don't I have to be 100% cop -- to get the case finished and all that?
Okay. If 50% art critic is what's needed to free me from rote repetition, so be it. (Opt in.)
No. I cannot risk another copo-diversion at this point. Go away! (Opt out.)

Exactly. It's not *only* your duty to only catch the criminals of the street, you must also apprehend criminals of the printing press and the gallery -- the trite and derivative artists and writers of the world!

dialoguetext: "After life death."
"Good, I've unlocked the filament. After ending the call please press PRINT to access the filament."
"This is the police. Please open this thing!"
The voice recites: "I am contractually obliged to protect the privacy of the filament holder Fortress Accident. Without filing a warrant with Lintel I cannot give you access to this filament."
"I'm afraid we're not doing that. Unless we want to wait for a month."
"Now, can you please repeat the password?" the voice in the machine asks again. She sounds cold in the damp air.
"What's Fortress Accident?"
"The company on whose name the terminal you're currently using has been registered to."
"Do you have any other information about this company?"
"One moment..." You hear her flip through a catalogue, before she reads out with studious care:
"'Fortress Accident SCA produces revolutionary interactive call-in radio games' -- that's what the catalogue says."
"Wow. So conceptual."
"And what's that -- this 'interactive call-in radio game'?"
The static drowns her response. "Any other questions?" you hear her ask when the connection finally improves.
"Let's try this again. I think I may have the right password for the personal log."
"Let's look around. There's no use trying to guess the answer."
"Maybe *he* knows something." The lieutenant nods toward Tiago.
A machine stands in the corner, watched over by the figures on the stained glass window. It's turned on and quivering with soft electricity.
The lieutenant doesn't say anything, but you can sense that he doesn't like you meddling with the machine.
Machine's keyboard is still illuminated, revealing virescent PLAY and PRINT buttons.
The first entry, made on the 4th February '51 by an unknown author, is short and concise:
Doesn't it get lonely, sitting there all by herself?
"Lonely?" For the first time you hear her chuckle through the rustle of static. "Why would it get lonely, I get to talk all day to people like you over a warm cup of tea."
"Doesn't it get lonely, doing this job?"
Let it go.
"I looked inside the core, but the tape on the filament just said "LOG (FEB-MAR)".
"Sorry, I forgot to look inside the core to check what filament is inside."
"Please end the call and do that."
The lieutenant leans closer, scouring the printout over your shoulder. Just as you finish reading he looks up, muttering under his breath:
Read the second entry.
Let go of the printout.
"Fourth of February? That's over a month ago... Whoever set up those machines has been here for quite a while."
"Do you think this log might be connected to the case?"
"Our case? No, I don't think so. It must be some local..." his eyes wander to the various machines around him, "*eccentric*."

"6th FEB, '51: Had a little chat with the local fishermen. Said I shouldn't go near that place, that the church was *spooky* and ridden with *narcotics*. It's a little spooky, alright. Still haven't figured out the electricity."
Read the third entry.
See? Even one of the spookers themselves says it's unnerving.
What was that about narcotics? This could prove to be interesting.
"Wait, *narcotics*?" (Look around the derelict building.)
"I doubt that we can find any. It's just idle fishermen's gossip to scare away the kids." He looks at the stained glass window.
"Nothing *spooky* about this place either, it's just abandoned. And cold. And in an awful part of town..."
"7th FEB, '51: Finally got the electricity in! Next on the agenda: a new antenna. I'm thinking ESKER series? Something advanced."
Read the fourth entry.

"8th FEB, '51: Bought the antenna, had some problems setting it up, called Simo for help. Heard the others are back to *making art* (drinking somewhere out of town). Sulisław started a rock band again, Lexie has been seen asking money from strangers..."
Artists, yet again!! Harassing citizens, stealing badges, 'occupying' public spaces with 'installations' like the one here...

"But at least the artists have their act together -- they're qualified labour, they can get work anywhere: graphic design, ads. The programmers are doing fine too, I mean, they're programmers. The writers, though... they're fucked."
Read the fifth entry.
"Artists, programmers, *Lexie* -- who are all those people?"
"Her friends, colleagues?" He shrugs. "She must be quite educated if she knew how to set up all this machinery."

"I just have to find out what caused that data loss and be done with it. Still don't understand how it managed to wipe out the backup when the backup *wasn't even connected to the front*. I know, I know... everyone thinks it's impossible; they say I must be lying. I'm here to set it right."
"A data loss?"
"Seems like something to do with radiocomputers -- unfortunately, I don't know enough about them to understand what the author is saying."

"12th FEB, '51: Brought some food from the grocery store. Apparently there's a strike going on in the harbour. Definitely not happy to see the Martinaise people again. Everything's now set up in the church, going to start working tomorrow 8 AM."
"The strike..." He strokes his chin. "We're nearing the date of the murder."

"25th FEB, '51: I've been sending data up to Lintel for a while now, trying to recreate the data loss, but nothing. Didn't even feel like logging in the disappointment. But I did discover a curious *audio-spatial* anomaly at the back of the church. I've named it *the swallow*. (It swallows sound.) Need to get some mics."
Read the sixth entry.

"28th FEB, '51: Yes, the first recordings confirm that the swallow is real and I'm not just losing my mind. It's a pillar of silence with a diameter of approximately three meters. Seems like the higher I go, the less I record. This might be a coincidence. Or it *could* be connected to the data loss that led me here."

"MARCH, '51: Some kind of young *discomen* have appeared next to the church. I've been trying to record the silence to find the epicentre, but now it turns out I've also been capturing the future of dance music, one neo-disco song over and over again..."

"Fortunately, the song is so monotonous I was able to devise an algorithm to factor it out. The other day one of the discomen came in. Before I could even say hello, she got scared and left. Good, I don't want anyone distracting me from my work."
Read the seventh entry.
"The pillar of silence! She *is* talking about the silence... Is she suggesting it's more than just an architectural quirk?"
Read the eighth entry.
Read the ninth entry.
"She must be describing Acele."

dialoguetext: "The girl on the ice? Sounds like her, yes."
"MARCH '51: A new 2m AUX cable, noodles, crackers, Ping-Ping energy drinks, water, TOOTHPASTE, gum, also some canned air..."

"MARCH '51: I got a call from the repeater station. Someone has tried to access the radiocomputer in our old office in Martinaise. Can't do anything about it; the storekeeper still doesn't want to let me inside the building. Thinks I'm part of some kind of *curse*. How Martinaise of her."
Read the tenth entry.
"Why would she need an antenna?"
"Why would anyone need *any* of this equipment here?" He steps on a wire running on the ground, inspecting it with his boot.
"Is she talking about...?" The lieutenant looks to his right, toward the silence.
"But what could it be?" (Look at the water basins behind you.)
The lieutenant doesn't answer. He follows your gaze, studying the basins. The water shines in them. No ripples.
"That's me. I was the one who broke into that radiocomputer! And the storekeeper must be Plaisance..."
"I knew it wasn't a good idea to meddle with that machine..."
"We should talk to her," the lieutenant whispers, "after she has rebooted the machine."

"Arrived at the church. The door was boarded up, so I used a crowbar to get inside. Looks like the place has been deserted. Nothing out of the ordinary, but I'll ask around. Need to figure out how to get the electricity in."
See -- *ridden* with narcotics. Just like Andre said.
"Keep reading, I'm interested now -- I want to know what's that radio anomaly that sent this person here in the first place."
"Something about the backup data getting destroyed... and how everyone thought it was the author's fault." He adjusts his glasses. "Let's just keep reading."
Then why doth the lieutenant protest against spending time here? So often?
This is a *human interface* -- a retired person sitting behind a switchboard somewhere.
"I wouldn't know, I'm only here for passwords."
That's why she does this.
A hint system is not part of the protocol for repeater stations.
Press PLAY again.
"I think these people worked in the radiocomputer games business. The one we saw in the Doomed Commercial Area. They must be her former co-workers."
No-no. It was a great idea. You're learning things. This is how you learn things about machines.
Password. Of course it would have a password. That's why there's a human administrator involved.
You should ask her for a hint.
That sounds bad -- a log-in *attempt*. Something a criminal would do.
"Yes, but this machine looks just like the one in Doomed Commercial Area."
"It's also quite similar to the one we have down at the station. Must be the same model." He inspects the machine's framework, careful not to touch anything.
The one you saw earlier was the Rehm Civic -- this is the Rehm *Prefect*, a model number RC7024, equipped with a Feld mainframe and a Rehm-compatible Interim printer.
A quaint little box of radio waves.
The Rehm Prefect is the governmental version of the commonly used Rehm Civic model. Although mostly based on the same technology, the Rehm Prefect is equipped with better noise attenuation circuits.
"Fortress Accident... like the one in the Doomed Commercial Area?"
"I have two machines registered to this company name in Martinaise -- one on Saint-Brune, the other on Rue de Saint-Ghislaine."
"Saint-Brune -- that's the church," the lieutenant gestures around him, "and Rue de Saint-Ghislaine, that's the Doomed Commercial Area."
Saint-Brune -- that's the church; Rue de Saint-Ghislaine -- the Doomed Commercial Area.
"Anything else I can help you with?"
For setting up her radiocomputer.
She must be talking about her former colleagues from Fortress Accident. They all sound like *radio game people*.
A shiver runs through you as you look to your left, toward the silence.
That discoman? Must be Acele.
"Okay then, thanks." [Leave.]
"Have you by any chance heard the *viejita* say the password to her radiocomputer?"
"Too many times, ese. You need it for something?"
"I think we're done here, ese." The figure crawls off into the darkness above.
"Hey, who's there?"
"This is the police. Show yourself!"
"Habitual alcohol use has made you into a scared little pussy, homes. But don't worry, everything's gonna be alright -- you've come to the right place."
"You must be the crab-man."
"What are you doing here?"
"Do you know where the other spooker is?" (Point at the strange machines around you.)
"You've been here a long time. Do you know why the church was abandoned?"

dialoguetext: "Other spooker? Oh, esa viejita muy estudiosa!" He laughs. "Dunno, homes."
"Oh hey, wey. There's coffee in the back... Oh, wait, I meant the Mother's love."
Say nothing. Be quiet for now.
The man leans forward a little, fixing you with a steady, unreadable gaze, then speaks...
Hold your peace.
"I'm not scared. I just don't understand why the female sexual organs have to be associated with weakness."
"You've really got a case of frayed nerves. *Pussy* in this usage comes from *pusillanimous*. Everybody knows that."
"Here you can receive the Mother's love, and, when you're ready, she will take your hand and lift you out of the despair at the bottom of the bottle."
The lieutenant whispers to you, quietly. "This man is obviously a habitual narcotics user. Do we really need to question him?"
I'm put off by this religious stuff, he thinks -- and maybe the ceiling-climbing, too. It's all very hard to square with the lieutenant's own view of reality.
He's a born preacher. Enjoy the rhetorical flourishes, but remain vigilant -- don't let him get too close. He's crazy.
"Chill out, man. Here you can receive the Mother's love, and, when you're ready, she will take your hand and lift you out of the despair at the bottom of the bottle."
Wait, what qualifies as *too* close?
I think I'm willing to try crazy. Anything to stop this suffering.
Giving away all of your possessions,  sacrificing a limb to appease an angry god, trying to live on air and light alone as though you were some kind of plant...
Vigilance is practically my middle name. I won't let anyone talk me into anything unreasonable.
That's right. You've got to watch your own back.
Seems it's already too late. Have fun on the kooky train.
The sinewy figure lingers on the wooden beams, blending into the shadows.
"How can you not know that when you both live here?"
"Don't really follow her comings and goings. Just see her typing on her computer now and then. We've got different interests."
"I'm doing a survey of passwords and passcodes, identifying regional trends. In the interests of public safety, of course."
"What'd you think of that? Makes me almost pity *la nihilista pequeña* when I hear it."
"Don't sweat it, vato. The password is 'AFTER LIFE DEATH.'"
That is true. But what comes after death?
"This is stupid. I don't even know what this is."
"I was like you once -- just dragging my feet to the next bottle... Shit was dark, homes."
"I know it's hard to admit that you have a problem... I was like you once -- couldn't take an honest look at the damage *el vino* was doing to my mind and my spirit."
"For some reason I feel like you have a point there."
Look at these crazies. What is this, a fucking intervention?
"You know, alcohol is central to my identity. If I wouldn't drink I just wouldn't be *me*."
"Oh, I'm very in touch with my suffering."
"Yeah, I guess I have a bit of a problem, and it's been getting out of hand lately, but..."
"How do you know what I'm feeling?"
"Not all of it. I was like you once. You don't know all the havoc *el vino* is wreaking on your mind and your spirit. Necesitas parar, homie."
"Great. More patronising. So original."
"*Estás crudo*, wey. I see deep inside you. Your body and spirit are suffering greatly from *overindulgment* and you don't even know it."
"I know it's hard to admit that you've got a problem. I was like you once -- couldn't take an honest look into my own heart and see I was in pain."
"Oh, hell no!" [Run away.]
"You've come back to face your cacodaemons. Good. You ain't gonna outrun them if you don't drop the bottle."
"Why do you keep talking about alcohol?"
"This is tiresome." [ Leave.]

"The grave's comin' for your little 'identity' sooner than you think, homes." He shakes his head sadly. "You sure you're ready? The Mother could set you free from all that shit." His words echo in the cold air of the church.
"It don't matter who *I* am, wey. I'm just bringin' you the message of the Mother's love. She don't want you to hang yourself on your own stubbornness." His words echo in the cold air of the church.
"Don't trust me -- trust the Mother. I'm only the messenger, homes." His voice echoes in the cold air of the church.
"You know what this is. It's truth, homes. Join me, become one with it -- aflame with the Mother's love." His voice echoes in the cold air of the church.
"That's all well and good, but we need to talk about the unlicensed occupation of ecclesiastic property."
"The only thing we need to talk about is how the Mother can really help you, homes." His voice echoes in the cold air of the church.
Wait, what does that even mean?
"This is the Church of the Mother of Silence. You are welcome here." He sways gently on the beams, waiting for you to take it all in.
"...your place among your fellows, your place in the world. I ain't got no use for such a place anymore."
"The right place for what?"
"What are you doing here?"
Hold on, stop it right there. "Pussy"? What's with this?
"I'm here to receive the Mother's love. You can, too, homes. And, when you're ready, she will take your hand and lift you out of the despair at the bottom of the bottle."
"I'm a police man. I need to talk to you about police things. I don't know anything about 'alcohol use.'"
"Oh yeah, sure." His eyes remain fixed on yours. "You don't know anything about alcohol use. You've got it *all under control*, wey. I can smell the control all the way over here."
"Oh yeah, sure." His eyes remain fixed on yours. "You don't know anything about alcohol use. You've got it *all under control*, wey. I saw you hide that control behind your back."
"I'm a police man. I need to talk to you about police things. I don't know anything about 'alcohol use.'" (Hide the bottle behind your back.)
"I was like you once -- just dragging my feet to the next bottle... Shit was dark, homes."
"I know it's hard to admit that you have a problem... I was like you once -- couldn't take an honest look at the damage *el vino* was doing to my mind and my spirit."
"This conversation is making me uncomfortable. Let's talk about something else."
"Okay, fine, I'm struggling. But you don't need to lecture me -- I know what I need to do."
"Not all of it. I was like you once. You don't know all the havoc *el vino* is wreaking on your mind and your spirit. Necesitas parar, homie."
"I know it's hard to admit that you've got a problem. I was like you once -- couldn't take an honest look into my own heart and see I was in pain."
"I'm doing just fine, thank you!"
"You know, actually, since we're here -- you may want to pay attention to what the ceiling climber is saying."
You know, he may be strange, but you might want to pay attention to what he's saying.
If the lieutenant agrees, then maybe, just maybe -- you should pay attention?
Look at these crazies. What is this shit?
"Coffee in the back"? Something familiar about that. Coffee and stale cookies...
"What was that about coffee? I feel like I've heard it somewhere before..."
"Look, man. I'm at liberty to talk about the sacred blaze of the Mother's glorious heart. But not about the coffee."
Is that... a man? Looks more like part of the carpentry of the building came alive and is now studying you intently.
The crab-man!
"Uhm... are you the crab-man?"
Hey and what was that about *the bottle* again? You haven't even drank that much lately! Lay off it already. Sheesh.
"This conversation is making me uncomfortable. Let's talk about something else."
"You don't know me. You don't know what I've been through!"
"Who do you think you are? Some crazy guy under the roof? What is this shit?"
'Tis not an act, my liege -- saving, perchance, he hath deceived his very self. This man is a zealot.
Whatever it is, he's quite confident about it -- just look how gracefully he sways.
You have no idea what the fuck he's talking about. Is he just trying to throw you off your game?
"Who's this Mother of Silence you keep talking about?"
"Oh, that's no simple question, ese. She is one who can't be painted or sculpted..."
"To be fair, it's really more like a spider."
He considers this for a moment. "I always thought of myself more like a *flame*. Flickering along the rafters and beams." He pauses. "It may be that I gotta work on my technique."
"Wait, did you also carve all those sculptures?" (Point at the nearest pillar.)
That's not the only technique he's working on. Look at those carved sculptures. And is that a satchel of tools over there?
"I was in a gang, wey. But my memories of that time are fading... Most of them are already gone."
"So you used to be in a gang, but you don't really remember it? Sounds convenient."
"I lost my memory, too. And it haunts me."
"I lost my memory, too, but I like it. It's like I get to create a whole new me, start again from scratch."
(Shake your head.) "So many people losing their memory... A certain portent of *doom*..."
"Convenience has got nothing to do with what goes on up there..." He gazes up at the ceiling.
There's a profound longing in that gaze. Like he wants to be one with whatever is up there, shrouded in darkness.
"No, man. You gotta let that shit go." He looks at you as if he wants to pat you on the back. "Then the Mother's light touch will fill you with rapture..."
"That's not really the point, ese." He frowns. "You gotta give yourself over to service... Service of the Mother, that is..."
"Sure am. Whittling wood used to be something I just did to busy my hands..."
"...now I use those same hands in service of something greater than my own restlessness."
"Naw, ese, it's not like that. Best thing that could happen to you -- losing your memory..."
"Do you remember your name, sir?"
The lieutenant is not particularly interested in this information. He's just trying to assert some control over the conversation.
"Tiago is my name. But those syllables don't mean much to me these days. A name isn't just your identity, but also, so to speak..."
"Tiago's my name, by the way, though the syllables don't mean much to me. A name isn't just your identity, but also, so to speak..."
"We are all one, who sing the Mother's glory."
"That's not quite right, but you're getting somewhere." He smiles enigmatically. "Any one of us could have been anything else..."
"Maybe that's why I feel so lonely -- without a name, I have no place."
