dialoguetext: I'm not doing that cross either.
Make the same gesture.

Good call. She left us all in the shits, don't give her a single thing. Just stand there in the apricot-coloured light of the window, secretly grinding your teeth. The woman smiles her distant smile, unmoved, struck in half by the crack in the glass.

Your fingertips touch your chest four times. When it's done, you're still standing in the apricot-coloured light of the window. The woman smiles her distant smile, unmoved, struck in half by the crack in the glass.
Serves her right. She only cares about her sovereign's orb and her silk robes and getting to the aerodrome on time -- to *leave*.
Leave me alone, woman. [Leave.]
There she still stands. In white, silver, and apricot, the young mother of humankind. A crack runs across her body. She is impossibly tall, oval-faced and sad -- a dark and radiant majesty.
"The old woman in the village was right..." He looks around. "This must be the Dolorian Church of Humanity in Martinaise -- or the Small Pinewood Church in some records..."
"You knew of the place?"
"It's a minor landmark, not easy to find. Most maps misplace it..." He lowers his voice. "It was built not long after Revachol's founding, 300 or so years ago by first-generation settlers."
"What else do you know?"
"There used to be seven stave churches on the coast. Les Sept Soeurs they call them -- The Seven Sisters. Only one remains. The rest were burnt in the Revolution, or used for building materials."
"We should be respectful here, although the building appears to be deserted. I do not believe we'll find the instigator here. Something else, perhaps..." He looks at the machinery lying around.
"We should be respectful here, although the building appears to be deserted. We have already found the instigator -- I'm not sure what else we could want from here..." He looks around.
"Yes." He looks around. "I wasn't sure before, but this must be the Dolorian Church of Humanity in Martinaise -- it's called the Small Pinewood Church in some records..."
On the coast of an uninhabited archipelago, where only animals had roamed before. In the wild reeds.
There it is again -- a small pang of guilt. It's time to ask him what happened here.
A pang of guilt? The lieutenant is leaving something out.
Respectful? Is the lieutenant a follower of Dolorianism?
"Do you know *why* it was abandoned?"
Better to not intrude upon him.
Cold air seeps in through the crack in the glass. The woman is keeping her colourful eye on both of you.
"I have a theory, yes." There's a pause, then he continues: "There was a police raid a while back. I heard the place was shot to pieces."
"The old woman in the village was being tactful with us when she didn't mention it. She has more respect for the RCM than many around here."
"You're not sure?"
"If I was here, I should find out what I was doing." (Proceed.)
"Better to forget about it." (Proceed.)
"Who conducted this raid?"
"Well... your station was involved, I hear. Although I can't be sure."
How come the lieutenant isn't sure? Is this confidential information?
"Three Precincts were involved in the raid and people say Precinct 41 was one of them."
"I don't remember being here."
"I..." (Look around.) "I guess I could have been here."
"I am pretty sure it was a clandestine operation. I don't know anything more about it. Why it was conducted, or who participated... I try not to pry into extra-district matters."

"I'm sorry, I'm not saying you were..." There's a pause. "It was a clandestine operation. I don't know anything about it. Why it was conducted or who participated. I try not to pry into extra-district matters."
"Good luck. You will not get information on a confidential operation from your station secretary just by calling. If you really don't remember -- it might be better to keep this one forgotten."
"I agree. It happened a while ago. It's unimportant to our business in Martinaise now."
"It happened a while ago. It's unimportant to our business in Martinaise now."
"Kim, are you a follower of Dolorianism?"
"Yes. We all are. Her name, body, and rule are synonymous with humanism. The laws we enforce are Dolorian in origin."
"It's not spiritual. It's constitutional. The Dolorian system does not demand faith -- only accordance."
"I didn't think you were spiritual."
"Hmm..." (Stroke your chin first.)
"I don't like her. She looks like a *leaver*."
"I have no idea what you mean by that. We've been standing here long enough. We should look around, or get out."
The woman looks by in silence, smiling enigmatically.
"It's Dolores Dei..." he says in a hushed voice. "I believe we are in the Dolorian Church of Humanity in Martinaise. Or the Small Pinewood Church in some records."
"It's Dolores Dei..." he says in a hushed voice. "The old woman was right. This is the Dolorian Church of Humanity in Martinaise. Or the Small Pinewood Church in some records."
Nothing, just the edge of the crack sparkles in the dark. There may have been a writing here but you cannot make out what it said.
Who is this older woman?
The motto? What does it say?
"Lieutenant, this used to say: 'After life, death -- after'..."
Step back.

The escutcheon on her throne says: Irene the Navigator. She is depicted as an older woman wearing thick rimmed eye-glasses, holding a golden *reichsapfel* in one hand and a scepter in the other. This is the queen Her Innocence Dei advised -- above, she herself is whole.

Small figures of wise men, common men, worshippers walk up the stairs to stand at her feet. Secret servicemen -- Therriers -- stand in a row guarding her. It must have taken years to produce this work in all its dizzying detail.
Below both women, in luminous blackletter: APRÈS LA VIE - MORT; APRÈS LA MORT - LA VIE DE NOUVEAU.
And then along the left side: APRÈS LE MONDE - LE GRIS; APRÈS LE GRIS - LE MONDE DE NOUVEAU.

AFTER LIFE -- DEATH; AFTER DEATH -- LIFE AGAIN. AFTER THE WORLD -- THE PALE; AFTER THE PALE -- THE WORLD AGAIN. This is the great leitmotiv of humanism, a summary of the effect of the discovery of this isola -- the Insulindian -- on human thinking. A tremendous sea change akin to finding life after death...
The mother of humanism towers above you -- a wax painting on a cracked pane of glass. Nothing has changed in her expression.
"...death, life again," he nods. "After the world, the pale; after the pale -- the world again."
Could these words be the password that unlocks the filament memory?
"This exaltation is common in Dolorian sacralism. In the early years it was even incorporated as the RCM's slogan. No more, however."
"Why?"
"What is the RCM motto now?"
"'Justice, Union, Prudence, and Force'."
"It was deemed *subservient* to use a strongly Moralintern-related motto. We're already suspected of bootlicking. The sentence was also seen as... too feminine. It was a macho thing."
"Cool."
"Not very feminine."
"I like the other one better."
"So do I."
"Not at all."
"Ice cool," the lieutenant nods.
"I like this. Puts the fear of god back in the f****ts."
"You are brutal and *dumb*." He says, his voice ice cold.
There is silence in the church. He wants there to be.
Wait, what exactly is an *innocence*?
Okay. When did she rule?
The highest category of historic individual -- an embodiment of the World Spirit.
A ruler?

More. An innocence is elected to office by the Founding Party, a precedent that has taken place a mere six times in the entirety of History. The legal system of the Reál Belt is built to accommodate innocentic rule, should it coincide with our time.
A tyrant?

In a way. An innocence is elected to office by the Founding Party, a precedent that has taken place a mere six times in the entirety of History. The legal system of the Reál Belt is built from the ground up to accommodate innocentic rule, should it coincide with our time.

An innocence is infallible. The decisions made by one are not decisions. They are inevitabilities -- what would have happened anyway, only accelerated, packed into decades instead of centuries. An Innocence is a continuous, compressed event, a sacred human being. It is an honour and a glory to live when one is in office.
Is one in office now?
No. We are alone.

Three hundred years ago, in the wake of the discovery of this isola -- the Insulindian -- by explorers from the continent of Mundi. She is, among other things, the innocence of interisolary travel and the connected world.
What else do I know about her?

Many things. You know she was a woman of the court, the wife of an influential *marchese*, and eventually the principal advisor to Irene La Navigateur, Queen of Suresne (modern day Sur-la-Clef). Also, that she was gorgeous beyond beauty.

Terribly. Women of the court were expected to play both contract bridge and chess sufficiently well to prove an interesting challenge to a man -- a similar grasp in matters of philosophy, theology, and science was encouraged. She was, by all means, a kept woman...

She made the most of her position in the Antedolorian court -- a court visited by the most prominent thinkers and artists of the day. In secret, she was becoming the era's pre-eminent philosopher of the state. A scalpel, a piercing gaze...

She was an almost preternaturally magnetic and intelligent individual. To her contemporaries she appeared out of time, a messenger from the future of the species. We *all* fell in love with her, head over heels. Even before she was declared an innocence her influence was tremendous.
Draped in ancient sadness. Are you sure you want to remember this bit of historic trivia? Standing under her long slender form like this, dwarfed...
Yes -- big bummer. Boring history. Gotta keep it light, man, keep it moving. Get fucked up instead.
Right. Better not to go poking any further.
Okay, what else? Was she smart?
Where is this coming from?
The past. It's a *silo* of sadness. Fermenting. You should keep away.
Fuck this pain, bratan. It's unhealthy.
Exactly. Back out of this corner of your mind by choosing the bottom-most option: "To hell with this."
To hell with this.
But... she was not hell. She is the opposite of that, the wind of paradise, stripping away the covers from the hearts of men...
There you stand, below her once more, with your hands on your side. Momentarily at a loss as to what to do with yourself.

It was on her advice that Irene La Navigateur sponsored a number of voyages into the pale. A costly, often tragic endeavour, ultimately vindicated by the discovery of the *New New World*, the piece of reality you're standing on...
I want more.

As did we all. The lands of Mesque and the Occident and even far-away Supramundi -- altogether twenty one of the forty Mondial nations of the time -- immediately accepted innocentic rule. Even before her crowning.

In a city called Advesperascit, in Vesper-Messina, her homeland. The name of the city means 'Evening comes,' but it happened on a winter's morning with the canals frozen and slush falling out of the sky.

Wow indeed. When her innocence was declared -- and the queen she had advised for years fell on her knees before her -- she was so overcome with emotion that her *lungs* started *glowing* in her chest...
How come?
That is why the lungs are the symbol of love for the cultures of the Reál Belt.

Oh yes... She looked like humanity's young mother, a perfect mother. Insultingly beautiful. It was as if her face and shoulders and hands were covered in a soft down of under-feathers. You know this well -- very well.
One of the men in this secret service killed her -- 22 years later. A young man who had come to suspect that Dolores Dei was not entirely human, but something else.
Wow.
I don't care.
Okay. When her innocence was declared -- and the queen she had advised for years fell on her knees before her -- she was so overcome with emotion that her *lungs* started *glowing* in her chest...
Her crowning?
She was crowned? Like Sola?
She must have been beautiful...
I don't care how she looked. I don't care. It doesn't hurt me.

Oh, she was insultingly beautiful. She was humanity's young mother, a perfect mother. It was as if her face and shoulders and hands were covered in a soft down of under-feathers. You know this well -- very well.

Yes. In a city called Advesperascit, in Vesper-Messina, her homeland. The name of the city means "Evening comes," but it happened on a winter's morning with the canals frozen and slush falling out of the sky.

She was dressed in a white and pearl dress on an emptied-out plaza, with the crowd far away. Already her *Therriers* -- the secret servicemen of the innocence -- were worried about an assassination attempt.

Midwinter snow was beating the cobblestones around her. A small attaché of officials stood by as her Therriers placed a white gold wreath on her head. The crowning was mostly witnessed by secret servicemen.
Then what?
What?

Something that had walked in our midst, watching us stumble for hundreds, if not thousands of years, until it decided to interfere -- interfere in the course of our history. 'We were supposed to come up with this ourselves!' the man was reported to have screamed at the innocence...
This *inhuman* quality was witnessed by many others as well -- glowing lungs and all. It is commonly attributed to mass hysteria and religious psychology.

Dolores Dei was shot in the chest with a fowling piece, eight times. The man, thought to be insane, said he once touched her and her body had been unnaturally warm, like a furnace -- and that sometimes while on duty he observed her forgetting to breathe for over ten minutes...
Was there something... *terrifying* about her?
*Terrifying* is a term too emotionally charged for your semantic memory. Or what remains of it, but...
Suggesting those who fight against it are not part of humanity.
Terrifying. It's a simple word. She was *bad* for humanity and you shouldn't have started thinking about her!
Although she is often considered to be the greatest human being to ever live, there *was* something ominous about Dolores Dei -- constantly surrounded by her Therriers...

She adored chess, yes -- but also military war games. Dolores Dei often holds a tiny tin soldier between her index finger and thumb -- in icons such as this. She was also blonde, the blondest woman you have ever seen, with green eyes the colour of the Pisantic *mare interregnum*...

She was the most socially secluded and least self-aware of all the innocences. Some modern thinkers would consider her a war criminal for the campaigns she waged against the Mesque state. And then there were the resettlement programs...

The Mesque state tried to detach itself from innocentic rule. Parts of the world were experiencing whiplash from accelerating into secularism. Her mandatory education programs and mass resettlement of upstream Magritte were problematic as well. Dissenters were suppressed by a military force she called “The Army of Humanity"...

Little is known of her marchese husband. It's as if he vanished from history after completing his role -- which was to introduce Dolores Dei to court. In conclusion, yes, there *is* something lonely, paranoid, and even terrifying that people seldom mention, but *feel* when they think of her...
This subtle terror is part of her iconography.
You're right. Time to heed the warning.
No -- was there something *bad* about her, I want to know...
You already do. Although she is often considered to be the greatest human being to ever live, there *was* something ominous about Dolores Dei -- constantly surrounded by her Therriers...
Good. Now back out of this corner of your mind by choosing the bottom option: "To hell with this." You've been standing here long enough.
What happened?
"Officer, you've stood there for over five minutes..." The lieutenant's calm voice echoes in the cold air of the church.
"What are you thinking of, if I may ask?"
"What are you thinking -- you okay?" He seems a tad worried.
"Hey man, you've stood there for like... half an hour!" The hedgehog-haired man yells from across the coldness of the church.
"She's somehow connected to the case."
"Why did we tolerate this bourgeois woman that long before we shot her?"
"Glowing lungs... That's fucked up..."
"Nothing. Just looking around."
"She's not human."
"She's been dead for three hundred years. I am almost a thousand percent certain she isn't connected to the case..." He takes his glasses off to clean them.
Yell: "War criminal!"
"She's beautiful..."
"None of this is, in fact. This church. The coast... This isn't a good place to get lost in."
An imperceptible tinge of fear. The lieutenant is afraid of this place.
"That's mega cool, man, you coming up with theories in here like that. Right on."
"That's mega cool, man, you coming in here and questioning religious symbolism like that. Right on."
"Yes. Glowing lungs are quite unusual. After that one time, they have not been reported to glow." He takes his glasses off to clean them.
"You know... this church. The coast... we shouldn't linger. Finish what you came here to do and let's move on. This isn't a good place to get lost in."
An imperceptible tinge of fear. The lieutenant is afraid of the church. He does not know why, but he is.
"That's mega cool, man, you coming up with wild left-wing stuff in here like that. Right on!"
"She introduced us to the idea of public education, retirement, and modern diplomacy." He takes his glasses off to clean them.
"Either way... this church, we shouldn't linger here. This isn't a good place to get lost in."
"That's not left wing, Andre. I don't think we should have that spooker adorning the club..." Another voice from the back of the church...
"This church. The coast in general... we shouldn't linger here. This isn't a good place to get lost in. We should conclude our business and move on."
"Right on." A voice from the back of the church. "She was inhuman. You've got a critical mind, cop-man. Yo, Andre, we should board that window up. No one wants that spooky shit when they're dancing."
"Okay..." He takes his glasses off to clean them. Then, after a while, he says:
"That's mega cool, man, you coming in and accusing her of not being human like that. Right on, man!"
"We should board that window up, Andre." A voice from the back of the church. "People don't want to see that woman when they're dancing. It's unhealthy."
"This church. The coast in general... we shouldn't linger here. This isn't a good place to get lost in."
"Cool, man! Yeah! Look around as much as you wanna, this is *your* place too!"
"Okay. It's just that you've been looking at that window for quite long now. And it's cold in here..." He takes off his glasses to clean them.

"I told you, Andre." A voice from the back of the church. "People don't want to see that woman when they're dancing. It's unhealthy. And we're *not* putting disco lights on it. That would only make it worse."
"Cool, man! Yeah, we should light her up with disco lights. People are gonna lose their shit when they see a club for anodic music with this kind of... sacred shit."
"That she is. A great sacral piece. I wonder what we're doing here, however..." He takes his glasses off to clean them.
"In this church I mean? The coast in general... we shouldn't linger. This isn't a good place to get lost in."
"Yeah, glowing lungs *are* fucked up." A voice from the back of the church. "We should board that window up. Bad sines, you know?"

"Right on." A voice from the back of the church. "She was inhuman. You've got a critical mind cop-man -- furthermore, Andre, we should board that window up. No one wants that spooky shit when they're dancing."
"Either way -- this church, the coast in general... we shouldn't linger here. This isn't a good place to get lost in. We should conclude our business and move on."
"Uhm..." Andre doesn't know what to say. "It's cold man, you've been looking at that window for like forever now, man. You should dance, get some warmth!"
"I don't know about that..." He takes his glasses off to clean them. "It was a different time. A different war."
"We should board that old spooker up, Andre." A voice from the back of the church. "It'll only disturb the people while they're trying to dance, unshackled by the failure of humanism."
"How about we *don't* do that, Noid?" Another voice. "She looks cool."
"Okey-dokey."
"Okey-doe-doe," he whispers in the silence of the great building.
A touch of absurdity there, nice!
A very, very skilled thespian would detect a touch of drama when he says he doesn't know why it was conducted...
"You're leaving something out."
"I assure you, I'm not." He looks up at the stained glass window.
Stonewalling. Good technique.
What shattered this mosaic?
Unknown.
Something during the raid the lieutenant mentioned? Or just hooligans looking for something to break.
Your heart knows. But it does not want to say, not yet. Let these things be unknown for now.
Looks like I can't give this figurine to her.

dialoguetext: Why?
Because she's a stained glass window.
That does seem to be a problem... maybe you meant something else?
Like what? Is the task still on?
I don't know. What are we thinking of? Part of your mind has gone on to other things already...
Only a strange little sadness remains.
Okay.
Do the same.
Your fingertips touch your chest four times as you stand in the apricot-coloured light of the window. Above you, the woman still smiles her distant smile, sundered by the crack in the glass.
As that soft word passes through your mind, you rise -- into the apricot-coloured light of the window. The woman keeps smiling her distant smile, sundered by the crack in the glass.
As that lonely word passes through your mind, you rise -- into the apricot-coloured light of the window. The woman keeps smiling her distant smile above you, sundered by the crack in the glass.
With that terrible word ringing through your mind, you rise -- into the apricot coloured-light of the window. The woman keeps smiling her distant smile above you, sundered by the crack in the glass.

As that great and desperate thought passes through your mind you rise. From your knees and into the apricot-coloured light of the window. Above you, the woman keeps smiling her distant smile, sundered by the crack in the glass.

"We should be respectful here, although the building appears to be deserted. I do not believe we'll find anything connected to the lynching here. Something else, perhaps..." He looks at the machinery lying around.
She was crowned two years after the first expedition returned, setting in motion what is widely considered the greatest era in history -- the Dolorian Era.
Bystanders reported golden filaments lighting the already sunlit chamber around her, clearly visible beneath her dress.
Bystanders reported golden filaments lighting the already sunlit chamber around her, clearly visible beneath her dress. I repeat: *Her lungs started glowing*. Do you care now?
Open your eyes.
"Tiago said the place was abandoned because of a police raid. Do you know anything about it?"
"I do." There's a pause, then he continues: "I heard it was a particularly bad one. The place was shot to pieces."
"If this man was really here when it happened, then it's better for all of us that he doesn't remember what happened."
No. You *must* know.
A motor carriage? A gunshot? Someone falling into it? Or maybe just hooligans looking for something to break.
The silence in this part of the church -- it's almost palpable. All the shifting matter and shuffling of living things is gone. Nothing seems to exist beyond the church anymore.
Wait, I think I still hear something...
And then it's gone. Almost all of it -- but for the faintest of hums.
Yell as loud as you can.
(Turn to Kim.) "What's happening?"
Look up into the bell tower.
The orderly rows of ceiling panels become barely visible, then disappear completely in the darkness of the tower overhead.
It's like there's something moving up there -- a shadow has emerged from the tower and is making its way *toward* you through all the other shadows.
Try to see beyond the shadows.
Just darkness without end -- it makes your head spin.
(Blink.)
You see something hanging from the rafters, looking straight at you with dark eyes.
It's not a shadow anymore -- becoming more substantial as it gets closer. The shape of an *animal* descends.
Oh no! You've lost sight of it. Where did it go?
The lieutenant points to his ears and shakes his head. Then he leans closer.
Your voice is barely audible -- not a howl, but the softest of whimpers.
Stomp your feet and clap your hands.
You produce a few muffled thumps, after which the silence feels even more... *total* somehow.
"Can you hear anything?"
"Almost nothing, and it's beginning to worry me."
"The church just has... strange acoustics -- some engineering trick."
On the ceiling?
Follow the shadow's movements.
Yes. The darkness makes the ceiling feel infinitely far away...
Try to make out something -- anything.
There's nothing. You're dizzy and disoriented as you see dark and more dark -- rising...
What's the darkness like?
Filled with vague shapes of woodwork. The sense of a great height.
You see something hanging from the rafters, looking straight at you with dark eyes.
(Blink.)
What if I don't *want* to know what's up there?
The silence, the darkness -- they've enveloped you, as in a cocoon. You cannot move anymore.
"Not really, but it's extraordinary. I've never experienced anything like this."
"I wonder why the... church was built with such strange acoustics..."
His detached tone conceals how uncomfortable he is.
Maybe the church was designed in this way to prevent boisterous activity -- singing and dancing -- on its premises?
"Maybe they wanted to discourage singing and dancing."
"Hey, what if it's something *paranatural*?"
"Whatever it is, it's definitely real. Something odd is happening around us."
"Hmm, could be..."
"Please, detective, not this again."
He's trying to act dismissive, but at this particular moment, he's more open than usual to the idea of paranatural phenomena.
Maybe if you were to stand in just the right spot, even your footsteps would be completely silent...

dialoguetext: It seems that sound here is detached from its source somehow, if not blotted out outright. Truly unusual.
Sounds like the pale.
It's unnerving.
How do I know what the pale sounds like?
No. Let me just listen.
From recordings. Of the far pale. You've heard them. We all have.
You can hardly hear your own breathing.
You know, in the middle of the last century, there was a group of Revacholian painters who famously disdained the use of black.
What did they have against black?
Why only Revacholian?
Can I use this to see through the darkness up there, somehow? (Proceed.)
No, this is just an intellectual musing. In fact, it's probably dangerous to waste time like this. You should stop.
Revachol was an overwhelmingly colourful place back then. They made most of the world's dyes here.
They wanted to capture what it really felt like to look at the world -- to be *inside* colour, to be blinded by early afternoon light glittering on the crests of sea waves.
Such an effect is best achieved by using the juxtaposition of complementary colours -- rather than the addition of black -- to create contrast.
Hmm, maybe I should take up painting.
Seems unfair to black. I like black, look at it!
It's unclear if you have enough years left in you to make up for your lack of technique...
Sometimes an encounter with an opposing aesthetic is required for one to truly grow into one's tastes and preferences.
It would likely be easier to explain with a hands-on demonstration. Alas!
Sounds complicated.
Prepare for an attack!
"Officer, is there something up there?" The lieutenant follows your gaze, attempting to see whatever it is that you are seeing.
Look up into the bell tower.
"Hmm, maybe. Darkness often has that effect on people."
Maybe it's possible to... talk to it?
"Officer, what are you looking at?" He follows your gaze, attempting to see whatever it is that you are seeing.
It's like you see your own face reflected back at you in the vanishing geometry -- a strange, alien image that's supposed to be you.
Maybe it's possible to... talk to it?
"It's probably nothing, just our imagination."
The lieutenant doesn't reply, but you can sense him tense up next to you.
He doesn't seem entirely convinced, though.
But to what? There is almost nothing.
"Can't hear shit."
Relax. It'll be okay.
It's *climbing*. Climbing down, holding on the beams.
It's awfully silent again, as if someone turned off the entire world outside those walls. Water inside the bowls stands still.
Move the fourth bowl from the left five centimetres to the right.
[Leave.]
Move the third bowl from the left two centimetres away.
It moves like a ghost without creating a single trace of sound.
Some water spills out of the bowl, wetting the floor.
Oh boy, this is going to be good.
The lead programmer sends you an encouraging thumbs up from across the hall.
This task is an insult to your mental skills.
Measurements have been marked down around the bowls, each chalk-drawn line representing a centimetre on the floor.
Time to run back! Or maybe walk, this *is* a sacred place after all...
*And* your leg still hurts from the tribunal.
Hey! Her Innocence Dolores Dei liked little figurines, right? Liked holding little men between her fingers, remember?
What?
No, I don't remember anything, I don't want to think about this. Good bye. [Discard thought.]
You have the Headless FALN Rider figurine. You should give it to her. Win her back!
You have the revolutionary soldier figurine. You should give it to her. Win her back!
No... it would have been *beautiful*. Really tiny. Thoughtful. Clever!
Whatever this was, it feels like you made the right choice not to peek into it.
What? (Look around.) Win who back? I can't win her back, she's a long dead historical figure.
I should yes. This is a TASK of mine now.
Forget about this... [Discard thought.]
Don't be so pessimistic. Love doesn't die that easily!
This isn't funny... you have a bad feeling about this one.
So very, very, *very* nifty... nifty and mysterious. This is surely what the figurines are for!
They really have an interesting set up here. Like kids preparing for a school science fair. It's pretty neat.
Are we sure about this? Something smells fishy...
"Hey Andre, what's all this?" (Continue.)
"This? Oh, we're trying to see if we can come up with some cool new special effects to add to the visual aspect of our club experience..." He gestures toward the set-up proudly.
"We tinker with things. Art, music... chemistry."
"Some chemicals when mixed can, you know, change colour, or sort of -- blow up..."
"BLOW UP! BLOW UP!" The young man with the large head pumps his fist in the air.
"Not, like, you know, in a dangerous way," he throws Egg Head an uneasy glance, "or, well, we're not going to do it in a dangerous way."
"Yes, chemistry has many uses. In police work, too," the lieutenant says, deadpan.
The lead programmer turns to look at you for a moment, her gaze impassive, then returns to her work.
"I hope you get to experience one of our light-smell shows sometime, sir," he says with a smile, nodding his blond, spiked head vigorously. "It'll be a blast."
"Feel free to come back later and 'have a blast' with these exemplars of youthful avant-gardism. But we really need to return to the present now."
Nah, that's just the smell of healthy experimentation. And lots of chemicals.
The young man looks startled for a moment, but then flashes you his most winsome smile.
"I hope you get to experience one of our light-smell shows sometime, sir," he says, nodding his blond, spiked head vigorously. "It'll be a blast."
I hope I did stuff like this when I was a kid.
I'm sure you did. You have an exploratory, creative streak -- just like them.
"I'm not sure I'm buying what you're selling. What kind of effects?"
"Okay, sounds cool." (Nod along.)
"Besides, did you know that *smell experiences* are all the rage now at the most forward-thinking venues?"
"Very big in *art circles*." She looks up for a moment.
[Leave.]
An inconspicuous pile of the roofing material, eternite.
What is this?
Why am I looking at this pile of the roofing material?
It's nothing. Someone just left some roofing material slanted against an old shack.

Glad you asked. When junior researcher Õlari Taal invented eternite in the Värtna Polytechnic Institute, some thirty odd years ago, he thought it would last forever -- hence the name eternite. Sadly the only lasting thing turned out to be the material's highly carcinogenic effect.
Because it's nice and orderly. Well laid pallet. Easy on the eyes.
Rhythmic pattern -- calms your mind. Mammals like this stuff.
No, there's more to this. You get this strange *feeling*.
Hard to say, it's gone now. Feelings pass, you see. Especially the small ones.
Discard the feeling.
What feeling?
There it is! You see a shabby little door.
Because there's a secret door hidden behind the panels of eternite. That's why they're *too* orderly.
Pull the panels aside.
"What is this, then? A tool shed?" He peeks inside. "Let's investigate."
It reveals no secrets at this time.
All around you, the hisses and chirps of locusts fill the musky air. The earthen floor of the shack has been shaped into mounds of mud dotted with little holes for windows.
Like skyscrapers, spires of dirt and sand rising. Accommodations for their insectoid inhabitants?
"Of the locusts. For the missing locust case, which is a sub-case of the imaginary insect case. So at least *that's* going well."
"Yes, precisely what I was thinking!"
"Stop being so sarcastic, Kim."
"Oh, I'm not being sarcastic *at all*. We are making *real* progress here."
When someone says they're not being sarcastic, it's usually a good sign that they're being *very* sarcastic.
"Yes." He nods. "I feel we are nearing a *real* breakthrough."
"You think the Insulindian phasmid is nearby?"
"We should talk to Cuno about this. Get him to stop." [Leave.]
"If anything, the presence of the locusts points to the opposite -- the phasmid did not take the bait from the traps. It was Cuno. The phasmid doesn't exist..."
Use your powers of deduction! You knew the magic bug was nowhere near here. The phasmid is impairing your judgement.
He shrugs. "But what do I know?"
What is this?
I should go and ask him to stop then. [Finish thought.]
Heaps of leaves are rotting among the mud-cake towers. Dozens of little locusts feed on them, buzzing away with vicious joy. Cuno has really outdone himself here.
It's an ode to self expression.
It's the work of a self-taught visionary.
Sounds like you found the locusts, detective.
"I'll let you handle the Cuno side of things. You're doing just fine."
"Well, detective, it appears you've solved the case..." The lieutenant looks around, writes something in his notebook, and turns to you...
"Well, detective, it appears you're on the way to solving the case..." The lieutenant looks around, writes something in his notebook, and turns to you...
"The missing locust case, which is a sub-case of the imaginary insect case. So at least *that's* going well."
Sounds like you found the locusts, detective.
I need to tell Morell...
As you turn away, heaps of leaves are rotting among the mud-cake towers. Dozens of little locusts feed on them, buzzing away with vicious joy...
"Yes. We need to tell Morell about this immediately."
"Wait -- could this mean the Insulindian phasmid is nearby?"
"If anything, the presence of the locusts points to the *opposite* -- the phasmid did not take the bait from the traps."
"Instead, it was a kid's prank." He shrugs. "But what do I know?"
Use your powers of deduction! You knew the bug was nowhere near here. The phasmid is impairing your judgement.
"Of course. I'll leave that to you. You seem to have a *handle* on the phasmid-trap-insect situation."
"We should talk to the kid outside. It was probably him. Get him to stop." [Leave.]
Heaps of leaves are rotting among the mud-cake towers. Dozens of little locusts feed on them, buzzing away with vicious joy. The kid in the yard has really outdone himself here.
"I'll let you handle that side of things. You're doing just fine."
The lieutenant isn't studying the powder in the mirror. He's studying you.
"Someone has taken narcotics here. Perhaps the police should interfere?"
"I wasn't thinking about taking it, I swear! I was thinking about *justice*."
"Perhaps not?" He looks at you. "This is below our pay grade, detective. However..." He points to the ladder in the corner.
"I've heard amphetamines make you a really good detective. Are *you* a... really good detective?"
"Of course, detective. *Swift* justice. Don't worry, we don't have to investigate every trace of narcotics..." The lieutenant points to the ladder in the corner.
"No, I'm just a *regular* detective. Thank you very much."
Be still, my beating heart... it's amphetamine, sweet amphetamine!
Lick it. Big-style.
Don't lick it.
"But that there was an interesting find -- an alternative path into the harbour that the kid uses. Well done."
There's a good vague way to ask where he stands on drug use. Professionally, I mean.
Yeah, swift, lightning justice! Faster... Harder... Justicer!

dialoguetext: "See that *ladder* there? It's probably another way into the industrial harbour, no? A secret path the local kids use."
Lick it, but only a little. An itty-bitty little lick.
Responsible drug use. Just a faint bitter taste on the tip of your tongue. There wasn't enough to get a grown man anywhere.
You run your tongue across the plate four or five times. Like a dog. Still, just a very faint, bitter taste. This isn't enough to get a big man anywhere.
Yes, there isn't enough anyway. You'd only be *fooling* yourself.
"That's charming."
There they both are -- two identical shoes, both *copiously* green and *indiscriminately* snake-skin. Reunited on your feet!
How do they fit?
[Discard thought.]
Go ahead, just as long as you don't discard those crocodile babies.
Like two baby crocodiles.
Good. They're balanced. Comfy. Feels like the only good thing about you right now, truth be told.
Wait, these do not look like normal cop shoes...
It's pretty clear a *normal cop* is not what you are.
You may be what they call a *big dick cop*.
"Hi."
"Hello, sir! Step right in, the store is open!" A young girl with chubby red cheeks waves at you, smiling. Her nose is also red from the cold.
"What is your name?"
"It's a bookstore, sir! We sell books, postcards, and some board games." She points at the window. "It's called *Crime, Romance, and Biographies of Famous People*."

"My name is Annette, sir. My mum, her name is Plaisance, she owns the store. She's inside, minding the register... or organizing the stock." The girl gazes at the window, then suddenly jolts, her eyes wide, as if recalling something:
"What is this crime business?!"
"Crime fiction is about murders or burglaries or things like that. And the work of a policeman or a private detective who's trying to solve a crime and catch the criminals."
"Why would anyone want to *read* about crime?"
"It's exciting to people, I guess. They get to imagine dangerous things. And it's kinda like a puzzle, where you can guess who the criminal is or how the good guys are going to catch him. "
"I'm a policeman myself, by the way."
"If I looked like Mr. Mullen, all the criminals would go off running the very moment they saw me. This way I can go undercover, blend in, collect evidence."
"Okay, then maybe I'm not a policeman? Or should stop being one."

"Didn't mean to offend, sir, sorry, sir. It's just that you don't look like Dick Mullen." She points to a book cover, on which you see a strapping Vespertine officer. He stands grimly over the body of a dead woman.
"I used to be exactly like that Mullen guy. Then I decided to *live a little*."
"If you grow up to be clever, you'll discover there's no such thing as a 'grown-up.'"
She doesn't know what to make of that. But she'll remember it.
"Okay... sir."
"And everything's better now, sir?"
"Yes."
"No."
"I don't know."
"Maybe you can show me some *real* police work, sir? Like in the books!" The cover image of Dick Mullen seems to stare at you with harsh disapproval.
She looks at Dick Mullen, frowning.
"He isn't even drawn right. This is not how human shoulders work, the perspective is all wrong."
"Anyhow, it's much easier to work undercover if one doesn't look like him."

dialoguetext: She examines the picture, trying to find whatever is wrong with it. She then shrugs and puts the book aside, unconvinced.
You fail to deduce anything substantial.
"Come on, anyone would notice that!" She rolls her eyes.
"What is romance?"
"It's the type of book where there's a rich lady and she has to choose between the good man and the bad man." She smiles at the thought, perhaps imagining herself in that situation.
"What about a book where the *man and lady business* doesn't work out at all?"
"I don't think it's a romance story if the main characters break up, though..." She pauses, trying to figure out the appropriate answer.
"What about a poor man getting a rich lady?"
"It happens. But usually the guy gets rich in the process, or should actually be rich himself, but has lost his family property unjustly, like during the Revolution or something."
"I see."
"Maybe I will."
"Shouldn't you be at school or something?"
"I do my studies at home at the moment. I have to help Mum keep this place running."
"How's the business going?"
"Mum says it's peachy. She was a little afraid at first, there's talk about this house being..." She looks over her shoulder. "Cursed."
"Cursed? In what way?"
"I don't think curses are real."
"Cursed in a way that makes them say that no business has ever really thrived here, sir. That they all go..." She's looking for the right word...
"Bankrupt."
"Ass up."
Say nothing.
"Exactly. But we've been doing fine so far."
"I wouldn't really say it like that... but I guess so." She blushes.
"Well... they run out of money and have to stop doing business."
"They shouldn't be, but they seem real. Anyhow, they say that these grounds are doomed for businesses."
"Okay, I'm going to *deduce* something now."
"You're uptight because of your mother and the pressure she's putting on you."
Dismay flickers in her eyes. "Maybe so, sir." She sighs. "Okay, I know, it's a bad habit and I shouldn't."
"Rats have been nibbling on your fingers. Child labour in dismal working conditions..."
"What rats? I just read books. Haven't seen a rat in this building in forever."
"Chewed-on-nails... means you're recycling your body material."
"That is so gross."
"One could say that entire economies are doomed, as they tend to crash every once in a while."
"Yes... sir." You realise she doesn't have the faintest idea what you're talking about.
"Why are they doing that?"
"That is a book." She points at the stands. "They have stories inside them -- it's like someone told you a story in a really long letter."
"Interesting. Thanks."
"And you're standing out here in the cold because...?"
"I'm signalling that the store is open." She nods eagerly. "Otherwise people might not know... they'd miss out on the *Crime, Romance, and Biographies of Famous People*."
"Hmm... I actually had other questions."
"More about books, maybe?" Annette nods eagerly.
"Who are these... famous people?"

"Oh, kings and queens and generals of old, or artists and writers, or musicians, those kinds of people. There's usually something extraordinary about them." She scratches her cold-reddened cheek, then continues:
Seems like most people who read those books fail to get more famous from reading them.
"Reading those doesn't make the readers more famous, does it?"
"These famous people sound like a bunch of dorks."
Annette's expression remains ever so helpful, but she doesn't say anything.
"But it does make the famous people more famous!" She smiles gleefully.
"Right, I had a different question in mind."
"Never mind... I literally had nothing else to say."
"Why would they do that, sir?"
"Because I'll be a superstar cop, in the papers and everything! That'll show 'em."
"Hmm... why indeed? I'm just an old, tired cop. What use am I?"
"You're not that old... maybe you'll do something really important. Something that *wows the world*!"
"You think so?"
"Yes! There's hope... a lot of famous people got famous late, or even after they died."
"Thanks, girl. You are very kind."
"Yes, sir!" She smiles and takes a sip from her vacuum bottle.
"That sounds like a nice story to tell yourself at night. Maybe fame isn't that important after all."
"Some can't get noticed, others can't get properly forgotten. That's life for you."
"You're cold. Can I help in some way?"
"Kind of you to offer, sir..." She doesn't know what else to say.
"You can stop calling me 'sir.' I am but a working man."
"It's an intense dedication to the Way of Business. There are no riches without personal sacrifice."

A line of motor garages with armoured carapaces, hunched in the cold. A mechanic is hard at work, patching up bullet holes in the side of a Coupris 40. These are the garages of Precinct 41. Patrol Officer Judit Minot stands in the corner, beneath the narrow awning that hangs over the main entrance. She is watching the snow absent-mindedly as she searches for her gloves in her briefcase.
"Where are hell are they..." she mutters under her breath.
"It's not like that. They're what is called *hetero-sexual life partners*. They have a battle-tested relationship. A 'bröderbund', if you will."
"No, nothing. It's just... Judit went to his place and found the Monday mail unopened. I think he's still there. You didn't, like, drink with him over the weekend did you?"
"What?"
"With that animal? Never again, man. What, is he still down there, in... you know, south of the interchange? The... what was it?"
"Huh? Yeah." He takes out his gloves and struggles to pull them onto his hands.
Satellite-Officer Jean Vicquemare rushes down the station stairs, angrily hunched over in the falling slush.
"Hetero... sexual. Life... partners."
"That would have been irresponsible."
"Funny apery." Vicquemare finally manages to pull his gloves on. There's a small tear along the inside seam of the left glove. "Male-centric workplace humour. Have you seen him?"
"In Martinaise. He's in Martinaise."
"Is there something wrong?"
"Where's your homo, homey?"
On the bridge, Officers Torson and McLaine are standing guard. The muscular Torson wears jeans and a leather jacket. When Vicquemare passes him, the young man remarks...
Around you, the snow continues to fall. To the west, the ocean swells.
It's the only home you have now. But you can't go back. Not like this.

The raised motorway, 8/81, separating Martinaise from Jamrock. Vehicles whoosh past one another day and night, while those who reside in the labyrinthine alleyways beneath the motorway attempt to carry on with their lives in the snow and the slush. And south of the 8/81 is the Pox.
The Pox...
No, it was home. I want more.

The stairs descend -- to Central Jamrock. A man named Kuklov has a snow-covered stall there, in the market across the bridge. He sells kebab infested with fly larvae to your colleagues who believe eating it will make them immune to food poisoning.
The surgeon watches her for a moment, pulling on his cigarette. "You know, it's not so cold that you're going to get frostbite without your gloves."
She nods, then looks down at her hands. No frostbite, sure, but a web of thin red cracks around the wrists. She is visibly embarrassed by the delicacy of her skin.
Suddenly, she smiles at some thought that had just come to her, nods to the surgeon again, and sprints down the stairs, gloveless, into the falling snow.
Snow falls on the utility district: the library, the florist, the Saramirizian restaurant that offers homemade wine. And also on the brothels and drug dens, and the chop shops of the zemlyaki.

All of this built around a lake that formed in a meteorite strike. At the centre of this lake, there is a little ship. There are lights at the bottom of its hull. They are lights directed toward the sea floor, looking for something, like whiskers...
"Wonder if Vic's found his hetero-sexual life partner yet." The man in the fishnet wifebeater looks over at Chester McLaine.
"Damn, I don't know. Even a real *bröderbund* like that can't survive everything..."
The abandoned church. One of two remaining stave churches which were collectively called les Sept Soeurs. The other six sisters were destroyed during the Revolution.
The abandoned church, its walls covered with hoarfrost now. One of les Sept Soeurs. The other six sisters were destroyed during the Revolution.
An abandoned church that's being turned into a dance club. Four youths are hard at work there, making it ever harder core.
And further north?

A serpentine strip of land weaving its way into the Martinaise inlet. Unfortunates on the run -- from the law, from themselves -- sometimes hide out on nearby islets. Little dots in the ocean that are occasionally submerged when the tide is high and the weather foul.
Then there's Ozonne... but the snow falls too thick. You cannot see that far.
The remains of a camp on a jagged piece of rock -- a tent, old dishes and cutlery. Long since abandoned. A hermit crab scuttles among the debris, looking for a new shell.
Further out, the lights burn bright on Résurrection; way beyond Martinaise -- a popular spa destination for ample-bodied Ozonne kids with equally ample pockets.
Before that? Before the curtains are drawn...
The Bay of Revachol, vastness, great depth -- over 1200 m at its deepest. Water, air brinier than here. It is crisscrossed by huge cargo ships bearing company logos: Wild Pines, ZAMM, Moriyn.

And, at the farthest reaches of the Bay of Revachol -- the shadow of Coalition Warship Archer, on perpetual patrol duty, ready to unleash artillery fire if you were to rise up against the market. You shudder.
And on the islets?
And on the other side of the inlet?
That's where Cuno said he's gonna go...
Yes. To peel the gold off with his fingernails.
The snow falls lazily, making the beach sand paler still, mixing with the rust-coloured sewage run-off.
Look around you.
How does it feel?
What is there?
Below the old mines -- L'Ossuaire Municipal, Revachol's underground cemetery. *Les petits rats* brave the underground passageways, trying to get to Le Royaume...
Look around.
A chill comes over you, crawling down your back. The sand under your feet is wet. Somewhere in the south, tarpaulin flap in the wind.
For what?
Someone's stuffed a big old polar anorak into a concrete pipe under the boardwalk. It would keep you warm. You will probably never happen across it, but who knows.
Tell me a secret of the sands, wind.
No need for secrets.
No need for anything anymore.
But still...
Where is Ruby?
Near. Snow falls into dark water. She prays, though she doesn't believe. There is a hum in the air.
That's all.
A drop in temperature. An easy flow of air: an empty street. Before you, a thoroughfare unjammed with lorries. No more drivers smoking on hitch steps. Just... silence.
Let go of the moment. [Discard thought.]
What did the smoke smell like?
Chemically sweetened. Across the road, a forgotten bus stop; corrosion has opened a hole in its roof. An elm tree watches over the building. Its branches are dripping with rain and snow.
The road is smooth and motley. Craters filled with a black asphalt. The asphalt first laid is grey already. A row of tenements are under construction in the distance.
What about the bus stop?
That is enough. [Finish thought.]
Who are the people who live across the road?
A dead dog?
A tub warm with water, white with soap. A man bathes while radio waves transmit the lottery numbers: 4, 18, 21, 4, 1... A modern washing machine rattles a drawer full of silverware.

#312D. Young girls used to come here, huddled up, hoping for more warmth than their thin coats give them. The bus took them to school. It has not run for eight years; there were not enough girls to sustain its cost.
There's one bump on the road: a dead dog lies flat about two hundred paces away, right at the turn.
Craters pocked the surface. Children played in them, until heavy trucks full of black pitch rolled in. The landowners have filled the craters with money. It is a vital artery of flow of trade.
Tragedy came from the wheels of a fast RCM vehicle, hurrying to work. The cold washes over you. The sound of the sea has grown distant.
The wind moves the aerosol. A detective stands behind the boom barrier; a breeze moves a curl of his hair.
What about the road?
His boyfriend is on his way home. He brings tins of meat and vegetables with him. Their pockets are heavier with money; but only slightly.
Wait -- take a longer look at yourself and how you're reflected in that slick chemical rainbow. What do you *see*?
Some kind of metaphor for me?
[Discard thought.]
The engines of fortune once roared here. Great wealth poured into Revachol, the Delta. As did smoke, waste, sickness, life...
The engines stopped. The West Revacholian industrial base was dismantled after the war. Now, extinguished coke furnaces dot the landscape. A landscape despoiled by industry.
I don't see the problem. Revachol moved on to a service industry. Get with the times, yo.
There was a serious dereliction of duty in this clean up.
Right. Here's some advice that's good for business and life: never fight a losing battle. I'm not even going to argue with you.
Filth! This needs environmental action -- now!
Perhaps you could dedicate your life to cleaning it up. But you're a cop. You must concern yourself with different messes. Even so: it's pretty to think.
West Revacholian industrial base? That's so me.
Yes. Fortune left you too, leaving only pharmaceuticals and a sub-par service based industry.
Just me, I guess?
Some nasty water?
This is more important than you. That's the blood of industry you see before you. The run off from Coal City, further down the coast.
No! For a second, think about something other than yourself -- think about *the blood of industry* here before you. The run off from Coal City, further down the coast.
Exactly! The *blood of industry*. The run off from Coal City, further down the coast.
Metaphor. It's always metaphor.
What happened?
The light vanishes inside the concrete slit. The structure goes deep under the earth.
[Finish thought.]
What's in there?
Maybe it's just a storm drain for the sewer?
"Kim, any idea what's down there?"
"No idea." He takes his glasses off to polish. "Could be connected to one of the buildings around here..."
"Think we might find Ruby down there?"
"We might find her down *somewhere* -- there's an old storm drain system beneath Martinaise that's mostly collapsed. Revachol's sewage system has been built and rebuilt four or five times now."
Yell "Ho!" into the slit.
There's no echo -- and no answer.
The silence of god? Sorry...
He puts his glasses back on. "In conclusion -- she could be under any building."
"But not in there?"
He looks into the slit and sighs. "I hope not."
The remaining windows rattle from a strong gust of wind. They're covered in a thick layer of grime. They must have been like this for forty years.
Try to see inside.
Dripping water falls from a high place. All you can see is the shadow of a collapsing staircase.
[Finish thought.]
"Lieutenant, can you make out what's inside?" (Point at the windows.)
"No." He shakes his head. The windows rattle in their frames. "I won't even try. You know..." He takes his glasses off.
"I had a partner once. They called him Eyes, because he had to show me things. It's that bad."
There's rust and corrosion on the bars, they're foaming with it. And a small layer of white salt from the sea.
"Can you still shoot, though?"
Just nod. [Finish thought.]
This partner of his, Eyes -- things didn't end well. It saddens him to say his name. Don't even ask. He wouldn't answer. Maybe some other small talk?
"Well enough, actually. It's odd how that works. I'm no sharpshooter, but I pass my shooting courses 7 out of 10."
His hands lead the way when it comes to that. And his shoulders. It's reflex.
There's no way the perp is in here, officer. Look how scarred the boards are -- all attempts to pry them off have failed.
Nothing more to do here then. [Finish thought.]
Can *I* try to get in though?
Not this time. The opposition is insurmountable. But I like the spirit -- have some *points*! It's lonely and cold without points.
"Kim, you think she's in there?" (Point at the boarded up building.)
"The suspect? God, I hope not -- I can't see a way in..." He inspects the bars. "Though many have tried."
And dangerous. Dangerous too.
You see that seagull up there? Remind you of anybody?
Um... me?
Kim?
What? Kim? No, it's you! You! You and the seagull are just alike!
Exactly!
Why am I like a seagull?
Think about the seagull's story. It's one of endurance -- and adaptation. The seaside was paradise once. They were birds of that paradise.
No time for that sentimental bullshit. They're hustlers, getting shit done. They're one pair of track pants away from gangsters. Just like you.
I guess I *am* a bit like the seagull.
But I'm not like that! I'm still romantic.
Sure, *inside*. But outside it's a tough world. You've got to do whatever it takes to survive. And you *do*. Question is: will you admit that to yourself?
Exactly. The seagull does what it takes -- and so do you. You've got that same spirit in you. When the time comes, you'll push yourself.
Fuckin' right. Whatever it takes to survive. I AM THE SEAGULL!
Own it! Steal hot dogs, shit in the sand -- whatever it takes to keep going!
Okay... well, let me re-consider.
I will not, no. [Finish thought.]
I'm not going to have a seagull conversation. [Finish thought.]
No one comes to mind.
You! You and the seagull are just alike!
Then their paradise became *shit city*. And what did they do? They became urban survivors! Eating burgers out of trash cans! Killing and eating pigeons!
Good boy.
Hold on. Have I ever eaten a burger out of the trash?
You have. The body remembers.
It's only a red chair. Just a red chair in an empty shack -- with what looked like a dusty bow tie on the shelf. Nothing to see here, right?
[Discard thought.]
Sounds like we need to investigate it, then.
"In someone's abandoned shack. On the coast. In Martinaise..." He looks at you. "In Revachol."
"Hey Kim, where are we?"
Investigate the blood red chair? You're going to leave it alone, Harry. That's what you're going to do.
He's afraid you've forgotten suddenly.
You suddenly feel afraid of the chair. It looks like blood is peeling off it...
"What's with the red chair?"
"What's with the red bow tie?" (Show it to him.)
"It's just a piece of clothing you've picked up. You do that, officer -- you collect clothes sometimes."
He sounds a little worried. It's an odd habit.
Don't be worried, lieutenant. Clothes are therapeutic.
You better not fucking think about ditching me for some shitty cum stained bow tie. You and I are gearing up for the *final showdown* that's gonna be off *all walls*. You wait and see.
You took *me* off for that shit? YOU FUCKING IDIOT! Put the horrific neck tie back on immediately -- or you will miss out on the FINAL SHOWDOWN. This is your last warning. Put me back on.
Your neck tie sounds very scared. It's unsafe not to wear it. Put it back.
Yes. Agreed. You should never take your neck tie off. Ever.
Your neck tie sounds very scared. NEVER take it off.
"Nothing. It's just a piece of furniture." He looks at the chair gathering dust.
Red paint is peeling off it. Looks like blood, no?
"Could our suspect be staying here?"
"Here?" He looks around. "I don't see signs of recent habitation. This place is abandoned."
See? He doesn't like the *vibration* from the red chair either.
"All right. Let's move." [Finish thought.]
"Good lord..."
This is it -- the scene of the party. The fire pit, cigarettes, and empty bottles all evidence it.
Not as such. I'm talking about what came after -- the party scene.
Looks like they were here a while, judging from all the bottles. The sunken motor carriage provided them a focal point -- like a goose ice-sculpture or a chocolate fountain.
Hold up -- don't you mean scene of the crime?
Yeah. Sure does look like a lot of folks partied here.
(Dismiss thought.)
"Hey, Kim. Looks like we've had a couple of party-goers here."
Guess I'll be on my way. (Finish thought.)
"Looks like it."
"Hey -- let's keep moving, detective." The lieutenant adjusts his glasses.
"Not as such, no. Let's keep moving, detective."
"Looks like they had a great time laughing here."
"This was some kind of theatre to them. A circus production by a great clown."
"Was this party against the law? On the ice like this -- it was probably a public danger."
Somehow he doesn't want to dwell on it...
Rust peels off the bent iron posts of the swing. The wind whistles through the skeleton of the small house behind you. There's desolation... everywhere.
"What happened here?"
What happened here?
"In this yard?" The lieutenant looks at the small building. A flock of grey swallows takes off in the distance.
"Someone thought they could have a summer house in a *bloc obscur*. For cheap. It didn't work out. They abandoned it about a decade ago."
He's assessing the situation. How long ago was it abandoned.
"Wait, what's a *bloc obscur?*"
"So this part of the coast is a *bloc obscur*?"
"A black bloc, a part of the city left unrenovated after the war. Or one that has fallen to gang violence. Or has become inhospitable in some other way."
On aerial photos, bloc obscures look like dark squares. Hence their name.

"Practically. It's not an official term in any way, but..." he spreads his arms, "look around -- no sewage, broken power lines, crime, drunks... Life is tough in the blocs. It's no place to build a summer house."
"At least they left some old music behind." (Tap on the tape you picked up)
"Maybe they left something useful behind?"
In this yard? Someone thought they could have a summer house on the beach. For cheap. It didn't work out. Looks like they abandoned it.
[Discard thought.]
Yet someone used to live here. Laugh here. Thought it was a good idea to build a *swing* even...
"Yes -- and you picked it up as part of the Jamrock shuffle." He gives you a weary smile.
It's not meant as nagging, just an observation.
"We should move. I don't think we will solve the murder with forays into the urban hinterland. At least in this phase of the investigation."
"We should move. I don't think our suspect is in this particular yard. No place to hide, and besides, it's too close to Martinaise."
"Yes -- for you to pick up as part of the Jamrock shuffle." He gives you a weary smile.
"You're right -- it's no place. Let's go." [Finish]
A long time ago, someone used to live here. Laugh here. Thought it was a good idea to build a *swing* even... an intense loneliness comes over you.
This is a good place for a nice *sad* drink. Uncork a velvety bottle of red wine and think about life for a moment. Really *philosophise*.
Great news -- the boat is big enough for a grown man like you to fit underneath it in a supine position.
Wait, what would I be doing under there?
"Great news, I found somewhere new to sleep."
[Discard thought.]
I don't know? Sleeping? What do people do under boats? This is merely a measurement from your visual cortex, do with it what you want.
Oh no. He's pretty much a bum now.
"Huh?"
"I said: great news, I found somewhere to sleep." (Point at the boat). "Under this boat here. It'll be free."
"I can pretty much finish the case from under that boat there. It's dry, weatherproof, and *free of charge*."
"I'm gonna live under a boat now."
"Sarcastic self pity is not what we need at this moment, officer."
"Self pity is not what we need at this moment, officer."
"I understand the situation looks grim, but we must continue with our investigation."
Sleeping. Was it not decided that you're a *hobocop* -- more hobo than cop -- or was that fine irony that your visual cortex somehow misunderstood?
The elements are rough around here. I don't know about this...
Think of it as a salvation.
You have a home, somewhere. All cops do. When this is done you can return.
Great news then. I do need somewhere cosy.
No, wait -- sorry. My bad. There's a rotting dog carcass under there and old fish too. You wouldn't fit next to the mummified canine's mausoleum.
Damn dog, taking up all your space. The fish smell is too rank too, though.
You have a home, somewhere. All cops do. When this is done you can return.
Just finish the case and you'll probably have somewhere to go. Hopefully.
He sounds tired of it all.
Your loss. Farewell, rain-washed wall at the end of the world.
Your loss. Farewell, light-drenched wall at the end of the world.

dialoguetext: Your loss. Farewell, snow-flecked wall at the end of the world.
Your loss. Farewell, wall at the end of the world, draped in shadow.

dialoguetext: Cindy the SKULL has all the necessary materials. Talk to her?
Blank, conveying nothing.
Why am I looking at this wall?
[Leave.]
You have no clue. It's just a wall.
Yeah, why? It's a wall, an ordinary wall.
Because -- you see it, finally -- this wall is *sublime*! LOOK AT IT! The shadows, the colours...
Maybe this would be a good wall for dodge ball?
So many walls all over Martinaise -- weatherworn, cracked, their paint peeling...
The lieutenant sighs. "Why must we stop to look at this wall every time we pass by? We have business to attend to."
(Let the conceptual joy flow into your pupils and blossom into thoughts in your brain.)
More!
O WALLFATHER!
"Kim! I *must* paint this wall, add even MORE beauty to it."
Yes, I must paint this wall, ADD to it! (Get task.)
No. There is nothing to add to perfection. (Back off.)
Look the wall over again, carefully. Think about what you could paint there...
[Leave.]
This is a wall on the side of an apartment building.
Just an ordinary wall. Nothing to see here.
The wall waits mutely.
[Leave.]
Absolutely. Now you just need the materials.
"Huh?"
Cindy the SKULL has what I need.
I'm sure I'll find them. And then I'll return to this wall.
"I must talk to Cindy. Get the necessary *materials* from her."
"I'm sure I'll find the materials. Then we can come back to this magnificent wall."
He sighs, then adds in a resigned tone: "If you must."
"I suppose we'll have to pass by it again at some point anyway," he says in a tone of resignation.
Yes, great thinking, go talk to her. The wall will be waiting.
Yes, do that. The wall will be waiting.
[Leave.]
"First, I know you're tired, Kim, but take another look at this wall. Draw *nourishment* from its beauty."
"Mhm, sure." The lieutenant looks up at the wall reluctantly, then back at you.
Your hands shake as they reach for the wall...
There it is -- the most beautiful of walls. Stop and admire it for a moment.
Because this is no ordinary wall. It is *sublime*! LOOK AT IT! The shadows, the colours...
Cindy the SKULL has a paintbrush and paint. Talk to her.
You already have the heavy fuel oil to use as paint, and Cindy the SKULL has a paintbrush. This is completely doable.
All the other walls on all the other houses must make a pilgrimage in adoration of this, the uncontested pinnacle of wall-craft. Colour peeled from the very face of god.
You already have the heavy fuel oil to use as paint -- it's red! -- and Cindy the SKULL has a paintbrush. This is on.
The paintbrush in your hand is like a loaded revolver. What will it be, desperado? Quite a few things come to mind...
"MOTHER OF ALL WALLS"
"RENE LIVES!"
Let the wall remain blank. For now. [Leave.]
"WHAT SHADOW LIES THERE, BENEATH THE BRIGHT GLEAM"
"I LOVE YOU CUNO"
(Draw a 3,500 year old pictogram of a human being.)
"SOMETHING BEAUTIFUL IS GOING TO HAPPEN"
You've spoken. The wall will now silently repeat the message. For a decade or so, until the sea air degrades the paint, adding another layer of *detritus* to the city.
"NO PARKING"
"THIS IS REALLY A MIRROR"
"FUCK THE POLICE"
The lieutenant looks at the wall in dismay:
"But we *are* the police..."
"Yeah -- fuck us."
"You're right, you're right. Is it too late to change it?"
"But why? We work twelve-hour shifts. We get shot at, spat on..."
The lieutenant raises his eyebrows, then sighs.
Hah! Maybe there's a *reason* for that!
The wall towers over you with its indelible message.
"But what do we work on? KEEPING EVERYTHING THE WAY IT IS."
Keep it to yourself.
You've spoken. The wall will now silently repeat the message -- for a decade or so, until the sea air degrades the paint.
Paintbrush -- check, heavy fuel oil -- check... Now the only thing left to do is paint the wall.
"Very poetic." The lieutenant nods in appreciation -- it doesn't sound sincere. "Real poetry. Should we return to our murder investigation? I hear there's a really *bad* one we're supposed to solve."
"Hmh..." Just a hum. No reply.
You've spoken. The wall will now silently repeat the message. For a decade or so, until the sea air degrades the paint, adding another layer of *detritus* to the city.
A row of mugs sits on the shelf. Each one depicts a human figure: a dark-skinned woman grinning amidst mysterious symbols, a broad-shouldered man shovelling potatoes, and others.
Tap on the mugs.
Whip out your Yellow Man mug and compare.
Recall the Yellow Man mug you found in the Whirling trash container.

dialoguetext: Move on from the mugs. [Leave.]
A little ring. Though cheerful, the images on the ceramic make you vaguely uncomfortable.
There's something disdainful in the way the curves and lines of the bodies were drawn.
The images betray a lack of interest in human beings. They are merely unflattering caricatures.
Yes, your broken mug friend would feel very much at home here. The same humour, the same mocking lines...
Yes, your broken mug friend would have felt very much at home here.
What do I mean *uncomfortable*?
The owner of these mugs doesn't like people of other ethnicities very much.
It looks like the artist is celebrating diversity, but underneath he's just making fun of these people.
Typical asshole.
So what? They can think what they want. This is a free world.
Thanks, good to know. I have no opinion on this.
This person is unhappy.
Of course. So very free.
Anytime.
Cynical slippery bastard.
I don't see these as stereotypes. I think they are honest acknowledgements of difference.
I don't think I like the owner of this apartment.
You ain't gonna change someone's mind by calling them a bastard.
Of course... You slippery bastard.
No one's telling you to like him. You might learn something from him, though.
The lieutenant picks up one of the mugs, then puts it back down with a look of disdain.
"I'm beginning to feel better about breaking into this man's apartment."
"There's the missing tin soldier," the lieutenant looks at the mugs next to each other. "Whoever lives here might have used the Whirling's container to dump his trash..."
"And now they've drawn the ire of the Union. The plot thickens, as they say."
The owner of this collection could be dumping his trash in the Whirling's container.
"Do you really think it's the same person who put the dead man's clothes in the trash?"

"Who knows?" The lieutenant opens his notebook. "I'm not expecting too much from this *clothes in the trash* lead either way. It might turn out to be some random local matter. But still -- a nice coincidence."
Who knows? Could be, but this 'clothes in the trash' lead doesn't really seem like it's going anywhere. Still, good thing to keep in mind.
You could ask Evrart who this person is? Once you're done here...
An interesting little clue. Let's see where this goes. Clues have a way of magically connecting to other clues -- down the road.
And so *fun*.
Perhaps you should break into apartments more often?
"I'm really not sure we should be in here."
The spread pattern of these bullet holes makes your chest ache. Your breath grows heavier.
"Kim, look... more bullet holes. Someone has been shot here."
Another set of awfully old bullet holes.
More old bullet holes, at least half a century. A different era altogether.
[Discard thought.]
The lieutenant inspects the wall, then nods. "Another set of old bullet holes from the Revolution."
"Man, how many people got shot during that Revolution?"
"Figured as much." [Discard thought.]
