dialoguetext: More old bullet holes, half a century at least, from the Revolution.
"A history of violence streaking all across Revachol."
"Plenty."
The streets ran red with blood. Dust swirled above the ruins. The pressure change from artillery fire ripped people apart in the top floors of the building above you...
Examine closer.
You peer into the faded marks in the stone... they peer back like an endless row of tiny black holes. Sweat starts trickling down your brow.
"These bullet holes look like the bullet holes we saw before."
"Bullet holes generally look the same, so... probably." He leans in to inspect the wall. "But you are right, more old bullet holes from the Revolution."
"What's with all these bullet holes? I've seen a lot of them around."
The lieutenant looks at the wall. "Remnants from the Revolution. These are over half a century old."
"Okay. But what can you tell me about the Revolution?"
"Not much. I don't have a *fresh perspective* on it. Should we go?"
"No, we're not constructors and renovators. And these bullet holes do not warrant an investigation."
"So, no crime has happened here?"
"Perhaps *a* crime of a sort, ages ago... but no, these do not warrant an investigation."
"Is there something we should do about these?"
"Never mind, then. Let's go." [Discard thought.]
The lieutenant nods.
This is bad mojo, man! Fuckin' horrible mojo. The end draws near!
Your chest feels tight, looking at them. It's closing in... caving in, ever tighter. Your breathing grows even heavier.
"You okay there?" The lieutenant's sudden voice cuts like a blade, bringing you out of the stupor.
(Breathe out sharply.) "Huh, yeah-yeah, I'm fine."
"Man, I started feeling really bad for a second."
"You were looking pale there for a second. What are you looking at?"
"Might be the after-effects of your... past escapades. What are you looking at?"
This must be it. The basement door is weather-worn. The copper nails holding the upholstery in place have turned green from sea air and there's a knocker, shaped like a lion's head.
Carefully knock.
Use Mañana's key to unlock the door.
[Leave.]
You knock silently. The upholstery muffles the sound. No response comes from the apartment.
Press your ear against the door.
The door is slick with rain. You don't hear any movement inside.
The leather upholstery is worn and rough against your jaw. You don't hear any movement.
Finally, the door unlocks with a small clack. Thoughts race through your head...
The sound of the key turning still echoes in the yard. Hopefully no one heard.
The door to cryptofascist's shabby apartment. It has been locked again.
"I guess no one is in." The lieutenant looks uncomfortable.
"Lieutenant, what is your opinion of this task we're undertaking?"
"As I already said," the lieutenant replies, adjusting his glasses. "I understand this can't be avoided."
"Let's be honest, this isn't what I joined the RCM for. But -- every day tells you something new about yourself..." the lieutenant replies, still inspecting the padded door.
"Apparently, working with the local Union boss to get info on an investigation is not something I'm squeamish about."
"So you don't mind if I unlock the door?"
"Got it!"
"If the merc tribunal happens before we solve this..." His eyes meet yours. "We're looking at casualties. What's one unlocked door compared to that?"
"I mind that a local thug is using the RCM for his busywork, but if this gets us to the bottom of this hanging then I'm willing to look over it."
"On the other hand..." He looks at the surrounding windows uncomfortably. "We *could* just leave and tell Evrart we opened the door. No one seems to be tailing us to see if we actually did it."
Well buddy, you opened it. No need to go inside. It would be *rude*.
Good job. Let's go now. I'm sure there's *nothing* interesting in there.
There's *nothing* else to do than leave and tell Evrart. No *conceivable* reason for you to intrude on the premises.
As you hold the opened door you can feel the air moving. A little draft. A whistle...
The Royal Lion. Guillaume's Kitten. This knocker will last a lifetime and then some.
You feel eyes on you, watching you from the windows overlooking the yard.
"Lie to Evrart? That's also an option?"
"Yes, presenting a fabrication is known to get results here and there." He crosses his arms. "You took this task. You make the call."
The door is right here. You can just open it and be done with this.
Besides, if you never open it, you're never gonna find out, what's *behind* the door.
You try to be as silent as you can. It takes a bit of rattling of the handle to loosen the bolt.
There *might* be important information in the apartment... I mean... there *might*...
Only *curiosity* could account for stepping over that threshold. Maybe there's treasure in there? A white alligator? A fountain of quicksilver?
"But we do need to get the key from this 'Mañana' Evrart mentioned." The lieutenant glances at the door. "Cause we are *not* gonna break the lock."
The lieutenant merely nods in response.
"It is," the lieutenant remarks. "However, we should definitely get the key from this 'Mañana' Evrart mentioned. That would drastically increase our credibility."
The door to the 'Weasel's' Den', guarded by the lionhead-knocker. Both have seen better days.
The Royal Lion. Guillaume's Kitten. This knocker will last a lifetime and then some.
The door has braved the elements for decades. The copper nails holding the upholstery in place have turned green from sea air and so is the knocker, shaped like a lion's head.
Press your ear against the door.
Knock on the door.
[Leave.]
Use Mañana's key to unlock the door.
Someone is moving around in the apartment. You hear the water being turned off and the sound of dishes clinking together.
Not a sound. The silence is eerie.
The tenant must be cleaning up. That means you're too late. Nothing more to do here, better report back to Evrart.
Even the darkness is holding it's breath inside the apartment.
Something hits the ground and shatters inside the apartment.
A plate, glass or a mug.
Then a running tap is turned off and the complete absence of sounds feels... tense.
The key stops mid-way in the lock. Something's blocking its path. You hear a dish smashing and shattering inside the apartment, then everything falls very silent.
The tenant's key is in the lock.
The key stops mid-way in the lock. Something's blocking its path. Not a sound is coming from the apartment.
No answer.
"I know you're in there!"
"That already defeats the point, doesn't it?" The lieutenant glances at the surrounding windows. "Let's get out of here."
No answer.
You're too late -- the weasel's already back in its den. Let's see what Evrart thinks about it.
You're *pretty* sure the owner of the apartment isn't here. It's safe-ish.
In fact, it's oddly silent in the yard around you. No birds chirp.
I don't know... you're a *pretty* good liar. Are you as good an *infiltrator* as you are a liar?
This must be the door Evrart mentioned. You still need to get the key from Mañana first though.
"That's probably the door Evrart mentioned. We still need to get the key from this Mañana first though."
This must be the door Evrart mentioned. You still need to get the key from Mañana first though.
"That's probably the door Evrart mentioned. We still need to get the key from this Mañana first though."
As you turn to leave, you hear footsteps on the other side -- yes, someone's definitely home.
"We should leave," the lieutenant whispers, "and go talk with Evrart, tell him what happened -- that we couldn't open the door. Maybe there's a workaround."
Maybe it's a good thing you didn't get to open this stranger's door? Go talk with Evrart, tell him what happened.
The lieutenant looks first at the door, then back at you, then signals you to back off from the door.
You should leave. Leave! Before anything happens...
The door is closed again. Nothing to do here anymore.
You hear someone inside, walking from room to room... whoever lives here must be back home.
This is the flag of Revachol the Suzerainty.
What's with the sun?
That's good to know. [Discard thought.]
This isn't just one sun, but there are little suns dancing around the big sun. This is the Sevenfold Sun Miracle.
What's the Sevenfold Sun Miracle?
It's an optical atmospheric anomaly the first settlers saw. Happens in cold weather: six small suns around the big one. This complex halo-phenomena is how old Revachol got its flag.
"Mhm." He looks around the apartment. "The tenant is an *old fashioned* guy."
"Lieutenant -- the old flag of the Suzerain." (Point)
Bow down before the flag. [Finish thought.]
Don't bow to the flag. [Finish thought.]
By 'old fashioned' he means 'very right wing'.
The flag accepts your honourable salute with quiet dignity.
The lieutenant does not bow to the flag -- it accepts your salute with quiet dignity.
The flag doesn't seem to mind, it's just a colourful fabric with a sun sewn onto it. Like all feudal flags, it looks like a children's drawing.
It is but one of the many strange *optic-atmospheric* phenomenon on this wondrous archipelago. You're sure you once saw sundogs -- in your youth. And blue flares....
It is not my flag, he thinks -- my flag is the signal blue of the Zone of Control.
Why?
Maybe it's the bed's fault?
Check the pillow.
Check the blanket.
Roll over to the other side.
It's a little better... Colours, scenes, and half-formed phrases still litter your mind. Part of you is still trying to solve the case, isn't it?
Its synthetic filling has separated into hard lumps. The pillowcase smells oddly.
It barely covers your toes, stretching over your soft belly. This is your body here, intimate and warm, breathing...
Smells of alcohol and sweat. And grease.
A bit tense in the muscles -- relax.
Breathing, are you sure? Your heart beats a little bit faster at this unnerving thought.
Who killed him? Who?
No more thoughts. Fall asleep now...
Something to do with... What was it that the lieutenant said? Union? And it's gone again, your thoughts lost between the slowing brain waves.
Your breathing steadies. A great silence washes over you... until your eyelids *twitch* in your sleep and images... images start forming...
And then -- sleep doesn't come.
Under your thrumming eyelids, you see a dizzying array of colours. You won't get off this carousel quite so easily.
But I *want* to sleep...
Obviously -- you're in bed with your eyes closed. But it's not happening.
Do you remember the scent of your childhood?
I can get it all back.
I remember nothing.
I was born in a hospital where people usually go to die.
I don't want to come back.
What *is* this?
God... there's *another* type?

You know who I am. I am the bad day. The one where you ask her, and then later in the streets, wandering... It's the worst day of all time, Harry dear, and it's coming. She will hear about it on the phone.
Do you remember your wife's hand on your face?
Reality will turn into a grotesque nightmare. This'll be the last thing you did to her. Tell me -- do you remember the love of your life?
Stinky boy.
You're not kidding anyone, Harry. You don't remember shit. Tell me...

Oh yes, party boy. And it's *worse* than the one before! Just think of the shit you saw! Here it comes too, so soon already! A silent alarm goes off in your head, like clockwork, barely let you sleep at all... Time to get those clothes on, Harry!
I was left.
You're not coming back from shit! Thrashing around in that *high-conductivity state* of yours, bumping into things and acting like a *clown*. Who are you kidding?
I left.
I'm trying to solve... trying to solve this case.
TELL ME WHAT THIS IS!!! I'm not answering before you tell me who you are.
That's right, funky-baby, and you just stood there. One hand on the bottle and the other on your dick -- watching her go. Let it all be dragged away from you.
I can come back from this.
What it says on the can, Harry. Answer the question.

Your mind is what now? I can't hear you, the rest is just a word-dream. Jumbled up garbage. The pictures are gone, the bed rises to meet you. A thin, sleep-like state. More glass than velvet, *grinding* in your head.
You'll be back in those cold snake skins in no time, sweating up the bed...
What? No!
Oh no, funky-baby, you *stayed*. It was the rest of it that left. While you just stood there. With one hand on the bottle and the other on your dick -- watching it go.
Help me...
Everything. The pale and the isolas -- on the surface -- the outer magnetosphere... Burning, furious truth, eight thousand years of written history.
Tell me, where are your friends? Human beings have friends, Harry-boy. Where the hell are yours?
So-something is *wrong*. Sleep shouldn't be this bad. This dry. This un-nourishing. There's something wrong with your thoughts. Some kind of... new type of hangover...
No, Harry. You were just talking to yourself. That's all you ever do. Even in your dreams. And the act is wearing thin, the spots of the disco ball fade around you...
You said... who?
I've seen you before...

Help you, why? I can't hear you, the rest is just a word-dream. Jumbled up garbage. The pictures are gone, the bed rises to meet you. A thin, sleep-like state. More glass than velvet, *grinding* in your head.
You really dropped the ball, Harry. Four point six billion people -- and you failed every single one of them. You really *fucked up*.
They were only cramping your *descent into the abyss*. Now they're gone. Three times gone and never coming back -- all of it. You failed. You failed me.
What is Elysium?
Do you remember the warmth of her thighs, between her legs and in her mouth?
No. It's gone. Three times gone and never coming back. You failed. You failed me.
My mind is tired and broken.
You failed Elysium.

You're trying to what? I can't hear you, this is just a word-dream now. Jumbled up garbage. The pictures are gone, the bed rises to meet you. A thin sleep-like state. More glass than velvet, *grinding* in your head.
No, you haven't. You're just sleep-talking. And the act is wearing thin too, the spots on the disco ball fade around you...
Time to go to work in the shit factory!
Good going, buddy.
What the hell is going on with me?
You mean why are you so tired? Too tired and *down* to even think? It *is* worrying, isn't it. You can't be a detective like this -- detectives need to be able to think.
Why is this happening?
No, that's not it. *Really* I feel super-good.
It's just that your heart has finally pumped all the *speed* out of your system, buster. Time to get some more.
Don't do that. Stay strong. The hangover will wear off. You don't need to keep doing this to yourself.
Wait. What *is*... speed?
No. I can take this. I am not going to go looking for speed.

Are you sure? Ready to live as this pathetic shell of yourself for days?  Basically a week? Let's be honest -- two weeks, maybe three? You won't make it. Half the town will be dead by then. You will be fired.
Who am I kidding? Of course I want some speed. (Opt in.)
That's a lie. I can do this without the speed. Half the town won't be dead... (Opt out.)
Suit yourself, slow, sad shell-man. See how you do without your spark.
Fast recovery, man! Quick turnaround.  Superdetective back in action.
Speed is a potent central nervous system stimulant. It kept you propped up all day yesterday despite your debilitating hangover. How else did you think you even got up from this floor?
It's power, man. It's professionalism. It makes you feel like you're young again and ready to *detect*! Ready to go to war against the world!
I think Cuno might have speed. I should ask him and start blasting again. (Opt in.)

dialoguetext: Oh my god, what the hell was that...
I just had the most beautiful dream. Uplifting. Rejuvenating.
Is that how it's going to be now when I close my eyes?
Oh, just a dream. You have ones like that all the time. You feel even worse this morning than you did last night.
Really? Because you feel even worse this morning than you did last night.
Yes. Wait till you see the one with the chick in it, it's gonna be a good one. You feel even worse this morning than you did last night.
What chick?
You don't know? Some broad that messed you up. It'll come to you. It always does.
That's not really true. Your heart has finally pumped all the *speed* out of your system, buster. Time to get some more.
You got up from this floor because of a holy vow you made sixteen years ago. With *me*. To wake up exactly 07:30 every morning until the day you die.
Don't be silly. There was no vow. You were high on speed. That was the only reason you got up. You can't *detect* without it, it's that simple.
You're too weak to say 'no' now. Waking up is the worst part. Maybe somewhere down the line you could decline...
I need to get more of it then. *Detecting* is my life. (Opt in.)
Of course! Martinaise is speed-central. You just gotta poke around, follow your nose.
You and speed will be happy again. You will make her come home. This time it will be different.
Crawl in.

dialoguetext: No time to rest yet. [Leave.]
The sheets feel at once coarse and clammy against your skin. The bed sags beneath your weight as you stretch out and finally close your eyes...
The bed is cold and not particularly inviting, but it's yours. The sheets look awful...
The bed is still cold from the broken window, and not too inviting. But it's yours. You've earned it.
Go to sleep.

The bed is comforting, if a bit run down. Still, you've earned a rest.
Across the room, the heating system hums its soft lullaby. The mattress feels soft and sheets warm. It only takes you moments for the world to fall away...
The sheets feel at once coarse and clammy against your skin. The bed sags beneath your weight as you stretch out and finally close your eyes...
The day has not made the sheets any less coarse. The bed sags beneath your weight as you close your eyes and fall into uneasy sleep...
Across the room, the heating system hums a soft lullaby. The mattress feels soft and sheets warm. After some time you fall into uneasy sleep...

dialoguetext: And then sleep doesn't come.
The option to go to sleep becomes available every night after 21.00.
The bed's a little nicer now. You could get a good night's sleep here.
The window is fixed, the sheets are new, it's easier to fall asleep than ever before...
He draws out a disgusting snort, then mumbles, waving a finger in your general direction: "Ugh... Abigail... don't ya... fuckin'... call Abigail."
The dozing man mumbles something inaudible.
"Don't call Abigail," grumbles an unshaven man with a ruddy nose. He narrows his eyes at you as if in recognition, then turns his head away.
"Tell me about your friends." (Point to the others.)
"Who are you? What's your name?"
"Why shouldn't I call Abigail?"
"Where am I? What is this place?"
The noxious odour emanating from the drunken man is strong and familiar.
Walk away. [Leave.]
"Don't... call Abigail..." he whimpers softly, his voice trailing off into nothingness.
"I'll call whoever I want, don't tell me what to do."
"I am the law."
"Who is Abigail?"
"This is making me uncomfortable." [Leave.]
"Right, you might have found the one person who doesn't know you are the law, given how drunk he is."
"Abigail... oh, Abigail..." He mutters while trying to brush something off his extremely dirty trousers. His movements are slow and awkward.
The lieutenant sighs. "You really don't have to... Besides, he will understand you anyway."
"Have you seen any women around here lately?"
"Abigail!" He grunts. "Don't... don't call her." He waves a finger in your general direction.
"Hey, I'm on an important official investigation, I demand you answer my questions."
"There's no use in yelling at drunks," the lieutenant interjects. "He's barely holding it together."
The drunk man starts coughing, a really disgusting hacking cough.
"Abigail?" His voice perks up, then trails into a string of random babbling. "Abigail, where are you?"
He glares at you. "Don't ya fuckin' call her, hear me." His voice trembles with every word, becoming ever weaker. "Abigail," he whimpers in the end.
The man hiccups, then mumbles something unintelligible.
His eyes move around erratically, the look in them hazy and unfocused. "Don't call Abigail," he says.
He snorts and beckons you to lean in closer.
"Don't ya call her, ya hear. Don't call Abigail..."
"Don'... don'..." the man stammers, "don't call..." Slowly, his head nods off to the side and he passes out, tongue dangling from his mouth.
"There was little chance he'd be a reliable witness, anyway."
Lean in.
Don't lean in.
He waves his hand, as if shooing you away, all the while murmuring something indecipherable.
His breath smells harsh like a toxic swamp as he whispers to you: "Don't call Abigail. Don't call Abigail!" He then waves his hand, as if shooing you away.
He does not sound well at all.
"Don't call Abigail." The drunk man looks at you with his sad, swollen eyes.
"Don't call... don't call her..." The drunk man speaks in his sleep. Drool dribbles from the left side of his mouth and down his jacket lapel.
There's no waking him from his stupor. His mind is elsewhere.
"Hey, wake up!"
Let him sleep it off. [Leave.]
You're not going to get anything from this guy. He's too drunk.
Never thought you'd see such a thing in your life, but this guy's a little *too* drunk.
Abigail is his wife or girlfriend. Chances are, she's gone. Calling her wouldn't make it any better or worse.
"Oh..." He gets a proud gleam in his eyes. "The system's been good to old Rosemary here and I'm milkin' 'er like a bitch goat in the backyard."
"In the civilized world, it's a custom to tip the shopkeep, friend. But come back anyway." He waves you off.
"Good to see you, friend! Do I have *deals* set up for you, buddy-boy!" He spreads his arms as if wanting to embrace you.

"So whadda'ya want?" He tilts his head. "I got smokes. They're cheap. Very cheap. I got pilsner. Great deal. You won't get a better deal on that piss... Spirits I can let go for 300 reál. I also have speed. And by *speed* I mean amphetamine."
"Quite the business venture you've set up here."
"I'm off." [Leave.]
"Here you go, friend." He hands you a tiny bottle with a straw. The powder looks clotted and quite mouldy.
"Bottoms up, captain!" He hands you an ugly brown bottle.
"My kinda guy," he mumbles, handing you a pack. "Here you go, friend."
"Good to see you too, friend."
"What are you talking about?"
"I'll just have the spirits and not the story today, thank you."
"I thought about it and you know what? I can pay 3 reál for the spirits."

dialoguetext: Nod -- let him speak.
"You know, it's funny, actually..." He bursts out laughing, then takes three gulps of his pilsner and stares at you intently.
"Right... right..." His tone cools considerably. "As I said, that'll be 300 reál."
He's finding it difficult to focus his watery gaze.
"What is?"
"What?"
"What do you mean *what*? What did you think was funny earlier?"
"This guy, this guy..." He says and shakes his index finger at you.
"Forget about it, I just want the spirits!"
"Okay, can I just get the spirits if that's okay with you?"
"You know what?! I don't even want the spirits anymore!"
"So what do you want then?!"
His tone is aggressive. You're getting on his bad side now.
The alcohol boiling his blood causes the agitation. It burns!
"Where did you get the bottle of spirits from?"
"Oh, this is medicinal spirits. The good stuff. Got it from the doctor's office."
He ain't shitting you. Medicinal spirits are a blast, *bratan*. The flaming truth of this joke of a world.
"I got one of those scientific ampoules a few months ago. 'Torpedo' they call it. It's supposed to keep a man from takin' a drink." He spits a nasty yellow clot on the ground before you.
"Didn't stop *me* for shit, that's for sure!" His voice rings with pride. "Five lemons with half a pack of butter and you're good to go."
"That's a good tip, I should remember it."
"That sounds dangerous."
"It was," he croaks. "In a week the goddamned kidneys started giving me all kinds of hell. Finally the missus took me to a private doctor's office -- not a charity, the real thing..."
"Those assholes!" He gets visibly angry. "Those assholes charged me *four reál* to remove the damn thing. But I came out on top after all!"
"But the idiots left me alone in there. Now, I used to teach high school biology. I *know* what doctors use to preserve dead thingies..." He gets an excited gleam in his eyes.
"Have they no shame taking money for a service they provide!"
"Assholes..."
"Swiped three cans of this blue medicinal stuff from the back room. Threw the snakes out and voilà -- what's left is this beautiful blue stuff." He shakes the bottle. "98.7%, almost pure alcohol."
"Two I already sold to these fine gentlemen here," he nods at his companions. "But this last one is yours for three reál, if you want it?"
"I think it will prove... useful. Yes."
"No, not really."
"Can I smell it first?"
"Here..." He uncorks the bottle and holds it under your nose. "Be careful, it's extremely flammable. One spark and the entire city of Revachol is wiped off the map."

Feels like someone set a mustard field ablaze right inside your nose, then drenched it in tear gas. Your nose is a singular source of pain... but at the same time you don't remember the last time you felt so alive.
"Feels like someone's trying to jam an angry hedgehog down your nostrils, doesn't it, buddy-boy? Wait for the adrenaline-tsunami, it's *really* great!"
Did I not tell you, *bratan*? This is it -- this is our party drink. This is what we're having, baby! Please get it for me! (The tie vibrates excitedly around your neck again.)
"So, what's the deal, friend? Want the spirits or not?"
"Three reál and it's yours, friend. The deal of a lifetime!"
"Here's the money for the spirits."
"What do you mean?"

"You see, friend," he raises his index finger, "man makes his own luck -- and I made mine real good. Got my hands on three bottles of *liqueur exquise*, sold two to the fellows around here and *immediately* invested the profit."
"Bought cigarettes, bought beer, even bought a bit of speed. And look at me now... I got everyone on my hook." He spreads his arms and smiles a crooked toothless smile.
"Looks like you're on your own hook, too."
"Impressive entrepreneurship." (Point to his vice-stand.) "I approve."
"Got a permit for this little shit-show?"
"Of course, of course, of course..." The drunk raises his pilsner and nods. "It is what it is, you know? What it's always been. People, buddy-boy, it's the people."
"Sell me some speed."
"I want a pack of smokes."
"Here's the money for a pilsner."
"The legend returns. You know the deal, legend-man. Smokes are smokey, pilsner... gets you drunk. You've already cleaned me out of spirits... and speed." He looks sad.
"The legend is here. You know the drill. Smoke up, pilsner up... buy the beautiful bottle of blue spirits. It's..." he spreads his arms, "*magic*."
"The legend! He's back. And thirsty." He nods. "I got smokes and piss and a little... speed to spice things up."
"The legend returns! You know the dance. Smokable smokes. Pissable pilsner -- drink it, then convert it to piss! And there's... spirits and speed too."
"Why does the bottle of spirits cost 300 reál?"

dialoguetext: "Amphetamine?"
Does he actually know you or is he just shopkeep-friendly?
"Friend? Do we know each other?"
"Sure, friend! You know it!" He points a finger-pistol at you and squeezes the trigger. "*Chck-chck*."
"Don't mind ol' Rosemary here, he's a buffoon." The tracksuited man waves his hand at you. "Let's have a word after your high-concept transactions, I'll give you the lowdown."

"See, friend..." He brings out a one-litre bottle with blue-ish liquid. The mouth is corked shut. "It's *real* valuable. Worth every reál, if you catch my drift. Got it from a bit of a business venture..."
"No one can buy spirits for 300 reál, that's crazy."
"Here's the money for the spirits."
"Whoaaa," he gasps as he hands you the bottle. "My investment hit *big bank* this time around... Look, Doom Spiral, look!"
He hands you the bottle. "Jus' make sure to *enjoy* that one, friend!"
"What?" The man in the dirty tracksuit turns his head. "Big bank?"

"Naturally, the situation required me to climb over the gate, which I did. There was no climbing down, because I slipped and landed on my ass."
"Reality was looking rather grim, just then -- me lying on my ass in a mud pit in the middle of a heavy shower. But when life knocked me down, I always got up..."
"So I made my way across the yard. Standing in front of my apartment door, fumbling with my pockets, I realized that I'd *also* forgotten my apartment key!"
"You've got to be shitting me!"
"I wish I were, Tequila. I wish I were." He turns his head towards the skies. "Instead of my apartment key, I'd taken the key to the office."
"Okay, so what happened next?"
"I rang my neighbours' buzzers. It was late, and most of them didn't even answer. Those who did assumed I was trying to sell them something and hung up before I could even explain the situation..."

"People are naturally wary of ad men, you see. One moment someone chats you up, five minutes later you've bought a box of edible lingerie and a strap-on. I don't begrudge them, especially since I was known to be one of the best..." He pauses meaningfully.
Heavy is the head that wears the crown.
"Just then I experienced a moment of clarity: I still had the key to my office! I could wait out the storm there..."
"But when I reached my office I remembered that I'd asked one of my producers to change the locks that day -- and since I hired only the best, he'd already done it, and I couldn't get in..."

"Anyway, long story short, life spiralled out of control. I haven't gotten into my apartment for years, and my girlfriend left me because she didn't want to date a homeless man. The company, well, you see where I'm going with this..."
He pinches his thigh as if to check whether this reality is *the reality*.
"I've only been a hobo cop for a few days now, but it doesn't seem so bad."
"The hobo lifestyle definitely has some perks -- not having to pay rent, first and foremost. Not being responsible for twenty other people is nice too."
"Look on the bright side -- you've got one hell of a story."
"There's this black point in the world, a hole. It's already claimed an entire commercial area, maybe you're another one of its victims?"
"This would explain a lot -- I always believed it wasn't my fault that I ended up homeless on the beach with these two bums." He looks at his partners with a glint of sadness.
"Yeah. Maybe I've exaggerated certain parts over the years. When you tell a story too often, it begins to take on a life of its own..."
"But what matters is that it's true to my subjective experience. Anyway, that was all the story one bottle gets you." He looks at it. "Almost empty this one..."
"I don't need to hear any more." (Conclude.)
"It's a hard thing for a man to confront his past." He nods. "That's why I avoid mine at all costs."
The gleam in his eyes and the slouch in his posture is so incredibly familiar...
You might get scammed here.
So this is how being on the other side of the barrel feels.
He clears his throat: "Summer of '44. Seventeen-year-old Gertrude Het is walking home from a late shift at the harbour. It's almost midnight. She stops for a cigarette near the canal..."
"Wait, I thought that the Headless FALN Rider rode a bull?"
"Our heroine finds herself enjoying the peace and quiet the canal provides..." He looks up to the skies as if searching for peace himself...
"There are many variations on the basic story, and the details often conflict. What everyone agrees on is that nobody knows the exact nature or identity of... the phenomenon."
"What she doesn't know is that her peace is about to be shattered. From behind her comes the clattering of hooves. Startled, she turns around, and what does she see?"
"I don't know, what?"
"A horse?"
"A headless man, wearing a FALN tracksuit, riding a horse. That's right. It's the *Headless FALN Rider*. "
"Well, yes, but it's the man *on* the horse that's of interest here. A man..."
"Rumoured to be searching for his legendary FALN cap that went missing when he lost his head."
"... with no head on his shoulders! Wearing a FALN tracksuit. Searching for the legendary FALN cap that went missing -- when he lost his head."
"That sounds pretty implausible to me."
"That's super spooky."

"Yes. According to legend, young Gertrude Het had to endure years of psychotherapy before she was able to look at a horse or tracksuit again... And she's one of the *lucky ones*." He takes a sip from his bottle.
"Well, there are many versions of this story, the most peculiar of which has the Headless FALN Rider riding on the back of another headless man."
"If I hadn't lost my keys that one time, I'd agree with you. But... life is a cruel mistress..." He takes a sip.
"Gertrude Het may have been the first to witness the *Headless FALN Rider*, but she wasn't the last, oh no..."
"I thought that he rode a headless pig?" The lieutenant says with a little smirk.
"Who was the Headless Rider before he died?"
"Some say he was an undercover cop who blew his cover and got beheaded by the vicious gang he had infiltrated -- Now he rides, searching for his lost FALN cap, plotting revenge."
Oh, headless brother, where art thou?
"Others claim he was a professional jockey who veered off-course during a steeple chase, ended up in somebody's back yard, and got decapitated by an exceptionally taut clothes line..."
Even decapitation couldn't stop his commitment to the sport. Are *you* that committed?
"Personally, I think he was just some guy who hanged himself from a really tall tree and the fall was so violent that his head came clean off..."
"Coincidentally, at that exact moment, a horse happened to pass under him and his beheaded corpse mounted it, where it remains to this day... But then, no one really knows."
"Okay. Whatever became of the Headless FALN Rider?" (Conclude.)

dialoguetext: "I actually do have one... the strangest of them all. But I'll need to *fortify* myself before I can tell that one..."

"I want to hear the story of your name again."
"I'd like to listen to the tale of the Headless FALN Rider again."
"Can you tell me about the Cocaine Skull again?"
"Of course -- drink first, story later." He holds out his palm.
"Interesting." He grabs the thermal cup and shakes it. "Ah, this is what they use to keep the working man going."
"Right... a story specific to Martinaise and its history." He takes a sip and gargles the drink to prepare.
"For some reason the name Tequila fills me with foreboding. Maybe I *shouldn't* learn what it means."

Oh yeah, that's totally your style...
The lieutenant's brow is furrowed. He's listening as casually as he can.
"Oh yeah, not the first time this comes up." (Cough awkwardly.)

"Hey man, I'm not judging." He waves the bottle towards you. "This life's a valley of woes. Some of the highest-concept people in history have killed themselves -- *and* been drunks."

"Either way, it was a late Saturday night, when we, the Union of Moribund Alcoholics, got our drink on. Nothing remarkable about this, we get our drink on 24/7. Makes everything warm and glowy, I trust you know the feeling."
There is no train. Just you and the cold light of truth.
"Okay, I changed my mind. Sing me the song of Tequila Sunset."
"No, not really... you talked a lot about some sad churches and how everyone's just out to fuck you."
"Nothing much, you didn't want to talk about it. You just kept mumbling inaudibly to yourself."
"Mostly you kept shouting 'I am The Law' and talking about how you were going to bring the law to all lawless places with your law jaw."
"What, like you've *never* threatened to paint the wall with your brains in front of some strangers?"
"Whuh...? Uh... geez," he stammers. "I told you I wasn't much of a storyteller. It's okay, I didn't want to tell them anyway."
...is what you almost say, but the words choke in your throat. Do you really want to miss out on all this good stuff? Perhaps it's *significant*.
(Yes, say it. Say it!) "Stories *SUUCCKK*! I don't want to hear any of them. Ever!"
Oh, no. I wouldn't want that. Not at all.
Exactly. So you know what to say.

There might be interesting details, fresh experiences, exciting rewards... you'd really ignore it all?
"Yeah, you look like someone with a lot of cool stories. Wanna tell me how you even became Idiot Doom Spiral?"
"Every word I said was true. Tequila Sunset will break the looms of reality."
"Yeah -- looms. Why not? Then you jammed the pedal and ploughed right off the jetty and through the ice."
"When we finally got there you were sitting on the beach, crying. You said that your badge and uniform were in the car. It was too late to get in there though, the carriage had sunk too deep."
"That's not my name. I'm Raphaël Ambrosius Costeau. That's what you should call me."
"Nah, that name sucks. You're Tequila Sunset. Just embrace it, brother."
"My real name is Harry."
"No, that's just what your mother called you. Your real name is Tequila Sunset. Just embrace it, brother."
"Ouch!"
"I would've landed on my feet. I've got feline reflexes."
"Ouch, indeed. Reality was looking rather grim, just then -- me lying on my ass in a mud pit in the middle of a heavy shower. But when life knocked me down, I always got up..."
"So, now you've heard my tragic tale. What do you think? Like nothing you've ever heard, huh?" He takes a long swig of his drink.
"I literally can't believe it."
"Tequila, I've thought about this series of events for a long time. If there was anything else to it, I would have thought of it by now."
"Wait, is that it? I feel like there are some steps missing."
His eyes are your eyes.
"It was a day not unlike this one here..." You both glance skyward.
"*Wet*, okay? It was raining really hard." There's a trace of derision in his voice.
"Are you telling the story of the Headless--"
"Shut the fuck up, Rosemary!"
The streets are warmed by a southerly breeze. The lights of a passing motor carriage bloom and fade in the distance...
"The Headless FALN Rider?"

"The wind picks up, a sky already dark now blackens. Water starts falling from above, the first cold rain of the season..."

Two women stand on a small outcropping of rocks. One of them is wearing a purple raincoat. Thin lines reach out from the rods into the sea. Small droplets start appearing on the surface with increasing frequency.
"The women are caught in the downpour. They act quickly. Eva gathers the rods whilst Ulla turns around to reach for the tackle box..."
"When she sees something! Her shriek is so violent that the residents of the nearby apartment building believe lightning has struck..."
"Ulla makes a run for the shore, but Eva slips on a wet rock and disappears into the cold, cold canal with nary a sound..."

The man falls ominously silent for a moment. "Her body is never recovered." He looks you straight in the eye.
Don't turn around, don't turn around!

"During the investigation it became apparent that there was a love triangle, the third party being some small-time businessman -- I don't remember the exact details. The leading theory was that an argument broke out on the jetty and Deponte pushed Delgado into the canal, then cooked up this stupid cover story."

If it sounds like it makes no sense, that's because it doesn't.
"Why do you keep losing all your stuff?"
"Good fucking question, Tequila! If I knew the answer, you think I'd be hanging out on a beach in this formerly premium but now extremely dirty two-piece Lickra(TM) tracksuit?"
"I used to own my reality situation. My business buddies and I had our own creative services agency. I had a nice apartment, an even nicer piece of ass, but somehow it all got away from me..."

"What was the name of your agency?"

"What about the other drunks?"
"What's up with the tracksuit?"
"Let me ask you something else." (Conclude.)
"My agency, man..." He takes a long, melancholic sip. "The Boom Boom Room. Our concept was combining high art with the lowest forms of marketing -- the colour red, breasts, and oil painting..."
"I convinced my partners to reinvest some of our profits in an even-more high-concept 'cultural incubator' called 'Thin Air'. The artists were happy, the clients were happy."
"I was financing a group of poets in East Revachol who were developing a new, universal poetic language... but then it all went to shit..." He looks toward the bay.
Sounds intriguing. What say you, art cop?

"The female isn't yours to objectify, not in art nor anywhere else!"

"That's nothing. I've got an even *crazier* story."

"Yeah? Why don't you go eat shit, Tequila? There's no way you know a better one than that."

"This last one is the most Martinaise story I've ever heard..." He takes an almost comically long swig. Thus fortified, he continues.

"Cryptids?"
"Your lost keys?"
"A place to call home?"

"Hey, HEY. Fuck you, Tequila," he says, his voice level.
"No, Tequila. Most people already know where they live. It's guys like you and me that are the exceptions..."

Wait, there's a tingling back here... the stirring of a faint sensation...

Can't be what?

"There was this designer, his exact name is lost to history, but in life he was a legend. Made it big in Oranje, where he did some real pioneering work on grotesque and sans-serif typography. A fucking genius, man..."
He takes a swig, wipes his mouth, then continues. "That is, if he even existed. Who knows? It's an urban legend, after all..."

"Anyway, sometime later he started his own personal studio here in Martinaise, and that's when he started working on some *really* wild stuff. I'm talking some glass-smooth, forward looking design language, the kind of thing that would totally overthrow the old regime, design-wise."
He existed alright. You feel it deep within your basal ganglia. He was as real as you are...

"You know, Tequila." He taps the side of his nose twice. "*Nose* candy. The white railroad. *Party powder*!"
HE'S TALKING ABOUT COCAINE.

WRONG, NERD! Where there's a will, there's a way.
WRONG AGAIN, NERD. Where there's a will, there's a way.
"That's right. Two-hundred fifty grams of blow had *accumulated* in there over the years. We're talking high-grade Saramirizian pure, not that cut-rate shit your grandma does."
"There are those who believe that the designer was buried with this quarter-key of nose candy still lodged in his sinuses. *That's* what those expeditions are looking for..."
THE COCAINE SKULL.
"*The Cocaine Skull*!"
Wait... There's no way... It can't be... or *can* it?
He existed alright. You feel it deep within your basal ganglia. He was as real as you are...
Uhh... all the time?
"Okay, I'm convinced. Let's go find it!" (Undertake it!)
"Surprisingly, I'm not interested in looking for the skull."
"Rosemary, you said something about islets?"
"What have you learned from the other expeditions?"
"The Cocaine... Skull..."
"Don't listen to him or his grandma. He's just making things up."
"No, my grandma told me -- I've heard other people say it too. That it's underwater. Or, no..." He thinks. "Maybe it was the storm sewers..."
"Or maybe it's in the *air*? Or in an ancient steppe pyramid off shore?"
"They're pretty vague about it, in general. The gangsters like to claim they're looking for the grave of a friend... with picks and shovels..."
"The junkies, for some reason, are pretty upfront about it. They just say they're looking to snort some blow out of a dead man's nasal cavity."
"By now I'd say I know about as much about it as anyone on the coast."
"The archaeologists act all official about it, saying they're conducting 'serious research'. Honestly, I think they're not really scientists, just rich."
"Good thing, because I don't think you can find it right now anyway."
"Your loss. Could've been an amazing, ridiculous adventure." He shrugs.
"That's alright. We've got plenty of adventures for one case."
"Whoa, whoa, whoa. Hold on just a minute. Finding it right now is literally impossible."
"Why?"
"For one, the way is blocked... by that big lorry that says 'Delta Logistics Company' on the side. You'd *definitely* have to search the area behind that lorry too. Yet it is impassable."

"It's just not feasible within the economic and temporal frame of our current setup. Matter of fact, unless a bunch of money just falls out of the sky, we might *never* know what's up with that skull."

"And second, outfitting an expedition like that is expensive. It'd have to be a *big production* to do the Cocaine Skull justice. You need new gear, people who know what they're doing, all kinds of provisions..."
"I have to agree. We barely have what we need to solve the case we've got now. We can't afford to run around chasing after quasi-mythical pieces of drug paraphernalia..."
"Besides, it would look *extremely* bad for the RCM to be caught up in something that has the word *COCAINE* writ large on it. The PR is tricky on this."
"Damn, that's too bad."
"Yeah, well, that's the reality situation for you. Who knows, though? Maybe someday we'll get our chance..."
"Who cares? It was an idiotic idea anyway."
"What exactly are we talking about here?"
Along with a number of more banal street names: Blow, of course, but also flake, powder, pearl. Really anything that's white will get the idea across.
"I know, Tequila, I know..." He takes a swig, considers pouring some out for this lost genius, then thinks better of it.
"A skull filled with cocaine?"
"Oh, dear god," the lieutenant says, his palm rising to meet his face.
Honest men on an honest quest. You should join them.
WHAT?
"Do you have anything to fortify ol' Doom Spiral? Tell me you got some story juice."
"I changed my mind. I'll help you find your missing jacket."

dialoguetext: "Ah, Tequila, I *knew* you'd come through. That's fucking great, man!"
"Let me see. What? This isn't my jacket. My jacket was beautiful. This is fucking filthy! What am I supposed to do with this?"
(Give him the jacket.)
"I'll start right away."
"You're a god damn hero, Tequila!" He raises his bottle in salute, then takes a gigantic swig.
"Look, I just stumbled upon *another* dead body. I don't care about the jacket."
"What do you expect? You left it outside for a week!"
"I'm sorry. I found it like this."
"I'm not taking a disgusting pile of hobo rags. I may be in an irrecoverably decaying orbit, but I've still got standards..."
"Either bring it back the way it was before, or find a dumpster to burn it in." He hands it to you.
The lieutenant inspects the jacket in your hands. "You know, despite the *guano* it looks like the jacket itself is stain-resistant. It may just need a good scrubbing."
"My jacket?"
"Yeah, the one you had me clean the seagull shit off of."
A look of consternation crosses the man's face. He looks at you, then at his bottle, then back at you...
"What the fuck are you talking about, Tequila?"
"What the fuck are *you* talking about?"
"So you're saying this *isn't* your jacket?"
"'FALN'? That's medium-concept stuff. Not my style at all... I can't believe I'm saying this, but maybe you should lay off the booze -- It's fucking with your head."
"Rosemary, what the fuck is Tequila talking about?"
"Aye, that's the jacket you stole two weeks ago. From the kid who was making it with his gal on the beach."
"That's disgusting. I've never done anything like that in my life. You're both delusional." He scoffs. "'FALN'? That's medium-concept stuff."
"Your loss. I'm keeping the jacket for myself." (Keep it.)
"That shit is so medium-concept I wouldn't touch it with a stick. But yeah, okay, I'm sure it looks great on you."
"Yeah, it was pretty filthy, though, so I got it cleaned for you."
Underneath the accumulated filth the jacket itself appears to be stain-resistant. Maybe it just needs a good scrubbing?
Wait! Maybe there's another way... maybe up around the coast? Don't give up now!
What are you talking about? Don't give up! Maybe there's another way... maybe up around the coast?
"I already found a filthy jacket near the boardwalk."
"Holy shit! Tequila, how did you? Never mind -- I don't care, just let me see the jacket."
"I found a little more than I bargained for."
"What's that supposed to mean?"
"Nothing." (Give him the jacket.)
"There was a dead body nearby."
"What's that got to do with my jacket?"
"Probably nothing. Forget about it." (Give him the jacket.)
"It's a pretty freaky coincidence."
"What do I care about some local stiff? You gonna give me the jacket or no?"
"Fine, take the stupid thing." (Give him the jacket.)
It becomes abundantly clear to you how this man managed to lose his keys, business, friends and girlfriend.
"I went through a lot of trouble to get this for you. Take the fucking jacket." (Give it to him.)
"You know what? Fine. Maybe I can pawn it for some booze."
"Aye, good thinking."
In the harbour's dark, her cigarette is a beacon, dancing alone. The image comes to you effortlessly, as though you'd walked the same streets yourself a thousand times.
"That shit is so medium-concept I wouldn't touch it with a stick. But yeah, okay, I'm sure it looks great on you."
As you've already determined, the actual number is just over 200 -- but what's a little embellishment between friends?
As you've already determined, the actual number is 216 -- but what's a little embellishment between friends?
"I have this blue oblong pen." (Lend him your pen.)
"Don't know if I've mentioned it, but I used to be a businessman and *as* a businessman I am going to keep the pen for my trouble." He nods confidently.
"Fuckin' cops, man, always hasslin' the poor folk." He shakes his head. "You know what? I'm keepin' the pen and that's the end of it."
"I've got this blue medicinal spirit, how about that?"
He raises his palm as if to shun you back to wherever you came from. "No-no-no, contrary to popular belief, I enjoy being alive."
"Oh, right, I've seen that!"

"Second, outfitting an expedition like that is expensive. It'd have to be a *big production* -- to do the Cocaine Skull justice. You need new gear, people who know what they're doing, all kinds of provisions..."
"Right, okay. Never mind that I asked."
He taps against his head. "Askin' is how you get ahead."
"Now the only things I haven't lost are these two drunks."
"It's an okay jacket." The lieutenant shrugs. "If you're into that look."
"Okay, let's step aside for a second, I have something I want to talk about."
“You mean *this* jacket that I discovered on the boardwalk and had cleaned on a whim?”
"Hmmm." The man examines the jacket for a moment, a look of consternation on his brow...
"At least you got a nice jacket for your troubles." The lieutenant shrugs.
"Nah, this isn't it. 'FALN'? That's medium-concept stuff. Totally not my style."
"So you're saying there's *another* lost jacket out there somewhere?"
"C'mon, man, this *is* your jacket. You just don't remember it."
"No fucking way. Idiot Doom Spiral never forgets a piece of premium menswear..."
"It's a big world out there, Tequila. Lotta lost jackets in it. Don't know why you'd think this could possibly be mine..."
"Tell you what, Tequila: Why don't *you* just hang onto that one. I'll get another jacket, some day..."
"Ey, Doom Spiral! Ain't that the jacket you stole the other week?"
"Not on your fucking life, Rosemary! What's wrong with you people? Like I'd be caught dead wearing 'FALN' like some low-concept bicycle courier..."
"Thank you for your services, gentlemen." He turns to you. "Should we go and mail this? I think I saw a mailbox on the plaza."
"Anything else this merry band of adventurers can do for you, or do you need to go and mail that serious looking document of yours?" His face lightens up. "I think I saw a mailbox near the plaza."
"A few more questions first."
"Mailbox... plaza... got it!" [Leave.]
"Okay, what's on your mind?"
The man mumbles incoherently.
Not exactly an expert forgery. Don't Call Abigail would have signed something more like *Domwtclall Abheqoeel*.
Nooooo! That was my favourite thing, of all the things you have.
"I got a freebie, when I purchased a whole carton of cigarettes." He produces a white pen with brown logos. "Smoke cigarettes, get a free pen. Deals don't come any sweeter."
The writing under the tiny crown logo reads *Royal Extra*.
My favourite is the gun.
My favourite is the gun he lost.
Tequila... Tequila Sunset... Something ominous there.
"Okay, here's your jacket. Fresh washed!"
"I don't have any on me right now." (Lie.)
"You've done a great service to the community, to the RCM and to Revachol."
"That's it then. The deed is done."
"Mailbox, plaza -- got it! Bye!" [Leave.]
"Thank you for your help." He turns to you. "Should we go and mail this? I think I saw a mailbox on the plaza."
"Hey, guys -- I'm a hero!" He hands you the envelope, and waves his hand erratically at his companions.
"I wanna ask these guys a couple of things first."
"Glad to have been of assistance!" He gives you a thumbs up, and the envelope also. "After all this time, I feel like I've made a difference..."
"Hell yes!" The red-nosed drunk brings his hand up to his head for a salute.
"Anything else this merry band of adventurers can do for you, or do you need to go and mail that serious looking document of yours?" His face lightens up. "There's a mailbox on the plaza."
The incapacitated drunk lays there snoring like an ancient rusting tractor.
"Don't call Abigail!" The drunk in the pipe snorts and takes a swig from his bottle. The bottle is empty.
"Okay, what's on your mind?"
My favourite was the gun he lost.
My favourite is the gun.
"Don't know if I've mentioned it, but I used to be a businessman and *as* a businessman I am going to keep the pen for my trouble." He nods confidently.
"Uh, can I have the pen back too?"
"Don't know if I've mentioned it, but I used to be a businessman and *as* a businessman I am going to keep the pen for my trouble." He nods confidently.
Nooooo! That was my favourite thing, of all the things you have. This had better be worth losing the pen for.

"I don't think you're ready for that *grade* of reality yet. It'd be ill-advised for me to tell you. You gotta go do the *intro* yourself -- come back when you've been to the motor carriage, Tequila." He sips his beer.
"Idiot Doom Spiral... I am ready now. I've seen it. Tell me the story of Tequila Sunset."
"So, uh -- can you tell me the Tequila Sunset story now?"

"Didn't I already say, I don't wanna be the one who breaks it to you? You have to get acquainted with *the event* first! It'd be irresponsible..." The man shakes his head. His gray eyes look into yours.
"Alright!" He grabs the pen and paper and carefully, scribbles on the dotted line -- next to Lilienne's signature -- 'Idiot Doom Spiral'.
"Thanks, Rosie." He grabs the pen and paper and carefully, scribbles on the dotted line -- next to Lilienne's signature -- 'Idiot Doom Spiral'.
He points toward the waterline with his bottle.
...and also scary to tell you.
You need to face up to it. Go to the sea, inspect the machine.
"Please... please don't call... don't call..." begs the man in the pipe.
"Okay, we're drinking. We're drinking alcohol -- that's what we're doing. I *tried* to save the world once, a long time ago, with enterprise, creativity and willpower, but that didn't work out."
"So now it's a pirate's life for me."
"Mhm. Let me take a sip to moisten up my chords..." He takes a big sip, then begins: "Tequila Sunset rolled into Martinaise last Friday. And by *Tequila Sunset* I mean *you* -- the man, the myth."
It is.
Your hands cramp on the steering levers.
It's not meant as a joke. He's sorry for the Hermit Cop.
"You also kept pausing to knock the heel of your hand against your temples, saying 'Boring, boring, boring.'"
"All kinds sir. Beer *and* wine."
"What happened?"
"God bless them, though. I'd be alone without them. Anyway, that was all the story one bottle gets you." He turns his eyes to the bottle. "Almost empty this one..."
"I'm almost homeless myself. Doesn't seem so bad."
He's right. It's incredibly annoying.
You of all people should empathize with this. Perhaps this lost jacket is something you could help with...
A lost jacket? Sounds like a mystery you could look into...
"That's a lot of places."
He really has no idea who this Ruby is, sire.
I'm calling it -- it's neurological.
...the pause is long and dramatic...
"It's the *Headless FALN Rider*. A headless man wearing a FALN tracksuit. Riding a horse. In search for the FALN cap that went missing -- when he lost his head."

A shovel hits the sand somewhere behind the reeds, near an abandoned construction yard. The young men look over their shoulders, suspiciously. The sound of their digging seems loud in the sudden silence.
You know...
I'm talking about...
"I'm not surprised. Many men find it hard reaching that final level of genius without blow."
All day, baby...
"Wow."
"No," he corrects you: "WOW!!"
"And why wouldn't they, ey? Sounds like right strong stuff."
"I'm pretty sure they all just want to snort it, though."
Bullshit. They just want to snort it. But you could beat them to it, Harry. *You* could snort the magic skull cocaine instead...
"What do these expeditions plan to do with it?"
"The archaeologists say they want to put it in a museum. The gangsters say they want to sell it on the black market. And the ad agency guys say they're seeking inspiration..."
"And why do people think the skull is here, in Martinaise?"
"Here's the kicker -- this designer, this *lead designer* of a world famous design studio -- was *born* in Martinaise. A local boy. Martin Martinaise."
"That's why he brought his studio here -- back to where it all began. And that's why  they buried him here too -- perhaps right under Abs' pipe there..." he points to the pipe.
"Or probably further down the coast? Or in some yard in Martinaise proper. A hidden mausoleum? No one knows exactly."
"No, my grandma' always told me his grave lays somewhere on the islets on the bay..."
"This is ludicrous." The lieutenant turns to you. "And physically impossible. Sinuses can't contain that amount of anything."
Now, now detective... always the sceptic.
My only question is -- where does one get a *shovel*?
In a pyramid? Now that *would* be something...
He says it like it's obviously your name. Like you call someone Billy Brunuel or 'Leader of the Fourth Street Gang'.
Good, these people know your *true* name. Looks like it has preceded you, Mr. Sunset. More on that later.
I like this guy. You should, too. He *respects* you by calling you your *true name*.
This guy's your buddy-buddy. You feel it immediately: you belong to an organization. A fraternity. Of *drunks*.
*Idiot Doom Spiral*, huh? This is bound to be a good, high-concept conversation. At last!
It's a touchy topic. He hasn't gotten laid in *ages*.
No-no. You need the *wisdom*.
Oh yes, you do, *bratushka*. The only thing better than that is pushing the pedal to the metal after you kiss the tie. And off we go...
"No one's fucked me. *I* do the fucking around here."
"Abigail..."
It's more like you were cramping theirs.
"Wait, on the second thought -- I've heard enough."
"So you *don't* want to just hear the same story again? Okay, okay. Huh." He looks taken aback.
"Do you know any Personal Brand Strategists? I need to start building my image." (Show him the certificate.)
He scans the document and lets out a long, low whistle. "Things have really turned around for you, haven't they? You've got *big money* problems now." He looks back at you, eyes gleaming.
"What do you need to know?" He leans forward and takes another sip from his bottle, brows knitted together in mock seriousness.
What you truly want to know is -- can you really trust your entire fortune to a drunk who lost his house keys while out for a jog?
He doesn't exactly come across as responsible. Are you sure you can trust him with your *entire fortune*?
"Let's talk about improving my personal brand again..."
"Right on." He swigs his beer. "Have you made your mind up?"
"So I checked out the horseback monument..."
"No one does it better than me, eh?" He claps his hands in delight. "I was able to get it all together -- and *so fast* too. No wonder I used to be an industry leader..."
"Don't be shy, Tequila. Of course I'll do it." He ploughs a thumb into his chest. "I'm your man."
"What do you mean you're 'my man'?"
"Sorry, I'm already taken." (Nod at Kim.)
"No, you've misunderstood me -- I want you to *recommend* a Personal Brand Strategist, not become one."
"Tequila, Tequila... You don't know what you're missing out on. Those other guys? They'll just steal your money while providing meagre service."
"Now *me*, on the other hand? I only provide *very* high-concept ideas. And as I already understand *your* needs I can marry them with your brand easily. I'll help you make your mark."
The lieutenant is about to say something, but gets cut off...
"But I've got something the others don't. I'm on *your* level. And as I already understand *your* needs I can marry my high-concept ideas with your brand easily. I'll help you make your mark."
"Your Personal Brand Strategist man. Now I know I'm not your 'typical' choice. I don't wear a suit, I'm not a hundred years old, I'm not about to die tomorrow..."
Not so sure about the last part, with all that drinking...
"Listen, I'm not about to come between you two. I know my place, eh? I'll just be your Personal Brand Strategist man. Your high-concept idea generator. Yeah?"
*Great* can-do attitude! A billion reál mindset. Clinically *insane* energy! Hire him on the spot!!
"That's it, you're *hired*!"
"This voice in my head tells me to hire you, but I'm not so sure..."
"No, Tequila, no..." He sighs heavily. "I'm a *professional*, you see. I insist that you give me a formal interview. It wouldn't be fair on the other candidates if you didn't."
"Relevant experience?"
"I have reservations about your... personal responsibility."
"How does your drinking impact your work performance?"
"Alright, give me your best pitch."
"Sure, my man, let's circle back whenever you want." He hiccups. "Take your time. I'll be here."
"Let's come back to this later."
Grill him a bit, see how he performs under pressure.
"Like what -- any examples?"
"I used to be a moderately-high-net-worth individual myself, if I can say so. I've *managed* big money before, played the game, hustled the movers of the marketing world..."
"Remember when Maria Kapaleva caused an uproar by walking the red carpet in those slippers -- the ones with the stick-on jiggly tits?"

"Numbers? How about fifteen fucking years of jamming *art* into people's heads? That's hundreds of high-concept ideas developed *and* executed for those fancy corp boys in their suits. The result?" He leans back, ready for his mic-drop...
"I need numbers -- years of service, P&L statements..."
A subtle smile lights up his puffy face, like a ray of sun breaking through the stratosphere. He likes reminiscing.

"At the Boom Boom Room I directed a team of *talent architects*. People so high concept their names were nothing but a single letter. We had *manic* ideas, fuelled by copious amounts of coffee-flavoured whey powder. We did stuff no one had ever seen before -- or *since*!"
We're going to need examples here -- just going by one of your initials doesn't cut it.
You're after measurable performance, not tales of happy memories. Numbers, please! How many years did he work, what profits did he earn?
"That was *me*. I did that." He looks up at the sky, victorious and content like an old cat. "We sold a lot of slippers that year..."
Yes, yes we *do* remember that...
No, we don't?
But why don't we remember that??!
It's because it's not *cool* or *stylish*. It's lame and *out* -- even Ms. Kapaleva couldn't pull it off.

Alright, here we go -- Ms. Kapaleva (née Olga Grebennikova) was once known as East Revachol's premier vedette and sex symbol. Her role in director Do Do Chakan's sexploitation motion picture 'Psychotronic Stripper' launched her into stardom. She's been voted Most Captivating Woman by La Fayette *three years* running.
Three years, you hear that? Three years... how hot did she have to be?!
"*Millions* of reál generated for clients. I've made my name in this world."
And then he lost it all by going for a jog... not exactly *inspiring*.
"Tequila, Tequila... Whatever's going on in my reality situation doesn't have any bearings on yours. This is all about *you* and *your* future. Ask me about *that*."
"Okay, okay, let me get a sip first..." He manages to down half a bottle, then sits up straight, a hazy but oddly determined stare in his eyes. His finger shoots up.

"You see, net worth means *nothing* to the people of Martinaise. Nada. Null. For them to see your wealth, to really *respect* that, you need to convert it into something real, something *tangible*. The bigger the better." He peers into his bottle for inspiration.

"The horseback monument!" He snaps his fingers. "That's the centre of the district -- they'd *have* to pay attention to that. We could get your name up there in lights. Damn thing's due for a *re-conceptualization* anyway."
"What are you talking about? I'm the hottest shit in town. I'm as *real* as it gets."
"There's nothing more real than the *End of Everything*."
"Yeah, okay. Real like paying your bills or eating malt fibre in the morning."
"To never even *grasp* the idea of economic nonentities... I feel sorry for them."
"You're aware that monument is *supposed* to look like it's exploding? It doesn't need renovating."
"I didn't say renovating, I said *re-conceptualization*. It's medium-concept shit is what it is," he says, spitting out each word.
Hmm... the level of conceptualization *could* always be higher, yes.

"Drinking is the fuel to my fire. Moistens me up to ensure the high concepts have a smooth landing." He tries taking another sip from the bottle, but misses and pours some of its contents inside his collar.
But what would it cost?
"Ah, shit..."
He could definitely work more on his Hand/Eye Coordination...
"How much is this going to cost me?"
"We really haven't got time for this," the lieutenant says, getting impatient. "In case you've forgotten, we're supposed to be investigating a murder."
"Nothing up front. That's 'cause I always put the client first. My cut'll come out of the back-end, *after* we've made you a sensation...."

"And forget about contractors and the like. This job I'm handling *personally*, concept and execution," he continues. "Any unexpected expenses we'll take care of later. Can't let price compromise the work. Easy."
"Okay, let's do it, you're hired!" (Accept his offer.)
You should hire him and ask him to stop drinking. Everyone deserves a second (or third) chance.
"That's it, I'm *BACK*!" He takes a celebratory swig -- a *big* one. Too big. The brown liquid cascades down his face and floods his nostrils. Once he's finished choking he spits on the ground.

"Sorry about that, my friend. This isn't about me, this is about *you*, of course. A chance for you to give back to the community. To get your brand out there. To teach them your *name*." He spreads his hands across the sky...
"I can already see it -- Tequila Sunset -- spelled out in cathode rays. Luminous against the evening sky. There won't be a single kid in this town who doesn't know who you are."
This is a good moment to bring up his drinking... He'll get nothing done if he continues like that.
"One more thing -- you're going to have to cut back on the booze."
"Whoa there!" The man looks taken aback, hands high in the air. Tiny droplets of beer flicker in his beard like miniscule pearls.
Yeah, whoa there! What is this, the fun police?!

"No need to worry about *that*," he says, his inebriated mouth twisting into odd shapes, "I've got it *all* under control. Besides, it helps with my creativity. Gets the business juices flowing, y'know?" He finishes it off with a wink.
"Good, when can you start work?"
"Give me half an hour, my friend. In fact," he raises his grubby finger again, "I demand you to *sit down here* and *not move* until I'm back. Open a beer, chat with your old pals..."
The lieutenant massages his temples and looks down at the ground.
"*Relax*. I see you both running around like maniacs, just back and forth, back and forth. Gotta live a little, enjoy the sun."
There is little time for this...
"*Relax*. I see you both running around like maniacs, just back and forth, back and forth. Gotta live a little, enjoy the day."

"I don't think I have time to just sit and wait..."
"Sure, sounds like a much-needed break from all the work."
"No, Tequila, let me take care of it."

Then try to strike up a conversation with Don't Call Abigail about something other than Abigail (to no avail)... It's all about Abigail.
"Exactly! Just give me a minute or two..."
