dialoguetext: The lieutenant sits silent the entire time, preferring to focus on his notebook.
"Here he is -- the man of the hour!"
"All finished?"
"We've pissed off the lieutenant!" (Look at Kim.)
Clearly we have better things to do than sit down and chat with a bunch of drunks!

"I know, I know. Ran into some problems there -- material shortages and the like -- but don't worry, genius *thrives* under constraints!" He points at himself, proud and happy. "That's why you pay for the best..."
What an athlete! There should be a new word for drunk moves like that -- like alco-lete or gin-nast!
He can't even walk straight. How did he write your name in cathode rays?
"You seem a bit drunk. You sure you're happy with your work?"
"Good, good. Can I go and take a look at the monument now?"
The lieutenant closes his notebook and nods at you, ready to go.
"Just head on over to the horseback monument. You'll see. World's gonna *know* -- about you, me, and the shiny numbers in our bank account."
"Of course I am. When you're ready -- and I don't think you ever will be..." He pauses to pick up his bottle.
"But if there's anything else your old friend can do for you, let me know." He takes a mouthful of beer, swishing it around in his mouth like some kind of sommelier.
"Yes, whenever you're ready -- and I don't think you ever will be..." He pauses to pick up his bottle.
"If I can do it, so can you."
"Well, I guess if it helps with your work..."
"I know what you mean, I become a *superpower* when I'm drunk."
"I don't think *I* can do it. Sorry." He stares at the bottle in his hand, then lets out a deep sigh...
"No, you're right. I've *got* to do this. I *need* this." He pushes a balled fist into a thigh. "Alright, you know what, Tequila, you old rat? I'll consider your request."
Some complex calculations are taking place in that intoxicated mind of his...
Suddenly you feel sad, looking at this man and his bottle... somehow he looks *ancient*, these thoughts having chased him for years.
"No, you have to stop drinking. I insist."
"Exactly! We're partners, you and I -- partners in drinking, partners in business..." He chugs in celebration.
"No can do. Sorry." He stares at the bottle in his hand, then lets out a deep sigh...
"Exactly! I just know I wouldn't be able to deliver the hot shit you're after without it." He has a quick swig from his bottle.
"Listen, I can feel it in my guts -- a bright future awaits you, the one and only *Tequila Sunset*! You're already building great brand equity. No doubt the profits will come rolling in shortly."
This little weasel still isn't owning up to *ripping you off*!
"That's it? It's just a bunch of scaffolding!"
"It was extraordinary. Truly a feat of the century to get that scaffolding up so fast."
"Listen, I know you're trying to *rip me off*..." (Take a threatening step forward.)
"Of course not. Your trademark will be all over it as soon as the workers can get to it. The strike's holding them up. Not much I can do about that." He shrugs, then takes a swig from the bottle.
"Ya hear that, Rosie? I'm back -- *big time*." He reaches over to his buddy to clink the bottles, then turns back to you.
"Whoa! Rip you off? What is this, a radio novella on Channel 8? Friends don't let friends start ripping each other off! No, that's not how we operate here."
"Listen, I know it might look a little *lacking* right now, but you gotta trust the process. I've got it all under control. Once the strike is over, the workers will be all over the monument..."

"And that's only the start. Wait until the strike's over and the workers can finally deliver the product. I *guarantee* the papers will pick it up. You'll be the talk of the town -- -- investing into the community, creating value, giving back..."
*Papers*? Maybe she'll read the papers and see your name... Maybe it will bring her back...
"I *guarantee* the papers will pick it up once it's all finished, with photos and everything. You'll be the talk of the town -- investing into the community, creating value, giving back..."
"I *guarantee* the papers will pick it up, with photos and everything. You'll be the talk of the town -- investing into the community, creating value, giving back..."
Hey, your new Personal Brand Strategist still hasn't laid off the drink -- even though he promised.

A woman is sitting by the kitchen table, eating buttered toast and drinking herbal tea. She opens the Salzneben Report, a quarterly business magazine. There, in shiny tricolour print -- *him*, triumphant and victorious, like an apparition from the past...
"Weren't you going to drink less while on the job?"
"I wonder what the newspapers might say..."
"Alright, I trust you to deliver the final final product." (Proceed with the quest.)
"I'm pulling the project. I don't have confidence it will ever get finished." [Cancel the entire task.]
"What would you like them to say?"
The strike might take forever... Maybe you should just cut your losses while you can.
Here's a man who knows how to play the media -- by starting with the right question.
"Very nice. You could be your own PR agent, Tequila." He nods.
"Tequila... you know it isn't that easy yourself. I promise you I'm *working on it*." He winks, his fingers tightening around the bottle.
He isn't 'working on it' -- he'll never stop drinking.
He sighs. "It isn't that easy... But I'm working on it. I really am. I even signed up for this evening group in Jamrock."
Sire, he's telling the truth.
"But Tequila..." He hangs his head in despair. "For what? I really tried to make it work this time -- for you, for me, for the triumph of *high-concept* ideas..."
"Don't spend a single brain cell worrying about it, just leave it all to me... the final outcome will be *spectacular*. Just takes a little time..."
"Nightclub owner reinvigorates youth culture, makes a fortune!"
"Local bankruptcy curse lifted by stock market mogul!"
"Philanthropist rescues local kid from violent father, town pays tribute!"
"Local detective solves murder while making his fortune!"
"Wealthy businessman renovates local eyesore!"
"And I didn't even lose anything!" He stares into empty space, eyes like discarded bottle caps. "Okay, guess I'm back to where I was before. Square one. It's not like I haven't been here before."
"Anything else you want?" He takes an enormous swig from the bottle, swaying back and forth.
"But we *haven't* solved the murder yet," the lieutenant says. "We might have if you hadn't gotten distracted by this."
"Anything else?" He throws one leg over another, smug and content.
"You want my opinion on the re-conceptualization?"
"Yes, show them *real* art, then they'll be able to appreciate the majesty of my finances."
"Here he is! The man, the reality, the *financial czar*." He presents you to the group as if on a stage. "You seen it yet?"
"What can I do for you, boss-man?"
"The re-conceptualization? I had a quick look but I haven't really taken it in properly."
"Seen what?"
"The re-conceptualization? I've been busy with other things."
"Oh, I see what you're doing. Keeping us waiting for the verdict, drawing it out -- I like it. Really builds up the suspense." He looks to his drinking partner. "Forever the showman, this one."
He's covering up any nerves with the tried and true method -- excessive drinking.
He's struggling to cover up his nerves now that he's having *one* less beer a day.
"Well, no rush, but it'd be good to know what you make of it when you get a chance."
"The re-conceptualization of the monument? Your new reality situation?" His words are stale with alcohol and utter disbelief.
"*Other* things? We're talking about your big moment here, your time to shine, your ascension into a household name."
"The re-conceptualization? Yeah, I've seen it."
"Great!" He scans your face for any telltale signs of a verdict. "Great."
"Yeah, two secs." He slurps from his bottle then wipes droplets from his beard with a sleeve. Satisfied, his stomach sends a muted eruption to his throat, where it turns into a damp growl.

"Right, let's hear you then. I put a lot of work into that project, Tequila, a *lot of work*. Had to bring back my hustle game and call in some old partners to pull it off. So, c'mon, tell me what I want to hear."
"It's good but the timing is unfortunate."
"It doesn't quite meet my expectations."
"It's gonna have to wait. I have important business to attend to first." (Put it off indefinitely.)
"What important business? I'm your *Personal Brand Strategist*, Tequila -- you're supposed to run all business matters by me. That's how this works."
"It's police business."
"This is different..."
"They finally caught up to you, have they?"
"Something like that..."
"Yes, they have," the lieutenant says, unamused.
"Alright, I understand. We'll do this some other time, when you can focus on yourself and not this *inconvenience*."
Painful images replay in the lieutenant's mind as he lies still in his sick bed: gun fumes, the flash of metal, and occasionally a clumsy stack of scaffolding...
You hear the lieutenant suppress an almighty scoff.
"Different *how*? Business is business. Doesn't matter if it's small or large, I handle it for you now -- that's what you hired me to do."
(Applaud.) "I love it. Pure, naked brilliance."
"It's an all-round disaster. Just awful."
"You love it? Shit, Tequila, that's just made my day." His face lights up as his drinking buddy gives him a congratulatory pat on the back.
"What do you mean? The timing couldn't be *better*. The traffic through town will return now that the strike's over. Don't worry, I've *thought* about this."

"That's... disappointing. But, okay, I can work with that. I'm used to dealing with fussy clients and retrogressing from my highest concepts for them. Can't expect everyone to be on..." He points at himself with both thumbs. "...*this* level."
"You're kidding me? This is a joke?" He hangs a confused look off you. "You're  being serious? Alright..." He takes a gulp of beer.
He dares to sit there in disbelief when you confront him about his own *scam*!
Be *professional*. He probably doesn't even know what happened to you, why the strike is over...
It's bad PR and therefore bad for business. Tell him you don't want anything to do with it -- or him.

Plastic bags heavy with tins and deformed vegetables swing from the fists of a young mother crossing a roundabout. Her mouth falls open as she looks up at the central structure. 'C'mere, Luc. Over here now, please,' she says to her curious toddler. The bags beat steady bruises into the mother's calves as she hurries him away.
"So where does this leave us? Do you still want me as your Personal Brand Strategist or what?"
The utter *genius* of its design -- conveyed beautifully through his commitment to a singular aesthetic. He's gone above and beyond!
What more could you want? He got your brand out there while giving back to the community. He hit the brief perfectly.
It's an image of you that will stand the test of time. People will remember this for an age.
It's like he knows *nothing* about you. Stinks of a man doing what's best for him, not his clientele.
Picking the right praise to give is just as important as picking the right critique. People shape themselves according to any and all feedback they get.
"I've never seen marketing as inspired as that. It really is *high concept*!
"This is an event. It's *history* -- people will remember this."
"I'm amazed you were able to do it so well and for so cheap."
"It's exactly the brand image I want to present to the public."
"It's a load of shit! I knew you'd rip me off."
"I don't want anything to do with it. You have to take it down."
"Your timing is awful! People died over there, then you go and do *that*."
"That isn't the right image of me to present to the public."
"'Awful' is very strong, Tequila. You're gonna have to explain how I missed the mark by *so much* if that's the case. What don't you like about it?"
"Gimme more, gimme more. What do you like most about it?" He's giddy -- both from the drink and the anticipation.
"Let your Personal Brand Strategist handle the timing, alright? You just focus on telling me what you liked about my work up there."
"Bet you're glad you hired me as your Personal Brand Strategist now? So, what's next, boss?"

The wooden clack of bilboquet comes to a halt before the central structure of a roundabout. Awe whistles through the air as the onlooker takes in every angle. Eager eyes fill nearby windows, brought to the glass by the sound of the toy, but now also taking in the sight of the striking new installation.
"Go on then, what exactly isn't doing it for you?" He wraps both hands around his bottle and leans forward, ready to listen.
"I knew it! That's what you get when you hire me -- customer satisfaction guaranteed. Woo!"
"Didn't I tell you?" He turns to his drinking buddy. "I told him, didn't I? Several times. This is what I *do*."
"Fuck yeah they will. Tequila Sunset is on the timeline. They'll be talking about you for years. The one and only."
"That's how I roll. Best results at a low cost. Isn't that what the business game is all about? Let me tell you -- it is! I'm its biggest and best player." He winks at you.
"Take it down? Is it really that bad?" He drags a hand down his face. "This is *fucking me up*, Tequila. I thought you'd love it -- honestly."
"What are you talking about? Who died? I think I would know if anyone had died over there. Would have heard *something* about it. There's no need to make up little stories, Tequila."
"It isn't? I thought that's what you were all about." He drags a hand down his face. "This is *fucking me up*, Tequila. I thought you'd love it -- honestly."
"What are you talking about? *Rip you off*? Stop with this bullshit. Just say you don't like it. There's no need to drag my name through the mud like this."
"Sure am! Not sure what's next yet but I know you'll nail it."
"Actually, I think you've done enough for me. I no longer need you."
"I do. I'm willing to give you another chance."
"Nope. I'm going to have to let you go."
"You bet your ass I will. Tequila Sunset is just getting started. No one's ready for the shit we're going to pull." He beats his chest a couple of times. "Feels good to be back."

"Good one, boss." He laughs weakly but stops when he realises you're being serious. "What -- really? That's it? You can't cut it short *now*. We're just getting started. At least give me an explanation."
"Phew! Alright, you had me going there. I thought that was it for me -- back to rock bottom I go!" He lets out a nervous laugh.
"Fuck..." He lets his head drop between his arms. "Well, that's that. At least I tried." A long and heavy breath out, a few sloppy sucks on his bottle.
"Thanks for sticking with me. I'll make sure I do better in the future." He exhales with huge relief. "Let me make it up to you. Anything I can do right now?"
"Thanks for the opportunity. Gutted that I fucked it up... but what have I really lost?" He tries to shrug into a more carefree existence.
"Fine. You know what? Fuck it. You'll be back, Tequila. You wanna go -- you go. This isn't the end. I'm taking you all the way to the top."
"Thanks for this, boss. Just what I needed. Is there anything else I can do for you right now?"
You wince as your injured leg throbs with fresh pain. The drunk doesn't notice.
Pretty sure you could dial up the melodrama to max and he still wouldn't figure it out.
"The market moves fast and with extreme casualty."
He better not let you down again. Remember, this is *your* money and *your* reputation he's playing with.
"Calm down! I'm only yanking your leg. Of course I'm not firing you."
He freezes in his seat, motionless except his pupils, which quickly flick from side to side.
"Fucking hell, Tequila. Don't do that to me. I appreciate being kept on my toes, but *man*!" He shakes his head to straighten himself out.
Is he reading a book about his life so far to figure out which reality he's in?
He doesn't know whether to expunge or consume. What will pacify the wrenching feeling in his gut?
He cracks open a bottle and sucks the bitter foam welling at the top. "Do you want anything else or can I concentrate on my drinking?"
Business buddies, huh? This guy might be just what we're looking for. Ask him if he knows any Personal Brand Strategists who can help you out.
"What are you doing?!"
It's Idiot Doom Spiral -- he's *back*. Like a beast made of jaundice and fetid polypropylene, he returns locked in stiff combat and with a most fearsome foe...
"Let's just move on. Anything else you want from me?"
"Do you want anything else? If not, I've got some serious drinking to do..."
He turns his swollen nose to face the sun, cheeks ruddy from the biting wind.
He turns his swollen face against the snow, droplets of beer freezing in his beard.
He turns his swollen face against the wind, freezing rain battering his cheeks.
He turns his swollen nose to face the moon, cheeks ruddy from the biting wind.
Before you know it the man has put down the bottle, stood up, and left. Minutes pass; the clouds change shape up in the sky...
Hmm, he seems even more drunk than before...
"My *style*? What about it?"
"Anyway, we should probably get back to the case. Let's go."
"For starters, you're wearing *the exact same* outfit I first met you in..." He holds his nose.
"Have you even *smelled* that jacket? It's like some wretched night-wandering creature died in it."
"It's disco, Kim."
"Yeah, maybe I should let these threads air out a little bit."
The lieutenant's right. You're the acrid sweet smell of decay that makes people evacuate the room.
You have developed a bit of a *rind* over the past few days.
Somehow you thought you were *concealing* it, but now you know that *everybody* has noticed.
"Now, now, no need to despair, detective. You know the expression 'The clothes make the man'? We just need to find you a *new style*. That jacket you just acquired is a decent start."
Seeing you on the verge of tears, the lieutenant realizes he was maybe overly direct vis-a-vis your sartorial situation...

The lieutenant regards you for a moment, unsure whether you're making a joke or not, and if so, whether he should acknowledge it...

dialoguetext: "For starters, you're dressed like an old fascist. Is that really appropriate?"
"I don't care about their politics, it just *looks* cool."
"Well, all that FALN gear makes you look like a bicycle courier. All you're missing is the shirt."
"To be perfectly blunt, you're dressed like a blood-hungry mercenary."
"That's not quite what I was going for."
"Yes. And this 'mega-binoclard' knows how to sew a lapel and center a back vent." The lieutenant raises one eyebrow at you.
"I'm not taking 'style' tips from someone who dresses like a mega-binoclard."
"So if you want to wake up next to anyone other than *Commodore Red*, you might do well to take notes."
"Then maybe you should change your look..."
The lieutenant sighs. "It might feel good to play *super-merc*, but you might want to ask if it's actually helping you solve the case..."
"What happens when I find the shirt?"
"Who knows?" The lieutenant shrugs. "Perhaps something *miraculous*."
"Really? You think so?"
"Officers above the rank of sergeant are granted wide discretion when it comes to their uniforms..."
"The idea is that civilians are more likely to open up to someone who's not dressed like a typical cop..."
The lieutenant sighs. "Is that really the impression you want to give people?"
"Okay." (Nod.) "You're a sharp dressed man. We could be style buddies."
"I'm wearing it in case we get into a firefight."
The lieutenant's right. It gives you all the *panache* of a bicycle courier, daredevil and commander of the city streets!
That's right. You're protected in your ceramic carapace. Whatever harm you inflict on that world won't be visited on you.
You're wearing the vestments of *order* and *hierarchy*. You have nothing to answer for.
Except all the war crimes the people in those vestments perpetrated, but what's a few atrocities here and there if you *look cool* doing it?
Your half-brother is proud to stand beside you.
'Eclectic' is for pop music with 'indigenous' percussion. *You're* a sartorial maverick.
"They're just clothes, Kim. Who cares?"
"To be perfectly blunt, you're dressed like a bum. And you smell like one, too."
"Then maybe you should change your look..."
"That's not quite what I was going for."
That's right -- You're an entrepreneur of the peace, here to disrupt legacy law enforcement with buzzwords and privatization schemes.
"It's just, well, you look more like a high-flying businessman than a police officer."
You have developed a bit of a *rind* over the past few days.
The lieutenant's right. You're the acrid sweet smell of decay that makes respectable people wrinkle their noses, the room-evacuating fart...
"But the gloves keep my hands warm -- look." (Show him the gloves.)
"Then maybe you should change your look..."
Somehow you thought you were *concealing* it, but now you know that *everybody* has noticed.
"That's not quite what I was going for."
"I'm the hobocop, Kim, what do you expect?"
Seeing you on the verge of tears, the lieutenant realizes he was maybe overly direct vis-a-vis your sartorial situation...
The lieutenant sighs.
"Let's not get ahead of ourselves, detective..."
"Office Harbinger."
"Regular-core?"
"Superstar Casual." (Click your tongue.)
"Hobo chic."
"Formal apologetic."
"Well, I can't say it doesn't *fit* you..."
"Still, you might try *branching out* a little. You know the expression 'The clothes make the man'? The right outfit, in the right situation, can make all the difference in the world."
"That's not quite what I was going for."
"Then maybe you should change your look..."
"Well, yeah, I want everyone to know I'm here to defend traditional values and stomp communards."
"Then maybe you should change your look..."
"That's not quite what I was going for."
"Well, yeah. You never know when you're going to need to pitch a business proposal."
"Oh, I just thought that this was how professional people were supposed to dress."
"Oh, god. Don't start *talking* like those people, too..."
"There's nothing *wrong* with it, per se. It's just... a little much..."
"I'm not taking 'style' tips from someone who dresses like a washed-up TipTop racer."
"This 'washed-up TipTop racer' knows how to sew a lapel and center a back vent." The lieutenant raises one eyebrow at you.
A warm smile.
That's why his clothes fit so well...
That bottle, *bratan*! Just look at that bottle!
I really don't care about any bottle. I don't want to look at it.
Where? Bottle? What?
You stop mid-step and put your hand on the garish necktie.
In this drunk's hand -- on the pipe there. Glowing blue, a mysterious, otherworldly blue. Filled to the brim with holy mysteries!
It's hard to know what exactly your vivid interior is speaking of here, but I'm guessing it's got a lot of alcohol in it.
Okay. Cool. What do I do next?
[Discard thought.]
Oh I think this is about so much *more* than cool. Please go talk to him. See what it's about. I'm *drawn* to it.
You *should* care. I'm getting a *very* special vibe from that bottle. Please go talk to him. I need to look at it closer...
"That's just life, friend."
"Are you drinking that?"
"What was I gonna say?"
"I'm not running tabs. It's bad for business."
"Doctors are idiots, buddy-boy."
"Look, opening it with my eye-socket again... No problemo."
"The way she goes, buddy-boy..."
"The way she fucking goes..."
"Gotta ride this one out."
"Not sensing a lot of concept in this."
"Where's my lighter?! Oh, holding it again."
"But are you *really* cornering the market is the question?"
"I should definitely start thinking about jogging again."
"Don't sit on it. Keep the hard stuff moving."
"It's a jungle out there... and in here."
"Pass it on, Rosie."
"Don't 'ya dare to call' er..."
*whimpers*
"Abby? Don't call Abigail!"
"Just please don't call 'er."
"Abigail!"
"Don't call Abigail."
"Shit, Abigail... please don't call 'er."
"Ar'ya... callin' Abigail?"
An old monument stands in the middle of the traffic island. It is surrounded by scaffolding that has been haphazardly erected around it.
[Leave.]
Who is this?
Something with great kinetic energy seems to have impacted the cuirass... around where the 'heart' is. A bullet?
Someone's shot him in the heart. Interesting.
What indentations? What do I see?
A silver plaque on the statue's pedestal reads: 'I am Filippe III, the Squanderer, the Greatest of the Filippian Kings of Revachol; Son of Filippe II, the Opulent; Father of Filippe IV, the Insane.'
Not a good track record of mental health in that family.
"Lieutenant -- has someone *shot* the king?" (Point to the indentation)
Don't mention it.
The monument stands high above you. Mute and indifferent to your sightings.
"Okay..." He cleans his glasses before looking up. "I can't see it. But I'll take your word for it."
"What do you think?"

"Well... Martinaise is riddled with bullet holes. This place saw a lot of action during the Revolution. But the statue *is* recently renovated -- so maybe a joke? Target practice? Or a political statement?"
"Yes, a practical joke."
"Mhm, target practice."
"Political. It's a *king* and he's shot."
"None of the above. Maybe it's connected to the murder?"

"If we connect every bullet hole in Martinaise to the murder, we'll get an overwhelming amount of loose threads..." He takes his notebook out. "But then again, our guy *was* shot. And that hole would be recent."
He takes a note. "It's not *completely* tangential -- at least worth noting down. I wouldn't hold my breath, though."
We'll see.

"If we connect every bullet hole in Martinaise to the murder, we'll get an overwhelming amount of loose threads..." He takes his notebook out. "But then again, we don't really know what we're dealing with here, so..."
He takes a note. "I've made a note. Don't hold your breath."
The king stands high above you, surveying the bay. Mute and indifferent to your sightings.
"Why not?" He shrugs. "What this shows us is guns aren't too uncommon here. And people still shoot them. Sometimes at kings." He takes a note in his notebook.
What did this king do?
The more you ask yourself, the less you know. One thing is for certain, though: you're brain-damaged. It's serious. And permanent.
High above you, the king stands triumphantly oblivious to your memory trouble.
Even by the standards of the Filippian kings, Old Sumptuous Filippe was known for his profligacy.
In what way?
Beneath the cold waters of the Insulindian Bay, thrown there by the revolutionaries after they cleaned out the royal mausoleum.
Well, he blew through the whole national treasury, starting the decline of one of the penultimate century's greatest superpowers: the Suzerain of Revachol...
I don't want to know.
His own maladministration foreshadowed the fall of the monarchy during the Antecentennial Revolution, an end to his family line and the monarchy on the Insulindian isola.
How did he manage to blow through *the entire national treasury*?
A group of marble pleurants still surrounds the king's vandalized tomb... A deathly cold wind sweeps up candy wrappers and old newspapers.
Fair enough, I have other questions. (Stop the knowledge from pouring in.)
Stories have it that he had his bedroom converted into a treasure chamber where he stored unfathomable wealth: *krugerrands*, bars of gold, ornate weaponry, armour, and various chalices.
Filippe III's ludicrous bronze likeness looks defiantly up into the sky.
That's what the revolutionaries said -- 150 years later. Right before they emptied out the royal mausoleum and dumped His Majesty's mortal remains in the Insulindian Bay.
His Majesty's courtiers said it helped him connect with the *Higher Realms*.
He called it the *Sol Aurum*. It was obscene. There were whispers he slept on a huge pile of gold-dipped feathers like some obese dragon, instead of a bed like a normal person.
Not just *any* nose candy, though. We're talking royal *Filippian* blow, allegedly twice as potent as the stuff you find nowadays. And purple, Filippian cocaine was purple.
The man certainly knew how to live!
So he was addicted to nose candy. A bloated druggie?
The what now?
But wait! You haven't even heard about his fabled cocaine addiction.
You see, Old Filippe wasn't just good at squandering the national treasury on gold and ceremonial weaponry. He was also a prodigious snorter of nose candy.
A deplorable farce. No wonder everything went to shit.
This is... a lot to process.
Wait, really? There's no way that's true.
Okay. Where is he buried now? (Proceed.)
I would like to sleep on gold. Hustler-style.
The king is the king and he can do *anything*.
Okay, what is nose candy?
Cocaine.
This is slander. The king was just and beautiful. The revolutionaries made this all up.
What happened to the statue?
The original was blown apart by communards, then further damaged during the landing of the Coalition's airships during the Turn-Of-The-Century Revolution. When Martinaise was levelled.
That's such a bad idea.
Who restored the monument?

Some years ago a group of liberal, artistically inclined individuals (designers mostly) thought it would be *ironic* to restore the statue of the most wasteful ruler of Revachol in the poorest part of the city...
The statue is supposed to capture the moment it was blown apart, like *an instant frozen in time*. A rare butterfly, trapped in amber, floating on a sea of... shit.
Most historians think the Coalition's hasty landing may have ultimately *saved* the statue: If the communards had more time they would have reduced it up to even *finer* pieces.
Neither do people in Martinaise. The statue has proved to be *controversial* in a neighbourhood mostly populated by the left-leaning working class.
That's brilliant! So funny and nihilistic.
I *really* don't get art.
Not that he ever did in life, either.
People in Martinaise tend to disagree, as do many prominent art critics and thought leaders with more *nuanced* social awareness than the young ironists.
People in Martinaise tend to agree, as do many prominent art critics and thought leaders with more *nuanced* social awareness than the young ironists.
Filippe III, the Squanderer, however, with his bronze face up in the air, doesn't seem concerned about what the *hoi polloi* think of him in death.
Those critics might have it wrong, though. There's more to it than just 'ironism'... but you can't say what precisely. Perhaps this art mystery will be solved at a later time?
What did he do? You have no idea what *you* did a week ago! How would you know what this guy did many centuries ago?
As you look up, you notice something about the statue. There are some odd indentations on the king's chest piece...
Examine the scaffolding.
A matrix of metal tubes and wooden planks jut out at odd angles. A miserable tarpaulin covers up the horse and rider, flapping in the cold coastal air...
This is *not* what that Personal Brand Strategist of yours promised. No one even knows that you're paying for this re-conceptualization! Go and have a word with him. Find out what's going on.
There's not an *ounce* of artistry here! It's even worse than expected.
The scaffolding around the old monument has been taken down. In its place are the spoils of your investment. Numerous rods and ropes still hold the original reassemblage in place.
Reflect on the re-conceptualization.

dialoguetext: An old monument stands in the middle of the traffic island, pointing toward the sea. It's been covered in posters with radical slogans like 'NO KINGS, NO BOSSES' and 'AGAIN, AND ONCE MORE AFTER THAT!'
At the bottom of the posters, in smaller lettering, are details about meeting at a local coffeehouse.
"Looks like the students took your advice to heart, detective."

An old monument stands in the middle of the traffic island, pointing toward the sea. It looks as if it's been reassembled piece-by-piece, secured and mounted in the air with the aid of numerous ropes and rods.

An old monument stands in the middle of the traffic island, pointing toward the sea. The whole thing is wrapped in vibrantly coloured cables and coiled wire. Where the horse's head should be, only twisted pieces of rebar remain.
An old monument stands in the middle of the traffic island, pointing toward the sea. The horse and rider appear to be struggling against the vibrantly coloured cables and coiled wire.
There are no lights that spell out your name, no workers with calloused hands leering from above -- just construction materials displayed as if to mourn your misplaced dreams.
That son of a bitch scammed you! Probably to *make fun of you*...
The old king looks defiantly to the west, wrapped in makeshift scaffolding like a mummy...
The roundabout is quiet, almost eerily so under the brilliant sunlight. The doom crier in the centre waits to be swallowed by the bright sky, his cardboard omen flapping in the wind like live bait...
The roundabout is quiet, almost eerily so under the brilliant sun. The king of disco is lit up like a stage, anticipating a funky beat that will never come...
The roundabout is quiet, almost eerily so under the brilliant sunlight. The penumbral griever is a silhouette against the bright sky, the flowers lifting him in requiem starting to wilt...

The roundabout is quiet, almost eerily so under the brilliant sunlight. The tickets remain true to their duty -- except for a few that have come unstuck, now assigned to brushing dirt from the asphalt below...

The roundabout is quiet, almost eerily so under the brilliant sunlight. The formless complexion glows at the centre, while the old architecture surrounding it groans in the heat with looming irrelevance...
"Just plug that in there, would you?"
"Got it. Are we ready?"
"It's done. I believe we're ready." The lieutenant wipes his brow.

"Yeah, as ready as we're going to be." He cracks his neck before putting on a pair of headphones. "Grab one of these can sets. I've got it rigged so that we can both listen, but only your cop-talk will broadcast..."
"No idea what we're gonna hear when I turn this thing on, so be prepared for *anything*. Trick is to keep transmitting your request until the Big Bad acknowledges you. You got that?"
"Wait, what if they *never* acknowledge me?"
"Yes."
"Hold on, I need a minute."
"Honestly, that might be for the best. Like I said, the sines coming off this whole project are seriously uncharted..."
"Good. We're live in two... one..."
"No time. We're live in two... one..."
"Don't know how much juice we've got, so we better get to it. You ready?"
A soft rustling. The snow seems to have gotten between your ears somehow...
A soft rustling. Between your ears, a winterscape with fast falling snow...
Where's the sound coming from?
Ignore it.
"That's your cue, lawman."
Every lightswitch, every motor carriage, every doorbell, tea kettle, and radio in Martinaise, all mingled with electrical interference caused by scattered thunderstorms over Ozonne.
"Hey, lawman. We're waiting on you."
"Coalition Warship Archer, this is RCM Officer Firewalker. Please acknowledge."
"Coalition Warship Archer, this is RCM Officer Tequila Sunset. Please acknowledge."
"Coalition Warship Archer, this is Detective Raphaël Ambrosius Costeau of the RCM. Please acknowledge."
"Coalition Warship Archer, this is Lieutenant Harrier du Bois of the RCM. Please acknowledge."
"What should I say?"
"That's up to you. I don't know your *callsign*."
You're all alone out there, wandering a blasted heath, calling out to the night, but there is no reply, except for the buzzing of invisible machines...
I-i-is there anybody th-th-there?
The lieutenant looks up at you with a nervous glance.
"Give it another go."
"Coalition Warship Archer, this is Firewalker. Please acknowledge."
He is nervous for your sake, of course, but also his own.
Looking at him now, with both hands on his headphones, you see very briefly what the lieutenant must have been like when he first joined the RCM...
Nervous for who, though, you cannot say.
Then he turns to you. He gives you a half smile along with an almost imperceptible nod of encouragement.
Then he turns to you. His expression seems to say, 'You'd better not leave this mess for me alone'.
Then he turns to you. He shakes his head slightly and looks back at the amplifier.
Perhaps you're simply imagining it, but it seems as though you're learning to pull apart the fibres of this auditory felt. You focus on one strand in particular, one that sounds very nearly human...
"Nein, Liebling! Das lasse ich nicht zu … Wie kannst du unseren Jungen bloß auf einem dieser *Dinger* nach Vredefort schicken?"
"Nein, Liebling! ... unseren Jungen... nach Vredefort ... einem dieser *Dinger*..."
"Hello... Archer? Do you acknowledge?"

"Marianne ... mir erzählt, dass Oskar nicht mehr ... seit er auf einem Luftschiff aus Graad zurückgekommen ... halten ihn die Psychologen für vollkommen normal ... aber sie hat das Gefühl ... seit seiner Rückkehr ... einem Fremden zusammenzuleben..."

Something about her son going to Vredefort on an aerostatic... to see some psychologists? Or maybe the psychologists are saying it's normal... to have feelings for strangers? Foreign languages were never your strong suit.
You can't make out a word of this gibberish.
A slight frisson at the point where your neck meets your spine. Something about the lieutenant's words, directed at you, but not *you*...
A slight frisson at the point where your neck meets your spine. You can *feel* the lieutenant's presence, even though he's nowhere to be found...
"Kim, don't clog my connection."
"What are you talking about, Kim? It's perfectly nice out."
"It's really coming down, now that you mention it."
"I didn't say anything, detective."
"Mention what?"
"It's cold, like you just said."
"...someone has been maintaining it. The wiring has been repaired..."
An uncomfortable silence falls over the connection.
"... It's been a long winter... Long and cold..."
"Are you going to tell me you didn't say *that*, either?"
"Maybe it's your twin brother?"
"I promise you, I didn't, even though it certainly *sounds* like me..." The lieutenant seems to wince at the sound of his own voice.
"I can assure you, it's not my 'twin brother'. Though it certainly does *sound* like me..." The lieutenant seems to wince at the sound of his own voice.
"It must be entroponetic crosstalk. It's the only explanation."
"What is happening?"
"So your partner's haunting himself. Trying to warn him off his current path, most like."
"Sounds like your partner's being haunted by his past self. Or maybe he's trying to warn himself, from the future, most like. I don't know much about radios."
"It's eerie, for certain, but also harmless. I just wish I could remember what I was talking about..."
"It's just a little bit of pale interference, detective. A little *eerie*, perhaps, but perfectly explicable..."
Outwardly, the lieutenant exudes reassurance, but you can sense a lingering doubt in his voice.
"Kim? How did you get on my connection?"
"Whoa, the cop's *own partner* is a radio-spooker. That's some *other core* business right there..."
"...someone has been maintaining it. The wiring has been repaired..."
"What is he talking about?"
"There's no sense to it. It's just spooker-talk."
"I've encountered this before. It's entroponetic crosstalk. This is a piece of the past mixing in with our signal."
"Does that mean Kim's... *a ghost*?"
"What..."
"It's been a long winter... Long and cold."
"What have you gotten us into, lawman?"
"Natürlich halten ihn die Psychologen für vollkommen normal..."
"It's been a long winter... Long and cold."
"No telling, lawman. You ever confirmed that he's, you know, *flesh and blood*?"
"Yeah, we've gone for an Ace's High before."
"I guess Kim's always had an *ethereal* quality to him."
"I'm going to continue believing that Kim's just hanging out on our connection."
"Sounds like some dark cop rituals. Don't think I want to hear any more..."
"Could be he's your guardian spirit, your cop daemon..."
"Yeah, shut your ears to the truth. That's the safest way forward..."
"Roy said this transceiver came with some kind of *signal purifier*. Maybe we should turn that on?"
"Maybe we should try again later?"
"So what can we do about it?"
"Is that what this switch does? I'll flip it now."
"No can do. This is it. The only way forward is the hard core way, straight through. Now give it another go."
"You just have to embrace the spookiness. Now give it another go."
"... someone has been maintaining it..." The lieutenant's voice suddenly grows faint and distant, as though he were speaking from a passing motor carriage...
"Sounds like the de-spooker worked. Lucky break. Now give it another go."
(Sigh.) "Coalition Warship Archer. Do you acknowledge? This is Firewalker."
"But someone has been maintaining it. The wiring has been repaired..."
"Coalition Warship Archer. Do you acknowledge? This is Firewalker."
"... Warship Archer. Are you there, Firewalker? Please acknowledge."
"... Walker? Please acknowledge."
"Archer! This is Firewalker. Can you hear me?"
"Archer! This is Firewalker. Can you hear me?"
"Liebling, bitte… Er ist unser einziges Kind..."
"... Warship Archer. Please identify."
The signals are getting increasingly mixed. Plucking Archer's signal from this will be like isolating a single strand from a tangle of hair...
"This isn't looking good."  The speedfreak removes his sweat-drenched headphones. "The radio-spookers are winning."
"Bad news." The speedfreak removes his sweat-drenched headphones. "Even with the de-spooker flipped, the signal is still too weak to get down with..."
"What can we do?"
"Okay, let's do this." (Climb the monument.)
sequence: SemiBlack(true,0.3); BanishInterface(true)@2.5; FocusCamera(MonumentClimbCam)@2; TravelTo(Tequila Sunset, MonumentClimbMarker, 2, false)@2; SemiBlack(false,1)@3; PlayAnimation(Tequila Sunset, monument_climb)@3->Message(inPosition); FocusCamera(MonumentClimbCam2)@4; BanishInterface(false)@Message(inPosition);

dialoguetext: "Don't know. If we can't get around the interference, we're in deep trouble. Hold on, I think Egg gave me some kind of checklist..."
"Hmmm. Says here, 'MAIN STEP: VOLUME TO THE MAX'... That's not too helpful. Okay, it also says: 'INSPECT CONNECTIONS FOR HARD CORE CLARITY,' so let's try that..."
You don't exactly cut a lithesome figure, but after several moments of scrambling you manage to hoist yourself atop the monument.
sequence: Hold(); BanishInterface(true); PlayAnimation(Tequila Sunset, monument_climb_cont)->Message(inPosition2); BanishInterface(false)@Message(inPosition2); Release()@Message(inPosition2); FocusCamera(MonumentClimbCam3);

dialoguetext: Your gloves give you a solid grip on the metal bar. This feels pleasingly familiar...
The metal bar is cold and slick with precipitation. For a moment it feels as though you're about to slip, but you concentrate all your attention on your pectoral muscles and squeeze...
The cold metal chills your bare hands. Some part of your brain tells you something is missing...
Keep it together, champ! You've got this...
Chalk powder. Absorbs moisture and keeps your grip firm.
... and before you know it, you're safely perched atop the monument.

dialoguetext: ... but before you can decide what, you find yourself safely perched atop the monument.

dialoguetext: "Did you *see* that bar work?"
"That was pretty bad. I hope nobody saw it."
Examine the connections.
"This cop's got serious crab-like properties. Must be some kind of *law-crab*."
The connection itself is nothing more than a little braid of exposed wire wrapped about the hoof of the horse, a copper fetter it cannot slip...
The whole monument is covered in a thin but durable layer of oil and grime. It's obvious no one has cleaned it in years.
"What good is that supposed to do?"
"What are we supposed to use to bend the antenna?"
"Hmmm. Good question. Maybe he's saying we're casting too wide a net, got to *narrow our receiving band*, so we pick up the Big Bad without the spookers."
"It says here 'MUSCLE-STYLE'."
"Since you're already up there, I say you should do it."
The speedfreak is right. The responsibility is yours and yours alone. There's no turning back now.
Look at the horse.
Attempt to narrow the receiving mode manually.
This faithful steed is in nearly as poor a condition as its rider.
Your grip is firm, yet controlled. The swelling in your headset guides your hands as much as your hands guide the bronze horse head. It's almost like you're hearing *through* the horse itself...

dialoguetext: You allow the broken hunk of metal to clatter to the ground. It wasn't clear to you it did anything anyway...

dialoguetext: "Looks like it's working. Keep going, just a bit more..."
"... Nein, Liebling!"
The signal is clear, the storm has passed. This is another voice, a live voice, on the other end of this invisible bridge you've established...
"Try it now."
"Coalition Warship Archer. This is RCM Officer Firewalker. Please acknowledge."
"Firewalker, this is Coalition Warship Archer. We are acknowledging and accepting you."
"There it is, the Big Bad. Now be quick. I'll keep us aligned as long as I can."
"Please be advised that you are speaking on the public frequency. What is your request?"
This is it... you're finally getting to speak with those who hold *real* power.
And by that, we mean the ones with the guns and the warships.
There is so much you wish you could ask. Your efforts have bought you some time, but you can't forget what you're *really* here for...
There is so much you wish you could ask, but you probably only have time for one or two questions before the signal is lost...
"Nein, Liebling!"
"Huh. Sounds like that was a false move. Signal's even worse now."
"Probably because you broke it."
"The thing is, trying's not enough. Now it's the results that count."
"Look, I'm not a blame-layer. I'm just saying, things were bad, and now they're worse."
"I'm going to turn all the dials to maximum. Probably gonna burn out our power supply, but that might be the only way..."
"That piece of junk didn't even work!"
"I'm sorry! I was trying to do good."
"It's not *my* fault the statue broke."
A maelstrom of sound, swirling and swirling around an invisible point. It's mounting, mounting...
It's too much! Your ear drums are throbbing, about to burst!
... and then, nothing.
"Try it now."
"... nicht mehr derselbe ist, seit er auf einem Luftschiff aus Graad zurückgekommen ist..."
"... Firewalker? Please respond..."
"Archer! Is that you?"
"... a long winter... Long and cold..."
"This is... Warship Archer. We are acknowledging and accepting you... though we're still getting quite a bit of interference..."
"This is as good as it's going to get. I'll keep us aligned as long as I can, but this isn't a *social mission*, you got it?"
"Who am I speaking with?"
"What does Revachol look like from up there?"
"What does the Moralintern *really* want?"
"When is real democracy coming to Revachol?"
"Hang on, Archer, I meant to ask you about the Committee of Responsibility."
"Sorry, I messed up and we ran out of time."
"Firewalker... please repeat... your signal is *very* weak..."
"I said there's no time. And now you're going to leave too..."
"Er kann doch auch nächstes Jahr zur Akademie gehen..."
"... nothing important, bad connection... Going to update the receiving frequency..."
"You are currently speaking with Coalition Warship Archer, flagship of INSURCOM forces in Revachol."
"Are you the captain?"
"Sure, but who are *you*? I need to know your name."
"No, the captain of the Archer is deeply classified intelligence. We are the second signaller."
"Our name is not important. All you need to know is that we hold the position of second signaller aboard the Archer."
Wait-wait, she's an *El-something*, you just know it.
You really don't have the faintest guess what her name could be. You were never very good at this sort of thing...
There's something in the way she refers to herself, always with the first-person plural. A deliberate blurring of the boundary between herself and the institution she represents...
Not to mention the airborne artillery platform she works on. Her every word is backed up by the most powerful ordnance available...
"Just one thing, why do you keep referring to yourself with the plural?"
"I bet I can guess your name."
"What's it like, being a second signaller?"
"Because it's standard practice for signallers to use the *pluralis officialis* during the course of our duties. It's meant to serve as a reminder that we don't speak only for ourselves."

"For instance, as second signaller we represent Coalition Warship Archer, which in turn represents INSURCOM and the Coalition more generally, which in turn represents the Moralist International, which itself represents the interests of 1.2 billion people across the world."
Meaning she's the voice of all those living souls!
"So when I'm talking to you, it's like I'm talking to *all of humanity*?"
"That sounds like an awesome responsibility."
"Sounds like kind of a hard job."

"No, of course not. There are many nations outside the Moralintern's umbrella, in Seol, Samara, and elsewhere. At most you might say the Moralintern represents between a quarter and a third of humanity."

"Perhaps you could say that we represent the interests and hopes of a great many people, but you could say just as easily that we are the assistant to the secretary of a factotum, no more remarkable than the lowest cashier of a common Frittte..."
"It all depends on your perspective."
"Who is the secretary?"
"Who is the factotum?"
"The Moralintern is *nothing* like a Frittte -- you don't even sell the fun stuff!"
"The chief signaller, our superior. They are ultimately responsible for all communications aboard the Archer..."
"Why, the Archer itself..."
"If by 'fun stuff,' you mean alcohol and cigarettes, that's true. Actually, we don't even have Fritttes where we're from. In Messina they're called Averros..."
"But now we've wandered quite far afield. What was your request?"
Averro, SRL, is a chain of high-end pharmacies found only in Vesper and Messina. They are *much* nicer than your average Frittte.
"It's an important responsibility, but we don't consider it any greater than those borne by countless people all across the world..."
"It may be a *demanding* job, but the Coalition is committed to ensuring those in its service maintain a healthy work-life balance..."
"Now... your request?"
"Really, it's not important. We would strongly prefer that you state your request."
"You sound like an Eloïse to me."
"You're an Elena, aren't you?"
"You're an Eleanora, I'm sure of it."
"You're 100% an Eliška."
She laughs. "Do we sound like we're from Sur-la-Clef to you?"
A moment of stunned silence. "How did you know that?"
"We don't believe there is anyone younger than 70 named Eleanora..."
"You are 100% wrong..."
"Just a lucky guess."
"It was obvious. No other name would fit you."
"Now, please dispense with the games, Firewalker. This is a public frequency..."
"I... We don't appreciate whatever game you're playing, Firewalker. Now, what is your request?"
Did you catch that? A crack in her otherwise solid edifice.
Is it possible to *hear* someone blush? Because you're sure that's what she's doing...
"It's a great honour and responsibility. In addition to monitoring public frequencies, we are tasked with maintaining some of the most sensitive communications equipment aboard the Archer."
"How's the work-life balance?"
"How are the benefits?"
"Do you believe in the mission?"
"Quite good. We enjoy all the standard benefits for Moralintern forces on active duty assignments: Excellent healthcare, foreign service pay, a fully funded pension system..."
"Oh, it's fine..."
"Yes, of course. There is no higher calling than serving humanity."
"... six-weeks paid leave, bilingual childcare, vocational certification credits. Really, it's quite a good career."
Hold on, you can tell she has more to say...
"Me, I'm a workaholic. It's just what I do..."
"That's good, I wish the RCM gave me more time off..."
(Wait for her to continue.)
A scoff from the lieutenant's channel.
"Then you would like being on an aerostatic, there's always *something* that must be done..."
"Oh, yes, we could always use more time off." She laughs politely, but doesn't elaborate.
"... of course, serving on a Coalition warship does require some *personal* sacrifices, but we have to be willing to make them, if we believe in the mission..."
"What kind of sacrifices?"
"As long as you believe in the mission, it's all worth it."
"Nothing remarkable. Really, we have been very fortunate. But we do sometimes wonder what we might be missing out on, back in Messina..."
"Yes, of course. There is no higher calling than serving humanity."
"But now we have gotten quite far afield. What was your request?"
"Hmmm, that's difficult to say. We have a very particular view from our observation platform up here."
"Particular how?"
"What can you see?"
"Perhaps the best way to describe it is to say we have a *very wide perspective*, but not an especially detailed one."
"Oh, it looks quite lovely from here. From our porthole, we see rolling hillsides, a public park filled with grand oak trees, men and women going about on horses..."
Le Jardin, Stella Maris, Saint-Batiste. She is looking down on the suburbs of Revachol East.
"You're above Revachol East then."
"Where are you, exactly?"
(Look around.) "Huh, I don't see *any* of that stuff."
"Ah, that must be. We have only recently been detailed to the Archer, so we are still learning the names of all the many districts..."
"We cannot say for certain. East, it must be? We have only recently been detailed to the Archer, so we are still learning the names of all the many districts..."
"Perhaps you are in a different part of the city? We have only recently been detailed to the Archer, so we are still learning the names of all the many districts..."
She needs to see *you*, down here. That's the only way she'll really *get* what you're about.
"Can you see Martinaise from where you are?"
"Martinaise, Martinaise... That is to the west, yes?"
"Yes. Look across the River Esperance."
"Uh, sure. Let's go with west."
"I thought it was to the south?"
"Nope, it's to the north. Definitely north."
"Stand by a moment... we are adjusting our viewfinder..."
"Hold on. We're adjusting our viewfinder..."
"To the south. Let us see..."
"But to the north is all water..."
"Yes, we are looking at the river now. There are small islands in the middle of it. It's very nice, actually..."
"Ah, we are looking at a great river now. This must be the Esperance. It's very nice, actually..."
"No, that cannot be right. That way is only sprawl. We were under the impression that Martinaise was nearer to the Bay..."
"That's right. Martinaise is a highly experimental *sub-aquatic* district."
"You're right. I just got turned around. It's probably to the south."
"Hmmm. Maybe it *is* to the west, then?"
"Interesting. The west of the city looks *very* different from the east. There's a large motorway dividing it nearly in half. This must be the 8/81, no?"
"Ah, we see. You are playing a practical joke. Very funny..."
If it's so funny, why isn't she laughing?
"Enough jokes, then. What was your request?"
"A *motorway*? I have no idea what you're talking about."
"Maybe follow the motorway as far as it goes?"
"Exactly. Follow that west for a few kilometres, until you see the lake."
"Very well. Now we are looking at an area that seems to be in urgent need of *revitalisation*..."
"It appears to go on for quite a while. There's a heavily industrialised district that seems to abut Monte-Martin..."
"Really? It seems quite important. It may be the largest road in the city..."
"But now we seem to be quite turned about. We'll have to consult a map in the future. Now, was there something else?"

dialoguetext: "I am the Foreteller of Ruin, and I’ve come to tell you that the end is very, very nigh."
"The thing is, I can't remember *anything*."
"We're not sure we heard that clearly. Are you suggesting that you may be responsible for the very murder you're investigating?"
"Yeah, I did it. And I need you to stop me before I do it again."
"I'm not *sure* it was me, it's more like a working hypothesis."
"For the last time, detective. You. Did. Not. Commit. The. Murder. Archer, please disregard his nonsense."
"Detective, what in god's name are you saying? Archer, please disregard that..."
"No use. The Big Bad can't hear us, just the main cop."
"I don't understand. I thought he was making progress..."
"This absolute lunatic! But why am I surprised?"
"Firewalker, surely you are aware that it is a civil offence to maliciously or frivolously obstruct a Coalition radio frequency..."
"Please confirm. Are you saying your partner is somehow *impeding* your investigation?"
"Nah, he's a solid investigator. In fact, we get along great apart from the ass-riding."
"Totally. I would've solved this thing *days* ago if it weren't for the ass-riding."
"Just... all day, every day... I turn my head and there he is, on my ass, riding like there's no tomorrow."
"Are you completely out of your mind, detective? Archer, please give us a moment!"
"No use. The Big Bad can't hear us, just the main cop."
"I don't understand. I thought he was making progress..."
"This absolute lunatic! But why am I surprised?"
"Now, please excuse us while we update the receiving frequency. This connection will be cleared in four... three..."
"We're not sure we understand. To what 'end' are you referring?"
"The final seal has been broken, and the blood-dimmed tide is rising."
"I'm saying you and me and everyone we know is going to die, probably very soon."
"Technically, according to some cultures, it's less of an 'end' and more like a change in states of matter."
"Enough with the apocalyptic drivel! Archer, please disregard, he's not in his right mind."
"No use. The Big Bad can't hear us, just the main cop."
"This absolute lunatic! But why am I surprised?"
"I don't understand. I thought he was making progress..."
"So you're experiencing acute memory loss. We don't see how this is the Committee's business."
"Good god, here we go..."
"I’m pretty sure it has to do with the prodigious quantities of drugs and alcohol I consumed."
"I’m pretty sure it all goes back to an *ex-something*."
"We're afraid we don't understand. Are you requesting medical attention?"
"Yes, I think I might be."
"No, we're *way* past that."
"I already talked to my station lazareth and he wasn't helpful *at all*."
"Then we are not sure what assistance can be rendered. This is quite beyond the purview of the Committee of Responsibility..."
"Then we recommend you speak with your station lazareth. This has nothing to do with the Committee of Responsibility..."
"We're afraid we don't understand at all. What does this 'something' have to do with your lost memory?"
"If I knew that, I wouldn't *be* in this situation!"
"I'd really prefer to speak with the Committee directly."
"We are sorry to hear of your loss, but personal tragedy is quite beyond the purview of the Committee of Responsibility..."
"Unfortunately we cannot accept your request. We really have no idea what you are talking about, but we're quite sure it is beyond the purview of the Committee of Responsibility..."
She can't treat you that way! Let her know what you *really think* of her!
Quick, hang up on her first!
"Go ahead and leave, you stupid whore!"

dialoguetext: ... and the line goes quiet.
She must have cleared the connection a few seconds early...
You didn't have to do that, you know. There were *other* options...
The lieutenant slowly removes his headset and turns to you.
"Women, am I right?"
Say nothing.
"Kim, why did I call that woman a whore, just now?"
"You really don't know?"
"Maybe I *do* know, it's just... hard to talk about."
"Probably I just misspoke. I meant to say something else."
"Nope, not a clue."
"Really? I don't think this is the *first* time you've *misspoken* in that way."
"I suppose that's possible..."
"Yes, I imagine it must be."
... but that's no excuse to unload on a bystander, he allows to remain unsaid...
He means that it's becoming an unfortunate *fixture* in your vocabulary...
... but not likely, he does not feel compelled to add.
"Hmmm. Well, in that case..."
"No, you ridiculous fool. You're *not* right. You're not even remotely right."
"It's as though *right* is over here..." He holds up one hand. "... while *you're* over here..." He holds up his other hand, as far apart from the first as possible.
The last time you saw the lieutenant this upset was after that *thing you said in the church*...
Uh oh, you've never seen the lieutenant this wound up before...
"In fact, if right were a country, you would be deported immediately. You would be *persona non grata* in the Country of Right."
"Okay, Kim, I got it."
Let him keep going.
"Really? Because I'm not entirely sure that you *do*, detective."
"What I'm trying to say, is that in your own twisted way, you're *almost a genius*, a genius who's dedicated his entire malignant existence to devising new and spectacular ways to be *wrong*."
The lieutenant takes a deep breath, appearing to gather even more energy and rage, but when he opens his mouth to continue his fulmination, he just sighs...
"Do you know what the worst part is, detective? The more time I spend with you, the more I feel myself *becoming* like you..."
"Sorry, detective. That wasn't entirely justified. You're not *all* bad. It's just that sometimes, you, well..."
"I apologise, detective. I let my emotions get the better of me just now. You can be a fine police officer, but sometimes you, well..."
"Now, get down from there. We've got work to do."
There's nothing to add, he thinks. The situation speaks for itself.
Are there more terrible words to hear from your half-brother?
"No, no, no -- please don't go..."
Say nothing.
"Two... one... 'Après le monde, le gris'..."
"'Après le gris, le monde encore'..."
Disconnect before she clears the line.
... and the line goes quiet.
There, you really showed her.
Showed her *what*, though?
The lieutenant gives a long sigh as he removes his headphones. He looks up at you.
"I think it's best for you to climb off the statue now, detective. Your real work is down here."
"Took a dark turn there. Told you we shouldn't have gone and aligned ourselves with the Big Bad. Gonna need some seriously hard core ablutions to wash this shit off..."
"Now, come down here and give me a hand with this gear, would you?"
"Just give me a minute."
"I'm coming." (Climb down.)
There's a damp cold running up the insides of your thighs. Your legs have grown stiff. You've been up here quite a while.
The sun-warmed bronze tingles beneath your fingertips and between your thighs. Your legs have grown stiff. You've been up here quite a while.
There's a damp cold running up the insides of your thighs. Your legs have grown stiff. You've been up here quite a while.
The cold bronze tickles your inner thighs. Your legs have grown stiff. You've been up here quite a while.
You look around. The strike breakers are still shouting their slogans and waving their hand-painted signs. Beneath you, the speedfreak has begun disconnecting a few cables...
You look around. Most everyone has already gone home for the night. It's really just you and the speedfreak left...
You could stay a while longer, if you wanted.
Wait a little longer.
Climb down.
There's really no point. You're beginning to feel like the little child who refuses to come down off the carousel.
Climb down.
Out on the bay, a pair of dinghies bob and roll in the waves. The breeze drags the voices of the fisherman toward the plaza, faint and indecipherable.
Further out, a few dirty icebergs drift to and fro. Further still, at the outer edge of your recognizance, the ancient ruins of the seafort lay piled on the horison...
"Everything alright, detective?"
"I'm fine."
"I don't know. Maybe."
"I'm not kidding, detective. It's time to come down."
"Come on. My leg's starting to twitch. Means we've been here too long..."
The lieutenant is right. There's really nothing more for you up here.
He's right. There's really nothing more for you up here.
Climb down.
"Listen, I understand that you're disappointed that things did not turn out how you might have hoped..."
"But you made the *right* decision, the more difficult decision, in my mind, at least."
"But you *did* accomplish your task. You reached the Coalition. I must admit, I didn't seriously think you could do it, but you've proved me wrong."
"But that's just how things go. We all must accept our own shortcomings and limitations."
"I'm still not sure."
"Yeah, you're right."
"How do you know?"
"Because I can see you're still agonising over it. In my experience, when you make the wrong decision, you can tell right away. It's the right decisions that won't leave you alone..."

"Yes, I know..." The lieutenant allows himself a sheepish half-smile. "In my experience, when you make the wrong decision, you can tell right away. It's the right decisions that won't leave you alone..."
"You may feel that way for some time yet. In my experience, when you make the wrong decision, you can tell right away. It's the right decisions that won't leave you alone..."
Perhaps someday the lieutenant will tell you about some of the decisions that won't leave him alone, but it won't be this day.
"Now, come on. It's getting late."
"Now, come on. We still have a long day ahead of us."
Climb down.
"About time. You grab that amp. Forget the cables. Need to leave some evidence of our antenna to inspire future generations..."
The lieutenant sighs. "What's *one more trip* across the waterlock?"
