dialoguetext: "Coalition Warship Archer. This is RCM Officer Firewalker. Please acknowledge."
This faithful steed cuts a dashing figure with the replica sabre between its teeth.
That performance was, frankly, an embarrassment.
"What is this 'balance of terror theory'?"

"It's an elegant idea, one of the cornerstones of the modern era. In short, it holds that durable, lasting peace is possible when the major powers are capable of inflicting unacceptable and irreversible destruction upon one another..."
"Because no rational state is willing to accept the risk of such a calamity befalling its own people, all powers are incentivised to *de-escalate* conflicts before they reach the point of no return."
"But what if states *aren't* rational?"
"And has it worked?"
"A state is like any other living thing -- it wants to survive and grow. A state that doesn't value its own existence is not a state at all."
"Yes, I've also discovered an entroponetic phenomenon here in Martinaise."
"I said, 'I've discovered an entroponetic phenomenon here in Martinaise'."
"Yes."
"Good. First question: Are you currently in the vicinity of Sereglee, the North Arcade Islands, or Near Pale Offshore Platform 'Insulindico'?"
"I've never heard of any of those places."
"You already know exactly where I am."
"No, I'm in Martinaise."
"Please answer the question."
"Very good. Next question: Would you describe the phenomenon as *internal* to the isola, or *external* to the isola?"
"Internal."
"External."
"I have no idea what you're asking."
"Answer the question, please."
"Next question: At the time, did you experience *sense objects*?"
"Uh... can you elaborate?"
"Yes. Examples may include sound, memory, light."
"I can only describe it in terms of curdling milk."
"When the raver put the compressor through the other thing, it made the beat really hard core. Like, *too* hard core."
"I experienced nothing. A complete lack of phenomena."
"Final question: Were you alone?"
"Mhmm. Let's go on..."
You hear the sound of a page ripping.
Her tone has shifted. She's no longer herself.
She's reading from a script. Your words have activated some sort of *procedure*.
"Wait, what's going on?"
"Never mind that. All you need to do is repeat what you just said..."
Do as she says. There's no other option.
Yes. Unquestionably, *irrevocably* alone...
That reminds you, where has your half-brother gone?
"Yes."
"No."
There's no need to overthink this.
How could you be alone? You're a *star*, man. You've got an *entourage* and adoring fans wherever you go...
You are the Doom-Speaker. It is your lot to ply these somnolent roads, declaring your lonely truth...
You don't need anybody else. You're the *lawbringer*...
Your head is so full of colourful thoughts, you never *feel* alone...
You are part of a large family. You are never alone...
Of course not. The radio-programmer was there...
How could you expect anyone to stay around with all your *standard-issue* thoughts and opinions?
"Acknowledged. Listen very carefully, Firewalker. We are going to ask you a series of questions. It is imperative that you answer as directly and truthfully as you can. Do you understand?"
"... We're afraid we must ask you to repeat that, Firewalker."
A-a-afraid? What is she afraid of?
"Thank you, Firewalker. Please stand by while we transmit our summary..."
"I don't know where this case will lead us, detective, but in a sense that doesn't matter. Our job is to follow the evidence where it leads, consequences be damned..."
"Because the thing you're running from is *inside you*, detective!"
"But I embrace it *because* it's my role, and it's yours too, detective, whether you accept it or not!"
"Oh, it looks quite lovely from here, even with the rain. From our porthole, we see rolling hillsides, a public park filled with grand oak trees, men and women going about on horses..."
"Oh, it looks quite lovely from here. From our porthole, we see rolling hillsides covered with snow, a public park filled with grand oak trees, men and women going about on horses..."
What she means is... actually... you have no idea what those words could mean in this context...
"It was a kind of gradient."
Her wishes are sincere. You can take heart from that, at least.

"We're sorry we did not come bearing better news. But we must say that it has been... *a privilege* to speak with you. We believe you are a credit to the RCM, and we wish you good fortune and safety during the course of your work."
No, you *know* this tone of voice. You've heard it before. She's about to deliver some bad news...
"I'm here, Archer! What's the news?"
"Why do I feel like you're about to tell me something I don't want to hear?"
"Firewalker, surely you are aware that it is a civil offence to maliciously or frivolously obstruct a Coalition radio frequency..."
"Firewalker, surely you are aware that it is a civil offence to maliciously or frivolously obstruct a Coalition radio frequency..."
"Kim! Answer me."
"No use, man. Don't think he can hear you."
"I've got a feeling this is related to the pale, some piece of the past that's mixing in with our signal."
Just *run*. Unplug that headset and get as far away as you can.
"Whoa, the Coalition has *talking* warships?"
"Of course not. It's simply a rhetorical convention, a common synecdoche. We are the second signaller."
"We can assure you, it is coming as soon as possible."
"In a few months, then?"
"That's certainly possible. Though of course it depends on the contingencies."
"What do you mean 'contingencies'?"

"You must understand, the Moralintern is responsible for ensuring the continuance and flourishing of mankind for the next 3,000 years. The planning division must account for a great many possible outcomes and chance events."
"Fortunately, we have contingency spreads to help guide our decision making."

Originally developed by mechanical engineers at the Isherwood Branch of CZU Industries around the turn of the last century, contingency spreads are used to model complex events in a number of fields, including business, public health, radiocomputer science, insurance, and international diplomacy.
"Of course, there is no one spread that can reasonably account for all these possible events. But at least we're able to prepare for the most likely eventualities."
"Wait, how do these contingency spreads actually *work*?"
A sigh. "You are thinking about this metaphor too literally..."
"It's not really our area of expertise, but we can try to explain. Picture a smooth hill made from fresh dirt. Now, if you stand atop this hill and pour a glass of water over it, what will happen?"
"The dirt will get wet?"
"I won't have any water?"
"The water will run down the hill?"

"Precisamente. We know only that it will run down, but not what course it will take. If we place a rock in the water's path, will it divert to the left or the right? We cannot say, but we may predict which way it might run in either event..."

"The point is that we know only that the water will run down, but not what course it will take. If we place a rock in the water's path, will it divert to the left or the right? We cannot say, but we may predict which way it might run in either event..."
"That is the essence of the idea. You might also imagine these spreads as a kind of tree, with every juncture representing a different event, and every branch representing a different timeline."
"You're saying the Moralintern uses contingency spreads to see the future?"
"Not exactly. No one can know the future. But with contingency spreads it is possible to predict what the future realities *might reasonably* look like."
"But we shouldn't overstate their importance. They are simply one of many tools used by the Moralintern to set policy."
"Hold on, does that mean some realities are *less reasonable* than others?"
Meaning there are more and less reasonable futures. You should follow up on that.

"Well, yes -- just as some events are less probable than others. While we expect the vast majority of realities will fall within a normal confidence interval, there must necessarily be some that fall *outside that range* as well."
"This is... a lot to take in."
"Would you say the reality we're living in is more or less reasonable than others?"
"Who are we to say? We're only a second signaller, not a metaphysician. This is the only reality we have ever known, so how can we judge how reasonable it might be compared to any other?"
"So where does Revachol fit into these contingencies?" (Proceed.)
"That's impossible to say. It may be that Revachol has a great role to play, or no role at all. That is the nature of contingencies."

"You must understand, when we speak of contingency spreads, we are talking about *the most fantastically complex* data visualisations human beings are capable of producing, with thousands of events -- from elections and wars to natural disasters or scientific miracles -- and millions of possible outcomes."
"Why does thinking about these contingencies make me feel so *bad*?"
*Hyyyngh!* It makes your brain swell just to think about...
"It's completely natural. Studies have shown that the untrained mind is only capable of considering so many possibilities in place at once, usually no more than three or four..."
But... didn't the Wild Pines representative say that Revachol would *resolve* history?
"Almost certainly. Not many realise this, but, the Moralintern is constantly reviewing and revising its contingency spreads in order to improve our own decision-making..."

"It may be the case that, under certain scenarios, Revachol is vitally important, as it was during the Coalition landings in '08. It may also be the case in many other equally plausible scenarios that Revachol is simply another once-great city, like countless others throughout history."
"Only in the sense that the entire world has to 'wing' its way through history. The Moralintern simply aims to 'wing it' as little as possible..."
Did she... just admit that the Coalition invading Revachol was one of those 'contingencies'?
"Yes, we would say that is a fair and reasonable way to describe it..."
(Look around.) "Yeah, this is definitely a place whose time has passed."

"Perhaps, perhaps not. Could the Perikarnassians have foreseen the role Revachol would play in events to come? In truth, history only appears to rhyme because we cannot perceive events in their full complexity..."
"Are you saying the Coalition invasion was one of these 'contingencies'?"
"But one must consider that the world was in the midst of a global catastrophe brought on by an unstoppable pandemic. No amount of contingency planning could account for *all of that*."
"So you're saying the Moralintern just had to wing it?"
"History loves to rhyme. I'll bet Revachol has its day again."
"I still feel like there had to have been a better way."
"So you're saying the Moralintern had to make difficult decisions during an unprecedented situation."
"Impossible to say for certain. Human beings are notoriously bad at predicting all the different ways events might unravel..."
"For this reason, responsibility for developing contingency spreads is only assigned to highly trained analysts working with advanced radiocomputers and a steady supply of drouamine."
"Okay, but I *still* want to know when real democracy is coming."

"Of course. While the content of individual contingency spreads is deeply classified, many degrees beyond our access, everything we have heard from the Provisional Commission indicates that the transition is proceeding according to the appropriate timetable."
"What's this 'transitional advisory council'?"
"Who picks the slates of candidates?"
"Does that mean democracy is *here*?" (Look around.)
"But what if some people want democracy to come *faster*?"

"That is extremely admirable. Of course, the Coalition supports the Revacholian people's desire for full democracy. We encourage you to contact the offices of the Provisional Commission if you are serious about getting involved."
"The first phase of democratisation."
"Well, not yet. Right now it's more like a simple seed, buried out of sight..."
"What are you talking about?"
"I met a gardener earlier, but then she turned out to be a lawyer. Is she involved somehow?"

"Oh, there are many things you can do. If you're interested in learning how to canvass for signatures, manage a polling place, or register voters, the Commission would be more than happy to direct you to a workshop..."

"Real democracy doesn't just happen. It requires the support of a great number of stable, interlocking institutions. *That* is the only way to channel popular sentiment into a legitimate mandate to govern. Otherwise, what are we left with?"
"Esattamente. But the Commission's hard and diligent work may soon be bearing fruit: Revachol is nearly ready to begin the first phase of democratisation."
"Well, that isn't very realistic, is it?"
"An institutional crisis?"
"How can I get involved?"
"But what if I want real democracy, like, *right* now?"
"How many of these 'phases' are there until we have real democracy?" (Conclude.)
"Gardeners and lawyers are both essential to a beautiful and well-functioning society, but we're referring to something else..."
"Mob rule?"
"In most cases, the Provisional Council selects them from a cross-section of the local population to ensure the slates actually reflect the people they represent."

"The council is modelled after similar bodies developed in a number of transitional democracies. Its role is to devise and shape the future institutions of Revacholian democracy, according to local conditions..."
"Soon, the people of Revachol will vote for slates of candidates who will make up the transitional advisory council that will oversee the second phase of democratisation."
"Our best theoreticians believe that three to five phases are appropriate for states that lack strong democratic traditions, which would certainly apply to Revachol."
"In fact, you may have picked the perfect time to get involved: Revachol is nearly ready to begin the first phase of democratisation."
"Within a couple of years, surely."
"That's... rather optimistic. Though of course it depends on the contingencies."
"Within my lifetime?"
"Oh, most likely. Though of course it depends on the contingencies."
All major cities in EPIS-aligned nations, you can't help but notice.
"It's even possible the cities that will resolve the questions of the future have not been founded yet."
"Enough of this. I have another question."
"Acknowledged. We are at your disposal."
"Once elected, council members will even have the opportunity to join one of several officially sanctioned political wings, depending on their ideological beliefs and policy preferences."
"A very important question. The wings are carefully selected to represent a wide spectrum of political thought."
"What do these 'wings' represent?"
"Of course, such a situation is not ideal. We would all prefer for Revacholians to nominate their representatives directly. But that is why it's a transitional council."
"How do I access my *personal contingency spread*?"
"Even though we are only a second signaller, we can tell you with great certainty that there is no contingency spread for you, Firewalker."
"You must be mistaken. I'm kind of a star around here."
"Is it because I'm a miserable failure?"
"That's impossible. I am the doomsinger, the herald of desolation."

"What you are describing is the attitude of a child. The Moralintern is not 'humanity's stepmother', despite what some critics may allege. Responsibility and freedom are deeply entwined, and both are essential in a flourishing society."
"We're sorry, we're not familiar with all the local offices in Martinaise..."
"It is a work-in-progress, but it is also the best way that humanity has found thus far."
"Our concerns exist on the scale of decades, centuries, and millennia. Sometimes we say the Moralintern worries about the future so that normal people may worry about today."
"Perhaps you are confused as to the scale on which the contingency spreads function..."
"Please understand, we are not some totalitarian enterprise. We are committed to and bound by the highest values of individual freedom and opportunity."
"Of course not. The Moralintern is committed to giving every person the opportunity to flourish..."
"That sounds like a moderate and reasonable way to organise a society."
"But what if I *want* someone else to make all my decisions for me?"
"Are you sure? I bet it's locked away in a vault somewhere..."
"The Moralintern is not Seol. There is no secret vault of files beneath Isherwood or La Cherte or anywhere else, because that is not the Moralintern's purpose..."
S-s-s-she knows perfectly well where they are! They've got one for everybody, all coded and filed away in a vast labyrinth beneath Isherwood...
"Someone told me we live in a precarious world, that every event is just a violent roll of the die."
"Of course. We're only a second signaller, not a metaphysician. We sometimes find it overwhelming also..."
"It may be. We're only a second signaller, not a metaphysician. It's a rather cold way to think about the world, isn't it?"
"The key, we believe, is to be open to meaning even amidst great uncertainty. But now we are only speaking for ourselves."
"So you're saying we *are* living in an unreasonable reality!"
"We are living in the only reality we know. Our task is to make the best of it that we can..."
'Local conditions' in this case referring to incompetence, graft, and violence.

"Typically, there's a liberal technocratic wing, a social democratic wing, and even a conservative populist wing. You wouldn't believe some of the ideas they express! But a vibrant and free political culture requires that all perspectives be given voice, even those many may find objectionable."
"What do you mean?'
"Simply that there is no such thing as an individual contingency spread..."
"I'm not sure how much longer I can keep the signal clear, officer."
"You have to, Soona. Just a little longer..."
"Officer, I'm afraid the connection is beginning to collapse..."
"So... they're really coming..."
The programmer eyes you curiously. She does not understand why you're hesitating.
"I'm still not certain whether this was a *good* idea or not, but there is something extraordinary about summoning an aerostatic with your voice..."
"It's here."
"Archer can't hear us, I'm afraid. Only his microphone is connected to the transceiver."
"They can't hear us, I'm afraid. Only his microphone is connected to the transceiver."
"They can't hear us, I'm afraid. Only his microphone is connected to the transceiver."
"Officer, we have a long walk back to the church. It's time to come down."
"Hmm, what a disappointment. I was almost sure something *truly* interesting was about to happen. Oh well."
"You can come down now, officer. I'm going to begin packing my things up."
"Good. Now, give me a hand with these amplifiers. Leave the cables. I don't feel like making two trips..."

dialoguetext: "In what sense is the Moralintern the steward of Dolores Dei's legacy?"

"It was established by many of the same Founding Party members who elected Dolores Dei, and who, after her assassination, dedicated their lives to the continuation of her political and intellectual project."

The *other* members of the Founding Party moved to Sur-la-Clef and invented modern corporate finance. Their names may still be found on the pediments of some of the largest investment banks in the world.

"There are many. The communists say they are the next dialectical step in an inexorable spiral of progress. They claim to have resolved the 'inherent contradictions' of moralism and believe they're just one revolution away from establishing a humanist paradise..."

"The fascists say they are *both* the ancestors of and the successors to Dolorianism. In other words, they believe that Dolores Dei's reign simply represents a glorious phase of expansion within a greater Franconigerian heritage. They criticise the Dolorian project for accepting and integrating new peoples rather than forcefully subjugating them..."

"And then there are our prodigal cousins, the Vaasan social democrats, who hold our same values and have even adopted many of our same rites and iconography, though they persist in rejecting the umbrella of moralism."
For some reason it's the social democrats she sounds most exasperated with.
"If you believe so strongly in your own destiny that the rest of reality exists only as a warped reflection of it, how can it be contradicted?"

"Many political theorists have argued that communism accepts the logic of Dolorian humanism while abandoning its spirit. They offer a cautionary tale, in other words, about attempting to found a paradise atop bones and ashes..."
"Sometimes I wonder if the communists may have a point, at least intellectually speaking."
"What the fascists say makes a certain *gut-level* sense."
"Why do you resent social democrats more than communists and fascists?"
"Are there *non-ideological* threats to humanity's future?"
Whose bones and whose ashes, exactly? You don't think the Coalition pacified Revachol with *bonbons*, do you?
"Yes. Atomic war, environmental degradation, resource exhaustion, viral pandemic, super-volcanism, runaway entroponetic collapse..."
You know your people's history. You don't need some *foreign wöman* in a fancy airship to tell you what's what.
She speaks of them like a family member she's abandoned hope of ever maturing.
"We don't resent them. It's more that we are... *disappointed* that they have chosen to emphasise certain points of dispute over broad areas of accord..."
"And therein lies their danger. They 'feel' true without *being* true..."
"Who are the highwaymen and eschatologians you mentioned?"
"But it's a delicate and very complicated subject. And of course every belief system has something to recommend it."
"But of course, they also remain dependable partners in a number of centrist governing coalitions."
"How much time does humanity need to achieve its potential?"
"About 3,000 years."
She... really had that on the tip of her tongue. It's like she has the timeline laid out *right* in front of her.
"Of course, the number 3,000 represents the average of a great number of projections. The actual number might be closer to 2,800 or even 2,750, depending on the contingencies..."
"It is in all senses the most moderate and reasonable projection possible based on current science."
"That sounds about right, actually."
"That sounds like a very long time."
"That sounds like an *impossibly* long time."
"Something tells me we have less time than that. Like, a *lot* less time."
"Three-thousand years is just the blink of an eye. We need much more than that."
"It does, doesn't it? And yet there remains a great deal to be done in that span."
"Viewed from that perspective, we are nearly three-quarters of the way there."
"That depends on how you look at it. Since the Perikarnassian Incident, there have been nearly 8,000 years of recorded history..."
"Of course, the number 3,000 represents the average of a great number of projections. The actual number might be closer to 3,250 or even 3,300, depending on the contingencies..."
"Beautiful."
"It is possible. We grew up there. We have seen the lattice with our own eyes."
"Advesperascit... Dolores Dei was crowned there, wasn't she?"
"Where is Advesperascit exactly?"
"In Messina, of course. Not only was it the site of Dolores Dei's crowning, it was also one of the great cities of the Dolorian era, a glorious expression of humanity's highest potential..."
"She was. There are even those who say that Advesperascit *summoned* Dolores Dei, or that it was built in preparation for her, centuries before her arrival..."
"Impossible."
"That's why the old town is sometimes called 'The Ceremonial Heart of Humanity'..."

"Of course, such a city does not spring from nowhere, nor does it endure without effort. Its construction was the work of many generations, and its preservation is an equally monumental responsibility."
"Let us answer your question with a question: Have you ever seen evening fall over the old town of Advesperascit?"
"No, I haven't."
"Maybe? I've been forgetting things lately."
"If you had, then you would remember. It is one of the great wonders of the world, impossible to mistake or forget."

"The heart of the city, the old town, is a district composed of weathered marble, comprising thousands of columns and arcades arranged around a series of grand plazas. During the day it's a beautiful sight, equal to any of the great cities of Perikarnassis."

"But as the sun sets, the shadows cast by those columns and arcades weave together to form an intricate umbral lattice. When you see it, you suddenly understand: It was all built for you, for *this very moment*."

"Not only that, but you, you are also part of that centuries-long plan. When you cross one of the open plazas, your own shadow is effortlessly woven into the great latticework, a deliberate synthesis of humanity, art, and the natural world."
The name Advesperascit means 'Evening Comes.'
"Where does the RCM fit into all of this?"
"The RCM exists under the umbrella of the Coalition, just as the Coalition exists under the umbrella of the Moralintern..."
"Firewalker, was there anything else?"
"At the same time, the RCM is not exactly *of* the Coalition."
She's got you there...
"We're not that familiar with RCM lore and practice, but we believe that may be the case. As we recall, the décomptage originated with the Revacholian Commune itself."
"It's our understanding that the RCM's organisational structure predates the Coalition. We believe it may even be modelled after the communard brigades themselves."
"Of course. This is history we're talking about."
"What do you mean it's not *of* the Coalition?"
"You mean because of the décomptage?"
"That's confusing."
"There is some truth to that," the lieutenant whispers into his headset.
"But in a practical sense, it's the responsibility of the Ethics Division to ensure that both organisations are working toward the same ends."
"History is a river coursing ever downward. Occasionally its course is redirected in mysterious and unexpected ways."
"Why bother with the RCM at all? Can't the Coalition just run everything itself?"
"I suppose I enjoy casework too much. But surely you have more interesting things to discuss with the Coalition than my career path."
(Whisper.) "Hey, Kim. Why haven't you joined the Ethics Division?"
In other words, it's a fundamental part of the RCM, so you probably shouldn't ask her any questions about it.
"One now committed to upholding moralist values. Strange, isn't it?"
"So you're saying the RCM is a vestige of Revachol's communist past?"

"Because the Coalition has no interest in *running* Revachol. We'll succeed in our mission the moment Revachol rejoins the international community as a sovereign democracy. The RCM is an integral piece of that project."

The Ethics Division is the branch of the RCM that coordinates activities with the Coalition. It's composed of high-ranking RCM officials and their medium-ranking Moralintern counterparts. It's considered a career-making assignment for elite RCM officers.
"Firewalker, are you still there?"
The wind is pulling at the giant tarps that cover the blasted facade of the Capeside Apartments.
Air moving through what was once a row of apartments protected by walls and a roof. It sighs through the remains of bedrooms and parlours...
THIS IS YOUR CITY. DEFEND IT AT ALL COSTS.
DON'T FORSAKE ME, OFFICER. I AM YOUR RESPONSIBILITY JUST AS YOU ARE MINE.
"Yes, it is. We grew up there. We have seen the lattice with our own eyes."
A truth conveyed matter-of-factly, without pride or self-consciousness.
That sounds *much* better than the 5,500 reál the RCM calls a 'salary.'
"Pretty different from Adversperascit, isn't it?"

"*Extremely different*. We knew there were still parts of Revachol that have not fully recovered from the Revolution, but here the destruction is quite evident, even compared to the eastern side of the city..."
"For the most part, it has. The world is certainly not free of violent conflict, but in the modern era we have made great strides to reduce its frequency, duration, and severity."
"But we must stress that real democracy is an ongoing process and not simply an outcome. It must be cultivated and preserved if it is to endure."
"Like the city of Advesperascit, you mean."
"Esattamente."
"Beyond that, it may be said that we are the inheritors and stewards of Dolores Dei's legacy."
If the opportunity presents itself, perhaps you should mention the two-millimetre hole you recently discovered.
"This is why it is critical for the international community to work toward peace and cooperation between nations. There's simply too much at stake."
She's right. There's really nothing more for you up here.
The lieutenant sighs. "What's *one more trip* across the waterlock?"

dialoguetext: Keep listening.
"Liebling, bitte… Er ist unser einziges Kind. Er kann doch auch nächstes Jahr zur Akademie gehen."
"Just radio-spookers. We get them all the time around here. Keep trying."
"Liebling, bitte… Er ist unser einziges Kind. Er kann doch auch nächstes Jahr zur Akademie gehen."
"What's going on?"
"Keep trying. We'll get through these radio-spookers eventually."
What does this remind me of?
"Again."
"I can't understand a word of this gibberish."
"Liebling, bitte… Er ist unser einziges Kind. Er kann doch auch nächstes Jahr zur Akademie gehen."
"Me neither. Just keep trying. We'll get through these radio-spookers eventually."
"Liebling, bitte… Er ist unser einziges Kind. Er kann doch auch nächstes Jahr zur Akademie gehen."
It's strangely comforting to think of these voices travelling through the air, until you capture them, firefly-like, with your little metal antenna...
"Noid, I think there are ghosts in this radio."
"Liebling, bitte… Er ist unser einziges Kind. Er kann doch auch nächstes Jahr zur Akademie gehen."
"Yeah, sounds like some radio-spookers, alright. That's what happens when you get down in the mega-low range. You better keep trying anyway..."
"Noid, I think we're getting some entroponetic crosstalk."
"Is that what you call those radio-spookers? Didn't know they had a *technical* name..."
"It's cold now..."
"Either way, you gotta keep it up till we get through."
"Coalition Warship Archer, this is Firewalker. If you're there, Archer, please acknowledge."
It's just like that woman in the electronic doorbell... the circuit ghost...
"Coalition Warship Archer, this is Firewalker. Do you acknowledge?"
The rustling of dry autumn leaves. Waves breaking at a distance. A thousand wings beating at once.
Something here is eating at the lieutenant, as much as he would like to move past it.
Here it is again, this pale... If only you knew more about it.
Pale? Pale-pale-pale... Seems to be missing from your records.
Hold on, isn't the pale supposed to be thousands of kilometres from here?
Don't forget the lats, champ! You've got this...
"Yes, you're a natural gymnast, detective. Now would you like to do what you got up there to do?"
Pour some alcohol over the connections.
If you had something *alcoholic*, you could dissolve the oils, creating a cleaner (and clearer) connection.
Truth be told, you have no idea what you're looking for. It just looks like a cord attached to a piece of metal. You pick at the colourful rubber jacketing, not sure what else to do...
"Is this really the time, detective?"
"Wow, law-science comes through."
"Glad that stuff came in handy after all..."
"Are you partying up there?"
"Well? What's it look like?"
"That's not good. We should've cleaned the centaur-man first. Pretty rude that we didn't..."
"It is, it's the time of desperate measures. He's using his party fuel to clean the connections..."
"Did that help?"
Once the alcohol has had time to dissolve the oils, you wipe off the bar with your sleeve and reattach the cable.
"Huh. I don't know what to do then..."
Clean the connections with the ammonia.
"The whole statue's covered in weird oils. I don't think it's good for the connections."
"The connections are pretty dirty, but I don't have anything to clean them with."
"The connections look fine to me."
More than that, you're sacrificing something precious on the altar...
"Yeah... maybe some. Not enough though. Would've hoped between that and the de-spooker engaged that we'd be able to align with any frequency, but we're still just medium core, at best."
"Yeah, maybe it helped *a little*, but the overall picture is still pretty soft core, at best."
"... unser einziges Kind. Er kann doch auch nächstes Jahr zur Akademie gehen..."
"Hang on, I'm looking at Egg's checklist. He says: 'IF ALL FAILS, BEND ANTENNA. NARROW IS THE HARD CORE WAY'... That make any sense to you?"
Look down.

A few of the idle lorry drivers and strike breakers gesture at you with their cigarettes, more out of curiosity than anything else. From the window of one of the adjacent apartment buildings, an older woman leans out, her heavy breasts sagging...
She yells a single word you can't make out, and then shuts the window with a violent *thunk*.
Down below a little doll-sized lieutenant is looking up, shielding his eyes. He's worried for you.
Across the river, you can see the lights of Coalition Warship Archer floating above Revachol East.
A clear sky. The kind of day where anything might happen...
The sky is gray and overcast. Somehow, the raindrops seem to fall more slowly from this angle...
A clear night sky. The stars make for a brilliant display...
The sky is opaque with dark clouds. Somehow, the raindrops seem to fall more slowly from this angle...
Through the scrim, you can just make out the shadow of Coalition Warship Archer a few kilometres to the east.
Across the river, you can see Coalition Warship Archer tracing its gradual circuit above Revachol East.
Look up.
You turn to the east, but the visibility is quite poor. You see no sign of Coalition Warship Archer, though you know it can't be too far away.
His imperious gaze leads you naturally to his outstretched hand, which for some reason strikes you as sadly empty...
Look at the rider.
You are face to face with Filippe III. The bronze king looks toward the west. Something about his features seems bizarrely distorted.
Not intentionally. It’s a matter of perspective. The king was never meant to be seen from such an angle as you’ve attained.
He seems ill-equipped for wherever he’s going. A king should not go about unarmed.
You can't help but feel that *sabre* you picked up might just give this old king a little more panache *and* better reception!
To your surprise, the sabre's hilt fits quite snugly in the statue's hand. The king cuts quite the triumphal figure now.
Keep it to yourself.
"Everything in order, detective? You're really giving Filippe III a stare."
Come on! Kings and sabres are so *played out*. There's a *better* way...
That's brilliant! [Put the sabre between the horse's teeth.]
That's a little *too* out there. [Put the sabre in the king's hand.]
The king won't know what he's missing. He looks straight ahead, his expression defiant and verdigris.
Wait, what's this 'better way'?
Why not arm the good king's valiant steed instead? There seems to be *just* enough room between its teeth there...
To your surprise, the sabre slides snugly between the horse's bared teeth.
Attach the sabre.
Keep it to yourself.
"You alright up there?"
"Wow, this is a huge leap forward for hard core style. Good work."
"Nah, every bit helps. We need this antenna to be as hard core as humanly possible."
"There is no way *that* is going to make any difference..."
He's right. This was your responsibility...
"You're getting out-tangled by the Big Bad. Time to try something else."
"This line of argument is quite pointless. You should abandon it."
The programmer's words are nearly swallowed by the roar of the Laurel's main rotors...

dialoguetext: Whatever her misgivings about the Coalition, the fact is that you've summoned an aerostatic with your voice. An achievement she never thought she'd witness...
But where is your half-brother, the lieutenant? He should be here...
"How am I supposed to inspect the connections?"
"My guess, you climb up the centaur-man, see if there's anything obviously *interfering* with them. Maybe you've got some technical law-science?"
This isn't exactly your area of expertise, though...
"... someone has been maintaining it..."
No problem at all. You've already teleported up *way* greater heights.
"But what if I slip and fall..."
"It's got to be you. I'm manning the decks down here."
"But I don't know what I'm doing..."
"No problem. I've already mastered the art of teleportation."
"You actually haven't. But you have proven that you're a relatively capable climber."
Come on, son. This isn't anything but a common high bar! Just get a solid overhand grip and hoist yourself up!
Images of your body smashed against the pavement flood your mind -- this is *dangerous*.
"Then there's no problem, is there?"
"But that's what the invalids' fund is for, so don't worry about it for now."
Something about this set-up seems dimly familiar, but you'll be damned if you know what you're supposed to do about it.
"Maybe you break an arm, maybe you break your neck. Could go either way, honestly."
"Well, it's rather dark now, but from our porthole, we can just make out the rolling hillsides. We can see the lanterns lining the walkways through a public park..."
"Is everything alright? We lost the connection for a moment..."
"... Firewalker? Are you there?"
"Liebling, bitte... Er ist unser einziges Kind..."
"It's been a long winter... Long and cold."
"It's been a long winter... Long and cold."
"... Firewalker? Are you there?"
"Come again? We are picking up more interference..."
"Is everything alright?"
"Bad news, lawman. Signal's going down. These waves are receding. Time to let go..."
"This is it: Final question time. I can already feel our alignment getting shaky..."
"Signal's weakening. I'd guess you've got about two questions left..."
"Bad news, lawman. Signal's going down. These waves are receding. Time to let go..."
"This is it: Final question time. I can already feel our alignment getting shaky..."
You look around. Most everyone has already gone home for the night. It's really just you and the programmer left...
You look around. The strike breakers are still shouting their slogans and waving their hand-painted signs. Beneath you, the programmer has begun disconnecting a few cables...
"There are a few people on horses by a small pond. The homes and gardens are quite beautiful, very near like those in certain areas of Messina."
"Ah, there are children building a snowman by a small pond. The homes and gardens are quite beautiful, very near like those in certain areas of Messina."
"Ah, there are children running home to get out of the rain. The homes and gardens are quite beautiful, very near like those in certain areas of Messina."
"Ah, there are children playing by a small pond. The homes and gardens are quite beautiful, very near like those in certain areas of Messina."
That's sarcasm, she's clearly Messinian.
"No -- well, not quite. The Moralintern never *intends* to violate another nation's sovereignty. That would be a serious violation of international law..."
"We repeat: Were you alone?"
The lieutenant gives a long sigh as he removes his headphones. There's relief on his face as he turns toward you.
"Built by whom?"
"By thousands of people over many centuries, in keeping with a precise plan each believed in but never expected to see the final completion of..."
(Say nothing.)
"Built for *me*?"
"For you, for all of humanity..."
The cold metal chills your bare hands. Some part of your brain tells you something is missing...
Chalk powder. Absorbs moisture and keeps your grip firm.
"Good. Now, give me a hand with these amplifiers. Leave the cables. I don't feel like making two trips..."
"About time. You grab that amp. Forget the cables. Need to leave some evidence of our antenna to inspire future generations..."

dialoguetext: "And now if you'll just connect that here..."
"It's done. I believe we're ready." The lieutenant wipes his brow.
"Got it. Are we ready?"

"We're ready to try, at least. Please, put those on. I've configured the channels so that only your microphone is set to broadcast. We'll both be able to listen, but anyone we reach will only hear *your* voice."

"You will need to transmit your connection request while I attempt to locate the warship's public frequency. You will likely encounter some interference, but it's important to keep transmitting your request until you're acknowledged. Ready?"
"Wait, what if they *never* acknowledge me?"
"Yes."
"Not yet."
The programmer seems to consider the question for a moment, then dismisses it with a flick of her wrist...
"Then it will be exactly like every other moment of every other day. I ask again: Are you ready?"
"Good. Beginning transmission."
"Too late. I've begun transmitting..."
A soft rustling. The snow seems to have gotten between your ears somehow...
A soft rustling. Between your ears, a winterscape with fast falling snow...

"We're ready to try, at least. Please, put on these headphones, there should be two extra sets. I've configured the channels so that only your microphone is set to broadcast, officer. We'll all be able to listen, but anyone we reach will only hear *your* voice."
Where's the sound coming from?
Ignore it.
Every lightswitch, every motor carriage, every doorbell, tea kettle, and radio in Martinaise, all mingled with electrical interference caused by scattered thunderstorms over Ozonne.
"Officer? Are you in order? We're waiting for you to start..."
"Go ahead, officer."
"Coalition Warship Archer, this is RCM Officer Firewalker. Please acknowledge."
"Coalition Warship Archer, this is RCM Officer Tequila Sunset. Please acknowledge."
"Coalition Warship Archer, this is Detective Raphaël Ambrosius Costeau of the RCM. Please acknowledge."
"Coalition Warship Archer, this is Lieutenant Harrier du Bois of the RCM. Please acknowledge."
"What should I say?"
"We don't have time for indecision. Just say whatever first comes to mind."
You're all alone out there, wandering a blasted heath, calling out to the night, but there is no reply, except for the buzzing of invisible machines...
I-i-is there anybody th-th-there?
The lieutenant looks up at you with a nervous glance.
He is nervous for your sake, of course, but also his own.
"Try again, officer."
Nervous for who, though, you cannot say.
Looking at him now, with both hands on his headphones, you see very briefly what the lieutenant must have been like when he first joined the RCM...
Then he turns to you. His expression seems to say, 'You'd better not leave this mess for me alone'.
Then he turns to you. He gives you a half smile along with an almost imperceptible nod of encouragement.
Then he turns to you. He shakes his head slightly and looks back at the amplifier.
Perhaps you're simply imagining it, but it seems as though you're learning to pull apart the fibres of this auditory felt. You focus on one strand in particular, one that sounds very nearly human...
What does this remind me of?
"Soona, is this more of that entroponetic crosstalk?"
Keep listening.
"I can't understand a word of this gibberish."
It's just like that woman in the electronic doorbell... the circuit ghost...
The rustling of dry autumn leaves. Waves breaking at a distance. A thousand wings beating at once.
"It's very likely, based on what we've recently learned. Give me a moment while I attempt to narrow the receiving mode..."
"Soona, I think there are ghosts in this radio."
"What's going on?"
"Liebling, bitte… Er ist unser einziges Kind. Er kann doch auch nächstes Jahr zur Akademie gehen."
"Not ghosts, officer. Crosstalk. You have to keep trying until we get a signal through."
"It isn't gibberish, it's Walder. Now please, keep trying."
"Liebling, bitte… Er ist unser einziges Kind. Er kann doch auch nächstes Jahr zur Akademie gehen."
"It's crosstalk. In all likelihood they can't hear you. You have to keep trying until we get a signal through."
"Liebling, bitte… Er ist unser einziges Kind. Er kann doch auch nächstes Jahr zur Akademie gehen."
"Keep trying, officer. We'll get a signal through eventually."
"Liebling, bitte… Er ist unser einziges Kind. Er kann doch auch nächstes Jahr zur Akademie gehen."
"In the meantime, you must keep trying."
"Liebling, bitte… Er ist unser einziges Kind. Er kann doch auch nächstes Jahr zur Akademie gehen."
It's strangely comforting to think of these voices travelling through the air, until you capture them, firefly-like, with your little metal antenna...
A slight frisson at the point where your neck meets your spine. Something about the lieutenant's words, directed at you, but not *you*.
"Kim, don't clog my connection."
"What are you talking about, Kim? It's perfectly nice out."
"It's really coming down, now that you mention it."
"Mention what?"
"It's cold, like you just said."
"I didn't say anything, detective."
"I just heard you say, 'It's cold now'."
"...someone has been maintaining it. The wiring has been repaired..."
An uncomfortable silence falls over the connection.
"... It's been a long winter... Long and cold..."
"Are you going to tell me you didn't say *that*, either?"
"Maybe it's your twin brother?"
"I promise you, I didn't, even though it certainly *sounds* like me..." The lieutenant seems to wince at the sound of his own voice.
"I can assure you, it's not my 'twin brother'. Though it certainly does *sound* like me..." The lieutenant seems to wince at the sound of his own voice.
"What is happening?"
"I can't say with certainty, but it *sounds* very much like entroponetic crosstalk. It happens sometimes when sending transmissions across long stretches of pale."
"Could this be more entroponetic crosstalk?"
"Yes," the programmer cuts in. "A particularly eerie specimen, but still just a harmless piece of the past returning to surface."
"Right. I just wish I could remember what I was talking about..."
"Natürlich halten ihn die Psychologen für vollkommen normal..."
Something here is eating at the lieutenant, as much as he would like to move past it.
"Ah, yes, of course. That must be it..."
A slight frisson at the point where your neck meets your spine. You can *feel* the lieutenant's presence, even though he's nowhere to be found...
"Kim? How did you get on my connection?"
"There's no way the lieutenant has his *own* mega-low frequency connection. Very strange..."
"...someone has been maintaining it. The wiring has been repaired..."
"I believe you mean, what *was* he talking about."
"What is he talking about?"
"Are you saying this is more entroponetic crosstalk, then?"
"Yes, that's by far the most likely explanation. But the odds of us hearing him, though, out of all the voices in the pale..."
"It's been a long winter... Long and cold."
"...are astronomically low."
"Wait, what are *you* talking about?"
"It's been a long winter... Long and cold."
"It sounds very much like entroponetic crosstalk. It happens sometimes when sending transmissions across long stretches of pale..."
Here it is again, this pale... If only you knew more about it.
Pale? Pale-pale-pale... Seems to be missing from your records.
"What can we do?"
"How am I supposed to inspect the connections?"
"I did not expect simply locating the signal to be so difficult." She appears to be concentrating very intently.
"We must consider several variables: local entroponetic conditions, the sophistication of our transceiver, the quality of our connections, and the physics of our antenna itself."
"Fortunately, we have a more-than-adequate transceiver, so I do not believe it is causing any problems..."
"Our transceiver is perfectly capable, so there is no problem there..."
"And we're also unlikely to change our local entroponetic conditions. So the next step is to thoroughly inspect our connections."
"You need to climb up there and look at them for yourself." She stares at you as though it were obvious. Her hand gestures to the colourful cables dangling from the horse's forehooves.

"Actually, I don't want to know. I don't want to know what happened."
Oh, those again? I have been trying to wean you off them.
Off of what?
You know, when you put your gun, your *actual* gun, on your temple and pretend to shoot your brains out? Off of that. People don't like that.

Hm, I remember this. You were screaming things like "My brains are all over the walls, painting them red. I won't be seeing it, cause these are my brains. I can't see without my brains!" Very nice visuals there.
Some poor sod was trying to eat his pudding, while you were screaming, spit flying, imitating the *mercy shot* right next to him... Spat some in his food, I don't think he touched it after...
People tried to back away from you or even slip out of the door, but you screamed: I AM THE GODDAMNED LAW AND YOU HAVE TO LISTEN TO ME, YOU ARE ALL SUSPECTS IN A MURDER INVESTIGATION!
"I should have killed myself..."
"Why would I threaten to kill myself?! I mean, look at this world, I would love to stay!"
"Yes, but what happened to my gun?" (Just conclude.)
"No, please, no more suicide threats! Thank *god* you don't have that stupid gun anymore..."
Real policemen have uniforms too, by the way. Where's yours?
"Yes, well..." The static on the radio suggests Sylvie doesn't have a comment.
"Actually, I think I might be a birdie. A birdwatching enthusiast, you know."
Her voice reappears from the static: "That's wonderful, really. Maybe you should keep pursuing that hobby. Maybe it would calm you down a little."
"Okay, officer..." Her voice is withdrawing as if she's moving away from the speaker.
"It was a pretty bird, there since I started working in the Whirling. I really liked her. We called her Scotty..."
Crackling static... more static and yes, more of that sweet static. The violence of your words is obviously scaring her.
"Do you know how my paperwork ended up in the trash container behind the Whirling?"

dialoguetext: "Do you know who put the victim's clothes in the trash?"
"No, I don't know. It wasn't me..." She gulps. "I haven't been out there since... I was terrified of the stench and the corpse." She falls silent.
"Wait -- police documents?"
"I must have had some sort of official police documents on me. Do you know where they could be?"
That's where *you* step in. You're Lieutenant Love, matchmaker extraordinaire! Help the poor girl out, lest she turns into a *spinster*.
Oh my god, not a spinster!
Yeah. She's a woman. Probably just playing hardball with the goods. Women are just transactional.
What am I, deranged? A woman doesn't have to be married. She doesn't even have to be in a relationship. Also, feminism.
I'm happy to help, but maybe I could do so without all this internalized misogyny?
What misogyny? I'm just telling things the way they are. Can't a man be honest in his *own head* anymore?
Not a spinster, my god!
What *deranged*? I'm just telling things the way they are. Can't a man even be honest in his *own head* anymore?
You have to intervene on behalf of Love! First calm her down, tell her you've got everything *under control* -- and then go have a boys' talk with Garte himself.
Think you can do that, Lieutenant Love?
"Khm..." (To the microphone.) "Are you still there, kiddo? Listen... I've got everything under control."
"No. What?"
"You and Garte, right? A little trouble under the sheets? Say no more, papa's got this. Big Poppa."
Oh yeah. My point exactly. You know how they are -- transactional and hysteric. Loony broads.
You know what you've got to do. First you've got to calm her down, tell her you've got everything *under control* -- then go and have a little boys' talk with Garte himself.
"Daddy is going to take you on his lap, little darling."
Please no. I don't want to say any of those things. (Refuse the Love Quest -- although it's *wonderful*.)
"Oh god." The static appears to breathe heavily. "Please just stay out of my li..."
"I know, baby, I know. It's just that you've got that sweet woman-child thing that makes men go *crazy*. Especially a man like Garte."
You have to *act*, Lieutenant Love. You have to calm that hysteric down, tell it you've got everything under control -- then go and have a little boys' talk with Garte himself.
You're just a gimp. What, you want to be more *empathetic*?
Nothing's wrong, it's just *sssssexuality*.
You have to *act*, Lieutenant Love. You have to calm that hysteric girl down, tell her you've got everything under control -- and then go and have a little boys' talk with the man himself.
Khm... Correction: Lieutenant Double-Yefreitor Love.
Stop! That's Lieutenant Double-Yefreitor Love for you.
Of course. So much more love. But now -- react!
God -- what is happening in your HEAD?!
Big Big Poppa is happening.
"*I* am the authority around here."
"Okay." She obviously doesn't want to challenge your authority. You feel *much* better now.
"Wait, Kim," (Lower your microphone.) "Is she speaking truth? The Union is the law around here?"

dialoguetext: Words are not necessary to feel the lieutenant's discontent for the situation.
"What trouble?!"
"Okay, I understand."
"You don't live here, you *don't* understand. Squealing is frowned upon here -- everything is dealt with... well, by the Union. Internally."
You hear static. Her chin rub against the receiver. Then: "Please, I just didn't want any trouble."
"Hey!" The lieutenant interrupts with a flicker of anger in his eyes. "If you cannot restrain yourself then I'll be handling the interviews from now on and you can quietly take notes."
"You got your methods, I got mine lieutenant. Now let me do my job."
"Sorry, I don't know what came over me, I just lost it -- I might have an anger issue."
"Apparently so. Please do try to control yourself." The anger is gone from his eyes and it's almost as if his voice is softer than before.

Cop with an anger issue, underpaid, overworked and on the verge of collapse in both personal and professional life -- that's more of a rule than an exception. And the lieutenant knows this. He understands.
Breathing on the other end suggests that Sylvie is still on the line. She heard everything.
"Fine." The lieutenant clenches his jaw. "But know that I don't approve of such gratuitous volatility."

An angry cop refusing to face his demons and taking his frustration out on others -- just a badge and a gun away from those he's manhandling. A fast burning candle -- that's the side you just exposed to the lieutenant. He doesn't judge, has seen it too many times all ready -- you both have probably, but he takes a mental note.
"People don't have the money to have the cables put in again. They use the Union's phone or the one on the coast."
Yeah, I think she got it. Good job!
I'm going to let it slide. I don't need answers for every little thing.
Kim doesn't have a *uniform* and he seems real to me.
Not my uniform too! God, I should really look into that.
Right. It's better to not ask too many questions, lest people start thinking you're a *cop* or something.
There are officers who wear the signature Perseus Black uniforms to the highest ranks in the RCM and end up buried in them as well -- others do it more *casually*. Looks like you're one of them.
Somewhere in a dank rental apartment, two police officers stand in the dark. Trash and liquor bottles cover the floor. Things are not good.
It feels like you haven't worn yours in a long-long time.
Yes, you absolutely should. It's awful that you lost it.
He's in plainclothes. Voluntarily. It's different from not knowing where your uniform is.
"Great." There's relief in her voice. "Anything else?"
There is silence on the other end of the line.
One of the men, trying not to slip on old newspapers, makes his way to the window and pulls the curtains apart. Roaches scatter as the light comes in.

"Goddamn..." officer Michel 'Elfboy' Williams speaks to himself. His partner, Sundance Fischer, looks at the patrol uniform he's wearing -- then at an identical suit framed on the wall. It's blue and covered in dust. "Let's get the fuck out of here," he turns to Williams, "he hasn't been here in days."
There's genuine sadness in her voice.
"I've had sailors fighting, Union guys grabbing my ass, kids stealing booze. Once a guy was glued to the karaoke machine every night for two months. But *you*..." She pauses.
"Hold on, which song?"
"'We Go On' by the OO." She sighs. "I can't listen to it anymore, you've turned it into a parody."
"I, ugh... the ones I had to wrench out of your toilet."
"What happened to them?"
"I... dammit, I don't remember what I did to your damn papers! I don't remember every little thing I do." Resentment gives way to concern in her voice.
She's worried she might have accidentally done something bad. Then she remembers it's *you*.
"Anything else I can help you with, officer?"
You hear a sigh of relief on the other end of the radio. Wordless, the call breaks. Then the already familiar voice:
"Right, thank you for talking with me. Take care." [Leave.]

"Well." There's an uncomfortable pause. "You tried to jam it down the toilet, sir, clogging it completely. After I had *unclogged* the toilet and retrieved the paperwork I threw it out in the trash, thinking you didn't need it."
"I am sorry about that." She doesn't sound like she's actually that sorry. "Anything else, detective?"
There are *way* more inventive ways than a gun to leave this world.
"Call was terminated by the other party. Anything else, officer?"
"You mean why did I leave the bar?" You can hear her tense up on the other side. "Honestly, I'm... not really comfortable discussing it with you, sir."
"Wait, why aren't you comfortable discussing it with me?"
"Okay. Did you leave because of Garte?"
"Alright, I won't push you on this. Are you ever coming back to work?" (Conclude.)
"I, uh..." The static wavers. "Let's just say I left because I needed to get away from someone."
"Get away from whom?"
"You know whom."
"What?" She stops abruptly. "No, why would you even think that?!"
You think you hear a sliver of accusation in her words.
"Sylvie, don't be afraid of that pig. You have to stand up for yourself!"
"*Please* don't bring Garte into this, it's none of your business!"
"I already said I don't want to talk about this! You're messing everything up again!"
Don't be paranoid, she's obviously talking about someone else, not you.
"Maybe, I don't know..." She seems to relax a little bit. "I just know I have to take some time off right now."
"Yes, obviously. You were the worst client I've ever seen. And I have seen *so many* assholes in this place..."
"But... when I spoke to Garte it seemed like he thought you left because of *him*."
"Sounds intense."
"That's it? That's not so bad."
"And *then* I had to deal with your toilet. The one you clogged with *police documents*, causing water damage downstairs in the kitchen."
"What does this Union have to do with anything?"
"Wait, really? No, this is absolutely not true. I like Garte, I really do."
"Didn't he cross a line when he asked you out?"
"No, I was actually flattered, I've always liked him. It was just bad timing... with the corpse and all that."
"I didn't know *what* to say to him later. Then you came and destroyed the place. So I left without explaining. I should have told him maybe..."
There's a pause. You can almost see her on the other side, the telephone cord coiled around her index.
"I can tell him." (Accept.)
"Understood." (Refuse task)
"Right. Well... Are we almost done now, officer?"
"Okay, but... please don't mess it up. Please don't take out your gun or something."
There's no reply from the other end of the line.
"Huh, I don't even know what to say..."
"He told me he asked you out. Are you saying it didn't happen?"
"So you do agree that quitting your job just because someone asked you out is an *overreaction*?"
"You mean me? You needed to get away from *me*?"
"I *really* don't want to talk about this. Let's just forget about this, okay?"
Sounds like it's going to be bad. Do you really want to know?
"It almost looked like you pawned it, but believe me, I did *not* ask." She sighs.
There is *no* resentment in her tone. She wants you to ask her out. No question about it.
Garbage!
Push her *further*. Show her the error of her ways.
So the Union has a phone -- and there's one further down the coast. Got it.
"It was someone else." The lieutenant makes a note. "We'll find them sooner or later, officer. It just might take a while."
"You have to ask someone else. There are thousands of people in Martinaise."
Relax. You'll find them sooner or later -- this will just take some time.
Am I, though?
Rubbish! You're a green hat and feather totin' birdwatcher!
Or a cop with brain damage. One of the two.
"I won't even *mention* you waving your gun around, harassing customers, *threatening* to sing karaoke, threatening to kill yourself..."
Interesting... you still have to find it, however.
"Seems like Klaasje wasn't lying when she said it was her." The lieutenant makes a note. "This corroborates her story -- she made the call."
Seems like Klaasje wasn't lying when she said she made the call. This corroborates.
She iseth the fairest of them all. The ugliness of lies wouldst never escape her lips!
Are you *sure* lieutenant? For some reason, you have a little doubt about that...
I wouldn't be so sure, detective.
Interesting... you still have to find a copy though. Before you can blast it.
"Ah yes, *that* paperwork. I found it."
"Good. Then it's not lost." She seems a little relieved. "Just don't throw it in the toilet again. Toilets don't work like that."
"Especially when there's a hurricane loose. It's *your* fault for losing them -- not mine."
Something in you wants to immediately *forget* about this. As if there was a reason you threw them away.
"Are you *sure* you don't remember where the paperwork I flushed is?"
"Sorry about that." She doesn't sound like she's too sorry. "Anything else, detective?"
"Yes, I'm sure. Every time we talk about it I'm going to be *more* sure I don't know."
"I, ugh... the ones I had to wrench out of your toilet?"
"What happened to them?"
"I... dammit, I don't remember what I did to your damn papers! I don't remember every little thing I do..." Resentment gives way to concern in her voice.
She's worried she might have accidentally done something bad. Then she remembers it's *you*.
"Especially when there's a hurricane loose. It's your fault for losing them -- not mine."
Something in you wants to immediately *forget* about this. As if there was a reason you threw them away.
"I put them in my toilet?"
"Yes. You put *something* there. Causing bad water damage in the kitchen. I think it was that."
It's *on*. The Love Quest is on -- too late everyone! It's *on*. Take it to Garte now!
"God, why can't you just mind your own business..." she mutters.
The lieutenant goes pale. 'Missing badge?' he mouths to himself, silently.
"Sorry. Sorry about the song."
"To hell with that song..."
"I'm sorry."
Why not?
If she used to work in the Whirling-in-Rags, then you must have met her.
"Oh, all sorts of things. Some disco, rock too. So much disco and rock..."
"Okay. I don't know what to say."
"Me neither."
Whatever this Empathy failure tells you -- *don't* take the quest. It's not wonderful, it's ugly.
Vapour emanates from the large engine on the back of the vehicle. It hasn't had time to cool off yet.
Before you stands a motor carriage. The bodywork is covered in blue and white livery bearing the number 57.
This must be the infernal machine that tore you from oblivion.

Your fingers waste no time closing around the handle. Clutch disengaged. Release the handle -- clutch drops -- right foot yearns for the familiar touch of the accelerator pedal. You have synced with the machine's mechanical circulation.
This must be the infernal machine that tore you from oblivion -- the Coupris Kineema motor carriage.

dialoguetext: The pull-out toolbox slides back into its nest. Pre-heater gauge casts a warm glow on the steering levers and the radio on its hook.
Push in the pull-out toolbox.
The white suede feels luxurious under the touch and the metal clutch handle so very familiar in your palm...
Because it's lonely. Just like you. Seaweed and strange fish around it, limpets clinging to the carcass... The sounds of the streets above...
After a while you realize silence is your only answer. Do what you will with it.
Close the door. [Leave.]
Tap on the fuel pre-heater gauge.
Release the clutch and squeeze it again.
Run your fingers over one of the steering levers.
The smell of freshly treated leather, the lack of dirt and dust on the dashboard, and a neat little brush in the cup-holder all seem to be whispering:
Wait, does it mean I know how to pilot it?
Pull out the pull-out toolbox.
In the cabin you are welcomed by a set of steering levers, a radio-microphone on a hook, a pull-out toolbox under the seat, and the soft glow of the fuel pre-heater gauge.
At the bottom of the sea...
Do I know how to operate this machine?
You feel an uninterrupted connection to the mechanics.
[Leave.]
A metallic drawer slides out from under the seat and clicks into place. The tools inside are neatly organized.
Where have you been?
How are you, my friend?
Release the clutch handle.
A scent of leather-work and heavy fuel oils washes over you.
Open the door.
Of course it's only in your head -- of course it is -- but it almost feels as if the clutch handle is gently squeezing back.
I'm good, cherished and cared for, in the hands of a tending owner.
This is clearly feverish nonsense -- let's rationalize it away. Grab the radio, or tools, or do something normal.
The handle is pulled back. Somewhere deep inside the drivetrain the disk is mated to the flywheel again.
Take the rubber-handled chaincutters.
The lights unfold with a little click, casting electrical light onto the ground before the vehicle.
"Yes, hello!" A female voice greets you through static -- it sounds like she's million miles away from here.
"Of course. What is her number, officer?"
"Kim, didn't Garte give you Sylvie's number?"
"Actually, let's not do that right now." (Back.)
"Officer?" You hear phones ringing and people talking in the background.
"I'm done with the radio for now." (End call.)
"Fifty-seventh, over and out." Her voice disappears into the void.
Lieutenant Kitsuragi slowly begins to tap a little rhythm with his right foot. Quite a lot of time has passed.
Wait patiently.
Start slapping a marching rhythm on your thighs.
"Yes, hold on..." the lieutenant takes a look at his notes. "Her number is 005 1944 298."
"Received. Hold on, officer."
"I need you to connect me to a civilian -- a Sylvie. She may have reported a murder."
The frequency tableau lights up and a green button labelled PRIMELINE glows like a feline eye... and then you hear something.
Pick up the radio.
"This is Precinct 57! Hello, lieutenant, how may I assist you?"
"Hello, Alice, please assist our colleague from the 41st Precinct here. I'm putting him on."
"This is Officer Alice DeMettrie, Precinct 57. How may I assist you?" You could swear she was friendlier with the lieutenant.
"Come in, Delta-Ten, this is Firewalker, copy."
"Come in dispatch, come in dispatch!"
"Hi, Alice, this is the officer from the 41st Precinct speaking. Nice to meet you."
Under the green PRIMELINE a yellow SAVED button catches your eye... You wonder what the lieutenant's default radio station is?
"Change of plans, Alice -- connect me to *you*."
"What do you mean, officer? I'm not Sylvie."
"I don't know, Alice... just connect me."
"Sir, you're already connected to the 57th Precinct." Her voice is sharp.
Ignore Alice and press the button labelled "Saved".
