dialoguetext: Close the box.
It's made from some sort of wood and has been decorated with peculiar plant motifs.
You place the die into your pocket. It's always good to have luck on your side.
You see a man in ragged clothes wearing a lopsided hat and wielding some sort of a firearm.
You pick the figurine up by the base to meet your gaze. The little plastic man stares back at you, his face contorted into a disturbing shout. Then you pocket it.
With fewer items inside, the box now rattles with less enthusiasm. Only the map and booklet shuffle around, hitting the sides of the box.
"Huh, interesting. A communard."
A leftist revolutionary... a communard. He looks lost, a stranger in a strange land. Most likely, he was just stuck in the wrong box on accident.
Look at the map.

A reprint of a crude hand-drawn map. The top left corner reads: 'Lands of Wirrâl.' The map features both small villages and mid-sized towns (with odd names), in addition to meadows, forests, hills, lakes and seas (also with odd names).
You don't know much about dice, but this one looks pretty damn fancy.
It doesn't seem to correspond with anything you've seen thus far. It's not a very helpful map.
You hear the die rattling inside the box, bumping against the sides.
You hear the figurine rattling inside the box, bumping against the sides.
"What's so interesting about that?"
"That doesn't sound very Wirrâl-like."
An odd-looking fellow... he doesn't seem to fit the rest of the setting. He has more of a... *revolutionary* tinge.
"The figurine is not a part of the Wirrâl game setting... I guess someone misplaced it during the packaging process."
"It is not. The communards are not a part of the game setting... I guess someone misplaced it during the packaging process."
You stuff it back inside the box.
Look at the booklet.
The welkin come with a variety of exciting sub-races: high welkin, forest welkin, lake welkin, and snow welkin. But if you're not feeling experimental -- a basic welkin will always do.
Read about the faerie folk.
A very small race of flying people, known for being mischievous, full of trickery. They often lure people into their maegical traps. There are no sub-races for the faeries.
Read about the pygmies.

The least popular of the Wirrâl races, the pygmies are short, rotund and dim-witted. Pygmies live in small villages made of shoddy wooden dwellings. They spend most their days tilling the earth and smoking their pipes. There are no sub-races for the pygmies.
Read about the humans.
They're just humans... what else is there to tell? They're average in all stats and jacks-of-all-trades.
"A what?"
"A communard. One of the leftist revolutionaries in the Antecentennial Revolution."
"Does this mean we can't play?"
The lieutenant shrugs. "I have a feeling the figurines are more there to set the scene than anything else."
"Maybe someone should make a role-playing game set during the Revolution."
"Hmm. Good luck finding people who'd want to play as communards."
Flip through the pages.
"Madam, what's this book?"
"A highly educational primer. It's exceptional for the young mind... and obviously, very popular."
It's exactly like a primer -- a word on every page relating to a letter of the alphabet.
"Oh wow, that's cool. I want to become smarter."
"You're a grown man, though. It's a bit too late for that... this is a book for small children."
"Uh... you have kids?" She shudders uncomfortably. "Okay, I guess. Enjoy it."
I want to buy this Primer.
[Leave.]
You see a colourful primer. The title reads: "A Primer for Small Kids."
I'm not sure what you're planning to get from this. It's meant for babies. Literal babies.
Steal the Primer.
You peek at the storekeep, waiting for her to be distracted. When she's not looking, you deftly swipe the small booklet off the shelf and stuff it in your pocket.
Slowly, you move your hand towards the small book. Before you even can reach it, you're interrupted:
You now proudly own a primer book for small children which, to be honest, barely cost anything.
"Sir, please, no touching the merchandise."
The lieutenant coughs sharply, then whispers: "Let's not. Defrauding small business owners is not our *thing*."
"Okay. Cool."
Several maps have been attached to a bulletin board hidden inside the alcove. They're held up by small pins. The board has come loose from one corner.
[Leave.]
Look at the map of Insulinde.
Look at the map of Revachol.
Steal it instead.

dialoguetext: The maps look old and faded. Your eye catches a map of Insulinde, a map of Revachol, and a map of Martinaise.
She nods. "Always good to be informed of your surroundings."
You peek at the storekeep, waiting for her to be distracted. When she's not looking, you deftly rip the map off the bulletin board and pocket it.
Slowly, you move your hand towards the map attached to the board. Before you can even reach it, you're interrupted...
Look at the map of Martinaise.
"Storekeep, can I buy these maps?"
"I'm sorry, officer, the map of Martinaise is the only one available. The other two are not for sale anymore... and besides, you could scarcely afford them."
It's not really a map. It's a tourist thing -- a picture postcard with buildings on it, drawn from an isometric perspective. A date in the upper right corner says: '48.

This large map displays archipelagos. You see a constellation of small dots on the light blue emptiness of the Insulindic ocean. The largest, in the northeast, is "Le Caillou" (you are here). Another, far away in the southwest -- "Semenese Islands (Ile du Fantôme)".

Ozonne, Laurentide, Face-a-la-Mer, Archipelagos, North Arcade Islands... all just specks of dust on the vastness of the Insulindic. On the edges of the map, the colour fades into a blur of dotted lines. Black and white.

Couron. It's somewhere to live. Not bad. Then there's Jamrock -- it's *bad*. People shouldn't live there, but they do. Then Faubourg -- it's almost *as* bad and much larger. Then Coal City. It's the worst.
Still, it's detailed. Could be pretty useful for scouting ahead. You see the jagged boxes of an industrial harbour, even the Whirling-in-Rags there...
You're now the proud owner of a map of Martinaise, which, to be honest, did not even cost that much.
The lieutenant coughs sharply, then whispers: "Perhaps not. It's against RCM policy to defraud small business owners."
"Sir, please, no touching the merchandise. These old maps are... relics of the past."
"They're quite valuable, though they might not look it. The map of Martinaise is 90 cents, though."
"Why is the one of Martinaise so cheap?"
"You seem to underestimate my resources, but sure, okay."
"Yes-yes. Are you interested or not?"
"That old thing? It's an out-of-date map of a tourist location that never was nor came to be..."

"From when some *design-studio people* tried to spruce the place up, four or five years ago. They also renovated the horse-statue, set up those coin-operated viewers and designed the new street lamps."
The place does not look like a successful tourist trap, does it?
"What happened then?"
"They didn't get far... for some reason. A shame the project never got going. Would be nice if someone fixed Martinaise up. All these ruins are bad for business."
"Officer, discard the thought. For your brave efforts against those thugs you may have it for free."
"I want to buy the map of Martinaise."

dialoguetext: The lieutenant nods toward it and says: "Map of Martinaise. This could work maybe?"
Martinaise!
This one *could* work for seeing where the shot came from.
What else?

You can. On Caillou -- Revachol, a single black star; on Ozonne -- Fond de l'Air and Virmandeux; on Archipelagos -- Croyant-Morain, Villiers; on Semenine -- Olduvai. And on Laurentide -- Deora Of The Seven Seas...
In the northeast a dust mite stands on the north coast of Caillou. In a bookstore. It's you.
Radiating outwards from you -- the Suzerain Revachol. With a radius of 80 kilometres. Still, the crown jewel of this isola would be barely visible.
Disintegrating into mathematics.
Squint first -- can you see *cities* on the islands?
Look at the edges.
Lost little pearls of light. Tiny fires in the dark.
850 million people live on these little dots. An oceanic world of culture and commerce, torn apart by history.
Connections to other worlds. Worlds past the Insulindian, unknown to you. You only know you've never been there.
850 million people live on these tiny dots. An oceanic world of culture and commerce, torn apart by history.

You have little idea what they are -- distant stars? gods? -- but looking at them makes you feel almost non-existent. Whatever they are, the *isolas* are immeasurably large compared to you. And very, very far away.
Perhaps they *are* gods. Gods of distance and outer dust.

The north coast of a verdant island is shattered by the delta of a river. It is the River Esperance. Countless bridges put the shards back together, connecting city blocks to river islands. *La Delta*, says a great, artificial heart in the centre, teeming with lifeforms and construction.
To the east, rolling hillsides: Le Jardin, Stella Maris, the suburbs of Saint-Batiste, swallowed up into the megacity. They sound *rich* to you. This is Revachol East.
And west of the river?
And Martinaise?

It's so small you can't even see it on the map. No... wait. There it is! North of Jamrock, the strip of coast next to the Greater Revachol Industrial Harbour. It looks downright despondent. It's almost Coal City, to be honest.
You feel you're *just* west of Coal City. Somewhere above Jamrock and close to Coal City.
No. Coal City is worse. A charred limb. Rain falls on its slick black streets. And then there's the Burnt-Out Quarter in the heart of Jamrock... is it cold in this bookstore, or is it just *you*?
No. This is somewhere to be. This is all you have, but it's still something. Streets and sodium lights. The sky, the world. You're still alive.

The display rack is brimming with worn paperbacks featuring an extremely muscular, sword-wielding barbarian on the cover. Nearly all the titles contain the word *Hjelmdall* somewhere.
[Leave.]
"Storekeep, tell me about the muscleman books."
"I want to buy the 'Hjelmdallermann' book."
Look through the display of books.
"I want to buy 'Man from Hjelmdall and the Devil Woman'."
"Oh, *Man from Hjelmdall*. A very popular series of adventure novels." She looks at the book with some disdain. "They're awfully immoral and violent books."
"Blood and violence, scantily clad women, epic narratives, all those mystical things he encounters. They're bound to grab those with little imagination and nothing to do."
"Why are they so popular?"
"Who's this Man from Hjelmdall?"
"At last, someone sensible..." She fiddles with her pendant. "However, I still urge you to buy one. Can't judge a book by the cover, they say!"
"He's a 'hero' from the frozen northlands. He travels to all sorts of lands and mainly kills people. There are hundreds of books in the series... and they sell incredibly well."
She nudges her glasses. "It *is* a best-seller for a reason."
Do any of the books call out to me?
A twinge at the back of your head makes you flinch. Your eye starts twitching.
Nothing of interest. Only silence and the cosmic background pain-radiation.
"Oh yes, certainly." She rubs her hands together. "Another good sale."

Rows and rows of Hjelmdallermenn blur your vision. You make out some titles: "Man from Hjelmdall and the Mammoth-Riders", "Man from Hjelmdall: Return to Hjelmdall", and the solipsistic "Man From Hjelmdall and the Hjelmdall Man."
Good god, how many are there?
Enough.
The display rack before you is burdened under piles of Man from Hjelmdall novels.

Maybe a hundred? "Man from Hjelmdall and the Sages at the End of the World", "Man from Hjelmdall and the False-God", "Man from Hjelmdall and the Scorched Earth", "Man from Hjelmdall: The Hjelmdall Colonies", "Man from Hjelmdall and the Swamp Beast", "Man from Hjelmdall and the Snow Crabs."
Is that all?

Not even close! "Man from Hjelmdall in Hell", "Man from Hjelmdall and the Forest of Slaves", "Man from Hjelmdall Under the Lake", "Man from Hjelmdall: Hjelmdall Burning". There's even "The Trial of Death", a Pasternal combat game book set in the world of Hjelmdallermann, and so much more.
It's symbolic of vice and sin.
Especially those leering types who seem to wear nothing but an armoured bikini. There's also some sort of a snake-lizard beast slithering around her abdomen-chest-shoulder region.
Hmm, aren't all women devil women?
"Storekeep, this book is misogynistic. How can you peddle such filth?"
"Oh, sir, I know." The storekeep apologizes immediately. "This really isn't representative of our values. But the store has to cater to its customers."
"The entire series is also *endearingly* racist, if I may add."

Your hand reaches toward a book with glossy cover art of the very muscular Man from Hjelmdall -- in *chains* -- kneeling in front of a staircase leading to a throne. A woman sits on the throne, leering at the man.
She's laughing at him. Belittling him.

Between the throne and the Hjelmdallermann lies a bonfire, casting shadows on the wall. The shadow of the woman's head-dress looks like a pair of devil horns. The title reads: "Man from Hjelmdall and the Devil Woman".
Ugh, what is it?
Ow!
Interesting.
"That doesn't sound like something I'd be interested in."
"Sounds good. Which one should I start with?"
"What does it matter? They're all the same." She rolls her eyes, then fiddles with her pendant. "However, the customer is always right, they say."
"If you're a novice of the series, I'd recommend 'Hjelmdallermann: the Man from Hjelmdall.' It's supposed to be a good introduction to the series."
Those snow crabs are worse than they sound.
"Wow, more Hjelmdall..."
Mountains of it. Heroic quantities of Hjelmdall. Roy's puny shirt is nothing compared to the *real deal*.
This is entirely, *completely* you. You have found the *right* books.
It's pulp adventure. Takes place in a faux-mythological non-place called Hjelmdall. There is no such region on the Katla isola.

The shelves are littered with romantic tales from across time and space.
[Leave.]
"Storekeep, what's on this shelf?"
Does anything more real, more *you* stand out?
Look through the display of books.
"I want buy the 'Sixteen Days of Coldest April' book."
"Oh, such wonderful, beautiful stories. Stories of love!" She sighs wistfully. "You should definitely buy these."
"To be honest, I'm looking for something more *real*."
"No-no, sir, you don't want that. That's not proper romance... romance is about overcoming adversity and finding that *single millionaire* who wants to take care of you until the end of days."
Someone thought this was a romance story, but it's actually a thoroughly excruciating work of psychological realism.
You focus on the overwhelming mass of colourful novels to find anything of note, but it only ends up with your eyes aching from the strain.
"Huh, it's in the wrong shelf... Annette's been moving things around again, has she! That girl..." She shakes her head. "No matter, I hope you enjoy... this."
As you focus on the overwhelming mass of colourful novels, a discrepancy catches your eye -- one of the books is not like the others.
On the cover of the book there's a wall of concrete buildings, with a black-and-white rainbow over them. It's written by someone from a country where even rainbows are black and white.
They also tend to feature chisel-jawed men in dark suits. It's all such... glitzy garbage.
Being a rough, *hard-boiled* detective, you can only be pleased by something more real, more *authentic*.

You see a foamy mass of pinks and reds... colourful covers filled with risqué imagery. These books are most oft adorned by women in skimpy clothes, thighs revealed... a few roses and sometimes even some pistols.
Is there anything here that calls out to me?
I think I'd enjoy reading a few of these.
No, you wouldn't. Being a rough, *hard-boiled* detective, you hope for something more real... more *authentic*.
A grey book has lost itself between all the romance. The title reads: 'Sixteen Days of Coldest April.'
Why is it out of place?
What's this all about?
Help, I don't want to do this...
Turn away, this is a bad idea.

You'd have to buy the book to be sure. But the book cover is a wall of concrete buildings, with a black-and-white rainbow covering them. It's written by someone from a country where even the rainbows are black-and-white. So it does seem like it'll be a downer.
These shelves are overburdened with books from the same series. You see the name "Dick Mullen" over and over.
"Storekeep, what's all this crime fiction?"
Look through the display of books.
Who is Dick Mullen?
[Leave.]
What do we have here? Mistaken identity...
Shelves filled to the brim with crime novels featuring the supposedly stalwart Vespertine detective, Dick Mullen.
"Oh, crime, robberies, murders..." She lowers her voice. "Even *sexual* crimes. We're fortunate to have Dick Mullen and his stories to sort all that out."
You see: "Dick Mullen on the Job", "Get Me Mullen!", "The Stalwart Adventures of Richard P. Mullen", "Dick Mullen and the Murder in the Orchard", "The Sordid Affair of Dick Mullen"...

"A Killing Is Declared", "Dick Mullen in the Murderhouse", "The Final Case of Dick Mullen" (an obvious lie), "Dick Mullen in the Clock Tower", "The Ordeals of Dick Mullen", "Dauntless Dick", "Dick Mullen's Funeral Pyre", "The Murder of Dick Mullen"...
"You're a... a police officer... apparently. You should buy *all* of these. They really do teach a person how to be a proper detective."
Crime fiction... is a disgrace. An asinine misrepresentation of the physical attributes and the arduous everyday work of actual police officers.
Sure thing.
Oh god, no.
Dick Mullen *dies*?!
Oh no, turns out he faked it to solve a case.
Are there any more?
Okay, let's stop now.
Yes. There's also: "The Dame Who Did It", "Farewell, My Mullen" (faking death seems to be a common trope in the Mullen series), "The Morbid Tales of Dick Mullen", "A Dark Tide Turns"...
"Tragedy Calls for Dick Mullen" (another one with fake death), and, of course, "Dick Mullen: The Murderer", in order to catch a murderer, Dick Mullen must *become* the murderer.
Come on, this is *not* the way real police solve crimes. The *real* police are some twenty kilometres away, sitting in an armoured motor carriage.
Your quick eye notices a small caterpillar crawling across the spine of a book. The title reads: "Dick Mullen and the Mistaken Identity."
Your attempt to grasp at the answer fails... it seems very close by, pulsating just out of reach.
After all this, you still haven't found the answer to the one question that matters: Who *is* Dick Mullen?
These books *greatly* overstate the excitement of police work, glossing over how long it takes to actually follow up on leads and eliminate dead-ends.
Not a single mention of all the stress this work creates upon the officer's *family*. Detective fiction just doesn't tell the truth at all. Now, would you like a list of the books found on the shelf?
What's more, they completely ignore the psychological hardships of, year after year, coming into contact with people during the worst days of their lives.
A couple spook novels hide amidst all the detective books. Thrilling tales of spycraft and derring-do.
"Come on, Chester, tell the story again." A bald man turns toward a lean man and pats him on the back.
"Again? Man, I tell that one at least once a month. It's not that interesting," Chester replies.

"The *fuck* it is," the bald man replies. "And these guys haven't heard it." He motions to the civilian sitting in the back seat. "You see, Chester here," he pokes his finger at the lean man. "Chester *faked his own death* once!"

"Yeah, sure came close," Chester mutters in return, then turns to the rapt listener. "Alright, so I was tailing this guy called 'Francis the Shoe'..." The inside of the motor carriage is thick with cigarette smoke. Outside, it starts to rain...
"A very fuckin' dangerous case, ain't that right, Chester? They almost got you that time."
"Hrm, of course." She shudders. "Such violence and immorality... uh, I mean, enjoy!"
"I want to buy this Dick Mullen novel."
A worn paperback from Dick Mullen's classic *hard-boiled* phase. The premise seems to be that Dick Mullen is framed for the murder of his best friend, and has just a few days to prove his innocence.
Hmm. Why does this speak to me?
Could it be the motifs of unstable identities and shocking betrayals?
That's probably right, I'm a complicated guy, full of contradictions.
No, it's gotta be something *else*.
Perhaps you're drawn to the dark and *noirish* atmosphere?
Yeah, I'm pretty intense. I'm all about that dark stuff.
No, that's not it either.
Is it because the smoking dame in the slinky red dress on the cover is giving you a hard-on?
Oh, right. That's definitely it.
See the way she's suggestively holding that pistol? That's *symbolism*.
Yeah, this is the book for you.
Then this is the book for you.
What? No. That's not what's happening.
Yes it is. The bulge in your pants is embarrassingly obvious.
Quit staring -- You're in public! There's plenty of time for that later... in the privacy of your own room.
"Something the matter, detective?"
"Nope, all good here." (Casually adjust your pants.)
"Kim, would you describe this woman as a *smoking dame*?"
The lieutenant nods. You think you detect the faintest trace of a grin on his face, but you can't say for certain.
The lieutenant narrows his eyes and contemplates the book for a moment.
"I would certainly say she fits that description, providing that's your type."
Wait a minute, all this told us *nothing* about who Dick Mullen actually is...
Sssssire, you could learn much from thisss Mullen, if you underssstood who he issss....
Sex crimes *did* pique your interest, but still -- this Dick Mullen person only gets your pleasure centres *down*.
NOTE! Reading about Dick Mullen will not actually make you a better detective.
Furthermore -- they have NO IDEA how hard it is to simply remove a body from a tree.
Relax. It's not that bad. Also, this means your bloodflow is returning to normal. Good news, really.

"Gosh, why?" One civilian looks on, amazed. The bald man bellows a reply:
A small mountain of colourful board game boxes. There are numerous types of games for all ages. A lot of shelf space seems to be taken up by Wirrâl-related merchandise.
Look through the pile of Wirrâl-related items.
"Storekeep, what board games do you have here?"
"I want to buy the *Suzerainty* game."
[Leave.]
"I want to buy the *Wirrâl* game."
"Wonderful board games, sir. 'The Viticulturist' is a classic for sure, or perhaps you'd like 'Archipelagos of Insulinde', a very educational game for those interested in geography."
"'Raubritter' is a fun game of economic competition, but can get quite intense after a while. We have games for the whole family. You can play with your children!"
"Lousy auras there!" She shudders. "No, *role-playing games* are popular among those types... you know, who're into those kinds of things. Personally, I don't like it. Not at all!"
Wow, I have children? A family?
Do I have friends? (Look at the lieutenant.)
"Wonderful choice, sir." She smiles at you. "A wholesome *family* game."
"If you say so." She gives you a curious glance. "But you better stay away from those immoral occult rituals."
Who are you going to play board games with? Do you have friends or family?
It certainly feels like whatever you are will die with you.
Are you actually friends? Or just colleagues thrown together by circumstance?
"I don't feel as if I have any kids."
"Friends are technically like family." She fiddles with her pendant, thinking.
"Look at me, who'd want to have children with me?"
"Don't be so hard on yourself, sir. You just need to clean up a bit. And technically, friends are a bit like family." She fiddles her pendant.
A towering mountain of colourful board game boxes and Wirrâl codices.

"I've heard they turn people into occult-enthusiasts. That they have rituals, where they try to summon entities. Highly immoral stuff... You can still buy them, though." She looks at the table, crossing her arms.
An endless variety of sourcebooks, lorebooks, and codices litter the table. The top-most book is titled "Welkin Compendium, Second Edition."
Hm, maybe I'm not into all this binoclard stuff.

There's a box that says: "Wirrâl. Third Edition Mega-Setting Supplements Module". The side panel notes: "A *fantastique* adventure board game. New maps and miniatures!" A sticker on it displays -- 25 reál.
Anything that really catches my eye?

There's also a large hardbound tome with intricate cover art: "The Hunters of Katuak: Boreal Creature Compendium," and a pick-your-path adventure gamebook titled "Tales of Wirrâl: Cavern of Velkraag."

dialoguetext: "*Cursed*? Who said that, Annette?" She blinks. "I will have a word with her... This place is not cursed, it has a robustly *magnetic* energy. Good for commercial activity. My business is *thriving*, sir!"
The lieutenant shoots you a sideways glance. "And I am his private partner, John... Shao. Together we run the pre-eminent spousal surveillance firm in Revachol."
"What nonsense are you two going on about? This is not relevant at all. And besides," her lip curls in disgust, "*my* husband would never do such a thing. We are proper people."
"You shouldn't be so trusting of your husband. Men are filthy, treacherous pigs."
"Mind your manners, John. This isn't the great Shao Empire, where you can talk about sex stuff so openly!"
"Alright, enough nonsense. The point is that we sometimes take on *unusual* cases."
"That's right. When not spying on the love affairs of the ultra-rich, we solve unusual mysteries by the lorry-load."
"Our sincere apologies, ma'am. No more nonsense. We're offering to assist you with your troubles, *pro bono*." Despite his apologies, there's a twinge of amusement in the lieutenant's eye.

Shao is what the Seolite Empire was called in the Occident, back when far less was known about the people. It was a barbarian Other, ever so mystical, on whom you could project any kind of exotic fantasy. The legend of it persists and a lot of people still think the 'Shao' is a thing.
Some penetrating sarcasm from your colleague there.
"This so-called *curse* is nothing more than a simple case of collective delusion."
"No, no, don't mock the spirits like that! They don't like it... it only makes them angrier. Leave it be."
"Look, ma'am, I really need to get in there. I'm a compulsive detective. I can't sleep until I've solved the mystery."
Convince her to let you investigate the Doomed Commercial Area.
Her façade has dropped. Now you see the curiosity behind the fear.
"This is nothing but fear for the success of your business given a shape."
"Too many failures for it to be a coincidence... they were not careful. I will not take such risks. Leave it be!"
"Sometimes it's necessary to resort to extreme measures."
"Dealing with ghosts is simple. You have to show them who's boss."
"It's a *proper* place to live -- one of the most peaceful neighbourhoods east of Jamrock. You may know it for its massive housing projects..."
"Who's the little girl standing outside?"
"Annette, yes. My daughter. I hope she wasn't slacking off again with her nose in science fiction! Tell me, was she at her post, doing her job like a proper girl?"
"Depends. How much do you pay the kid?"
"Good sir, what does a young child do with money anyway? No, I save it for her, as a fund. She's securing her financial future out there."
"In some more developed countries this sort of thing is two felonies. Child labour and slavery."
"Those countries will realise they've raised a lazy and spoiled generation." Her tone is decisive, not at all angry at the insinuation. "Are we done with the jokes now?"
"Is she an only child?"
"Yes, I'm afraid so. A real treat she is. It would be nice if she had..." She pauses for a second. "No, we couldn't have afforded more children really. Not in this economy."
"Ten. She's certainly very polite and helpful."
"All this pressure has made her really anxious. You know she's been chewing her nails?"
"God, ugh, I've told her not to do that. It's such a disgusting habit." Her voice is firm. "She'll get over it. Anxiety is a part of life."
Denial is the way she copes with criticism.
"Welcome to Crime, Romance, and Biographies of Famous People. My name is Plaisance." The clerk extends a greeting.
She has fine-tuned her voice to find the most welcoming approach for attracting new customers. It doesn't work.
Her face looks powdery and painted from all the make-up.
"What if I want to buy a book?"
"So what types of books do you have?"
"Everything is on the shelves, take a look yourself." She nudges her glasses. "The shelves compel you, don't they?"
She's attempting to mentally direct you towards the shelves. She only wants you to buy the goods, she doesn't care about books.
"No thanks." [Leave.]
"Do you even know what books you have for sale?"
She scoffs. "Truth be told, not really. My sister brings in most of the goods. I'm sure it's all very literary stuff, with *well-written prose*..."
"But you don't learn about the *important things* in life from fabricated stories."
"Where do you learn about the *important* things then?"
"Wait, shouldn't a storekeeper know about her wares?"
"I provide a valuable service. As long as people buy books, I'm fine." She wiggles her bony fingers at you.
"The truth is available if you just know where to look. And you have to open and free your mind to *understand*." She nods at you, cryptically.
"God, I've told her not to do that. It's disgusting. And I told *you* to mind your own business." Her voice is firm. "Clearly you have no idea how hard it is to raise a girl in this economy."
"And your husband's also involved with the bookstore?"
A glimmer of sadness blinks through the well-crafted exterior.
"We're quite busy people, you know, my husband and I. Quite busy." Her voice wavers a bit. "Children are a lot of work. You don't look like a father, so I don't expect you to understand..."
"He made the initial investment. Since then he's been what you might call a *silent partner*."
"Alright, I'll take a look then." (Conclude.)
She smiles and nods, seemingly relieved.
What in god's name is she talking about?
"Sir, I am well-educated in the commercial and esoteric arts. I know what to do and what to avoid." She nudges her spectacles.
"A dead what?" Her eyes widen with shock at the mention. "Oh my god, a victim of the curse? The curse has started killing people? It's *killing* now?!" She grabs her head with both hands.
"Most of the buildings are empty at the moment!" Her smile is wide. "It's a great opportunity to get ahead of the crowds. Better times ahead, for sure."
"I wasn't kidding when I said we're para-psychologically done! You clearly don't care about the consequences. What gives you the right?"
"Before we go on... you seem to be well off enough, can you give me some money? I feel there won't be an opportune moment to ask later."
"Sir! Don't be ridiculous. I certainly will not give you money." She gives you a disapproving look. "I would be doing you a grave psychic disfavour..."
"Ma'am, I am a renowned private investigator, a paragon of law and a specialist in all things criminal."
"Ma'am, do you know how me and my partner are known to our colleagues back at the station?"

"Once we've caught our client's spouse *in flagrante delicto*, we blackmail them and pocket the money ourselves, because that's what private investigators do. Now, I see that *you* are a married woman..."
"This is preposterous, a waste of my time and of no help to anyone." She looks displeased.
"It's not good to talk about the curse, not in detail. The negativism..." She shivers. "It's dangerous. Talking about the void wraiths angers them!"
"Most certainly not! I don't want anyone who's not familiar with the psychic arts to get involved in this mess. Stay away. Leave the spirits be, so they can return to their slumber."
Slither up to her, you silver-tongued fiend. Show her what world-class perfidy looks like!
Time to fire up the old lie machine!
"Okay, I'm willing to listen. We are set on the path... there's little else to do." She shrugs, apparently dejected.
"Do you take me for a complete fool?" She's getting irritated. "Leave it be and just go look at the books."
"And others have to suffer terrible consequences just so you can sleep at night? I think not!"
Wow. *Void wraiths*. You have new words.
"You think Dick Mullen could solve this? No way, time for a real detective..." (Flex them biceps.) "...to shine."
She gives you a curious look -- you don't really understand what to make of it.
She's into your masculine posturing! Your lean -- uh... husky and chubby brawn -- is pure animal magnetism.
Wink at her.
Do not wink at her.
"Oh for the love of... no!" She rolls her eyes, although a vague blush nearly cracks through her façade. "Go look at books instead of this nonsense."
"I am the law."
"I don't know. Nothing really. I don't have any right, I'm sorry."
"I'm a rebel -- I live by my own rules."
"We are truly private in our partnership."
"But wait, there's more!"
"How can I believe you after all that foolishness?" She looks somewhat irritated.
"It's a good offer, ma'am. I urge you to accept our help, it may be the only chance to save your business!"
"What better way, than to ask us --"
"So, are you the owner of this store?"
"I am. The proudest owner of our little shop of culture." Her voice is high-pitched, as if to give it more penetration.
"You... broke down... the back door?" She looks very sad, resigned even. "The wards... the door... it's all gone now. Dark psychic energy, leeching onto my shop..."
"I don't know what I was thinking, barging in like that..."
The woman before you scans the store, her shoulders rigid and tense. Every now and then she nudges her glasses.
"I sensed the psychic emanations from afar. The Sleeper Beyond calls out."
"How does this curse manifest itself?"

"Oh, this?" She holds the pendant in her palm. Its ochre heart glistens under the lights. "No. It's a special *Himean amulet* blessed by desert pygmy shamans with a *spell of compulsion*. It's to compel people to buy books..."
"Is your pendant part of the wards as well?" (Point at her necklace.)
"Would you like me to take the case? I could investigate, see if the curse is real." (Conclude.)

dialoguetext: "The dark sarcophagus..." (Pause dramatically.)
"Yes, yes? How was it?"
"Hold on, I actually haven't done anything yet. I just wanted to ask a few questions."
"It was a charnel house of failed business enterprises, leeching life energy from this bookstore."
"Honestly -- a dump. Nothing to see there, just heaps of garbage. Someone should let the sunshine in."
"But... what else did you find? Did anything survive? No. Of course not. Have you located the... Entity?"

"Goodness, you were already doing good browsing the shelves. Why'd you stop?" She fiddles her pendant, then waves her bony fingers directly at you: "Don't you feel compelled? Go, go -- get back there. The books await you."

"Then why are you talking to me? Everything is on the shelves to browse. Don't you feel *compelled* to buy anything?" She fiddles with her pendant, then waves her bony fingers directly at you: "See those shelves there, go, be drawn."
Quietly, she mutters to herself: "He isn't doing what he's designed to do... isn't the spell working..."
"What spell?"
"Huh?" She flinches at your remark. "Nothing. No one's cast any spells of compulsion to draw in customers. What a silly idea!"
"Don't expect my help from now on. The back door is locked and I threw away the key. I won't trifle with such forces." She fiddles with her pendant.
"Do look at the books, though. The books compel you. You *may* be able to make up for this by buying a lot of books. I hope you're a voracious reader!"
"Wonderful! Did you talk to her?"
"My precious! Her dedication brings joy to my heart." She's immensely satisfied with the answer. "If you have children, I hope they turn out as great as my Annette."
"Yes, of course."
"No, she was definitely slacking off."
"Yes."
"Not really."
"Why not? Was she not friendly enough? Were you not compelled to talk to her?"
"Great! On a scale of one to ten, how compelled were you to buy books after talking with her?"
Her opinion of her daughter depends on how well she lured you into the store.
"The way you're handling her strikes me as wrong."
"Mind your own business, sir." Her posture becomes very rigid. "In *our society*, people don't get to tell each other how to raise their children. It's none of your or anyone's business."
"Annette is quite the trooper. She's a great value-add."
"Five. I felt some interest."
"One. Not impressed."
"I'm not going to grade a human being. I don't do that."
"I guess it's better than nothing." She shrugs. "She'll have to try harder next time."
"I knew it." She sighs and shakes her head. "Shameful behaviour. She's incorrigible."
"Come now, it's not personal, it's about proper sales practices and market research." She crosses her arms. "I expect an answer."
"Oh, yes? How's my precious doing? She's a good girl."
"That *is* true -- and obviously the will of the market -- but maybe make an exception for your daughter?"

"There," she returns with a nod. "I don't know what to say to you. My husband, he tries to teach me business lessons. I have... what my mother called a *dull mind*. All this stress..." She stops, but her mouth keeps moving.
"I don't think she can do anything about it."
"Okay. Forget it." (None of your business.)
"Come on, ma'am. It's obvious she can't do anything about it. You're placing an unnecessary burden on a young child."
"Is this husband Annette's father?"

"Yes. My husband is a successful entrepreneur East of the river. If only he were more *involved* in the business we're running up *here*." She says gloomily. "No matter, soon we'll both be off for Grand Couron!"
"Wait. Grand Couron? What's that?"
"She told me she doesn't go to school anymore."
"Yes? Oh, I hope I can make it up to her. She's my precious kid."
"What you're doing is wrong. Even I know that, and I usually don't know anything."
"Oh," she exclaims with some irritation. "Shameful girl, what is she up to this time?!"
"No, I must've been mistaken. She's right outside, very attentive, yes."
"This is actually none of my business, let's talk about something else."
"Okay.... Let's change the subject."
"I'm here to dismantle the free market and abolish child labour."
"I don't know, I just walked right in here instead."
"I'm not interested in talking to a kid."
"I was afraid she'd call me a f****t like all the kids around here."
"Sir! Watch the language." She crosses her arms. "My child would never do such a thing."
She lightens up. "Oh yes, okay, that makes sense. It's working then... yes. Do browse our books, sir!"
"What's wrong with her?" She shakes her head. "Can't she do anything right?"
She rolls her eyes. "You must be kidding, there's nothing like that happening."
"Oh. I guess I was mistaken."
"Indeed." Her voice is decisive and sharp as a knife. "Are we done with the jokes now?"
Slap the cuffs on her!
Such criminal behaviour would not happen in more developed countries.
"I formally reprimand you for your corrupt activities."
She raises an eyebrow. "Oh, of course, officer. Good work. Are we done with the jokes now?"
"As a young girl should be. With the proper attitude she'll have a bright financial future."
"She can, if she has enough *willpower*. This is what's called *growing pains*. Life isn't easy, life doesn't give breaks."
She stands stiff and severe, silently fuming. Ten or so seconds pass without change.
It sounds like both the husband and the mother treat her the way she treats Annette.
"You're like Annette to your husband. And your mother."
"Oh..." She nudges her glasses nervously. "Well. My mother was horrible, of course, absolutely *perverse* energies around that person, but my husband..." She shakes her head.
"Alright. I had something else in mind." (Conclude.)
The woman looks aloof, her features much softer. Occasionally she glances at her daughter's silhouette.
"Yes, we've had quite enough fun here, right." The lieutenant taps his foot.
Your head feels light and dizzy... a cold breeze caresses your flesh.
Shudder, let it pass.
What's going on?
Monstrous buildings loom over Grand Couron. A cold wind howls in the empty halls of homes built upon delusions.
Why?
There is no life in Grand Couron. No one can afford to live there.
"Why not?"
"All the pressure has made Annette really anxious. You know she's been chewing her nails?"

dialoguetext: "She's been too busy, helping me here, so she's studied at home this trimester. This is a temporary solution, of course." Plaisance nods.
I don't want to say all that.
Yes, you do.
You're right. What could go wrong?
No. It's really stupid.
"Oh my god, will you stop with the  incessant yammering? It's too much." Her palm goes to her face. "If you wanted the key to the back door you could have just asked for it."
"Enough funny business. Will you just give us the key already?"
"Absolutely not!"
"Fine, I'll ask for it. Can we have the key?"
"But I don't want to ask for it, asking is beneath me."
"Oh? Well good for you, because you're not going to get it anyway!"
"Not this nonsense again. I already said *no*!"
"I detected psychic emanations from within and was compelled to investigate."
"What have you found?" She seems anxious. "And also, do buy the books. There may be *teachings* in them."
"You've hurt yourself now! I told you not to mess around back there. What are you even trying to accomplish, you fool?!"
"Absolutely not." She is mortified. "It's more dangerous than I ever imagined. I definitely can't let you in now, we have to contain it."
"Enough of this mumbo-jumbo, I have a decomposing body rotting away as we speak. Just let me in!"
"The presence is real in this building. I have felt it. It lurks. It hungers. But I can bring peace."
"I had a few more questions about the curse..."
"Okay, but please, only a few questions." She peers at the curtains. "You wouldn't want to disturb the spirits..."
"Why didn't you just tell me right away it's the curse?"
"There are numerous spells cast throughout the store. I had the books anointed with a different inducement spell, for example." She nods. "It's guaranteed to boost sales *fifteen percent*!"
"*Extreme violence*. The wards only make them invite their ghost-families. And the Semenese want that because they're in league with the ghosts."
"What does that even mean?"
My liege! You know what this case calls for? A para-detective!
"You're right..." She is mortified. "It's worse than I imagined. We definitely have to contain it now!"
Yessss, this is your chance! This is your chance! Only a *para-detective* can solve this case.
"You're alive and well! Don't keep me waiting now. What's in there?" She's looking for the right expression. "In that dark sarcophagus?"
"Oh." Her disappointment is obvious. "What about?"
Tell her how *ghasssstly* it was! You know it's what she wantssss to hear...
"I knew it!" A tremor runs through her. "Oh, such horrors that have been thrust upon us..." She shakes her head.
"I have returned from the void. A para-detective from a long line of para-detectives."
"Ma'am, I came here to help. I've handled *paranatural* situations before."
"Are you sure?" She looks sceptical. "Don't think I haven't seen *charlatans* before..."
"You're no para-detective. You look nothing like one -- and you're clearly a drinker. Pardon me for being so blunt, but..."
"You see, it's necessary to drink the *spirits* in order to contact the *void*."
"I used to live on the shadowy isles... the wild wisemen taught me their rituals."
"I admit, I've had my share of drinks, but only because *mediation* is so draining."
"Al Gul hails from beyond the veil, ma'am. Al Gul guides the way."
Wait, what if I don't want to lie...
You're not *lying* -- you're giving her peace of mind. The meanssss are thus jusssstified.
"I know the Remote Viewers Division, they have taught me perception beyond this world."
The lieutenant keeps his usual stony calm. He silently picks out his notebook.
"Just ask my partner, Kim. He'll vouch for me."
"Oh, uh..." the lieutenant mumbles in minor confusion. He has not been listening closely enough. You've put him on the spot.
"Certainly so, ma'am. I can assure you my partner is eminent in this *particular* field."
"I am the Void-Revenant. I have the powers to de-bad all the bad energies."
"I should have realized... a pattern lies within the fabric. The hand of fate guides us, our meeting couldn't have been mere chance."
She shudders. "I'm not sure I can trust your claims -- honestly, you look like a bit of a drinker. I'm sorry for being so blunt, but..."
"No, it simply can't be!" She looks at you with some puzzlement. "How can I trust you? You're clearly a heavy drinker, don't get me wrong..."
"How do you... *know* all this?"
"Your wards brought me here in the first place. The Semenese blood also runs through me."
"Oh my, I should have known! You do have that *wild-man* look. Our meeting couldn't have been mere chance!"
"You're part Semenese?! Oh, it means our meeting couldn't have been mere chance... the hand of fate guides us."
"If you promise, good officer... then." She shuffles nervously. "You might be our last hope. Do you swear it?"
"But... I am not the only one at risk, I have to think of my daughter. You are certain you can help us, keep us safe? I can't allow any *collateral damage* to hit us."
"No problem whatsoever, your family is safe, the phantoms are no match for me."
Wait... That's it? I don't want to say that!
Stop being such a fussy prude! You can't convince her without liessssss.
Okay, I guess I'll give it a try: "Crime Bros." (Nod at Kim.) "We're called *crime bros*, my partner and I."
No, it's really stupid.
"Sir, I really don't have time for your jokes. The situation is very serious."
Blech! You deny your own Revacholian blood for the sake of a lie!
Hey now, hey. Hey! Hey. You need the booze to focus, alright?
Perhaps you truly *are* the one to deliver this woman from the doom...
(A hand on your heart.) "On my honour."
"Actually, I'm not really feeling the vibe anymore... The psychic force has left me."
"Come now!" Her eyes light up. "Enough with your jokes, no backing down anymore. Do I have your word?"
These ideas are all worthless.
Thy sweet tongue drips not with honey today... yet, try thou must!
Goddamnit, you're completely unhelpful.
'Tis a poor craftsman who blames his tools!
"Nothing... I'm just terribly clumsy sometimes, sorry." (Rub your aching forehead.)
"I thought it was obvious: I tried to smash through the door by using pure physical force."
"I'm trying to find a way to the fridge downstairs -- it's an urgent police matter."
"You're only making things worse! Stop it. Be compelled to look at the *books*." She fiddles with her pendant. "*Go to them*!"
"Look, I've got this decomposing body I *really* need to put in a fridge down there."
"You fool! You've gone and unleashed unimaginable evil, all for the sake of a refrigerator!"
"I suppose... it's all over now?" Her shoulders slump, as if a heavy burden lies on them. "I guess there's no escape."
"It was the only way to get this investigation going."
"Well, I've looked around... I can tell you what I saw."
"You... broke down the back door?" She looks sad and confused. "Why? I gave you the key."
"I hope you can find the solution quickly. The wards are broken, the passage has been opened..." She shudders. "Now tell me, what's back there?"
"Real men don't need keys."
"I'm not sure, I don't know what I was thinking."
"The door was giving me shit."
"Never mind, I had other questions."

"Oh my god, things have gotten out of hand!" She unloads immediately: "I thought the psychic stuff was bad, but the crime... it's even worse. I haven't been able to come to work for *three days*, the shop has been locked. No sales, gang-bangers running around, shooting everyone. I know I shouldn't have bought a shop in this *ghetto*."
"In the meantime, do buy the books. As many as you can. They won't be here for much longer." Determination shines in her eyes. "Is there anything else I can help you with?"
A golden pendant hangs around the woman's neck, in the shape of what looks like a tiny fish head trapped in amber.
"A curious pendant you're wearing." (Narrow your eyes mysteriously.)
"Oh yes, helps to have an anchor in these times." She clutches the pendant and narrows her eyes as well.
"One has to earn one's success, even if one is a police officer. Handouts are nothing but manipulation, all they do is make you dependent."
Certainly there are good things to be said about dependence.
"It would forge ties between us working people -- good practice for fighting our common enemy."
"You misunderstand me. I'm a powerful feudal lord. I demand tribute. This is about traditions."
"Damn, you're right. What kind of a business relationship would that kick-start?"
"Excuse me, I don't even know why I said that. A lapse of professionalism that does not represent my values."
"Now hey there." She raises her finger. "Sounds like someone isn't taking responsibility for the energy they bring into this space..."
"Now hey there." She raises her finger. "Sounds like someone isn't taking responsibility for the energy they bring into this space..."
"Exactly. In this kind of a business relationship I could come and critique your work any time. I could demand things from you, limiting your creative freedom."
"Fighting, enemy... my philosophy is everyone just getting along."
"Tribute, power... these are not the traditions we're used to in this part of the world."
"We wouldn't want that."
"Oh my. Of course." She looks at you and adds, "What a man."
She's energetically impressed with you and your values. This is sincere. She's the kind of person who believes in telling a man that he's *quite the man* while he's being very manly.
"It's always nice to see you here. You bring good energy."
"Hey, I'm the one who got shot here. In the leg... *and* in the shoulder!"
"Uh... I'm the one who got shot here, ma'am."
Say nothing, stare at her.
"And you... oh my god, just look at you! It looks like even the *police* can't take care of all this. Someone should do something about this." She rubs her pendant between two fingers, thinking.
"Oh my god, even the *police* can't take care of all this. Just look at you! You're a wreck. Someone should do something about this." She rubs her pendant between two fingers, thinking.
"Oh my god, even the *police* can't take care of all this... just look at that limp! Someone should do something about this." She rubs her pendant between two fingers, thinking.
"Maybe... I should close the bookstore and open a *psychic studio*! Yes!" She nods to herself. "It makes sense. Crime is the sixth element, you see. The darkest element."
"I could teach people to protect themselves against bad energies and to fight crime."
(Nod.) "Sounds like a plan. Life must go on, after all."
"Honestly, I'm not sure what to think of it."
"A 'psychic studio'? This is even worse than a bookstore in Martinaise..."
"No need to be modest, good officer. You've convinced me -- it is a great idea! Thank you for the inspiration."
"No, no... you're right, officer! You've convinced me -- it is a great idea! Thank you for the inspiration."
"Exactly. It's a brilliant idea. Thank you, officer! I'm going to start drawing up business plans right away."
"Yes, what Martinaise really needs is more vigilantes roaming the streets."
"You *have to* let me to the cellar. There's something I desperately need from there."

dialoguetext: "Who, what? I don't understand what you're talking about. I can't, in good conscience, risk releasing the *bane of doom* upon all because you need something from the cellar."
"In fact," she pauses to think, "It's odd how many of these troubles started with her departure. How do I know she's not behind the curse?! We definitely have to contain it now."
"Have you ever thought about a sale? Maybe this could lure in some customers."

"So we just give up?"

"He could be a witness, him or his *Sunday friend*. It's worth looking into..."
"He could be a witness. And either way we need to look into that *muscular type* who's asking about our case..."
"He could be a witness. We shouldn't rule out the possibility..."

"What's your friend's real name? Did he see something?"

Time to bring out your secret charm: tears and begging! Show him your *emotional* side, throw yourself before his very feet like a dog!

"As you wish." He takes another drag.

The God Himself has denied you absolution.
"I get it. Nothing wrong with looking good."
He gives you a honeyed smile, before shaking off the cigarette ash.

A downy blanket of white to cover up the miserable poverty of the scene.

"There won't *be* a next time." He takes a last drag of his cigarette, before stubbing it out in the balcony snow. "I really need to get going."
"Good luck with the investigation."

She's truly desperate -- she thinks she has no other options. You need to give her options.
You should know the words to say. You've been here yourself. So why is it not coming to you?

"You're under arrest!"

(Whisper over your shoulder.) "You okay, Kim?"

"Don't know anything about it. No one's been around since I set up camp. But I'm sure I'm not the first vagabond to..." Her voice trails off into white noise in your head. It feels like an aneurysm approaching.

"When I threatened to arrest her, Klaasje broke... she told me everything."
"How did you manage to... come up with a plan? So quickly?"
"Who ratted me out, by the way? Was it Titus? No," she hesitates, "he wouldn't have broken first..."
She looks shaken. She wasn't surprised to be ratted out -- but *framed*?
So she says she didn't do it -- and she doesn't trust you. Is it you specifically or the Citizens Militia that she distrusts?
"Klaasje said... you seemed to have a plan... prepared when you got there."
"I know you're feeling pretty uncomfortable right now. Don't move too much or fight it. That'll just make it worse," says the shadowy figure by the machine.
"Do you know about the... bunker... next door?"
"Fine, if you really want to talk, I can dial it down. I've also got a gun, by the way." She steps reluctantly out of the shadows. The pain lessens.

"If you've got something *really* important to say, you can do it through the white noise."

Cover your ears!

(Yell through the static.) "You're under arrest!"

"Right, sure. You don't know."

"I'm no one's... agent. I don't even know who La Puta Madre is!"

She doesn't want to talk about this, but not because she has something to hide -- she doesn't want the guilt.
"Do you know something about the tribunal... the mercenaries are planning?"
She chuckles. "*Tribunal* is an awfully fancy word for what they're going to do. But, yeah, I was listening to their frequency. They've finished their 'investigation.'"
"Now they're going to put on a show before meting out punishment." She pauses, biting her lip. "Even though those assholes gave me up... I'm worried for the boys."
She sighs. "Yeah. The mercenaries are about to set up a tribunal and execute someone for killing Lely."
"How do you know this?"
"I was listening in on their frequency." She pauses, biting her lip. "Even though those assholes gave me up... I'm worried for the boys."
Squirm in pain.
Hold very still.
"875263... 23621837... for that special someone..."
"I know it's bad -- try not to move."
"There, there, I told you it's best not to move."
"And you -- watch out for yourselves. You seem to have a habit of walking into traps."
"They're planning to set up a trap for us?"
"Why is everyone always against me?"
"I'm guessing you don't know that a third mercenary has come to town just in time for the tribunal -- now you do."
"I'm asking myself that right now too. Anyway, I'm guessing you don't know that a third mercenary has come to town just in time for the tribunal -- now you do."

"We've checked the buoy with Klaasje's documents. I want to hear her take on why it was empty before."
"Okay -- why not. Whatever goes down might also affect her. The Union is watching her closely now..."
Not closely enough, you suspect. But still -- good idea to visit her once more.
"Do you think whatever happens will affect our cryptozoologists?"
conditionstring: (Variable["whirling.lena_intro_done"]  or  Variable["whirling.lena_main_main_hub_reached"]  or  Variable["coast.morell_greeting_done"])  and  Variable["TASK.report_to_lena_done"] == false

dialoguetext: "You mean Lena? I don't see how cryptozoology and the murder investigation are connected. But... the situation in the city will get tense for everyone."
If it gets that tense, the amateur zoologists might not be able to do their job.
"How bad do you think things could get?"
"Well... we're not responsible for what we can't predict, are we? I don't think the *entire* city will be razed to the ground." He smiles in the dark.
If you can't predict it, there's nothing you could have done.
"What do you think is waiting for us there?" (Conclude.)
"I think I see a cavern..." The lieutenant's whisper echoes down the tunnel. "Maybe more cellars? I think we've been careful enough -- we still have the element of surprise."
I wouldn't be so sure. You haven't exactly been sneaking.
"Or... maybe not." He puts his hand to his holster. "Either way, once we go deeper, there will be no turning back."
It's a minor point. Don't worry too much about this. There are bigger fish.
"You mean Morell? I don't see how cryptozoology and the murder investigation are connected. But... the situation in the city will get tense for everyone."
"I don't feel it, but..." He looks ahead, beyond the arch. "We should still be careful. There were footprints back there. And I'm pretty sure they were fresh."
Let's *try* not to worry, he thinks.
"We've still got a date with The Pigs... and *my gun*."
"We absolutely cannot skip that appointment." His face is stone. "Consider that 100% confirmed. I fear you'll need your gun for this..."
His hand rests on his holster. It's not enough -- you need a gun in your hand, too. *Your* gun.
"Maybe we should finish looking into the Speedfreaks FM mystery?"
"If you want to do that, then yes. We'd be advised to finish every lead. I don't think we'll have the chance to after..." He looks down the dark tunnel. He does not finish the thought.
"Is everything all right in there, officer? Could you let me in?"
A moustachioed and mutton-chopped man, amateurishly depicted, gazes at you with sad eyes. A plaque reads: "K. Mazov." There is a spider web in the lower left corner of the portrait.

Kras Mazov (nom de guerre), was an economist and a theoretical historian. He was a leading figure in the Graad side of the Turn-of-the-Century Revolution, where he headed the Eleven Day Government. Mazov is considered the father of scientific communism (Mazovian thought or Mazovianism).
"Who is K. Mazov?"
"Look, Kim! It's Comrade Mazov!"
