dialoguetext: "Well, my amnesiac friend, Mazov is the father of scientific communism. His theories about economic history greatly influenced -- some would even say *sparked* -- the Antecentennial Revolution."
"So my comrades were here."
"So... this must have been the hiding place of some antitraditionalist murderers?"
"So his ideas tend to stir up trouble?"
"So... this must have been the hiding place of some naive leftists?"
"Why would someone have a portrait like this?"
"Yes, I can see that. Looks like some communists were hiding out here. They left a long time ago."
The lieutenant does not seem to share your enthusiasm.
"Yes. Looks like some latter-day radicals were hiding out here. They left a long time ago."
"Some radical -- or radicals -- were hiding out here. They left a long time ago."
Brush the dust off the portrait.
Wonder: who is K. Mazov?
The man in the portrait looks back at you silently. He knows who he is, but he isn't telling.
Years' worth of dust is shaken off. The full head of hair, matched by an ample moustache and sideburns, look a bit silly.
"Yes, some radical -- or radicals -- were hiding out here but left a long time ago."
"Yes. And it looks like some latter-day radicals were hiding out here but left a long time ago."
"If you wish. At any rate, looks like some Mazovians were hiding out here but left a long time ago."
"Looks like some radical -- or radicals -- were hiding out here but left a long time ago."
The lieutenant does not seem to share your enthusiasm.

Someone crouches, heels digging into wet sand. Hands sweep across the sand, grains sticking to the frayed skin of the fingertips. An old man sits on a slab of concrete and taps his fingers against the glass of a scope... you shudder.
"Maybe I should move in here. Seems cozy."
"What's this still doing here?"
"What most people think of as *history* has a tendency to linger in run-down neighbourhoods. Martinaise being what it is, no one has gone through the trouble of cleaning out the old bunkers."
"I won't stand in your way -- but only after we're through with this case."
"A long time ago? How long?"
"Half a century? This was probably part of the network of defence posts the communards built against the amphibious landing." He looks around.
"I think the purpose of this bunker was to produce propaganda. It would have had radio equipment back then, but that's all been looted."
A good hiding place for someone who's up to no good.
"Could someone have stopped through here recently?" (Conclude.)
"You mean, like Ruby? No. I think we've stumbled on a piece of history." He looks at the dust.
"Could it be connected to the Mazov bust we found in the student's room?"
"Millions of depictions of Mazov have been produced. They're not all connected -- besides, that looked like some student. The youths always go for this kind of stuff..."
Could this have been the killer's hideout, and this narrow window -- the point of origin of the shot that killed the mercenary?
This does look like an *embrasure*, a slit made for shooting out of.
Peek out.
Outside the window -- another day. The beach sand soaks up the drizzling rain, growing darker and darker.
Outside the window -- desolation. Snow falls softly onto the coastal sand, where it melts almost instantly. On rooftops, it lingers.
Outside the window -- the day is clear, and as mild as can be in early spring.
You hear the rain's susurration across the sea water. The night shudders.
In the darkness, you can barely make out the falling snow. It settles, making the night still quieter.
The lights of Martinaise shine coolly in the clear night.
Would this have been a good hideout for a sniper?
No, it's not. No matter how you crane your neck, you can't see the whole of the Whirling-in-Rags, and certainly not the relevant segment of the top floor.
"It's a great place to hide, certainly, but there hasn't been anyone here in ages."
"It's a great place to hide, certainly, but there hasn't been anyone in here for ages."
It's a good place to hide, but doesn't look like anyone has stayed here in a while.
It's definitely a good place to hide. You barely found it yourself.
Is it feasible to hit a target in the Whirling-in-Rags from this window? (Conclude.)
"Kim, I can't see the Whirling-in-Rags... The shot didn't come from here." (Conclude.)
"Indeed. No one could get a clear view. Well, at least we've been thorough. I like thorough."
The lieutenant's voice betrays a slight disappointment, which he glosses over by reasserting control.
"In fact -- I think we're done with this bunker." He looks to the exit. "After you, officer."
A thick journal. The cover is worn, like someone used to carry it around in their back pocket.
Unwind the strap. (Move on.)
Put the journal away. [Leave.]
The thick journal bound in brown leather is full of candour and diagrams.
Flip through the pages.
The journal falls open. About two thirds of its ruled pages have been filled.
Study the handwriting.
Examine the cover.
It's made of full-grain leather. The lower left corner of the back cover sports an embossed brand name: "SCHNELLER."
Schneller is a stationary brand from Gottwald beloved among architects and engineers.
She's got good taste and must have taken whatever she recorded here seriously.
She had good taste and must have taken what she recorded here seriously.
It's a mix of logistical notes, diagrams, and personal reflections, all dated.
How far back do the entries go?
What kinds of logistics?
Anything personal?
The large cursive of someone who writes quickly and confidently.

The first entry is from August 2nd of last year. It reads simply: "I know my position is precarious. All I can do is make myself as useful as I can while looking for a way out. (Remember: no one is indispensable.)"
Hard to tell exactly -- it's mostly noted down in code. Looks like contact information, quantities, directions.

Short, wry observations of people and places -- probably a way to pass the time on the road. Also, what appear to be attempts to sort through some difficult decisions. There are a few passages with many questions in them.
"There could be useful information about local operations in those notes. We have a junior sergeant at my station who's good with codes -- I can give this to her after we finish this."
The way some of those question marks trail off into ellipses -- she was going through a tough time.
(Look at the cover again.)
What did she write the day Lely died?
Nothing on March 4th... March 5th, though: "Well, *that's* bound to come back and bite me in the ass. I'm bad at this -- loyal to a fault. Except... But that's another matter entirely."
Anything about... La Puta Madre?
That name isn't mentioned as far as you can tell.
What's the most recent entry? (Conclude with journal.)
What are the diagrams of?
Esoteric radio technology. The most recent ones probably pertain to the Latitude Compressor: sketches, calculations of distance and density. You make out a familiar spiral shape.
The most recent entry is from today. It reads:
Read the entry from March 9th first.
Read the entry from March 12th.

"Great. M's peone is coming to town, no doubt to investigate the lynching, but also -- I feel it in my gut -- to finally put a bullet in my head. While I'm napping in my lorry or on a smoke break... Well, I won't stick around just to twist my own neck by constantly looking over my shoulder."

"Been holed up here for three days now. I'm used to being alone and all, but -- I don't know when I'll be able to leave, or if I'll be ratted out. They *will* rat me out, of course. I've made it a point to believe in the best in people (the boys, for example), but -- experience tells me..."
"Then again, isn't that what I've been doing ever since I got the call."
Things played out just as she had feared. Except *you* didn't shoot her.
Were you *supposed* to find her, even apart from the investigation, then? On M's request? No, you wouldn't do something like this. This must be a mistake.
It's in you to do something like this -- kill her. Physically at least. You could pull the trigger if you had to.
You didn't follow through. You should have shot her in the head.
Goddamn right, I should have.
No, I couldn't.
What a coincidence...
Yes, you could. You'd pull it one, two, three times -- and watch her fall.
I'm okay with the idea.
Is it? Can you be sure? What if you are secretly being manipulated by La Puta Madre as you pursue this investigation. What if he wiped your memory on purpose?
That's a good, pragmatic approach.

"Did M feel truly betrayed by me? I was feeling threatened -- he'd have to know if he threatened people, they'd take measures to protect themselves. Even I know that. Economic measures first of all. Gotta make a living, right. I can still hear his voice in the receiver, taste the plastic..."
The entry ends abruptly.

"Even when I leave here (if I leave here alive) -- what's my next move?... Staging a lynching is a crime, even if I'm not accused of murder on top of that. Forever on the run? Not really my idea of the open road. 

Man, I was really looking forward to winning."
Too late to do that now, *assassino grande*! Better start looking over your shoulder now.
"The head of a major Jamrock gang specializing in drug production and trafficking -- a very bad person."
"Could have been Titus. Then again..." He pauses to think.
"Kim, am I really a La Puta Madre agent?"
"It looks like she might have been... framed?" The lieutenant taps on the page.
"No, I don't think you are." He looks you straight in the eye for a moment, then sighs. "Ask someone in your precinct if you want to be sure."
"She was in plenty of trouble even without the murder charge." He looks down. "Still, it's a nasty business."
"Who *is* La Puta Madre?"
"So she died for nothing?"
"Either way, we need to keep an eye on him. Somewhere along the way, we might have been fed a lie or two..."
"Seems plausible."
"I don't know..."
"Maybe she had an accomplice. Either way, we need to keep an eye on her."
"No, it's dirty."
"She killed the merc, then turned the gun on herself -- case closed. It's so tidy!"
He's not 100% sure you're not indebted to this very, very bad person.
Kim's posture is unusually rigid -- he's used to this sort of thing, but he's not particularly happy about being used to it.
"Then who do you think killed Lely?" (Conclude.)
"But no one heard the shot..."
"Klaasje was the one who pointed the finger at Ruby. Perhaps she was trying to steer us away from herself? Or..." He stops to think.
"I wouldn't go so far as to say that -- we have other reasons to arrest her." He frowns.
"One thing is for certain: We have business back in the Whirling-in-Rags. Questions to ask. We should get to it."
"Seems plausible."
"I don't know..."
"Besides, I'm not sure her life as a fugitive is going to be much better than with us."
"Either way, we need to keep an eye on her."
"But no one heard the shot..."
"If she didn't do it, then maybe it's good that we didn't catch her?"
"Maybe there's a Hardie boy we've yet to meet who acted as his accomplice? Either way, we need to keep an eye on him."
"I don't think she killed the mercenary." The lieutenant taps on the page. "It looks like she might have been... framed?"
Perhaps too confidently -- many phrases and even paragraphs have been crossed out, with tiny corrections scrawled above and in the margins.
"We could learn a lot from this."
"It's good she left in a hurry. We could learn a lot from this..."
Professionalism is his coping mechanism.
Staff issues, always tough on the leadership. You smell traces of betrayal.
She is referring to betraying her previous employer. Does this suggest she did it in self-defence?
Small wonder -- would you talk about La Puta Madre in your journal? You do see an 'M' though -- La Puta Madre? 'M' is mentioned on March 9th and March 15th.
"What about this 'M'?" He points at the page you're staring at. "Could this be La Puta Madre? Here: March 9th and March 15th."
Not now.
"The call"? Did M call her personally? Why?
This is not me. I wouldn't do something like that.
Maybe it's the old you? Or maybe she was just paranoid...
On purpose? That's pretty far-fetched.
Am I sure this is a mistake? Look at me.
This is a coincidence. I would never kill people for a mob boss.
Whatever you may *look* like, you don't *feel* like a hired assassin.
The thought steadies your nerves. The journal stops shaking in your hand.
That must have been one hell of a conversation.
The call was a courtesy. He must have held her in high regard to personally tell her he knew about her plan to run drugs for the competition.
"No mention of La Puta Madre..."
This whole thing was a detour -- and a fatal one, he thinks.
That would be a first -- or a fourth -- but who's counting, he thinks. Very rarely does anyone actually get framed.
"Okay. What do you mean, framed?"
Don't get emotional.
"By the Hardie boys, by Klaasje, by us."
"T-man wouldn't fuck me over!"
You should show all this to the lieutenant, see what he makes of it.
Flip through the pages again.

"Even when I leave here (if I leave here alive) -- what's my next move?... Staging a lynching is a crime, even if I'm not accused of murder on top of that. Forever on the run? Not really my idea of the open road. 

Man, I was really looking forward to winning."
This was important to her -- when it was still hers.
You have no idea what she means. These are personal notes, don't expect to understand all of it.
No, stop... He wouldn't do that.
No, not even the old you. No you would do that.
He truly does not believe you are. Perhaps he shouldn't be so trusting...
His trust is well placed. You aren't. You can *feel* it.
Something tells you you should be extra careful from now on.
"Yes, I'm sure. And, anyway, as I said before, the shot had to have come from afar."
"Yes, I'm sure." She pauses. "In fact, the shot couldn't have possibly come from the roof -- otherwise we would have heard it downstairs."
"Hmh... No one mentioned *hearing* any shots. And a rifle like the one used would have been *loud*. She's right... I don't think the shot came from... the roof."
"Klaasje looks like... a girl in one of your posters. She seems to be *your type*."
"Not even wildflowers? May bell... for example?"
"These weren't just flowers -- they... symbols... of... Revolution." (Push through the pain.)
"But Klaasje was... mourning..."
"I never did understand why, when someone dies, a hothouse's worth of flowers has to die too."
"You don't feel... sympathy for mercs? It's hard work."
She raises her eyebrows. "Nope."
"Plenty of broken people who don't come with that kind of body count. Besides, they're paid well for what they do."
"So now I'm leaving Revolutionary symbols around... Come on."
"Okay, so you... didn't leave May bells..." (Conclude.)
"No, I did not."
"Really? Trigger..."
See her confident gaze, her toned arms -- yeah, she wouldn't have had much trouble in the intimacy department.
"There's nothing more... personal that you had against him? Perhaps his... way with women?"
"You think I was envious of his conquests? Look, pussy's not a problem for me. And definitely not a reason to off someone."
"I didn't like him. Hardened mercenaries aren't particularly likeable types."
"Would you say that Lely was... a *likeable* person?"
"And... despite everything, you helped her by staging the lynching?"
"Is that the only reason you... hung out on the roof?"
"What's... so great about her antenna?"
"Yeah. The girl seemed terrified. The merc was beyond caring what happened to his mortal coil. It was a no-brainer."
"So you're... *sure* you didn't shoot the merc... from the roof?" (Move on.)
"You... liked Klaasje *a lot*."
"Okay, let's take a... step back." (Conclude.)
"Do you like to... hang out on rooftops?"
"It's very powerful. I used it to tune into RCM frequencies. That's how I knew to be prepared for your arrival."
"Who doesn't? Oh, you probably mean Klaasje's rooftop. Sure, I've hung out there. She's got this great antenna..."
"The view's pretty bomb too, but you might say the antenna was the main attraction there, yeah. Along with Klaasje."
"Do you... collect guns... maybe old rifles?"
"Sure don't."
"Did you feel... protective of the Union?"
I hate to be the bearer of bad tidings, but I don't think she's perjuring herself.
"Yeah, sure, and I didn't like Wild Pines sending in those foreign hirelings -- me and a fuck-ton of other people around here."
"I have other questions." (Conclude.)
"My type? She's everyone's type. She's *your* type. Are you sure you're not the one who was excited about the peephole?"
"No, they're not practical. Break too often."
"I considered her a good friend, yeah."
"And?"
"She said you wanted to run... away with her."
"There are... other things I... ask about." (Conclude.)
"That's a very sentimental way of putting it. We both had *pasts* we didn't want to catch up with us. And we enjoyed listening to music together. Why not go on a road trip?"
"Where did you get it?"
"The gun store."
"What gun store?"
"Trigger-Happy Jack's."
"Never really got into weapons trafficking. Especially not old weapons -- they break too often, and you don't want unhappy customers among gun collectors."
"What did you think? That I'm going to squeal on my gun supplier? Sorry, I'm not that kind of gal."
"That doesn't... sound like the name of a real store."
"Did you leave any... flowers for Klaasje on the roof?"
"No, gifts of flowers and candy aren't really my style."
"I see it's a front-loader. Do you have another... gun somewhere?"
"Look, I'm not aware of any hole in Klaasje's wall. And if I had been, I would have told her to get it sealed -- that's what friends do."
"I'm not following your clever insinuations, detective."
"It's just, the hole in Klaasje's wall is.. pretty suspicious..."
"I know you don't like old things, but do you... sell antique rifles on the side?"
"A Nachtwey 80 front-loader. Two-barrelled -- not really what you were looking for, I'm guessing."
"But you wanted to be more than just *friends*."
"Oh, so that's where you were going with this." She shakes her head. "Do I *really* seem like someone who would do something as lame as committing murder out of jealousy?"
"I can't quite tell... what *kind* of gun is it?"
"Is peeping... one of your hobbies?"
"You have a gun."
"There's a... hole in the wall. You can see into Klaasje's room... I wouldn't blame you if you've.."
"So you *haven't* been.. watching Klaasje through a hole in.. wall?"
"Klaasje said... you may have used the *peephole* in her wall to spy on her..."
"Damn. That girl's pretty, but not *that* pretty. In fact, no one's pretty enough to waste time skulking about the Whirling, drilling holes in walls..."
"If I want to stare at a pretty girl, I can pick one up at a bar -- or, worst case scenario, look at a naughty photo. Who has time to go skulking about the Whirling, drilling *holes* in walls?"
"Wow. Pissing, pinball, and now peeping. I'm just not following your insinuations, detective."

"Nope. Look, she has an *effect* on people. That je ne sais quoi that makes it impossible not to look at her when she walks into the room -- and very difficult to look away. But -- travel enough, and you realize..."
(Wince.) "There's other evidence I want to ask you about." (Conclude.)
"Yeah. *Evidence*."
"Do you have an... alibi? For when Lely was shot?"
"Man, I was with the boys the whole night. I hope they at least bothered to impress *that* upon you."
"They did say you left to take a... really long leak. Fifteen minutes."
"There were... ten minutes they couldn't account for."
"You mean, the length of a toilet break? That wouldn't even have been enough time."
"Yeah, and I'm sure they also made some FUNNY remarks about it -- they always do. I've driven a lot of long haul and chugged a lot of beer, man."
She scoffs. "Can't do either without some power of mind over bladder. And, anyway, that wouldn't have been enough time."
"Our investigation..." (wince from the pain) "has shown that fifteen minutes was *just* enough time to commit the murder."
"Wow, now I'm curious. Please, explain."
So you know she's not an antiques enthusiast. Not my jurisdiction, man, but it also doesn't sound like she used that secret route. At all.
She looks you in the eye impassively, making it clear that she's not planning to comment on the matter any further.
That's a pretty good question, actually. She clearly doesn't know anything about the secret passage.
"Why are *you* so hung up on elevators?"
"Why not?"
"Not murder mysteries, either, if that's what you're thinking."
"Wait..." (wince from the pain) "what kinds of mysteries interest you, then?"
"Not particularly."
"Do you or don't you?!"
"Yeah, and probably some ghosts from the time of the Suzerain. I'm not really interested in supranatural mysteries."
"I'm not really into old shit for old shit's sake."
"Not even..." (grab your head) "quaint old rickety ones?"
"What about... elevators? Do you like *elevators*?"
"The fuck do elevators have to do with anything?"
"That's a shame... because I happen to be a para-natural detective."
"Play... pinball much?"
"Cool. They sent a ghost-cop after me. Congratulations."
"No, not since I was 14 and hanging out at the only diner in Dardanne. Haven't been into low-risk, no-reward games since moving to the city."
"There are some... mysterious pinball machines in some pretty... mysterious rooms in the Whirling..."
"Why?"

Somewhere on the outskirts of Faubourg, a scrawny teenage girl stands by the side of the road, greeting passing vehicles with a calloused thumb turned upward. She's tired. She wants to leave. But she knows she will come back.
"Okay then... I have other questions for you."
"Look, there's a... secret way from the first floor of the Whirling to the roof."
"I think we may have gone a little off-topic."
"And that topic was what? Staircases? Ladders?"
"Don't know it. But also..." She frowns, studying your face.
Evaluating your competence as a police officer.
"...the shot couldn't have come from the roof. Or we would have all heard it downstairs."
"She has a... point there. No one mentioned..." The pain stops him from finishing the sentence.
"I'm listening."
"Klaasje said you got very... angry when she started seeing Lely -- threatened her."
"She rejected me with some wishy-washy bullshit about how she was confused because she felt so close to me and valued my friendship so much, and how guilty she felt for leading me on..."
"I knew that wasn't the whole story, but thought, fine, I'll take it and move on."
"Yeah, one time when we'd both been drinking, I said some heated things about how dangerous her patterns with men were."
"I was a little worried she'd blow it out of proportion in her head -- all the drugs she was doing can make you feel like you're living in a Dolorian tragedy."
She touched that radiant beauty, that silver wellspring of desire?
Klaasje only said they "maybe kissed". Someone is lying here.
"Wait -- Klaasje said you only kissed..."
"Hold on, Klaasje only... likes truly buff men!"
"Then what happened?"
She rolls her eyes again. "If that's what she wants on the record, so be it. I'm not about to go into details for you to jerk off to later."
"She does know how to pick 'em."
"Okay, fine." She rolls her eyes. "I was into her. Klaasje was into me too, for a time, I know it -- we even fooled around once. And, yeah, after that I thought maybe we could make a go of it."
By the way! Dolorian tragedies are still held in high regard for innovation in language and motifs. They are also know for overwrought emotions leading to catastrophic outcomes.
"You're running... drugs for the Union. I've been through your lorry."
"So, heart-of-gold Tommy fucked me over too..." She shakes her head, slowly. "Never trust a musician."
"You're a... criminal. I can't trust anything you say."
"This means you're... already a known killer. Because *drugs* kill people!"
"You had... a financial incentive to kill the merc." (Move on.)
She scoffs. "That's your prerogative."

"Drugs don't make people abuse them; hopelessness does. As for the drug trade -- it would continue with or without me. I like to think that my efficiency as an organizer has at least prevented some internal conflicts."
"Man, it's to get *away* from all that murderous shit that I left Jamrock -- my previous employer -- for the Union."

"I got lucky being a dispatcher -- never had to do any of the *really* dirty work myself. This gun," she glances at it, "has only been used for self-defence against serious scum." She turns the knob down just a millimetre.
"But... you're threatening us with it!"
"Based on what I've heard about you -- you *are* serious scum," she responds, holding your gaze.
She's proud of her organizational abilities even now -- and trying to raise that pride as a bulwark against the desperation.

"Nope. Look, she has an *effect* on people -- or had, before you sent her off in your Moralintern meat grinder. It's impossible not to look at her when she walks into the room -- and very difficult to look away. But -- travel enough, and you realize..."
"...for the same reason that she's everyone's type as an object of desire, she's not irreplaceable."
"Oh, so that's where you were going with this."
The lieutenant watches her expectantly, occasionally shaking from the pain.
She didn't hate him, okay?
"Hold on, *no one* takes a fifteen-minute leak."
"Look, fuck you, man. I might have also stopped by the bar."

"What is she like, Ruby?"
"Is the room exactly as she left it?"

"I cleaned it, like I always do."
"One thing. Officer, if you do find her, please go easy on her..." She looks around. The air is getting colder.
She planned on fuckin' shooting herself in the goddamned head.
"I have a possible explanation in my mind."
Your hand twitches. A single bullet hidden from sight. Remember the way it slides into the barrel. The muzzle of the loaded weapon pointed at your heart -- it feels familiar, doesn't it?
"Aye? Do tell." A seagull flies overhead -- obviously a bad omen.
"It's an exit plan."
"On second thought, I'd rather not say. It's not something I want to think about."
"Exit from what?"
"That bad, is it?"
"Her life."
"No..." She tilts her head to the side, looking up at you, deep in thought. "She's a fighter."
"She's a good girl, whatever she's gotten herself mixed up in."
"Although I guess she was pretty handy with the mechanical and technical stuff. Even fixed the heater in the shack. You should be thankful for that."
The sun sets for everyone.
"I had a few more questions about Ruby..."
"What more do you want to know about that poor girl?"
"You'll never find her, you know." Her tone is without malice. "She knows the coast like the back of her hand. *You* only just arrived."
The lieutenant stops writing for a moment. He looks at you, then at the old woman.
"I wouldn't worry about that, ma'am. We're persistent."
You're not sure about the melody, but it might be South Samaran, possibly Siigayan (also known as the Apricot Suzerainty).
"I'm a cop, I don't cause trouble, I take care of trouble."
"What he said. We're cops: We don't cause trouble, we take care of trouble."
"We're not here to cause any trouble, madam."
"We're cops. We're hellraisers. Click, click. Bang, bang!"
Trouble? Say the second thing, *bratan*! Shows you got style.
"Oh, of course. Last time we saw you around here was... twelve years ago. You also came to take care of trouble then. Which you *did*... but, still, in Martinaise you're considered an ill omen."
"No, you're not. I've seen you around here before. Twelve years ago. You didn't raise any hell -- you were quite helpful, actually. But, still, in Martinaise you're considered an ill omen."
"Wait, I've been here before?"
"No, not you personally. I meant the RCM. Some of the men got into a fight, one of them killed another. Locked himself in that woodshed over there," she points to the building behind her.
"I *am* an ill omen, alright." (Proceed.)
"He was brooding, needed some help opening the door. You got it open for him and took him to think about what he'd done in a more secluded place. Somewhere more quiet."
She says it as if he was on some kind of spiritual retreat.
"If I'm considered an ill omen, why hasn't anyone told me that?" (Proceed.)
"Maybe they're afraid."
"Why?"
"Because you're an *ill omen*. But you're still welcome here as long as men with guns aren't chasing you. And maybe even then, because that's the kind of fishing village we've built."
"I'm sorry there's not a lot of room to park your motor carriage. And not a lot of houses. Or a lot of people. My kids are long gone... searching for treasure. So are others'."
"You're not. No one around here considers us an *ill omen*. People would have told us."
"You're still welcome here." She nods. "As long as men with guns aren't chasing you. And maybe even then, because that's the kind of fishing village we've built."
"What kind of an ill omen are we talking about?"
"Oh, the usual. Dark tidings. Black hound."
"The policeman." She squints at you. "What can our village do for you?"
"Our tenant, the policeman. I hope the waves don't keep you up at night. What can I help you with?"
"I got shot!"
"This is no time for jokes. Can't you see I'm in pain?"
"What do you expect? Police officers get put into dangerous situations all the time. Sometimes they get shot. It's a rough trade you're in."
"What is the song you're humming?"
"A lullaby my mother used to sing. I sang it to my kids too. It's an old Samaran children's song."
"I guess you were right. The men with guns were coming for me after all."
"I'm not sure those were the last of the men with guns, either." She nods. "There are always more coming for your kind, officer."
Convince her to sign Evrart's document.

"If you say it is," she says, shrugging.
"No, I have no idea where they heard it. They've been in earshot all week, and no radio."
"Hm..." The lieutenant furrows his brow. He looks back to the children and sighs.
"Is there anything else I can help you with?"
"Thank you, Kim."
"Must be exciting for you, Kim. Calling the station you're *accidentally* tuned into."
"I'm ready when you are." He turns his face away, toward nothing in particular.
"I'm ready when you are." He turns to the old woman. "Thank you, ma'am."
"Let's just get it out of the way as fast as we can. Contact dispatch from my Kineema and ask them to connect you to the station. Maybe they can shed some light on this."
"Anything else?" A cold breeze rushes by. The old woman smiles.
"Let's just get it out of the way as fast as we can. Contact dispatch from my Kineema and ask them to connect you to the station. Maybe they can shed some light on this."
"Anything else, now?" The old woman frowns. Her wrinkles frown with her.
"Harrier Du Bois, but call me Harry."
"Lieutenant double-yefreitor Harrier Du Bois."
"We're cops. We're hellraisers. Click, click. Bang, bang!" (Point your finger pistols at her.)
"Suliram, suliram, ram, ram..."
"Suliram yang manis..."
"Adu hai indung suhoorang..."
"Bidjakla sana dipandang manis... "
"Do you, uh, want to *talk* about what just happened?"
You get the feeling you're being handled with kid gloves because your cheeks are still soaking wet.
Convince yourself that you *didn't* melt down just now.
"Good. Controlling your emotions sounds good."
"A crygasm."
"Weakness is strength."
"That may be so, but such is Revachol and this is what is expected of us -- in Revachol."
"Thank you."
"You don't. But you *will*."
"Yes. A clever ruse. I see."
"A what?"

"In the future, could you please refrain from emoting too much on duty? The quasi-legal status of the RCM means we need to project strength twice as consistently as any other police force in the world."
"I experienced a minor malfunction. I'm okay now."
"What? Nothing happened!!"
The lieutenant blinks. "So you're saying you *didn't* break down in tears just now and nearly tear your shirt off?"
"Okay, then it isn't strength. You're right."
"I've never cried once in my life..."
"Sounds like typical macho bullshit to me."
"Uh huh."
A performance that would make the star of a radio melodrama blush.
"Okay, I'll control my emotions."
"Not when projecting strength -- then it's just weakness."
"Glad to hear it was 'minor.' Can you go on?"
"Right. I mean, who *cries* in public, like for real?"
"That's us. Revachol Citizens Militia. The police."
"Who indeed?"
"It's when you totally break down and it feels a little better afterwards. I don't know where I got the expression from. I may have just invented it."
"The RCM?"
"It was nothing." [Leave.]
The lieutenant merely nods.
"Don't worry, Kim, it was *all a ruse*." (Wink at Kim.)
Believeth in thyself, my liege! 'Twas all a clever ruse.
Thy pen of lies runneth dry. Best to simplie deny the Truth baldfacedly.
'Tis possible thou couldst persuade the lieutenant 'twas all a part of thy 'unorthodox' method. But can thou persuade *thyself*?
"That's probably a good idea."
"What's there to talk about?"
"So, what do *you* think happened?"
"Normally I'm opposed to discussing one's feelings, especially on-duty, but I think this is an exceptional case..."
"... you could torture me, abandon me, even *divorce* me, and I'd be dry as a desert, yessir." (Wipe your eyes.)
Hrmm, methinks my liege doth protest too much.
"Okay, right. Enough of this."
"Yes, I've definitely never seen you cry before, nor lent you my handkerchief to dry your tears."
"Absolutely. Superstars always get back up and try again."
"Yes. It is my duty, after all."
"The end is near anyway, I might as well see this through..."
"I can. And I'm sorry, Kim. I promise this is the last time."
"Then let's go."

"So you had a talk with Andre, and now you want to discuss things with Noid? Good." Skin shows through the holes in the speedfreak's too-large sweater. In front of him -- an open toolbox full of carpentry tools and parts.

"It's good you talked to Andre first. Gave me time to get a reading on your *sine*. Can't really talk to people before you get a reading." He runs his hand through his hair, which is combed back in mock seriousness, and continues to fiddle with some gears.
"You look like a woman with those earrings."
Noid shakes to the beat. There are no tools in his hands at the moment. He appears to ignore you.
"Okay, I'll speak to Andre." [Leave.]
"Yes. But that's what makes it an achievement."
"Why are you so suspicious about everything?"
"It's short for *paranoid*."
"My head is spinning. It's hard to keep up with the times."
"It is."

"Many non-Occidental cultures share a beat at their heart. Thus, they are closer to true, hard core life. There's just never been enough of them, and they had to rely on some extremely basic percussion."
"What if I want to speak to you first?"
"Seems awesome." (Nod in agreaance.)
No need to get over-excited about it right now. Where were you?
"A sticker... you mean the yellow one? Can you describe it to me?"
"I mean this one." (Show the sticker on your ledger.)
"Oh wow! Right on your cop ledger! You like it?"
"It's this one, are you familiar with it?" (Show him the sticker inside the ledger.)
"Yeah, it's cool."
"It's super stupid, that's what it is. I think it reminded me of myself."
Just like that the speedfreak is right in your face, his eyes burning. His comrades look on worriedly.
"It's very modern. I'd like to learn more about it."
Lord of the western plain! It is really happening, right here, the migrants are contaminating our youth!
"Seems like my creation has found its way into the legal bureaucracy. What did you want to ask about it?"
"Okay. It's a yellow circle -- the human face -- with X-es for eyes and a smile underneath. I think the X-es mean the guy is dead."
He considers this for a moment. "Yeah, that interpretation holds."
"Why describe it, if you already know what I mean?
"Maybe you're being too specific about it. Try consulting with your spinal cord."
"So I can hear you do it. Sometimes the outside gaze helps us reflect on things."
"Noid, don't bother our guest with your games."
"That was vague. Dedication, something else, superlative..."
"Piss off, Andre, me and Mr. Cop are trying to discuss art."
"You shouldn't talk like that."
"Happy to help."
"Yeah, you should be more respectful."
"So you had a talk with Andre, and now you want to discuss things with Noid?" He's stooped over his toolbox as usual, shuffling bolts around angrily.
"I don't mind a little foul language here and there."
"Right, noted, sorry. Anyway, what was it like?"
"Cool. The ban on foulness, that's the moralists' plot to alienate us from our bodily functions so they can control us more fully..."
"Thank you for clearing that up."
"Anyhow, what was the sticker like?"
"Take care, Noid." [Leave.]
Produce your ledger and show him the sticker.
Produce your ledger and show him the sticker.
"I'm thinking maybe the smiling dead guy is a symbol for communism. It's also dead, but doesn't care."
An off-handed *sorry* if there ever was one.
"The term *hard core* also denotes a strain of pornography that depicts penetration, did you know that?"
"Yeah!"
"That's a pretty hard core coincidence, don't you think?"
"I'm not telling. Let me ask you something else."
"C'mon. Okay, then." He looks surprised and a bit disappointed. "You don't have to describe it. What did you want to know about the sticker?"
"You know what I think? I think *man*, *woman*, and *child* are arbitrary divisions which serve to bind humanity to serfdom."
"Let's change the subject.
"I guess one could write an entire treatise on the thing. But what for?"
The one with the bleached hair is not really pulling rank on his friend here. He's just trying to create the impression of himself as a reasonable, moderate leader figure.
"I think we've exhausted the subject for now."
"What are you suspicious of?"

"Oh, it'd be easier to list stuff I'm not suspicious of. I'm not suspicious of sound and colour. Mechanics and chemistry also have a trueness about them. Most anything else deceives. Wants to steal your life away."
"You mentioned *true life*. What would that be like?"
"And what are the *most* suspicious things?"
"A life is true if it's free from fear and internal division among oneself. And others -- mankind has seeds of greatness in it. A germinal will come, a return to trueness. It will be hard core."
"Hey, it kind of *does* look like you." He thinks for a moment. "Surely a sign of things to come. What did you want to ask about it?"
"The original mistake was assuming that words have more being than bodies. That's what led us astray, far from our true lives. But we may yet find a way back."
"That's ridiculous."
"Alright, I'll do that."
"What's bad about cereal grain? Having enough food could be a precursor for greater things."
"Yes, having food is a means to an end. But the Left never talks about the end, only the means. Caps are likewise suckers, constantly sleepless in worry."
"Talk to Andre. No point in standing here -- the sines are really out of tune." He glances at the others.
"How would you go about *returning* to this true life?"

"Beats and bright lights to shatter falsehoods. Nerve impulses for the collective body. We are very much alike in basic structure. A hard enough beat would awaken everyone to a truer calling -- in unity!"
"They'll come in handy for fixing the church exterior."
The young man is dead serious about this.
"What's it supposed to be?"
"So you're advocating a noise-based society?"
"These are my consumer items and my means of production. I enjoy them."
"What do you do with all that stuff?"
"I should have known! You're taking after the kipts, that's why you're so wacky!"
"Enough now, Noid, you have had enough fun bothering our guest with your crazy theories. Leave him alone."
"I'd have a whole lot more stuff if I had a place where I could keep that stuff."
"A dead guy smiling."
"Well, that was certainly stimulating. I want to ask you about something else now."
It's a bit hypnotizing if you look at it long enough.
His eyes flicker.
"You have a whole lot of stuff."
"Utmost dedication. Thoughts from the spinal cord. It's a potent superlative as well."
"You're right, it's the harbinger of a new era. What would you like to know?"
Nod.
Noid is a bit disappointed it's *just* cool.
Rejection of the right-left axis, emphasis on *unity*, appreciation of some primordial mode of being -- what does that remind you of?
"I have all kinds of screws." He holds up a handful.
"Sort of like fascism then?"
"Nationalism, militarism, racism, and emphasis on a leader character are totally absent in *hard core*." The words echo through the church majestically.
The contents of the young man's toolbox are organized in a neat, yet eclectic manner. He is constantly checking out the various tools and parts and rearranging them slightly...
"Fair enough. Just making an observation."
"I didn't mean it as a bad thing."
Just stand there and observe him.
He picks up a wrench and scratches his head with it, unaroused by fascism.
"It is cool. But it's also more than that. *Much* more."
Maybe you should just stand there, watch him rattle his toolbox. Get to know *his* 'sine.'
"I suck at socializing, man. If you go speak to Andre, I'll have time to *tune in*. Get a reading on your *sine*." Before he's finished talking, he's already turned back to his tools.
"Good, good." He likes what he's hearing. "What did you want to know?"
"I saw a sticker on the padlock. Can you tell me anything about it?"
"And what does it mean? Why is the dead guy smiling?"
"He defeated History. We are living in the age of History, and in the eyes of History we are always already dead. How can we ever smile, then? Because History is a lie, and so are its deaths..."
"The present moment and life are the hard core. The hard core expels death."
He thinks. "Or maybe he's not dead, maybe he's just really ecstatic about the beats."
Or drugged out of his mind, come to think of it.
"He could also be drugged out of his mind."
"Or drunk, or in a clinical coma, or glad to be dead, but those versions suck."
"What makes the sticker so modern?"
"Simplicity was brought to us by classical Solaist modernism, but that was a *tasteful*, harmonious simplicity, right?"
"You keep mentioning *hard core*. What does it mean to you?"
"Well, hard core is not tasteful or outwardly harmonious. It's a warning shot: 'This will be dangerous.' The echo of man's loss, haunting him."
The term also signifies certain varieties of pornography that depict penetration, just so you know.
"The sticker, the clothes, the music -- same thing."
"Egg Head actually has a better concept of the hard core. He just really likes saying 'hard core'."
"You come up with this stuff by yourself?"
"Hard core!" His friend shouts from behind his mix table, with a smile surpassing your own in wideness, a total moon-face, and eyes full of naive wonderment.
"Not alone. Many people are thinking the same thing right now. There's a gathering at The Paliseum. The beat is the same for all."
"But shouldn't the ones that are more hard core rule over the ones that are less hard core, offer them guidance?"
"What do you think about this church?"
"If some want to lead and others want to be led, I think they are welcome to it."
"What's with the clothes?"
He shrugs. "They're hard core."
Dedicated. Hyperactive. Unified. You will have to add something of your own to understand this list of loosely formed qualities called hard core. You need your own entry. Make it!
Internalize the hard core aesthetic. Don't just nod along, really *feel* it.

Aggressive. Monotonous... but also somehow sacral. Primitive, yet futuristic, like a machine man. Nothing exists, but the here and now. All are one, one purpose... All you've managed is a list. The parts don't form a whole.
The young man picks up a thin metal saw blade and nods.
"See? It's already going wrong. Sine is off." The young man picks up a thin metal saw blade and examines it.
"Go speak to Andre. I'm just the Noid," a strangely dressed young man says without looking up from his toolbox.
"Got it. Tell me something else."
"Good call, not exposing yourself to stuff like that."
This is a good, dangerous line of questioning. You should prod him on!

"I don't have a top ten list of things I'm most suspicious of. But if I *had* one, the left-right complex would be number one. Number two would be their sole accomplishment -- the pig/wheat paradigm."
"Tell me more about the left-right business."
"What's suspicious about the production of pork and wheat?"
"Don't you mean the left-right *paradigm* and the pig/wheat *complex*?"
"Nope. Politics is an inert complex of daily corruption and inane thinkpieces. The real paradigm is economic and it concerns pig and wheat."
"This is where the innovation happens. It's only a theory, but I suspect they're breeding a pig/wheat hybrid. Probably in Graad."
"It's our only shit." He shrugs. "We should make better use of not being animals -- or cereal grain -- ourselves."
"What's bad about animals? Animals are cute."
"Nothing, animals are cool guys, I like animals too. But that doesn't mean I have to be one myself."
"Yeah. It's our only shit and we fucking suck at it!"
He can't help but doubt your sincerity in this matter. There is no other way -- you are a police officer.
He gives you a long, suspicious look. "Correct."
"Don't assume I like the status quo, because I'm a cop."
"Precisely! The status quo doesn't need to be loved."
(Look him straight in the eye:) "Shit, piss, cunts, dicks, f****ts! Fuck the World!"
The young man looks startled.
"I was being sarcastic. This world has its fair share of problems, but it's not like you guys are going to solve them."
"Neither will anyone else."
Say nothing.
The young man doesn't say anything either. After a while he takes out a magnet and runs it over some nails in front of him.
Whatever this *true life* is, you feel it's the real centrepiece of this mythology.
"What about now? Are the sines all right now?"
"Na... huh. Still strongly out of sync. Stage gamma dis-alignment."
"May I ask why? What good is being suspicious?"
"A reasonable question. Say, I get hurt. I want to make sure it never happens again. So I analyse the situation. Exercise caution. Caution is suspicion."
"Oh yeah. Sure thing."
Hard people. Hard republic. Hard cell. Hard party. Hard riot. Hard government. Core membership. Core secretary. Core teachings. Core fighters.
Predictable, but solid.
This is taking place in Revachol, hard core rising. It could only happen here, in the bottom of the geopolitical abyss. Those are the warhorns of today. We'll be given a fresh start.
Oh yeah it feels manly. Beautiful.
Long live the world that gave shape to hard core to complete itself! A true heir to Dolorian values. Three-and-a-half centuries and the gift still keeps on giving.
Endless are the wonders borne out of the cultural collaboration so wisely facilitated by the free world!
I've got the money, I've got the place/ You've got the figure, you've got the face/ Let's get together, we're jumping all over the world!
JUMPING ALL OVER THE WORLD!
Test your limits. Surpass them. Dance till you drop. Dance till you die, if you must.
I am going to truly wreck myself as a machine of modern party in a final showdown between flesh and spirit!
That's a good way to go.
I am the law.
Start the war (Hey! Hey!) Hit the floor! (Hey! Hey! ) We need more (Hey! Hey!) Army of hard core! Yea.
I'm thinking of wearing sports apparel as my hard core getup to maximize the mobility of limbs.
Jumping around, as this sort of music requires, is actually a taxing physical activity and should be dignified with a sports suit.
You might as well make it complete with a whistle, then.
I want to have fuck with you.
Say that again?
I want to have fuck with you!
You know it, baby!
Overwhelm them with moves. Try to have the most moves going on.
Thinking of cornering the moves market. They won't know what hit 'em.
Yeah, you should even try to put moves inside your moves.
SEE THE SUNSHINE/ WE AIN'T STOPPING/ KEEP ON DANCING/ TILL THE WORLD ENDS!

IF YOU FEAR IT, LET IT HAPPEN.
KEEP ON DANCING TILL THE WORLD ENDS.
You know it feels unfair, there's a party everywhere.
That level of conceptual thinking is not part of your skill set.
Your conceptualization accepts this in solemn admiration and gratitude.
I don't seem to have anything to add to the core.
So you've come empty-handed and pure, without burdens. A hard-core supplicant. That will have to do.
Something is off here... you feel like it should be the other way around.
"Really?"
"Why do you think that's so?"
"Really."

"Good to know. Tell me something else."
"I would much rather tell you about true life than this pathetic *something else*, but you are, after all, the law of the land."
"That's it?"
"Okay then."
"It's my friend and accomplice. It makes me party harder."
"I can see that. And you've partied *very* hard for a *very* long time, haven't you?"
"It looks like you're trying to hang yourself with it. So large, too. So many different patterns. It's crazy man, I like it."

"No, it's just a vest of suspenders made to resemble a human rib cage. Plus some lady-clothes to piss off the sex-system." He points to your tie. "Now tell me about that hard core necktie. It's fucking primal."
(Look at your tie suspiciously.) "What's so hard core about it?"
"They're just clothes."

"It's just a style, you know?"

"No, these are just boring, normal, hard core clothes. That..." he points to your necktie, "*that's* outlandish."
(Look at your tie suspiciously.) "What's so outlandish about it?"
"RESPECT TO THE MAN!"

You suddenly realize the patience and respect this speedfreak has shown you is partly because of your *style*. He's probably not like that with everyone.
Conjuring terrible visions of the future, which you apparently don't care for.
This is for your posse. They got to keep it up. They got to move. You are the major mic enforcer.

He cringes. "Weird stuff. Specialized. There was a data processor and some sort of long-wave machinery."
"What's wrong with the supra-natural?"
The People's Republic of Samara (SRV) is a product of Revachol's sister revolution on the isola of Graad. It's known as a severely degenerated rogue state.
"Wires going into water. Gives off a spy sine, or some fucked up Samaran science sine... you know, the kind that goes head first into the supra-natural."

"Don't be too hard on Samara, they're all alone in the world. Half of what we know of them is just propaganda."
"I know, man, I was just talking about the aesthetic."
The sickest. That is perhaps *why* it should be researched.
"Psionic powers, pale-related diseases, *pretenders* pretending to be human, folk rites, that kind of stuff."
"Most of it doesn't exist, but there's also stuff that isn't *allowed* to exist because the moralists think it's too *dangerous* for the plebes."
"Nothing's wrong with it. It should definitely be researched. You can still do sick shit with it, though."
"Why are you called 'Noid'?"
"The hard core aesthetic is esoteric. It is not meant to be discussed with the law at this moment." He picks up some sort of a widget.
"Does this mean... we need sine matching?"
"Yes, further sine-matching would do good for us. One way to achieve this would be by getting us into the church."
"I don't understand what that means."
"I can see that. Further sine-matching would do good for us. One way to achieve sine-synchronicity would be by getting us into the *church*."
"What?"
"You heard me." He examines the small metal bolt in his hand.
"Okay, maybe I'll come back later. [Leave.]
"Huh, I see you're here again, off-sine-man." He rummages through his tools. "Did I mention getting us into the church would help?"
"Suspicious people are esoteric people. We don't go around spilling everything to Johnny Law. They don't call me Noid for nothing."
"Yo, man. What's on your mind?" He drops a bolt into his toolbox.
It's not easy to reach a harmonic resonance of sines without some adjustment.
"Sure." The young man cracks his knuckles.
"Why *are* you called Noid anyway?"
"It took us setting out for this whole enterprise to get our sines synced..."
"You got us in, cop. I can't believe you got us in..." He looks around the hall, examining the carpentry.
"That's fine, man. But I've gotta warn you -- our sines are still off. It will take some time for me to get my psi on."
"Between you and me -- I don't know if you've noticed this about me... I'm a little *suspicious* of authority. But you -- you really came through for the hard core underground."
"Yes. You really came through. For the hard core underground." He spreads his arms, looking around at the speedfreaks setting up shop. "How come?"
The would-be leader is cutting some futuristic shapes on the floor, sweating profusely.
Acele using her contact mic to listen to a tree, underwater.
The one with the large head is blasting the dance track on repeat, while the stained glass window behind him is rattling from the bass.
With wonder in his sharp eyes.
Andre is busy cutting some slightly less lame, but still quite ungainly shapes on the church floor, sweating profusely.
"Does this mean you are mentally ill?"
"*Mental illness* is a term the powers use to homogenize people. I think I don't reach mental illness. I am merely politically ill. A suspicious element."
"Cool. You're Noid right? Do you have a moment to talk?"
"Mega. I'll be going now." [Leave.]
"That's me. A friend and an ally to the hard core underground. Have a moment to talk?"
"These kids got spunk. I admire that."
"Better here than in that tent." (Shrug.) "It wasn't safe."
"I'm genuinely into the *hard core lifestyle*. You wouldn't understand."
"I'm a corrupt cop, Kim. This is a corrupt scheme."
"I did it for mankind. For *all of mankind*."
Sire, the tent -- 'twas a *securitie risk*! And in here? Sanctuary! 'Twas only noble of you.
"Okay." The lieutenant keeps it laconic.

What he means is: You can't possibly have handed them this real estate for such a flimsy reason -- then again, whatever keeps your nose out of the bottle and on the job.
What he means is: I don't care if you have a corrupt scheme, almost everyone does. Whatever keeps you sober and concentrated on work.
What he means is: I don't believe you actually think you did it for all mankind. But whatever keeps you in high spirits is okay by him.
What he means is: You're right. I do not understand. Do whatever you have to do to keep your nose out of the bottle.
What he means is: You're right, actually. The tent was a safety hazard and this place was deserted anyway.
He nods: "What's on your mind?"
The young man gives you an uncharacteristic smile as you're turning to leave.
"My dedication to the hard core underground is tenuous at best. I have questions, however."
"What's on your mind?" He looks up into the darkness under the roof.
"It's a miracle of carpentry. Dead bodies carved into *total* shapes. Now it can be something more." He rubs his hands together.
"What style is this church built in?"
He shakes his head. "I don't say much anything as a carpenter anymore. They tried to make me into a reckoner and a leveller. Made me a bit manic, y'know?"
"You say that as a carpenter yourself?"
"I regret the time I dedicated to that profession, and that worker collective. I say things more as a member of the hard core psi-dance community these days."
"What did you mean by *dead bodies*?"
"Dead bodies of perennial plants." He taps on the wood. "Sigma functions have left this place. It's a good thing we came along -- the spiritual collapse has been total."
"How old do you think the church is?"

"Three-hundred and twenty years. A little more. The first settlers built it, plus six more like it. On the coast here. Was one of the first things they did, must've been really scared of something. I understand..."
"That's right. The first settlers built it, plus six more like it. On the coast here. Was one of the first things they did... must've been really scared of something. But I understand..."
"Alone on an uninhabited archipelago, forced to face themselves and nature. Pre-industrial quantities of solitude. The sea. Perhaps something more... fundamental."
He means something para-natural. He must...
"I would want to build a safe place for myself and my own as well..." His voice echoes in the wooden cavern of the church.
"A cop who's into building critique." He taps a floorboard. "Okay then. This is folk Dolorianism, lawmongerer. It's a subset of early *Dolorian* architecture."

"*Total*. Everything between an ancient concrete cathedral and a glass cube is Dolorianism. This is just a homespun version of it, folksy stuff, early mass production. They made thousands like this. Does that help you out?"

"Liked to show off large and intricate structures, arches, spires. Put you down with them. They were really into painting everything white too. Virginal shit, you know. Marriage shit. Virtue and tyranny."
"Stands to reason it used to be white on the outside." He peeks out of a small window in the dark. "Before the sea wind took all the paint off."
"This church isn't painted white, as far as I can tell."
"Okay -- and what is Dolorian architecture like?"
"Yeah, enough architecture."
"I'm not just a cop. I'm an Art Cop."
"Hard of core." He nods appreciatively.
The church creaks in response. The speedfreak is too busy listening to it with a suspicious expression to say anything.
"What would a Dolorian building look like?"

"Like that woman there," he nods toward the stained glass window. "Vertical, thin, white, a false image of grandeur. The source of the system is up there, you're at the bottom. They really dug that power vertical."
Year after year, flake after flake, white washed clean, then covered in green moss...
Slowly peeled by the wind... Your skin crawls from the sensation as you look around.
It was probably white and gold, with light red flower motives. Part of you -- assumed to be lost to nerve damage -- knows this style to be Ubi Dolorianism.
"Is there such a thing as *Ubi Dolorianism* or did I just make that up?"
I don't wanna sound like an art guy.
"Good catch, Art Cop." He crosses his arms. "The herdsmen of the Ubi Sunt? islands came here on the first boats. Their flowery version of Dolorianism could be what we're standing in."
"True." He crosses his arms and nods. "The herdsmen of the Ubi Sunt? islands came here on the first boats. Their version of Dolorianism could be what we're standing in..."
Then why do you have all this cultural analysis up here?

The Ubi are known for their partiality to socialism and sheep. They come from an island called Ubi Sunt?, drifting in the pale off the coast of Vesper. It's the only place in the world that has a question mark in its name. Things are not well there: It's an island of poverty and entroponetic collapse.
"How are you settling in?"
"Let's talk about something else, Noid."
"It never was. A three-thousand-year-old regime of History, built by hundreds of generations of self-appointed *intellectuals*..." He looks around. "It's false to the core."
"Spiritual collapse?"
"Okay, then."
"Okay," he nods.
"End of quote. This is a high-quality carcass." He kicks the floorboard. "The power of anodic beats and hard bass is needed to reanimate it."
"'I saw some piglets suckling their dead mother' -- have you heard this one, cop-man?" He continues without waiting for an answer: "'After a short while they shuddered and went away.'"
"They had sensed that she could no longer see them and that she wasn't *like* them anymore. What they loved in their mother wasn't her body, but whatever it was that made her body live."
"First, where is that quote from?"
"What you're saying is: religion has stopped being *hard core*?"
"What you're saying is: you're not a big fan of the innocentic system?"
"A Seraise man, who lived a long time ago. An ancient hard core brother."
"Then I did right not to agree with all that talk about the Ecclesiastes being okay with this then."
"How do you like the glasswork?" (Point to the stained-glass window.)
"What exactly *are* you saying?"
"This religion of History is false-core. It has collapsed."
"A three-thousand-year-old tyrannical regime of History, built and maintained by hundreds of generations of self-appointed *intellectuals*..." He looks around. "It's false-core."
The way he says it, the *false* in false-core is invested with twenty kilotons of disgust.
"But you guys said the Ecclesiastes were all about love and hard core -- before, remember?"
"*I* only said: *Unity*. One word. Figures of authority always misquote you." He points to his friends.
"I even agreed with you. About the Ecclesiastes being okay with this..."
"The Founding Party doesn't give two shits about this place. Look around." He spreads his arms. "They do not have enough love for the *human crew* to oppose anything anymore. We're on our own."
"But were you wrong? The Founding Party is okay with everything. Look around." He spreads his arms. "They do not have enough love for the *human crew* to oppose anything anymore. We're on our own."
"And you propose dance music will supplant this system?"
"*Anodic* dance music," he nods. "Regular dance music wasn't hard enough. And yes, I do."
You know what this kind of stuff goes well with?
"Only a little."
"Don't you have to be on drugs for that though?"
I don't need to be a narc.
Your pleasure response was more like... just wondering if he has any?
"Cool."
"Not cool." Shake your head.
"All large human gatherings are narcotic. Ask any such undertaking in history -- this included." He nods toward a human-shaped pillar nearby. "Chemistry is true to its word."
"It's a necessity. All large human gatherings are narcotic. It's just the way of the spinal cord."
"Khm," the lieutenant interjects: "There is a difference between narcotics and group elation. One kills you, the other does not."
"The supercharged humanism that the innocentic system has been feeding us, on giant city squares? That's not a drug? The sugar and wheat it feeds us is healthy?"
"Forget it." He waves his hand. "It would become an imbecilic discussion. You two continue. It's more *hard core* that way."
"You're not going to ask me how I knew?"
"Understood."
"Why? You're a cop. I carry carpentry tools."
"The material knowledge is mega, though." He looks around the hollow hall of the church. "Guild shit. Teaches independence."
"Something more fundamental? You mean the sound anomaly?"
"Right."
"Maybe." He looks up under the rafters. "Maybe they were unable to face the nature of the world -- perishing."
"People are always afraid of all sorts of shit. They're right to be. The world is a trap..."
"Marriage is shit, yeah."
"Hey, marriage is great. Marriage is sacred."
"You're entitled to your wrong opinion." He inspects a pillar nearby, with a sharp gaze.
"Right." He takes a bolt from the toolbox and spits on it before shining it.
"Andre doesn't care about the Ecclesiastes. He just wants the operation to run smoothly. And Egg is a demi-beast. You shouldn't listen to what people say, you should listen to what they are."
He does not feel left out. In fact he probably just wanted to say "hard core."
It *does* feel good to say it. Maybe the speedfreaks are on to something?
"I don't." He looks over his shoulder. "Fucker giving me the evil eye."
That's still a lie! RE-ASSERT YOURSELF.
"Perfidy! You lied to me. I am *tired* of people lying to me."
That wouldn't be cool. I want to be cool.
Mewling wimp! Pathetic...
"Well..." The young man pushes his chest out, the skeleton of suspenders rattling...
"Noid-man! Mellow out," the dancing hedgehog yelps at his friend. "Stop aggroing the law!"
His chest returns to its normal proportions. "I'm sorry."
"That's Her Innocence Dolores Dei, mind your words."
"I'm getting some real negative vibrations from her too."
"You wanted to get inside the church and now you don't like the stained-glass window."
"You defend her, law-minion." He cracks his neck. "She was a *mass murderer* -- what's up with that?"
"But she's the innocence of humanism. Humanism seems to be a pretty big deal around here."
"Humanism leads to eating sugar and pigs. Humanism was invented to mass produce billions of humans. Billions of humans can mass produce *hundreds* of billions of pigs."
"She liked games. Her legacy, the thing we're living, isn't *real* life. It's a strategy for some kind of victory. Against a long-dead opponent. But -- yo -- I'm only the Noid. What do I know?"
"Mellow, man! Mellow!" yells his friend. "No one's a mass murderer, this is a house of *love!*"
"Mass murder on the floor!"
"No wonder." He cracks his neck. "We have to get rid of it. Dismantle it. Can't dance with a giant *mass murderer* lookin' at you. Not a good look for the club."
"I didn't know it was in here." He cracks his neck. "We have to get rid of it. Dismantle it. Can't dance with a giant *mass murderer* lookin' at you. Not a good look for the club."
"I wanted to talk some more about this place."
"Dead body, spirit entered. What is there to talk of?"
"Let's talk about that glasswork again."
"The mass murderer? Why?"
"But she's pretty."
"Yeah, but, like, who *isn't* accused of being a mass murderer these days?"
"I *do* feel there is something terrifying about her."
"Isn't she supposed to be an embodiment of the World Spirit?"
"Yeah, I'm done talking about her. I don't want to think about her anymore."
"The resettlement programs were totally okay. I'm a big fan of resettlement programs, for some reason."
And many, many more tons of sugar!
"She invented the beauty you're feeling. She and her glass-cutters and iconographers." He turns to look up at her face. "You set the standard, alright..."
"Then you meet it. It's effective like that. But it is also very soft-of-core, that so-called 'beauty' of hers."
"You're right, I like it harder-core."
"It's anything but *soft* core. It's terrifying."
"Then it seems I like it soft, because..."
"Hmh." The young man nods, he looks worried. "You may be on to something, copper-man. She's got those mass murderin' hips."
"You wouldn't be the first. Millions liked her." The young man frowns, worried. "She's got those mass murderin' lips."
"In the true life of tomorrow, every woman will be an innocence. They will wear neon headbands and leggings, and they will glow in the dark." His eyes smile enigmatically.
But you don't like that, you liar. You like this one, the softness of her core is dear to you...
Oh my living god, it's dear. Suddenly you feel like you need to *plummet* into it. Look away, say something!
"*No one* says Arno van Eyck is a mass murderer. The anodic pioneer Rietveldt is not a mass murderer. He is not accused of mass murder..."

"Likewise, no one says Germaine Egg-Head or Andre are mass murderers. You can live *entirely* outside that suspicion. Billions of people go about not being guilty of mass murder." He nods up. "Just not her."
"Are you a commie-cop?"
"I am."
"No." (Lie.)
"Hmh. Then it's inexplicable. Whatever." He picks up his toolbox, then puts it back down again.
"Then that's why. Communism is just a bloodier humanism, if you ask me. Has *her* love all over it." He nods up.
"There is. She is a party-repellent and must be taken down before we can begin partying in here."
No, that's not it... it's something more. Something closer to your skin...
"Take her down. Crash it. Destroy that window."
"Keep it. Keep the beautiful sharp shards. Keep her long face and her hair."
Say nothing, stare grimly into the distance.
The speedfreak looks the same way. It is dark there, in the back of the church. For a moment the music echoes strangely.
"No, Noid! Stop twisting my melon, man! People are gonna love it. It'll be our *thing*..." His friend disagrees. "Plus it keeps the cold out!"
"Will do." The speedfreak nods and pets the toolbox as if it were a cat.
The speedfreak's eyes narrow with suspicion, as if he's looking at a man possessed.
"It's not coming down. People are gonna love it. It'll be, like, our *thing*." His friend keeps dancing. "Plus it keeps the cold and the rain out!"
"The World Spirit does not have a body. It has *organs*. Hard core is an organ of the world spirit." He raises his left hand.
"This Arno van Eyck track is an organ. The carpentry and glass-cutting that built this house are also organs. She's a thief if you ask me. An organ thief. All innocences are."
"Okay." The young man appears constantly worried. It's just the way his brows are built. The worry never leaves his face.
What a strange choice of words...
That can't be healthy. What's happening here? Why do you keep coming back to this window?
Caustic, overflowing with negativity.
Nothing, everything's okay.
I don't know.
It's a nice window.
Why do you keep saying that if it isn't making you feel well? Don't come back to this anymore, stop talking about that damn window!
Well -- you shouldn't. You shouldn't come back to this anymore. Stop talking about it, please.
But it isn't. And you shouldn't come back to this anymore. This should be the last time. Stop talking about that damn window, please.
"Would you say she was... you know, *human*?"

"Ha!" The young man stretches his ribcage made of suspenders. "I like this question, cop-man. She did not live the life of a human. She lived like someone who is playing a game. The life of an operator..."

"Ha!" The young man stretches his ribcage made of suspenders. "I like this theory of yours, cop-man. This one I like..." He nods. "She was not human. Not really. She was an operator, playing life like a game..."
"That's not the life that humans live. She was adored. Humans aren't. I don't know about you, but they *hate* me. And they do not think I'm *innocent*, or some shit like that."
"Yeah, they hate this, too." (Point to yourself.)
"I don't know what you're talking about. I have thousands of fans. I am surrounded by love and support all the time."
"Mhm, she was a player! She played us all! It's just a game to her."
"Uhm, yes." He lets go of the suspenders and they hit his chest with a slap.
"Fame is a false existence. It doesn't happen inside the *head*." He nods mysteriously, then lets go of the suspenders and they hit his chest with a slap.
"Well, they *loved* her. They put all their love in her and forgot all about the rest of us." The young man lets go of the suspenders and they hit his chest with a slap.
This speedfreak does not quite understand the sudden escalation of emotion in that argument, but he agrees nonetheless.
"Alright, I'm done talking about her."

The Ubi are known for their partiality to socialism and sheep. They come from an island called Ubi Sunt?, the only place in the world that has a question mark in its name. There's something else important you should be able to remember about Ubi Sunt?, but all that's coming to mind is the sheep.
"What did Tiago tell you about the church?"

"The crab-man's been lurking here for a while. He's experienced things. Things that give off *bad sines*. As far as we can tell, the Ubis built this place about three hundred and twenty years ago as a sarcophagus."
"What's it for?"

"Encasement. Confinement. Of something they were afraid of. Something new and unheard of on the isola." He looks up, into the darkness  beyond the beams. "I think that's what the crab-man is experiencing when he climbs around upstairs..."
"Like, this is some old world shit the Ubis had heard about... and thought the best way to deal with it was to build a church. Surrounding it. To contain it."
"I don't get it, contain what exactly?"
"I dunno... and it's not something they properly understood either. What it does. But it's what this Soona person is looking for, and trying to measure." He nods toward the woman.
"It'll be fruitless, though. She won't be able to measure it. People like that always want to measure everything, all those things they really can't."
The wood creaks as a gale blows by outside. Dust particles fall through the darkness, settling down on the age-bleached floor boards. The structure does not feel particularly durable.
"This building seems... less than structurally sound."
"Anodic music will *definitely* contain whatever we're dealing with." His words echo in the chamber...
"Sounds like a job for the Remote Viewers Division."
"And if it *can't*, well..." He shrugs non-committally.
"Maybe *you* can figure things out, cop-man. I think we got on a good level here... the sines are syncing up well."
The young man shrugs. "I doubt it. I don't even think the Ubis properly understood it. What it does. But it's what this Soona person is looking for, and trying to measure." He nods toward the woman.
"Do you mean there are dead bodies here?!"
"Huh, spooky. Let's talk about something else."
He shrugs. "I don't know. Maybe. Maybe not. It's not a thing we can answer, cop-man. Even I have limits -- I'm a limited-psy person."
"Seems to be the trend around here, doesn't it? You can't measure shit like this... it's not like... with substance."
"Not like a *literal* sarcophagus. I'm just being... metaphorical."
"Now that I think of it, it doesn't sound plausible."
"Well, if it's without substance I guess there's nothing to worry about."
"You think there's any merit to the theory?"
The young man rubs his chin, in silence, then mumbles: "... like a concentric ring spreading out... the struggling villages..."
"No, it's pretty fucking *un*-sound if you ask me. They should have built a club for anodic music around it instead." He grins...
"What makes you think Soona's going to fail?"
"... and that is what caused the communards to fail in defending the beachhead. Yeah, a lot of failure has gone down around here."
"I found a Doomed Commercial Area in Martinaise proper. Maybe it's the same thing the Ubis were trying to contain?"
"Hard to say, cop-man. Sines in here are distinctly *wild*. Gonna take a while before everything's properly *synced*..."
"I did get to talk to the crab-man, though."
"You mean Tiago?"
"The crab-man?"
"Yeah, you know. The guy who lives in the rafters, walks around upside down on the ceiling. You know, like a crab."
"Are you sure it's a *crab* he reminds you of?"
"Oh, right. Crab-man, got it."
"Of course I'm sure. What? You think I'm *confused*?"
"Eight legs, walks upside down on the ceiling, spins webs sometimes..."
"No, you're definitely right. That's entirely crab-like behaviour you're describing."
"Yeah, a crab."
"Anyway, he's been giving me kind of a *psychic rundown* of this place..."
You begin to wonder if this speedfreak has ever seen a crab before.
"Dude's seen some crazy shit. But he's actually a lot like us."
"You mean all his *Mother's love* stuff isn't too *spooky* for you?"
"You mean all his *sobriety* stuff isn't too *restrictive* for you?"
"What do you mean?"
"Talking to him, I realized that sobriety can be pretty *hard core*, too. I gotta respect it..."
"Have you been listening to what Egg's been saying? Love is *hard core* man, and a mother's love is the hardest core of all..."
"The man picks up on stuff. And he knows *a lot* about the church. I got a lot to learn from him..."
"Good thing you didn't squash him."
"But I thought we'd be okay now -- sine-wise."
"Interesting."
"That's ridiculous."
"I suck at socializing, man. Even now our sine synchronization is way off. But I'll see what I can do." He continues to rearrange his tools.
"See? Our sines are way off." He looks down at his tools. "I can already tell this social relationship is gonna take a lot of work."
"'Sine'?"
"Yeah. Gotta compare, see if we can align."
"I'm doing what I can." He continues to rearrange his tools.
It's not easy to reach a harmonic resonance of sines without some adjustment.
Scared? Angry? It's hard to say which this man is.
He's just scared.
It's not easy for him. It probably took him years to get used to Andre.
He looks like a *well thought out* individual. The synchronization might be worth it. In the long run.
Interesting. He wants you to *describe* it, though he already knows what it looks like.
Better not mention it.
He blinks, waiting for the next question.
"Okay, *now* I'm ready. Let's contact Archer."
"I found a radio transceiver."

"So any cop-prep you've got to do, you do it now. We'll wait if we have to."

"I'm ready now. Let's do this."
"Yeah, I should get some things in order first."
"Wait, didn't you say we need some kind of power supply?"
"Rest of the crew has got to stay here." He gives you a solemn nod. "Can't afford to let the beat drop right as we're getting off the ground."
"Do what you have to do. We're not going anywhere."
"How should I know? It's up to everyone to know their own needs. Whatever keeps your *body and soul* in top working condition..."
"Don't sweat that. Egg found something down near the waterlock. Some maniac *abandoned* a perfectly good power source..."
That 'maniac' is obviously you, which makes the 'power source' your half-sunken Coupris 40.
An 'abandoned power source'? What could he be referring to?
Whatever it is, it was abandoned for *good* reason. Best to leave some stones unturned...
"You mean the motor carriage that I crashed into the bay?"
"What do you mean someone *abandoned* a power source?"
"Ah, well as long as it works, I don't need to know the details."
"That explains why it was covered in cop colours. Whole thing's totalled, but lucky for us the engine on the back is still perfectly good..."
"I know, it's completely mental, but someone drove a *perfectly good* Coupris MC straight into the bay. Carriage is totalled, but luckily the engine on the back is still working..."
"All I have to do is run a cable from the engine up the centaur-man's memorial. It won't last forever, but it should buy us enough time to get you synced up with the Big Bad."
"Right, that's your call then."
"Personally, I'm gonna make sure I've got a steady supply of PREPTIDE handy."
*Now* he's playing your tune! Better make sure you're ready to blast while circuit-bending!
The speed is to get you through the tedious *detail-oriented* parts of the work. Maybe this freak will spot you some?
But what's this? You're all out! Maybe this freak will spot you some...
(Whisper.) "Say, Noid. My PREPTIDE supply is a little low -- think you could *hook me up*?"
Nah, I'm good without it.
Hope you don't get any little wires crossed because you lost your concentration, Mr. Clean-and-Sober.
"Here, you'll like this. It's got a little straw and everything so you can slurp while you work."
The lieutenant politely averts his eyes as you make a drug deal in a house of worship, but make no mistake: He's *less than thrilled* about it.
Fuck what the lieutenant thinks! We're off to the races, baby!
HEIGH-HO, HEIGH-HO, it's off to the races we go!
"MUCH LOVE TO MY HARD CORE ANTENNA BROTHERS!"
"Back across the waterlock. At least we're getting our *exercise* in today."
"Now give me a hand with these cables. It's a long walk to the roundabout..."
"Hard core church! Nowhere else to go!"
"Could you use your *sine-sense* to help me contact a Coalition warship?"
