dialoguetext: "This is a major setback. We're going to have to find some *other* way to generate those mega-long waves."
Come up with a site for a mega-longwave radio antenna.
This is easy. Antennas are basically just tall things, right?
"We could use the steeple of *this* church." (Point up.)
The young man looks straight up, following the line of your finger. A frown comes over his face.
He's being uncharacteristically polite. He means they don't make *any* pinewood antennas. Because it's such an obviously bad idea, you see.
"Not likely to work. This whole church is made from pinewood. They don't make too many pinewood antennas."
"Ours will be the first!"
"Hmm, that's a good point, now that you mention it."
"No, it won't be. There can't be a first of something that can't be."
He shrugs, as though the point were rather obvious.
That's fine. You're just getting warmed up. Your next idea will *definitely* be better.
Alright, brainstorming time. Remember, this is just the ideation phase. There are no *bad* ideas.
"Here's an idea: Maybe there's an antenna in the harbour we could use?"
"I've got it. Why don't we use the mast of a giant *boat*?"
"What, are you some kind of *aquatic cop* now?"
"I know the Wild Pines rep. She'll lend us her boat for sure."
"Let's just say I have an *extremely* wealthy patron."
"No way I'm getting on a boat owned by the Wild Pines. Everything about them gives off a real *shadowy* sine."
"If that's the case, though, not sure I want to get mixed up in your patron's boat business."
"Oh, I get it. You're a *gigolo cop*, then. Makes sense..."
Hmmm, this really didn't seem like it was going to be that hard. We'll just have to try again...
"Something tells me Ms. Messier would be *less than thrilled* to hear you'd like to commandeer her boat so you can talk to a Coalition warship."
"You want to get the Union in on this plan?" He gives you an incredulous look. "Is that a good idea?"
"One-hundred percent. Evrart's an old friend of mine."
"Hmmm, maybe not."
"Yes, you two have grown *quite* close over the last few days. Always doing little *errands* for each other."
"I'm not sure I'd use the word 'friendly' to describe Mr. Claire's attitude toward us."
"I don't trust the fat man. Gives off a hard core würm sine, real manipulative, if you ask me."
"Didn't think so. You gotta watch out for those guys. Give off a real *hostile* sine, if you ask me."
Your thinking about this has gotten way too rigid. Time to flip the whole *antenna paradigm* on its head.
"Hear me out: What if we built the antenna *underground*?"
"Underground, huh? That *would* be pretty hard core..."
"It would also be incredibly stupid. Detective, did you not take Elementary Radio Operations? I thought it was an RCM-wide requirement."
"Underground antenna! Waves so hard core only moles can hear them!"
"Egg makes a good point. An underground antenna's probably not the best way to contact your aerostatic."
Nope, nothing. The idea factory is closed until further notice.
Close your eyes. Unfold your mental map of Martinaise. It's morning. You're standing on the plaza before the Whirling-in-Rags.
The wind pushes a piece of tare across the cracked tiles. From the north comes the malicious laughter of two children...
Turn to face the bay.
Turn to face the apartments.
Turn to face the traffic circle.
Your eye follows the tiles west. You see a bench and a few twisted, pitiful trees. Then, just water...
Beyond the unkempt backyard rises a monstrous assemblage of concrete, plaster, and corrugated sheet metal...
You turn around. The morning sun is blinding. You bring your hand to your brow and a great shadow materialises before you. A towering beast, frozen in mid-air...
"Centaur-man is made of metal. With the right gear we could make it work."
"YEEEAGH! Connect the centaur to the lorries, unite the whole roundabout in hard core waves!"
"Huh. Sounds like Egg's saying you could use some spare cables to rig up the stalled motor lorries and increase the wavelength..."
Effectively transforming the entire roundabout into a single, fractal antenna.
"Sounds like madness, but I think it could work."
"Which would pretty much make the whole roundabout one giant antenna."
"ONE ROUNDABOUT, ONE WAVELENGTH! HARD CORE!"
"About time, those other antennas were cramping my style."
"We shall call it: The Herald of Destruction."
"As long as it gets the job done, I'm not interested in the details."
"Are you sure that's legal? I feel like I'm going to need to apologise to someone."
"That's... a very big antenna."
"It's gonna be the most hard core antenna in Martinaise, and probably all of Revachol West."
"Pretty hard core, but maybe it would be better to go with something more positive?"
"You're really going about this the wrong way, then. The details are the best part."
"You're a lawman, lawman. Don't *you* get to decide what's legal and what isn't?"
"Probably the biggest antenna in all of Revachol West." He seems very pleased with himself.
"We have the amps, we have the cables! We're almost ready! Yeeeagh!"
"He's right. All we're missing now is the transceiver itself. Soon as you find one, we'll be all set."
"Where am I supposed to find a radio transceiver?"
(Point to Egg Head.) "Doesn't he have something we could use?"
"Alright, I guess I need to find one of these transceivers then." (Conclude.)
"Can't do it. We just got this place set up. Can't go risking Egg's most important equipment..."
"I don't know. Buy one? Steal one? I don't know your cop ways."
"While you're gone, me and Egg will get the rest of the gear together. Meet us back here when you've got it."
"And before you ask: No, you can't have the radio from my Kineema either."
"You know what, Kim? I'll find an even *better* radio on my own."
"I highly doubt that. When I crank the volume on my DynaWave, it's like you're in the front row at the National Concert Hall."
"I didn't know *Speedfreaks FM* had a concert series."
"Alright, Kim, challenge accepted."
"On second thought, this is childish. I'm just going to look for a regular radio."
"Joke all you want, detective. Whatever radio you manage to scrounge up won't lay a *finger* on my set-up."
"A cop-on-cop challenge, not bad. Let's see what you come up with... Though I have to say, cop cars and lorries usually pack the best equipment in town."
He shrugs. "It's your transmission. A regular old transceiver should work fine, it just won't be as *hard core*, you know..."
"Well, cop-man, we've re-paid the favour. Guess this cements the cop-hardcore alliance."
"Sure, you have to say that now, but it's alright..."
"Alright, cop-man. We've held up more than our share of this collaboration. I hope you *recognise* how much the hardcore underground came through for you."
"I've got my own case to worry about, but if I have time, I'll be back."
"YEEEAGH. WE ARE COPS NOW."
"Sure, I've heard that before..."
"Easy, Egg. We're still hardcore music venue organisers, first and foremost. But maybe this *does* make us pillars of the local community..."
"I'll put this tech away later. Think there's an extra can set, in case you want to grab a *souvenir* or something. Don't think anyone will miss it."
"I would never let my hardcore brothers down."
"If you want to show your appreciation, we could still use your help. Egg is the one to talk to."
"No need to fake it, we know you're still a cop at heart..."
"HARD CORE! MUTUAL AID!"
"It's been good working with you... gentlemen."
"Acele's right. He's one of us now."
"Acele's right. He's one of us now."
"Good luck, guys."
"Try to squeeze in a promo spot while you're on-air, we've got to start putting the word out."
"Could you use your *sine-sense* to help me contact a Coalition warship?"
"Don't think so. Big Bad frequencies are extremely negative: thought suppression, dream implantation, memory revision. Pretty *out there* stuff, not sure I want to get involved with it."
There is fear there, but also curiosity. He just needs a *reason* to help you.
"Besides, our own sines aren't even synced yet. So how am I supposed to get *you* synced up with the Big Bad? It doesn't make any sense, law-lover."
"Do radiocomputers have transceivers in them?"
"Yeah, probably. Thing is you'd have to be an engineer to get it out. I'd stick with *regular radios*, if I were you."
"I think I saw a radio in that office near the harbour..."
"Hmm, some equipment from harbour could work. Worth the leg-work, at least."
"Do you think the pawnshop will have one?"
"Maybe, if you want to pay money like some kind of... money lord. Yeah, pawnshop could have one."
"A radio transceiver. Cool. I've got this. I've seen *plenty* of those lying around."
"Exactly. You could buy one, you could steal one..."
*Lorries*, huh? You could check out the abandoned one by the roundabout...
The voice again, more urgent now: 'Nay!'
Just a moment. That voice isn't human, and it's not saying 'Nay!' -- It's saying 'N-n-n-neigh!'
"Maybe not that big, but pretty big."
"An antenna hard core enough to shake the whole world!"
"The horseback monument."
From behind you, a low, spectral voice whispers: 'Nay.'
The young speedfreak gives you a suspicious look before returning to... whatever he was doing.
"You sure that's a good idea? Those are some serious frequencies you want to mess with..."
"Like Egg said."
"You'll probably wanna take a minute to get your *gear situation* sorted out."
His look is intensely suspicious.
This young speedfreak seems to know a lot about 'sines'... could he be the techno-tinkerer you're looking for?
This young speedfreak seems to know a lot about 'sines'... could he have the technical skill you're looking for?
This young speedfreak seems to know a lot about 'sines'... could he be the techno-tinkerer you're looking for?
This young speedfreak seems to know a lot about 'sines'... could he have the technical skill you're looking for?
You really should look into this totalled MC when you have a chance. Seems important...
At the very least, you should make sure you're wearing a good pair of gloves.
"Now give me a hand with these cables. It's a long walk to the roundabout..."

dialoguetext: "Sorry." He points his thumb at the lieutenant. "We barely have room for one."
"You go ahead, I'm too old for this..."
Squeeze in.
"No way." [Leave.]
"C'mon! Get in, the warm stuff is getting out."
"I'm sure you will feel right at home. I'll keep watch." He gestures for you to squeeze in.
I'm actually not, he thinks. I just dislike delinquents.

The tent is just tarpaulin fabric covering a pile of stuff. The flap is open. Inside, three young men are listening to some new form of music. It's like nothing you've ever heard. One of them looks at you.
"C'mon! Get in and close the flap behind you! The warm stuff is getting out!"
It's safe to assume this is their leader. Or at least he thinks he is.
You leave the lieutenant outside and squeeze in.
"Okay."
"Why wouldn't it be?"
"Tell me about Andre."
"I don't know man, have you *been* down Boogie Street? It's a little bewildering."
"Tell me about Noid."
"Tore it to pieces."
"Oh, I'm sorry... have I not told you I'm a raging alcoholic who recently drank himself into an oblivion so deep he can't even remember what sounds like the biggest street in the city?"
"Andre? He's a cool guy. Doesn't really come off as one, but he is. To me at least..."

The worst of the *banlieues*. A wretched heap of closed-down mines even west of Jamrock, on the dusty slope of Mont Martin. The remotest possible area of Revachol, no one even wants to exploit those people anymore.
"Who do you want to know about?"
"He's in some kind of a self-destruction mode with that hair of his. Bleaching it like that. Probably wants to get rid of it altogether."
"Is there a law that would stop me from lying, though?"
She rubs her sides, but not from cold. Her shoulders are relaxed. She must have taken a hit or she's on an upswing.
"But I'm a police officer. You *have* to answer me."
"What does he do?"
"He's a Faubourger I guess, like the rest of us. Okay, maybe not Egg, I don't know about him, but Noid and the rest are from Faubourg, making the pilgrimage up north to visit The Paliseum."
You wish you'd been there.
This is the first time you've heard her laugh.
"It means I don't answer questions about myself."
"Come to think of it, yes!" She laughs.
"What do you want to know?"
"Could it be that he's balding? Him thinking it's his last chance?"
"Okay, lets leave it at that then."
"He takes care of shit. Sorry, I mean he's got a *vision*. Of what life should be, you know? He tries to push things until everything falls into place. He's an organizer."
"What's the deal with Egg Head?"
"What do you mean?"
"What does that mean?"
"Thank you. Some other questions."
"Uh, yes. Anyway."
"What does he think he's doing when he yells all that stuff?"
"Where's he from? How long has he been with you guys?"
"Tell me about the others."
"Oh, that... he's the party boy."
"What's a party boy?"
"I'm a silver bird."

"Anodic music doesn't really do vocals in the traditional sense. Vocals are thought of as *rock*. That's to say they're a bit *backward*. No offence if you like rock music, though. Rock music is cool by me."
"On his mother's love?"
"Uh, okay..." She nods.
"Anyway, even if you don't have vocals you still need someone to say something every now and then, right? To urge things on. That's where the party boy comes in..."
"God damn right, rock music is the coolest. Rock music forever!"
"No offence taken, go on."
"You don't have to tell *me* rock music is dead. I abandoned rock music a long time ago. Can't disco to rock!"
Ptew ptew! Sweeesh! Your credentials as the resident Futureman of Revachol are being questioned. Show her you're hip with the times, gramps!
"On life?"
"Unfortunately, I can confirm that."
"Tore that shit up."
"Tell me about the others."
"Yes." She nods studiously. "Forever..."
"Yes, better that way..."
"He basically just stands on the stage and dances and yells how awesome everything is. It's very catchy."
"Thank you."
"Fair enough."
"I understand. People are usually afraid to do things if others aren't already doing them. Dancing makes you dance like sneezing makes you sneeze. Or yawning makes you..."
"Yes, I suppose we did."
"Anyway..." He looks around, a little embarrassed of the enthusiasm of his interjection.
"Actually, no."
"What do you want to know?" She smiles a little.
"Yes, I forgot. Tell me about yourself."
"That would depend on the circumstances." The lieutenant taps his foot.
"Actually, we don't know where he's from. Or who he is, really."
"Me?"

"Egg was yelling along to some jams someone was spinning, all night long. Just kept yelling until he didn't have a shred of voice left. When the sun came up over the mines... there were mines? Yeah, it was in Coal City!" She nods.
"Egg came with us. He made this wheezing puppy dog sound all the way back. Couldn't even speak."
"Actually, do tell me about *yourself*."
"One time we were out partying, somewhere in backwater Faubourg. Or maybe even Coal City, I can't remember. Maybe it was Coal City..."

"It was definitely Coal City, because it took us two days to walk back to the Fau. He just wheezed the whole way, we never really asked him why he came with us. Or who he was. I think his name is Germaine..."
"People are sweet," she says quietly.
"It's unlikely I'll make it there. Chest pains. Need to continue drinking. But thank you."
You can see it must have been a great night. The memory causes her to go silent for a moment or two.
"Okay." She shrugs. "To each his own."
"Is Andre your boyfriend?"
"It's just something poor Faubourg kids do every spring, to pass the time. We walk the entire length of Boogie Street, up to Jamrock. Or as much as possible."
"What is this pilgrimage you're talking about?"
A quick response. She's very sure of it. He's someone she feels she can trust and even control, if need be.
"I might just do that if I make it there alive."
"Let's say I *haven't* been down Boogie Street."
"Oh, and I'm also a raging fascist who doesn't approve of *different people* -- so no, I don't think I'll be going."
"Tell me more about Egg."
"We certainly saw that in practice, didn't we?"
"What has he organized?"
"Nothing. But then again... there's nothing to organize around here either. He really wants this church thing to work..."
"I've never seen him so psyched about anything though -- and he's often psyched. Looked sort of desperate, like it's his last chance or something. Or maybe he was just high..."
"I mean, not that he does drugs. Just *high* you know."
"Yes." She nods.
"Relax, girl. I am a police officer, but I'm perfectly corrupt. You can tell me about drugs and shit, I don't care."
"Uh... no?"
"He abides by the hard core, sir. You would have to ask him yourself."
"Yeah. Drugs. Shit. Fuck. We don't care." He smirks.
"Tell me about the others."
"Actually, tell me about the others."
"What do you mean, 'do'? Like for a living?"
"Okay, then you should go and take a look, I guess. Boogie Street is cool. It's got a lot of immigrants and all kinds of different people."
"Yes."
"There is."
"No, I meant for breakfast. Of course for a living."
"Alright." She picks up the tape recorder and looks you in the eye...
"He's a carpenter. Trained and all. He's very good, he just doesn't have the mindset to work like that -- in a shop somewhere."
"Sure..." she says, slightly disoriented. "What do you want to know?"
"Is that because of his beliefs? The hard core and the ribs, the... spinal cord and stuff?"
"What kind of mindset is that?"
"Not to sound too dramatic, but I wouldn't make light of his belief system when he's around. Noid's a serious person. He's serious about the lifestyle."
"Tell me more about him."
"Wow. You really *have* talked to him." She smiles. "Indeed. Noid serves no master but the beat."
"There's more to you than you let on. What am I not seeing?"
"And you?"
"Because I'm not. Now tell me something else about Noid."
"Sir," she gives you a switchblade smile. "I abide by *the law*."

A strange feeling... like before, when you caught her lying better than she should have. Every now and then something feels off about the way she speaks. She doesn't exactly change tone, but you feel as though there's more about her than she lets on.
"Yeah," she says, then opens her mouth like she's about to add something, but doesn't.
"Well, I am."
A strange feeling... Every now and then, something feels off about the way she speaks. She doesn't change tone, but you feel as though there's more about her than she lets on.
"They do say death is an avenue. Like all the others." She's silent for a second like she's going to add something. But she doesn't.
"Acele."
"And your surname?"
"Acele who? I'm not a young suitor, this is official police business."
"Why?"
Her hair is dyed blonde, with dark roots showing. There's a coarseness to her features, some masculinity below that timidness.
"Okay..." She hesitates. "It's Berger."
You have little reason to doubt that's her real name, but... she's not all that surprised by this cop-show questioning, is she?
"I'm from the police. It's for the paperwork."
"Why indeed? Forget it."
"Must have taken it as a sign when he found it abandoned like that. Said it was an *augury*. I don't know where he got that from." She smiles. "Andre's not super intelligent..."
"He's real hard core about the lifestyle."
"What do you think of the crab-man?"
"Tell me about Soona."
"Oh, the crab-man." She shudders. "Still gives me the creeps, the way he moves... But he doesn't actually come down that much, just climbs around the rafters."
"What does he do up there?"
"Thanks. About the others..."
"Oh, he talks to Noid? What for?"
"Beats me... Noid said they get along, somehow. They're both crazy enough, I guess."
"Who knows?" She shrugs. "He doesn't really answer our questions, see. Not that it's easy to ask them. What are we supposed to do, yell up at the tower?"
There's that phrase again. It really reminds you of... *something*.
Hang on, that phrase. You're suddenly reminded of... *something*.
"Uh... she's a bit odd, I have to say. Doesn't talk much. I'm not really sure how to vibe with her, y'know? Seems like she's not in a very good mood most of the time."

"But earlier today she told me about... welkins?" Acele grimaces, as if it's the first time hearing the word. "And she seemed oddly happy. Like she had had some idea with those... little creatures. Some artistic idea. I didn't really listen, I was busy with my mic."
"I just try to stay away from the crab-man, but he talks to Noid. They seem to have some 'thing' going on."
A very common name.
"This?" She breathes on her freezing fingers. "It's a portable recording device. It's for field recording. Low quality, but still."
"And the wires?"
"What's a 'contact microphone'?"
"A contact mic records sounds from inside things. Like this ice."
Your mangled brain would like you to know there is a boxer called Contact Mike.
"You know, Contact Mike doesn't *just beat people up*. Contact Mike is a role model."
"Actually just one wire, I picked on it till the braiding came loose. The wire leads to a contact microphone."
"Does this have anything to do with Contact Mike?"
"How does that thing work?"
"Uh..." She's confused. "Yeah, I record stuff with it."
"The mic? I don't exactly know. Somehow it doesn't pick up vibrations from the air. The box said it only picks up *structure-borne sound*. If you like technobabble."
"I... don't know what that means."
"No, I mean the boxer Contact Mike."
"No, I mean... forget it."
"Sorry, I don't know why I said that. There was something else I wanted to know..."
Yeah? Any news on my own name?
Nope.
What am I supposed to do with this?
No idea.
"Ah! No. This is a *contact microphone*, it's for recording *inside* solid objects. Contact Mike just beats people up."
"What's The Paliseum?"
"Oh man, you haven't been to The Paliseum?" She forgets herself for a moment. "It's *the* coolest place in this whole drug-addled shithole."
You're welcome.
"Yes?"
"Sure."
"Where did you get the mic from?"
"Same place I got the recorder from. The Paliseum."
"Tell me more about the microphone."
"Never mind all that. I had questions about that mic..."
"Mhm..." She breathes on her fingers again to warm them. "Thought so."
"Yeah, I got that, but what *don't* you have a problem with?"
"Oh yeah..." She looks you over, assessing your age. "Guess you wouldn't know van Eyck. Or really be a Paliseum-going kind of person... "
"Sounds like a place for congregating homo-sexuals."
"Yeah, there might be some. I don't think they look down on the homo-sexual underground there. The Paliseum's not that kind of place. It's cool."
"Sounds interesting. Who is this *Arno* guy?"
"Never mind, let's talk about that contact mic instead..."
"I get down."
"You're right. Time has deserted me."
"Because I have a problem with homo-sexuals. Major problem."
"Don't get me wrong. I'm all for it. This *Paliseum* just sounded like their kind of place."
"What *don't* you have a problem with?"
"That's real cool. Hope you don't mind missing out on all that great homo-sexual content the world has got to offer."
"Okay then. That's cool."
"I don't know what that means either."
"On second thought, let's go back to the contact mic."
"I grind."
"Oh no, you completely misunderstood me. I might be a homo-sexual myself."
"Oh! Well, good for you."
She breathes on her fingers. Looks like she doesn't know what to say.
"Self respect is not meant to float any boats but your own."
"Yes, you heard right. You should try to be more like Contact Mike: a successful athlete and an *inspirational figure* who has overcome social, physical, and mental obstacles."
"Man, you are one weird cop."
"Neither do I actually. I have no idea what I'm talking about. Get down? Grind?"
"Okay, if it floats your boat I'll be more like Contact Mike and less like me."
"What is it with you and this Mike guy?" She pauses. The question is rhetorical.
"It means I'm hip beyond my years."
"Nor do I, but I have concrete evidence that I rock. In the form of a wrecked tape player and a completely trashed hostel room."
"That's cool." She breathes on her fingers. Looks like she doesn't know what to say.
"I also have a problem with alcohol."
"Fuck that! I'm completely problem free, you can't tell me otherwise."
"Actually, I had some non-mic questions for you."
"You do understand it all just sounds like Mike to me, right?"

"On second thought, screw Contact Mike. He's not a champion -- you are! Look at you here in front of a saggy tent, picking your nose to drug-addict music. The world of sports is in awe of your faith and dedication."
"This isn't about me. This is about your lack of respect for one of boxing's greats -- and for *yourself*."
"Yes, that does indeed float my boat."
"I'd say I'm just about normal. Now about that mic -- Not Mike. Mic."
"Recording, I guess."
"And what is it you're recording exactly?"

"I *think* I'm recording cracks in the ice, but there's no way to tell. Not without headphones. I think I just recorded your footsteps, too. Not sure how that will sound..." She scratches her forehead.
"Yup." She squints her eyes a little. "They were pretty... I'm sorry we sold those."
"Wait, what happened to the headphones?"
"And what are these recordings for -- the cracks, the footsteps?"
It's probably amphetamine -- It makes you *feel* impervious to the elements, but doesn't actually make you any less cold.
"My boyfriend sold them."
"Music stuff mostly. Like this tape recorder, but bigger. And there's piles of it."
"What for?"
"I don't know, man... things. Just stuff you need for life."
A lie. They were probably pawned off for something ssssuspicious.

"The musicians in The Paliseum use them for making music. They loop the stuff, cutting the tapes together. They make music out of cracks in the ice and keys jangling... crazy sounds like that. It's hard to explain."
"You mean like those headphones your boyfriend sold."
Just nod.
"They got too much stuff crammed in there. No room."
"Anyway, I thought I'd make some, too. It's supposed to be, like, a music place anyway..." She rubs her shoulders and looks around.
"I don't really know what I'm doing. They use synthesizers, too. I don't have a synthesizer."
"Stuff like what?"
She looks at the recording device, the thing she thought would fill her hours with joy and escape. It's turning out to be an empty fantasy. She feels childish, very useless all of a sudden.
The sharp drop in endorphins is almost visible. Like a warm blanket has fallen off her shoulders -- the wave of chill, the quivering jaw. Indications of a drug high.
She is on some kind of stimulant -- amphetamine or mephedrone -- and its effects are wearing off fast. She will begin to experience more and more valleys now. And fewer peaks.
"Take this, you're cold." The lieutenant begins to take off his jacket.
"Now *this* is where a hat would come in handy."
"No man, fuck that, I'm cool... I'm sorry I said that. I'm sorry about the *fuck*."
"Why? Why can you take it?"
"It's okay." The lieutenant backs up. He throws you a glance.
"Why not just leave some of it outside so you don't have to freeze?"
"Yeah... maybe you were right about the hat."
"I got my recordings to do, I feel better outside..." A wave breaks close-by and covers her in a cold spray.
"You said *it's* supposed to be a music place. What is?"
"I had some other questions." (Conclude.)
"Why are you freezing out here, while the boys are inside?"
"That." She nods toward the church. "The boys think it could be a *place*, like The Paliseum or something. Stupid. It's really..." she pauses, "not gonna be a Paliseum, that's for sure."
"That stuff is more expensive than I am. More expensive than any of us, really. Doesn't matter. I can take the cold."
"The boys?"
"Yeah, Andre and the guys. They're inside. In the tent."
She's shivering a bit.
"All right then."
"See? That's the appropriate way to give a girl a hat..."
(Let it go.) "Got it..."
Sigh.
"No, man. Fuck it, I'm cool... I'm sorry I said that. I'm sorry about the *fuck*."
"Want my jacket?" (Start taking it off.)
(Give her your hat.) "Here. You need this more than I do."
"Thanks." She puts it on. It's a bit large for her.
And why is that?
"Have you been questioned before?"
"Once or twice, yeah. I'm sorry I haven't had the *Revachol experience* they get east of the river."
"Well, it's just questioning, right? You're questioning me -- it's what cops do."
"We do, don't we? Mind if I question you some more?"
Fast and clean! A good one. Can't quite say it's a lie, but feels like one. She's better at lying than she'd like everyone to know.
"Why did you need to move out at such tender age?"
The girl is truly proud of herself.
"Okay... it's a huge ghetto just south of Jamrock."
"My dad was a drunk. Plus, I guess I just wanted to drink too, you know? Get my *party on*."
"What's east of the river?"
"So, what trouble you've gotten into -- with the police."
"I *know* what Jamrock is but... let's say I didn't."
"*Rich* people. Rich people are east of the river."
"What's *the usual*?"
(Look awestruck.) "Who are these *rich people*? They sound wonderful! I'd like to be one too."
"Good luck crossing that river on your police salary then."
(Sneer.) "I bet they're *really* rich. They must be very special people to be so rich..."
"Drinking, partying and disco music are bad for you. You should take me as a warning example."
(Lean in and whisper.) "Let me guess, these rich people are not from around here..."
"Strange. The existence of rich people does not stir any emotions in me."
"You know, drinking, getting into fights. The ugly stuff that happens when you move out of your parents' place at thirteen. In Faubourg."
"Bet they like it that way," she mutters. Quietly, under her breath.

A respectful nod. You proved something here.
A pincer manoeuvre.
Dammit, take it, don't you just want to see what's *in* there?
Catch it.
"THE CAGE OF THE RAGE, ROUGH BLAZE!"
"Egg means the situation is monitored." The man nods grimly. "It's 'relatively' safe. No one has died yet."
"Sure, man. Tell us what you wanna know, let's do it!"
Glimpses? Who are these people, secret agents? Stealth operatives?
This machinery is of the deeply mystical variety.
For this man even regular silence is awful enough. But that was... something greater.
"The woman -- red hair maybe? A lorry-woman?"
"Sure, why not! Yeah!"
"But not really," the other one adds. "Brown hair. Old. Heavy, dark sines."
So brown and older? Ruby might have dyed her hair? Though it seems like a stretch at this point.
Ruby's gone. The woman is someone else.
"So which one is it?"
"What Noid said!"
You have to see for yourself. These people are not reliable.
Odd. Crabs are usually marine creatures. And not known for climbing walls.
There probably is no crab-man. Don't let them draw you in with this nonsense.
The implications of this are... too numerous to consider. Proceed with caution. Learn all you can before entering that dark building.
Why not! Let's go with that.
"Sure. What?"
It's like he's lying to you, my liege. But he's slippery enough that there's nothing for you to grab hold of.
A shrug is good enough for us! Why say it when you can *shrug* it.
Keep on it, sire.
You're not *completely* satisfied yet.
He nods enthusiastically. No doubt a *little* relieved.
So he hasn't even been in there lately? Is he afraid?
Must be. Even Cuno knew that.
"Right. I don't really want to hear about what happened in the tent. Let's get going."
"Hmm... I heard about the assault after it had already gone down."
"What a shame. Look at all the damage done to the church..."
A young man with peroxide blond hair holds up a Harmon-Wowshi tape player, nodding along to the music. He looks at you with a knowing smile and says...
....as though you're supposed to be sharing some tremendous, evangelical secret...
"Hard core."
"Is it?"
Say nothing.
"HARD CORE TO THE MEGA!"
Still say nothing.
"But is it? I mean, really?"
"HAAAAAAARD COOORE!!! AAAAAAAIGHH!!!" He lets out an agonized roar over the feeble-ish, obviously not too hard core beat below.
"HARD CORE!"
Say nothing.
"INTERNALLY COHERENT!"
Still say nothing.
"IT'S HAAAAAAAAARD CORE!"
"SO HARD CORE!"
"No, but seriously... I'm a little worried it isn't."
"YEAAGHH!"
This young man adds a capital *G* before the *H* in his *YEAGHs* and *AAGHs*. This produces a guttural, *Gottwaldian* accent and makes him sound more animal, more *in it*.

Or maybe it's not Gottwaldian, maybe it's *Oranjese* -- probably an homage to Oranje, where Arno van Eyck is from, judging by his name. Could you be listening to an Arno van Eyck creation *right now*?
"Is it, though?" He stops dead in his tracks, tilting his head to the side.
The skin on your back is crawling. For a second you can't even hear the music anymore.
There is a hawthorn tree on Rue de Saint-Ghislaine, right next to the canal.
"IT IS!"
"I was just thinking that a moment ago!"
"ONE MIND! ONE SPIRIT! THERE IS NO OTHER WORLD -- THERE IS NO OTHER LIFE!"
"The question is, what is the question?"
"I am the mic enforcer, I am the chicks checker, YEAGH!"
Say nothing.
"But is it? I mean, really?" He tilts his head to the other side, like an owl.
"THE QUESTION IS, WHAT IS THE QUESTION?!"
"I was thinking that too!"
"No, but seriously... I'm a bit worried it isn't." He frowns, then starts bobbing his head back and forth once more.
"There's nothing wrong with it. I'm still in love with the hard core." He turns pensive all of a sudden.
Don't be alarmed! Everything is okay. He isn't actually *worried*. Everything is still super hard core! What he probably means is -- it could be even more so!
"Isn't something holding it back? From being hyper?" He thinks for a moment, then his expression clears...
"You said you were worried. What do you think is wrong with the music?"
"Are you a thought reader?"
"Is your real name *Germaine*?"
"NO NATION, BUT TRANCE NATION! NO WAR, BUT CLASS WAR!"
"Does that mean you're a thought reader?"
"So you're not a thought reader, you're a communist?"
"He's not a communist. That's just something he likes to yell. He picked it up from a tape-jockey at The Paliseum... *she* was a communist though."
"YEAH! WITH A REBEL YELL!"
"But why aren't you a communist? Communism is the truth."

dialoguetext: "I can be a communist!" He nods. "If you want that -- do you want me to be a communist?!"
"Please don't turn him into a communist."
"Oh yeah, turn him into a communist, c'mon! It would be super!"
"Be a communist, Egg Head. The future needs your help."
"Don't be a communist... wait, what am I saying? Of course be a communist!"
"Don't be a lunatic. Of course he isn't. Germaine here just yells random things. Odds are, sooner or later one of them will come off as thought reading."
"Yeah! REVACHOL IMPERATIVE!"
"Unless you were thinking 'REVACHOL IMPERATIVE' right now... Anyway, I've had a similar thing happen with Egg's yelling, I know what you mean."
(Lie.) "But I *was* thinking 'Revachol imperative'!"
"So it's the world that's the thought reader?"
So, it's not this one. It's the world that's the thought reader in this equation?
THE WORLD IS A COLD SINK.
YOU ARE IN ITS ARMS.
The young man picks up a level and inspects it against the floodlight. The water sparkles in the small measuring tube. "Yes," he says after a while. "I think it's correct to say that."
"AIIIIIGH!!!" he yells. You guess he is a communist now.
"That's fucked up, man. Lying like that. And a cop too..."
"Tell me something else, Egg Head..."
"Yeaaargh!"
"Don't be a communist. That path is *too* hard core."
"AIIIIIGH!!!" he yells. You guess he won't become a communist after all.
"You're right, I wasn't thinking that."
"Hard Core Superstar!"
"Yeagh!"
"Right on, comrade luminary!"
"Almost there. Could use just a bit more work..."
"You're wrong. Communism doesn't rule the nation."
"I'm sorry."
The young man drops his oversized head in shame. He is truly sorry he couldn't come up with a proletarian yell that would satisfy The Great Leader.
"HERE COMES THE SUN!"
"The worker must MOVE YOUR ASS!"
"Superb!"
"No, that's still not it."
You could swear you feel the bright future of the working classes reflected off Germaine Egg Head's giant smile and right onto your face! Revolution makes your toes curl in anticipation.
"It's like it's only *ultra*."
"I think it's super hard core, but you're right, it's not *hyper* hard core."
"I am The Law and an expert in these matters. Let me be the judge of what it is: hyper, super, or ultra hard core."
"It's hyper hard core."
"It's super hard core."
The young man looks at you reverently, as if observing the judgement inside your head. Growing, taking form.
If anything, it sounds a bit *proto*. Like it's not fully formed yet. You might be a moribund alcoholic and a failed cop, but you are pretty certain a thing cannot be both *proto* and *hard core*.
"It's only ultra hard core."
"It's proto -- not hard core at all."
"How much is the fish?"
"I could settle it for you, but not right now. Tell me something else, Egg Head."
In the background, his friend drops a heavy electric drill. He, too, waits for your judgement with undivided attention.
"This is a serious matter. Stop talking about fish. Fish has got nothing to do with this."
"Psst..." You can hear the would-be leader whisper to his friend: "Don't let him know he doesn't understand the fish thing."
"We can all hear it's not hyper hard core. If figures of authority keep telling us things are hyper, when they're clearly not -- how are we ever supposed to evolve to hyperdom?"
"It is, isn't it?!" He nods in agreement. "I knew it!"
"Fuck yeah, I knew it!"
"You can't. But you do."
"I don't really have an answer for this. Tell me something else, Egg Head."
The young man smiles and nods. Slowly he picks up two hammers at once.
"THE R, THE C, THE M, THE THEOLOGY! AROOO!"
RCM? That's the acronym for Revachol Citizens Militia -- you! Does everything this man yells mean something? Is it truly *internally coherent*?
"Okay, I've changed my mind."
"Uhuh?" The young man raises the tape player higher in anticipation.
"WHOAH! Culture Cop!"
For a moment you almost think he's going to put the tape player down. But that would be ludicrous.
"I think you might be right! But how could it *become* hard core then? I know it in my heart, but cannot think it in my head. If this is not hard core, how could anything be..."
He *seems* sure, but you are left with the nagging doubt you might have overestimated the hard coreness of that jam...
"But how could it *become* harder-core? I know the answer in my heart, but cannot think it in my head. If this is not hyper, how could anything be..."
"Wait! I just remembered something! I'm the police!"
Try to think if anything could make it... harder-core?
"Uh-uh?" The young man is bursting with anticipation!
"And I have a job to do instead of this absurd idiocy! Goodbye." [Leave.]
"Nothing. Me being the police isn't going to help us."
"Actually, it's more likely to *hinder* us."
"I can't help you with this right now. I need something else, something *extra*..."
"YEAGHH!" (He's not even the slightest bit disappointed.)
As your mind works, the beat recedes from your ears. You hear your own blood pulsing through your head, nourishing your thoughts with oxygen. The rhythm is familiar...

The abstract shapes swelling in the foreground have done so in vain. This is a core matter. The answer, in the double-kick that moves the millilitres through your mind. The dark thud is the source of all rhythm, the inspiration behind mathematics...
"Whaaaat?!" He looks at you with customary amazement. "Guys, there's something happening in his head!"
Think even harder.
But you're not. This is almost certainly a matter that surpasses the limits of reason.
Feel the movement of blood through your head.
"Oh yeah! He's DOING it!"
The hard core.
"My imagination fails me."
"I know, so does mine!" He laughs and shakes his head.
Did someone say *disco*?
No, that would be silly. Your body isn't for thinking. It's for robust, wholesome things. Things like discus, javelin, and 400 metre hurdles. Mmm... discus.
Maybe your body can tell you what Arno van Eyck's jam is missing? To make it... harder core.

"Sometimes I just feel like anodic music is in its infancy, you know? For example, take this Arno van Eyck jam I've been pumping for the last month... and will continue pumping for the rest of '51..."
"Sounds suspiciously like a *question*. I thought the question was: What is the question?"
"No, this is THE ANSWER!"
"Alright. Goodbye, Egg Head." [Leave.]
"Alright! HERE COMES THE NIGHT!"
"D'accord hard core! Germaine Egg-Head."
"You know about him..." He moves his mouth, but sound doesn't come out. His eyes are the size of saucers. Looks like you've rendered him speechless.
"Who is this "van Eyck"? Did he make this music?"
"So this is the famous van Eyck I'm hearing?"
"Uhm, basically, yes it is."
"You know van Eyck?"
He's overcome with some mysterious emotion. It's not merely adoration for what a Hard Cop you are either. It's more. Could it be *gratitude*?
"Yeah, I'm a major Eyck-head."
"Your friend Acele mentioned him."
"No, it was just a turn of phrase."
You know it in your lungs where the pressure should vibrate, in your heart that's alone, and in your solar plexus where the hits should land... so does every chordate animal...
"Back to the heavyweight jam!" says the young man with the tape player and the large boiadeiro boots. Lung-shaped trees sprout on his silver belt buckle.
The young man with the tape recorder acknowledges your return. When he looks at you, he squints as though you were the setting sun...
"You're just gonna keep saying it's *hard core*, aren't you?"
"I don't know what to say to that."
"Skibadee, skibadanger! I am the rearranger!"
Could there have been a *right* way out of this garden of forking paths, you think?
"YeaaaaaaGH!"
"Yeaaaah!"
"You can *yeah* and say random things all day long, but the track still doesn't sound all that *hard* to me."
"Lakierski materialski!"
"Spinning out lyrics since the day I was born."
"And the amount of lyrics I got is against the law!"
"The Y to the E to the A to the A to the A to the A to the A to the G to the H to the exclamation mark..."
"YeaaaaaGH!"
He missed one 'A'!
"You missed an 'A' there. I yelled mine with six 'A'-s, so you have to yell it with six too."
"You missed an 'A' there, but that's okay. I'm a pretty lenient cop."
"It's nice to be important, but it's more important to be nice!"
"I'm the hard rhymer, the track attacker, the mic enforcer, the *six* checker! I am the law!"
"Alright!"
"HERE COMES THE NIGHT!"
"I was wondering if you knew who killed the mercenary hanging behind the Whirling-in-Rags hostel?"
"Good morning, yeah! One, two, three! Yekokataa, the place to be!"
"Please tell me, what exactly are you doing?"
"Good morning! Yeaaaaaah! Pump it up, pump it up, pump it up!"
"I am beginning to think this really doesn't have anything to do with the case."
"Why is this *Yekokataa* the place to be? What does that mean?"
"It's the message so listen and you will see. No illusion, the spirit is what you feel!"
"Yekokataa is a hard core place!"

"Yekokataa" is an abbreviation from the Graadian term "Zone of Ecological Catastrophe," an agricultural megaproject in the extreme south east of the Graadian isola. It involved cutting-edge approaches to irrigation and a completely new type of fertilizer.

An intricate system of irrigation networks pockmarking the earth, intermittent seas of phosphorous mud, ripped tarpaulin fluttering in the wind... A pair of molten rubber boots also comes to mind. All in all -- a truly hard core place.
"ALL CORE! ALL RIGHT! YEAH!"
"I'm the party boy, it's my job!"
"What is a party boy?"
"HARD CORE PARTY 25/7 BEYOND THE WINTER'S ORBIT STYLE!"
"I think I'm also a party boy."

There is a place far away in Katla, beyond a certain latitude known as *winter's orbit*, where there are 25 hours in a day. It is a tremendously cold place, abandoned to drunks and failed rock stars. Full of eternite, depression and half finished ski flying hills. The Suru live there.
"Gotta get the people going!"
"Why?"
"Two on a track, watch your back, watch out for the heart attack!"
"I see."
"Yeah, request! I want everybody as close to the stage as possible!"
"That would have been good, if I had asked you a question. But I didn't. Now it's just idiotic."
"Just answer the question!"
"But there was a question..."
"But there was no question..."
"This is hard core."
"Hard core!"
"We're close!" says the young man with the tape player and the large boiadeiro boots. Lung-shaped trees sprout on his silver belt buckle.
"True, hard, full core!"
"I don't know what to say exactly..."
Feels like you should reply with the very pinnacle of idiocy here, so that things get totally transcendent. But you haven't gotten there yet, so you don't know what to say.
"Under the radar, OVER THE TOP!"
"Why are there lungs on your belt buckle?"
"Needs more bass."
"What?!" The young man makes a sudden move, like he's about to turn the volume down. But that would be ridiculous.
"Wow, okay! We should start with the melody. But where would we get that stuff from?"
"I don't know. I was thinking *you* would know..."
"Nowhere. I'm not gonna become some sort of Anodic Cop too, I've got enough copotypes already."
"Oh..." For a moment he doesn't know what to say.
"Okay, I get it, man. The party goes on!"
"I'm sorry, I don't know anything about anodic music, I'm just the party boy. I get the people going and say it's hard core..."
He feels ashamed he can't be of more service to the future of dance music.
There is a hawthorn tree on Rue de Saint-Ghislaine, right next to the canal. A reel of magnetic tape is caught in its branches, like bronze ribbons blowing in the wind...
"Before I go on, where is Rue de Saint-Ghislaine?"
"It feels cold."
Shake it off.
"Oh, I know! I know this! I can tell you where it is!"
"Saint-G is the boulevard before the canal bridge. The one that takes you to the Whirling-in-Rags and the Industrial Harbour. It's got the lanterns and the---"
"I knew that! I could have said that!"
"And the mosaic sidewalk."
"Does it?" He looks around, looking for the cold.
The large-headed youth has closed his eyes, lost in the music. Sensing you, he opens them...
"Lungs are for love!"
"Good to know."
"Why would lungs be for love?"
"When Dolores Dei was anointed innocence, her lungs started glowing through her body, for the world loved her and she loved it back! YEAGH!"
"Really?"
"I think so."
"That doesn't sound like a thing that would happen."
"But that's what everybody saw. Explain it as you please, but it doesn't really do to just deny it ever happened."
"Oh. Well, it really is him. It's an honest to god van Eyck beat. Well, actually a reworking of a Pepi Popikarnassos track, but let's not get too deep into that whole mess."
"Good, good."
"Wow!"
The skinny wraith looks at you with some disbelief.
"This is Arno van Eyck! ARE YOU READY?"
"So am I! SO AM I!" He begins to shake his head so everyone would understand.
"Oh!" Andre almost falls over backward from the realization. "Is *that* why they call you Egg Head, because..."
"Eyck-Head to the mega! The K became the G! The boy became the man!"
"THE ADVENT!"
"Oh yeah. That makes perfect sense."

"LOVE!" he suddenly yells and the world seems to stop. "In a woman's lungs! Lonely as I am, I'm not afraid! This strange, damaged feeling grows on and on, 'cause I've never loved someone like you before!"
"Bourgeois love from a bourgeois god-queen towards a world getting rapidly more bourgeois, that's lungs for you."
"Objectively, it was good for its time. And they sort of screwed it up after she passed, like they always do."
"Don't listen to that retrograde class warrior, Egg."
"L'amour, la compassion, l'autodiscipline."
"Thank you for the story."
"Rhymes that keep their secrets will unfold behind the clouds!"
Why wouldn't they be? Are the lungs not the place where you hold the breath of your soul?
"Well. The lungs are where you hold the breath of your soul, aren't they?"
"Heiligeili!"
A dopamine surge accompanies the words. It feels like electricity flowing down your scalp, dissipating into your neck. Feels good, like a spark of life in that moribund sponge you call your body.
"Okay, I'll look into it. In an official capacity. It's up to the police to make the beats go harder." (Take the task.)
"Alright, I'll see if I come up with something on my own. A citizen investigation." (Take the task.)
"No, I really don't have time for this." (Don't take the task.)
The young man falls silent with appreciation. He even tries to contain his smile, as if it could hinder your investigation.
"And a melody. A good melody is what makes the song really *stick*, so that you can't get it out of your head anymore." (Point at your head.)
"Dolorian church, the place to be! Make some noise, my church people!" Large speakers are set up behind the young man, blasting a familiar song.
"It's good you're not a communist anyway. You should be an ultraliberal."

dialoguetext: "I can be an ultra!" He nods. "If you want that -- do you want me to be an ultra?!"
"Please don't turn him into an ultraliberal."
"AIIIIIGH!!!" he yells. You guess Egg Head is an ultraliberal now.
"Oh geez, please don't do that. There's enough exploitation in the world."
"Don't be an ultraliberal. That path is *too* hard core."
"Be an ultraliberal, Egg Head. Capital needs your help."
"Don't be an ultra... wait, what am I saying? Of course be an ultraliberal!"
"AIIIIIGH!!!" he yells. You guess Egg Head won't become an ultraliberal after all.
"I can do that!" He nods. "If you want that -- I can be a conduit for the mystical nationhood!"
"Please don't turn him into a fascist."
"AIIIIIGH!!!" he yells. You guess Egg Head is a fascist now.
"Oh yeah, sure, this is *exactly* what we need."
"Don't be a fascist. That path is *too* hard core."
"Be a fascist, Egg Head. Our future needs your help."
"Don't be a fascist... wait, what am I saying? Of course be a fascist!"
"AIIIIIGH!!!" he yells. You guess Egg Head won't become a fascist after all.
"Oh sure, I can do that!" He nods. "If you want that -- I can avoid taking a stand!"
"Please don't turn him into a moralist."
"AIIIIIGH!!!" he yells. You guess Egg Head is a moralist now.
"I don't... even know what to say to that."
"Don't be a moralist. That path requires a sensible examination of all nuances unattainable to most people."
"Be a moralist, Egg Head. The balance needs your help."
"Don't be a moralist... wait, what am I saying? You should consider your choice carefully and rationally."
"AIIIIIGH!!!" he yells. You guess Egg Head won't become a moralist after all.
"I'm sorry."
"You're wrong. Capital doesn't rule the nation."
The young man drops his oversized head in shame. He is truly sorry he couldn't come up with a profitable market strategy.
"THE MARKET REGULATES ITSELF!"
"No, that's still not it."
"Superb!"
"Almost there. Could use just a bit more consolidation, a tad less regulation..."
"EAT THE POOR!"
"Right on, Lord Raubritter!"
You swear you feel the profit margins reflecting off Germaine Egg Head's giant smile.
"I'm sorry."
"You're wrong. The nation can't bend all to its will."
The young man drops his oversized head in shame. He is truly sorry he couldn't come up with a heart-felt yell that would satisfy The Great Leader.
"WELCOME TO REVACHOL!"
"No, that's still not it."
"Welcome to Revachol!"
"Almost there. Could use just a bit more heart..."
"WELCOME TO REVACHOL! WELCOME TO REVACHOL! MYSTICAL NATIONHOOD!"
"Welcome to Revachol!"
The bright future of Revachol reflects off Germaine Egg Head's giant smile. A world of Revacholian domination, where its shores are bereft of ill influence.
"INCREMENTAL CHANGE!"
"Appropriate."
"Almost there. Could use just a bit more... something..."
"I'm swiftly moving toward a solution which pleases nobody!"
"Obviously. One shouldn't get too hasty with their decision-making."
You feel Germaine Egg Head's smile is too enthusiastic, but it'll have to do, for now.
"Yeah..."
He stands on stage behind a table, nodding along to the music and waving his hand in the air. In front of him -- the audio mixer, one reel spinning.
A hawthorn tree on Rue de Saint-Ghislaine. Tangled in its branches, something bronze flutters in the wind...
"Good morning! YEEAAAHHH!" He waves his hand in the air. "Harder core!" The words echo magnificently throughout the nave.
Vibrations thump through your blue soul. The music sounds much better in the church.
For a moment you almost think he's going to put his hand down. But that would be ludicrous.
But there's something else that hasn't failed you...
"Oh no, please become one... you'll miss out on so much good content otherwise. It's like being the greatest cop on earth!"
"Please. Please?" The young man smiles at you widely, bright and innocent as the summer sun.
His pleaful smile is disarming, but you can withstand it's glorious assault, if you just put your heart into it.
You don't have time for this nonsense. You've got safe boring things to do.
"Yeeaaaagh! Back on the case, no disgrace!" He pumps his fist in the air. "Bring it down to party place!"
"How do you like it in the church?"
"THE FIRST PAGE OF THE SECOND CHAPTER!" His voice echoes all around the grand hall.
"I found this reel of tape, maybe you can use it to hard-up Eyck's jam." (Give him the fixed hawthrone tree tape.)
"Hey, I have a tape with me, maybe you can use it to improve van Eyck's jam."

dialoguetext: "But... it needs to be played, on the turntable. And it's broken." Seeing this abuse of music brings a twinge of sadness to his face.
"Wait, what do you mean?"
"Alright, where can I get it repaired?"
"Look around! You gotta help it, help it survive. Can't leave the tune like this." He hands back the bundle of magnetic tape.
"Tape goes around spool. I spin the world 'round, with my mic in the ground! Yeeaaaahhh!"
"Tape, yeah!" He grins. "Spin the tape until the space escape, yeah!"
"I got you this banging Megamix." (Give him the Great Doorgunner Megamix.)
"What about this one?" (Give him the Smallest Church in Saint-Saëns.)
"Aiiight!" He snatches the tape from your hand and attaches it to the empty reel slot. One hand on his headphones, he listens to the audio. Then, shaking his head, he says:
"Righteous!" He takes the tape and attaches it to the empty reel slot. Hand over ear, he listens, then shakes his head:
"No. No, no, this is gonna make people scared!" He hands the tape back to you. "Keep it positive, keep the *love* in the house!"
"No. No, can't do, this is gonna make people sad! This isn't sad-core." He hands the tape back to you.
"I found this over at downtown Martinaise." (Give him the bundle of magnetic tape.)
"Okay, never mind."
"Yeagh, re-mix time!" His voice booms through the church as he takes the tape and attaches it to the empty reel slot. "Tape goes here -- into deck B." He clicks a switch, the tape starts spinning...
A hand on his ear, he listens to the audio through his headphones, and shouts...
"Wow..." His face lights up with delight. "Did you get this from Arno himself?"
"Whooh, hear that?!" He wipes his brow. "The sines match perfectly!"
"The sines match perfectly!"
No, this is definitely part of the same song. Something cut from it. It fits too well.
"What is this?" Acele looks up from her contact mic. "It's *good*. How did you guys do that?"
"Do what? I just found a random tape and brought it to Egg Head. He's just incredibly good at remixing."
"You're right, it's uncanny how well it all goes together. Something else must be going on here..."

"Yes, but what if van Eyck based his remix on some forgotten local melody -- like a folk song? And you just found the original piece that inspired him to create this jam. That would explain why it fits so well."

Look at the sticker.

Run your hand over a beam.
Back up and look at the door.

Au revoir, sticker!

A great whoosh of air rushes into the dark innards of the church, as though rushing to fill a great vacuum...
Feels like electricity and a very small piece of nothingness.
The pathetic old wood, rusty screws (and one nail) stand no chance against the forces of *leverage*. From deep within, a bellow rips...

Look at the broken tool in your hand.
The broken edge of the snapped prybar is smooth. Took the tip right off...
A bad omen. Beware of this church.
This was surely just a freak accident.
As you do, you hear and the echo of the Doomed Commercial Area. Its black halls and dusty machines. Then the feeling passes.
Nice try, son, but this is not something you should be attempting to do with your bare hands.

There is a touch of something in his voice. Hard to say what.

These forces of future have chosen to depict something that reminds you of... you.

There's something on the sea ice there.
Your muscles do not know. This shouldn't happen. You're sure the wood looked weak.

...but just *imagine* the moves you could pull to this futuristic beat!

Don't be fooled. He's watching you to make sure you don't act unprofessionally.
(Look at her) "You seem surprised that I made it."
She chuckles. "Drinking men aren't known for keeping their appointments."
The wind ruffles her hair as she looks at the sunlit coast across the water.
"Here it comes," she says. As she turns back to the sea, the weather begins to clear under her steady gaze.
"That's the second time you've done that! Are you some kind of sea witch?"
"Wait... did *you* just do that?"
"You know, I have special abilities too. Pa-ra-na-tu-ral abilities."
As she turns to face the sun reflected in the waves and the skyscrapers rising across the bay, you cannot help following her steady gaze.
"Me? No, no, no." She laughs. "Just grew up on the sea. Know which way the wind's blowing and all."
"Knew the weather'd clear up once we got here -- otherwise it would've been a less pleasant stroll, nay?"
"Wait, do you think *I* did that? Nay, I just grew up on the sea, that's all. Know which way the wind is blowing."
"As for your 'paranatural abilities' -- I'd love to hear about them sometime, really, but can't we just enjoy the view for a moment?"

The sun reflected in the waves and the skyscrapers rising across the bay is mesmerizing. Your mind clears for a moment as your senses take it all in -- not just the glass skyscrapers, fragile-looking in the shimmering air, River Esperance flowing into the bay...

"Isn't it strange," she breaks the silence abruptly, "For this all-powerful thing, the sun... to be so generous towards us? You know, the best time to go out fishing is usually toward sunset, when the water is warmer..."

There's salt in the air and the cries of the gulls and the skuas; grit of the sand and the green glint of broken bottles. But still your gaze always returns to the dazzling streaks of light, wherever they may be reflected, their opulence...
Across the rusty water -- that's La Delta, the financial district. In the mist-covered distance, towers rise as a rebuke to the poverty of this coast.
The sun also falls on the cape-side tenements and war-torn ruins. An old sea fortress juts out, seemingly impervious to the sheen cast over everything else, shaking you out of your reverie...

"It's bringing us spring, summer... It's entirely on our side, no matter what we do or who we are. For absolutely *no* reason. It's unlike no other powerful being -- certainly no powerful organisation, or government? How can that be?"
"I'm not sure desert people are happy with too much sunlight."
"Is that why you named your boat 'The Sun'?"
Just enjoy the view. (Continue.)
"Oh, that was a bit of pride, and a bit of superstition..."
The Sun does little for the dead, and those hopelessly lost in their own minds.
Or people living in desert climates with sparse vegetation and little drinking water.
The sun isn't always that great. Think of people living in desert climates with sparse vegetation and little drinking water.
And a bit of conceptual unity too, it being yellow and all...
"Now you're just nitpicking." She smiles. "But aye, I concede -- maybe *desert people* sometimes disagree."
"The sun isn't exactly an organisation."
"Well, *something's* gotta be on our side."
"No." She smirks. "And it will outlive them all."
She nods. "I guess we wouldn't really *be* here if that thing wasn't on our team..."
"You have fish-hooks in your ears."
"Do you wish you were out there fishing right now?"
"This was nice. Thank you." (Conclude the date.)
"These?" she turns her head and they dangle. "These aren't real fish-hooks, silly. They're earrings shaped to look like fish-hooks. A drunk called Rosemary brought them to me. I kept them."
"Aye, always do... I like it. It's like being on another planet. A water planet. With water worries... and water joys."
"Don't you want to go visit La Delta?"
"Ha! It's enough that my fish goes there. Fifty reál a piece they ask for spring cod..."
The lieutenant makes a show of glancing at his watch and tapping his foot.
"It didn't suck," she smiles. "I'll let you get back to your business now. The twins probably found a land mine by now..."
No! Keep quiet about your sordid past.
"You know, a past incarnation of myself called himself 'Tequila Sunset.' I wonder why that is."
"It's a common Revacholian expression." She narrows her eyes. "Means drinking yourself to death."
"And what about you? Keeping the name?"
"Found a corpse recently. He'd had a Tequila Sunset moment."
There's a little pause. "So are you going to keep the name?"
"Might as well. I don't really have any others."

dialoguetext: "Well, then..." She shrugs and turns toward the sunlit sea.
"Lately I've been going by Detective Costeau."
"Well, then, detective Costeau." She chuckles and turns toward the sunlit sea.
"Who am I kidding? I'm probably going to drink myself to death whatever name I choose..."
"I think I'm good with Harrier Du Bois these days."
"Harry's my name. I don't need any others."
"This is a new model of me. It will need a new name."
"Well then, Officer Du Bois..." She nods to you, then turns toward the sunlit sea.
"Well then, Harry..." She smiles and turns toward the sunlit sea.
"Can't wait to hear it." She smirks and turns toward the sunlit sea.
"I prefer just going by my initials. It's more conspiratorial that way. Call me H.D.B.!"
"Well then, H.D.B...." She smiles and turns toward the sunlit sea.
"Hell yeah! Tequila Sunset all the way!"

Out on the terrace of Les Fruits de Fond, a hip business lunch spot in downtown La Delta, glasses clink over a spread of oysters. Someone can't decide what to eat. Someone recommends the ceviche. Someone shields her eyes, trying to see across the bay...
"Aye." She nods. "I better head home to the kids."
