Doesn't look like he's imagining it.
"... and realize your mind -- everything that was *you* -- is gone."
"... and realize the man-body, with *you* in it, is just a husk now. All memories -- erased."
"... and realize you've pushed yourself too far. Past the point of no return."
The lieutenant looks up from his notes and nods to the old carabineer.
"I still feel terrible, René. Sickly, panicky, outright sad -- you name it."
The lieutenant sighs audibly, but keeps his eyes on the notebook.
"You're talking about getting black-out shitfaced drunk and going into delirium, right?" he asks impatiently.
"Okay, I admit it -- I got so drunk I forgot even *who* I am."
"Hey, a man needs to decompress every now and then -- nothing wrong with that -- I got it in check."
"Yes, from the looks of it you deserve a medal for the *excellent* handle you have on things." He snorts. "Here, have one of mine!"
Your sarcasm will be your undoing, old man.
His tone is like that of a drill-sergeant addressing new recruits.
He mumbled: "You certainly had me fooled."
Extremely rigid principles this old soldier has, don't leave room for a change of heart or backing out. The medal is yours.
Feels as though you should do more honourable things. As if there's some kind of a... secret reward. If you just commit enough honourable acts.
This feels *honourable*. You did the *right* thing not taking the medal. The *good* thing. Your chest is buzzing with pride.
"I knocked Cuno out" (Point to the yard.) "The kid needed discipline."
"The twelve-year-old junkie, whose alcoholic father beats him?" His eyes light up. "Why did you do that?"
"I needed to make him respect me."
"No, okay -- we're actually cool now. I even stole some drugs from his dad."
"You're right, I shouldn't have hit him."
"He was screaming that I'm trying to molest him, while I clearly wasn't."
"Officer," he says with obvious disdain, "this is unacceptable for anyone bearing an insignia. A man should lead by example, not terror."
"If you don't have any more questions we'll return to our game now." By the looks of it he's still trying to wrap his head around what you told him.
For a moment frozen in time this old soldier is your superior officer, inspiring you to be a better man. It feels good. Comforting.
Well, if you phrase it like that it doesn't sound too good.
"Actually nevermind, I don't wanna lie."
The old soldier shakes his head in disapproval. "What do you want, officer?"
"It took us nearly seven hours. Fifi died in my arms, when the water was only knee deep... She was a good dog."
"Please stop."
"You're right, this isn't very believable, is it?"
"I'm not gonna dignify this with an answer." He frowns. "We're gonna get back to our game now if there isn't anything else, officer?"
"Son..." He's slowly shaking his head. "I don't know why you're feeding me this horse shit, but I'm not biting. Can we get back to our game now?"
"René..." (Lower your voice.) "I'm ex-army too. Special Forces. Black ops. Secret soldier."
"Really?" Suddenly it feels like he's entitled to question you. "What was the unit?"
"The Cyan Berets."
"This information is classified."
"The 5th?"
"Harry's Hounds."
Something with colours and headwear. Soldiers identify with those things.
Say it's *classified*. An old soldier should understand.
Mumble incoherently.
"Actually I don't wanna resort to lying after all."
"Good call." Not a muscle in his face moves as he slowly nods. "Think we can get back to our game now?"
"That's what I thought." He nods. "We'll get back to our game now if you don't mind."
"Are you asking me or telling me?"
"Asking?"
"Telling."
"I'll stop you right there, son." He raises his hand. "I'm old, but I'm not stupid. I *know* a soldier when I see one."
"We'll get back to our game now if you don't mind."
"That's what I thought." He nods. "We'll get back to our game now if you don't mind, *officer*."
"Mhmh..." He nods. "We'll get back to our game now if there isn't anything else?"
Strange, he didn't buy it.
Strange, he didn't buy it.
Odd, he didn't buy it.
"You tell me."
I'd rather just ask him some questions.
Of course, it's your call. But he would have been *really* impressed.
"Was there anything else, officer?" he asks impatiently. Looks like they both want to continue the game.
Unless you wanna tell him how you took Cuno down. The decisiveness you exhibited in that situation would surely impress a man fond of order and discipline.
Lying just isn't my style. I'd rather get back to questions.
But of course, sire. Looks like they're waiting for you to speak.
Just like that. He analysed the situation, accepted the facts and moved on. Like a soldier.
"Of course, officer." He waits for you to speak.
"Already got one, smart ass." He utters through his teeth. "Comes with the rank and my service record."
"Why don't *you* get a tomb yourself!"
"That sounds blissful, but right now I've got some questions for Gaston."
"What do you mean, officer?" He looks startled.
Oh, he knows what you mean. Keeping it to yourself now, may yield some leverage if you ever need it.
"Cut the crap, bozo! I saw you cheating!"
"Getting older does present a whole new set of challenges..." (Keep it to yourself.)
"Ugh... it's not very good, officer. I'm an old man and sciatica is gnawing on my joints." There's a look of hopelessness in his eyes. "Some days the pain is almost too much..."
"I saw what you did there, Gaston. How's your back?"
"Nothing... just a lowly law-man rambling to himself." (Tap on the side of your nose.) "Watch that back."
"Why don't the two of you get a tomb and take your whining there." He looks at you, disgusted. "I am ashamed to even stand in the same crater with you."
"Easy now, René." He snickers. "I *will* join the seniors swimming class later, but right now I don't want to keep the officer waiting -- police business is usually urgent."
"Goddamn right, son!" The old soldier nods in agreement. "No use complaining about it."
"Lately my eyes just aren't the same and even getting out of the bed is pretty difficult..."
"What?!" The man tries to act surprised.
"Uh... thanks. Is there something we can help you with, officer?" He avoids your gaze.
"Should've built yourself a better body, Mossback. The kind that lasts." (Secretly flex.)
"Who did you think you were fooling with your moaning, Gaston?" He doesn't even glance at his partner.
"I know what you mean, officer," he says excitedly. "Then there's the blood sugar and don't even get me started on the bladder troubles..."
"Yes, yes. I'm sorry, officer." The senior is visibly shaking before you.
"Good. Gaston finally understands the rules now." An evil smile runs across his lips. "Let's see if it makes him a better *petanquista*."
"Oh? The goal is to throw your *boule*..." He holds out the orb. "... as close to the *cochonnet* as you can."
"Interesting. Tell me more about it."
"You'll put that knowledge to good use in twenty... I mean fifty years. I'm sure of that officer."
"I think that's all I need to know about pétanque."
"That's the *cochonnet*." He points to a small wooden ball in the middle of the crater.

"Well... first you draw a circle about a half a metre in diameter. We made ours out of rope," he explains. "Then the order of play is determined by a coin toss. You win it -- you get to throw the *cochonnet*."
"Is there *anything* else you can tell me about pétanque?"
"The opponent has a right to re-measure if he has doubts about the result and..." He is trying to think of something else to say, but then -- seeing your beady eyes -- stops.
"I was hoarding information and had a seizure. I'm fine now."
"Sure. We got a case to solve!" [Leave.]
"No. I want to talk to him. I promise it won't be about pétanque."
Is he *denying* you information, when you clearly requested it?! That's it. We're blowing the lid off this man-jar! You *need* to know... things!
"I'm relieved to hear that." He peers at you over his glasses. "Are you well enough to move on to something else now?"
"I don't like where this is going, officer. Don't you think we should do something else now?"
"We should leave quickly before it happens again." He looks around. "Right now is a good moment."
"What was that all about? Some experimental interrogation technique you're honing?"
"Honestly, I don't know what it was."
"Then the players aim to throw their *boules* as close to the *cochonnet* as possible. They must stay in the circle and keep both feet planted."
He sighs. "Hurry up then."
"Trivial? Ha. Ahaha." (Grin at the man.) "You can still tell me, you know. Before anything *happens*."

"Uh..." Your keen interest is making him uncomfortable. "Then there's measuring the distance between the *boule* and the *cochonnet*. I always measure ours, but usually it's done by the player who threw last."
"I could, but I'd rather not." He smiles. "I don't want to take up your time with trivial details, officer."
He's faking.
He got the message.
This guy can act. Not sure I would have caught it if we hadn't *seen* him cheating.
"*Pardon*, René," he quickly turns back to you. "We must pick this up later, I'm helping the officer right now."
"I know what I saw, cheater."
"Actually..."
"The hangovers must be getting worse too... Don't think I used to lose my memory every time I had a little drink..."
"But *not* with a monetary pension unfortunately," the checkered suit snaps at his partner and turns to you. "What can I do for you, officer?"
But do I really and *why*?
Yes, yes, you do. Knowledge is power, bathe in it, empower yourself, trust me.
All that blunt data must have triggered an information hoarding reflex of sorts. Think of it like a small seizure. It will pass.
Can you believe this clown?! This is information you MUST have and he's stalling. Lives *could* be on the line and he's just running out the clock?!
"Stop stalling and talk, goddamnit! Is that all?! Cause I swear to god, if you're holding back..."
"This is getting weird, better hit the brakes."
... aaaaaand that's how you break a man if the good cop and the bad cop have left for the day. Disturbing Cop to the rescue!
"*So* weird... what was that, officer?" The old man is visibly shaken, but tries to force a smile. "Actually, *please*, let's talk about something else."
"You were a rat when we were boys and you are a rat now. Of course I knew!" He spits. "Your deception was so bad at first I thought you were play-acting for my amusement."
"Six months go by and I realize you must think I've gone blind from all the shrapnel in my head. Because only a blind man wouldn't see through that."
He's known Gaston all his life. Probably knows his every move better than himself. Of course he saw right through the deceit.
That guy is a fraud.
If you wanna expose him, get straight to the point. If you start japing about old age, it's *never* gonna happen.
Let's cool Mr. Fight-Or-Flight down, before he kills someone. He gets overstimulated. But seriously, enough with the pétanque already.
Oh, he must have already figured out Gaston's cheating.
"Yeah, how did you know?"

"I know a *Weird Cop* when I see one." The lieutenant adjusts his glasses. "It doesn't work. *Weird Cop* only confuses the suspect and the *Weird Cop* himself, while all he should have done was ask normal questions."
Just please ask them normal questions.
That hurt. The man knows where to sting.
"I don't understand, René..." He looks around with an expression of complete bafflement.
"Yes, officer, yes!!! I swear, I don't know anything else about pétanque! It's all I know, I swear!"
"I think I get it. Thanks, Gaston!"
"Really? You know *absolutely* nothing?"
"Let me think..." He looks at the clouds, wistfully. "I heard someone was hanged and left on a tree for a week, but that's all I know really."
"Shame. Maybe you can help me with something else then."
"Of course, officer, I mean I hope I can." He nods enthusiastically. "What's on your mind?"
"No, officers, I'm sorry. And I really *would* like to assist," he adds, smiling apologetically. "You are both good guys. I can see that."
"Then help him, you wimp." Reproach fills his eyes. "You rub plenty of shoulder with the *gauche caviar* in the Union. Someone *must* know something."
"I wish I could, but I just don't know anything." His cheeks turn red. "I always keep my nose clean and don't gossip. Everyone knows and respects that."
"Sounds a bit like you're holding back."
"Of course he's holding back." The carabineer crosses his arms. "His mouth is so full of Union prick he can't even speak properly."
"Can I at least finish my fucking sentence before you piss on it? Is that okay, René?" His eyes are furious. "I'm not anyone important in the Union. I just know Evrart."
"C'mon, you must have heard something..."
Odd... He doesn't seem to be lying, but there's something off here.
"I'm *not*," he assures you. "I'm not even anyo---"
He means caviar-socialists.
"How do you know Evrart?"
"Are you a Union member?"
"Thanks, that's all for now." (Conclude.)
"Everyone in Martinaise knows the Claire brothers," he says solemnly. "I taught these boys human studies and history in the gymnasium."
"What do *you* know about history?" The carabineer snaps at Gaston. "You never witnessed history. Only heard about it -- years later -- when it had already moved on. You don't know history."
Hmm... so Gaston taught both Easy Leo and the Claire Brothers.
The old soldier mumbles something under his breath and turns to face the sea.
"Let's try not to get caught in the..." The lieutenant lowers his voice: "Crossfire."
"*The blind leading the blind* doesn't even begin to describe it," is what he said.
Lest we leave riddled with bullet holes. This animosity is ancient.
"Are you a *caviar socialist*?"
*Gymnasium*. I love that word.
"What a prick," the jolly man declares, with a sigh. "The officer was addressing me, not you, *capitaine*. Where were we?"
"Oh..." His cheeks turn red again. "In many ways, yes. Like an honorary member. I attend meetings and parties. Help with little things. Evrart, Edgar, and the older *Débardeurs* all know me."
"'In many ways'?"
"Not in the technical sense..." His eyes fix on the boules in the crater. "I don't have a vote or a membership card. But Evrart keeps me on the payroll. Just for the little things."
"What are the 'little things' you do for Evrart?"
"Can you help me get inside the harbour?"

dialoguetext: "Of course he's not a member! He's not a member of anything. I knew that." He frowns. "He's a weathervane -- turns to where the wind blows and tries to look important."
"Respects?!" The old carabineer can't believe what he's hearing.
So that's what it was, before! Him hiding something. He tries to make it look like he's a big deal in the Union and now the illusion is disintegrating before your -- and René's -- eyes.
He doesn't know anything, because no one tells him anything. He's an outsider.
"I hate the socialist rabble," he continues, "but even siding with *them* is better than living your entire life on the fence, never committing to anything. Pick a damn side already!"
"Writing work mostly," he smiles. "Occasionally he needs something written and I happen to have a way with words, people say."
"What kind of things do you write for him?"
"Oh, nothing official, I assure you. Just essays for the newspapers. About Martinaise and how things are and how they *could* be. Evrart and I have these long talks where..."
"Where he tells his little *penman* exactly what to say! It's commie propaganda, plain and simple. You should be ashamed of yourself."
That's why Gaston isn't a Union member. Evrart needs a 'neutral' party to speak his ideas.
"I do 'little things' for Evrart myself. Nothing wrong with that."
"I do 'little things' for Evrart too. I feel terrible about it."
"Let's stay on the track here, guys."
"On the Union-track?"
"That's just the way things work around here," he declares merrily. "No reason to feel bad about it."
"Thank you officer," he nods, smiling wide. "For being a consummate professional. You'll have this case wrapped up in no time."
"No, I'm sorry, officer." he shakes his head. "I don't even have a keycard. Evrart usually sends someone to get me, when he wants to talk."
"So you *are* a 'weathervane'?"
"I prefer *highly-adaptable* myself," he chuckles merrily. "Has a better ring to it, don't you think?"
"I don't even consider myself a regular socialist. Politics is not really something I involve myself in, officer."
"Wait, how can you write those newspaper pieces if you're not *political*?"
"That's smart. I keep my nose clean too."
"Officer, I have a vivid imagination." He laughs again. "And like I said, I have a way with words. That's enough. No need to sink into politics."
"But you need to believe in *something*. Freedom, the people, Revachol or even money..."
"I believe everyone has the right to think and do whatever they want. Even if it's nothing at all. I'm very *adaptable*."
"Just easier that way," he nods in approval. "Besides, life isn't as black and white as René's of the World try to make it seem. It's all shades of grey really."
"*Mon dieu*..." the carabineer closes his eyes, like he's never going to open them again.
'Where were we' -- what a joyous way of putting it.
There he stands. Proud, rigid, and alone, like a cracking marble statue.
"All right then. Change of topic."
"Of course, officer, I hope I can help you." He nods enthusiastically. "What's on your mind?"
"So you're not an actual member?"
"Oh yes."
He just fluffs it up.
"Of course -- don't *sink* into anything. Don't sink into any fight. Only sink into your couch."
All right, this is how we're gonna do it:
"Oh..." he looks down for the longest time. "You're right of course, officer. It can't be good for my health. Please, take it off my hands."
"Sure, but I'm going to need yours as a *prototype* first."
"I admire your handiwork,*chéf*, but there are a few things I'd do differently."
A man so principled about his sandwich calls for a principled approach. Time to get political.
"How is your back, Gaston?" (Tap on the side of your nose and point to the sandwich.)  "Is it... *jerky*?"
"That *would* certainly have been an improvement."
"The bread you built this wonder on, could have been toasted beforehand."
"Well yes, I mean... uh... no need to..." He raises his arms to signal you to stop. "I'm not sure I understand what's happening here, officer."
"Ee... okay, sure sure, I'm not worried. We're here all the time. Every day. Impossible to miss us, officer."
"Don't worry, about it." (Give him a wink.)
"I hope you are not just tricking an old man out of the little he has left." He says solemnly and hands you his sandwich.
"I got a keen eye and it's telling me this sandwich is gonna destroy your back."
"Wait... But I thought..." The old-timer, visibly disappointed, pockets the sandwich and sighs. "I'd really like to get back to the game now, if there isn't anything else?"
"Like what, officer?" His eyes rest on the sandwich. "This is as good as they come in Revachol, I assure you."
"No. No one can." (Gaze at the distance, slowly shaking your head.)
An array of delicious recipes flashes through your mind. Salads... Salmon... Sandwiches. Bingo!
"*Ce serait délicieux*! he shouts excitedly. "Can you make that sandwich, officer?"
"I'll do you one better -- the air pocket between cheese and ham could house pre-roasted paprika."
"Envision bread as black as the soil it came from..."
"No, that's too old school. How about...?"
What is *political*?
I'm already tripping knee-deep in politics, baby.
*This* right here is political...
"Your blood-sandwich" (point to it) "is a tool of the oppressors, designed to keep the proletariat docile."
"This city's going to shit. Sooner or later some foreign anarchist is gonna *steal* your sandwich. That's a fact."
You really do. Now, *unleash the fury*!
"I'm not going to listen to this commie-*connerie*," he utters through clenched teeth and turns his back to you.
"Eh... I don't think that's gonna happen." He chuckles. "Why would you even...?"
"Oh...? Still, the *over-abundance* this sandwich embodies is inherently evil."
"The Lawbringers?"
"The Vigil Flame?"
"Revachol Curbstompers?"
"*Now* you are talking sense, son." His eyes light up. "All three of us, working as a group -- we can make a difference."
"Salt is essential -- there can't be too much -- because isn't proletariat the salt of society?"
"How about what?!" Judging by his tone the old carabineer really wanted to honour his old unit.
"It's dignified. We need dignity. And you..." He points to Gaston. "Get excited."
"Yes, officer." He proudly displays his culinary miracle. It is magnificent.
"It's got class. And roots. I like it."
I'm sure we can come up with something with a bit more *oomph* than that.
"I don't want to," he argues, glancing at you worriedly. "Look, officer, I like different, *classic* food. Fine dining, not soil. Please, just drop it."
"Let me ask you, comrade, did *you* make the sandwich yourself?"
"Agreed. What about the whole group?" He quickly adds: "I propose *Épées de la Couronne* -- Swords of the Crown, in honour of my old unit."
"I really don't understand how my sandwich could..." he starts, but falls silent.
"Huh?" The jolly man is scratching his head in bewilderment. He doesn't understand the situation.
"First they take our jobs, then our women and when the sandwich is all you have left -- the anarchists will come for that too."
"That sounds *horrible*." A grimace of disgust runs over his jolly face. "You really don't know your way around the kitchen, officer. Food and politics don't mix."
The scepticism emanating from the merry senior could be sensed all the way to the Semenine Isles.
"But imagine a sandwich covered entirely in fine metal dust from an industrial plant..."
"But imagine a sandwich absolutely minimal in design. Sleek, efficient, simple."
"Look, comrade, the *over-abundance* this sandwich embodies is inherently evil."
"He won't care." The old veteran glances at his partner. "As long as there's food in his fat belly, he'll lick any boot that's kicking it to him..."
"We'll be unit one, *Ghost Dogs*. You and Gaston are unit two -- *The Royal Hounds*."
"I'll be unit one, *Ghost Dog*. You and Gaston are unit two -- *The Royal Hounds*."
"Guillaume's Lions?"
Tell this lost comrade what the People's Sandwich would be like. Distil the essence of the Working Man... in a sandwich.
"The Filippian Four?"
"I would rather just have this one, officer." He's avoiding your eyes. "It's really good."
"Men, let's review and, possibly, *redistribute* our resources." (Continue.)
"What do you mean, officer?" There's a look of suspicion is his eyes.
"Wouldn't you rather have a proper sandwich? A sandwich with a soul?"
"Don't you guys get it? Us, local boys, gotta stick together. Make the people feel safe again."
Sorry, but at this point, all that's left to do is beg and hope for the best. Beg like you've never begged before.
These options seem awfully fascist or communist -- what if I don't wanna say them?
"No, officer." The culinary genius shakes his head with unexpected resolve. "Please let it go, It's making me really uncomfortable."
"Please, please, just *PLEASE* let me have the sandwich, Gaston!"
Say one of these fascist or communist things or fuck off.
I'm not gonna beg.
It's probably for the best. People don't like beggars.
Whoa... easy there, Gold Mouth. He doesn't *have* to say anything. Re-engage cop-mode and bail out, if you like.
"Back to police-mode." (Smile and nod.) "I have some questions, Gaston."
No. You're gonna starve to death.
You're not. Everything is fine.
"Alright." The jolly man smiles. "Let's hear them, officer."
"I don't either, but wouldn't you rather eat a sandwich free of the *bourgeois* guilt-baggage?"
He's not imagining it.
"Melting butter, yellow like the sun shining on the backs of workers on the fields..."
"Now turn it upside down, black bread -- like a symbol -- on top, to salute the coal mines our heroes worked."
"I don't eat worker-food!" he blurts out, immediately regretting it. "Look, officer, I like different, *classic* food. Fine dining, not *worker backs*. Please, just drop it."
The sandwich owner looks at you, eyes filled with anguish. "You're describing prison food, officer. I like different, *better* food. Fine dining, not *jailtime*. Please, just drop it."
"No, everything would fall off," he argues, glancing at you worriedly. "Look, officer, I'm not a miner. I like different, *tasty* food. Fine dining, not coal. Please, just drop it."
"What the hell are you talking about? What *foreign anarchist*?" the lieutenant asks, confused.
No time to bring him in. Just keep your eyes on the prize and ignore him.
"Cause that's how foreigners *are*, Gaston. They won't stop 'till you have nothing left."
Good, René's on board too -- time to take back the streets. Right-wing populism, here we come!
"Revachol is calling -- she needs us. Not tomorrow, not *soon*, but right now. Let's take our home back."
Whatever you're selling there -- he's buying it. In bulk.
"I'm actually already a member in a group tasked to keep the streets safe," the lieutenant marks. "You are too. We call ourselves *The Police*."
"On second thought... I don't wanna organize a vigilante group after all." (Drop it.)
"So..." The sandwich-owner looks at you, obviously confused. "Is there something I can help you with instead or...?"
"Goddamnit, son..." He pushes back his cap. "Once you realize Martinaise -- all of Revachol -- is *actually* going to shit, it will be too late."
"Kim, I got this." (Wink at him.)
"Are you sure?" The lieutenant raises his eyebrows. "Cause right now it looks like you're organizing a vigilante group."
"Guillaume's Millions?"
"Suzerain Solution?"
"The Three Boiadeiros?"
"The Migrant Bashers?"
"Frissel Firing Squad?"
"It's weird. I don't like it. We'll go with mine for now and you..." He points to Gaston. "Get excited."
"Alright, alright," the old man is taken aback by René's commanding tone, but dares not dispute him. "I have a bad feeling about this."
His tone leaves no room for arguments. Giving orders is a second skin to the old carabineer.
"It's dignified. I like it. We need dignity. And you..." He points to Gaston. "Get excited."
"Good good, now that this is done -- GIVE ME THE SANDWICH!"
"Just one small thing -- your sandwich. I wanna hold it for a moment."
"It's okay, Gaston, just *please* give me the sandwich now."
"Oh..." His eyes light up in understanding. "You went through all that trouble for my sandwich? I'm flattered, officer, but my answer is no. Now how else can I help you?"
"Actually, let's honour your old unit -- *Épées de la Couronne* it is!"
"What?" The lieutenant gives you a sharp glance. "What *oppressors*?"
"Nothing. Actually, let's talk about something else."
"I'm listening, officer." He nods.
I'm not so sure about this...
Too late. Daddy's already fighting the bad fight. Make it stick.
Ignore him. You are addressing the entire group now.
Oh my god, stop this scheming and just demand the sandwich!
"Stop it! I *just* want the sandwich. Give it to me!"
"Goddamnit..." the old carabineer looks at you, disgusted. "I thought I had you measured, but you can't really measure a slug, can you?"
"Oh..." His eyes light up in understanding. "All that for a sandwich? I'm flattered, officer, but you can't have it. It's mine."
Not speaking from experience, but yes, you can. It's a common practice among the slug-enthusiasts.
Manipulating his patriotic impulses like that? René is gonna remember that.
"*Mon dieu*, that is an excellent idea!" he exclaims. "That would virtually negate the component loss."
"Had you put a large slice of Olduvaian cheese crosswise from the ham, it would minimize the component loss via crumbling."
This calls for an engineering angle. Structural rigidity, exposed rafters, lattice-works -- that type of approach.
Lattice-works? Like *Lettuce-works*? I see what you did there. Don't ever do that again.
Beautiful, now bring it home with paprika.
No problem, you just need *his* for research and development first. Just as a prototype of course. Stall now and the sandwich is forever lost.
"Initial development takes time of course, but in six to nine months you *will* eat 'The Sandwich of Gods'."
"Or god of sandwiches maybe?" he tries to pitch in. "But in the meanwhile, what can I do for you *here* and *now* officer?"
"Ee... okay, sure sure," he quiets you. "Everybody wins, but is there anything I can help you with right now to *speed up* the process?"
He looks worried.
"Is there anything I can do for you right now?" he asks. "Maybe to speed the whole process up a bit?"
He knows exactly what's going on.
"Just give me the damn sandwich, so I don't have to explain."
Point to the sandwich in silence.
"I understand the situation," he says quietly and hands you the sandwich. "Please... just take it slowly. Give her the attention she deserves."
He nods, understanding the finality of the situation, and hands you the sandwich. "Please... just take it slowly. Give her the attention she deserves."
The old man nods and turns away from you.
And now we both walk away and everybody lives.
"Step back everyone, it's gonna get messy." (Eat the sandwich.)
You jam your teeth into the sandwich and immediately feel a series of taste explosions go off in you mouth. It's like someone's carpet-bombing your tongue with ambrosia.
He shrugs. "I mean I'm not hungry and therefore am not gonna take it. Thanks though."
"No."
It really is every bit as good as it looked and smelled. The different components all chip in and compliment each other, forming a flavour that is unique to this particular masterpiece.
When you hold something up long enough, some people are compelled to take it. Try it on the lieutenant.
"I'll pass," the lieutenant replies with a polite nod. "Thanks."
Slow down, feel the texture of the components and subtle nuances in taste.
"Here, Kim! Let's share." (Hold out the sandwich.)

The bread, as the foundation of the sandwich, is slightly moist due to tomato juice and mayo, but holds together nicely. Almost nothing falls off the sandwich. You feel like you really got everything out of this experience.
You really ram into the sandwich, *deep*. The tomato slides off, mayo drips everywhere (including your moustache and clothes), bits of ham fall onto the ground...
"Camaraderie?"
"What do you mean 'you'll pass'?"
Keep holding the sandwich.
Take giant bites and swallow them half-chewed.
Get into there and do some real damage!
This is what angels must taste like. Your saliva production increases tenfold. You can barely contain it all.
"This isn't about hunger, Kim, it's about camaraderie."
Hold the sandwich up for the lieutenant to take it.
"Thank you, but no, I'm not hungry."
"Okay, I guess I'll keep it for later."
"Yes! By sharing this sandwich you and I solidify the bond between us."
Hold the sandwich up, moving it closer to the his chin.
"It *really* is."
The lieutenant nods.
"Is this necessary?! Is friendship necessary? Is brotherhood?"
"No."
"I just thought it would be a nice gesture. I'm sorry..."
"Then sure. Let us 'strengthen our bond'." The lieutenant breaks the sandwich in two and quickly eats his half.
"Is it really necessary?"
Lower the sandwich.
Do not lower the sandwich.
"Okay-okay. They are all necessary. Let's share the sandwich, if it matters that much to you." The lieutenant breaks the sandwich in two and quickly eats his half.
You can barely feel the taste, but it seems decent enough. At least it gets your stomach nice and full. Good sandwich -- durable!
"For the brötherhööd!" (Eat your half of the sandwich.)
"Stop that!" He doesn't sound amused.
"...some people would feel compelled to take it. Yes, I know."
Have the sandwich-interceptor circle in front of the lieutenant's face and then gently nosedive against his lips.
"You know, Kim, if I were to hold this sandwich up long enough..."
"Sure, sure." The lieutenant nods impatiently. "Time to go solve a murder investigation."
This man does not crack under pressure. Stars would die before he'd succumb to any kind of manipulation. With this realization comes a sudden flash of pride.
The lieutenant's eyes express an absolute lack of interest.
Move the sandwich around in front of the lieutenant's mouth and make aircraft noises.
The lieutenant stands next to you, but he might as well exist in a parallel realm.
"No, it's... it's okay. Let's share it, okay?" The lieutenant breaks the sandwich in two and quickly eats his half.
"No."
"Officer. We have serious matters to attend to. I suggest we get to them right now." He seems completely unfazed by the situation.
"Hey!"
The lieutenant slaps the sandwich out of your hand faster than you could ever hope to react in your sorry state. It lands in the dirt and falls apart.
Proceed with the mission.
One look at the lieutenant immediately tells you he is ready for your Assault-Sandwich.
A bad idea. Men like the lieutenant are not won over by such childish manoeuvres.
"I'm just not hungry."
Send the HAM fighter-craft for another mission.
"Okay, but *why* don't you want it?"
"Not you, though?"
[Put the sandwich away.]
"I cannot be bought!" (Throw the sandwich on the ground.)
The ham-sandwich looks fresh and nutritious in you hand, begging to be eaten.
"Great." The lieutenant shakes his head. "Wonderful. Good job. I mean why *wouldn't* you throw it... wait, turns out I don't actually care. Leave it and let's go."
So worth it -- can you feel how liberating that was? De-compression completed.
The taste-assault in your mouth abates for a moment... wolfing it down is efficient, but lacking in appreciation.
A treat of this magnitude should not be enjoyed alone.
The bonds between officers -- partners -- are *paramount*. That's how trust is built. Trust saves lives.
The sandwich falls to the ground with a splat, tomatoes and lettuce flying everywhere, mayo spilling out like blood on a crime scene.
The sandwich falls to the floor with a loud splat, tomatoes and lettuce flying everywhere, mayo spilling out like blood on a crime scene.
You mean semen, right?
"Oh, okay then."
The wrapper -- soaked in tomato juice and mayo -- is not gonna hold out forever, but for now the sandwich retains it's impressive composure.
Ouch... he did *not* like that.
The lieutenant nods and adds, "But you go right ahead."
"No, you're right. Let's just drop it."
"Go through all that and then just dump it?" The lieutenant smirks. "You better just eat it, no need for dramatic gestures."
It's a little joke the lieutenant made. He knows what you meant.
"This is good shit." (Eat your half of the sandwich.)
"Friends forever!" (Eat your half of the sandwich.)
Eat your half in silence.
"Good." The lieutenant nods. "Very nourishing. Let's go solve crimes now."
"Look what you did..."
"Great, that's 2000 kilo-calories wasted right there."
"Congratulations, Kim. It was a test and you passed."
"*Mon dieu*," the jolly man exclaims. "Good job, officer. That was an excellent throw!"
"Perfect throw? Well, I still feel defeated."
"That's just how Johnny Ballgame is -- extraordinary."
"Right," the old soldier says slowly. "Was the demonstration *it*, or do you still need something from us, officer?"
"You vandalized our game, son." He tries to calm himself. "We can't play pétanque with five *boules*."
This felt... wrong. Wrong like touching your sister's breast. You threw your sister's breast.

dialoguetext: "What the HELL is your problem?"
"Not a weak right triceps, that's for sure."
God, this is right -- you feel the familiar tremble of excitement and adrenaline that precedes every victory. Time has frozen.
"I don't care if you are a cop -- you *do not* just ruin someone's game. It's so goddamn disrespectful!"
"Wait... what?"
"Don't be a sore loser, it's still a fair game between you two. Second place is a podium position."
"I'm sensing anger. And I don't understand why."
"Your guess is as good as mine, officer. Maybe you're just one of those men who's never satisfied with anything?" He shrugs. "Regardless, what do you need from us?"
"Spring slush on bare feet can make a man feel like a failure." He points at your naked toes. "For a reason. Now, do you need something from us?"
"What are you talking about? You just executed a pretty much perfect pétanque throw!" His tone is full of admiration.
"How are you ever going to get the officer's shit off your nose, Gaston? Or even climb out of his ass?" He shakes his head in extreme disdain.
Let go. Be the ball. (Continue.)
Take in the surroundings.
It wasn't *merde*. The shot was at least 23 metres. Probably 24 and then some. Nothing to be embarrassed about.
Already your muscles are adjusting to the weight, the nervous system calibrating, until you and the ball have merged into a single entity. The *manball* is ready.
There is time for a last glance inward. Who am I?
An embodiment of pure motion. A fine-tuned *locomotor* running at maximum efficiency.
Feel the ball.
"Problem? I don't understand."
A chilly breeze ruffles your hair as you stand there, feet firmly planted. All sounds, smells, even the wind -- everything fades until the only thing left is the union of Man and Ball.
"Probably because those rooster pants are squeezing you senseless. What ever happened to practical? Durable? Revachol-made?" He shakes his head. "Now what can I do for you?"
"Yes, officer..." The lieutenant gives you a quick side-glance. "What *do* we need from these gentlemen?"
"I'm a god of track and field. Why would I have a problem with anything?"
You are immediately surprised by the ball's lack of weight. No matter. You'll make it work.
Hold on, why *did* it feel so wrong?
"The throw was terrible and you know it. No need to mock me."
"The damn ball was slippery as fuck! How do you expect me to throw this piece of *shit* when it's got old man spunk all over, Mossback?!"
"I thought something way more spectacular would happen."
"I was going for something cool, but I screwed it up, like always..."
The man in the uniform says nothing. His gaze is fixed on the horizon.
His merry partner is staring at the ground like he's trying to see right through to the other side.
The lieutenant is looking at you. His face is expressionless.
Everything has gone very quiet. It seems as even the waves have ceased their crashing against the promenade. It feels heavy.
"*Merde*!" the old soldier yells in outrage. "*Bordel de merde*!!!"
There are no two more harmful words an athlete can hear than *good job*. And this was downright embarrassing!
Mossback and his shitty ball are mocking you. You need to get angry. Use swear-words. Mention *spunk*.
Something about it was completely unnatural. Corrupted. Your muscle memory knew what to do and went for it, but there were gaps...
Yeah! Gaps you tried to fill with *thinking*. We don't *think* in sports. We *DO*!
It felt like you were going for a thrust or a lunge -- there was definitely gonna be jumping. Maybe you scored a point, but this is a *fiasco*.
Look who's talking -- that cockatoo uniform must give him a real advantage. When fighting in *the circus*.
The cold metal ball is surprisingly smooth against your neck. It has a pattern on it. (Probably a sponsored ball.) Yours would only be covered with bumps of learning and scars of victory.

West, in the Grand Couron Arena, a sharp overhand left from Arsène-Luc Edelbrock, sends the Samaran heavyweight champion, Kostya 'Mjasnok' Koštunica, flying to the mat. The crowd goes wild. Revachol loves her heroes.
Behold the fear and confusion reflecting in the eyes of the two feeble geezers -- they are in awe of your superiority. You are a God to them.
"Oh, pétanque, I understand..."
"No, no you don't! Our pétanque game is ruined!" He's getting angry again. "We want our *boule* back."
"I thought it was shot-put."
"Well, it damn well isn't, it's pétanque," the man snaps, raising his voice again. "You ruined a pétanque game. We want our *boule* back!"
"Sorry, an honest mistake. Are we good?"
"Yes, pétanque," the man says, raising his voice again. "You ruined our pétanque game. We want our *boule* back."
"No, we are not *good*, goddamnit!" A vein on his forehead is bulging alarmingly. "We want our *boule* back!"
"Pee-tank?"
"Okay, I will try to fix this." (Accept the task.)
"Good." He nods. "Mistakes are forgiven, when men at least *try* to right their wrongs. I believe you will try. Now why did you approach us?"
"A fine example you are setting here today, officer." He says, slowly shaking his head. "I will remember this. And Gaston will too."
"Listen, guys, the ball is gone, and I have a murder to solve, alright?" (Refuse task.)
"It's okay, officer. Forgotten completely. It was my *boule* and I have a spare." He produces another ball from his pocket. "Everything is good and we're ready to assist any way we can!"
The lieutenant says nothing, but his face is rigid. It seems he does not approve of your athletic displays.
You are an officer of the law with way more important things to worry about than *boules*. Don't take this crap.
"Take it easy, René." The jolly one tries to defuse the situation. "This is just a misunderstanding, isn't it, officer? No harm done."
"Of course there's harm done, you orange slug!" The heel of his cavalry boot slams in the ground. "You owe us a goddamn *boule*!"
He's trying to avoid conflict at any cost.
It's your refusal to take responsibility I don't like.
A man his age getting worked up like that? Better watch that blood pressure.
"I'm sorry."
With a pinch of fear.
A *whorehouse of shit*?
It wasn't *whorehouse of shit*. The shot was at least 23 metres. Probably 24 and then some. Nothing to be embarrassed about.
"I don't have a *boule*, but will this do?" (Hold out the shot put ball.)
"Will this...." He falls silent and stares at the ball. "No, it will *goddamn* not..."
"Thank you, officer." The jolly man quickly takes the ball and bounces it in his hand. "This is really something... Honestly I think it's better than our old *boule* even!"
"*Mon dieu*..." he mumbles, rubbing his temples. "Alright. Alright. Fine. What do you want, officer?"
*Some* would still say you're a cop, but I guess we're beyond that now.
Just talk. It'll smooth things over. Old people like attention.
Yes... why *did* you come here? It's unlikely they know anything about the murder.
You never know, he *might* know something. This is a good vantage point.
"Wait, who are the 'communards', again?"
"Was it made by a sea monster rising from the depths?"
"No," he says without even smiling. "It was left by heavy artillery fire."
"No," he replies, gaze wondering over the bay. "It was left by heavy artillery fire."
"Was there an earthquake here?"
"Does it have anything to do with all the bullet holes I've been seeing around?"
"Yes," he replies with a reluctant nod. "It was left by heavy artillery fire."
"Yes..." The man nods. "The terrain here provides an interesting variety to a familiar game."
"Why what?"
"Did *you* use artillery fire against them?"
"Do you know what created it?"
"Why was heavy artillery used?"
"I do," he nods, straightening his back. "Fire from heavy artillery."
"Okay, it's a crater left by artillery fire -- but why?"
"Commies, communists, socialists, anarchists -- call them what you like. They just chose the name to feel special." The carabineer frowns. "Senseless sentimentality."
"Sadly, no. It was the foreigners who brought them to their knees. We fought valiantly -- too valiantly. So valiantly we got licked," he adds, squeezing a *boule* in his fist.

"Should've fought dirty. Like they did with their suicide sex cult propaganda and *mad anarchist women* strapped to shrapnel bombs. We didn't though. And we lacked *calibre*. God bless him, but the suzerain's cannons simply weren't big enough.“
It was probably a bit more complicated than that.
"Why shell them here in Martinaise?"
"Because this place is the damn Beachhead," he says, pointing to the bay. "Had to soften the commies up first."
"The Beachhead?"
"Yes," he nods, inspecting you with some disdain. "The military-coordinated amphibious landing to take back Revachol."
"Martinaise was used as one of the three footholds in Revachol during Operation Death Blow in '08. The other two are off in Stella Maris and the Delta." He points to the northeast.

"This here is blood ground, where Coalition boots first made landfall and cleaned those rabid dogs out. Most likely," he says, looking down at the soil, "we're playing pétanque on their mangled corpses."
"Blood ground..." The other one shakes his head. "You got old René going there. Like he isn't angry enough already..."
"Hold on -- the Coalition?"
"Is that why everything is so bombed out?"
"Ah, that explains all the war damage."
"Mhmh," he grunts. "Don't get me wrong, officer. I hate those foreign dogs. But the enemy of my enemy and all that. They're the lesser evil."
"Actually I already know all this. I just wanted to know if you do too."
"Yes, dammit -- I know! They laid the fire of hell on this city before they stormed it. And it worked, too." There is a strange gleam in his eyes.
"The rest of the city got cleaned up, but Martinaise they keep as a *monument*." A dark shadow runs across his face. "And now the Union socialists are practically running the place."
He approves of this radical approach. Knows it was *necessary*.
"That's how it should be. Soft socialists paving the way for the *hard* working class to take over."
"Foreign powers cleaned up our mess and now they rule us." (Shake your head in shame.)
"This Coalition seems quite capable, actually."
"Commies just don't understand how money works."
"Damn right, son. They laid the fire of hell on this city before they stormed it. And it worked, too." There is a strange gleam in his eyes.
"They're *not*. And I'm sorry it had to be them. After eight years of fighting those hyenas, boiling cats for food and drinking piss in the mountains..." He takes a deep breath.

"Instead, all that is just, holy, and beautiful in the world was wiped away and now it's neon signs with toothpaste ads everywhere. Foreign influence peddling garbage and stupid music on the radio." He sighs.
"I *would* have preferred if the right honourable King Guillaume returned to Revachol or even if that damn clown, Frissel, had risen from the grave and led us. Sadly that was not the case."
This *Royal* failure weighs heavily on him.
"This is just what the commies wanted. This was their plan all along. *This* is what they wanted to replace the rule of the Suzerain with."
"Who was this Frissel?"
"You mentioned Guillaume?"
"Hmm... what exactly is a *suzerain*?" (Conclude.)
"No, they don't. But I'm sorry it had to be the Coalition. After eight years of fighting rabid commies, boiling cats for food and drinking piss in the mountains..." He takes a deep breath.
"I'm sorry it had to be them." He looks down at his boots. "After eight years of fighting those hyenas, boiling cats for food and drinking piss in the mountains..."

"Damn Frissel -- he was the king we couldn't protect. The carabineers failed him... and the crown." The old veteran falls silent and massages his chest. "He died in the hands of the *hoi polloi* in a very public execution."
"A true King in both blood and mind. Led Revachol before Frissel. He would have been better, but the damn commies drove him into exile."
Wait, Joyce said Guillaume ran and his nephew, Frissel, was shot in his place.
Exiled? Joyce said Guillaume ran and his nephew, Frissel, was shot in his place.
"Commies didn't drive Guillaume out. He left, when things got bad and left Frissel to take the hit."
"This is communard propaganda! Guillaume would never do something like that. He is *LE LION*."
"The Suzerain is the King. Has everyone forgotten already?" He then slowly nods and says to himself: "They've forgotten already."
"It's no use talking to you. You were still in daddy's balls when it happened. When *we* took our last stand against the filth and rode the cavalry straight into gunfire."
There is not a shadow of a doubt in his mind that this is the truth.
"Oh, okay."
"What else?"
"Because that's what happens when communards hijack your country, execute your supreme leadership, and turn your capital into a slaughterhouse. You use *heavy ordnance* to clean up your home."
"Maybe we can do this history lesson later."
"Fine," the carabineer replies sharply. "What do you want now then?"
"They should have chosen a place away from people and buildings."
"This place is the damn Beachhead, son," he says, pointing to the bay. "They had to soften the commies up first."
Nod thoughtfully and turn to look northeast.
Shake your head and look down at the crater.
"Death Blow... sounds grim."

"Preposterous! Surely you don't mean it." He frowns. "I'm just sorry it had to be them. After eight years of fighting those commie hyenas, boiling cats for food and drinking my piss in the mountains..."
"How does Filippe the Third factor into this?" (Point towards the monument.)
"He doesn't," the veteran replies sharply. "That was one hundred years ago. Ain't got nothing to do with anything."
"You don't even *begin* to truly understand the players on the table, let alone the specific circumstances surrounding the..." He stops mid-sentence and turns to you. "What do you think?"

"Well, it's your own damn fault," the jolly man remarks. "You, we, the Coalition, Revachol -- whoever you wanna blame -- never finished the job. Officially the Party never surrendered. Of course they still hold influence."
"Nothing. I *don't* think. I just *do*."

"I'm just so damn sorry it had to be the Coalition..." He isn't really paying attention to your words anymore. "After eight years of fighting those hyenas, boiling cats for food and drinking piss in the mountains..."
*Heavy* artillery fire you say? That's the best kind of artillery fire. Very interesting.
(Look around) "I understand. I'd bomb this place too."
"This place is the damn Beachhead, son," he says, pointing to the bay. "They didn't do it because they didn't *like* it. They had to soften the commies up first."
He finds your lack of historic knowledge troubling. A sign of mental deterioration in the proceeding generations.
Thinking men have *opinions* on these things. Present one.
Some manner of self-deceit is present in his thinking. Sounds like this Guillaume abandoned him and he doesn't want to admit it.
He slouches as he says that. It makes him smaller, admitting they left the king to the mob.
Soon they will forget everything. Him too... Then he chooses anger over melancholy.
An extremely inadvisable strategy against automatic weapons. Be sure not to make the same mistake.
Something moves in your gut. It's almost like a tug.
That's our guy! The way he speaks about the war and the bygone days -- Kingsman through and through -- ask him how to turn back time!
"Never thought I'd miss that angry prick..."
"Maybe fishing... or crossword puzzles?"
"I wonder if Leo knows pétanque..."
"Have the days always been this long?"
"I should be hungry -- why am I not hungry?"
Awful lonely here. No ruckus. No old men playing their little ball game.
Yeah, where did the old guys go?
That's just how craters are. [Discard thought.]
"You mean the guys who were playing pétanque?"
The pétanque players?
"Yeah, where did they go?"
Yeah, where did they go?
"Have you noticed people sometimes appear and disappear in places? It's called *doing things*."
Home? To work? To get something from somewhere? Who knows what people are doing when we're not looking.
"Wait, maybe they died during the mercenary tribunal?"
"But what if I wanted to talk to them?"
"Right. Let's move." [Leave.]
It's very unlikely. Everyone scattered once the tribunal started. They're probably fine.
"They didn't," the lieutenant calms you. "Trust me. I saw the bodies."
"You'll get them next time," the lieutenant replies, looking at the empty crater.
You'll get them next time. But let's be honest, they weren't even in the suspects list.

"And, I mean... it would be one twist too many if it turned out these two old men were our killers. That's just unlikely. No..." He seems pleased with himself. "We would only have wasted our time here."
You would have wasted *so* much time talking to these two pensioners. Precious case-time.
He's probably right.
"Damn, I missed asking these guys about the dried May bells."
No need to beat yourself down over it. It probably wasn't the definitive piece of the puzzle. Still, somehow it feels like May bells matter somehow.
"Don't beat yourself up about it. I think I gave you a pretty exhaustive answer about those flowers and what they mean."
Enough with the goddamn flowers already! Are you a cop or a florist?
It was probably nothing anyway. Just a little thought you had.
*Still* you can't shake the feeling that somehow these may bell do actually matter. If only a little bit.
The lieutenant is thinking of all the time you've spared. He likes it.
"René... I need to go back in time. Can you help me?"
The lieutenant flashes you a quick side-glance.
His posture tenses.
What are you up to now?
"What?!" The old soldier scowls at you, unamused.
He thinks you're playing a joke on him.
"Now, now..." His partner raises both hands in a calming gesture. "I'm sure the officer means it figuratively. Like a forensic technique or something, right?"
"No, I need to go back to a time when *love* was still possible."
"No, I literally need to go back in time. For Revachol."
"Right, right... A forensic technique. Can you help me or not?"
"Forget it. Let's move on." (Drop it.)
"Forensic techniques are your forte, not mine, officer." Something stiffens in the man. He shakes his head. "Find another fool, I will not be part of your... joke."
"I thought you were a busy man, officer. Or at least you should be, so I won't comment on this... eccentricity. Now what?"
"*Bon sang*, son. You must have a loose screw up there or something." He taps on his temple. "Sounds like you really mean it."
"Alright, I will entertain this... *fantasy*, if you tell me, what interest does an RCM officer have in... 'time travel'?"
"Oh, you're in for a treat, officer. Seeing the playful side of old René is about as rare as a red rainbow."

Not actually *that* rare. It's just that red, or monochrome, rainbows usually occur at sunrise or sunset, when blue and green wavelengths are scattered before reaching water droplets. Fewer eyes to see them then.
He doesn't know anything, he's too old. Doesn't have that *fire* in him anymore. But no worries, *we* will carry on. *Semper fidelis*, kingsman!
"Love. It's about love."
"It's always about love, isn't it?"
Was that a smile on his wrinkled... nevermind, it's gone.
"But it's never *only* about love, so what else, officer?"
"Men have lost their way. I want to guide them back. Like a beacon."
The old soldier nods. "Even after the Revolution, after the Beachhead, there was a chance. Had we just stayed true to our *values*..."
"I'm not sure, to be honest. Just going with the flow."
"It happened slowly, like a seedling growing into a tree. Tiny incremental steps. Imperceptible till the thicket was so thick you couldn't clear it with a flamethrower..."
You could *definitely* clear it with a flamethrower.
"I *know* I can get history back on the right track."
"I just want a second chance. Gonna do it right this time."
"Well, that depends on the flamethrower..."
"It really does, doesn't it?" The old soldier produces a strange croaking sound -- with laughter-like qualities -- then quickly massages his chest. "But honestly, why?"
Keep the war-crime jokes coming and you'll end up on his good side.
"The 'right track'? This *is* the right track! The only track." He gets visibly annoyed. "This is the world we shaped, a reflection of what we are: cowardly, ugly, and numb."
"'This time'?!" He's becoming visibly annoyed. "What happened to the first time? Did you make a mistake? Did you *fuck up*? Everyone did!"
"And there are no second chances. We don't deserve them! You can't just go back and restart -- that would make everything *MEANINGLESS*!" A shadow of pain comes over his face.
There's something *substantial* moving in him, trying to get out.
"Exactly what history needs." He spits on the ground between the two of you. "More drifters, confused wanderers, weightless men..."
There's so much bitterness in his voice it barely even registers as sarcasm.
"I can't help you officer," he says coldly. "There are no second chances in life. We don't deserve them. This is the world we shaped -- a reflection of what we are. Wasted, ugly, and numb."
The lieutenant clears his throat. "I think we're done here unless you have questions *not* relating to 'time travel' for the gentlemen?"
"It *is* an ugly world..."
"You know, it's not actually that bad."
Just nod.
"Such a downer, I'm not even sure how to respond..."
A heavy silence falls over the crater. The man in the checkered suit doesn't know where to look or what to do with his hands. Finally he speaks:
Only to break the silence.
"Officer, you must forgive Old René. Holding a conversation has always been... problematic with him." He flashes you a quick smile. "Try asking him something else."
Don't worry, he doesn't know anything useful, the man's almost expired. No fire in him. But *you* will carry on the flame. *Semper fidelis*, kingsman, anything is possible.
"Easy, René, take it easy." There's genuine concern in his face. "You're right, absolutely right. What was, *was* and that's it. Isn't that right, officer?"
His eyes seem to be pleading with you.
He would sooner die than let it surface.
What is it?
Even thinking about it is invading his privacy. Better let it go.
Regret.
Honour walks and virtue follows. You are truly a Detective-Saint, for you refuse to veer even when *no one* is looking. Bravo!
"Sure, why not?"
"*Everyone* deserves a second chance."
"Look, I just want to turn back time. Can either of you help me or not?"
"*Imbécile, un putain d'imbécile*..." The old veteran clutches his chest and tries to steady his breathing.
*Something* about this topic was very personal to him, but the moment has passed.
*Something* about this topic was very personal to him, but the moment has passed.
"*Imbécile, un putain d'imbécile!*..." The old veteran clutches his chest and tries to steady his breathing.
"Enough, officer," the other one says with surprising resoluteness. "We can't help you. Not with this. Such an *emotional* topic..."
"But don't worry, I'm sure there's something else old René or I can assist you with."
The carabineer is too old and feeble to be useful. But you will carry on. *Movere tempore*, kingsman. For the tenacious no road is impassable.
"*Imbécile, un putain d'imbécile*..." The old veteran clutches his chest and tries to steady his breathing.
"No, officer." He shakes his head meekly. "We can't help you with that, maybe there's something else we *can* help you with?"
Regret about what?
No, this is going too far. I should respect his privacy!
Him.
You know the answer, don't think -- just say it!
You catch the old carabineer's gaze slowly leaving his opponent's wrinkled face as his dark eyes meet yours -- whatever turmoil raged in him a moment ago is quelled for now.
Like the last rays of the evening sun gently kissing the day goodbye, before giving way to unfathomable darkness.
Willed back into the darkest unexplored depths of his mind -- never meant to be shared, seen or confronted.
A true master of his emotions.

"Mikael? Mikael's my son."
"Wait, what was up with the kid then?"
"No problem."
"Oh... okay. Sorry."
"So what are you *special consulting* here?"

"What indeed?" He looks at the dilapidated shacks, then you. "I was asked to share my take on some of the more *obscure* theories developed in Königstein in the Thirties. Like -- partial psychotraumatic amnesia, group personality theory..."
"Okay, you're Trant Heidelstam. Special Consultant. I get it."

"Again..." He looks around. "I was asked to share my take on some of the more *fringe academic* theories developed in Königstein in the Thirties. For example -- partial psychotraumatic amnesia, group personality theory..."
"See? He really *doesn't* remember. It wasn't a 'sick joke' -- at least that's good."
The two aren't mutually exclusive.
"Wait for fucking what? I'm Cuno. We come from Death Island."
"Look what the tide brought in," the man says in a measured tone. Suddenly, his expression changes and he tilts his head...
"What is this about?" (Move on.)
"No one else seems bothered by my *style*."
"My jacket... no one else seems bothered by it..."
"Yeah, fuck the world. No one else seems bothered by that."
"No one else seems bothered by my FALN gear."
"Harry, you're a cop with 'Pissf****ts' on his back! Do you have any idea how hard the liberals are going to fuck us for this?"
"No one else seems bothered by the bleeding."
"Bothered by it?! Harry, you look like you need a fucking organ transplant!"
He takes a deep breath. "Fuck it, let's not get into that."
"Oh really?! They don't seem bothered by it? That's because you're a cop in an exoskeleton!"
"Yes... I am a goddamn cop."
"Oh... that explains it."
"Actually -- are you? Are you still a cop? There's so much disco going on, it's hard to tell."
"Yes, that has *always* explained it."
This is not the first time he's seen you all decked out in wacko.
Now that you start thinking about it -- maybe they *were* afraid of you...
"Harry, that's because you're a cop with 'Fuck the World' written on his back."
"Special Consultant Trant Heidelstam, Patrol Officer Judit Minot."
...aaaand he's said it.
"No, Kim, you've gotta have my back. Let's destroy them."
"Don't worry, *many* people have seen me like this. No one said anything."
"Okay, I see. Yes."
No, no, no! You've sensitivity tested this!
"Harry, there are probably pictures..." The full gravity of the situation dawns on him.
"They're going to fuck us to death."
"Yes," Trant Heidelstam says. "There could have been cameras. This needs damage control."
"There weren't any cameras around." He stares at his boots. "They don't have cameras..."
"Cuno's liking this tense shit."
As if he recalled that he's, in fact, a decorated police lieutenant, and not a naughty boy.
"Pissf****t. Singular."
No one has been afraid of you without you knowing. They all felt perfectly safe.
Everyone felt perfectly safe in your company. He doesn't know what he's talking about.
"I *know* when people are uncomfortable around me. They haven't been."
"Believe me, they felt uncomfortable."
"No... Trant, it's too late. You're part of this shit now!" He turns to you. "What have you got to say for yourself, shitkid?"
Whatever this is, it is completely unimportant compared to what you've just *seen*.
"Forget about all this, there's a giant..."
"We're not forgetting about anything -- look at you!" He points at you with both hands.
This is the Man with Sunglasses from the Whirling-in-Rags! But where are his sunglasses?
"Wait... you're the Man with Sunglasses."
"That's right, and you're some kind of a... urban scarecrow thing."
"That's right -- and you're bleeding."
"Yes-yes... What's *wrong* with you?"
"That's right -- and you're some kind of... murder machine."
"That's right, and you look like you got twenty STDs."
"Cuno, you still have my back, right?"
"We're all pigs here." He nods to you, then straightens his back.
Even though we're all pigs here, you and Cuno are more pigs than the rest of the pigs. He'll have your back -- only later.
"What's a shitkid?"
"You. *Shitkid* -- that's you."
Despite *all* that you've done -- the deserter, the phasmid, the case?!
"Despite *all* that I've done?"
Better not to piss him off by arguing.
"No -- *because* of all that you've done."
Good idea. It doesn't look like he thinks you're in a position to correct him on the shitkid issue.
"Now nothing. Now we're just going to stand here."
"Really?"
"No -- now we discuss THAT." He points to the water. "What the fuck did you do to our motor carriage?! Why is it *there*, Harry?"
"And it was. Good work, Harry. You're insane now. There's one less person for me -- and everyone else -- to rely on."
"Did you? Or did you think I was a god damn FIREFIGHTER? We've been partners for how long, Harry?" He adjusts his tie. "Don't answer that -- you don't *remember*."
"Did you? Or did you think I was a god damn MALE NURSE? We've been partners for how long, Harry?" He adjusts his tie. "Don't answer that -- you don't *remember*."
"Did you? Or did you think I was a god damn ANIMAL HANDLER? We've been partners for how long, Harry?" He adjusts his tie. "Don't answer that -- you don't *remember*."
"We're still friends, I just have a stupid head."
"How did you know I was here?"
"The cafeteria manager you fucked over told us where you went."
"After all that Sylvie stuff, he betrays me..."
(Turn to face the general direction of the Whirling and yell.) "Damn you, cafeteria manager! You've betrayed me for the last time!"
"I understand. Okay. Garte told you."
"Shitkid," he says, shaking his index finger, "he didn't *betray* you. He just told us the direction you went in. Who's Sylvie?"
"Uhm, and..." she interjects, trying to defuse the situation. "People on this street helped us too."
"I saved his establishment and still he betrays me?!"
"Sylvie's a whore. She rides the cock carousel... and foreigners."
"No one. It's not important."
"It better not be."
He means: "You better not be *partying* with this Sylvie, shitkid."
"Super," he says with a nod. "Whore. Foreigners. Hatred."
"You're a legend among the drunks, Harry. A legendary local *drunk*."
"Strange. He didn't mention that. In fact, the establishment didn't look saved at all -- there was a giant *aero-graffito* in front of the building. It was on fire."
"Speaking of which. The giant *aero-graffito* in front of his building, in red, government-marked fuel -- did you do that?"
"Strange. He didn't mention that. In fact, the establishment didn't look saved at all -- there was a giant *aero-graffito* in front of the building. Mixed with *blood*."
"Speaking of which. The giant *aero-graffito* in front of the building. The one that's *burning* -- did you do that?"
"It was this one junior delinquent."
"Yeah, I wrote that. It was a poetic gesture." (Lie.)
"Yeah, I lit it on fire. It was a poetic gesture."
"I don't know..." He squints at you suspiciously. "It had *shitkid* written all over it."
"I knew it. Didn't I tell you, Trant? I told you it was our shitkid."

"The line is from Lu Jiatun's 'Mirova Cycle', isn't it? About Girl Child Communism -- the titular *returning* character. The ghostly apparition of..." He looks around and, noticing the impatience of his companions, stops himself. "Good choice, Harry."
"I knew it. Didn't I tell you, Trant? I told you it was our shitkid."
"Uhm, and..." She looks around. "People on this street helped us too. With your whereabouts."
"You're a legend among the drunks, Harry. A legendary local *drunk*."
"Don't encourage him, Trant."
"Okay."
He is correct. It was the Seraise poet Lu Jiatun who in the Fifties of the last century composed a...
"Have you been *spying* on me?"
"Yes, I *was* spying on you. I was in the bar, wearing a wig and stupid sunglasses. You didn't *recognize* me -- your own partner. Walked right past me..."
"I heard you'd lost your mind *and* your memory. I wanted to see if it was true. And it is, Harry -- you're totally insane now. Good job."
"In the crowd, there was a man and a woman in RCM uniform," he says to you, then turns to Vicquemare. "In his defence -- we were in a hurry."
"Cuno knew dress-up-pigs were in town. Cuno meant to dust them -- Cuno pig-duster -- but didn't, 'cause Cuno cares." The kid nods solemnly.
This is the Horse-Faced Woman. I don't know *why* you named her that, but it was beyond idiotic. You should *never* address her using those words again.
"You fucking idiot. You stupid fucking idiot. You're even worse than before. How is that even *possible*?"
"Okay." Another sigh. "You're my commanding officer. I... I really want to respect you. I want us to have a normal relationship."
"That will never happen, Jude. He's the rudest man on Earth. He is the reason why the rest of us have to take sensitivity training. And I *hate* sensitivity training..."
It's true. You have a problem.
"Okay." Another sigh. "Because you're my commanding officer. I... I really want to respect you. I want us to have a normal relationship."
"You." (Nod to the female officer.) "I'm sorry I didn't recognize you before."
"It's okay," she sighs. "I didn't come here to gloat, or to fool you. Neither did he, actually." She gestures toward Vicquemare. "We're just worried."
"That's right -- 'worried'. I'm always worried about you. Every time you don't show up to work, or when you do -- but *stink*."
"You're a *worry-fest*. She's worried about you. I'm worried about you. Even Special Consultant Backpedal is worried about you. Everyone worries -- instead of *working*."
He's got a very, very solid case there. Actually, I've been trying to find a good moment to tell you...
You're worried *too*?
Yes. You often sound like a brutal idiot.
Fuck you too! I don't need help!
Listen to yourself. You sound like a brutal idiot. No matter what I do.
"So, *Trant Heidelstam*. What are you *special consulting* here?"
"He's here to see if you're insane. He's smart. Let's move on."
"Oh yeah?! What was up with all the *interesting history*? Spying on me?"
Him being there with his son -- it was not a coincidence. It's difficult to see, but he was worried about you. And *also* interested in the Feld building.
"No. I was just interested in the Feld building and the Martinaise Beachhead. And Mikael wanted to see Martinaise. It was a coincidence."

"What *am* I?" He taps his foot. "I was asked to share my take on some of the more *fringe academic* theories developed in Königstein in the Thirties. Regarding partial psychotraumatic amnesia. Group personality theory..."
"He's here to see if you're insane. He's smart. Let's move on."
"Duped again! No one's who they say they are!"
"*Duped*? Hey, here's a brilliant idea -- don't be a morbid drunk and you won't be duped so easily."
"It's the gardener situation all over again..." (Turn to the lieutenant.) "Tell me at least *you* are who you said you were."
"Gardener, scab leader, *this*..." (Turn to the lieutenant.) "Tell me at least *you* are who you said you were!"
"Okay. That... does have something to do with it, yes."
"Yes. I'm still Kim Kitsuragi -- still a lieutenant from Precinct 57."
"Fuck, pig..." The boy looks slightly uncomfortable. "The name's Kuuno, not *Cuno*. It's... lamer. My name's lamer than I said it was."
He looks repentant. "Just try not to shit yourself -- please."
"No. Everyone's just a brilliant master of disguises."
"Yeah -- Major Crimes Unit, under Lieutenants Du Bois and Vicquemare -- ring any bells?"
"Refresh my memory -- who *else* is in this?"
"Yeah. Totally. I get it. Major Crimes Unit."
"Refresh your memory? It's a god damn Major Crimes Unit. There's you, me, Jude, Trant fucking Heidelstam, and Guillaume Bevy..." He stares at you.
He looks at Minot. "He doesn't remember."
"Yeah, that's *very* good."
"Yeah, um -- first, who's Guillaume Bevy?"
"Okay. So what does the unit *do*?"
"I'm technically just a civilian advisor."
"Fuck you, you're part of this shit-show."

"Oh, that's an interesting story, actually!" He's not smiling. "Guillaume Bevy is a police reporter who joined our team. He was really good. Then he left, because he lost faith in your ability to lead the unit."
"Other people have left too. Good, smart people. People we won't get back. Only me and this *really patient* patrol officer are still here. And Trant -- because I'm *forcing* him to stay."
Is this Guillaume Bevy blond and partial to sunglasses?
"Is this Guillaume Bevy blond, with sunglasses? Like you were..."

"See -- there!" He wags his finger at you. "He's getting it! I was *impersonating* him. Look at me, I'm G-Bevy. It was going to be funny. But then you really did have brain damage -- so not so much anymore."
He sincerely thought it was going to be amusing. For both of you.
"Do? It's a Major Crimes Unit! We clear the desk of cases so Precinct 41 doesn't look like the worst station in town. We're *shit tier* now, Harry. Because of you."
They're your posse. Or what remains of it. Hand-picked. Hand-lost.
"You told us to fuck off. You said we're *cramping your style*. You're *Detective God*. Fuck everything. All will burn. Detect or die!"
"Goddamnit, Harry..." He shifts his weight, crosses his arms, and looks you in the eye.
"You talking about Cuno?" He points to himself. "Major Cuno wasn't abducted, you fucking fat dink! Fuck outta here..."
"And you were probably right too -- I would have never let you abduct a kid and take him on a creepy boat trip in the middle of fucking March!"
"All *will* burn, Satellite-Officer Vicquemare. Make no mistake about it."
"Why didn't you detect or die then?"
"Why would you leave a literal *Police God*?"
"I said all those things? I'm not like that anymore."
"Sure..." he squints at you. "You're not a... *superstar law official*. Talk on the town is you're Guillaume Le Million reincarnate. I know this shit. Nothing has changed."
"You were crying hysterically. You were drunk, breaking things, being emotionally abusive. You said we were going 'into the abyss'."
"Oh, you think it was *cool* -- you saying that? *Aesthetic* somehow? You were crying when we got here. Breaking things. You said we were going 'into the abyss'."
"Here we go -- alcoholic delirium. *Visions*. All must pay..." He shakes his head.
"Where have you *been* all this time?"
"Wait, so you let me face a squad of trained killers alone just to teach me a lesson?"
"It wasn't like that..."
"Fuck you, Harry -- we didn't *know* there was gonna be a tribunal, did we?"
"Sure..." he squints at you. "Talk on the town is you're the 'mouthpiece of the Gloaming.' Deranged apocalyptic rhetoric... Nothing has changed."
"Yes. You're *sorry*. You're the sorriest cop who ever lived. Nothing has changed, Harry. I've heard this *repentance* shit a million times over."
"Are you sure?" He squints at you. "So you haven't been telling everyone what a *boring cop* you are -- and that you should kill yourself? People say you've been out of your mind. I asked around."
"None of us wanted to see the abyss, so we fucked off." He sighs. "Like you told us to."
"The *bells* aren't ringing because you have brain damage. Trant," he turns to the blond, "this is where you come in -- how bad is it?"
"Well... He doesn't have visible tremors. He talks without slurring. He can drive a boat. He's standing, reasoning. All good signs. But -- complete retrograde amnesia, episodic *and* semantic..."

"As displayed in the station call, our interactions with him, and -- I don't want to be a 'snitch'," he makes air quotes, "but also mine with him before, when Harry did not seem to know who I was... It's all very interesting."
"Interesting?"

"Yes. Interesting. I have my theories, but I would like to hear Harry's thoughts first. Harry," he turns to you, "what do *you* think happened to you? Neurologically? Psychologically? And -- why not -- *socioeconomically*?"
Meaning: you forgot both who you are and the definitions of 'money,' 'isola,' 'pale,' and so on.

"As displayed in your interactions with him here and previously, at the bar, and -- I don't want to be a 'snitch'," he makes air quotes, "but also mine with him before, when Harry did not seem to know who I was... It's all very interesting."
"As displayed in our interactions with him here, and also his interactions with the locals, where he did not remember being a law official... It's all very interesting."
"Wait, socioeconomically? You think I'm so *poor* I lost my memory?"
"I drank so much I lost my memory. And I'm now *slowly* recovering it."
"I made it all up. It was a fantasy, a stupid joke. I know what I am."
"It might have something to do with an anomaly in the church. A two-millimetre hole in the world."
"I am a highly experimental detective. This was a method I used to solve the case."
"Interesting. So at first he dipped his toes into it. Prepared. That's where he would have gotten the idea -- yes. Practice. And then he used alcohol to 'get there', so to speak..."
"Not when you phrase it like that. But I don't think critical theory -- I know everyone thinks this is far-fetched, pink academia, but still -- I don't think it should be off the table here."
"What?! He lost his memory because of *capitalism*?"
"No, not like that, I'm not talking Vredefort School here. But, Harry, I asked you -- what do *you* think happened?"
"And what is that?"
"A drunk and a loser."
"A heartbroken drudge."
"A police detective."
"Something so sad happened to me that I couldn't be me anymore. It was a defence mechanism."
"Capitalism. Capitalism fucked me beyond all recognition. Trant is right."
"Well it's *not* capitalism. So we can cross that off the list, you lefty dink."
