dialoguetext: "Lefty dink? Well, actually -- I don't consider myself a classical leftist at all. Not in the Mazovian sense at least. But, fine -- theory aside, what happened?"
"What do you mean?"
"He is -- he's getting better. And I can confirm that he drank a *lot* of alcohol prior to it happening."
"I believe he *drank*," he turns to you. "People do that -- especially this one. What they don't do is forget their *whole life* because of drinking."
"I believe you *drank*. People do that -- you especially. What they don't do is forget their *whole life* because of drinking."
"But, Detective Vicquemare," she interjects. "He *has* blanked out before."
"I have?"
"Yes, a couple of times. After some of the more... serious benders." She pauses, remembering. "One was after the Two Drunks case, the other when we looked into that mural."
So you don't *remember* not remembering. Beautiful.

"Well -- here is my theory: What if this is an absolutely normal reaction to the world we're living in? What if this is *not* a significant anomaly at all, something to be explained, approached as a defect? Look at the sensory input here..." He gestures toward the scenery.

"Look at the ruins, the neon, listen to the radio, the multitudes. The people. Live here for forty years... As a police detective, he's like a magnetic reader on the world-tape -- to borrow a known metaphor. Harry's been pushed *flat against it*. Total input."
"Okay, Trant, thank you. That's... absolutely meaningless. I'm glad we brought you. Will he or will he not be able to work in the Major Crimes Unit? Is he a cretin now? I want to know *that*."
"Hard-wired to the free market..." He nods confidently. "He just needed for it to end."
"Okay, Trant, thank you. That's absolutely meaningless. You really are a lefty dink. Will he or will he not be able to work in the Major Crimes Unit? Is he a cretin now? I want to know *that*."
"He is *not* a cretin. And he *is* able to do work -- if not in his previous leadership role, then as a line detective."
"What now?" (Proceed.)
"I'm ready to lead again."
"Line detective is good for now."
"He's wrong. I'm too far gone for work."

"No one even *mentioned* that." He looks at you, then at Trant. "I misphrased my question. It should have been: Is he able to put his clothes on, and use the potty, or do we need to get him on a disability pension?"
"For *now*?" He looks at you, then at Trant. "I misphrased my question. It should have been: Is he able to put his clothes on, and use the potty, or do we need to get him on a disability pension?"
"That is what I thought -- at first. That it was a fantasy. But... I've seen him work. It's not. He really is experiencing something out of the ordinary. He really does not remember."
"Lieutenant, I'm sorry, but you've been *bewitched by the shitkid*. It happens. I know it's hard to accept, but he made it all up -- because he's a psychopath. It's a simple explanation."
"I can believe that. Shitkid made it all up to fuck with us -- because he's a psychopath. This is typical Harry behaviour. A sick joke. I told you, Jude."
"Detective Vicquemare... he *has* blacked out before. We should take this seriously."
"Corresponding to the twenty-centimetre hole in your brain? Sure. This theory has great symmetry. I see how it folds into itself neatly."
"I knew you would be too closed-minded to understand *the anomaly*."
"I'll explain later, but there's another man who's lost his memory. A *crab-man*."
"Take this seriously. I suspect there might be something wrong with Martinaise."
"Thank you, Lieutenant Kitsuragi. Just to clarify -- I do not think isolary entroponetics are a hoax. Pale produces global phenomena -- it's proven. However..."
"This sounds odd -- but I was there. The church on the coast was shaking from an audio-spatial anomaly. It may have been entroponetic, or perhaps related to radio waves..."
"*Crab-man* is an unfortunate choice of words -- but I was there. The church on the coast shook from an audio-spatial anomaly. It may have been entroponetic, or perhaps related to radio waves..."
"Either way, I have put this into my report -- you should read it. I do not, however, think it has anything to do with him drinking himself to the point of brain damage."
"Either way, it was real. I've even put it in my report -- you should read it. I do not, however, think it has anything to do with him drinking himself to the point of brain damage."
"...what has *not* been proven is total memory loss after drinking too much Commodore Red. Honestly, I think he's just lying to us."
"Crab-man... Look, I get it. In your delirium you came up with an *entroponetic* explanation for why you're such an insane drunk."
"Yes-yes. Anomaly. Look, I get it. In your delirium you came up with an *entroponetic* explanation for why you're such an insane drunk. And I understand."
"I've been there: Perhaps it's *not* because he's a petulant teenager in a 40-year-old man's body. Perhaps it's pale-related? Perhaps it's extraphysical?"
"Or perhaps it can be cured with mesmerism? But then I think: No, that's unlikely. He's probably just an *asshole*. A drunk asshole who *pretends* to have amnesia to get out of shit."
"Son of fucking Lung here! Detective Far Out Son of Lung on the case!"
"Is it really so hard to believe?"
"I have accomplished things no normal detective ever has. I have detected a..."
"This is all *pointless*. I have completely TRANSCENDED all of this. You have no idea what I just saw!"
"Yes. It's really, really hard to believe. Because it's *idiotic* and *not true*. It's not possible to wipe your own memory. Even with the amount of *Potent Pilsner* you down every *hour*."
"He *did* present this theory to me -- once before. I had trouble believing it then, but he seems to be convinced. And I've seen him work. His methods are... unorthodox."
"With all due respect, lieutenant -- you're *bewitched by the shitkid*. It happens. What doesn't happen is a cop wiping his own memory to solve a case."
"In fact, it's not possible to wipe one's memory -- at all. Even with the amount of Potent Pilsner he downs every *hour*. He's simply lying. Or insane. Or both."
"You're simply lying. Or insane. Or both."
"Detective Vicquemare... I'm not saying he's the Son of Lung. But lying? I mean -- he *has* blacked out before..."
"Shut up! You didn't wipe your own memory. We're not even *considering* that option. It's not possible. Even with the amount of *Potent Pilsner* you down every *hour*."
"Who's Son of Lung?"
"It's an urban myth -- a police detective who employs highly experimental investigative techniques. It's a *cultural* reference, detective."
"Psychotraumatic amnesia? Trant?" He turns to the special consultant. "I can go for that -- shitkid is a broken man, always has been. Who isn't? I know I am. But you know what?"
He turns back to you. "I keep my shit together. Also, I *know* a person can't wipe their own mind -- however traumatic it gets. That doesn't happen. You're lying. Or insane. Or both."
"Look at F. Booho here! Victim of the ethanol-industrial complex. What are you, an inva-communist now? You think this is a joke?"

He turns to the special consultant. "Asking him was a mistake -- he's a teenage psycho. I asked *you*. It's not possible to wipe your own memory with alcohol alone, right? He's either lying or insane."
"Fuck all of you, I don't *want* to be in your unit."
"No, Harry -- FUCK YOU. You already fucked us -- I've already explained this shit to Pryce *twice*. To Berdyayeva -- *four times*. I'm your partner. I answer for you when you're not there."
"Agreed, Harry." He nods. "Just don't expect us to get you a disability pension. Cops who actually gave a shit are waiting in line. You're not gonna hog their seat."
They can keep that pension, you're rock solid. You can put your clothes on *hard*.
When you clocked out, *I* became responsible for your cases -- and your special task force.
"Hold on, in the ocean?" (Feign ignorance.)
"It was stolen by Jacob Irw."
"That wasn't me. It was stolen by traffic hooligans."
"I drove it into the ocean when I was drunk."
"Yes. In the ocean. Under the sea. Our work vehicle -- with fish and clams and other sea-shit."
"I thought the killer would be underwater. He wasn't."
Lie. Just -- bide your time, ask something. Then lie.
"The time had come. Tequila Sunset."
"Jacob Irw?"
"The famous TipTop Tournée driver."
"I *know* who Jacob Irw is. I wanted to give you a chance to stop *fucking* me. How naive of me. You drove a 45,000 reál police vehicle into the ocean -- what did I expect?"
"I don't know. I don't know what it's doing there."
"Oh -- well, if it wasn't *you* then it's okay. You only let someone *steal* our 45,000 reál police vehicle, drive it into the sea -- and then just *left* it there."
"Don't answer that." He exhales to calm his breathing. "Your badge, Harry. Show me your badge."
"What I *do* have is this futuristic armour." (Point to yourself.)

dialoguetext: "We're not armour-cops, we're cop-cops! People don't know us by our armour, they know us by our badges. Where the fuck is your badge?"
"For the record, you pressured us into getting it. 'It'll be cool Jean, we'll have wheels, rapid response...' I was fine being an equestrian cop. I hope you're fine driving a *bicycle*."
"So *refreshing*. He just admits it. Thank you for your honesty. Thank you for destroying 45,000 reál of police property that's coming out of *everyone's* payslip."
"I do. You drove it into the water. Everyone on this street saw you do it. It's going to be a local landmark too -- on the brochure. Thank you for fucking us, Harry."
"Ha-ha-ha, ho-ho-ho." He grabs his stomach in mirthless laughter. "Tequila Sunset -- not Sunrise, because you're almost dead. So funny, Harry. Thank you for fucking me."
"Ha-ha-ha, ho-ho-ho." He grabs his stomach in mirthless laughter. "Underwater killer. So funny, Harry. Thank you for fucking me."
"Thank you for destroying 45,000 reál of police property that's coming out of *my* payslip. You know that, right? You're gonna get fired. And I'm gonna pay till I die..."

dialoguetext: The elevator stands open, inviting you to step inside.
This small elevator is dimly lit by a bulb that's been glowing for ages. The latticed cage is open, inviting you to step inside.
(Close the doors and go up.)
Go down.
[Leave.]
The elevator screeches and rattles, like the belly of some ancient beast, as it carries you upward...
The elevator lurches and squeaks, like the belly of some ancient beast, as you descend....
Look in.
[Leave.]
Smells of nougat and sweat. Your head brushes up against the ceiling. There is a control panel to your right -- and just enough room for two people to fit in.
The maintenance card under the control panel reads: 'Last Maintenance: 10 July '88'.
Look at the elevator controls.
There are large rectangular buttons: 'Monter', 'Descendre', and an international: 'Call for Emergency Assistance'. That third one appears to be broken.
"It says the last maintenance was in '88."
"That it does." The lieutenant peeks in. "I say -- let's brave it."
"This elevator was last maintained in the *future*?"
"That means it's not really that safe, is it."
"Look on the bright side: if it fails, we will only sustain minor injuries. I'm talking three, maybe four months in the hospital. Maximum five."
"No, it was maintained in '88 of the *previous* century."
"So it's *not* a message from the future?"
"That's disappointing."
"No, I think the bureaucrats just forgot about this back-room elevator after the Revolution."
"If some form of time travel becomes possible in the future, I doubt its inventors will use it to repair elevators in Martinaise,” the lieutenant responds with a grave voice.
What were you used for, elevator?
The deep scratches on the floor suggest it was used as a freight elevator -- for transporting heavy machinery. And one man.
"Seems so, although it's pretty... quaint for a freight elevator." He taps on the guttering light bulb -- it's golden in the dark.
"Seems like a small freight elevator for transporting machinery. For that -- it's pretty quaint." He taps the on the guttering light bulb -- it's golden in the dark.

dialoguetext: This elevator must have been used to transport pinball machines to and from the upstairs workshop.
"I wonder what this elevator was used for."
"This elevator must have been needed to transport the pinball machines up and down."
Could this have been for moving pinball machines up and down?
Looks like one would fit in there, yes. Although it's also surprisingly human -- in the golden light of that ancient bulb.
A small steel plaque reads 'Halter 800'. Halter is a Königsteiner lift company who went out of business a long, long time ago.
"Eighty-eight... This elevator was maintained a long time ago."
"At the end of the last century." He nods. "Look on the bright side. If it fails, we will only sustain minor injuries -- I'm talking three, maybe four months in the hospital. maximum five."
It appears his whole enthusiasm is sarcastic.
Feels like it might jump back to life any moment, the lights illuminating the white robed woman.
Run your finger across the dust of the 'White Deora' machine.
[Discard thought.]
All these mesmerizing machines, just waiting to be plugged back in and played.
"What's 'White Deora'?"
"What about that other one -- the Franconigerian Ball. Wanna play that?"
"How about we fire one of these bad boys up and play some ball?"
"Some kind of..." He looks around, thinking. "Inane pinball theme -- probably related to Messina during the Dolorian age. The *history themes* are the worst."
The lieutenant grimaces, looking at the machines.

Deora was one of the three *Crown Cities* of the Dolorian era, on the Mundi isola -- the others being Rheasilvia and Advesperascit. This theme is all about early airships and beautiful, sad, pearl-laden women. It's quite nice actually.
"No."
"You can't *fire* them up, they're broken. Only that one machine in the main hall works. The Royalist Pinball." He looks away.
What a dumb name -- Royalist Pinball. If they weren't broken, he would kick one of these machines about now.
"Sounds like you don't enjoy pinball, Kim."
"No, I love it -- I love pinball. Who doesn't love pinball? Let's move on."
He doesn't.
Think: Kim Kitsuragi... Kim Kitsuragi...
Kim 'Pinball' Kitsuragi!
It's strange that he doesn't like pinball. Kim here is a Seolite. His people are incredibly dextrous, and they all *love* pinball. Matter of fact...
"Hey, didn't you guys, like, *invent* pinball?"
"Us *guys*?"
"You know -- Seol guys. Massive pinball people."
"Seol is an *extremely* protectionist isola, inaccessible to the rest of mankind. As it has been for over a thousand years. I have no special knowledge of them, despite my heritage."
"No matter. This is a failure. I'm failing and I'm going to stop."

"But even *I* know that they don't play pinball. They have a rigid class society, and a punitive justice system..." He looks around. "We should continue with our exploration of this place. It doesn't matter."
Stop.

"Okay." He thinks for a moment. "I don't like pinball because I had to learn to play it for an undercover job at a pinball ring. And it's a lame, boring, and unchallenging game -- there. We can move on now."
Super. Tip-top! This went pretty well all things considered.
"So you're not all, like, pinball aces? Because I could swear I know you are."
"Okay."

"Okay." He thinks for a moment. "I don't like pinball because I had to learn to play it for an undercover job at a pinball ring. And it's a lame, boring, and unchallenging game -- there. We can move on now."
You still feel he's holding out on Seolite pinball tricks, but fine. Explore on then.
"Let's move on then." [Finish thought.]
"No. *They're* not -- let's move on. There's more to this place than pinball machines."
Kim 'Pinball' Kitsuragi, AKA Kimball?
Exactly. That's what he's known as. His reputation proceeds him!
"You're Kim 'Pinball' Kitsuragi."
"Hey, Kimball."
I'm not gonna talk to him about that.
"So *now* he remembers..." He looks at you in the silence of the workshop -- then takes his glasses off and cleans them.
"What?"
Of course, of course. Just something that swam to the surface. Go on, do real police work. This isn't a pinball mystery.
"Fine. I'm Kim 'Pinball' Kitsuragi." he puts them back on. "AKA The Kimball. You remembered -- congratulations."
"You don't seem to really 'like' pinball."
He also really doesn't want to talk about it.
"No human being should. It is a game that requires no skill and a childlike affinity to flashing lights. And to *fantastique*, science fiction, and historic romance franchises."
"It is *lame*."
"Then why are you called Pinball?"
"I am not *called* Pinball. It was used to taunt me -- a long time ago. *Before* I became a homicide detective. And got my lieutenancy."
"I'm gonna call you Pinball now."
"Don't worry, I'll keep calling you Kim."
"You're Lieutenant Kitsuragi to me."
"I'm gonna call you *Kimball* now."
"Not only to you -- I am *Lieutenant Kitsuragi* to everyone." He nods. "Now -- we really need to continue our sweep of what appears to be a secret path through the Whirling."
"How did you..."

He puts his glasses back on. "Fine. I was a juvenile police officer -- for over 15 years. It's how I started out in the RCM. Once I had to infiltrate a pinball ring. As you do -- when you're a juvie cop."
"End of story."
"You were a juvie cop for 15 years?"
"That time is over now." He looks at the pinball machine and breathes in. "I was already a 38 year old man. It was unbecoming. As was playing pinball."
"Lieutenant Kitsuragi is good too." He nods. "Now -- we really need to continue our sweep of what appears to be a secret path through the Whirling."
"Wait, but I still can't remember anything *else*."
"Wonderful. He *only* remembers hearing about the *pinball policeman*."
"Okay."
"Lame."
"Unbelievably," he nods. "To do that I needed to become a... *pinball champion*. I trained for nine months. The job was successful and I was moved out of the juvenile wing -- to homicide."
"It was not okay. I needed to become a... *pinball champion*." He shudders. "I trained for 9 months. The job was successful and I was moved out of the juvenile wing -- to homicide."
So that's why he doesn't want to talk to Cuno. Trauma-and-Stressor Disorder from being a juvie cop.
"Wait, so *that's* why you didn't talk to Cuno."
"It's best if *you* handle the juvenile delinquents," he nods.
"No. You're *gonna* call me Lieutenant Kitsuragi -- or on rare occasions 'Kim', because it's shorter." He nods. "Let's go."
Any plan to call him Pinball or Kimball is immediately wiped from your neocortex, as if with some sort of mind altering device. It is simply not going to happen.
Signage is put up and taken down, shop windows boarded up and reopened once more. What remains constant -- voyeurism, always unhelpful. And, at times, quite fully helpless.
Is that why that hole in the wall is there? Voyeurism?
It doesn't even matter why it was put there in the first place. That's something it could have been used for.
[Ignore thought.]
It's not my fault this pinball operation failed.
No, but how does it make you feel, to dig through its trash?
Like I should be grieving something, but I'm not sure what.
Like a good investigator.
Like a survivor.
Like an intruder.
But why? None of this belongs to anyone anymore.
There are too many places to start, aren't there.
Then do your job.
But of what conflict or catastrophe?
You can almost *see* the shape of a man and a woman, writhing inside -- bathed in drug sweat and dirty linens. Bottles lie around everywhere...
"I think I can see into Klaasje's bedroom from here."
What were those people doing -- in there?
[Finish thought.]
You lean closer to the peephole, instinctively. I bet they're doing something quite *unnatural* there. Sensationally unnatural.
If your mesolimbic reward pathway were to venture a guess: one of the bottles is probably being *put* somewhere it doesn't belong.
And were your glands to venture *another* guess -- they would add that *another* bottle is being put somewhere very close to that. The bottle is a bit smaller you see.
Also! You can literally put speed up your asshole, did you know? Enters the bloodstream right through the mucus membrane! So yeah, that's definitely *also* taking place.
He leans closer to inspect the peephole. "You can barely see through. Better not to jump to *sensationalist* conclusions here."
"The footprints on the floor, however..." He points to the marks nearby, on the floor. "*Definitely* suspicious."
Boring footprints. I want to jump to sensationalist conclusions.
So this is where they brought faulty pinball machines to fix them up -- a long time ago. Everything is covered with dust now...
This seems to be some kind of workshop. For fixing up pinball machines -- a long time ago. Everything is covered with dust now...
"Looks like they gave up on fixing the pinball machines at some point."
"At some point -- twenty years ago? Fifteen maybe. Before pinball went out of vogue."
"Doesn't look like that pinball machine will ever get fixed."
"This used to be a... pinball workshop."
Not interested. [Discard thought.]
"Looks like it. I'm guessing Martinaise North 22 used to be a pinball arcade before it became a hostel. There are machines left over..." He taps his foot.
A creak, some dust falls off a shelf.
"Downstairs in the hall -- next to the main door. One of them even works. I've seen one of the Hardies bang away at it."
Remember the *Dicemaker*?! Then that means...
"Whirling-in-Rags was once the East Delta Pinball arcade. This is all left over from that."
"Ah, yes -- as the novelty dicemaker said." He makes a note in his notebook. "This has absolutely nothing to do with the case, I'm sure. But I do like a nice little *connection*."
"Could this mean the Whirling-in-Rags really *is* part of the Doomed Commercial Area?"
"If that's true then our *cafeteria manager* is not going to like it." He looks around. "We should tell him what we found up here -- *omitting* that suspicion."
But then it went bankrupt... your skin crawls from making the connection!
"He does not appear to be the kind of man who likes his establishment to be part of a neighbourhood ghost story. About *bankruptcy*."
Yes. Pinball hasn't enjoyed a heyday for fifteen or twenty years.
Yes. Martinaise North 22 used to be a pinball arcade.
And it has been forgotten. Now, there is only one working machine in the main hall -- the rest is lost to dust.
As the Dicemaker said, yes; it all fits. Not that it has anything to do with the case, but it is a nice connection!
Yes. It would mean that.
And Garte would not like that. He should probably be made aware that his establishment is part of the neighbourhood ghost story.
Stupid superstition. But still -- it would be *interesting* to see what the cafeteria manager thinks of this...
It's not a ghost story. It's a curse -- and Garte ought be made knowledgeable so he can perform counter-spells.
The lieutenant looks around the dusty, crowded room, inspecting the tools on the shelf.
You *clearly* see footprints in the downy carpet of dust covering the workshop floor.
Crouch, study the footprints.
[Leave.]
Large prints, most likely made by boots. The size is hard to determine (sole could be bigger than vamp). The soles have left a pattern -- uniform, horizontal lines.
Shoe size is 41-42, maybe 43. It could be a large-footed woman or a small-to-average-footed man. This is, unfortunately, the worst, most vague shoe size there is.
Someone's been back here -- *recently*.
"Jackpot." The lieutenant takes out his notebook. "These, unlike everything else here, are *new*."
"Three weeks maximum -- from the dust coverage. It could easily have been *one* week too. You know, officer..." He looks at you.
This is good. He likes it. That's a little smile there -- in the dark of the workshop.
This is so good it makes him forget the whole *Kimball* memory.
"The blue door was a *mega*-investigation after all -- it has now converged with our main investigation, which I would say is *quite* large."
What does this *mean*?
"It was a *stereo-investigation* after all. It has now converged with our main investigation. Adding a new fact to *consider*."
"This isn't bad at all -- it was a *good* idea to see where that door leads. Commendable work bringing us to this place."
"It means someone snuck through what seems like a secret route -- behind our rape victim's room. In the recent weeks. This may prove to be significant."
"It means someone snuck through what seems like a secret route -- behind our rape victim's room. In the recent weeks. This may prove to be significant."
"It means someone snuck through what seems like a secret route -- leading to the roof. From where you can *shoot* our victim. This is significant."
"It means someone snuck through what seems like a *secret route* -- leading to the roof. The roof, from where you can *shoot* our victim. This is significant."
"These prints, officer, could be the prints of our killer. And if not -- at least they're a good argument for this *Ruby* doing it. To present to Titus."
"These prints, officer -- could be the prints of our killer."
Of course! Damn...
This print is unlike one left by a regular worker boot. It is not a *brand* sole, with logos on it. It seems custom made or old fashioned.
"This print doesn't look like the Odd-soled print we found at the hanging, Kim."
"This doesn't look like the workers boots from the hanging, does it?"
He inspects the tracks closer. "The size looks about the same, actually. They're not the same *shoe*, but they *could* be the same person."
"No. These little... horizontal lines are different. They look custom made to me. Or some kind of foreign print? Hard to say. Still a *boot* though."

dialoguetext: "I wouldn't rule out Ruby coming here yet. This isn't an argument against her. People change shoes, you know. But it's not argument *for* her either."
Get up. (Conclude.)
"The prints look like one person went back and forth."
One person has been here. They've gone back and forth. The tips point both ways.
"Between that," he points to the elevator doors in the corner, "and that," he points to the barred door.
Everything around you is quiet. The prints criss-cross the workshop floor.
The dust has not settled again where these footprints have been made. The displacement in this dusty hell tells a story.
This print doesn't look like the Odd Sole.
One person went back and forth.
This doesn't look like the workers boots from the hanging, does it?
Get up.
The footprints are still there. They have told their story.
The footprints do not speak. They simply exist here, a product of the dust; just as the footprints outside are a product of the mud and apparently different shoes.
The footprints are of one type. They do not congratulate you for correctly recognizing what type they are not.
The footprints go up the length of the room and back down. That is all they do.
Neither the footprints nor the dust speak their secrets. But you know: it means that someone has been back *here*.
"Goddamned pinball."
The door is small but heavy-looking. It's barred from the inside.
This is the inside of the barred door you've seen before.
This is the barred door you tried to kick in before.
Lightly punch the door once more. Just in case.
Unbar the door. [Leave]
Let the door remain barred. [Leave.]
The door shudders a bit, as though it were laughing at you.
"So what's on the other side?"
"Unless we've veered off into a folded M dimension, I'm expecting to step out on the roof -- we could ask Klaasje about this route, see how she reacts?"
Folded M dimension. A reference to the popular science fiction series *In System*. Look who's in a good mood suddenly (and reads science fiction).
"Unless we've veered off into a folded M dimension, I'm expecting to step out on the roof."
Yes. It *is* quite likely that we will re-emerge on the M-Plain. Brace for psychokinetic impact. (Or the roof.)
*Bratan*, now is the time!
Time for what?
Go away necktie. You're just a figment of my imagination.
*Bratan*, don't push me away. I want to be there for you. Also -- how can you be sure *you* are not just a figment of *my* imagination?
Oh... you will see. (It feels like the tie is rubbing itself against your chest like a cat in heat.)
Okay, then tell me -- it is time for what?
Get lost, necktie! I don't want to be your friend.
But, *bratan*... I... I understand. (The tie loosens around your neck.) I just wanted you to have fun. I... I never meant to be a burden.
Necktie, you and I are done. Both professionally -- and as friends. Begone! (End the tie.)
Necktie... I'm sorry. I didn't mean it like that.
The lifeless necktie looks like a colourful intestine of some dead animal: oily, alien and otherwise disgusting. What could have driven a man to wear something so repulsive around his neck?
Seems you'll never learn the answer to that question.
No, *bratan*, no need for that. You and I are *bratannoi* -- brothers. Brothers fight. But when they're done fighting, you know what they do? They party. They fucking party!
First, the spirits -- the blue medicinal spirits. Grab the bottle and uncork it! It is time to unleash the Other-World.
Wait, right now? A woman just died and you think now is a good time to party?
Wait, right now? Ruby's gone. I don't really think there's anything to celebrate here.
Yeah... what's the problem here?
Slowly uncork the blue medicinal spirit.
Hush-hush, *bratan*, now is not the time to celebrate, now is the time to get *ready*. Trust me on this. This is what it's all been building towards. It's gonna be off the hook. Off *all* hooks.
You know what, I'm done with this crazy talking necktie bullshit!
But, *bratan*... no. Please uncork it. I can make it good again.
*Bratan*, life and death are inseparable. There's a party when you're born, a party every year to celebrate that birth, and a party when you're put in the ground.
Why shouldn't there be a party when you die? And, beside, this isn't even about that! You have no idea what this is about... this is gonna be so off the hook. It's gonna be off *all* hooks.
The bottle opens with a silent, mysterious hiss. The fumes rising from its mouth are as crisp as the northern winds.
Howling somewhere, lashing the boardwalk with brine and rain -- an ancient warmth crawls under your skin.
Now, *bratan*, take me off.
What? I didn't know I could do that...
Take the necktie off.
*Bratan*, have I ever lied to you? Just take me off. (The necktie tugs encouragingly at your neck.)
Your fingers manage to undo the oily knot and the necktie slides off. It looks so frail sitting there in your hand, weighing almost nothing.
Now what?
Now put me in the bottle.
But... why?
Put the necktie tie in the bottle.
Begone, foul necktie! Finally I rid myself of you! (End it. Throw the necktie as far as you can.)
The oily rag flaps miserably in the air and lands close by in the dirt. It looks like an inanimate object, completely devoid of life.
It was just trying to help....
Trust me -- just trust me. You and I are going to have so much fun it should be illegal!
I suspect that it might be.
But that's *too much fun*.
Just put me in the bottle, *bratan*. I'm not gonna let you down. You and I are, like, the same person.
As the necktie slides into the purifying liquid, large stains of grease rise off from it and float to the surface. There they quickly dissolve and disappear completely.

Cleansed by the blue spirit-fire of 98.7% pure alcohol, the fabric looks almost new again. No longer like a disgusting worm of the lower intestine, but like a colourful and deadly poisonous reef-snake of the Insulindian ocean.
So... what next?
The necktie floats in the blueish liquid with almost unearthly grace.
It's like an organic sample brought back from a distant star system inhabited by sentient neckwear.
Necktie?
Cork the bottle and put it away.
There is silence.
The lieutenant has been observing you quietly all this time.
He's struggling to keep silent, but finally seems to give up.
"I've got to ask..." he says, a peculiar look in his eyes. "What are you doing?"
"Mind your own business, binoclard!"
"I don't really know, but I'm eager to find out."
"Alright." The lieutenant's face stiffens as he turns to look at the road ahead. "I won't ask again."
"That makes two of us." He shakes his head slowly. "Let's not waste any more time under this boardwalk. We need to clear this all up... somehow."
"In my family, you put a piece of clothing in some hard liquor and drink it for good luck. It's silly, but no harm done, right?"
"No harm? In drinking 98.7% alcohol with a god-knows-how-old tie in it? I wouldn't be so sure." The lieutenant tilts his head slightly. "However, I'm not here to judge. Let's go."
"Okay, Kim... I didn't want to tell anyone, but my necktie has been talking to me lately."
"Of course it has." He doesn't even look too surprised.
"Forget it, you're not *open-minded* enough to understand anyway."
"It started when I woke up in the Whirling-in-Rags. It's been talking to me ever since."
"A relationship between a man and a talking necktie? No, apparently I am not." His voice rings of insincere sadness as he turns to leave.
"And what has the necktie been telling you, if I may ask?"
"It mostly urges me to party harder."
"It teaches me about life, Kim. Sort of a father figure."
"We're buds. Mostly just goofing around."
"Wonderful. Very useful."
He doesn't actually believe it's wonderful.
"Okay. So why did you put it in the bottle?"
"Why not, lieutenant?"
"Because it told me to."

Total annihilation. We got annihilated, Harry. You never had any power, you never were a moralist -- or anything. You can't even be insane or shit any more. You have to be *nothing*. Nothing without the light and grace of love.
"You're right, it isn't nice. It's shit and I should kill myself."
She doesn’t say anything. It’s excruciating.
Sleep is merciful this time, brother. Not too deep. Lit by the continuous sound of the sea outside.
And the shape of the insect, its cyclical praying motion just... going on and on. That thing. Looking at you. You -- two things standing in front of each other...
And a little something in there... a sensation. The bow drawn across a string. Something small and crustacean-like.
No. Relax, man. It's just the comfortable darkness. Interrupted by the pain in your body. A telegraph, far away.
Far enough not to hurt for a while.
And your mind healing too. Weaving itself back into shape.
You did it... you solved the case.
Somehow you managed to dodge it all... The church, the window *and* the bad book in the store. On the shelf. You made it. Across the black sea unharmed...
What?
Turn to the other side.
Nothing. Just threats that passed by -- outside in the world. Ill omens from another life. Not this one. You ignored them. Good. The sleep is nourishing. Take more of it.
You do so many times. Until dim light starts peeking into the hood you're under. The rough karakul. More and more each second. Time to face it again -- the world. Anew...
[Open your eyes.]
Turn to the other side.
The young woman raises a cigarette to her lips.
"*Officer*? Am I military personnel?"
Turn your bloated face away from her beauty and just keep on walking. [Leave.]
"Uh... no." She seems perplexed by your question.
"Wait, I know! I'm a businessman. *Chief executive officer*, right?"
"Then why did you call me an officer?"
The young woman shakes her head slowly.
"Okay... Chief technical officer?"
"No..." She looks you in the eye. "You're a *police* officer, sir."
"Because you're a police officer, sir." She pulls on her cigarette.
"You're shitting me!"
"Who in their right mind would let *me* be an officer of the law?"
"God damn right, I'm a policeman! And don't you forget it!"
"I'm not. Unless *you've* been shitting *us* all this time..." She takes another drag.
"And what business is that?"
"I couldn't say. In truth... so far, mostly drinking."
"There's a mercenary out back. He's been hanged. The body has been there for a week now. The locals probably got tired of it and called the cops."
"I didn't mean to overwhelm you with information. You seem a bit... lost, officer."
"Don't be so harsh on yourself. They let almost anyone be a police officer."
"Could it be because of the drinking?" She raises an eyebrow. The cigarette sizzles.
"Okay, cool. I won't."
"I should get going now." [Leave.]
"I'm at death's door, bloated, a goner. And still..." (Sigh.) "Does the longing ever stop?"
She erupts in laughter, all the fatigue swept from her face. "What was that!? That's not even how *words* are used. What did you say? C'mon, say it again!"
"I said I wanted to have sex with you."
"I want to have fuck with you."
"No, you see, that's not what you said. You said..." But she's unable to finish, consumed with laughter.
"I said *I want to have fuck with you*."
"God damn right you did, you crazy asshole, you!" She wipes the tears from her eyes. "What kind of cop *are* you?"
"I'm a Cop of the Apocalypse."
"Superstar Cop. I can no longer deny it."
"I'm sorry. I don't know why I said that. You're pretty... I'm sorry. I'm the Sorry Cop."
"I'm not sure I'm a cop at all. I sure don't remember being one. I think I might have lied."
"Don't be, it was funny. And, anyway, who gives a shit? Who gives a shit about any of it?"

"So what if you can't pull Grade A pussy anymore? There are other things in life -- more meaningful, more fitting for a man your age. This..." She gestures towards herself, draped in silver. "This is *fata morgana*. One thing, though..." She extinguishes her cigarette.
"It's gonna suck for you later when you have to interrogate me."
"And, for the record: No, I didn't do it."

dialoguetext: "No, I don't want to."
"Has the time come already?" She raises an eyebrow.
"Cops walking around with no memory of who they are, saying what I just said... The end can't be more than two days away."
"No, we still have some centuries to go."
"You're one intense cop. Anyone ever tell you that?"
"I wouldn't know. I have no recollection of anyone ever telling me *anything*."
"All right, then. Looks like I should go and prepare for what's to come. And thank you, this has been delightful. I do hope it happens *sooner*. Otherwise..." She extinguishes her cigarette.
"Okay, that's cool. Or... if I can just maybe ask you to elaborate on that superstardom a tiny bit?"
"It means I'm a bloated old drunk with sideburns and disco pants. If I don't have a joke up my sleeve -- it's on me."
"I sincerely think I'm a superstar. It's a theory I'm developing."
"I have certainly been entertained. Thank you. Whatever you are, you should stick to it. Otherwise..." She extinguishes her cigarette.
"Okay, sir, I have to ask: do you really not remember? Just like that..." She tries to think of a likelier explanation, but fails. "You drank so much you lost your memory?"
"I don't think there's any more to it. I'm a joke of a cop, or I joked about being one, and I drank too much. I'm also old."
"No. There is a massive, otherworldly mystery afoot here. And I am at the centre of it."
"I'm sorry." She puts out her cigarette. "I didn't mean to hurt your feelings."
You have no doubt about the drinking, but do you strike yourself as a tight-lipped drunk? She must have heard *something*.
She speaks matter-of-factly, but there's a sadness in her voice.
She means it. She wouldn't defy authority, however sweaty and bloated it may look.
She hasn't had time to put her make-up on -- this is her morning cigarette. She looks tired, her beauty waning faster than it ought to at her age.
She appears to genuinely want you to understand it's okay.
Try *The Expression* on her -- let her know you want her. Physically.
"Alcohol raises testosterone levels, especially in men," she says matter-of-factly. "The levels remain elevated after inebriation ends and the pain begins. You seek comfort. It's only natural."
She puts out her cigarette.
Her eyes are brown and her face is speckled with birthmarks. She can't be more than 28.
"'Officer' is my stage name, right? I can see myself as a middling disco artist called 'The Officer.'"
*Officer* could be an artistic statement. You're already prone to those.
*Officer* could be an artistic statement. A claim to *official* renown.
"Are you sure?"
"I am, yes. Unless you've been feeding us a set of very well rehearsed lies all this time..." She takes another drag.
"Good. Now, how did you know I was a police officer?"
"No need to be alarmed. I was just getting into character, you know."
"First I have to ask: Are you okay, sir?" All of a sudden, she looks genuinely concerned. "You look like you're about to throw up... Can I bring you something?"
"I might not know who I am, but I do know when someone's not telling me the whole story. What am I *doing* here?"
"I might not know where I am. Or who I am. Or what a *Coupris Kineema* is; how I know what one sounds like..."
She nods.
"...but I do know when someone's not telling me the whole story. What am I doing here? What's my case?"
"Okay." She breathes in the silvery smoke.
"How did you know I'm a police officer?"
"Sir, you've been here for three days. On *official police business*, as you put it."
She's right. Something wants to come out -- through your mouth. But you can keep it down because your body does not control you.
"I'm fine. Answer the question."
"I feel wretched. Tell me, how do you know I'm with the police?"
"It's a small wonder I'm able to even formulate this very thought. But I'll be fine. How did you know I was a cop?"
She's right. Something wants to come out through your mouth, right in front of her, right here... It makes you put your hand on your stomach and swallow.
"Sir..." For a moment it looks like you're going to blow, but you manage to keep it in. "You've been here for three days. On *official police business*, no less."
"Sir, you've been here for three days. On *official police business*, as you put it."
"Actually, I can see why they would entrust me with the law. I have the right character."
"No. In the course of our conversation I have masterfully suppressed the urge to throw up. This is a sign of professionalism."
"No. I realized you were withholding information. Something lit up in me. A killer instinct."
"No. I *deduced* that I'd thrown my shoe out the window from the direction of the shards."
"No. My mind keeps coming up with titbits of information -- all sorts of facts, trivia. Gives me a detective-y vibe."
"No. I think I saw a sadness in you when you told me about the hanged man. Others would have missed it."
"But I wasn't sad." She tilts her head.
"Never mind. It's more likely someone made a mistake somewhere..."
"Thank you, sir." She smiles, lazily. "I mean that."
"Of course." She pulls on her cigarette.
"A fondness for contradictory statements?"
A glib remark. Don't let it stand -- assert yourself.
Better let it go. Say nothing.
Retreat is not a winning tactic.
Something stirs in you as she's about to go. Call it an instinct, a need -- the need to ask *questions*. It's like you've said the words a million times before...
Something stirs in you as she's about to go. Must be that *killer instinct* again -- the need to ask *questions*. It's like you've said the words a million times before...
"Before you go I have some *questions* for you."
What if I don't want to ask questions?
"Of course." She puts out her cigarette. "Be careful, officer. They don't like the police around here."
"C'mon man, pretty please! One more time!"
"Yes, we are mere minutes away from the total collapse of reality."
"Mere minutes? I should go and prepare then. Thank you, this has been delightful. I hope it does all come crashing down. Otherwise..." She extinguishes her cigarette.
"I am a scion of Guillaume le Million."
"Or maybe you *are* Guillaume le Million? He'd be about your age now... Think about it! One thing, though..." She extinguishes her cigarette.
"Yeah, I guess I'm pretty intense."
"It's obvious. Someone did me over. I got fucked -- bad."
"I'm sure I'm usually less intense. I don't know why this *stuff* is coming out of my mouth. "
You're a cop, Harry. It is *unnatural* of you not to want to ask questions.
"Wait! I have some questions before you go."
Let the moment pass.

dialoguetext: "Yes?"
"What is this place? Where am I?"
"Your room is almost next to mine. Did you hear anything last night?"
"You're in a hostel, sir."
"No -- *where* are we? Where in the world?"
"We are in Revachol."
Revachol is the disgraced former capital of the world, divided into zones of control under foreign occupation -- half a century after a failed world revolution. She is central to our moment in time.
"Should that mean something to me?"
"Revachol forever."
"How about you tell me something else instead?"
"Yeah?"
Those words -- "tell me something else" -- feel like something you've said innumerable times before. Your mouth is the very shape of them.
"For ever and ever."
"Tell me what year it is."
"What century?"
"Okay, tell me something else."
"The Current Century."
"And that's what? What number?"
"Centuries don't have numbers, they have names, and this is the current one."
"How many centuries have there been, then?"
"Civilization has existed for eight thousand years, sir." She grins.
"What's so funny?"
"You're right." Her expression turns serious. "There is nothing funny about civilization."
She hates civilization. She feels betrayed by it.
"You sure look like you're from Revachol. Revachol parties."
Her accent suggests she is not from around here. She's from Oranje, another part of the world.
"The dockworkers are pretty cocky. They think they're police enough. At least here on the coast -- I can't say about the rest of the city."
"What is it that they have against the police here?"
"There was the usual ruckus." She shrugs. "Loud disco music."
"Did I have any visitors?"
"I couldn't say -- it's impossible to hear people speaking from over here." She nods toward Room #3.
"Loud disco music?"
"Tell me something else."
"Yeah, we go on, alright."
"It mostly just gets hard, doesn't it?"
"Maybe we should stop going on then? Doesn't the 'going on' cause the 'getting harder' part?"
In that case, doesn't life get hard *because* we go on?
"I think you might have come to the same conclusion last night. At around two o'clock, the disco stopped, and there was a change of pace."
"I don't know about that... At around two o'clock, the disco stopped, and there was a change of pace."
"It would appear so. At around two o'clock, the disco stopped, and there was a change of pace."
"Oh yes, various artists. Ostentatious Orchestrations prime among them." She raises an eyebrow, waiting for the name to connect with you.
"OO were *huge* where I come from. I was very young then, of course. Like seven. 'Life gets haaard!'" she sings, "'But we go ooooooon!'"
Oh, *that*. Yeah, whooh... The less said about OO, the better.
"What happened?"
"Okay. You can go now." [Leave.]
"Glad to have been of assistance."

dialoguetext: "A slow, sad song started playing. Like organ music, on repeat. That went on for quite a while. Some of the time you were yelling along to it."
"What was I singing?"
"Was I singing this?" (Show her the empty case of "The Smallest Church In Saint-Saëns".)
"I've heard enough."
"Okay."
"Yes! There was a church in there. A really small church. Like the smallest, saddest church in the whole world. It was about that. And also..."

"That it doesn't *matter* anymore. And that we're *alone* now. It was difficult to tell -- the song itself was very quiet and soft, but you sounded like a wounded boar, sir. It was hard to understand what you were singing on top of it."
"What else?"
"Then what happened?"
"When you say *wounded* do you mean that in a *cool* way? Like a *wild beast*?"
"I'm sorry."
"Yes. It was very cool."
It's impossible to say whether she's being sarcastic or really means it.
"Then you started screaming and trashed the place."
"Don't be, I was going out later anyway. It didn't bother me."
"Are you sure I wasn't being assaulted?"
"That's so *me*. What did I do?"
"You're making this up. I would never behave like that."
"No, it didn't sound like there was a fight. It sounded like someone was trashing their room."
"A window was smashed. The tape player probably -- the song stopped -- and furniture too. A real destructothon. There was screaming. Then, I think, you passed out."
"Yes." She looks at you. "Never."
"Was there anything else?"
"Please tell me there wasn't anything *else*."
"It prides me to hear this. Tell me there was more."
"There was. I think you screamed that you... didn't want to be 'this type of animal' anymore. I may have misheard, but it was sort of memorable."
"What happened then?"
"I went out afterwards. Everything was quiet by then. Around four or five." She nods. "And that was it."
"Ah yes, *officer*... about that."
"Yes, sir?"
"How did you know I'm with the police?"
"Unless you've been feeding us a set of well rehearsed lies, you've been here for three days. On *official police business* no less."
"That's it."
"Good monologue!" She smiles, flashing her pearl-white teeth.
You don't have to. No one is forcing you to be a cop.
*Try The Expression*? C'mon, why are you still doing this?
The words have already left your mouth...
"Officer." The woman nods to you, still smoking her cigarette.
"Why don't I remember being a cop, or anything else?"
"I'm sorry. I was being glib." She pulls on her cigarette. "I'm sure you're a great cop."
"Extraordinary." She pulls on her cigarette and nods.

And ever and ever... Out of the corner of your eye, you see the hair on the back of your hand standing on end. It feels as though low-grade lightning is coursing through you. You must be hypersensitive from the hangover.
"Okay."
"Don't worry, I'm not going to vomit."
"What kind of business?"
"I can see that."
"Do you know why?"
"Good."
"Is it?" She raises an eyebrow. The cigarette sizzles.
"Find someone else to laugh at."
"In that case, I think I might have a *premonition* for you..." The silence is foreboding as she extinguishes her cigarette.
"I'm sorry..." She extinguishes her cigarette.
"Goodbye."

dialoguetext: A silver jumpsuit falls off her like scale armour, sparkling. This is the sparkle of too many nights out on the city.
She doesn't actually think it's all that extraordinary.
She remains unconvinced...
"This is your morning cigarette. I deduced this from your lack of make-up. Also -- you *party*. A lot."
"Not as much as you..." She pulls on her cigarette. "I'm sorry, sir. I didn't mean to be glib. I'm sure you're very good at your job."
"Of course." She pulls on her cigarette.
Isn't it the other way around? Heavy drinking decreases testosterone... and believe me, you would know.
There's only one solution to this. You're a businessman.
"All this time?"
"You've been here for three days. On *official police business*, no less."
She looks back at you, a light glinting off her eyes.
Don't back down now. Say what you said again -- *proudly*.
"And why didn't you just tell me that?"
Whoah! Something wants to come out of you -- a bit of vomit? Thankfully you keep it down, because your body does not control you.
No, she's not! Reassert yourself by being *flirtatious*.
"And no, it never stops."
That feels like a jab, but honestly -- you deserve it. Plus, it would be *rude* to reprimand her.
Sounds like you were in some real *fundamental* pain there, muscle-man.
"Hello, officer."
You should pick that fat, juicy cigarette butt from the tray, light it up and smoke the living shit out of it!
Am I a smoker?
Nah. [Discard thought.]

Who knows what you are? A monster, a murderer, the Gnome of Geroma? You *feel* like a smoker, especially when you look at that juicy, succulent, seductive cigarette stub. Still smouldering deliciously...
But she broke it at the filter. I can't smoke that.

How very astute of you! This renders it ineffectual. You should look for a *whole* cigarette. Or better yet -- an entire pack! Strike that, a CARTON! Make sure they're all healthy and able-bodied, then smoke them all.
Yes, I should do that.
I should enthusiastically do that!
I should not *not* do that.
I'll make it Priority One.
Or -- you could *not* do that. No one is making you.
Well... I'll think about it.

Good. They'll make you stronger and better. You're too old to be cool now, but find cigarettes, smoke them -- blam! Instantly a cool renegade man, a mystical red dragon with smoke rising from his nostrils!
Good! *Thinking* about yummy cigarettes in your mouth is the next best thing. Make sure you think about juicy sticks of tobacco *all the time*, though. It doesn't count if it's not all the time.
And when you're done thinking about them, graduate to *getting* them.
The what now?
THE LIVING SHIT. Your mesolimbic reward pathway does not mince words. It wants smokes.
Plus, smoking them gives *massive bonuses*.
The idea seems to make your neck expand. Suddenly, the garish tie feels very snug.
Like a cat rubbing itself against its owner's calves. (A cat that wants you to smoke a lot.)
The door is closed.
Try the handle.
Knock.
[Leave.]
This door can only be opened with a key or from the inside.
As you hold the metal you sense the warmth left there by her hand.
There is no answer.
You hear the shower being turned on, somewhere inside.
A tremendous loneliness comes over you. Everybody in the world is doing something without you.
"I'm so alone."
"Why are you doing this? Don't do this to me..."
Swallow the emotion.
Knock again.
Still no answer.
Still nothing.
Knock again, much harder.
You should punch a fucking hole in it.
"Fucking whore!"
Punch the door.
Suppress the urge.
The murmur in your ears recedes slowly, your breathing normalizes. That's one lucky door.
That felt good. Everyone is a whore. Now punch a hole in the door.
Don't. Everyone is a whore? What does that even mean? Breathe in and walk away.
Breathe in.
You hear the murmur of blood in your ears. Your back slowly relaxes when you breathe out. That's one lucky door.
You slam your fist into the vinyl. It does not produce a hole. The door sits sturdily in the frame and your fist hurts. This was all a very good, normal thing to do.
The door is mute and indifferent. Your despair is a joke to it.
The door is indifferent to your loneliness. The world does not care.
"Beauty, don't abandon me in all this ugliness!"
The door does not care.
The door probably thinks you're a has-been loser too. You feel your funny necktie becoming tighter and tighter around your neck...
The door is closed.
Knock.
[Leave.]
There's still a dent in the vinyl -- where you punched it before.
Run your finger across the dent.
This little depression is all you could inflict on the door.
The words still echo in the hallway...
Fucking whore.
Just knock again.
There we go-- *fucking whore*. What a nice thing to say, Harry. Everything is A-Okay with you.
The door feels cold.
You're just as alone as the last time. Whatever kept you company in this world -- what kept you safe -- has left your side, never to return again.
"Why are you doing this? Don't do this to me, please!" Remember? Who *was* that meant for?
Beauty has abandoned you in this ugliness, honcho. And then some! You cannot even remember the *name* of beauty; what beauty was...
You swallow, like you swallowed the last time. Whatever bitter emotion was swimming to the surface then -- and now -- subsides. Submerges. Sinks back into you.
White Mourning. It was mourning all along. You should've seen it coming, it was right behind her eyes...
Knock...
Caustic Echo. It was darkness all along. But you were young and it was summer. You just had to take a dive...
Knock...
There is no answer -- it's nighttime, officer.
A young woman like this is probably out partying the night away. Drink and drugs, sweet drugs are involved. Loneliness begone...

In the Jamrock Quarter, The Paliseum for music, company and men... or the Door To The River, for death and synthetic opiates. Or, way in the East in Couron, in a starlit *boîte de nuits* like *La Cherte*... far from here and you, shivering dog.
"We should come back in the morning."
"Who is it?" A woman's voice answers -- muffled by the door.
Tired. Controlled.
"This is the police. Can we come in?"

Somewhere not far from here the lieutenant is preparing her file. "Klaasje Amandou," he writes. You realize the detective should be here for what comes next. It could prove... *dangerous* to go in alone.
"Come on up -- the door is open!" She shouts: "I'm drying my hair..."
Sounds like it's coming from upstairs somewhere -- you could snoop around before going up...
The door is closed.
Not to mention *great* exercise!
The lieutenant gives you a quick glance.
He doesn't like where this is going.
"Hey! What is your problem?"
"Stop that!" The lieutenant sounds angry.

dialoguetext: Force time isn't happening. You've jammed the prybar under the lid but it just isn't bending.
You stick the prybar into the fissure beneath the lid and push down. It doesn't take much force -- with a satisfying *crack,* the metal gives way. You can open the lid now.
WHAT IS THIS? Your triceps ache for the metal to bend, but it resists... this calls for a potent curse to help break it's resistance. Utter the POWER WORDS!
"The FUCK kind of metal is this, this is fucking SHIT!"
Kick the container.
Hang from the prybar with all your weight.
"That's it, I can't pry it open."
"The quality of metal is not the problem. From what I see, it's sturdy enough."
"Quit pushin' the blame on the metal piggo. Metal's fine. It's your arm that's shit."
He's enjoying your little failure. He finds it amusing, he's revelling in the sweaty rage on your face.
Unsatisfying. Hurtful. You hear a ringing sound, but not quite hollow. The can seems to be full...
*Full* of itself. Content, happy you failed. This snickering trash container is having a grand old time.
There's a creaking sound as the prybar slips under the lid. You hang from it, like a moron, huffing and puffing. Clearly the technique is wrong -- but nothing else comes to mind.
"The strange thing is -- we don't have to." He smiles. "We have the *key* remember. The manager gave you the key."
Give up.
"Cuno's gotta say, man, that was unimpressive. The fuck were you trying to do?"
"No he don't! He fuckin' lost it! The ape's lost the key too."
"Unreal."
"We should find his gun and kill someone with it."
"Let's ask the manager for the key, this is clearly not working."
"But I wanted to use the prybar... I feel like I'm losing out on something not using the prybar."
Let it go.
The dumpster is goading you. It thinks you're weak.
"You are. The prybar is quite satisfying and handy." He nods, without the slightest hint of irony. "But you are just not good enough at prying. We should get the keys."
"I was trying to open the trash."
Say nothing.
"Fuck you, Cuno."
"Yeah, I know but what were you trying to do pig?"
"Figures."

"No you weren't. If you were you'd stick that shitto..." He makes a move with his hands. "In that staple or some shit. That little ring that has the lock in it. Then twist that shit, it's the weak spot."
"What are you his fuckin' sidekick now, Cun'? Don't listen to him pig, you were good."
"Another time maybe." [Leave.]
Don't! Maybe you shouldn't...
Didn't I just have a premonition that *there's something in there*?
There is. But you won't *like* it. Sweat forms on your brow, your hand is still on the lid...
Open the lid.
The smell of rotten food rises to greet you. You see soggy cartons, dirty rags, and organic waste.

dialoguetext: "We should return later, officer. I don't think we were thorough enough. There may be more in there."
"That's one thing off the list..." The lieutenant sounds relieved. "I think we got it all."
The trash container stands in the spring snow.
'Maybe you shouldn't...' Of course you should! This is your time to shine, Hobocop! Dive into that dumpster for extra content!
Yeah! Crack it open Hobocop -- this is your time to shine. Dive into that dumpster for extra content!
It's just organic waste, cold and slimy on your hands. Apple and potato peels mostly, unidentified sludge, and the occasional chicken bone thrown in for good measure. But hey...
Wow, an Armistice calibre 50 nock cannon, half wrapped in paper tissues! So shiny...
What's a nock cannon?
Where?! I can't see it.
It's a giant rifle and it's very expensive. Not as expensive as that fat string of pearls snaking among the rotten banana peels however...
And is that a Cordon Electrics pre amp with Elektra f2 tubes? It is! That catches quite a price, we're talking 12,000 easy. Unless you're into hi-fi yourself?
I am into hi-fi!
I'll sell it.
That's too bad, because none of those things are actually in there. There's just food waste and crisp wrappings.
No you won't, because none of those things are real. They're not actually in there. All you see is food waste and crisp wrappings.
A cruel jest... there must be *something*...
I knew it. (Withdraw from the dumpster's cavernous depths.)
All you see is a broken mug with a racist depiction of *the yellow man* frolicking in saffron.
An antique?
(Take the mug.)
Only in its social sensibility.
"Mhm..." The lieutenant briefly glances at the mug, then returns his sight to the trash.
You betcha.
Never mind, look at that fat string of Archipelagoan pearls snaking amidst the banana peels!
Among the threadbare kitchen towels, something catches your eye -- a pair of denim trousers?
Are these the victim's clothes? The smell is not nearly as bad as the cadaver. These clothes could not have been in contact with the deceased for more than two days after his death.
"Cadaverine odour is faint." The lieutenant smells them. "If these belonged to the deceased, they were removed when he was still in the early stages of decay."
Bag the trousers.

"*Guitar* mark blue jeans. Pockets empty." The lieutenant quickly searches the jeans. "Or *emptied*? He wore them with a belt, too, a wide belt -- the loops appear stretched, but..." He looks into the container.
"The belt is missing. That's it. Do you see anything else in there? I have another bag here..."
Reach for it.
"Nope."
The lieutenant nods, then looks back into the trash container.
A drab long-sleeved shirt, olive-coloured, appears from the food waste, dripping with pus.
Bag the shirt.

"This is a military type over-garment. No label or serial number -- this is the kind of rib-knit shirt that's worn over light armour to conceal it in an urban scenario..." He nods to himself. "Anything more?"
The rest of the rags are just kitchen-variety waste. A yellow old mug that catches your eye. But other than that...
"That's all, I think."
"A thrown out towel, a mug. That's all."

This feels like something you should return to with Lieutenant Kitsuragi present. Also, it makes you feel like an idiot for not having an evidence bag on you -- what will you do with a dead man's trousers?

"Alright. We should go to Garte again and ask if he knows who put the clothes in the trash. It could be as simple as someone from the hostel cleaning the yard, or *that* one..." He nods toward the red-haired boy behind him. "I'd advise *against* confronting that force."
"The kid said he didn't know anything about the clothes."
"Yeah, we need to ask the kids who put them here."
"Damn, this reminds me: I got side- tracked asking Cuno about the rags... The damned FALN pants got in the way. We should ask again, Kim."
"Cuno can hear you, cop -- and Cuno don't know shit about the rags, okay? You don't have to come asking about them again like some bitch."
"See?"
"Information from that *source* has truly been invaluable to the investigation. I cannot wait to hear more."
"You think someone from the Whirling might have been... involved maybe?"
"Okay." (Proceed.)
"Not really. All we know is -- the victim's clothes are in the trash, the lid was locked, and this establishment had the key. It's just a *small* loose thread."
Open the lid again.
Nothing. It's nothing. Nothing more to see here.
What?
Elbows out, there's nothing more here.
A blue piece of plastic sticks out from the apple peels. It's *shiny*. Looks like the corner of something...
Pick it out.
Something larger -- a clipboard! A blue plastic clipboard with moist papers hanging from it. They look badly damaged, but you can still make out forms and notes. Written in a *man's* handwriting...
Not just any man's. This dense cursive -- it's *yours*.
"Officer, is that your... paperwork?"
"No. It can't be."
"I don't know *what* this is."
"The handwriting -- it's mine."
"Yes it is, look." He points to it. "This plastic has the RCM street grid on it. You've even got an autopsy form..." A miserable looking slip of paper sticks to the board.
"There's a *lot* of it too." He nods approvingly. "*And* you've got an autopsy form in there -- in the back. That light pink copy paper." A miserable looking slip of paper sticks to the board.
"It is, look..." He points to the clipboard. "The plastic has the RCM street grid on it. You've even got an autopsy form in there..." A miserable looking slip of paper sticks to the board.
"What is this?"
"You askin' me now? It's some shit, copper. How should I know?"
*Mine*? What is it doing in trash?
This makes a lot of sense.
You don't know. It *might* have been by your hand, though. Feels like that. Feels like you might have stuffed it somewhere. Not in this trash though. How it got here you don't know.
It does? Maybe it does. It *might* have been thrown out by your hand. Feels like that anyway -- like *stuffed* it somewhere. Not in this trash though. How it got here you haven't a clue.
Hey, maybe it's your paperwork, officer?
"If you don't mind me asking -- how did this get in the trash?"
"I think I didn't want to be a cop anymore, so I threw it away."
"It must have been cramping my style."
"Someone from the Whirling threw it in the trash? I don't know. I'm boring."
"It has a foreboding quality to it. Maybe I *needed* to lose it, for the Great Bloodletting to begin?"
"What are you *talking* about?"
"I don't know."
"I speaketh the tongue."

"Do-eth thou also thorough inventories?" He points to the ruined notes. "You should take stock of your notes, make sure it's all there. Official notes contain informants' names. If some of it has fallen into the hands of the RCM's adversaries, bloodletting may well ensue."

"I don't know either..." He points to the ruined notes. "You should take stock of your notes, make sure it's all there. Official notes contain informants' names. If some have fallen into the hands of the RCM's adversaries, bloodletting may well ensue."

"Officer, this is an official piece of paperwork. It probably contains notes on *numerous* ongoing investigations -- and could even list undercover operatives. Informants. I suggest integrating it into your *style*. For all our sakes."
"Well..." He doesn't know what to say.

"Lucky we found it. You should take stock of what remains, just to be sure some has not made it into the hands of the RCM's adversaries. Organized crime and the like. There might have been police secrets in your notes."

"Boring? Try *dangerous*. You should do a thorough inventory of that -- be sure some has not fallen into the hands of the RCM's enemies: organized crime, or worse... Official notes sometimes contain informants' names, even undercover operatives."
Grab them.
As the legs of the slime-covered jeans begin to unspool from the garbage, a rank corpse smell fills the air.
The garbage stinks in front of you, overflowing with soggy cartons, dirty rags, and organic waste.
"By *early stages* you mean these were taken from him no more than two days after his death?"
"Yes." He nods. "...if we're still assuming the clothes were taken off to get to the armour. They must have stripped him of it fast, the scavengers. In a matter of days."
"Yes." He nods. "I think the clothes were taken off to get to that armour he wore, then discarded. They must have stripped him of it fast, too, the scavengers -- in a matter of days."
"The fuck's he on about -- *kid*?!" the one behind the fence yells. "You hear that, Cuno? He thinks you're an infant or some shit."
"Did he? I must have drifted away... somewhere between the copious mentions of pigs and homo-sexuality."
"Fuck yourself, binoclard!"
"No, Cuno, it's just *bino!*"
"The fuck's he on about -- *kids*?!" The one behind the fence yells. "You hear that, Cuno? He thinks you're an infant or something."
Easier said than done -- how could this pathetic cabbage of copy paper and plastic ever become *très disco*?"
Challenge accepted. You should be on the lookout for stylistic elements that elevate this cabbage to heights unforeseeable.
What I should do is get back to that garbage. (Decline.)
Alright then. Seems like a good idea. Right after the garbage, of course. (Accept.)
I don't know, it seems foreboding to me somehow. Like there's something in there that's out to get me.
What are you talking about? No one's out to get you -- get real man! Upgrade that cop-ledger!
Soggy carton and some kind of food sludge welcome you back, uninvitingly. Smells like the wrong choice.
Good choice. Soggy carton and some kind of food sludge welcome you back, invitingly.
"Looks like we found your paperwork."
"Tell me, *see-eth* your bad ass more in there or are we done here?" The lieutenant peers into the trash.
"Okay, I'll do that."
Say nothing.
"I don't know, man. Sounds like an order. I don't take those."
"It would also not hurt to start taking notes on the case." He peers into the trash, where soggy cartons and rags stink, uninvitingly. "Now, tell me what your eagle eyes see. Or are we finished?"
"It would also not hurt to start taking notes on the case. Anyway, where were we..." The lieutenant peers into the trash container where soggy cartons and rags stink uninvitingly.
"I see, yes. You're what we call a *bad ass*, aren't you?" He makes little quotation marks around the words, indicating he is unsure of its actual badassery.
"Tell me, does your bad ass see more in there or are we done here?" The lieutenant peers into the trash.
Wow, went off script there, getting your ass handed to you. You shouldn't go picking fights if your rhetorical faculties haven't suggested it.
There's nothing more of interest in this sludge of peels and meat by-product. Try the carton or those stinking rags.
Not much to see here anymore. Just a burnt apron and some kitchen towels.
"I'd rather not to talk about it right now."
"Understood." He nods, reverting his attention to the container, still stinking in front of you.
Be untroubled. If anything, this small moment has made him respect you more.
His eyes express a rare condolence. Then he picks it up:
Well it is a *container*. Maybe you're prioritizing it?
He's being sarcastic. Do *not* ask what the Remote Viewers Division is.
"I agree. We should get someone from the Remote Viewers Division here."
"No, because they don't exist."
"Wow! Could we get them here?"
"What do you mean *feel*?"
I should get you open, trash container.
"We should still access this container. There may be evidence in there."
Beware. They're very *painful* secrets.
"There isn't -- but we should still access this container."
The lock says Whirling-in-Rags. Maybe the proprietor has the key? Who knows what secrets wait inside...
"I'm so disappointed right now. I thought there was a Remote Viewers Division."
It's remarkable how he can keep a straight face. Take note -- the lieutenant is well versed in dead-panning. Many of the things he says could be meant in jest.
"All the detectives from all the Precincts who experience extrasensory perception go to the Remote Viewers Division. Their work is invaluable to the force."
"What is the Remote Viewers Division?"
"Mhm." He leans in to inspect the lock.
"It's just a hunch. Maybe someone threw something in there?"
"Oh. Okay."
"There is no Remote Viewers Division, is there?"
The body is downwind from here. Maybe you prefer the smell of garbage to the smell of death?
*Just* a trash container? There is no such thing.
"There isn't."
"Lieutenant, what do you think could be in there?"
"Oh." He pauses. "It *might* also be evidence. The mob could have disposed of something in there. We should get it open."
"There is no need for sarcasm. I just feel strongly about it, that's all. Maybe it's not connected to the case, but still."
Keep the hunch to yourself.
The lieutenant leans in to inspect the lock.
"It's extrasensory perception. Whatever is in there holds a special *significance*."
"Trash? Food waste from the cafeteria? They lock these containers to keep the derelicts from flocking in. Could be evidence too."
"Yes, I *feel* like there's something in there."
Why am I looking at you, trash container? You're just a trash container.
Say nothing.
"Nothing."
"What kind of extra-natural abilities do they possess?"
"None. Because they don't exist."
"We could try using a prybar -- there's one in my motor carriage. Or..."
Did someone say *prybar*?!
"How do we get the lock open?"
Fuck yeah! Prybar!
What's a prybar?
Forget about the prybar.
Prybar, crowbar, leverage displacement tool of the gods. Your hands have held its paint-flaked metal one hundred thousand times.
"Or we could ask for a key from the manager of the Whirling-in-Rags. He probably has one."
Prybar, prybar, your palms yearn it's cold touch. To grasp it once more, as you've done so many times...
*Forget* about it? Like you forgot about your life? No! You cannot forget your own body, and your body cannot forget...
THE PRYBAR!
Really? Your muscles are down with either one.
"No *or*. Prybar!"
"*Or*, lieutenant?"
It's not a *pry*bar, it's a crowbar.
"We *might* want to ask for a key from the manager of the Whirling-in-Rags. He probably has one. And he also has *information*."
A box falls into pieces in your hands: Batiste *Soleil* cereal. There are plastic pasta packages below, and *Turbo* noodles. Nothing of note, however.
Used to what -- dumpster diving?
No, searching for evidence in the trash.
You see: milk, an egg-rest with one broken egg in it, some pasta wrapper... Picking up the soggy packages somehow feels familiar.
Dive further...
Good practice for dumpster diving.
You've done this before. The movements are recorded in your elbows, the methodology in your fingers... you're used to this.
"Drop them in here, officer." The lieutenant produces a black plastic bag marked *evidence* from his pocket.
...what's *this*?
Time for bed. Crawl inside...
This is where you belong...
The trash container has *somehow* been unlocked. It's all for you, Harry. The smell of rotten food rises up as you climb inside. This is where you belong...
Ask *the manager*? Bullshit! Go straight for the prybar and pry this baby wide open!
*Still* not force time. You're just not getting there... the prybar is primed, but you lack the ability.
Soggy cartons and rags look back at him. "Oh yes -- and it would also be appropriate to start taking notes on the case. It's what cops do."
"Officer..." the lieutenant says. "Now that you have your ledger back, it would not hurt to start taking notes on the case. Officially."
Now that your ledger is back in your possession, it feels like you should do something... *important*.
What am I supposed to do?
I'm not going to do anything.
I should... start taking proper notes on the case?
Oh, yes you are. It's *fundamental* to proper police procedure to start keeping notes on the case at hand. Open your official investigation.
Exactly. Open your official investigation.
You have to start taking proper notes on the case. Open your official investigation.
The mug, I'm getting that mug too.

Just a feeling. A warning from some part of you.

There's something in there. Not necessarily connected to the case -- but still...
Some items, such as the ledger you found, are interactable. Go to your INVENTORY and select the INTERACT tab to read your paperwork.
No matter how strong you think you are, this is really not something you should be attempting to do with your bare hands.
You force open the sealed metal lid with your goddamn *bare hands*. It is open now. It could not resist your supra-human strength.
An interesting little clue. Let's see where this goes. Clues have a way of magically connecting to other clues -- down the road...

He might also have information -- this is better than the prybar idea.

Your fingers start to itch just looking at that padlock...

Something slimy catches your eye...

His gaze is focused on something nebulous in the far distance. On nothing in particular.
[Close the lid.]
"Night, Kim."
With effort, he looks at you.
"Sorry it had to be this way."
"See you in the morning."
He puts the cigarette back, and says: "Me too."
He is as silent as the night.
No! Not like this! (Crawl out of the trash.)
The smell of rotten food rises up at you as you climb inside the trash container.

dialoguetext: "Good night, detective," he says, with more gentleness than you've heard from him before.
He nods. Absent-mindedly, he reaches for a cigarette; no sooner has it left his pocket than he catches himself.
The morning will never come.
Whatever he may feel in this moment is locked away deep inside him.
A few words also come through the metal: "Good night, detective." But they dissipate around you like the smoke; you hear the lieutenant's footfall carry him away.
Time for bed again. Crawl inside for real...
You crawl out of the trash container. The lid clangs shut. The fresh air rushes into your lungs, but does not clear them of the garbage stink.
