dialoguetext: "That's all for the tattoos. Thank you for your help."
"The sailor's soul would use it to fly back home if they should die abroad. This is a sort of... contraption. To be reeled back in by. The *silver cord*, they would call it."
"This one is going nowhere but the morgue."
"I've spoken to him. For now the soul is fastened inside his corpse."
"This one has flown quite far by now."
Nowhere. There is no soul.
"The times have changed."
She remains unfazed. "That is precisely what the sailors feared when they drew these maps. A fear of drowning -- within one's own corpse."
"I would say he's near the Arcade Islands by now, ready to exit the Insulindian and enter the pale. If I've read his home address correctly." She smiles.
The Old Old World passing by and the New New World already here.
"You said you can't read it -- seems like you can."
Where is he now?
An empire without an emperor.
...for about half a minute -- in silence.
"It's a matter of days, not weeks."
"Whatever I can help you with. We need to contain the situation."

"Then he made his way to the Preto Grande, through what I think must be Staadskanaal -- an artificial channel through the Occident. From the Preto he sailed to the Insulindic ocean. First the Semenese islands, then this..." She points to his heart.
"What next?"
"Then what?"
"What is that?"

*IN MARTINAISE, LOOKING INTO KRENEL*, he writes in one. Then the man puts down his pen and rubs his temples with both hands. Outside there is a siren, distant gunshots on the streets of the Jamrock Quarter.
"This man is no brother of mine, but this is his service history."
"Maybe it's a record of his military career?"
Leave it be.
"Is that all?" She puts down the photo.

"That makes sense to me. We have no more use for a Map of the Waterways. Just like we don't need sailors the way we used to. This is what the custom would morph into on the Occident -- mercenary tattoos."
For all the boys looking for adventure -- a blood spatter on the seas.
"His platoon members? The other contractors -- though I do *not* suggest you go and show them that picture. This man was their friend and comrade."
"I need the information." (Mark it down: ask mercs about tattoos.)
"You're right. Not a good idea." (Leave it off the schedule.)
It could go this or the other way. Maybe if you're tactful, it could be beneficial?
"Do what you have to do, detective. I don't think deciphering that tattoo should come before public security. But if you should wade into the mob to find out -- I couldn't stop you."
"I am relieved you think so. I don't think deciphering that tattoo should come before public security."
"We will be careful, ma'am."
She hands you back the photo. "Is there anything else I can help you with?"
"My bad, I thought you said *mud* bath..."
"You're right..."

The International Collaboration Police (ICP) is charged with coordinating law enforcement activities in complex, multi-national investigations. Their database is the single largest source of information in the world.
"It's not the first I've heard of this. Where did this assault take place? And when?"
The lieutenant consults his notebook, his eyebrows knitted in concentration...
"Odd... we haven't heard any reports about an *assault* in connection with the lynching. Where did it take place? And when?"
"Did you miss the part about *ceramic armour* and *automatic weapons*, detective?"
"That's less than reassuring."
"I'm not trying to reassure you, officer. Quite the opposite, in fact." There is a brief silence. Seagulls squawk over the bay...
"*Krenel* -- an Oranjese military company. As far as I know three arrived in Martinaise. They report to me sporadically, but they do not answer to me. To be frank, our relationship is deteriorating."
"Good. Then you've made progress. It's imperative that you move fast. The *tribunal* will not be patient."
Where *are* these mercenaries?
One is obviously the *Scab Leader* -- at the harbour gates. The one chanting the idiotic slogans. He's barely maintaining his disguise.
The other has a vantage point in a building South of the roundabout -- they were keeping tabs on you while you were canvassing the lorry drivers.
No idea. Maybe she's right -- it's a better idea not to confront them? Also, there's something wrong with your brain. This was so easy, how could you fail it?
One must be at the harbour gates, causing trouble. Directing strikebreakers perhaps? You can hear the sounds of the ruckus coming from there all the time.
This is so embarrassing. You have no idea. There's something *wrong* with your brain. Luckily the lieutenant still has his.
"And the other must be in one of the four-story buildings overlooking the roundabout. He or she was reporting back to you while we were canvassing the lorry drivers."
"That *would* afford a good vantage point." She nods, poised and unperturbed. "*Still* -- I hope you heed my advice. There's no need to kick the hornet's nest."
"Ma'am, with all due respect -- I've been around Martinaise and there's a giant hulk of a man in ill-fitting clothes at the harbour gates. Mr. 'Right to Work.' His heart *really* isn't in it."
"For all your talk of averting this catastrophe, the situation at the gates is a powder keg. Does this not bother you?"
"One must be the goon in ill-fitting work clothes by the harbour gates. The scab leader."
"One is probably in a building overlooking the roundabout."
"I had another question for you."
"Your concern may be appearances. Ours is keeping the peace."
"That may be so." She is poised and unperturbed. "I still hope you heed my advice -- there's no need to kick the hornet's nest."
"I hope I can answer it better."
"That *would* afford a good vantage point," she says. "In any case, it's practically inaccessible."
"Heavens no, I'm not an undercover agent. There's a shortwave at the ship's wheel," she nods toward the sloop's cabin.
"Where is your radio, for contacting them -- if I may ask? Do you have an ear piece?"
"Of course it bothers me, lieutenant, but my hands are tied. How would my employer react if it appeared I were intervening on behalf of the *Union*?"
Surely there are other people to ask about the tattoo. This is not necessary to complete the task, officer -- it's a dangerous side-task. Search elsewhere.
Challenge accepted! I say we do it.
"Could you contact the company? Tell them to call them off."
"I have. And they *will*. However, these orders take time to reach what is basically a rogue unit out in the field, here. Until they do -- it's all on us."
She's being truthful. She is pressing them as hard as she can.
"The remaining contractors. Their *tribunal*. It's what they believe."
"This does not come as news to us, but still..." He exchanges a glance with you. "To *your* knowledge, where did this assault take place? If you know."
"Either way, he's alleged to have sexually assaulted a woman. Sometime later a group of dockworkers got their hands on him..."
"And who was this woman?"
"That's a good question, officer. I don't have the slightest idea. As I said, it's a rumour -- about a rumour. In any case, it's what the colonel's remaining... colleagues... believe."
You'll meet her soon enough, you feel.
"I know the woman you're talking about. We have it under control."
"I can't. This man was no sailor -- and these are no ports. I can understand geographic fragments, but not their meaning."
"Then we're on the same page -- as grim as it may be."
"Boy oh boy, is that not good..."

"It's not good, no," a wave crashes against the side of her boat. "My only hope is that you provide a single, concrete suspect before the mercenaries indiscriminately pick theirs. Simply put..." She grabs hold of the mainsail:
"Not a terribly good actor that one. Still..."
Five days. Not more. Maybe sooner.
"Okay, I'll steer clear for the moment."
You wouldn't even know where to start.
"Occidental... that fits the statement of another witness," the lieutenant says, pleased.
The muzzle-loaders need to be reloaded after every one, two -- or in your case three -- shots, the automatics every one or two *minutes*.
She sips from her thermos.
She sips from her thermos. She does not look away from you.
It'll be all of them. The decision is already made.
Down a deep, black well.
Feels like there's a good response here, but you're not coming up with one. Carry on.
Must be hard to force your face to move in a new fashion. If you continue like this, you'll have an aneurysm. Then you'll have to, too.
Nothing is inaccessible.
The situation at the gates is a powder keg. She says she wants to avert catastrophe but that's where she draws the line? I call bullshit.
"How did you hope it would go?"
"Honestly, I was expecting you to use your *unorthodox technique* to keep her off-balance -- and you know... *not* volunteer us to be her henchmen."
"Oh, so we're henchmen now?"
"Her *proposal* was likely part of her design. This all is."
"The company must have more ears on the ground -- she could have known about my *condition*."
"This woman is running circles around us. She might have known about your *misplaced badge* all along -- or she's simply an adept improviser. Either way, we've played straight into her hands."
"I wouldn't go that far. Her reaction did come off as sincere to me... I think she's just quick to adapt. She is a professional, after all."
"Yes. Knowing this does not really change our position, however."
"What do you propose -- that we *don't* investigate the drug trafficking?"
"Let's get back to her then." [Conclude.]
"No. If there is reasonable suspicion, we must investigate. Otherwise she could claim we're siding with the Union. Or that we're on their take. We'd never hear the end of it..."

"What I propose is -- we ask her. Then we investigate. *Briefly*..." He adjusts his glasses. "But do *not* share the outcome of this investigation with her. We tell her it's done and demand for her information on the lynching."
"We could just, you know, find my badge."
"Oh," he nods slowly. "That would be *fantastic*. But do we have the time? The world is large -- and your badge is eight-by-six centimetres."
The situation might have changed drastically by the time you locate it. Time is of the essence...
"You could request a new one from your station but that would literally take *months*."
He doesn't let it show, but there is a limit to how much the consequences of your unprofessional behaviour can cost the investigation.
"I am sorry for putting us in this situation -- I'll handle it."
"I'm sure you will, detective."
"It would not hurt if you *tried* more in the future, yes."
"This isn't going very well."
"Really? I thought it was going so well."
Maybe this is all her plan? She might have heard about you.
"Would you say it was a bunch of apes dukin' it out?"
"Why of course -- we're talking duke-out central. Full-swing intraspecies warfare."
Now's your chance -- ask her who she is -- she won't get out this time.
"What is the Zone of Control?"
A dog barks, a gunshot echoes off the walls of some distant building. A woman's voice...
"And the apes -- were they evil?"
"No. I would say the apes were *neutral*." She looks at you, her gaze sharp.
"The Zone of Control is the third incarnation of Revachol. After the failure of the Suzerain and the Commune."
The wind stops and for a moment there's silence. The charge dissipates into the dark water. All is quiet on the Martinaise inlet...
"Sounds like evil to me."
"Okay -- neutral."
A dog barks, a gunshot echoes off the walls of some distant building.
"Then you would have died fighting against them. Long before the Beachhead... our time is a shadow cast by that day."
"On the other hand..." She turns north, to the bombed out buildings lining the waterfront. "Maybe you're right."
"On the other hand..." She turns north, to the bombed out buildings lining the waterfront, then shivers slightly.
The wind stops, there is silence on the dark water of the Martinaise inlet...
"It was a kerfuffle all right," the lieutenant mumbles from behind his notes.
"No way. I wouldn't have fought with the communards."
"Yes, an acute thiamine deficiency can be exacerbated by alcoholism." She blinks her green eyes. "Exacerbated means 'made worse.'"
"I see, yes. A deluge of geopolitical questions."
A dog barks, a gunshot echoes off the walls of some distant building. A woman's voice...
A dog barks, a gunshot echoes off the walls of some distant building. A woman's voice...
"I had a deluge too. In my head." (Point to your little head.)
"Truly a *kerfuffle*."
"Him and tens of thousands of his *wonderfully* fascist kingsmen. It was a *wild* time."
IT'S ALL YOURS.
POCKMARKED BY CANNONS.
"Yes, King Guillaume had a nose for bad PR. He ran before it -- what is the expression -- *went down*? Anyway, Gil got out alive and his nephew Frissel got shot in his place..."
"I prefer the term *risk averse*. King Guillaume was nobody's fool -- he could smell a PR disaster brewing. So he got out alive and his nephew Frissel got shot in his place..."
"Smart king."
"Cowardly king."
THERE IS PEACE IN THE HEART.
"With privatized healthcare and a work ethic that does not turn your brain into sponge tissue."
"The real king abdicated and lived out a long and productive life as a venture capitalist in Graad."

"Oh, lots of people. Even the king got shot in the head, or thrown beneath a horse. Or drowned. Accounts differ. It was  unceremonious." She shakes her head. "Just as well -- he wasn't actually the king. Just the king's nephew."
"Anyone else get shot in the head -- on the opposing side?"
"Until it's all mine -- every pigment-drenched black leaf of money in Revachol."
THE AGE OF MAN IS OVER.
IT'S ALL YOURS.
CAPITAL IS PAST.
"And after that?"
"The Twenties saw a decade of urban war: West of the river levelled, offshore platforms in flames... Still, it's regarded as an improvement on what came before: '08 to '19 was simply hell..."
REVACHOL FOREVER.

"The Thirties? Things settled down in the Thirties. Revachol East transformed itself into the world's largest tax haven -- with the international community's blessing. For the first time in a long time it seemed like things were *going* somewhere."
"This does not represent the official RCM opinion," the lieutenant says from behind his notes.
"Don't worry, Kras Mazov shot fifteen million people in the head. But that was all the way over in Graad."
A dog barks, a gunshot echoes off the walls of some distant building. A woman's voice...
A quietly simmering rage.
A dog barks, a gunshot echoes off the walls of some distant building. A woman's voice...
"Yes. The *Insulindian Deluge* they call it."
All that untaxed income must have fuelled *The New*. That can only mean one thing...
"Yes -- the red deluge. The *Insulindian Deluge* they call it."
A dog barks, a gunshot echoes off the walls of some distant building. A woman's voice...
"No. It was a market mirage fuelled by cocaine and quantitative easing. The Forties *dispelled* it like a cold splash. An isola-wide hangover, you might say. And here we are..." She curtsies.
"That's when they discovered Disco."
"Were they?"
"Yes. And quantitative easing. It was a market mirage, unfortunately. The Forties dispelled it. An isola-wide hangover, you might say. So, here we are..." She curtsies.
A dog barks and a gunshot echoes off the walls of some distant building. A woman's voice...
"Until the middle class, the gentry, and the workers are all gone and the age of man is over."
"Welcome to reality, baby."
"That's a tragedy."
"Khm." The lieutenant puts down his notes for a moment. "Opinions expressed here do not reflect the official position of the RCM."
"Sounds like they should have shot more people in the head then."

All she can see are vague outlines of a great winding down. The doldrums. People killed, but no great transitions of wealth. It makes her feel old -- and something else. Something you can't put your finger on...
For her to be where she is Wild Pines Group must have picked the right side.
Something tells you her life and yours are not that similar. Maybe it's because she has a boat and you have... that necktie? A pair of pants?
"Coupris is still around, aren't they?"
"Forever?" She cocks her head sideways. "In twenty years Revachol went from a king to a commune to a Zone of Control. She *is* forever. But the next thing she will *be* is something else."
From the looks of it the Fifties haven't been much better for the Zone of Control -- you can see it in her eyes. Days slipping away....
The wind stops and for a moment there's silence. The charge dissipates into the dark water. All is quiet on the Martinaise inlet...
She's silent a moment, contemplating. When she finally speaks, her tone is wistful: "We could have had so much *more*. Every one of us -- if only we'd played it right."
"Past?" She cocks her head to one side. "That's what Dobreva, the leader of the communards said, before she got a bullet in her head. Don't get me wrong..." There's sadness in her voice...
Her voice is almost wistful. "We could have had so much *more*. Every one of us -- if only we'd played it right."
"All yours?" She nods. "That's been the motto of many an indotribe. There is something *clarifying* about that strain of ultraliberalism..."
"Over?" She nods. "That's *entropolism*, the very height of late Modernity: evacuate this world. You may prove a truly Modern Man yet."
Say nothing.
"Liquidate the rabid, prion-infested *dogs* who want to kill everyone -- with cleansing artillery fire."
"You don't seem to be thrilled..."

"I've no right to be dissatisfied," she shakes her head. "This shirt is Barbara Muskova. This raincoat is impervious to rain and is guaranteed for a hundred years, my daughters will wear it. No, it's just..." She looks at the crumbling tenements, paint flecking from the stone...
"Good. Not that it would have mattered -- in the end, the Commune forced everyone to the barricades."
A dog barks, a gunshot echoes off the walls of some distant building.
The wind stops, there is silence on the dark water of the Martinaise inlet...
"Happily."
"Believe it or not, Wild Pines isn't even the most notorious example -- that would be Saint-Baptiste. You can go quite far with that attitude."
The cold runs down your spine -- she gestures toward the waters.
"That's enough about the times."
"Oh, and the anarchists too! They shot them well. So well one forgets they even existed."
"Then you would have died, most likely. Not far from here -- maybe even *right* here, during the Beachhead, defending the coast the day the Coalition took the city."
"Which side was Wild Pines Group on?"
She's not gloating. It's a relieved celebration.
"Anxious to hear more about mineral rights or who got shot in the head?" A flash of teeth in her feisty grin.
"So a quarter of humanity..." she calculates, "...simply lost their minds? And how would you stop a prion -- a complex folding protein; *un-life* -- with the technology 50 years ago?"
"That's it then. Another topic."
"Those would be the communists. Generally speaking, 40 million people got shot in the head during the World Revolution. But the communists -- they *all* got shot in the head."
"Modernity. They developed the marvels of interisolary communication, telematic milieus, radiation, coloured plastics. Meanwhile, in Revachol West, the *aftermath* continues for the fifth decade."
"What have we been doing all that time?"
"Capital *is* finished. But understand this -- its end won't *free* anyone. It will only lead to more suffering."
Here's some *wisdom* lady. SAY THE DEATH THING.
"Our lives are not the same."
"No doubt -- but we share the same time and position on the planet's crust. That counts for more than you'd think."
"Who got shot in the head?"
"Of course not. It was a highly infectious microorganism that destroyed brain tissue. The actual causes of the Revolution were material. The pandemic only provided the spark."
"Wow, really?"
"I don't know what I would have done differently."
A cold creeps up your spine, reaching its tendrils up your neck, toward the back of your head...
"I would have sought a medical solution. Sounds like *tzaraath* drove those people mad."
Your jaw clenches -- give the lady a taste of your *wisdom*.
"My position, ma'am? My parents got ripped to shreds in the Revolution -- I would have gone the same way. I was saved by being two years old. That's my position -- the abattoir."
"Okay. Maybe it's impossible. What happened had to happen. And always will."
"That's not Coupris, dear. It's just a brand name, snatched up by a Vespertine holding company. No, the real Coupris is as dead as the king they bet on."
"Good hygiene, really? A very *moderate* solution to an *extreme* problem. It's those sort of half-measures that doomed the authorities in Graad..."
"Liquidate?" She nods. "That's what King Filippe kept screaming from the Sol Aurum. *Liquidate, liquidate!*" she says in a sing-song-y kind of way.
Not so fast -- who is she in all this? Ask her who she is, she owes you an answer.
"What did this tzaraath do?"
"It made people overthrow their governments."
It was a funny time in history. They'd discovered transistors and rock music, but they didn't know anything about prions. Nobody did.
"A poor remedy for prion disease," she says. "That was the attitude of most of the more moderate indotribes, particularly those who supported the king..."

There is bitterness in her voice -- tempered with understanding. She is critical, but ultimately understands the cause.

The colour of moralism is blue. The official motto of the Moralintern, or Moralist International, is: 'A blue forget-me-not; a piece of the grey sky'. Unofficial: 'For a moment, there was hope'.
"Not just technically -- practically as well. I like what I've heard about these people."

"An almost endearingly moralist standpoint," she bows. "It must be hard to take a moderate approach to head-shooting in your line of work."

"A devout man of the centre," she nods. "Hard to come by. It's good to have someone who takes a moderate approach to head-shooting -- in your line of work I mean."
Rooty-tooty pointy shooty!
(Cock your finger pistols.) "Rooty tooty pointy shooty!"
"Rooty tooty pointy shooty!"
"That's the way of History." She nods.
"Or -- you could *not* eat all the candy at once, let the ma'am rest for a while, and return to this later?"

"I don't care about kings. Tell me one more thing..."
"About head-shooting?" She smiles.
The rulers of Revachol -- and also *the world*. These guys are strong.

"Welcome to reality, baby."
No. The tiny apes are doing all they can to be better. It's not their fault.
The apes will never change, they are all evil. End of discussion.
It takes time for the apes to change. And work. Perhaps what happened here was part of that time -- and part of that work.

We -- she's one of them. Of course.

She is not at all fazed by your genocidal sabre rattling.
A counterargument, but still -- your historic mass-murderer fantasies have only endeared you to this person.
Woah! What have we here?

A bridge with loose nails and rot-infested wood that creaks in the wind. A construction code violation if there ever was one!

"The bridge is fine enough. Locals use it all the time, after all. It's nothing to worry about." He adjusts his glasses. "Shall we?"
"But lieutenant, think about the splinters!"
Ruination has come. The broken arches betray the once grand history of this building. It towered over the harbour, until *it* happened.

Look at the ruins in the water.

From the eyes of a seagull: a nest of brown hair not worth the fifty foot dive. From a pedestrian on the dock: a rugged man staring out to sea, mere feet from fatality. From a guest on the balcony of the Whirling-in-Rags: a silhouette imposing enough to be seen at a distance.

"No matter -- Lilienne and I are getting on much better. For one, she appreciates the concept of *rent*."

"Of course. I hear you have singled out a *suspect* and are in pursuit -- this is cause for cautious optimism. How can I help you at this juncture?"

"Try not to be scared. This is just how the *real* city looks."

Say nothing.
"Forty-five percent is around where I operate. Things are getting better though."
"Maybe..." She leans against the railing, looking up at the grey sky.
"Of course -- how fortuitous that I'm so close at hand. What do you need?"
"The children carry them up. Come May, the streets will be flooded..." Outside the wind rattles the loose hatches. "*Flooded* with cheap weapons. In angry hands."

"Thank you, ma'am. Do keep an eye on your boat."

"Then there's the matter of that little scamp in old-lady clothes. She threatened to paint the Cor-de-Leite red. Like blood, you see. Well, I like it the way it is -- white."
"No -- the Insulindian isola."
"It's just as well -- Lilienne and I are getting on much better. For one, she appreciates the concept of *rent*."
"That's just Cindy being Cindy. You can ignore her."
"Have I told you how they discovered this place?" The wind picks up, her raincoat flaps in the gust.
"You're not alone. Neither do most of these people -- the literacy rate is around 45% west of the river. Fifty years of occupation have left these people in an *oblivion* of poverty."
"I'm surprised that woman hasn't put me to the sword yet. Maybe she will? You should ask your questions while you can."
"Do you know how they discovered this place?" The wind picks up, her raincoat flaps in the gust.
"You're right to be scared. This is all your fault."
"You're in no danger." (Whisper) "The working class have no idea what's happening to them."
"That they don't..." She leans against the railing, looking up at the grey sky.
"So am I -- and I *do* know how to use one..." She leans against the railing, looking up at the grey sky.
This story she will tell only before she *leaves* Martinaise. At the very end of her stay.

Aren't all...

*"What?"* She chortles, nearly spilling her tea.

"Don't be fazed, madam. He functions perfectly well. He only needs a... *lowdown* on all of reality."

Trying to gauge by your expression and demeanour whether you're joking. She concludes you're not.
"Such an acute encephalopathy... just doesn't seem possible." She puts her beverage down and stares at you. "Surely you're joking..."
"Don't be fazed, madam. He functions perfectly well. He only needs a... *lowdown* on all of reality."
"We may be here awhile, then." She takes a long sip of tea. "Ask away, officer -- I'll help however I can."
"Actually.... that's not why I need you to give me the low-down."
"Oh?" You've really piqued her curiosity now. "Then why?"
A wink. There is a mischievous streak to him egging you on. This might go beyond mere strategy.
"Yes." The lieutenant takes a step closer to you. "Why don't you tell Mrs. Messier what you told me, hmh?"
"Yes!" The lieutenant takes a step closer to you, rubbing his hands together. "There is a *stranger* reason, isn't there?"
"A sort of... spiritual quest? Something of ancient Iilmaraan origin?" There's more than a trace of irony in her voice.
"Yes, a spirit quest sounds like the thing I'm on."

She nods, attentively.

"Where are we?"

"What am *I*?"

"And why will it *resolve* History?" (Continue.)
"By that I mean conflicts. Ideological conflicts. The stuff of men."
"Why here?"
"They say it's where the *terrible* questions of our time will be answered -- the tensions are highest, the faultlines deepest."
"I want to know what *you* are."
What is... (Think of something close to you.)
The price of a 1.5 litre bottle of Commodore Red? The first line of the Firefighter's Code? Square root of three? I don't know what you mean by *something close to you*. Ask a normal question.
It remains a mystery what you mean by this *something close*. This isn't about you. It's about *reality*.
Six kilometres southwest -- in the Valley of Dogs -- junior officer Chad Tillbrook takes aim at a rabid, black dog licking its wounds in the grass.
To his left, his partner Émile Mollins whispers: "You heard what happened to Tequila Sunset? In Martinaise?"
"Yes, he lost his mind," Tillbrook answers, finger on the trigger. "Don't worry, Émile..." He pulls on it slowly. Slowly now... "He'll find it again."
"Are you sure he didn't die of auto-erotic asphyxiation?"
"You can't get a venereal disease from that, can you?"
What is... (Reach for something fundamental.)
A strange coldness comes over you, as you look at the world. The waves sway the sloop, slowly. That's all.
It's on the tip of your tongue -- a *doubt* of sorts, already in your head -- but it's not fully formed yet. You have to wait and return to this later, once the *Jamais Vu* thought is complete.
The doubt is fully formed in your head -- the alien feeling persists -- you just can't *word* the question yet. You have to complete the *Jamais Vu* thought first.
What is... all of this? The scent, the sound, the air?
OF REVACHOL.
"Indeed. There is a term of endearment they coined for it. In the Dolorian century, when humanity was *high* on this world, discovering more and more of it -- these archipelagos included..."
The Confederate Republic of Mesque -- the world's largest state by territory -- has fallen into an especially nihilistic strain of nationalism lately.
"Ma'am." He turns to her again. "This philosophical police detective is very *sensitive* and *impressionable* because of his recent medical episode."
"What is pale?"
"Got it. Tell me something else then."
"Of course." She seems slightly relieved.
"Achromatic, odourless, featureless. The pale is the enemy of matter and life. It is not *like* any other -- or *any* thing in the world. It is the transition state of being into nothingness."
The negation of being.
"The negation of..."
"That's right -- the negation of being." She tightens her hood around her neck, it's cold outside.
"Is it... here?" (Look around.)
"What are its physical qualities?"
"Is it *the pale* or *pale*?"
"If we're surrounded by pale, how do you get from isola to isola?"
"The pale can damage the mind?"
"What is *entroponetic*?"
"How much pale is there compared to the world?"
"Let's return to reality, please." (Conclude.)
"No, detective, we're safe." She points to the sea. "It begins there, 6,000 kilometres to the north, and even more to the south, east, and west. You are in the middle of the isola."
As your gaze instinctively turns north, a small black pit opens up in your stomach.
You hear your pulse rise, the air feels caustic and cold suddenly.
"And... (point north) ...there?"
"Six thousand kilometres from the end of the world?"
"Yes -- that is enough. Many cities are built *much* closer."
"An uproar of matter, darling, *rising* into the pale. Rolling. Evaporating even, a great vision. The area of transition between the world and the pale is called *porch collapse*."
"Imagine a grey coronal mist, cold vapour, marked by spores of an opportunistic microorganism -- a mould that's adapted to grow at the edge of the unrest. It's..."
"It's difficult to describe -- or even measure -- something whose fundamental property is the suspension of properties: physical, epistemological, linguistic..."
"The further into pale you travel, the steeper the degree of suspension. Right down to the mathematical -- *numbers* stop working. No one has yet passed the number barrier. It may be impossible."
There's a slippery article in there...
"Pale when it's particular -- this territory of pale -- *the* pale when it's pale in its entirety. Once you've seen it..." She tosses her head. "Language balks at the difference."
"Oh, it is..." Her lungs deflate, her words sound like a sigh, "...*so* difficult for us."
A squall of birds, hardware operating in the harbour. Firm, self-evident.
"It is possible to force dimensions on the pale -- in modern times we can even compress its latitude, bouncing radio waves from one end to the other. Shortening the path."
"But it is still hard for humans to navigate the pale without getting lost. Or having our minds damaged."
She closes her eyes and breathes out heavily: "... the most *disco* thing you will ever see."
"Extensively."
"How?"
"Some say the damage stems from extreme sensory deprivation. Others argue that pale somehow *consists* of past information, that's degrading. That it's rarefied past, not rarefied matter."
"They call it *the blend-over of the self*. The pale does not only suspend the laws of physics, but also the laws of psychology, maybe History, even... The human mind becomes over-radiated by past."
Who says and who argues?
"Who says and who argues?"
"The logical positivists say -- the dialectical materialists argue."
"What does this over-radiation feel like?"
"It feels terrible. Absolutely terrible. International standards strictly limit civilian travellers to six days of pale exposure per year..."
It's more for her -- way more.
"Up to my gills, officer."
"*You're* not a civilian passenger?"
Let it go.
"No, nameless detective of the Citizens Militia. I am a member of the *Entroponetic Business Class*. I'm cleared and trained for 22 days of pale transit annually."
Perhaps that explains her strange pining after the Revolution? Some degraded early memories...
"Are *you* over-radiated?"
"*You're* not a civilian passenger?"
She's looking out toward the sea, what at, it's hard to say.
She's over-radiated. And then some.
"No, Lieutenant Du Bois. I'm 'Entroponetic Business Class.' I'm cleared -- and trained -- for 22 days of pale transit annually."

"*Entroponetics*," she corrects, "is the scientific study of the pale. Or a recent iteration of it, by way of Graad. The study of the pale reaches back 6,000 years -- the Perikarnassians called it the Western Plain."
They had not travelled the entire circumference of the Perikarnassian super-isola. It was not merely in the West -- it was everywhere. Even then; surrounding them...
"Did they... cross it? The Western Plain?"

"There *are* signs of pretermodern crossings. Successful navigation of the pale relies not just on technical know-how, but intensive psychological preparation. Some of these tactics have been known for thousands of years."
"What has entroponetics changed then?"
"Nothing. We remain powerless before the pale. The only real advance in pale transit is the speed with which an aerostatic craft can pierce it. Less exposure leads to less... *effects* later."
"Aerostatic craft?"
"Hybrid airships, detective. Conventional rotors or jet engines no longer add velocity after the point of reference for motion is suspended -- once you've crossed from near pale to far pale..."
"In essence, we throw them in and they come out the other end -- if we throw them precisely."
"If we do not?"
"Then they don't."
"The pale outweighs reality two to one -- there is more pale than there is matter. And the ratio is slipping."
"Slipping how? To our detriment or..."
"What do you think, detective?" She looks you in the eye.
"It's shrinking. There is more and more of the world."
"It's growing. There is more and more of the pale."
"Oh no, detective -- it's not. One of the few measurable effects of the pale is that it is expanding at an unknown rate."
"Precisely. One of the few measurable effects of the pale is that it is expanding at an unknown rate."
"An intuitive conclusion of that development is that one day the pale will cover everything -- but this sort of talk is mostly left to extremists."
"It's not extreme at all. It's going to happen."
"Cover *everything*? That can't be. Where would we go..."
"Most people -- and indeed most private and government sector organizations; entire civilizations and religions even -- find handy ways to ignore, or downplay that knowledge."
"I suggest you do the same."
"Yes, sweet reality," she stomps her foot. "But before we do, tell me detective..."
"Is this the first time you're hearing this? Do you really not remember anything?"
"This isn't really an inquiry, is it? You can't remember a single thing -- this is the first time you're hearing about any of this."
"You're right. This is all new to me."
"No. Nothing like that."
"I'd like to discuss something else, if you don't mind."
"Of course, how *silly* of me. Another basic term perhaps?" She stands attentively.
There is no way in *any* reality that she's still buying your *shtick*. Better drop it.
"Of course, pardon my prying -- another basic term perhaps, or..." She stands attentively.
"Nothing. Just alcohol fumes and blackout."
"I sometimes sense vague shadows of a past, and it's not good."
"I'm getting a sense of who I am, but no, I didn't know this."
"Then tell me -- what do you *think* of the pale?"
"Beyond curious... Tell me -- what do you *think* of the pale?"
"It's terrifying."
"You were right. It's disco."
"It will end all life."
"Its advance can only be stopped with immediate, total, ruthless Communism."
"A powerful anti-communist force. Perhaps *too* powerful... but still. They have it coming."
"I'm worried. I have to say, it doesn't sound very *liberal* to me."
"I don't know how you've all survived with it -- it's a huge accomplishment."
"Who am I to think *anything* of it?"
"Hmhm..." Her eyes tense. Crow's feet radiate from them. She observes you: your bloodshot eyes and swollen face.
Your ailing constitution, sweaty forehead, the beads there and your heavy breathing.
"You really didn't know. This does *not* spell good for the investigation, detective. If you don't know even this, then..." She stops mid-sentence.
"I'll handle it. It's under control."
"Yes. I'm in serious trouble here."
"This investigation will be my masterpiece. The one they remember me by. I promise."
"It'll be a fucking disaster, I know it. All those people will die."
"Your colleague, Lieutenant Kitsuragi, is competent. I checked up on him. And you have me -- I will try to assist you in any way I can."
"I hope so, I truly do. If I may suggest -- hold on to your colleague Kitsuragi. I ran a check on him and he is very competent. In the meanwhile..."
Some of that assurance is meant for herself, as much as it's meant for you. She must have *a lot* on the line here.
Some of that assurance is meant for herself, as much as it's meant for you. She must have *a lot* on the line here.
"...you have me -- I will assist you in any way I can. Even if we have to do it one basic term at a time." She gives you a slight bow.
"Even if we have to do it one basic term at a time." She gives you a slight bow.
Someone *else* you've met may have been *exposed* as well. The strange grey-haired woman in her lorry.
"Do *lorry drivers* pass the pale?"
"Yes. Carried in the hulls of airships," she nods. "It's a horrific job. Automation will abolish it, soon."
An acidic smile on her lips. It's getting worse every year.
Gone -- like a skipping stone beneath the surface.
"One and all," she closes her eyes. "They say pale is death, but for the Universe."
"Off we go into the wild pale yonder."
Stay silent.
*Off we go...* you see the hanged man's mouth open.
Gulp.
"It doesn't look like you're *doing* the same. The suggestion was meant in earnest, detective. Live life."
Why should we just leave and leave -- and the world get left behind?
"That we continue to persist at all is a testament to our faith in one another."
Ask for Kim to step away while you discuss the pale.

All right. We're in. I know these *all* look good, but begin with the first, okay.

Vast, lukewarm and unknowable. Flowing in and out of sight.

The lieutenant looks at you and you can swear his jaw muscle is trembling.

"So very, very helpful," she repeats. "And how is that going? Do you have any *leads* on that gun?"

"Of course. Thank you for the advice -- I'm glad you were here to assist." She turns to you: "Your *other* dealings with Evrart are still of considerable interest to me..."

"How benevolent," she thinks for a second. "Hopefully they'll help you sort this whole business out... if they haven't already?"
"We cannot discuss the specifics of an ongoing investigation, ma'am." The lieutenant adjusts his glasses. "Besides, you haven't exactly been forthcoming yourself..."
"That's all I've got to say."
"What you've said is quite enough. You have given me a lot to consider -- and may have helped me prevent this conflict from escalating."
She nods. "That is only fair."
"I have reason to believe the lynching was a cover-up."
"It looks like you may untie this knot yet!" Her eyes smile and a tingle runs down your spine.
There's something in you that really likes the way she's looking at you just now.
"Oh my... *very* interesting. So the militant wing is protecting one of their own..."
Her mind races to the conclusion that most benefits her interests. That doesn't mean she's wrong, though.
"I've said all I can."
"Well, I hope it yields something. Otherwise you'll have opened that door for naught." She smiles. "Anything else?"
"Naturally, detective. There are lighter topics to gossip about."
Hear that, hero? Feels good, doesn't it? You should relay confidential information more often.
"Sounds like he has you running errands, detective. A well-established dominance ritual..." She thinks. "Where did he have you deliver it?"
"Here."
"To a nameless settlement, down the coast. Nearby."
"Ah yes, I've been meaning to go there..." She looks over the bay.
"Here?" She looks around. "Oh no... what does that bloated hellbat want with my little cinder block town?"
It's clear the village has already grown dear to her... strangely so. Why *did* she come here?
"No, don't tell me. I don't want to know what he has in store for this place... Probably a statue. It's a statue, right?"
"A giant statue of him or, better yet, his twin brother. Practically the same thing, but makes him seem less like a psychopath."
With longing... clear and simple longing. Strange. Why does she want to go there?
"He wants to build a youth centre here. For the children of Martinaise."
"What size boots do you wear, madam?"
"A youth centre with Edgar Claire's statue on top of it!" She looks down the jetty, remorsefully.
"Go ahead, help him. Make it so. I have no power to stop him."
"A youth centre with Edgar Claire's statue on top of it..." Her eyes run across the water, remorsefully.
The humidity crawls under your skin. Your eyes track her gaze: past the net picker... toward the concrete square of the nameless village off the coast of Martinaise.
The concrete plates cross to meet in an abstract shape, in them: small footprints -- impressions left by rubber boots. Small rubber boots.
Close your eyes.
Keep them open.
"What?" She looks at the soles of her tiny green rubber boots: "Thirty-five, I think. Why? I have mutant's feet. Very small."
"Yes. I'm sad I will never have the time, detective -- I've always wanted a dilapidating fishing village."
"Numb 12."
She smells the cold air, then withdraws her hand slowly.
"You're quite fond of this village, aren't you?"
"When you were a teen? *Slumming* it, like you told me before?"
"You've been to Martinaise before?"
"Yes, I was *slumming* it with some girl-friends of mine. We had boats and..." She smiles. "Don't hold it against me -- my *paramour* certainly did not."
"Hah! I think I was in my twenties actually. I'm ashamed to say I wasn't a teen anymore. It must have been my early twenties, because I remember a particularly *vile* disco track."
"I'm over-radiated, detective," she spurts out. "I do silly things sometimes -- out of pale-related sickness. Like sail over here. The moral of the story is..."
"I'm glad to see your *short-term* memory appears intact. In any case, I wasn't a *teen* anymore, I would have been in my early twenties. I remember a distinctly *vile* disco track..."
"Not overly so. It's not like this was the only place we visited -- me and my girlfriends from Ozonne with our shiny boats, like reavers..."
"Sounds like you miss those times."
Oh no -- she's sentimental all right.
And something more. Something deeper rooted, like a sickness.
Oh no -- she's sentimental all right. Why would she come here otherwise?
"If you say so."
"Why did you come here then? To this jetty?"
She is more defensive about it than usual.
An imperceptible droplet lingers. Sweet like the scent of chewing gum on some letter, long ago...
"He's probably dead by now -- even his shack is long gone... not that it matters. These buildings are all carbon copies of one another."

"Do not spend 22 days a year in pale transit, don't waste your twenties slumming it with your stupid friends, and don't deliver Evrart Claire's mail." Her bony finger is pointed like an arrow at your chest...
She's pointing it *quite* hard in there. Feels like a knife.
"Are you satisfied, detective? What else can you tell me about your *mail delivery quest* for Evrart? Do you think it will *improve* the place?"
"Full of ghosts and ancient memories." She smiles. "Has this errand yielded you any... information?"
"Until then -- is there anything *I* can help *you* with?"
The temperature between her skin and her hydrophobic raincoat rises, warming the Numb 12 perfume she's imbibed herself with. You have no other option but to say...
Below her hydrophobic raincoat, in the humidity between her skin and the neoprene. And on the silk scarf on her neck, a perfume. You have no other option but to say its name...
"Disco isn't vile."

"Not as vile as me..." She looks over the bay, her green eyes shining.
"It is -- but not as vile as me..." She looks over the bay, her green eyes shining.

"He's ready for a war. They all are."

"He has told me so in his own words -- he's taking it. He'll also use the drug trade to finance the harbour."
Green livery changing into red, blot by blot.
Like a cancer of the blood, metastasising...
"*Taking* it..." She looks toward the colourful mountain of crates, like toy blocks rising above Martinaise.
"Then we're talking about a *war*. Evrart needs to let me into the harbour at once. We need to talk about this."
"An insane goal." Her eyes return to you. "Krenel has a thousand men on their payroll. The next batch will be a platoon of twenty men and a gunship. You can't simply *trick* them."
"War is their goal. They think they can win before you even know it's started."
"An insane goal." Her eyes return to you. "Krenel has a thousand men on their payroll. The next batch will be a platoon of twenty men and a gunship, the one after that, a hundred."
"The war *is* their goal. I told you before -- Evrart has always wanted this to escalate."
"No," her eyes return to you. "It's naive of me. He sent you -- this *is* the negotiation now."
"I can ask him to let you in."
"And if he does not change course it will be a war negotiation, detective."
"I've seen the Union's forces. They're better organized than these mercenaries. They also have the support of the people of Revachol West."
"It will take more than Krenel to wipe them out. Wild Pines will need to send more and better-equipped men. Make no mistake, ma'am..."
"I am sure you have the money. The question is how many years and how many lives are you willing to sacrifice?"
"I have seen them. The Union is well prepared to take on Krenel."
"It will be a massacre, the Union is massively out-gunned."
"It will take a long time to kill them all. A lot of lives will be lost."
"You think Krenel is the only contractor Wild Pines employs? They'll only be the start. More will come. The question is how many years and lives will it take?" She falls silent.
"What do you suggest I do?"
"They have the support of Revachol West. They have the position... this will be a prolonged and bloody conflict. The only question is how long -- and how bloody." She falls silent.
Does it matter? Her mind's made up. It has been for some time. The choice was whether to *tell* her this. And you've already made it.
Does it matter? Or has her mind been made up for quite a while now?
"It's not the RCM's job to make these decisions."
"The workers should have the harbour."
"Cut off the snake's head. Evrart's pushing all this."
"You've already made up your mind, ma'am. What is it?"
"First, will this affect your decision making process?"
"Everything affects the decision making process, detective."
"Officer..." The look on the lieutenant's face conveys uncertainty. He doesn't even sound angry.
A constrictor knot of contrary motives: greed, fear. There may be a way to affect her through these microscopics...
"It's a bluff. Call it. Have them open fire and see how long they last."
(Look at your wrist.) "It's apocalypse o' clock. Time to commence the Gloaming."
"I wish there was a *disco* option."
"I'm afraid we won't disco our way out of this one..." she says, with considerable regret.
"Like the previous leaders of the Union were assassinated? I suspect by Evrart and Edgar themselves..." She considers it.
"I admit there's some *poetry* in the idea. And like poetry, it's also useless. There would still be Edgar. They've factored it in. The Union is them and they are Martinaise."
"They will last as long as the drug trade in Jamrock provides them with support. With all due respect, that will be a long and bloody time."
"One day you will realize you can't simply go around saying these things about the citizens we're here to protect."
"Of course. Your job is to clean up after them. And it looks like there will be a *lot* of cleaning to be done in the near future."
"Do you think it's within my authority to give it to them? Do you think I can control the board and the shell-shocked mercenaries they've sent?"
"There will be no *gloaming*. There will be slow, simmering, hideous civil war. The beginnings of a failed state. No rapture, just ugliness."
"So, what are you going to do?"
The lieutenant looks at his own watch and sighs. "Maybe so, detective, but that doesn't mean we're not obliged to try and stop it."
"He's right. There will be slow, simmering, hideous civil war. The beginnings of a failed state. No apocalyptic rapture, just ugliness."
It is. It is well within her authority. It's been clear for some time that this woman is more than she lets on.
All that's left is the denouement.
"Bring in everything you have and wipe them from the face of the earth."
"Such a thing isn't in my character."
It is. It is well within her character.
"I will take your advice, detective. I will surrender Terminal B to the Union."
"I will surrender Terminal B to the Union."
"Is that within your means?"
She puts her hand in the rain. She's silent for a second.
It is. It is well within her authority. It's been clear for some time that this woman is more than she lets on.

"Ma'am... This may well unravel property law this side of the river. If that occurs, we may never see the end of this kind of confrontation. The next time there will be two strikes..." He looks toward the harbour. "Then four, then a hundred."
"What happens will happen." She takes the end in her rain-slick hand and starts untying the knot.
And what about the next time?
"This won't be the last *strike*. There'll be another, then another, until the rule of law unravels."
Look to the water falling, without saying a single thing.
"Is this... safe though? I mean... Won't they start doing it all the time?"
"What will I do..." she says slowly looking around.
The wind blows, waves crash in the distance. She crosses her arms and asks: "Did I ever tell you how they discovered this isola? During our talks?"
Her arms fall to her sides, her spine relaxes.
"It may be the only *break* we've ever caught as a species. The last one for four hundred years."
"No, ma'am."
"You said you would. One day."
"You said I'm uneducated, remember?"
"Typically arrogant of me.... Absent-minded as well. Interisolary travel has left holes in my consciousness, I'm afraid."
"Tell me."
"Do we have the time?"
"We do for this, officer."
His arm rises for a second, as if he's about to put it on your shoulder. He doesn't, but the intention was there...
"We do for this," she nods.
"Why?"
"It was anything but *normal*. There was no precedent, people thought she was punishing the admirals, or had gone mad, or both..."
Each of those expeditions would have been led by an admiral. Sounds like a purge. Like she was purging her political rivals.
"Eight? Is that a normal number?"
"Slowly raining down until it formed a vast ocean."
There are rain circles on water all around, humidity crawls up your back like a piano trill.
Put your hand in the rain.
The droplets feel warm. Like spring rain.
So does the lieutenant. His mouth is slightly open as he looks to the sky.
The air is cold and scented with petrichor.
"'After life, death -- after death, life again. After the world, the pale -- after the pale, the world again.'"
Say nothing.

"A total shift," she nods. "In human comprehension of reality. On the second day, a great skua was shot down, above the flagship Lysergique. The bird was preserved and brought back. Along with pollen."
"Sounds cruel."
"Sounds *political*."
She nods. "There was no precedent for such an undertaking. People thought she was punishing the admirals, or had gone mad, or both..."
"Leaving us *here*."
"The great skua was the first bird they saw?"
"And this was the last break we got?"
"It's raining."

"On Caillou..." She studies your reaction. "The Pebble, the largest of the fertile, uninhabited islands of the northeast Insulindian archipelago. Four centuries and two revolutions later."
"The first living, autonomous organism. Proof of reality. It's the symbol of Insulinde, detective, the coat-of-arms of the Suzerain and the wings on the crest of the Commune."
"I seem to have it in for it. Or it for me. I broke one."
"In your defence -- it is a nasty creature, who plucks food from the throats of lesser birds. Yet much like Revachol, it is also magnificent. And rare. Imagine the suzerain of seagulls."
There was a sting in your heart at the mention... before. When she said its name.
"The nations of Mundi proceeded to discover five more isolae -- or they discovered us -- all in the rush of the great interisolary reconnection..."

"But these others weren't uninhabited. We had to kill people there, wipe out indigenous populations, gunboat economies. Or they came to do the same for us. Or had done to each other. But here..." she spreads her arms.

"There was no one but the skua. The Liliacea. And the blood beech and the River Esperance. It was the New New World. The Mondials used it to amass the greatest concentration of wealth mankind has ever seen -- Revachol the Suzerain."
"Revolution, poverty, and the mercurial rise of capitalism," she nods.
"What happened?" (Look around.)
"Well done, Suzerain!" (Nod.)
"But what was done exactly? Revolution, the rise and crash of capital, international intervention..."
"It is." She pulls the hood over her head. "Soon it will be spring and everything will blossom."
"The gangs will run wild." The lieutenant keeps his hand in the rain. "Jacking motor carriages, ferrying amphetamines through Coal City. Spring is tough in Revachol."
"We will see."
"The age of capital has only begun. I will talk to my employers in person. We will amputate and cauterize Martinaise -- if you handle the situation on the ground."
*We*? She generally avoids that term with her employers.
"You're going *now*?"
"Yes. Mr. Claire has a two-month head start. I can't let it grow any bigger. And I've exhausted all my options from here."
"Understood." (Let her go.)
There are no employers. She's a member of the board. Probably a partner.

You know what this lady needs? Some political advice. Even though she's a high-powered corporate executive and you're an amnesiac degenerate, you're pretty sure she needs to hear your opinion on this.
"You *are* the Wild Pines. There are no employers."
"You *are* the Citizens Militia. There are no superiors." She turns to you, rope in hand.
"What? Of course I have superiors."
"I am." (Nod.)
"That's right, detective. And next time you should confer with them before you go setting events in motion."
Despite his words he's not really sure whether to be annoyed with you or not.
Events are already in motion. Whether your actions accelerated or momentarily retarded their progress, even the lieutenant cannot really say.
"That's right. We're all answerable to someone."
"I answer for my own actions. I don't hide behind some faceless organization."
"Even after all this time I still don't really understand who you are or what your angle is."
"Wait -- that must mean you're *really* rich."
"I am." She tugs on the rope.
"Here I am. I am the face and I'm here to answer -- Rejoyce Leyton."
"I have not deceived you. I told you who exactly who I was -- Rejoyce Leyton."
"How far along are they? The tribunal?"
"Don't forget to shoot the bourgeoisie in the head."
"Don't forget to purge the world of degenerates."
"What further plans do you have for the age of capital, ma'am?"
"Use vague rhetoric obsessed with its own legitimacy -- like I do."
"I will try to do so, detective. If not for you, then for Revachol."
"In short, detective, we will revoke the pigment standard. Your money will no longer need to be black like chitin -- and there will be *so* much more of it."
"Wow."
"I *know*." She tugs on the rope.
"I don't want to do that, detective."
"I do not want to shoot myself in the head." She tugs on the rope.
"Why not?"
"Good."
"Very good."
"I will try keep the interests of the Moralist International in mind during our talks, detective."
"Is it?" She tugs on the rope.
"Keep the peace -- and I will keep my end of the bargain."

"I know -- because I, too, am insane. I just hide my illness better. And I'm rich."
"What do you have?"
"I'm over-exposed, baby. My travels take me through the pale dozens of times a year. I've got the longing -- and I've got it *bad*." She points to her heart.

"The same strict psychological regimen the eighth admiral developed when he crossed the pale and discovered this isola -- the *Volta do Mar*. It's used by interisolary travellers and other troubled souls even to this day."
"How do you keep your shit together?"
"How do you keep it together?"
"Goodbye, Rejoyce Leyton." (Conclude.)
She smiles. "Watch out for yourselves. They will strike soon."
"Goodbye, nether creature of the forbidden swamp." (Conclude.)
She smiles. "Watch out for yourself. They will strike soon."
"No, detective -- no one's as insane as you."
"Isn't *everybody* a little insane?"
"Don't worry madam. I am very sane."
"How far along is Krenel's *investigation*?"
"A confrontation is imminent. They have followed in your footsteps..."
"As your investigation reaches a climax, so does theirs. They are your shadow. Arm yourselves. Armour yourselves..."
"Protect their targets. Violence may be unavoidable, but we can limit the casualties."
"When will they make their move? Where?"
"Soon. I do not know precisely. They have cut off all communication, you see. They know I've been feeding you information."
"Goodbye, Joyce L. Messier." (Conclude.)
"One last thing, nameless detective." She starts the engine. "I've given the matter much thought and come to this conclusion: You're not an amnesiac. You're *insane*."
"'*Après la vie, la mort*,' they summarized it for the queen and Dolores Dei; '*Après la mort, la vie encore! Après le monde, le gris. Après le gris, le monde encore!*'"
"You would prefer something else? Not a youth centre?"
"First, there won't *be* a youth centre, whatever he's told you or the residents. It'll be something horrific. Perhaps even *worse* than a statue -- so yes, I do."
"A *fishery*. I've been speaking with Lilienne here. She gave me the idea. The infrastructure is all here, and with my connections..."

He's able to contain the anger and surprise.

This is going to be hard to recover from.

"I'm not sure, exactly, but you seemed to be caught in some sort of *loop*."

"That sounds like me."
"I have no idea what you're talking about."
"Now please, ask me something else before it happens *again*. Something that *preferably* doesn't include the words *mister* or *Evrart*."
"Nope -- you misunderstand. I turned the knob like this." (Turn the heat *down*)

"I should be." She nods -- there's that crooked smile again. "In my youth I had a brief dalliance here in Martinaise. He was an older man, with impossibly broad shoulders..."
"We told ourselves we were the worst thing to happen to the coast since the Coalition landed in '08. Imagine!" She tosses her head.
"You're wrong, detective. And next time you should confer with those superiors before you go setting events in motion."
"You misunderstand, detective. We're all answerable to someone."
"On the contrary, detective." She tugs on the rope. "It's a real *drag*."
Yeah, we need to pull the plug, there's nothing else to do.
Are you not afraid it'll kill him?
*Physically* he should be fine. Or at least no worse than usual...
"So you're sad you can't buy the place?" (Conclude.)

"It's not important if I liked him. I was doing my job."

"And if it *were* a conflict, the RCM would not pick sides. My colleague's *unusual* approach to police work does not represent the organization at this time."
"I've seen him and believe me -- it's a conflict. I've picked my side in the coming storm and it's you."
"Okay, yes, perhaps I misread the situation. And the era -- it's not feudal."
"Of course. And I don't expect you to share anything he told you with me. I'm not a *corrupt würm* myself." There's a pause. "However, if you felt like passing *some* information..."

"Well, I can't stop you, can I? Just understand that I don't *expect* you to share anything he told you with me. I'm not a *corrupt würm* myself." There's a pause. "However, if you felt like passing *some* information..."
"Of course, detective. Excuse me for implying otherwise."
"The RCM does not pick sides in this. I hope it doesn't come off any other way."
"I don't expect you to share anything he told you with me. I'm not a *corrupt würm* myself." There's a pause. "However, if you felt like passing *some* information..."
"Just? Hmm... in what way?"
"In a funky socialist way. He looks out for the people."
"In a nice, crunchy, white working class way of course."
"Yeah, he's not actually just, is he? He's useless."
"Of course. *Some* of them, at least. The ones who work for him -- how else would he have stayed in power all these years... no wait, actually..."
"Of course. How else would he have stayed in power all these years if it were not for *ethnic nationalism*... or wait..."

"Yes -- I have *chosen* his side in the class war. My loyalty does not have a price and is non-negotiable. Sorry."
