"I do not *expect* you to share anything Evrart told you with me -- not being a corrupt *würm* myself." She pauses. "However, if you felt like passing *some* information..."
"...how could I stop you? Are we not human? Are we not *curious* to hear another person's take? It's only natural. We would only be..." she smiles, "gossiping."
Don't fall for it, it's a ploy to get you talking. The honey-mouthed syllables, the smiling, the conspiratorial jokes, all of it!
Intellectually speaking... it would be quite *interesting* to hear what she has to say about these things...
"Incredible," she shakes her head. "Simply incredible -- and how is it going? Has this *detecting* produced a gun?"
"No need to flash my gun around. Let's just say I have it now. Thank god." (Pat your gun.)
"Thank god -- and indeed *Mr. Evrart* as well. In this investigation one may have *use* for a firearm -- you wouldn't want to get caught with your pants down..."
"Mr. Evrart helped me find my gun."
"Oh!" Her eyes become large and round. "That's so *helpful* of him..."
"Stupendous!" She nods, more than a bit surprised. "I didn't think he'd pull through."
Hmm... perhaps he is?
"*Beyond* curious. I will *choose* to interpret that as you turning the alcohol in the strike brew *down* -- for the sake of our professional relationship."
"Actually, I turned the knob like this." (Turn the heat *down*.)
"And because I don't like the idea of them any more drunk than they already are." She nods. "What else?"
"I actually *lied* that I opened the door. I didn't really do it."
"Stupendous." She takes a little bow. "Pulling one on the old würm. Commendably done. And... did this trick  yield anything interesting? I assume it was necessary -- for the case..."
"Detective, I advise you to be *very* selective with what information you choose to share. This may have consequences beyond our line-of-sight."
"The man whose door I opened planned to write an article into a local paper."
"About what?"
"The strike being funded by a protection racket."

"Precisely," she smiles. "Don't worry about that article -- regional papers are useless anyway. You probably spared the man his kneecaps. And *I* can be sure that the local shops have a bone to pick with Evrart." She smiles.
"One that has apparently driven local shops out of business."
"That would explain why the Whirling-in-Rags -- where the Union congregates -- is the *only* bar left open in Martinaise. Well that and Frittte because..."
"Nobody fucks with Frittte, ma'am."

"Don't worry about that one article, dear -- regional papers are useless anyway. You probably spared the man his kneecaps. And *I* can be sure that the local shops have a bone to pick with Evrart." She smiles.
A flash of satisfaction. She can use this, in the future. To turn the tide against Evrart on the streets.
This is good. It pleases her.
"I told him about the mercenary tribunal -- he didn't seem too worried."
"Brinkmanship -- or sabre-rattling... Was he surrounded by *Union men* he wanted to impress?"
"I told him a drug trader might be somehow involved in the murder. He denied participating in the trade."
"Well, of course he would -- that still doesn't mean he's not benefiting from the arrangement -- the lorries, the harbour, all of it. It just means he doesn't outright admit to it."
That is very, very likely yes.
"Well, of course he would -- I really hope you and I get to talk about this drug trade matter in the future. The company has been suspecting foul play for years. Anyway..."
Sounds like she'll solicit your help with something -- when she gets the chance.
"We were alone. And he seems very sure of his ability to keep things in control."
"Or he wants you and me to *believe* he's calm and in control. He's a politician."
Of course. Politics is showmanship. He is constantly performing for us... and lying too. I am sorry I don't catch more of his falsehoods, there are just so *many*...
No. It was more like he wanted things to get *worse* -- in secret of course.
"Nowhere. Let's change the topic."
"Of course -- to *other* matters you've discussed perhaps?"
"I'm over-radiated, detective," she spurts out. "I do silly things sometimes -- out of pale-related sickness. Like take this job. The moral of the story is..."
So it was a factor in her coming to Martinaise in the first place? Interesting.
"Like what?"
"Of course, detective," she simmers down. "You can always drop by later, should something come up -- now, what else can I do you for?"
*Now* say it: "Ma'am, this whole thing is a takeover."
For once, I don't seem to know what the right thing to do is.
"Good. They will start asking for more... And more..."
"And here I thought my modest payment of 70 reál would stick..." She shakes her head in mock regret.
"Side-shifting? Of course, *that's* why my payment of 70 reál didn't stick..." She shakes her head in mock regret.
We're pulling the plug on this. Nothing else to be done. Good luck, everyone.
She looks beyond you, despondent.
Here comes the dark. The plug will be pulled... now.
"Mr. Evrart is helping me find my gun."
She enjoys a small sip.
"Mr. Evrart is helping me find my gun."
She reconsiders that sip.
Could it be all my fellows have failed? Alack and alas, sire! Forgive me! I shall do my best to end this pantomime...
"Mr. Evrart is helping me find my gun."
"Mr. Evrart is helping me find my gun."
...is what you're about to say when a cold streak runs through your heart. Once said, there's no going back, Harry.
Yes. What if something happens to her and you've left *one* question un-asked. Sneaky little question escaped your eye.
Yes, there is still reality-based knowledge I can glean from her.
Right. She hasn't even told me what she knows about the lynching.
(No. Say it.) "Ma'am, this is a takeover."
Almost gave you a heart attack, that one...
Yes... come back to this later. This information could be explosive.
"Actually... this is not Evrart-related, but I tracked down a suspect."
The lieutenant narrows his eyes.
I do *not* think that's a good idea.
She looks positively surprised. "That's great. For the investigation, I mean."
"It went really badly. She killed herself."
"It didn't go too well. She got away -- *and* it doesn't look like she did it."
"That's really all I can say about that."
"A *she...*" The negotiator does not seem to be shocked at first.
Not even a flinch. That must take willpower. Yet below it, some little crack starts running in the foundation.
"I hope she wasn't a serious suspect then -- as to the suicide -- that must be *difficult*. Yet, in your line of work..." She tilts her head.
Not be too rare an occurrence.
"A she..." She raises a brow. "I hope she wasn't too serious a suspect. If she got away..."
"We're not at liberty to discuss that ma'am."
"Naturally. I completely understand. But... you mentioned something about Mr. Claire? Or something in conjunction with the Union even? I might have gotten the wrong idea, but..."
"But -- I won't pry further about the case. You mentioned something about Mr. Claire, I believe? Or something in conjunction with the Union? I might have gotten the wrong idea, but..."
Curiosity for the Union burns brighter in her than curiosity for the case...
"She didn't do it. She was framed."
"It's... not good. I did not do good there."
"I don't even know why I told you. This isn't about Evrart..."
"Oh, we humans just like to discuss things -- it's absolutely normal. I won't pry further. If anything regarding the Union has come up..." She raises a brow. "They won't talk to *me*."
"Unfortunate." She shakes her head. "I won't pry further into the details of your investigation, but let me just say -- I have *full* trust in your competence."
"This thing is what you call a..." she pronounces the word with sudden carelessness: "*clusterfuck*. I am saddened to hear the news, of course. But we must continue. Lest the situation worsens."
There's turmoil in there now -- but still she keeps it in check.

"And you too, lieutenant," she turns to him and stresses: "The situation is perilous, but I am *sure* you're dedicated to avoiding further loss of life. Unlike the Union, who won't even let me talk to them."
A barely perceptible nod.
Finally -- time to choose SIDES.
Tell her, she'll *like* you for it.
Yes! Your disgusting tie agrees completely. Let's *gossip*.
That's wrong! You don't get into loops!
Totally slanderous. Maybe you've gotten into *one* tiny loop once.
The lieutenant will be more lenient toward sharing those, hopefully.
"The company did not 'send mercenaries after the Union'. I told you, in great detail, about the mistakes my side made. And of course I accept them completely."
"I just hope you don't share Evrart's view on things. After all, as he said: one's *dead* now. The Pines certainly hasn't killed any of theirs."
Let's keep it that way -- she means to add, but then doesn't.
Look who's defensive suddenly.
"Hurry up on that probe. The moment you tell me you're finished at the traffic jam, I will *gladly* tell you the company's side of the story."
She must really want you to look into the drugs -- otherwise she'd tell you.
She was *worried* for a moment. That she's overplayed her hand by not sharing info sooner. Then she settles down, curious to hear more.
This gave her pause. She's pensive, suddenly. Hard to say about what...
Have I underestimated the Union's ferocity? She *has* to ask herself by now..
The prints are *hers*.
She's sentimental all right. You don't know enough about her to find out why exactly. She will keep her secrets for now.
She nods. "It may be the only *break* we've ever caught as a species. The last one for four hundred years."
After life, death. After death, life again. After the isola, the pale. After the pale, isola again.
She would die to return to it. The pale. The past. Anything one can return to.
You could use a little of it yourself.
With worry in his eyes. He does not know if it was the right thing to do. But he doesn't say anything.
You wonder what Evrart has to say about this...
Slowly, the sails turn a grey blue as more oxygen gets between you.
The lieutenant watches her boat grow smaller on the bay, its white sails fluttering.
Another woman gone.
When I said *be wacky* I didn't mean *wildly, grossly irresponsible and damaging to the RCM*.
Your stomach gurgles... something tells you that your chance to track down the reality rhizome has left. Better return to Measurehead, see what he has to say.
"Hey, up here, piggo!"
"Look at me when I'm talking to you."
"Yeah, you better keep walking."
There it is again! There's a spectral scent haunting this pier, no doubt. And it smells like...
There! Do you smell that?
Sea brine, mostly. Because it's a pier.
Years of turmoil, of hopes and dreams ground beneath the inexorable tides of capital.
Smell what?
I don't smell anything.
Can you not detect that inimitable whiff of dissatisfaction and restlessness, that sense that the world is in need of dramatic, even violent re-ordering?
(Close your eyes and take a deep breath.)
Are you saying there's a communist nearby?
What do you smell?
The first thing that strikes you is the overwhelming brine. You imagine yourself underwater, a hundred-legged arthropod scuttling along the murky silt at the bottom of the sea...
But then the unmistakable reek of *seagull shit* hits you, buoyed along on the air currents, an acrid melody atop mouldering chords of wood rot and heavy fuel oil.
Nothing. Or at least, nothing in particular. As far as you're concerned, your nose seems to be purely decorative.
"Still smelling for communists, detective?"
"Everything in order, detective?" The lieutenant gives you a quizzical look.
It smells like a pier, in other words. A completely ordinary pier, that provokes no ideological associations whatsoever.
Absolute rubbish. Your politico-olfactory cortex doesn't deceive you. The smell is coming... from that balcony over there!
Without a doubt. Your politico-olfactory cortex doesn't deceive you. The smell is coming... from that balcony over there!
You mean from Cindy?
You mean from that scary-looking girl in the old lady coat?
Certainement! A precocious communist youth, a symbol of a kinder, more hopeful future. Now's your chance to *establish contact* with your revolutionary brothers and sisters.
A chance to establish contact with the future! What a beautiful, *terrible* thought...
"It's kind of a personal errand."
"I'm smelling for communists, Kim."
"I'm working on developing my political consciousness."
"Just taking in the fresh air, like a normal detective."
"A personal errand."
"You're smelling for..."
"You're developing your..."
"There's a lot to take in, isn't there?" The lieutenant wrinkles his nose.
"You know what? I'll just leave you to it. Carry on, detective."
"I'm struggling to see the connection with our investigation, but I'm sure *all will be revealed* in time."
"You do remember that we're investigating a *murder*, yes? I would appreciate it if you reserved your political projects for after-hours."
The lieutenant lacks your highly developed politico-olfactory cortex. The smell is undeniable. And it's coming... from that balcony up there!
"Yes."
"Well, I'll be over here when you've finished." The lieutenant nudges a piece of trash with his foot.
"Uh huh."
"No offence, detective, but you're not particularly *subtle*."
"No."
"What makes you say that?"
His impatience is feigned. He's actually curious to see how this *personal errand* shakes out.
He'll tolerate this *personal errand*, but his patience is wearing thin.
The lieutenant issss *not* persuaded, sssssire.
The lieutenant's right. It's sort of amazing how *un-subtly* you're sniffing the air around you, almost like you're *trying* to call attention to yourself.

What the lieutenant thinks is irrelevant. Your politico-olfactory cortex is lighting up like a holiday display. The scent of communism is overwhelming, and it's coming right... from that balcony over there!
I *still* don't smell anything.
(Close your eyes and take a deep breath.)
I can *kind of* smell dreams being ground down by capital.
There! On that balcony. Do you see it? It's an artist!
A strong aura of *originality* surrounds the girl in question.
Quick, kill it with fire before it organises a *happening*!
How can you tell?
Yes, I can sense the *originality*...
All stations beware, it's a level three happening-alert!
Not now. I'm on a roll. [Leave.]
The dishevelled hair, cheap clothes, slumping posture that suggests an unearned sense of superiority...
Seems to be one of those conceptual types... not good. If we proceed cautiously we might get something tangible out of her.
Yes, this seems to be one of those *conceptual* types... not good. If we proceed cautiously we might get something tangible out of her.
Hints of deep emotional trauma that have led to ironic detachment...
It's all there if you know how to read people. Commanders of the streets like me have it down to a tee. I'll teach you. Listen up...
Alright, I'm listening. What's the plan?
I know how to handle this, no need to coach me. [Leave.]
A streak of individuality. As you wish...
There! On that balcony. Do you see it?
Cindy? Yes, that's where I'm headed...
See *what*? (Squint your eyes.)
Not now. I'm on a roll. [Leave.]
Straight into a bullring with no prep talk? No-no-no. It's your first sales negotiation, Savvy's gotta give you the do-s and don't-s.
The *artisto*. Now hold up, you can't go into a bullring without a prep talk. It's baby's first sales negotiation after all! Savvy's gotta give you the do-s and don't-s.
Oh no, not a *happening*!! I don't like the sound of that...
That's a pathetic-looking *bull*. Where are the sharpened horns ready to puncture your gristle? There's no real danger here.
Rehearsal helps fine tune a performance. Learn your lines so they can flow out of you like Herc Zeitung's legendary soliloquy in 'Hoppla, jetzt komm ich!'!
Alright, I'm listening.
Artistos are known to *repel* wealth. It bounces off their skin like rubber. The moment a reasonable business proposal enters their periphery, they go and get 'political'.
What you need to do is lure them in with a strong one-liner -- get them on your side before you've even finished a sentence. Show us what you've got -- pretend you're facing the SKULL-girl!
I've got this. Trust me. [Leave.]
A streak of individuality? As you wish...
It's true, some of them are known to turn the entire thing into a happening.
(Lean in.) Hey beautiful. Let's go for a walk on the *wild side*.
Hand over your art. Put it in the bag. NOW!!
Excuse me, could I please take a look at your art?
What is this, a dating agency? Are you looking for a Pretty Young Thing to sponsor? Never mix business and pleasure -- *never*.
It's your lucky day! I'm in the market for some original *art* by the crème de la crème.
Holy-moly, are we being arrested here?! Only tax inspectors and debt collectors speak like that. You don't want to start your business relationship with the wrong vibe.
Counterpoint! What if pleasure *is* your business? Gigolos make bank *and* get that wet-wet. It's never too late to change careers...
But it would catch her off-guard. That's *always* an advantage.
Boring... BORING... Yawning my jaw off here... Next!
Mamma mia, if this isn't the Top Seller in La Delta! Everyone knew you'd eventually get it right...
Hmm, it's a decent start, but you might need to change strategies down the line...
Okay then, off you go! Let's see what you've got.
Mamma mia, if this isn't the Top Seller in La Delta! No one expected you to nail this on the *first* try -- *congratulazioni*!
It's polite. What's wrong with being polite?
Nonsense, no one 'repels wealth', the businessmen just don't know how to entice them.
There! Right in front of you. Do you see it?
There! Right in front of you. Do you see it? It's an artist!
What you need to do is lure them in with a strong one-liner -- get them on your side before you've even finished a sentence. Show us what you've got -- pretend you're facing the girl!
(Whip out your finger pistols and bang them in the sky.) It's your lucky day! I'm in the market for some original *art* by the crème de la crème.

dialoguetext: "Joyce L. Messier. I represent the board of Wild Pines -- the owners of the harbour. You must be from the RCM..." She steps closer and holds out her hand over the railing.
Shake her hand.
Don't shake her hand.
"Joyce L? What does the 'L' stand for?"
"Leyton, my maiden name." Her bony hand dangles from the sleeve of her oversized raincoat.
"I'm glad to see you here." Her grip is tight and cold.
"I'm afraid my partner doesn't shake hands. Please don't take offence."
"I'm glad to see you here." The woman and the lieutenant exchange a brief handshake.
"None taken, officer." They exchange a brief handshake. "Either way, I'm glad you're both here now."
Like steel. There is strength there. If she wanted, she could sink her nails deep into your skin.
"I'm glad to see you here." She withdraws her small hand and picks up her cup.
She is unfazed by your rudeness, probably chocking it up to local custom.
"I was dispatched to handle a strike, not a lynching. Anything I can do to assist the RCM in this matter, I will, gladly."
"Thank you. That's all for now." [Leave.]
"Of course, detective -- take care."
"You're back. Good." She looks at the ripples on the water's surface. "What can I help you with -- not an umbrella, I hope. I don't need one myself, you see..." She pats her wet raincoat.
"What can you tell me about this lynching?"
"You seem smart, I need someone to give me a low-down on this... *reality* we're in."

dialoguetext: "You're on a boat."
"Joyce L. Messier. I represent the board of Wild Pines -- the owners of the harbour. You gentlemen must be from the RCM..." She steps closer and holds out her hand over the railing.
"What can you tell me about this strike?"
"What gave me away?"
"Nothing, honestly. I've said it to every drunk in town and you're the first one who's responded."
"Why, yes I am..." She looks at the deck under her feet. Green and white sails flutter overhead.
"Good afternoon, officer, I'm Joyce." She extends her hand in greeting.
"RCM -- what is that? I'm a little *foggy* here."
"Uhm..." She seems confused. "I meant *you* -- the Revachol Citizens Militia. The police."
She hasn't actually said it to every drunk in town. It was spoken in jest.
"The information I'm to share with you includes sensitive trade secrets. For the sake of my employer, I have to ask for your name and badge number."
"Of course, ma'am. We should have introduced ourselves..." The lieutenant hands her a piece of blue plastic. "I'm Lieutenant Kitsuragi, from Precinct 57..."
"And this is my colleague from Precinct 41." He points to you. "I'm afraid he doesn't have his badge at the moment. I hope mine will suffice."
"How curious." She returns the lieutenant's badge and turns to you. "Why is that, detective?"
"And this is my colleague from Precinct 41, Detective Du Bois." He points to you. "I'm afraid Harry doesn't have his badge at the moment. I hope mine will suffice."
"*Oh*. And what happened to yours, detective?" She returns the lieutenant's badge and turns to you.
Why should I blame it on an artist?
"Some artist types stole my badge. It was a mistake to trust them."
"Some damn *clown* stole it from me. It's a long story."
"You mean someone *stole* your badge?" Her brow is slightly arched.
"Not a lot of people on boats, are there?"
"Does she have a name?"
"Do you have a licence for this boat?"
"I think I have a handle on the boat thing." (Conclude.)
"Of course there are." She looks around. "We are on an archipelago. How else are you supposed to get around?"
"Wait, we're on an *archipelago*?" (Look around.)
"Uhm, Caillou? I thought we were in Revachol."
"Wait, I thought Le Calliou was one big island?"
"We are. And the city of Revachol is on the island of Le Caillou."

Technically, the neighbouring Ozonne and Face-à-La-Mer island groups are archipelagos, while Le Caillou, by contrast, is a single, fertile land mass, the fourth largest island in the world. It is not an archipelago.

"Okay." She gives you a crooked smile. "If you want to get technical. The point is we're *all* on islands here. And sail is still the most expedient way to get from one island to another. Especially when you're in a hurry to resolve a *strike*."
"Still. I haven't seen anyone else sail a boat around here."
"I haven't seen anyone else drive a souped-up Coupris Kineema motor carriage either."
"Actually," the lieutenant becomes defensive, "that motor carriage has been specially issued to serve as a patrol and *pursuit* vehicle."
"It's for crossing long distances in the Greater Revachol Industrial Harbour. It's not a toy."
"Neither is this." The woman pats the cabin hardtop. "A toy, I mean. It's a machine for crossing long distances in the bay of Revachol. Between the city and the islands."
"That's not mine. It belongs to my partner, Lieutenant Kitsuragi."
She's referring to Lieutenant Kitsuragi's motor carriage.
"No matter *whose* it is. A motor carriage is just a tool. You need it to do your job -- as I do mine. It's just a means of getting where you need to go."
"You lost me there -- I have no idea what a Coupris Kineema is."
"Pardon me, it's not especially relevant."
"There it is again -- the name of that infernal machine! I woke up to that sound, you know?"
"Hmm, I suppose that one *does* have a rather loud electrical engine." She does not quite understand what you meant. "A specific drone. In any case...."
"I drove my motor carriage into the sea, you know. It sank."
Let it be.
"In any case..." She takes a sip from her thermal cup.
"What a surprise," she says, not the least bit surprised. "That is one disadvantage of a motor carriage relative to a sloop like this one." The sloop bobs gently in the water.
"What do you mean -- archipelago?"
"Understood. About this boat of yours..." (Back off.)
"Of course. The situation is precarious."
"Good," she takes a sip of her thermal cup.
"I *mean* we are on Le Caillou, are we not?" She raises her brow.
"Yes, we are." She raises her brow. "We are on Le Caillou."
She nods attentively.
There is a pinch of *defensiveness* in her voice, but it is playful.
"Officer, I assure you I'm a highly qualified pleasure craft operator."
The crowns of her teeth are porcelain, white as the boat's hull as she smiles.
"I just renewed its safety inspection last month, officer. It is completely seaworthy. In fact, it's taken part in not one, but *two* Insulindic regattas, and finished once."
"Can I see your licence?"
"That's good enough for me."
"Actually, you don't."
"Still *need* to see a license, ma'am."
"I'm pretty sure I do. I police."
"What do you mean?"
"It is a little known fact among those who *police* that the Wayfarer Act specifically denies the RCM the authority to demand anyone's operator license."
"Wait, exactly how little known is this fact?"
"I was just being polite -- even schoolchildren know the Wayfarer Act."
"What happened the other time?"
"The other time I *would* have finished the race were it not for an urgent work matter, much like the one I'm on now."
"Makes sense, I guess. I mean, look at me!"
"So we *can't* pull over random civilians and demand their papers? That's weak."
"Unless it's their *passport*, no. Do you want to ask for the lady's passport?"
"No need to resort to self pity, detective. You can still ask for her passport."
"Why wouldn't it be? This is Revachol. Wayfarer act and all. *Anyone* can drive a boat."
"More like the Anarchy Act in my opinion."
"No need to politicize this. You may still ask for the lady's *passport*."
You need to save face if you want her respect. DEMAND that passport!
"Yes. I'm going to need to see your passport."
"No need."
The Wayfarer Act is one of the few pieces of legislation governing human interaction in the Revachol Zone of Control, along with the Emergency Trade and Aliments Acts.

It's one of the foundational laws in Revachol, designed to limit the authority of local institutions. Part of it prohibits the RCM from requesting most documents and licenses without permission from a Coalition representative...
The what now?
*Yawn*
The one time this busted up cabbage has something useful for your *job* you just want to stare at some boat. Fine. Knock yourself out.
It's a law that keeps Revachol what it is -- in limbo.
"The boat? No. *It* is called Cor-de-Leite '19 -- because that's the type of sloop it is."
"Of course." She searches the pockets of her raincoat, producing a bundle of documents in a sealed plastic bag.
She nods politely. "Of course. Any more questions about the boat, sir?"
The graciousness of her response makes you feel glad you didn't hassle her about her papers for no reason.
Look at her passport.
"Everything appears to be in order." (Give the documents back.)

The woman is silent, smiling while the waves lap against the hull. In your hand, under the plastic -- a light blue passport saying *REPUBLIC OF VESPER*. The coat of arms has a lion and an ostrich, sejant.
Look at the photo page.
The woman -- born in the year 3 in the Commune of Revachol -- smiles at you, face adorned with frown lines and crow's feet. The photo is recent. The name reads Rejoyce Leyton-Messier.
She nods and returns the plastic bag to her coat.
"You're from Vesper?"
"My husband is. I have dual citizenship. A Vespertine is handier when travelling."

The Republic of Vesper, formerly the Republic of Vesper-Messina, was once a dual kingdom. An amicable parting of ways produced two constitutional monarchies. Vesper, the richer of the two, is an Occidental nation known for its proximity to the pale and its exotic financial derivatives.
Anything else?

It is a stable country, and yet there has always been something *ominous* about its perfect stability, its place at the edge of the Mundi isola, overlooking the Ubi Sunt? isles fracturing into the Great Unrest of the pale.
"How about... Dolores."
"How do you like it?" (Conclude.)
The word *it* feels strange. Such a beautiful boat deserves a proper name...

A breeze ripples through the sails and tugs at your hair. Below, the sleek, fishlike shape of the hull parts the water. Beneath that -- a resounding darkness. You're reminded of something, or some*one*...
"Why *Dolores*?"
"I don't know... feels pretty."
"Hmm. Well, it means nothing to me. I think I'll stick with the factory name. But thank you for the suggestion."
"My sloop? I like it a lot." Her lips curl into a wry smile. "It's the *eel's hips*, baby."
"I'm enjoying this part of the interview -- it has *so* little to do with the murder we're investigating."
"Technically speaking, you *don't*."

"Okay. Tell me about this alleged drug trafficking."
"It's quite straightforward. Someone is using Terminal B to smuggle raw ingredients from the Samaran isola into Revachol with the Union's blessing. Wild Pines has suspected it for years."
Wait! She just admitted that the lynching and the strike are connected.
"So the strike is *connected* to the lynching?"
"Yes, I believe there is a connection -- but that's a subject for *later*." Her eyes narrow.
She is resolute in this, yet you sense that she *wants* to tell you. You'll have to earn her trust first.
"The money I owe is *so much* less than that."
"What kind of *ingredients* are we talking about here?"
"Ingredients for *what*, ma'am?"
"Meth- and dextro-amphetamine, GBL and various synthetic psychedelics. Honestly, it might be quicker to say what you *can't* make from the stuff."
"And you want us to investigate." (Move on.)
"Wild Pines seems to be *well apprised* of the local drug trade, ma'am. Do you mean to say the Union also *produces* the product? Sells drugs, I mean?"
"Yes. But you won't get anything out of Evrart and the Dockworkers' Union. Still --" she raises her bony finger, "every chain has its weak link."
The hand-off. The motor lorries at the roundabout.
"The lorries."

"The *lorries,*" she stresses. "Someone needs to move the ingredients from the harbour into the city. Once they reach Jamrock they're distributed to a network of local manufacturers, well beyond our grasp. But in transit they are *vulnerable*."

"*Precisely*. Someone needs to move the ingredients *from* the harbour into the city. Once they reach Jamrock they're distributed to a network of local manufacturers, well beyond our grasp. But in transit they are *vulnerable*."
How convenient that they're stranded like beached whales at that roundabout.
"Why didn't you come to the RCM earlier?"
"It's no coincidence the lorries are stranded there like that, is it?"
"What proof do you have that the Union is involved?"
"Actually, let's discuss something else for now."
Her irises are light green, like the River Esperance in bright daylight, upstream where it's clearer.
"I'll be explicit: if you find this driver, I will share company secrets with you."
"We *did*, on more than one occasion. Apparently there's some sort of inter-precinct disagreement about whose jurisdiction this area falls under."
"We know the company has launched its own probe into the Union's alleged involvement -- we also know it's come up empty. It's not just the RCM -- *no one's* been able to find any hard evidence."
"Well," she smiles and points toward the roundabout, "here's your chance, officers."
"No. We asked East Motor Tract to raise the drawbridge. The road company is a partner of one of our subsidiaries. However..." She pauses, looking to the sea.

"This is a limited-time opportunity. Once the complaint has been processed by the trade committee they'll have no choice but to lower the drawbridge -- and the operation will continue." She looks north.
"Thousands of litres of raw ingredients will pour onto the streets of Revachol. Not the East, across the river, but the West. The vulnerable, the weary..."
"How do you think they're financing this strike? There are thousands of unpaid dockworkers going strong for the fourth month straight."
"I've heard they shook down local business owners. Drove a few out of business to finance it."
"With all due respect to these desert cacti, the contents of a few cash registers cannot provide for *two-thousand* men. The local businesses can scarcely provide for themselves."
"There was a shakedown of local businesses preceding the strike. Many were squeezed to bankruptcy to fund it."

"It's true they drove a number of the local businesses to bankruptcy preparing for this venture. I've talked to a few business owners -- it was quite the shakedown. But the contents of a few cash registers cannot provide for *two thousand* men."
"So you think the strike is being funded with source ingredients for drugs?"
"Precisely. Smuggled out of that very gate at night, most likely. Then loaded onto lorries and driven to Jamrock. You simply need to find *one* driver who'll open up to you."
It sounds like she tried looking into it herself. But she's clearly not the type your typical lorryman would confide in.
It sounds like she tried looking into it herself, though she's clearly not the type your typical lorryman would confide in.

A cold breath rushes in from the bay, making its way down the alleyways and potholed streets -- from Martinaise to Jamrock. In the traffic you hear the clinking of glass vials, concealed beneath tarpaulin. Or is it just your teeth chattering in the cold?
(Shiver.) "Fucking misery."
"A lot of it," she nods. "It comes in from large Samaran factories. In South Safre, Siigay and Hsin-Yao. The literage they must get from this terminal alone must be *oceanic*."
"The lorries are still stuck at the roundabout -- if the police is asking, one of the drivers might admit to it."
She simply nods.
"I'll look into it, probe the drivers, see what it yields." (Accept.)
"We already have some suspicions that one of the drivers was present at the lynching."
"The two *might* even be connected."
"Or not -- though if you have evidence to the contrary I'm *eager* to hear it."
"As eager as I am to *share* it, lieutenant, once the job is done."
"There's no way I can take this case." (Refuse.)
"I am very sad to hear that, officer." Her voice is ice cold and laced with worry. "If you change your mind, please let me know. If not, good luck finding your badge -- and your memory."
"In the meantime, I'll still try to assist you any way I can. This disagreement is peanuts compared to what happens if you fail your main investigation."
"It may come to nothing, or it may just blow the case wide open. I can keep the drawbridge up for a few more days at least. You should have the time you need."
"In the meantime, let me know if there's any other way I may be of assistance." She takes another long sip from her seemingly bottomless thermal cup.
A waft of flowers and caramel reaches you where you're standing.
"Until you come up with something at that intersection I'm afraid I have little else to tell you -- but I'll try. Ask."
"I spoke with the lorrymen at the roundabout."

"On the contrary, officer," she smiles. "There are yet camionneurs you have not talked to. And don't look so surprised. In a time like this it would be strange if Wild Pines *didn't* have eyes on the harbour."
"Word has travelled, yes, but nothing of real substance has surfaced yet, I gather?" She smiles, then explains: "Wild Pines has eyes on the intersection -- but not ears."
One of the tall buildings overlooking the roundabout -- it would give them a read on the entire quarter.
They must have someone in an overlook position, near the gates...
"It appears we're being monitored every step we take, colleague." The lieutenant shrugs. "Did we have any other business here?"
"Yes, my eyes on the harbour have sent word to that effect -- what have you discovered?"
"In any case, it's a relief to know someone has looked into it. If I may ask -- will there be an official investigation? I assume you discovered there *is* an operation..."
"Wait, where exactly are these *eyes* located?"
"We have discovered enough to conclude -- for now."
"It doesn't really matter -- and I do apologize for the surveillance. Wild Pines can't afford to be blind at a time like this."
"Yes -- and? Will you start an official investigation?"
She's trying to conceal her excitement, but the slight glimmer in her green eyes tells you otherwise.
"Hold on, you seem anxious to know. Why's that?"
"I've kept my eye on the camionneurs -- even tried to get to know one. It's a *mystery* I'm already invested in: which one of them, if any, could organize such a complex operation?"
"There will be an investigation, that's all I can say."
"You sent us on a wild goose chase. There's nothing to investigate."
"*If* there is an investigation it will be part of an ongoing operation -- subject to confidentiality. I am sure you understand."
"Of course, detectives," she says, her tone more cautious suddenly. "In any case, you've held up your end of our arrangement. I trust you with the rest. Now it's my turn..."
"I wouldn't normally break protocol like this, but the situation demands it. If you don't solve this murder I'm afraid we may have a blood bath on our hands."
"I don't believe that for one moment, officer." There is a pause, then her stern expression clears. "I'm just going to assume that departmental regulations prevent you from saying anything more..."
"In any case, you've held up your end of our arrangement. Now it's my turn..."
"Okay. I thank you for sharing that much with me." She exhales, as though a weight has been lifted from her shoulders. "My employer thanks you as well..."
The lieutenant is about to interject. Cut him off. This decision should be yours.
Yes -- I should decide.
Let the lieutenant handle it.
Exactly -- but what?
"The scabs at the gate -- did you put them there?"

dialoguetext: "The... *scabs*?" She raises her brow. "You mean the huddled masses of Jamrock, come to plead for work where the Union refuses to?"
Don't let her answer it herself.
"If they were organized by Wild Pines or its affiliates then it would be a company secret. I could not share it with you -- not right now at least..."
"No, I mean scabs."
"Let's call them strikebreakers -- you put them there, right?"
"You're right, I don't know what got into me. Some of that degenerate dock worker lingo has rubbed off, it seems."
Let her continue.
It's implied she's open to discussing this matter with you at a later occasion.
"Yes. They were organized by Wild Pines. The contractors picked them up from Jamrock and drove them over. This is standard practice. The company reserves a right to man its stations."
"If these *workers* were organized by Wild Pines or its affiliates, then it would be a company secret. I could not share it with you -- not yet, at least."
"If these *strikebreakers* were organized by Wild Pines or its affiliates, then it would be a company secret. I could not share it with you -- not yet, at least."
"Ha!" She gives you a crooked smile. "If the workers were organized by Wild Pines then it would be a company secret. I could not share it with you  -- not yet, at least..."

"To answer your question -- yes. They were organized by Wild Pines. The contractors picked them up from Jamrock and drove them over. This is standard practice. The company reserves a right to man its stations."
"I have a photo of the victim's tattoos." (Show it to her.)
"Do you know something about these tattoos?" (Show her the photo.)
"Of course," her back straightens. "Anything to help."
"That's the man who was killed..." She almost takes the photo -- but then stops. "I'm afraid this is a discussion for once we've cleared the lynching question."
"Better not to tie the forestay to the backstay on this. I hope there is something else I can help you with?"
"Fine, let's return to it later."
"Why? How is you looking at the photo tied to the lynching?"
"So you know something about the tattoos?"
She *wants* to answer the question. Protocol keeps her from it.
"I fear I've told you all I know." She takes the photo. "It's an Oranjese Map of the Waterways -- or some version of it. It depicts the travels this man made while he was still alive."
"Your name is Rejoyce?"
"Yes -- but please don't call me that."
"Why?"
"*Joyce* is much more efficient."
...is what you *want* to say. But it isn't that easy, is it?
What, why not?
"YOU SEEM RICH. CAN I HAVE SOME MONEY?"
Look at that lady. Take a *gander*. Squint your eyes, bub.
Why yes! Tucked away under that sturdy green raincoat, almost rustic in its simplicity -- a silk shirt and matching scarf around her gentle throat...
These are the kind eyes of the rich-man, that seem to say: everything is possible...
You're thinking it, but your lips are not moving.
What nice fabrics.
What lustrous hair.
While dull orange pearls hang from her ear lobes, red from cold. Her light green eyes scan you, full of knowledge -- and worry. Wealth and all its possibilities.
A well-kempt, yet tastefully short bob of dark hair. Despite the first hints of grey, she's elected to keep it au naturale -- shaped into a permanent wave, late-Forties style...
Positively statuesque.
A breeze carries with it the faint scent of juniper and oranges.
...within reason.
Yeah, so?

Now look at you, you misery-clad simian, barely able to tie your own laces. Your armpits are lakes, a scythe of booze precedes you. Your hair sticks to your forehead and your underwear feels uncomfortable...
You're poor. Poor as balls. You can't ask this person for money. You're too...
What is this feeling? I've never felt it before.

Shame? You haven't really been in the presence of gentlefolk either, have you? What shame is there to be felt in front of these... dockworkers, cops and hotel clerks. But to *belittle* yourself in these eyes of Eau-de-Nil...

"As I was saying..." Her voice breaks the silence and suddenly you're back again. Nearby, a seagull pecks at a piece of garbage... "If there's *any* way I may be of assistance, please don't hesitate to ask."
I'm a god damn working man, I'm not *ashamed* to shake this leech for some dough.
As I should be -- for even considering it. This is a woman and I'm a *man*.
Yes. I should make my own god damn money by now.
Say it: "Can I have some money?"
You think your little *communism" protects you from this feeling? No. The more *demeaning* it is to grovel at her feet...
Yes. You should be able to take care of yourself. Not grovel at her beautiful feet, dishonouring yourself and your organization with this request...
Maybe you can ask her for some *stock tips* -- that's a *maybe*. Or a *job*. But you're sure as hell too ashamed to ask for cash buddy.
Oh god, the lieutenant is here too! Do not DISHONOUR the force!
I am sorry. It just doesn't come out of your mouth. What does is:
"Khnnnnnnnffff..."
"Money..."
"Excuse me, I didn't hear you." Her voice is kind, a little hoarse from the wind.
"Excuse me, I didn't hear you." her voice is kind, a little hoarse from the wind. "Did you say *money*?"
Surprisingly eloquent, really. The last one, not the first three -- those are ape-speak.
"I am the scum of the earth."
"My...." She doesn't know what to say: "Why do you say that?"
"I'm gunk."
"No, I didn't. Let's talk about something else."
"Of course." She makes a slight bowing motion.
She understands what you're trying to do -- ask for money. But shame is contagious and she doesn't want to offend you by saying it out loud.
"That's garbage! You're a police officer."
"No I'm not. I'm gunk."
"I'm the stuff people have under their fingernails. Let's talk about something else please."
"Shall we talk about something else maybe?" Her voice is kind, if anything she sounds a little confused.
What you meant to say was:
What is this? An athletic challenge? Scream it from the top of your lungs immediately, show that asshole!
Voila, you're doing it!
"You seem rich. Can I have some money?"
"Can I have some money, ma'am?"
"Help me, I'm poor. I need money to keep living."
"Why yes, I am rich. How much money do you need? Hopefully not too much, I couldn't bring all of it with me."
"I need a *billion* reál."
"I need 10,000 reál."
"I need 60 reál."
She's surprisingly nonchalant about this. If anything, your finally asking it has relieved some of the tension.
She's surprisingly nonchalant about this. Could it be that she somehow knows more about your predicament than she's letting on?
"Of course." She nods, she doesn't even smile. "How much do you need."
"Ah yes, of course, I'm sad to hear that." She nods, as if its self explanatory. "How much do you need?"
"MONEY!!!"
Really put your back into it. Yell it from the top of your lungs!
"I'm sorry, I couldn't hear you," she chuckles to herself. "The wind is a bit strong, could you repeat that?"
"I NEED MONEY!!!"
"HOW MUCH MONEY?!"
"I need 30 reál."
"I need 70 reál."
"I need 100 reál."
"I need 130 reál."
"Excuse me sir, I don't have a billion reál."
"Come now. Nobody carries that much cash on their person, particularly in a place like Martinaise... I'd get robbed."
"What? I thought you said you had like twenty billion or something."
"Oops, I must have misheard."
"That was the annual revenue of the *entire* Wild Pines Group, not my personal fortune..."
"Try again, dear. A little lower this time."
Her tone makes clear that you've violated some kind of rich-person taboo. Wouldn't be the first time.
"Hi-fi? I like high fidelity disco music too."
"Hydrodynamique E40? Sounds fast."
"It is. Fast and silent." She gives you a crooked little smile. "Try again, but lower."
"I like high fidelity *anything*, sir." She gives you a fast little smile. "Now try again, but lower."
"I need 1 reál."
"No, you don't. One reál won't get you two pieces of bath tissue to rub together."
"I would like 0.1 cents."
"So would I -- but woe! There is no such denomination."
"Ideas like this one are all part of his rare medical condition, ma'am. Nothing to be worried about."
"That's a reasonable sum -- not too small, not fantastically large." She reaches into her raincoat and pulls out a zip bag -- in it you see paper notes arranged like black gills.
She removes a few notes and hands them to you. The paper is cold and oily to the touch.
There must be about 200 reál in that zip bag. Maybe a little less. Plus some change at the bottom.
Whoa, whoa. Did you see how easy that was? Ask her for more! *Toot-toot* Train to moneytown!
"Can I have some more?"
Nay, 'twould be dishonourable, and mine honour is my life.
Can you eat honour? Are you an *honour-vore?* Give me a break...
"Uhm..." The woman dips her fingers back into the bag. "I really did bring as little cash as possible, to avoid attention. So here you are, the last of bit of filthy *lucre* I can share."
"This may seem like *odd* behaviour for a police officer, ma'am, but it's a perfectly common side effect of his..." He squints at you.
"... unusual medical episode."

"It's all right, lieutenant." The woman dips her fingers back into the bag. "I really did bring as little cash with me as possible, to avoid attention. So here you are -- the last bit of filthy *lucre* I can share."
"So," she returns the zip bag to her jacket. "I hope I didn't just *bribe* you, officer. It may not be technically *illegal* under the Emergency Act, but still..."
"So," she returns the zip bag to her jacket. "I hope I didn't just *bribe* you, officer. It may not be technically *illegal* under the Emergency Act, but still..."
"And even *if* I did I still would not give you ten thousand reál. I would rather buy something nice with it. Like expensive hi-fi or a new *Hydrodynamique E40* sail."
She removes a few notes and hands them to you. The paper is cold and oily to the touch.
"That's a good sum -- not too small, not fantastically large." She reaches into her raincoat and pulls out a zip bag -- in it you see paper notes arranged like black gills.
She removes a few notes and hands them to you. The paper is cold and oily to the touch.

"That's a good sum -- not too small, not fantastically large." She reaches into her raincoat and pulls out a zip bag -- in it you see paper notes arranged like black gills.
"You bribed me all right. I'm your little *peone* now."
"Certainly not. I am an *honourable* policeman."
"Funny that your worried about this and not your ruthless exploitation of the entire *human race*."
You illustrate the expression by holding an imaginary-- and very, very tiny-- *peone* between your thumb and index finger.
"I'm still getting my head around this whole *money* concept. You were just helping me out."
"You're right, ma'am, that donations are permitted under the Emergency Act, unseemly as it may be, as long as they're properly logged with the precinct..."
"Which he most certainly will do." She bows, and then raises a single eyebrow in your direction: "Now, how else can I help the RCM today, besides supplementing its salaries?"
"I want to talk about something else now."
"That's heartening to hear. There are too few honourable men in Revachol." She gives you a slight bow. "Now how else can I help the RCM today, besides supplementing its salaries?"
"Au contraire, officer. I also feel queasy about the pittance the Coalition calls your salary. Now is there something else I can do for you, or did you want to chat about *dialectics* some more?"
"It's quite the *phainómenon*, I agree." She bows slightly. "Now how else can I help the RCM today, besides supplementing its salaries?"
"Of course." She bows slightly. "Now how else can I help the RCM today, besides supplementing its salaries?"
She laughs out loud. It is a beautiful laugh, laced with glee and a certain sharpness. It travels far on the water...
She clears her throat. "Now, how else can I help the RCM today, besides supplementing its salaries?"
"What would you like to know?" She taps her foot on the deck.
"The *performative experience* has ended. Good -- what can I help you with?"
"I've got some more questions about *reality*."
"More lessons in basic reality?" She's positively surprised. "My favourite part of the day! Go ahead, ask me anything."
"Well, technically speaking I'm not *on* it right now..." She looks at the sloop sway in the waves.
"By the way, I've talked to Evrart Claire."
(Show her your badge.) "I found my badge, by the way."

dialoguetext: Fast, observantly. Like an electronic printer.
"By love, you did!" She inspects the piece of blue plastic, her eyes scanning from left to right.
She hands it back to you. "Pleased to meet you, Lieutenant Double-Yefreitor Du Bois. I am glad to see a man of high qualification -- the situation is precarious."
She is memorizing your badge number.
Seaweed drips from the badge in your hand. It smells of fish. "What can I help you with, lieutenant-yefreitor?"
"Good morning, officer. I'm Joyce." She extends her hand in greeting.
"Good evening, officer, I'm Joyce." She extends her hand in greeting.
"The people who live there now lead a different *lifestyle* if you know what I mean."
"It seems the architect of the operation has gone missing. An abandoned lorry is near the statue."
"Ah, good to hear. I wouldn't want to pry into a confidential police matter. But, in the event you'd like to share more... I *would* like to know who it was."
"I came upon a few hidden maps illustrating the range of the smuggling network."
"We turned up quite a few *interesting* things actually..." (Share information.)
"I found research about something called *ULAN* frequencies related to the operation."
"I saw a really advanced radio system with *a lot* of stations saved."
"It's possible there's even a connection to La Puta Madre."
"What is La Puta Madre?"
"A seriously bad guy."
"No, he's not. Our friend here has quite the sense of humour, part of his technique, you see?"
"A seriously bad guy. I might even be on his take!"
"Nevertheless, he sounds *terribly* dangerous. I urge you to take care, officer. I wouldn't want anything to happen to you."
"She's a fan of vintage movie stars. The inside of the cab was plastered with posters."
"High intensity microwave frequencies? They're used for navigational purposes, to compress the interisolary space. They may use it to communicate with incoming freighters..."
"It didn't have Speedfreaks FM."
The lieutenant's stone-like face remains impassive, yet in his eyes -- a flash of reproach.
"What is... speedfreaks FM?" She looks at you quizzically.
"It's Lieutenant Kitsuragi's favourite radio station!"
"A very loud radio station about motor carriages and rock music, I think."
Yes. *All* ears. That's how she operates.
"A runaway? Good work, this is a tangible lead towards solving the whole mystery."
"That speaks of the vastness and sophistication of the operation. Were you able to examine the radio?"
"We contain multitudes, do we not? It might not be pertinent to her... *profession*, but who knows? It may help you find her yet."
"Well, he sounds *very* dangerous. I urge you to take care, officer. I wouldn't want anything to happen to you. Not with what's coming..."
"I've told you what I've found, now it's your turn." (Conclude.)
"I appreciate you placing your trust in me. Thank you again for looking into this matter. You have my gratitude -- and the gratitude of Wild Pines Group..."
"It was the nerve-center for the operation. She could contact a whole fleet of lorries."
"I... fail to see the relevance of this station, but..." she smiles warmly, "I'll defer to your judgement. Was there anything else?"
"Taking it out of commission will deal a blow to the smuggling network. Excellent work."
"Unfortunately the dial knob was missing, the radio itself was inoperative."
She nods. "Sensible for her to disable access to such essential information."
"A first-rate find -- that should tell you all you need to know about their network, I would imagine."
"Now's neither the time nor the place to discuss such matters. What else did your investigation turn up?"
"Yes. They're spread all over Jamrock... and beyond. I couldn't even identify the exact end points."
"It's an octopus whose tentacles reach every corner of the city."
"An ominous vision..." She nods solemnly. "At least you understand the gravity of the situation. And the maps should prove very valuable indeed."
"So this goes *beyond* Jamrock... she looks inland. "At least you now understand the gravity of the situation. And those maps should prove very valuable indeed."
"Okay. I've made up my mind about the smuggling investigation..." (Proceed.)
"Yes?"
"The Union won *significant* concessions -- including overtime pay *and* a medical plan. This time their demands are more... I guess you could say *aggressive*."
She continues: "The literage the local producers must get from this terminal alone must be *oceanic*."
"That's not really my area. I just want to get to the bottom of this."
"Well," she smiles and points toward the roundabout, "here's your chance."
"The company has tried looking into the matter before -- to no avail. Perhaps someone with *your* authority and resources might turn over the right stones?"
"Huh, interesting. I had another question..."
"About the boat?" A wisp of steam rises from her thermal cup.
"Okay, forget the stupid Wayfarer Act. I had another question..." (Back off.)
"About the boat?" A wisp of steam rises from her thermal cup.
"Now they won't even let me into the harbour. There's a 2.20 m racist behemoth blocking the gates."
"What happened to this... Gaumont?"
"*EVERY WORKER -- A MEMBER OF THE BOARD!*"
"Mr. Claire told him to, how did he put it?" She pauses to compose herself...
"'Fuck off, midget.' Gaumont is short of stature, you see."
"Hmh. Okay then."
"And *now* people are getting *lynched*, I hear. Behind the Whirling-in-Rags... a disastrous situation if there ever was one."
"You know..." she puts her foot on the guardwire. "I don't mean to sound cold, but if you want something, you have to give something back. *More* than just guilt."
"I could've eaten it for all I know. I don't remember anything. This world, this city. Nothing."
"We're in logistics. It's our business to know -- and no. As far as the company knows, the Union does not produce it. They transport the ingredients. For a cut."
"Am I going to need bolt cutters for this?"
"What do you mean?"

"Unlikely, officer. I'm talking about the lorries. Once the ingredients reach Jamrock they're distributed to a network of local manufacturers, well beyond our grasp. But in transit they may be *vulnerable*."

"Perhaps you've noticed that a number of lorries are tangled in a traffic jam at the roundabout just now? Interview the drivers who are still hanging about. One of them might be waiting for a *crucial* shipment." She gives you a knowing look.
Shit yeah, baby, it's the Party Pipeline! Why would you want to shut that down?
"Why are you trying to shut down the Party Pipeline?"
"I assure you, officer, these are *not* the sort of parties you'd want to attend."
"Excellent." She takes a long sip of tea. "According to my reports there are at least three lorry drivers lingering near the roundabout. Hopefully one of them will know something."
"I suggest you go back and canvas for more suspects."
The lieutenant clears his throat audibly.
"Now, per our original agreement, it's time for me to share company secrets with you." There's a change in her demeanour. A caution comes over her. A tension.
"No matter, detective. We're losing the thread again."
She has no *idea* what kind of parties you've been to.
"How about the *Sleek Fish*."
"What?"
"Because it's sleek... and fish-like."
"Cool, but your boat really needs a name."
"The *Ex-Wife*."
"Thank you for the suggestion. I see the word has emotional resonance for you. For me, sadly -- none. So I will stick with the factory name."
"Okay. How about Cor-de-Leite '19. Why?" She taps on the side of the boat, it makes a hollow sound....
"How about the *Ex-* something."

She makes a point of being unromantic about it.

"This case is what I will be *known* by!"

Shake it off.
Ashamed?
I'm not ashamed!
Yes. You're too ashamed to ask this person for *money*, too scared to belittle yourself in her eyes -- those half-precious stones of Eau-de-Nil.
Oh, but you are: too ashamed to ask this person for *money*, too scared to belittle yourself in her eyes -- those half-precious stones of Eau-de-Nil.
"It's a she, by the way."
"Clever. Few suspect a woman in this sort of skulduggery. Good move on their part."
As the shipments approach Revachol? Hmm... somehow you suspect something more *sinister*.
*Qualified pleasure craft operator*... so charming. Where's the damn licence?
"His medical condition makes him a little *grumpy*, ma'am. I hope that's not a problem."
"Oh no -- not a problem at all."
It truly isn't. She controls herself very well.

"I don't seem to have my badge, actually..."
"I don't seem to have my badge, actually..."

Her nonchalance *might* be related to something called the Wayfarer Act -- a law that says she doesn't *need* a licence. Sly fox... you're not aggressive enough to harass her further on this.
"*Not* cool."

"Not *hard communist* enough for me."

"He can't be that bad."
"Uhm... yes."

"Let me get this straight -- the materials come from Samara to Revachol *through* the terminal?"
"Well -- at least this solves *one* mystery."

"I am sorry for the inconvenience, Lieutenant Kitsuragi. But we need them trapped here. This is a unique opportunity. I'm sure you understand."

... they're profiting from this trade.

"Okay then."

This one's a slippery eel.

All around you, rain keeps falling down. On the wooden boards she's standing on, and on the water around you...
One of the tall buildings overlooking the roundabout, most likely. That would give them a read on the entire quarter.

"But boring. You're not using my lovely brush to spread boredom."
"Oh, but I'm all out of fuel oil."
"You're a real sad sack, you know that? Go ahead, then." She drops the paintbrush at your feet. "Art it up. Just try not to hurt yourself. And *no self portraits*."
"You're a real sad sack, you know that? Go ahead, then." She drops her paintbrush into the puddle below. "Art it up. Just try not to hurt yourself. And *no self portraits*."
"Stop quivering like jello, then you won't get fucked."
She looks you up and down. "I think everyone would rather you didn't."
"There, there, piggy," she says in mock compassion. "I guess art just isn't really *you*. Cause you suck. In life. And in everything."
"Then you have time to find your own *fucking* brush."
"Sounds like you're just about to live out your self pity, not make a statement. I can't have shit art on my conscience."
"But I thought you'd like my idea!"
"What's your problem?"
"I'm sorry, was the image offensive? Did you survive an avian attack as a child?"
"But, Cindy, art is bigger than either of us."
"That's not fair!"
"Then get your brush from fucking *art*."
"Such is the bloody law of the bloody streets, you wankstain."
"I didn't realize you were so petty and insecure."
"Insult me all you want. You're still an art cop sans art materials."
"Didn't we all?"
You know what you've got in that fuel canister you scavenged from your Kineema? Red-dyed heavy fuel oil. Paint and a brush -- you're ready to do this.
You know what you should be able to find in your government-issued vehicle? Red-dyed heavy fuel oil.
"The streets will not flow red with anything. Who are you?"
"What's your name, miss? You seem to be engaged in an illegal activity."
[Leave.]
"Hep. Yeah, when were you last tested?"
"Had a battery of tests just last week. I'm practically a patchwork of interesting critters. Kind of like a man o' war." Despite the attitude, she puts the brush aside.
She's grown frustrated with her work and welcomes the opportunity to challenge authority in other ways.
"That's right. We've evolved."
"I don't have time for this." [Leave.]
"We cops don't *like* closed doors or unreachable perches. Or people having high ground on us."
"You're in trouble now, little lady!"
"Yes, Uncle Maynard. *Huge* trouble." She crosses her arms. "You're going to take out your metal detector and your collection of bottle caps and shrapnel."
"Yeah, I can see that. Cool mutations." She crosses her arms.
"Yeah, you got me now. The dynamic between us has completely changed." She crosses her arms.
"The streets will flow red once more. A great torrent, rushing down Rue d'Esperance. You wait and see." The girl stares at the sailboat by the pier.
"The streets will flow red once more. A great torrent, rushing down Rue d'Esperance. You wait and see." The girl stares at the sailboat by the pier.
"Is that bed in the coal room yours?"
"Ooh. Not only have you found my address, you've discovered my biggest secret: I'm a coal miner."
"I found some drugs in the coal room. Yours?"
"They just might be. Rough stuff. If you take the ride, you'd be wise to buckle your little pig-belly up."
Her neurons must be on fire, the heat creating waves and ripples in all she sees -- above all, in her painting.
"Does it make you see everything all... art-like?"
"I like bumpy rides. Know where I can get more?"
"I'm gonna have to take you in, kid. For possession of drugs."
"You really think I need to be high to see the world as art? Poor unimaginative piggy. How I wouldn't want to have *your* peepers."
"We apologize, but we're currently *not buying the entrapment you're selling*. Please call again later. Thank you." She smiles at her own joke.
"In which case, they are not mine, and I have several witnesses who will corroborate my statement."
This battle is not going to be worth your while. Let little miss sass here be.
"Really? You're a miner?"
"Don't you have a real home?"
"It's not the nicest place, but I guess it'll have to do."
"Yes. I keep hoping a shaft will collapse on me, but somehow it never happens."
"Does anyone, in a city like this?" she replies wistfully, looking around.
"It doesn't *have to* do anything at all. Nothing does." She looks at the paint dripping down the wall. "Like me. Right now, I'm doing nothing at all."
If there's pain about any particular home she's lost, she's buried it deep, fortified herself against it.
"Cool. I have other questions." (Conclude.)
"Shoot, piggy. It's what you do, isn't?"
To hell with the art part, man. It's all about the high anyway.
"Sure, any time. Us *shit* artists have to help one another." She looks down at the wall and frowns. "Besides, I was out of fuel oil anyway."
"I'm sorry, but I'm going to have to ask you again: Give me the brush, please."
You know what you've got in that fuel canister you scavenged from your Kineema? Red-dyed heavy fuel oil. Time to get to *proper* work, artiste.
Oops, my apologies. I guess I was trying too hard...
You're a police officer and a *grown up*. Why are you trying to impress her? Maybe try a different approach?
You're a police officer and a *grown up*. Why are you trying to impress her? Maybe try a different approach? Like climbing up there...
"So you won't talk about the murder -- but maybe you can tell me something about the murder victim's missing armour?"

dialoguetext: "What do I care about some fucking tin egg shells?"
"C'mon Cindy, just help me out here."
"You might find armour useful if the streets flow red once more."
"Ugh, alright, sad piggy. I'll give you this one -- I saw a little girl in the fishing village running around with military-grade hand-wear. Looked cute as hell."
"Could've been her. Small kid with giant white armoured hands. If you've seen one of them you've seen them all."
Could that girl have been Little Lily? It's not a bad place to start.
"I know a little girl in the village -- Little Lily."
"Isn't armour... art? Art for the, uhm, body?"
"If you haven't been there, the village is a shithole down the coast from the main plaza." She waves her hand in a general westward direction. "Have a good time."
There weren't any other small girls in the village.
She squints her eyes...
Her lips move. "On fire?" she whispers to herself.
"Do you have any idea what happened to the hanged man's armour?"
"Wait -- don't you wanna know how I knew to ask you?"
"Not particularly." Her eyes dart across the horizon. "I wanna keep this as brief as possible, you see. I want to return to painting the world *red*."
"Piss and Fuck told me."
"Okay, so tell me what you know then."
"I think you didn't hear me. Why would I care?"
"Fine. I don't care about those wannabe-SKULLS -- and I don't care about your armour."
"I have an opinion on this -- wanna hear it?" (Proceed.)
"Yeah?"
"Actually I don't have an opinion. I lied."
"Lying is cool, I guess." She absent-mindedly paints a red streak on her left cheek.
"Ugh, alright, piggy. I'll give you this one. I saw a little girl in the fishing village running around with military-grade hand-wear. Looked cute as hell."
This is the Cindy that misters 'Piss' and 'Fuck' said had the armoured gloves. Play it cool now...
Something about skulls, gloves... what was it? Maybe it'll come to you later.
A brush -- an artist? The red splatter is... urban expressionism?
The woman on the boat does not notice her staring.
She means the opposite.
You've *lessened* her desire to deface the building.
I don't condone the idea of using physical force on her. She's a *girl*.
The wannabe-SKULLS are dear to her. The armour less so.
She doesn't want to sound surprised at anything you say.
"And there's a little girl wearing the gloves there?"
"Got it."
"Piggy, I have no idea why I just told you that..." She looks at you, a little sad suddenly. "You look like a shaggy dog left in the rain for too long. I have a weakness for animals."
"I have a weakness for animals. It's the animal-thing again. Damn it." She looks at you, a little sad suddenly.
"No-no. That's all the snitching Cindy the SKULL does for today. Actually, I don't even know why I told you what I just told you..."
"Or a weakness for police officers, miss." He makes a note in his notebook. "Thank you either way."
She wants it to be something true -- and *total*.
Better not to.
She'd never admit to it anyway.
In this vision of hers, you are mutually opportunistic organisms. Growing like mould on the streets.
What is it with these SKULLS and *cooperation*? They have to be the nicest violent street gang in Revachol West.
She's probably not a good example of the gang either. *Or* maybe these SKULLS are more of an art movement than a gang.
"Got it. Enough of that then."
"Thank you for passing on the message -- now run along, piggy."
She did it herself. Pumped it out. She's proud of it, too.
She really did it. She's proud of it, too.
She *does* have eyes that seem to be smeared with coal.
The inspiration will come to her once *hell* is set loose on the streets. It's too calm right now.
"If you're *really* interested then I'm sorry," she whispers, "but I don't do anti-radiation drugs anymore so I don't know where to get them."
"Where did you get these then?"
"From a guy on Boogie Street. Porta Rosa. Go there after midnight and you can get all kinds of funny things. Veterans of the People's Pile selling their stash."
She immediately regrets telling you -- but it's too late.
Damn me and my affinity to farm animals, she's probably thinking. She hopes the information is useless.
Man, that's lame...
No-no. It's great.
But that would mean he *doesn't* say every pathetic thing that pops in his head.
She only gave it to you because she doesn't see you as competition.
The right idea is not coming to her. It's excruciating.
Damn, it was too strong.
"*Grand* art. Art DeLuxe. The artsy-est, the most ground breaking, the..."
"Let me stop you right there, piggy," she interjects, raising her hand. "You have no idea, do you? No idea -- no brush. Fuck off."
"You'll see. You will *all* see and tremble."
"Yeah... Not gonna hold my breath, piggy. You look like you'd suck. At... everything really," she quickly adds.
"Cool. No brush then. Not a problem."
"You're about to cry internally, aren't you piggy?" She utters a disapproving grunt. "Pathetic. Just give up, art isn't for you."
(Attempt to establish contact.) "Hey, sister. Let's talk *politics* for a minute."
"And what do *you* know about politics?" She squints at you suspiciously.
"I'm looking for comrades to help me fire up the Great Mazovian Sausage Grinder. Will you help me?"
"One of the Union guys said there's someone trying to organize an *underground revolutionary cell*."
"My nose told me that you're also a communist. We should team up, join forces."
"I'm searching for a bunch of *mole people*."
"An *underground cell*? My, my. Sounds big time..."
"Well, well. Sounds like quite the snout you've got there..."
"Pigs and moles, eh? Sounds like something out of a children's fairy story."
The girl erupts in a cackle that seems like it should belong to a much older woman...
"Oh, that's very nice. The little piggy wants to make sausages. Out of what, his little piggy friends?"
(Turn to Kim.) "Don't worry, Kim. I would never make you into a sausage."
"That's what we need to talk about. I don't *know* who I'm supposed to be making sausages out of!"
"No, out of the bourgeoisie."
"That's right. I'm gonna make juicy sausage links out of the entire 41st Precinct."
For the briefest instant, the lieutenant's hand hesitates above the notebook he's scribbling in.
"Wow. There's a proper *radical* piggy."

In the break room of Precinct 41, Sergeant Mack Torson is just now warming a grey sausage over an electric range. The oil in the pan hisses and pops. Torson is dabbing a spot off his pants when his partner, Satellite-Officer Chester McLaine enters, sniffs the air, and frowns...
"It was not a concern of mine." The lieutenant blinks once.
Your olfactory department wants you to know that it accepts no responsibility for wherever this line of interrogation leads you.
"Sure. I know someone who'd love to talk that ideological stuff. You're looking for Steban."
"So the little piggy is a big, bad communist now..."
"How sad. This little piggy doesn't know very much, does he?"
"It's not. It's very serious."
"I guess it does sound a little childish when you say it like that."
"Oh, did I hurt the very serious pig's feelings?"
"Yes, it really does..."
"Whatever. I know someone who's into some pretty underground stuff. You're looking for Steban."
"Who's Steban?"
"A right communist. Who runs a *mega cool* and *very secret* meeting."
"Does this 'Steban' happen to go around in a white jacket?"
"Do you know where to find him?"
"He might."
"I might."
"Will you help me find him?"
"Will you tell me?"
She pretends to think about it for a moment. "No."
The lieutenant lets slip a sigh that seems to suggest this turn was utterly predictable.
"Come on, Cindy. From one communist to another, help me out."
"Is it money you want? Here, take some. I've got plenty." (Offer her 5 reál.)
"I guess I should just give up, then. Nothing *ever* works out for me."
"Just tell me what you want me to do!"
"Keep your money. What I want from you's better than gold..."
"Oh, fine, I'll help. But first, I want something from *you*..."
"God, if he isn't the saddest pig in the world..."
A wicked grin extends across her face.
She's got you by the balls, chief. And she intends to squeeze them.
Don't look so deflated. Whatever she asks, you keep your chin up!

Incidentally, 'The Saddest Pig in the World' is the title of a popular Gottwaldian children's book, written and illustrated by Moritz Metzger. In '26 it received the prestigious *Kritikerpreis* for youth literature.
A laughing skull. Death hilarious. This is gonna be baaaad...
"What's that?"
"Oink for me, piggy. Just once."
"I'm not oinking for you."
"Come on, this is no way to treat your revolutionary brother!"
(With gusto.) "Oink, oink!"
(Reluctantly.) "Oink, oink."
(Through gritted teeth.) "Oink."
"Be a good pig, now. No oink, no goods."
"Wrong. This is exactly how I treat my little brother."
"Wow. That was easier than I expected. It's almost like you've been *wanting* to do it this whole time..."
"There, that wasn't so bad, was it?"
"Well, well. Seems like we're dealing with one tough pig. I'm impressed..."
A cool, damp feeling ripples through you. You realise you needn't have rolled over quite so easily.
It's not the worst indignity you've suffered the last several days, but it is up there.
Yes, somehow you managed to oink with at least a modicum of dignity.
The lieutenant, needless to say, is not impressed.
"Sounds like you're really serious about meeting Steban. It's touching, sort of."
"Steban's group meets only at night, in an old room in these apartments here. It just so happens you're in luck: Their weekly meeting is *tonight*."
"Poke your snout around sometime after 22.00 and you might just find them."
"Wait, how am I supposed to get into the apartments if I don't live there?"
"Hold on, what else can you tell me about this Steban?"
"That's very helpful. Thank you, Cindy."
"Hmm, why do I feel like there's a catch..."
"Use your little piggy brain. I'm sure *someone* will let you in..."
"Just that he's a real communist. Not like the play-acting you've been doing. The rest you'll have to see for yourself."
"Hold on. You didn't think it would be that easy, did you?"
"Oh, smart pig, because there *is*..."
"See, Steban's a bit on the paranoid side. He's got all these *mega secret passphrases*, to keep out infiltrators and the like. You can't join the meeting without one."
"Sure, I do. Steban trusts me."
"Do you know the passphrase?"
Hang on, could it have something to do with that strange *inside-talk* the boiadeiro mentioned?
But it won't be this one.
"Just not me."
"*Ahem*..." The lieutenant clears his throat.
"Not to interfere in your personal errand, but I wonder whether it might have something to do with that phrase Mañana mentioned overhearing."
"But you're not going to tell me, are you?"
"That's fine. I'm pretty sure it's 'Remember Dobreva and Abadanaiz'."
"But you're not going to tell me, are you?"
"That's really dumb. You should feel embarrassed even suggesting that."
"I was *totally* about to say that."
"Oh, right. Good thinking, Kim."
"Wait, what phrase?"
"You're right. How *foolish* of me. Won't happen again, detective."
"Of course you were, detective. Apologies for interrupting." The lieutenant smiles to himself.
The lieutenant nods.
The lieutenant consults his notebook. "'Remember Dobreva and Abadanaiz'."
"Guess this is what happens when two pigs put their heads together..." She seems slightly disappointed.
No, you weren't. Otherwise you *would have* said it. In truth, it was quite beyond your associative powers.
"Intra-piggy conflict. Very cool..." For a moment her eyes appear to light up.
"Now, let's see if you're half as dedicated a communist as you say you are..."
"That's enough. Off with you then." She makes a lazy shooing motion with her dangling hand.
"Huh. I guess this little piggy has done his legwork after all..." She sounds slightly disappointed.
"Why would I? That would be so boring."
"Why would I? That would be so boring."
"Now, let's see if you're half as dedicated a communist as you say you are..."
"That's enough. Off with you, then." She makes a lazy shooing motion with her dangling hand.
"Good fucking god, Mack. What is that smell?"
"What, like you've never reheated leftovers in the break room?" He skewers the greasy sausage with a small fork and removes it to a limp paper plate.
"Hey, if you wanna dress that up, I think there's still that old bottle of mustard logged in evidence..." He's already laughing at his own joke-in-progress.
"What, you mean the one Vic yoinked off..."
"... that hobo in front of the Frittte? Hahaha!"
Keep listening.
(Turn to Cindy.) "Okay, then. Will you help me find the communists?"
"Now you got to ask yourself, Mack. Are you desperate enough for *hobo mustard*?"
Torson chews thoughtfully at his sausage for some time. "Hey, Chester, speaking of... do you think Harry ever solved his money situation, or do you think he's gone full hobocop?"
Torson chews thoughtfully at his sausage for some time. "Hey, Chester, I've been wondering... do you think anybody's ever gone full hobocop?"
"You mean, like, is he out there right now, sleeping in a storm drain, chasin' down rats for leads?"
"Like, *really* hobocopped? Nah, that stuff's just an urban myth, Headless FALN Rider-level stuff..."
"Yeah, I could see it. He's always been weird about money stuff."
He chuckles. "Doesn't mean Harry isn't givin' it a good try, though."
"Okay, Cindy. Does that mean you'll help me find the communists?"
"I'm looking to acquire some original art. Do you have anything?"
