dialoguetext: "What's that? The piggy's looking to get into the art market?" Her eyes light up. "Watch out or you'll be auctioned off and face the chop!" She draws a line across her throat with a thumb.
The lieutenant straightens his back, waiting to see where this is going.
The *happening*, it's happening!!
Are we witnessing a performance, perhaps? Play along.
Relax, it's all part of her *image*.
No one speaks to a police officer in that tone. Show the little missy here her place.
She stares at you, fearlessly, waiting for a response.
(Step back.) "Is this a... happening?"
"I'm not a pig. I am *The Law*. Show me what you're selling or I will shake you down."
"Perfect, this is all very *on-brand* for you. Love that little persona you've created."
(Pretend you're a pig stuck in a cage.) "Help, let me out. I don't want to DIE!"
"This 'little persona' will grind you into a sausage if you don't stop. I'm not a sellout."
"Don't come at me with that. You've got nuthin' on me. Not a pork scratching."
"I don't do 'happenings', I like to leave a *mark*." She looks at you as if she's ready to wound you, then stares at the red paint running down the wall.
"Whoa! Calm it with that shit, cop. I don't have any art you can buy. Geez."
"No, we will not shake anyone down today," the lieutenant clears up, his voice calm and measured.
Words are one thing, but he's not letting you follow through with it.
"Fine. Whatever. I'll let it slide, but only because I'm interested in your art."
"Too bad, pork sausage, I don't sell my art. The whole point of graffito being on the street is so *everyone* can see it. No charge -- expression for all."
"The whole point of graffito being on the street is so *everyone* can see it. No charge -- expression for all."
There has to be a way to convince her... Everyone has a price.
Forget this *public* art. She must have something private and esoteric. Something that tormented her until she brought it into existence.
But how does she make a living? How does she keep a roof over her head? It must be hard.
I bet it's all about the scene for her. Tell her you can introduce her to some artsy jet-setters in Saint-Batiste. Maybe do some lines together in the powder room.
"I'm after something a little more challenging. I have an Actual Art Degree, after all."
"Don't you have anything personal? Show me your most conceptual *chef-d'oeuvre*."
"If all your art is free, how do you make a living?"
"If you sell me a piece, I can introduce you to some people. Free wine, celebrities, some sniff..."
"Alright, quit playing, tell me the price. I can make you rich and successful."
"I thought you were a pig?" She squashes her nose with a thumb so it resembles a snout.
"I don't do 'personal', if that's what you sickos are after. No navel-gazing pieces about what it means to be 'me'."
"You call this a living?" She gestures to her surroundings. "Look around you, hog-man, we're all bleeding out on the slab."
"If I wanted to whore myself out for some *Nasenbonbon*, I'd go to Porta Rosa. Or better yet, I'd take you with me and pimp you out to some friends of mine."
"I don't have a price. If I wanted to whore myself out, I'd go to Porta Rosa. Or better yet, I'd take you with me and pimp you out to some friends of mine."

"They'd be delighted to get their hands on a squealing pink thing like you," she hisses. "Cut off your ears, make some pig soup out of them. Now sod off! You've got nothing to offer that would make me change my mind."
"No one cares, I know I don't. So sod off, pig! You've got nothing to change my mind."
This place might be rotten, but at least it's hers.
"No, I'm an Art Cop. I chase down works of lazy derivation in the heated battle for original aesthetics."
"Yes, I'm a pig, but only if we decide to deconstruct what it *means* to be a pig."
"Both police work and art criticism require analytical talent and informed judgement calls."
"But you feel at home here, right? Besides, there's nowhere else to go."
"One day something will come along and pull you out of the muck."
"I'm sorry to hear that. I can only imagine the horrors you've seen."
"Ooh, little piggy knows the big words. What a waste of a perfectly good saucisson, stuffing it full of artspeak."
"Sorry, even with your fancy degree, you've got nothing to offer me."
A strong gust of wind knocks into her. Then she shouts: "So what, pig? You gonna mock me now? I don't need this."
"What, like your feeble business offer? Are you going to be the turning point in my shitty life story? A little fairy from above?"
"'I can only imagine the horrors,'" she mocks you in a squeaky voice. "I'm not your Channel 8 charity case. Sod off! No one here needs saving."

Nearby, a hoarse bark barrels through an alleyway that sits between two monstrous squats. No one walks down there anymore, but the nostrils of those who pass by in wet weather still detect the sickly scent of gasohol and burnt hair.
"Let me in. Let me hear what you have to say."
(Don't push her.) "Okay, okay. I'll back off."
"Fuck outta here," she bursts out laughing. "This 'let's get through this together' type of stuff doesn't work on me. Especially if it's coming from a pig!"
"Good call, piggo." She smiles to herself, satisfied.
Convince her to show you her art.
Sure, she's all draped up in ironic detachment, but everyone's gotta eat.
"I do have something to offer in exchange for your art. Money."
"Great, the little foray into the art world continues," murmurs the lieutenant, looking up.
"Blah-blah. I already told you, I'm not for sale, piggo." She looks almost disappointed by your lousy offer.
"Blah-blah. I'm not for sale, piggo." She looks almost disappointed by your lousy offer.
Turn it around -- it's the seller who wields the power in this relationship.
"Really? You're just going to let go of a chance to milk some stupid piggo rolling in cash?"
"I don't care what you sell me and I don't care what you do with your money. It's your choice."
"Uh-oh, you're manipulating me!" She sounds almost fascinated by this discovery. "I do like a chance to rip off some stupid piggos. And I need a pack of cigarettes. And some paint."

"Okay, whatever, piggy. Time to leech off each other like the parasites we are. Let me see what I've got..." She reaches into her heavy coat and pulls out a small piece of plastic coated thick with emulsion.
Even the lieutenant leans in closer to inspect the work.
"Here. Happy?" The plastic looks sad and damaged, as if it's been ripped out of some bigger piece. A glitzy barnacle of colours covers its surface.
Interesting. You can immediately see multiple ways to interpret this piece. What is the *experience* that the artist is trying to create? What *bodies* and *spaces* are they seeking to explore?
It looks like a palette. Nothing more than a board for mixing paint.
Remember, this is a *buyer's* market. You're the one who's in charge of pricing.
"Come on! Isn't there any other way I can prove myself worthy?"
She's locked up tight. What does she want? Maybe it's as simple as asking her. But whine about it so she feels superior.
"Squeal. Then maybe we can talk business."
(Turn to the lieutenant.) "Kim, you do it."
(Squeal, but only a little.) "Reeeh."
(Squeal a moderate amount.) "Reeehk, reeehk!"
(Squeal ignominiously.) "*Reeehk!* *Reeehk!* *Reeehk!*"
The lieutenant remains perfectly still except to give you a devastating case of side-eye.
Not in a million years.
"Not him -- you. I want *you* to squeal for me, pork chop."
"Come on! You really need to bring home the bacon." She chuckles.
"Do I need to come over there and pull on your curly tail? Squeal already!" She grins with power.
"Good little piglet," she says with words coated in butter.
"No way. Forget it." (Chicken out.)
"Awww, c'mon! I was just starting to have some fun."
Humiliation wasn't enough for her? How about you offer her something -- like a job?
What does she need? You don't have much to give her. Hmm, you could try offering her a job.
"How would you like a job? I can get you one. A real job with a wage!"
"Fuck-a-doodle-doo!" She stifles an outburst of laughter. "And what job would that be? Cutting you into rashers?"
"I want to see your painting again."
"Sure, piggo." She reaches into her heavy coat and pulls out a small piece of plastic coated thick with emulsion.
"Show it to me." (Study it closer.)
"Would you describe this as one of your signature pieces?"
"Let's talk about the price again."
"Let's come back to this later."
She juts out her hand, letting you examine the piece. Three red splotches have been shot at a diagonal across the surface. Tinier spots of various colours fan out from the same point of origin.
"Well, piggo, what do you make of it?" She sounds almost mocking, waiting for your reaction.
There's tension in these strokes of genius, a desire to step into a dialogue with the viewer, to provoke them. A meditation on... *Sein und Nichtsein*?
As said before, it's a palette. Nothing to see here.
It looks like a palette. Nothing more than a board for mixing paint.
The angle of the paint drops reveals that they were fired at the canvas with the force of a hand cannon.
It's one of those ink-blot tests. An invitation to connect with the *divine*.
"You're exploring the liminal space between being and unbeing. A cunning juxtaposition."
"It's just a mixing palette."
"Someone got killed here. A five millimetre calibre, point-blank range."
"I don't really have an opinion."
"Yeah, whatever, Art Cop." A wide smile crosses her face. "Spaces, bodies, shit. Hit me with that lingo!"
"Yeah, whatever." A wide smile crosses her face. "Spaces, bodies, shit. Hit me with that lingo!"
"Damn." She's almost ready to abandon the entire endeavour, but then changes her mind. "Well, it's also *art*. It's a conceptual illusion. Both the tool and the outcome."
Tool? Maybe she's onto something after all. Athletes are simultaneously tools and artists -- bodies chiselled to a singular purpose.
"Yes, my artistic integrity." It's impossible to tell whether she's being serious or not.
"Of course you don't. Why do I even bother? Just cough up the money!"
She is. Despite the demeanour, playing this game brings no joy to her. She cares about art and her private relationship to it.
"*Signature*? Oh yeah, pigster. I sneezed while holding a wet brush. Paint flecked onto the canvas, and voila. You don't get more signature than that."
"So you painted this with a sneeze? Truly remarkable... a clear sign of a *genius*!"
"That's disgusting."
"An exquisite commentary on the precious serendipity of the creative process."
"Interesting. What I really want to know is -- what do you call this new style?"
(Tickle the longest of your nasal hairs.)
"That's what I said, piglet."
"Says you." She looks you up and down.
"If you say so. I like to think that my trigeminal nerve painted it."
"Art-ishoo."
"How much do you want for it?"
"What about it?" She tilts her head, waiting for your offer.
"Sixty seven thousand reál. And your head on a silver tray."
Remember, this isn't about the art or the artist -- this needless purchase implies your *excessive wealth*. Art comes across as more tasteful than simply hanging cash on the wall.
"I can part with 50 reál."
"I'll pay 25 reál."
"How about 10 reál?"
"I have more questions about the painting."
"Suit yourself." She tucks away the painting and closes her coat. You hear waves breaking on the nearby shore.
"Not bad! I guess I'll take it." She holds back her excitement as she gives you the painting.
"Alright. Can't complain about that. You've got yourself a deal." She gives you the painting.
"That it? Alright. It all helps." She gives you the painting.
"Ask away."
She may antagonize you but she's still a struggling artist with no prospects. She *needs* as much money as you can give.
Lowball her. The wretched are used to rolling with the punches.
Is that all she thinks it takes to be an artist? Outperform her with her own style. Make it *yours*.

Splendid! Your first physical asset. But no time to stop -- money grows old unless it keeps moving. You need to find a *buyer*, preferably someone who will pay a high price for such an *exclusive* piece from a local artist.
"I met your friend Steban."
"I watched you go in, pig. You aren't telling me anything new."
"So did you two fancy each other?"
"I don't know how to put it, but I think we discovered something extra-physical together."
"Well, we got into a little *physical altercation*, but I think he got over it."
"He's a good comrade. Very advanced, ideologically speaking."
"Yeah, he's alright." (Shrug.)
"At first I thought that was just Uli putting me on, but then I saw Steb's cheek. You gave him a right love tap." She seems to approve.
"Heh. He was cooler before he started palling about with pigs..."
"God, you even talk the same now. Soon you'll be proofreading each other's homework..."
"Stop, pig. You're gonna make me heave..."
"Anyway, I told him you'd never go in for the posters. Shame. I had some really good ones all planned out."
"Anyway, at least you convinced him to put up the posters. Good to see the old king covered in proper slogans. I saw one old bird nearly faint coming out of the Frittte."
That's fine. You don't need her to tell you, because you *already know it*.
"You should listen to your partner every once in a while. He's not so dim as you are."
"Perfect, she isn't interested," the lieutenant murmurs to himself, "all the more reason to move on from this little side task."
"Your partner here gets it. Anything else I can *not* do for you, gentlemen?" She gives you both a mischievous smile.
"Nice vest, officer. Taking art classes now?"
"The Whirling-in-Rags just lost one of its staff."
(Point at Joyce.) "*She* could employ you. She works for the people who own the harbour."
"I know the leader of the Union. Bet they need an extra hand around the docks."
"You could work behind the counter at the local Frittte? Seems easy enough."
"The guy who owns the pawnshop could probably find you some odd jobs to do."
"You could work for me! Be a police officer."
She hisses at the boat rocking gently on the coastal waves. "She'd flay my skin. Wear me like a mink the first chance she got." A mad grin spreads across her face. "Unless I got to her first."
"Oh really?" Her eyes flash like stolen coins under moonlight. "Good to know. That makes even easier pickings."
"Oh, I *know* they need an extra hand. Especially after that cargo went mysteriously missing last week."
"You think he'd allow me back into his store? No chance. Not unless he wanted to lose his stock all of a sudden."
"I think you mean *boring*." She scowls. "Can't anyway. Technically, I'm banned. Not that it's ever stopped me getting my cigs."
"We have a policy that means we cannot hire any SKULL members onto the force."
"Me -- a brickman? I haven't got the snout necessary to snuffle around your filthy yard." She spits out her tongue.
"Is that all you've got, piggy? Looks like the job market has failed me *once again*." Wind howls between the nearby apartment blocks. "No job, no art. What a pity."
"Do you know something about that?" asks the lieutenant. His question goes ignored.
Try as you might, you just can't fathom what a young rebel dressed like a granny would want from you. She certainly isn't a flowers and chocolate kinda girl.
Cindy picks the dirt out of her fingernails as you stand there, quiet and clueless. Without looking up, she says: "Ask something or piss off, swine."
Told you! Told you these artist-types repel wealth.
You feel the biggest sneeze of your life itching its way to the centre of your face...
"Uh, what are you doing...?" She looks disgusted, her individual facial features racing to be the most dramatic expression of her disapproval.
"I'm an artist too." (Your nostrils flare involuntarily.)
"Nothing. Nothing! Khm..." (Stop the sneeze while you still can.)
You tilt your head back, close your eyes, and get ready to snap it all forward...
The coat gets flung over her head as she braces for impact.
But the rest doesn't come. You exhale softly -- no spittle, no shout. It's over. Just like that.
Perhaps not *everyone* is an artist after all.
"Was that it?" She looks relieved. "Stop playing with your snout and let's get on with this so you can go back to your stinky sty. You still want this painting or what?"
"AHHH--"
The pre-sneeze hype is unreal.
The mucous gripping the sides of your nostrils is cheering. All scents and odours seem to have left the world; your nasal chambers have become wind tunnels of *very* ticklish particles.
The lieutenant furrows his brow at another one of your eccentricisms.
The lieutenant is desperately searching for a handkerchief.
The lieutenant is desperately searching for another handkerchief.
"I see... blood-clot coins placed as offering to a pulsing threshold. But what does it *mean*?"

"It's a sign! Better pay up or you'll anger the terrible beast from... what did you say?" She knows -- she just wants to ham it up. "The *threshold*. Careful now, I heard it has a soft spot for smoked pork."
Hmph, her improv skills could do with some work. That was a *pathetic* performance. Are we supposed to be scared? NONE OF US ARE SCARED!

"What's that? The piggy's looking to get into the art market with a snappy business pitch?" Her eyes light up. "Watch out or you'll be auctioned off and face the chop!" She draws a line across her throat with a thumb.
His words are hiding a tinge of excitement -- he's not so detached from your pursuits after all.
What about Joyce? She's wealthy.
This place isn't exactly bursting with rich people.
I could sell it to Garte, hang it up in the Whirling-in-Rags.
Evrart can buy it on behalf of the Union.
The Mega Rich Light-Bending Guy seems blindingly rich.
And become a small-time art peddler? No, think bigger.
Hmm, doing business with communist dictatorships only works if you've got long-term plans in place... which you don't.
Good call. He's definitely the type who might be interested in art. Let's go hustle him and score us some extreme *moolah*.
Nah, she'd probably send the entire Wild Pines legal team after you if she knew you were trading goods around their harbour. She's ready and poised for a *hostile takeover*.
That high-net-worth individual -- wasn't he an investor? Let's go convince him to buy some *exclusive* local art.
That blindingly rich guy seems the type, the one you met in a container? Let's go hustle him and score us some extreme *moolah*.
That blindingly rich guy is the type. Sure, he said he doesn't carry much money on him, but he must have something else to trade. Let's hustle!
There must be *someone* around here with heavy pockets and an interest in the local art. Tell you what, have a wander round and I'll let you know if I hear any wealth.
That blindingly rich guy is certainly the type. He's already handed over 100 reál. Let's hustle him for even more *moolah*.
Wait, you can *hear* wealth?
Yes, if you know what to listen for. That's what happens when you've been in the game for as long as I have. Your senses get *tuned in* to more opportune frequencies.
I got some vibes from the harbour. Let's explore that area again. Who knows what we might find hidden among all those shipping containers.
Okay, where's a good place to start looking?
I got some vibes from that container you moved with the crane in the harbour. Let's see what's inside. There isn't a door yet that Savvy's VIP status couldn't open.
I got some vibes from that person inside the container you unlocked in the harbour. Why didn't you speak to them before? Let's head over there right now and fix that.
We haven't got into the harbour yet. Let's worm our way in and scope it out. Some of the best things in life come inside shipping containers.
Good call. Sure, he said he doesn't carry much money on him, but he must have something else to trade. Let's hustle!
Good call. He certainly seems the type. Let's go hustle him and score us some extreme *moolah*.
Good call. He's already handed over 100 reál. Let's hustle him for even more *moolah*.
"Anything else you want? I'm in a good mood -- but it won't last long."
"Look at us, coming to an agreement. Who'd have thought?" A breeze blows strands of hair across her forehead as she leans into the balustrade.
(Whip out your finger pistols.) "It's your lucky day! I'm looking to acquire some original art by the *crème de la crème*."

dialoguetext: "The room... it's clean."
"What did you say... sunrise..."
"What... happened?"
"Ouch."
"It's not *ouch* time yet. You just got a *drouamine* pill an hour ago. Wait until it wears off."
"Mr. Garte cleaned it. It took him an entire day."
"Sunrise, Parabellum. Sunrise, Prepare-for-War. It's an old revolutionary saying."
Drouamine. Then it's not *that* bad. Neither surgical, nor organ-damage bad. But still under-the-counter bad.
"Is it... war today?"
"How long have I been out?"
"Two days. In and out -- you've been up enough to take drouamine and curse. And drink water."
"The gates of the harbour are boarded up. The streets are a little more empty. Apocalyptic violence is yet to erupt, I am relieved to say." He looks out the window.
"I think we may have held it off -- for now." He unzips his bomber jacket. "Barely."
"A pity."
"Good."
"Ouch."
"Uhuh," he nods. "I see the drouamine is working."
"Pity?"
"I seriously want this... social order to collapse now."
"This is the end and I am its trumpeter, Kim. The quicker we get it done the better."
"Pity all the whores and traitors haven't been washed away! It's like I suffer... (cough) but for what?"
"You misunderstand me. (cough) I meant that in a... *disco* way."
"I see the drouamine is working."
"The whores, yes. That's good to hear."
"Cool."
Rhetorical flare. He does not actually welcome the return of the whores.
"Nothing. I take it back."
"No need, officer. You wanted things to go South outside -- that's okay, we all do from time to time. They haven't, though. Yet."
"Yes. We have also completely failed. But that's okay."
"That's right." He nods in agreement. "Ouch, indeed."
Isn't that written on your...
"My gun. It's engraved on it."
"Cops like it."
"How bad am I hurt?"
"What happened? You shot the major in the face. A firefight ensued."
"As retaliation, their rifleman tried shooting you. He missed -- or you dodged..."
"Is he dead?"
"What... happened then?"
"Yes."
You're a real killer, Harry.
A bloodstained killer.
"I'm a killer..."
Swallow...
"You're an officer of the RCM." He continues without waiting for a reply...
"Then I shot and wounded him while Glen took a bullet in the spine." He nods. "It was meant for me. Glen did not survive." There's a pause.
"Titus, Fat Angus, and Theo charged. Angus and Theo did not make it. They both died before they made it to intensive care. Titus survives. So do Alain and the musician, I forget his name..."
"I dodged."
"Then what?"
"You were bleeding out, you said something, I don't know what..." He thinks. "And you warned me. I was able to disarm officer de Paule before she got the jump on me."
"I killed her." The lieutenant takes a cigarette from his coat pocket and lights it. A bitter smell fills the room. "And that's what happened."
sequence: PlayAnimation(Kim Kitsuragi, StartSmoking); PlayAnimation(Kim Cigarette, StartSmoking);

dialoguetext: "I shot and wounded him. While Glen took a bullet in the spine. It was meant for me -- he did not survive." There's a pause.
"I thought you only smoked one a day."
"And they're all dead, all three... of the contractors?"
"How many casualties... on the Union's side? Total?"
"And that's..." (Conclude.)
"This is the one."
"De Paule was the last to die." He nods. "Evrart had their bodies returned to Krenel for a funeral. The company is yet to retaliate."
"Why?"
"Because we *deterred* them? Or Joyce did? Maybe the harbour -- in full lockdown -- is too costly a target. Or maybe..." he breathes in the fumes, thinking.
"Maybe they are simply taking their time and will attack soon? I don't know."
"Four: Glen, Theo, Angus, the fat one, he... took a lot of bullets." There's a pause.
"And Elizabeth too -- Elizabeth Beaufort was her name. The gardener."
"She did not make it?"
"No. She bled out before Evrart's surgeon could help her. Evrart sent his personal doctor but..." He shakes his head. "A costly loss for the Union. She was being trained for leadership."
"All." He nods.
"An absolute disaster."
"It's a total shit show, Kim."
"Not *that* bad -- all things considered."
"I don't see how it could have gone any better."
"Let's face it, officer -- and this is both of our fault..." he says calmly -- without accusation. "It could have gone *a little* better. Six people are dead."
"But what's done is done. The violence is cordoned off, the mercenary tribunal is neutralized. The worst scenario has not materialized -- yet."
"Oh no, officer," he says calmly -- without accusation. "It's pretty bad. Six people are dead."
"Yes, officer," he says calmly. "Six people are dead. It's not a success."
He did not expect you both to survive once you stepped between those two armies.
His smoking, his hunched back... you have it worse, but he took a real beating. That cigarette has *medicinal* purposes.
"Eugene?"
"Yes. He's still alive too."
"So you also killed."
He nods.
"As retaliation, their rifleman tried shooting you. He hit the cuirass... I heard it go off. I was looking for a clear line of sight to him."
"As retaliation, their rifleman shot you. He hit. With his carabine -- I was looking for a clear line of sight. When I found it..."
He sounds a *tiny bit* sorry he did not find it before you got hit.
"What happened? You shot the major. Unsuccessfully. A firefight ensued."
"What happened? You threw an improvised petroleum bomb at the major. A firefight ensued."
"You tried to throw an improvised petroleum bomb. It missed. Then you said *it's a fiasco, bratan* in a funny voice. A firefight ensued."
"The tie made me do it."
He does not answer, and searches for something in his coat pocket instead.
"What happened? We tried to take the diplomatic route and hoped they wouldn't attack first. They did. The major gave the command."
"Titus is dead?"
"Yes."
"You were bleeding out by then..." He thinks. "You warned me -- I was able to disarm Kortenaer before he got the jump on me."
"And the major..."
"... is in a private hospital across the river. Krenel claimed him from the local butcher shop, where Titus died. Turns out he's *insured*."
"We won't get to him anymore. The good news is -- he's not coming here either. I did some damage."
There is unveiled anger in his voice.
"Four: Glen, Theo, Angus. The fat one, he... took a lot of bullets." There's a pause. "And Titus."
"Five: Glen, Theo, Angus. The fat one, he... took a lot of bullets." There's a pause. "And Titus."
"Three: Glen, Theo, Angus. The fat one, he... took a lot of bullets." There's a pause. "And Theo -- he was just too old for combat."
"And..." he smiles: "We are still alive -- both of us."
"Let's face it, officer," he says calmly -- without accusation. "It could have gone a little better. You could've *not* missed."
"Let's face it, officer..." he says calmly -- without accusation. "It could have gone a little better. You could've *not* missed with the bomb. If you already threw it."
"Let's face it, officer..." he says calmly -- without accusation. "It could have gone a little better. The diplomatic approach was terrible. It was my mistake. I should have attacked..."
He was afraid.
"What happens now, Kim?"
"Reasonably bad. You were shot in the left quadriceps -- that's your thigh. It appears no major arteries were nicked. The bullet was removed and a bacterial infection treated with mercurochrome."
"Can I... walk?"
"We will see."
With considerable pain and the stitches tearing every now and then -- you should be able to do it.
Through tears and blood and stitches tearing it *should* be possible.
If it's possible, then by pure willpower alone. You are going to have to become... a psycholocomotor.
"The bruising in your shoulder is negligible. The armour took the brunt of the fire."
"Pretty bad, officer. You've suffered two wounds. The first is below your shoulder. The bullet passed through your shoulder blade, luckily missing your lung -- and heart."

"The second shot hit you in the thigh -- the left quadriceps." He points to your leg. "No major arteries were nicked, but the bullet had to be removed. A bacterial infection was treated with mercurochrome."

"Reasonably bad. You were shot in the left quadriceps -- that's your thigh. The outer side thankfully, no major arteries were nicked. The bullet was removed and a bacterial infection treated with mercurochrome."
You won't be able to dance much, that's for sure. You should be able to live with limping around though.
"I'm a psycholocomotor."
"Good. You'll need to be... whatever that is."
"Has anyone from my station been to see me?"
"No."
"If not my station, then who treated me?"
"I did."
"Thank you."
"I didn't know you could... do that."
"No need."
"It's part of a detective's task chain. You can do it too."
"They don't care about me at all."
"Good. I don't need them."
"Really?"
"Are you hurt?"
"Isn't that... strange?"
"I called your station after the fight. The injury was logged in. They told me they've sent officers to join you on the site."
"Odd. You haven't seen any, have you?"
There's a pause. "I'm sure they're worried about you."
"Okay."
"I'm sure they're worried about you."
No. They would be here if they were truly worried.
That means he hasn't seen them around while you were out. They're not *really* worried about you. If they were, wouldn't they be here?
"Not very." He rubs his chin. "I have a concussion from that woman beating me with the butt of her gun... I try to not move too much."
"Not very." He rubs his chin. "I have a concussion from the major beating me with the butt of his gun. I try to not move too much."
"Things would be worse if you didn't warn me." There's a pause. "Thank you. I did not see her coming. Stupid of me..."
"Things would be much worse if you didn't warn me." There's a pause. "Thank you. I did not see him coming. Stupid of me..."
"If they're so worried about me where are they?"
Better not agitate yourself further, it already hurts.
"I don't know."
Sorry.
"Okay...." (Get up.)
"Easy now..." The lieutenant turns double again, before your eyes. An orange hue of pain...
Your balance is *way* off. You feel like you're about to fall over on that thing...
You can take it. Just don't lean on that leg of yours too heavily.
"How are you?"
"My... disco days are done."
"I feel fantastic. Let's... rock."
"Who cares. Who cares about me. It doesn't matter."
"I'm very bad, Kim. Things are very bad."
"Gnhhhh..."
The lieutenant doesn't reply -- just looks at you teetering on your feet.
He thinks you should sit back down. Back straight, now... you're not sitting ANYWHERE.
The lieutenant looks at you -- teetering on your feet.
He nods.
"Your disco days should have been done quite a while back, officer."
"I honestly don't know."
You see the lieutenant's familiar shape in the orange jacket. It turns double -- then triple -- from the pain.
It's nothing. You're alive, that's what matters.
"*Sunrise, parabellum*," the lieutenant says. He's in the middle of a freshly cleaned room, with the fan above his head like a halo. His face is covered in bruises.
"I'm alive..."
"This is because I'm a La Puta Madre's peone, isn't it?"
"You don't... know?"
"But... I don't know either."
"Good, because I totally do."
"We can't talk to Evrart, the harbour is in lockdown -- everyone in there is outside our grasp now. And Joyce has left too."
"Joyce is gone?"

"Yes, she left yesterday morning. To meet the board of Wild Pines -- or that is what I've heard. There's a *pin* somewhere in the machine that keeps Krenel from sending in a death squad..." He looks out the window.
"Maybe it's her? Maybe she kept her end. Either way, Ruby's gone. And Klaasje too. We really should have arrested her, you know."
"Do you? Because we can't talk to Evrart, the harbour is in lockdown -- everyone in there is outside our grasp now. And Joyce has left too."
"Titus is *dead*?"
"Yes." He pulls on his cigarette intently.
"Who did it then, Kim? Who killed the hanged man?"
"Honestly I think our investigation has not produced a single credible suspect." His voice is calm, matter-of-factly.
"I don't know. I think your *incredibly dangerous* theory on Titus Hardie was wrong. More than six people saw Titus downstairs that night."
"I don't know. I think the *dangerous* theory you presented on Klaasje was wrong. We have not found a motive, or a weapon for her."
"I don't know. I think the theory you presented -- it's someone else, outside our circle of suspects -- was right. It'd better be. Everyone within the circle is either dead or gone."
"I don't know. I think your *incredibly dangerous* theory about *you* being the killer was incorrect, however. There is not one piece of evidence to support it."
"I don't know. I think the theory you presented -- it being Ruby -- did not add up. If we ever find her, we can pursue her on many offences, but not this one."
"That was our job to find out, wasn't it? Honestly, I just don't know. Our circle of suspects is dead and gone. It's not a circle at all. It's a ruin."
"Don't be narcissistic. Half the cops in Revachol West are his *peones*. Even if you are, it is not a decisive factor in this case."
"What about the hole in the... ouch... wall? Someone was checking her out."
"There's still a... 28% possibility the shot came from a distance."
"An antique bullet... from a Belle-Magrave, 4.46 mm. How hard can it be to find one? How hard can it *be*?"
"Something is creeping around out there. I sense it."
"What is?"
"The miracle hasn't happened yet. It's not over yet."
"It's simple, we have to locate *communism*. Communism killed him."
"There are all these... old bunkers and weapon caches around..."
"We could find thousands more if we wanted. All of Revachol is full of them."
"It's extremely easy. There are thousands lying around from the war. All completely unusable. It's precisely how *easy* it is that makes that bullet useless."
"We should go upstairs, rethink the ballistics *in situ*." A light nod, through some pain. "I agree with this. What else?"
"I don't know..." He rubs his neck. "That's been there for years."
"What?"
"The fucking *May bells*, Kim, the flowers."
"The god damn footprints!"
"Yes." He says. "God curse the footprints -- not solving the case for us. *Au diable*."
"What?"
"You know what I think about... solving crimes?" (Conclude.)
"Solving crimes is hard."
"I'm ready." (Conclude.)
"No." There's a short pause. "Are you ready to limp?"
"Solving crimes is super easy."
"Actually, I want to talk about this crime some more, before I tell you what I think about its hardness."
"I'm listening."
He arches his brow -- the ceiling fan patiently spins overhead.
"I'm ready to hear what you think about solving crimes now."
"Solving crimes is almost impossible."
"It really is *very* hard."
"It can feel that way sometimes, yes."
"Really? Because, to me, it seems solving crimes is *hard*."
He sounds surprisingly weary.
That concussion must be making him dizzy.
"You're not ready to give up, are you?"
"That's right. Let's give up. Time to start drinking."
Say nothing.
"Are you ready to limp?"
"I don't think so." There's a short pause. "Are you ready to limp?"
"Good." There's a pause. "Where do you want to limp to?"
"It's not *whether* I am -- I am. Jules told me so, he's from my station."
"Okay."
"Okay," he repeats.
"I've heard people say *I* am on La Puta Madre's take." He looks you in the eye. "And I am *not*."
He is definitely not on La Puta Madre's take.
"They were on the roof. I did not... I did  not catch them. Fucking butterfingers..."
"Every piece of garbage in the city is not connected to the case. You don't have to catch *everything*."
(Yank it out and show the dried flower, while it falls to pieces.) "This one, remember?"
"No, Kim. Every piece of garbage in this city *is* connected to the case."
"Okay."
He's wrong!
"Mhm."
"Okay," he concedes -- clearly not meaning it.
But they seemed so mysterious.
"I can't believe they're fucking useless!"
"I'm just gonna say nothing..."
There's a little pause -- he says nothing as well.
"No need to be melodramatic."
"*Something*."
"Nothing."
He does not know what to reply. Looks out of the window, then back at you.
"Hmh..." He hums -- thinking about something else.
"Something," he repeats. It does not sound like he's enthused about this *some-thing*.
"I'm afraid we may not be able to locate communism, detective -- on account of it being dead."
"Communism is making a *massive* comeback, Kim."
"Are you sure? I see communism *everywhere*, telling us what to think, stifling... ouch, my *leg hurts*!"
"Good. It's good it's dead. Communism is *stupid*."
"Ideology does not have anything to do with the murder investigation at hand, I'm sorry -- it does not."
"Okay. Yes. I can see how it's hard to indict someone who is not actually a person."
"I am glad that you do."
"You don't think it was a good idea?"
"I don't know what to think. It might not have been a *bad* idea. There is a *pin* somewhere in the machine. Something is keeping Krenel from sending in a death squad..." He looks out the window.
"The... Wild Pines representative?"
"Yes. Joyce Messier. On the boat, you know? She could have helped us. It's clear the mercenaries were working for Wild Pines. At least partially..." He looks out the window.
"Maybe it's her? Maybe she kept her end... Either way, Ruby's gone. And Klaasje -- well, at least *she's* safely locked away."
"Locked up? No, she would be of more *use* to us free, honestly. But it was the right thing to do."

dialoguetext: "Coinslot's dead."

"Hold on... There's something different about you, Cuno..."

"Nah... Cuno's just off speed for a few days..." There's a melancholy look in his eyes.

"Pretty fucking bad, Cuno thinks." He points to your left leg. "But you're one lucky pig. The doc took the bullet out and said you'll live."

The bullet must have passed through your shoulder blade, missing your lung and your heart. You lucky son of a bitch...

"Is that like a fucking street name or something?" The kid stops to think. "It's pretty cool to Cuno."

"I can suddenly see how it's hard to indict someone who is not actually a person, but an ideology..."
"Nothing."

Say nothing.

dialoguetext: "Fucking island is spooky as fuck. Cuno never liked it here."
"Cuno is present on the scene." He looks around with his hands on his hips.
"Talk to Cuno."
"A fucking giant stick insect..."
"Cuno's a pig now." He picks his tooth with a dirty fingernail.
"Shoot," he says with a nod. "Cuno knows this shithole better than anyone."
"Uh..." He looks confused. "Well you know, pig... Shit's fucked. And like... Cuno's got no time for this small time shit. Cuno's got *enterprises* to run."
"What do you mean, what's going on? This is good shit." He seems surprised. "You wouldn't believe the crap Cuno's getting from the trucks."
"Cuno used to hang there sometimes. It's a real shit-hole. Everyone is old or a fucking drunk or dead, except..."
"What do you know about the village southwest, across the canal?"
"Yeah, pig... yeah." He scratches his head. "It's a... seafort. For... It's for defence, pig. Don't bore Cuno with this historic shit."
"There seems to be a seafort in the bay. Do you know anything about it?"
"It's Cuno's," he says without pause or hesitation.
"Whose statue is it on the roundabout?"
"What are your thoughts on the strike?"
"Sure thing, pig." He nods. "What now?"
"Thanks Cuno, but enough about Martinaise."
"What's going on with the traffic jam?"
"Oh, pig..." A clever smile runs across his face. "Cuno's done with that shit. Cuno's a pig now. Living the pig-life. That reaver shit's behind him."
"What have you gotten there?"
"Wha-what?!" His face turns almost as red as his hair. "Are you fucking crazy, pig?! Cuno doesn't give two shits about that bird. Why do you even...?"
"Okay. Cool."
"You know... break shit, throw shit into the sea, throw shit into the windows, throw shit at the seagulls."
"Yeah, yeah..." He fidgets uncomfortably. "Of course Cuno's been there, but that was a long time ago and I was fucked. Been on the train for fucking days. Can't remember shit."
"Have you ever been there?"
"You bet, pig!" He appreciates your validation. "Cuno lives the life to the max. Lives every day to the mega. Cuno's in the *moment* like that."
"Cool."
Liar. He doesn't have the guts to climb in there.
Does he have a little *crush* on Lilienne?
"I'm pretty sure it's of Filippe III the Squanderer, the greatest of Flippian kings of Revachol..."
"You like Lilienne, don't you?"
"Cuno ain't spoiling this shit for you." He gives you something akin to a wink. "You gotta climb in there yourself and check it out."
He nods in agreement.
"Goddamnit..." He looks down, shaking his head. "Cuno can't believe you're making up shit about him. This needs to stop."
"Yeah? What's in there?"
"If you know that history buff shit, then why are you fucking Cuno with this?" He shrugs. "Cuno's a pig now. Has important shit on his mind. Pig shit."
"Cuno's been everywhere, pig."
"You ever been inside the ruined building?"
"Anything you can tell me about the boardwalk with the ruins and the fishmarket?"
"Like what?"
"Cuno had some business ventures set up in the neighbourhood. Had money coming in... But not anymore." He punches an invisible target in the air. "Cuno's a straight-ass pig now."
"Cool place. Lot's of shit to do there."
"Except nothing." He shrugs. "That shit is behind Cuno. Keep your nose out of it."
"What did *you* do there?"
"Except what?"
You know who isn't old, drunk, or dead? Lilienne.
"Cuno, I have couple of questions about Martinaise."
"Let's move!" [Leave.]
"Where is Cunoesse?"
"Cuno doesn't want to talk about this shit." There is a moment of thoughtful silence. He almost looks behind him.
"That toxic shit's behind Cuno now."
That is a look of a man who knows he'll be looking over his shoulder for the rest of his life.
He unzips his jacket again and pulls the pants from the plastic wrapping. "Here pig, we both FALN now. Performance Pigs. Let's try not to shit ourselves."
"I want to buy the FALN pants."
A crooked little smile. "Oh fuck, he's practically dyin' to big up how he did it. Just get him to cough it up. Cuno's got your back."
"Do you think he did it?"
"How do you think the questioning is going?"
"What can I put on him, to get him to confess?"
"I'm trying to get him to confess..."
"I'm slapping myself to get ideas!"
"Okay, let's do this." [Leave.]
"Okay, so, we've got the old fuck." The kid whispers, his eyes bugging out of his skull with excitement.
"Yes, Cuno can see that. You got this. Think of like..." He rubs his nose. "... what *other* shit he's done too. Cuno can tell he's a killer."
"Good." He nods. "I think it's going really fucking well." He leans closer. "Just cut it with the punching shit, alright? Makes us look like we got nothing."
"He's into some ancient warrior shit. Hate shit. Pressure cook him. Push it on him, like -- motive shit. Pig style."
Good. Talk to him, demonstratively pick it up, then push it along with the other accusations. This is a good idea.
"Well. There's the gun," he says, scratching his head... "Why you still haven't picked it up and used it against him is beyond Cuno."
"Cuno's in the game. Let's fucking do this, pig." he whispers, excitedly.
You hear that? He thinks you're very close...
"Also, the gun." The scratches his head. "Why you still haven't picked it up and used it against him is beyond Cuno."
"Yeah, Cuno can see that," the kid says seriously. "So can fuckin' murderoonie here. You should stop -- it's weird as fuck."
Of course -- why didn't *you* think of it?! Motive shit. Pig style.
"Tell 'em Cuno sent you. They'll know what it means."
"Ah, Cuno's not into that hallucinogenic shit -- that's for pussies."
"No, I don't think it's actually drug related..."
"If you wanna take a real blasto, go down the coast to the old church, where the speedfreaks hang."
"Mag?"
"Well, I have been partying a lot lately..."
"I've had these weird shakes recently. And something like... visions? Sounds familiar?"

dialoguetext: "You gotta hit *Magnesolam*, when you get off the train, pig. I always hit it to get the mag back."
"Totally, pig. Cuno's in the same shit every time he's coming off speed." His tone gets parental. "You need to *medicate* that shit."
"No, it's more than that. It's like the city is speaking to me."
"Magnesium, pig."
Apparently he has never formed an opinion on the matter and isn't going to do so on the fly either.
"So who's side are you on?"
"Small time shit. Got it."
The kid nods, obviously relieved.
"Whose side's Cuno on?!" His tone gets angry. "Cuno's on fucking Cuno's side, pig! This is beneath the Cuno. Don't talk to me about this playground bullshit. You're getting shit in Cuno's head."
Being put in the spotlight like this makes him feel exposed, makes him lash out.
He was probably collecting tare or stealing stuff that wasn't nailed down.
Just don't ask him about it. Boys in that age can be quite sensitive about such matters.
"It's okay, I like her too."
"I'm sorry, Cuno. I'll stop."
"Your secret is safe with me, Cuno." (Give him a wink.)
"Lilienne is nice though."
"About Martinaise..."
"Well *I* don't," the kid says, pointing to himself with his thumb. "Cuno's got no time for this shit. He's a pig now."
He tries to keep his voice casual and businesslike, but it trembles ever so slightly.
"You fuckin' better, pig!" His index finger is pointed straight at you. "We're partners now. You got to be professional with the Cuno."
"What fucking secret?! You gotta stop this shit with me!" He's trying to control himself. "Cuno's a pig. We're partners now. You got to be professional with the Cuno. Talk sense to him."
"She's okay," the kid suddenly speaks with a high pitched squeak. "I mean... With all the fucking drunks and relics around, she's like the only one who isn't a walking shit hole. She's okay."
Sounds like the kid has a soft spot for Lilienne.
"Yeah?" He places his hands on the hips, waiting for your question.
The kid is admitting falsehood, sire. He just doesn't know.
This is the extent of the boy's knowledge.
The *Train*. Speed-Train. Amphetamine Express.
"What am I missing? What haven't I done?"
"We never did that ballistics shit here." He sniffs. "Let's check out where he shot my gimp. You should know that shit, pig."
Good one, Cuno. It doesn't have to hold in court. Just establish a line of sight and he'll do the rest himself.
"We can take another look in the mini-tower, where the bed was." He sniffs. "Let's check out where he shot my gimp. Ballistics shit. You should know that, pig."
"Cuno's in the game. Let's fucking do this, pig." he whispers, excitedly.
Cuno doesn't say anything. Stares out the window. You're on your own.
Something tells you this is going to be a rough ride.
"What happened to your art thing?"
"Locust city?" He swallows. "Cuno dropped that art shit coz Cuno's fucking *poor* and has shit for brains."
A truly rare moment of self pity.
"You better not make Cuno fucking *cry* about his art-shit, okay? Change the subject, Cuno doesn't do that shit no more. Fuck that shit, fuck *everything*."
"We still need to get him back, but... yeah. We got our man."
"Makes you proud to be a pig," the kid says. "Oink oink."
The driver has adorned his space with a substantial collection of peculiar paraphernalia. Proclamations about *honour*, *strength*, and *purity* are glued to various panels.
It is the seal of Royalist-era Revachol.
What kind of stickers and insignia?
Fumes of heavy fuel oil waft over you, making your eyes sting. The odour mixes with cigarette residue.
The back end of the cabin has a small perch to sleep. Large ashtrays. There are several suns and wheels sown into the curtains.
What about the back seat?
"You think this lorry belongs to our tough guy?"

dialoguetext: It's clear this is your guy. Only the March edition of 'Power Man Monthly: The Pure Man's Magazine' is missing. It's clearly the rotund raceman's.
The windows are clear, they've been recently washed. You can see a lorryman's cabin with personal belongings, stickers, insignia...
[Leave.]
Look in the window.
[Leave.]
A large metal pendant hangs from the rear view mirror. The pendant features a sun crowned with wavy rays.
A book with ragged edges catches your notice. The front cover features a large, muscular man. The title reads: 'Man from Hjelmdall in the Lost City of the Pygmies'.
He was acting tough before. This probably scared him a bit. Who knows when it will come in handy -- a slightly scared racist lorryman?
There he is, in front of Frittte, smoking nervously. Hoping it's over.
A lorry stuck in the traffic jam. This big, heavy Graad-made machine is well kept for such an old machine.
"Racist-nationalist paraphernalia." He grits his teeth. "Not unusual in this part of town."
He was acting tough before. This definitely scared him a little, you being here.
"Relax, I was practising the time-honoured technique known as the 'lie'."
"It's basic biology."
"Look, what happens when the races get all mixed up?"

"I'm going to *stop* this conversation." He makes a sudden hand gesture. An open palm. "This is Martinaise. People have certain attitudes here. You will find plenty of citizens to agree with you. As for me..."
(Shrug.) "Let Nature sort them out."
"I've got nothing against them, but we have a responsibility to future generations."
"Well," he says after taking a moment to collect himself. "You've made your views on the subject quite clear..." Another little pause.
"I suppose that's a relief. Just be careful how often you avail yourself of this 'technique'. A lie may be useful in the short-term, but they have a way of catching up with you later."
"I was just trying to convey that I understood his grievances and wasn't judging him for having them."
"Everyone thinks they're better than other people. Some people are just particularly crude about it."
The lieutenant falls silent and looks down at his boots. Whether he thinks you have a point or not, he isn't saying. It's unclear what this means for your relationship. Then he speaks...
Yes.
"You're right. I didn't mean to cause trouble. Sorry about that."
"That's good to hear. I don't want there to be any unnecessary friction in our relationship during this *important* case."
Here we go. Zoom in on the mixed races part. It's the best one.
"I don't really want to talk about it." [Leave.]
The lieutenant looks at you in silence, though you cannot discern if he's judging you or not. "I suppose your reasons are your own."
"And what exactly do you think should happen to those with *undesirable* traits?"
Well, now you've done it. Let's see if you can talk your way out of this one.
The lieutenant narrows his gaze. "So you *don't* find his views... say, *unbefitting of a police officer*?"
"It's not about me. As police officers, we gain nothing by staking out the moral high ground over him."
"Of course. But he's also not entirely responsible for them. I haven't been in this world for long -- already I'm a product of my environment."
"There are tens of thousands of people who grew up in Martinaise and somehow managed to avoid becoming racists who yell 'Come here, saffron picker' at passers by."
"Our position in Revachol is already precarious: Many people think we're vigilantes as it is. I can't have them thinking we're *racist* vigilantes to boot."
"Well, *actually*..."
"Apology accepted, detective." The lieutenant relaxes. A weight seems to have been lifted from his shoulders.
Wait a second. Are you sure you want to go there? Even if you succeed, you're going to fail.
What do you mean? I'm in the right here.
On second thought, maybe I don't.
Are you sure about that?
Forget it, this was a dumb idea.
Hoo boy, we're really doing this.
"Maybe he's got a point."
"And what point would that be?"
"There's a difference between saying something crude -- and an ideological racist."
The lieutenant says nothing, waiting for you to continue.
"It's only rational for a society to select for the most desirable traits. That's how it works in Nature."
"That doesn't mean they don't have rights. If they're perpetrators, then we punish, if they're victims, then we help. That's all there is."
"Wonderful." The lieutenant falls silent. His expression is hard to read, but it certainly doesn't look *happy*. Then he speaks...
"Let me say just one more thing. As you've seen, these sorts of attitudes are quite common in Martinaise. So I expect this to happen again. And again..."
"Stop right there. I know what you're going to say. Don't. Also -- these attitudes are quite common in Martinaise. So I expect this to happen again. And again."
"I've had this conversation enough times in my life. From now on, I'm going to stay out of it. How you choose to respond is your business." He concludes: "Now -- let's get back to the task at hand."
Now you're thinking sensibly.
"Wait, am I becoming some sort of Death's Head Racist suddenly?!"
"I don't know what you mean by *death's head* but it certainly looks like you're becoming a racist, officer."
We know a *lie*, sire. And it didn't feel like one to us. He chooses to believe though -- for now.
"And one more thing -- as you've seen, these sorts of attitudes are quite common in Martinaise. So I expect this to happen again. And again..."
"I've had this conversation enough times in my life. From now on, I'm  going to stay out of it. How you choose to respond is your business." He concludes: "But be careful. Now, let's move on."
Okay... feels like this is going to be a *discussion* now.
Okay. You think there's a way out of this.
Peel off the cover on the passenger seat.
Examine the radio.
Unlock the door with the key Tommy gave you.
Smash the window in with the prybar.

dialoguetext: Try to peek in the window.
How am I going to get this open?
"Use the prybar to smash the window. Open it from the inside."
With a key -- or a tool. Like, say, a prybar.
The glass on the side windows is tinted and covered with dust. You can barely make out the shape of a seat and two steering levers.
With a firm grip you raise the prybar, a glint of light catching on the tip. Call down the hammer of truth and justice! Release your secrets, lorry cabin!
Prybar in hand, you take a hard swing at the window. A loud *thunk* rings out and the prybar bounces back, leaving a tiny spider web on the glass.

The smell of cigarettes and perfume welcomes you. The cabin inside is plastered with old movie posters, actresses smile from the walls. There's a radio transmitter in the front and a toolbox tucked under the driver's seat. Some tools lie scattered near the pedals.
Admire the posters.
Pull out the pull-out toolbox.
[Close the door.]
A lorry, abandoned by its owner, stuck in the interminable traffic jam.
There's something odd about the passenger seat... The seating fabric has been pulled tight over the lower side of the seat where the toolbox should be.
There's definitely perfume in the air. It's spicy, with a hint of ambrette, wafting through the bitter air of the cabin.

Voila! A stack of neatly folded papers has been stashed behind the seating fabric. You see three maps depicting a large metropolitan area. It's Revachol, some of its routes and highways have been outlined with a pen.
A metallic drawer slides out from the seat: It's empty, except for a folded newspaper.
Open the door.
[Leave.]
[Leave.]
Check the pedals.
Smash it.
The window shatters and droplets of glass fly everywhere, shattering over the lorry floor and pavement.
Looks like the window might be shatterproof. You may have to rethink your approach.
"Subtle," says the lieutenant and sticks his hand in the window -- like a common car thief -- and then opens it.
Study the centrefold.
Enough of the posters.
The movie stars are still smiling from the walls. There's a radio transmitter in the front and a pull-out toolbox tucked under the driver's seat. Some tools lie scattered near the pedals.
The actress is draped in a sheath dress, one of her shoulders bared. The faded remains of an autograph run across the poster. She's looking past the camera.
This is Tippe Tijonne, a starlet from the dawn of cinematography. Less known for her talent, than her tragic, untimely death.
She's delicate, yet lost. Ruined underneath it all.
A feeling of tenderness washes over you -- a longing even, perhaps. And gentle tragedy.
What happened to her?
She wasted away in a drug den called 'The Door to the River', not far from here on Boogie Street. A mixture of cocaine and morphine. She was a afraid of the world. And the camera too.
Stop and wonder: What's that smell?
The remnants of a sweet juniper-scented perfume. Probably 'Granate No 5'.

You wedge yourself under the steering-wheel to get a better look. Seems like the few tools lying around here -- a hammer, a pair of pliers, a rusty wrench -- have been casually thrown there by the disorganized driver.
This particular lorry is a FALN A-Z 'Tempo', a model infamous for its irritating design mistake: the slippery-smooth throttles.
Unfold the newspaper.
Push in the pull-out toolbox.
The pull-out toolbox slides back into its nest. The rest is as it was: radio, posters, a trace of motor oil smell under all the cigarettes.
It's an issue of 'Périphérique' from last Wednesday. A piece of paper falls out from its pages.
Pick up the note.
It looks like an article ripped out from a radio-enthusiast magazine. Complex mathematical equations explain the basics of something called 'the ULAN frequency system'.
Adapting a high-quality radio-transmitter to emit this frequency may make it powerful enough to transmit a signal from isola to isola. But that's just a guess.
These formulas look oddly *painful*. Maybe it's the hangover, but they give you a headache.
The lieutenant leans over your shoulder to examine the note: "The ULAN frequency system? I've never heard of that before. I know of FM, AM, UKV, but..." His thought trails off.
Looks like the frequency dial is absent. It requires a key to work, but the key has been removed -- likely by the missing lady driver.
The lieutenant leans closer to the radio and hums: "Strange. There are so many radio stations saved here... must be over one hundred at least."
"Why would anyone need so many radio stations?"
"What about the Speedfreaks FM? Is it one of the saved stations here?"
"Is there anything we can do with the radio?"
"No, that's on 78.9." He stops, coughing awkwardly.
"Doesn't look like it -- it's completely inoperable without the dial key."
"What else is here..." (Conclude.)
"I'm sorry." (Smash it, apologetically.)
Fold open the topmost map.
Fold open the second map.
Look at the third map.
Return the papers under the seat.
"So it would seem." The lieutenant examines the maps with a furrowed brow.
"Hard to say. This distribution network looks certainly large, yet still vague enough... It doesn't reveal much about the *besmertie* behind it."
"*Besmertie*? That sounds vaguely familiar."

"A besmertie is a Revacholian crime syndicate. They see themselves as the inheritors of the 14 Revacholian indotribes, but really they're just violent gangs vying for control on the West side of Revachol..."

"No luck?" the street vendor says, visibly disappointed. "Why not take another look, officer? Keep supporting the economy!"
