"You keep coming back. That's good, officer! Keep browsing those clothes, keep saving that economy!"
"Very cool. The economy thanks you, officer."
"Those socialists in academia."
If he really wants to save the economy he'd let you pay with net worth. Go over and ask him if you can
How about some premium-class service over here? Like paying with net worth. Go over and ask him if you can do that.
"Saffron picker! Welcome to Revachol!"
"Don't make yourself too comfortable!"
"Ha ha! Welcome to Revachol!"
"Welcome to Revachol!"
"Welcome to Revachol! Don't stay too long."
"Are you lost? You look lost. Out of place."
"Welcome to Revachol!"
"Welcome to Revachol!"
Alright, but these actually make your vision worse. It's like literally being under water.
Yes, but they also make your soul quiver like jello. So deep.
"The shine on these sunglasses lasts a lifetime, officer! One hundred percent guaranteed!"
There's a pile of cheap sunglasses in a small box, a variety of shapes and colours.
Rummage through the box.
[Leave for now.]
Try again, maybe you can find *some* interesting sunglasses in the box.
These are all boring. Boring third-rate ho-hum sunglasses made of cheap Seraise plastic. The kind of plastic that melts in the sun.
Ah, I see... A pair of waterblue shades. The writing on the left temple says: "Sub-Insulindic Rendezvous." The frame appears to be hand-carved out of bone.
No luck. All you find is this... lime-coloured cellophane visor? Produced by a bargain sportswear brand called Amphibian, apparently. There's a malformed green frog on its bent cap.
"You like sunglasses, officer? I've got the latest styles, right here!" The vendor takes a pair of sunglasses and sticks them under your nose.

"These are all first-rate sunglasses!" the man declares. "Premium design, superb material, *very cool* UV-resistant! These will definitely keep your eyes safe *and* cool while doing your dangerous police work."
Try them on.
"Oh, very interesting choice, officer, very *high-culture*..." For the first time the street vendor's voice trails off, as he watches you inspect the glasses.
"Wow, officer, you look so cool," the street vendor has picked up his pace again, as you observe the world through deep sea-tinted lenses.
"Kim, what about these?"
Put them back.
"I'll take those cool deep blue glasses."
"I'll take that Amphibian sports visor."
"Oh, that visor is perfect for you, officer. It'll definitely keep the sun out of your eyes while you're shooting criminals." The street vendor makes a bang-bang sound. "And all for a mere six reál."
Hey, at least it might actually offer some protection against the sun, not like those cheap plastic shades.
Those UV-stickers are almost certainly just there for show. If anything, these lenses probably direct more UV light *into* your pupils -- a UV magnifier.
(Turn to the lieutenant.) "Kim, are firefights something we should be prepared for?"
Put the visor back.
"You don't like it? Sure, square-jaw, no problem. Let's get you some real shades."
"I hope not," he says, looking up from his browsing.
Try the shades on.
Abort! These are hideous. What's more, they don't even fit your face. You can feel them pinching your nose and chafing against your brow.
"No," the lieutenant gently removes the glasses from your face, setting you free again. "You're definitely not buying those."
"Don't tell me what to do, Kim. I like those sunglasses."
"You're right, I'm too sensible for those."
"Damn, officer, you look like a mega-secret spy, very secret," the man nods eagerly. "They're practically made for you. I'll let you have them for... two reál and fifty cents!"

"No, I can't... We can't walk around with you looking like this." His hand has already risen mid-air, but he stops. "Okay, fine. Go ahead. If you want to look like a walking mid-life crisis, then who am I to interfere?"
"Are you sure? But they look so good on you!" The street vendor frowns. "You should think this through, officer."
"I'll take those ugly glasses."
"A good starter pair, officer! And when you're ready to upgrade, come back and see me!"
"A man who knows his style," the street vendor nods. "Much respect."
"Sporty *and* practical, officer! Good choice."
The lieutenant tilts his head and steps back, eyes narrowed in a thorough examination. It's a case to him.
"What, change your mind, officer?"
They're perfect for concealing your bloodshot and baggy eyes.
It's going to be very difficult for anyone to take you seriously with these things on your face.
"You look like a musician," he declares, eyes still squinted behind his own glasses. "Like a *blind* musician. But you could do worse. Take them if you want."
This is how a sea monster sees the world. You've become a sea monster -- giant, hidden and... strangely tender at heart. All is blue.
"And they can be yours for a mere three reál. My regular customers have passed them all up because they've got no taste, but *you* found them..."
The lieutenant's reverse psychology fourberie doesn't work on you. If you want to look like a mega-secret mid-life crisis, that's your choice.
"A pity," the lieutenant says. "Those actually weren't half bad."
Stylish shades, huh? They'd be even more stylish if you paid for them with net worth. Go over and ask him.
Damn, that felt *good*. Your heart's pounding nicely. You should tell people to fuck off more often.
Fuck yeah, motherfuckers!
"Kim, I think I should tell people to fuck off more often. It felt really good."
It's not really my style.
"Not as a general rule, but that one was justified. Better to get the lay of the land before telling people to fuck off."
That means you should do it whenever you feel like someone's disrespecting your authority.
No, you shouldn't. You're an officer of the law.
Never forget: The whole world's a wooden house and you're a god damn flamethrower.
Hey, I've got an idea on how to fix your style. Maybe you should just go fuck yourself? Yeah, ever thought of that?
That's the spirit!
"Seems like something police would do. What do you think of all this, Kim?"
"I don't think there's anything to discuss." [Leave.]
The lieutenant nods -- but he's not happy.

"I'm not sure what the ULAN frequencies are all about, but they may hold some significance. Perhaps it's a better way to connect between fleets while avoiding frequency bleed, or maybe it's used to tap into RCM networks..."
"Oh, and the maps we found. They reveal the *geographical* extent of the operation -- looks like they've used abandoned tunnels and access roads to stay hidden. This is useful info."
"How do you think this is connected to the Union?"
"My suggestion is -- we use it against the Union in any way we can. To our own ends. It's a slippery eel, but we just might be able to pin them down *indirectly*. Down the road."
"What about the movie posters? How do they factor into all this?"
"As... *elegant* as they are, I don't think they are relevant to the drug trade."
"I'm especially intrigued by that radio transmitter -- particularly the sheer number of stations it can connect. Looks like this alleged drug trade casts a wide net."
"Honestly, I'm quite worried by what we've seen so far. The evidence seems to point to a rather extensive and well-organized operation."
"So it turns out this *is* is connected to the Union."
"Okay -- debrief over?" [Leave.]
"We didn't find anything *conclusive* linking them to the smuggling operation, but somehow I doubt that Evrart Claire would be oblivious to something like this happening right under his nose."
"Like Joyce told us, yes -- logistically. But don't expect to bust this open during our stay here. At best, this is an angle we can use against them. To other ends. As extra ammunition."
Don't be fooled, desire always plays a role.
"Klaasje might have been right about Ruby -- she looks awfully lot like one of the poster girls in the cabin."
"And last but not least, it looks like the Hardie boys knew this driver, as we know that she was present at the lynching. This may be the Union connection we've been searching for."

"Perhaps you're right..." He stops to think. "This is one connection I find a little dubious, to be honest. I prefer not to profile people's emotions. Perhaps it's because I'm not very good at it, but still."
"Debrief over," he nods. "After you."
Actually, he's not bad at it at all.
"Yes, well..." He doesn't say more.
"A lot of women there. Especially for a lady driver's cabin."
"Maybe the trader is some sort of cinephile."
"Could the film industry be involved?"
"I'm going to say -- no."
Unimportant?
In short: this is a future angle. Possibly a good one.
Meaning: someone as slippery as Evrart won't be caught by a couple of cops and some stuff they found in some cabin.
"Will the RCM open an investigation into this?"
"We should return to the murder case. See what Joyce tells us about the lynching. When we're done for the day, I'll call my station and suggest our narcotics department look into it."
"There are more than enough grounds to start an official investigation -- some time later, when we're done here. We do *not* want to get caught in that..." He stops to think.
"What are you thinking?"
"The fact that one hasn't started already gives me pause. An investigation, I mean. Especially if the Madre grouping is involved... and I can't imagine they aren't. It's certainly worrisome."
"Corruption?"
He nods. "All the same, I don't like the idea of Internal Affairs descending on the matter. That won't help anyone either."
This means it's well funded. Technology like that... a major player must be financing it.
Listening in on your calls? Between you and your station? A worrying prospect...
The probe and the case *converged*, he thinks. This was quite the find.
He just doesn't like flimsy connections. Especially of *this* kind.
"And last but not least, it's *Ruby's cabin* we found. This is an undeniable connection to the Union."
"The Union really is in neck-deep with everything around here, isn't it?"

"One way or another, they seem to be -- logistically, if nothing else. But don't expect to bust this open during our stay here. At best, this is an angle we can use against them. To other ends. As extra ammunition."
The Delta Logistics Company truck stands here waiting, reflecting white light from the courtyard behind it.
Are there people in there?
Why is the light so strange?
Let it go for now. [Leave.]
Because this is a place of mystery.
Yes, people hard at work at their desks. They can barely tell if it's day or night anymore because the lights in the building are so uniform and bright. Who knows when they'll come out?
What keeps them motivated?
Could be. They certainly want to stir the pot. Remake reality in some new image.
Are they really so pressed for time to finish whatever they're doing? Sounds potentially dangerous...
Those don't sound like proper working conditions.
Sounds like a highly motivated bunch.
I hope they're working for the glory of Revachol, at least.
Irony. They're yuppies masquerading as Mazovians... Or was it Mazovians masquerading as yuppies? Even they get confused sometimes, out here in poverty-stricken Martinaise.
Yes, and it's rather ironic, because they believe themselves to be Mazovians deep down.
Could be. Not sure they remember what they're working for anymore themselves...
Yes, they are highly motivated by irony, being yuppies masquerading as Mazovians... Or was it Mazovians masquerading as yuppies? Even they get confused sometimes, here in poverty-stricken Martinaise.
Not yet.
"Whatever's going on there could hardly be of any consequence to our ongoing investigation." The lieutenant adjusts his glasses.
"You can come back to it on your own when we're done with this case."
Can't I get into the courtyard somehow?
You knew it would be here, blocking the gate.
A Stas-Rajko! One of the finest Zsiemsk-made motor carriages ever. An oldie but a goldie.
Bulky frame. Heavy. Hardy. Looks like a tractor.
Yes, built like a tractor. And used as one too in the Zsiemsk countryside! Take note of the Eight Antler emblem, the symbol of the Stas-Rajko. Proudly born to honour its humble roots.
That's cool, but I have policeman things to do. [Discard thought.]
"Hey Kim, check this out!"
What a beautiful motor carriage! I want to know more!
Glad to share! The value of the motor carriage has been seriously diminished by its colour: all Stas-Rajkos are baby-blue by default. The paint would be considered unforgivable to collectors.
"A Stas-Rajko, KK-2. That's a classic model," the lieutenant replies with a nod. "Never thought I'd see another one repainted after what happened last time."
"They should've left it baby-blue."
"You sure you're not Zsiemsk?" He shares a smile with you, only for a second.
Zaffer blue was also the colour Zygismunt the Great used for his banners... Strange. This is really all you know about the Stas-Rajko. And ancient Zsiemsk rulers.
No. Only that the motor carriage is typically baby-blue, the colours of Zygismunt the Great, an ancient Zsiemsk ruler. His banners were famously zaffer and white: the colours of the Stas-Rajko.
Hold on, maybe I can impress him -- do *I* know what happened last time?
"What happened last time, Kim?"
"An old case from my precinct. A couple of Zsiemsk migrants saw a Stas-Rajko stopped in the street, painted just like this: muddy brown. Murdered the driver on the spot."
"They said it was an honour killing. Hussar-style. The Zsiemsk community protested the trial, flying the banners of some old king or whatever." He shakes his head. "Five thousand came to protest."
Correction: four-thousand-three-hundred-and-ninety-five. The fourth largest public protest of a criminal trial in Revachol.
"Hate to correct you Kim, but only four-thousand-three-hundred-and-ninety-five people were on that protest."
"Is that so, officer? I'll take you at your word."
"Kim... could our hanged man have been the driver of this car?"

"Could it be another Stas-Rajko murder?" He gives you a crooked smile. "Honestly, that just doesn't seem like the type of vehicle our dead guy would drive, so my initial guess is the two are not related."
Who drives these?
Not many people outside of Graad – and Revachol West too, it appears.
Hold up. Is this a tractor?
"Who are the Zsiemsk community?"
"What'd they sentence the killers to?"
He studies his reflection in the car window. "Four years for murder in Reunion."
"People we're paid to protect." The lieutenant shakes his head. "Let's leave it at that."
"Interesting. Before we proceed, I've got an *opinion* on this paint-job."
"Yes, detective?"
"I think it looks better brown and black."
"Okay." The lieutenant takes his glasses off to polish. "I'm not going to honour kill anyone over this -- but I've *seen* it blue and white. It's much better that way."
The lieutenant shrugs. "The perps were remorseful. Their *sorry* knocked eight years off the sentence. That's the system."
Got it. [Finish thought.]
The prisons in the Greater Revachol Industrial Harbour are already full. Prisoners are expensive to maintain. The longer the sentence, the larger the cost.
Yes, you're sure you're not! Or if you are, it's only in that Revacholian way. (Four to five percent maximum.)
"Let me guess what happened last time, Kim: Blue and white are the colours of Zsiemsk. Someone painted it, got a Zsiemsk mad, and boom -- murder happened."
"That's... Well, yes. Exactly it, more or less. Except it was a crowd of them. Tore him out of the vehicle and ran him over with his own tyres."
"They said it was an honour killing. Hussar-style. The Zsiemsk community protested the trial, flying the colours." He shakes his head. "Five thousand came to protest."
Were you there?
"I try to avoid drawing far-gone conclusions like this before actually examining the body," the lieutenant says with a slight smirk. "But my initial guess is the two are unrelated."
"Could it be another Stas-Rajko murder?" He gives you a crooked smile. "You really should ask me to brief you on the case. But right now I'm just gonna go ahead and guess the two aren't related."

That page-three girl... she must be *the* most beautiful page-three girl ever printed. And look at those freckles! The origin of disco... makes you wanna dive into the boogie, doesn't it? Get closer to disco itself with Miss Page-Three.
No. This is not how I want to remember the freckled girl. [Finish thought.]
Yeah... I want to get into the groovy. Let's disco, baby. (Start unzipping.)
Hang on. Right now? Unzip?
Go on...
That's exactly what I mean. Unzip and party down on yourself, my man. No one's watching.
Except Miss Page-Three, of course.
PARTY WITH MISS PAGE-THREE ALL THE WAY TO DISCO ZERO!
L'origine du disco! Such a powerful conceit, and this is what we're going to do with it? The commitment of an act of gross public indecency?
It'd be indecent to ignore Miss Page-Three. Beauty is inviting you on a pilgrimage!
Hm... How *exactly* can I travel to the origin of disco with Miss Page-Three?
Oh, come on. Don't say you've forgotten *that* as well. You can *feel* what you wanna do. You wanna party, don't you? Party right now with Miss Page-Three. *Unzip* and party.
I don't think so... there's just something uncomfortable about all of this.
Should I invite Kim to travel to the origin disco with me?
Absolutely not.
Look at her thighs, *between* her thighs, and... what are you waiting for, man?!
... is what you're thinking. But you don't want to disco like this. Not really. Not in the deepest part of your soul, where the freckles only make you sad.
COME ON! I SAID PARTY!
(Party.)
I DIDN'T SAY PARTY THIS SECOND!
The usually unflappable lieutenant takes a surprised step back. "Officer... what are you doing?"
Party later. Party in *private*. Like you would if you ever prayed.
Why do I hurt all of a sudden?
The furnace has long been cold, despite itself. You're too sad to jerk off. This is not the first time this has happened, either.
"I, uh... had to zip *up* my fly. That's all. Let's move on." [Finish thought.]
Fuck. Fuuuuuuuuuck! But it's the origin of all disco, buddy! Why not?
Because she's the kind of pretty that gets me down.
There's more to the freckled woman than what you're suggesting. There's more to disco, too. And to me.
And more than that: you're sad. There's an absence inside of you, something missing that may have been freckled too.
Whatever, coward. Don't ride your way to the origin of disco. The page-three girl is too good for you anyway.
Oh, right. Of course... [Finish thought.]
A pilgrimage you can make with just your hand.
Hold on, is this what happens when you two get together?
Yes!
Sure is!
Yes! This is just like how it'll be in the End Times -- only me and Miss Page-Three. (Start unzipping.)
... is what you're thinking. But you don't want to party down. Not really. Not in the deepest part of your soul, where the freckles only make you sad.
Fucking right. Let me just tighten up a bit for you -- is that good, you sick, wild fuck boy?
Come ON, *bratan*! YOU'RE SO CLOSE TO DISCO! TAKE IT OUT AND JACK IT!
C'mon! Beauty is inviting you on a pilgrimage. A pilgrimage you can make with just your hand.
Come on, what are you talking about -- sad freckles? Freckles are fun!
Then it is truly over. You are beyond the help of the page-three girl. You are truly doomed.
... I don't want to masturbate on the street, okay?
You're right. There's an absence inside of you, something missing that may have been freckled too.
But Kim...
"Thank you for now." [Leave.]
"Before I came, you seemed... *away*."
"Blacked out. Should you be driving a lorry if you get like that?"
The woman is still hunched over the railing, her head swaying to the music, her eyes looking at nothing in particular.
"What do you mean?"
"Because I'm one of the best camionneurs around, that's why. I drive routes no one else will."
"You were in a dream. Inactive. Tuned off."
"Yes. What about it?"
"You go right ahead, lawman. Let me know when you find them. I can't wait to read their *report*..."
"This should be reported to the proper authorities."
"Huh?" That flicked a switch somewhere. "What is it? What do you want?"
Snap your fingers in front of her face.
"Never mind, sorry to bother you." [Leave.]
"I'm something of an expert in blacking out. You should take better care of yourself."
She looks you over and scoffs. "You're right, lawman. *I'm* the one who should take *my* health more seriously. Thank you for looking out for me..."
"Is that all you woke me up to say?"
"Is that all you wanted to know, lawman?"
"Show me the soles of your boots."

dialoguetext: "You seem like a woman who knows a thing or two about drugs."
"What is it that you're hauling, exactly?"
"What do I need drugs for, lawman? What I see, what I *feel*, the Great Adversary... no drugs can compare."
"How can you not know what you're hauling in your own lorry?"
"Just this month I made half a dozen trips from Saramiriza to Graad, on the U41-A. What do you think they take from Saramiriza to Graad, lawman?"
"I think I know what's going on with you."
"Now what do you want with an old woman's boots, *xerife*?"
"Did you just call me a *lady*, xerife?"
"No, lawman. Diamonds." She grins.
"Okay. If you're not involved with the drug trafficking then why are you still waiting here?" (Conclude.)
"Where do you want me to go? This isn't so bad. I can listen to music, or the seagulls. Look at all the colours and the features of this world. It's a good palate-cleanser, this jamboree..."
"What are you hauling?"
She shrugs. "Whatever stupid things they put in the lorry, I imagine."
"So you don't know what you're hauling in your own lorry?"
"What if the cargo is contraband?"
"I quit concerning myself with that a long time ago." She smiles a careless smile. "Besides, I don't drive the lorry for the cargo, if you know what I mean..."
"Then it's contraband, lawman. What? Do you want to take an old woman in? Be my guest. Lock me away like Bad Hand Hermenegildo."
The woman sways her wrinkled shell back and forth, a strange grin across her face.
"Well, that's good enough for me."
"It's for important police business, ma'am."
"Please? Help me out here. It's important."
"Nothing, I guess. Let's talk about something else."
"You said earlier you don't know what cargo you're hauling. Could it be drugs?"
"Who the fuck is Evrart?"
"Because of all those hauls through the pale?"
"That's not really what I was getting at."
"Where could I get my hands on an *experience* like that?"
She glares at you. "Oh, this *xerife* is a smart one."
"Then what *were* you getting at?"
"If you don't know, pfft!" She flicks her wrist in a gesture of casual dismissal.
"Evrart sent me." (Place finger on the side of your nose and tap twice.)
"I wanted to ask if you'd be interested in smuggling some drugs?"
"Okay. Let me put this another way -- are you smuggling drugs through Terminal B?"
Maybe if she thought you're... *corrupt*?
"Your *mãe*, lawman. What of it?"
Her shoulder bones crack as she shrugs. "Maybe. Probably not. Makes no difference to me either way."
"The Union boss?"
"*Ah*. And what do I care about the Union boss? He's not Gabriel, he's not Franconegro. He's not even Hermenegildo the Hand."
"Why would I want to do that?"
"For commerce, the lifeblood of the isolas."
"For the glory of the world republic. Liberation of the spirit and body."
"I don't know, the thrill of the criminal lifestyle?"
"Lawman... what in the name of god are you talking about?"
"Drugs!?"
"I don't know, that's why I'm asking you."
"It's diamonds, lawman. Obviously." She grins.
Damn this. Make her answer.
"I didn't ask you about diamonds, did I? I don't care about that."
"Are you making fun of me right now? You better start complying."
"I would never make fun of a real lawman, *xerife*."
"Or -- I can just relax and let my mind carry me back where it will. To the great plains..."
"Diamonds are good for you, lawman. You should try them sometime. Make yourself pretty like Eva Deshoras."
"Okay. Let me ask you something else, then."
"I guess that makes sense. Minding your own business."
"Of course it does -- what did you expect?"
"Never mind," she sighs. "I remember now. I'm still stuck in that traffic jam. In the *Fifties*," she adds with contempt.
"While *you* people were tearing each other apart over your petty little Revolution, in Mesque it was a golden age."
In all likelihood, it's a world that's only ever existed in her mind.

"He was the biggest star of his day. Girls used to faint in the aisles of the cinema whenever he came on the screen, and school boys used to memorize all his lines..." She leans back, savouring the world she's conjured up.
"Who's Gabriel Buenguerro?"
"Are you alright, ma'am? You were out."
"I was actually hoping *you* could tell me that."
"Me? I am the law around here."
"Where else would you be then?"
"*When* else would you be then?"

"Back in Mesque during the time of the Revolution." The smile returns to her face. "The sidewalks and cafes are filled with young people... I was on my way to see a new boiadeiro picture starring Gabriel Buenguerro."
The small wrinkled woman does not greet you. She nods along to something on her radio. A photograph is clutched in her hands and there is a warm smile on her face.
"Excuse me, ma'am, I'd like to ask some questions."
"Grandma?"
"She's just a distracted old woman. Better to leave her alone."
"If you say so..." [Leave.]
"Where am I? Who are you?" Like a magician recalling a subject from hypnosis, you've jolted her back to reality.
No response. Wherever this woman is, your words fail to reach her.
"Wait..." The lieutenant stops you before you can snap.
"Then I don't suppose you could tell me where we are, lawman?"
The woman still has her eyes fixed on the photograph in her hands. In the background, the radio plays.
The smile on her face has disappeared, replaced by the wary aspect of a cornered beast.
It's the warmth of a winter night's fire. Maybe she could give you comfort and shelter? Some cigarettes and food money? Maybe she's your...
"Nothing to do here." [Leave.]
"Until you came along, that is." The look she gives you is accusatory.
"If you want her attention you may need to be more forceful."
"Okay. What's that?"
"Of course not. To truly understand the boiadeiro, you need to listen to 'On the Western Plain'."
"I've already got too many records to listen to as it is. Change of topic."
"It's an old ballad about a young girl who falls in love with a daring boiadeiro. He promises to marry her as soon as he returns from the Western Plain."
"I'm guessing that doesn't happen."
"And they live happily ever after?"
"No, the boiadeiro strangles his beloved and throws her body in the Magritte. Then he rides off, because the Western Plain is calling to him."

"Of course not. The boiadeiro returns from the Western Plain a *changed* man. One night, as he and his beloved are out walking along the River Magritte, she pleads with him to give up his riding and settle down..."
"You have to understand -- a true boiadeiro needs a whole horizon to himself. He can't be tied down by man or woman. His beloved was selfish. She didn't know what it meant to love a *boiadeiro*."
"That's a terrible song."
(Nod solemnly.) "A beautiful song."
"I still don't really understand this whole *boiadeiro* thing."
"I think I see where this is going."
In the background you can hear the orchestra swell as the screen fills with the maiden's imploring eyes...
"I don't think I *do* know what you mean."
"Of course you don't."
"She's just a distracted old woman. We should maybe let her get back to her things..."
"You hear that, lawman? I don't think your partner likes you spending too much time with me..."
"Diamonds."
"Diamonds, really?"
"Of course not," she says, grinning. "But wouldn't it be marvellous if I was?"
"Okay, but what are you *really* hauling?"
"So he gives up his riding and settles down, right?"
"That's... not where I thought that was going."
No. This one is a monster in disguise.
"Why?"
"Why? I just told you why."
The photo -- an *ambrotype* from the turn of the century. As golden as her smile.
"Wait, what's so bad about the Fifties?"
"The men have small jaws and everything is made out of plastic. Why do you need plastic?" she scoffs. "When you can make the world out of amber?"
Snap your fingers twice.
"*This* is Gabriel Buenguerro..." She shows you the photograph in the lavish amber frame.
"Right. I have some other questions for you. Police questions." (Proceed.)
Snap your fingers in front of her face.
"They are someone's memories, boy." She gets gruff, suddenly. "What difference does it make if it's me or not?"
"Someone? Are these not your memories?"
A strikingly handsome man looks straight at you, his head crowned with a wide-brim hat. His hair is dark as an oil slick and his jaw is the most perfectly chiselled thing you've ever seen.
Take a look.
"Sorry to interrupt your dreaming, ma'am."

"I wasn't dreaming. I was *there*, lawman. It was early spring and 'The Man Behind The Black Sun' had just come out. The posters were twenty metres tall. Everything was golden..." Her eyes narrow and she appears to take your measure.
"So I take it you were in Mesque when you were young?"
"*Someone* was..." She nods as though her meaning were perfectly clear.
She seems to derive some bitter pleasure from this strange thought. As if the past will one day wipe the present away, like a tidal wave approaching.

"Why not, *xerife*? It's not like I have anything better to do in this hellhole." She settles back against the railing of her motor lorry. Behind her, mountains of memorabilia, photos, and knicknacks line the dashboard.
"They're beautiful. That is all that matters. Beautiful and true -- and they will win. They're *coming* for this, you know..." She looks around. "All of this."
"Lawman," she greets you. "You caught me at an opportune moment. This awful weather keeps me awake. You can entertain me with your questions."
She doesn't actually think you're that smart.
This line of questioning is going nowhere! Try harder!
"Well, aren't you a lady?"
"I was told of a woman driver. You're the only woman here."
The woman's malevolent cackling fills the roundabout.
"I'm not that either, *xerife*." Her smile dissipates. "I've gone too far from it all to remember what was between my legs. It doesn't work like that on the *long haul*."
"I'm a lady like you're Gabriel Buenguerro -- only in dreams."
"So... you're *not* the driver everyone is terrified of?"
"That's all I needed to know, thanks." (Conclude.)
"I'm only terrifying to small children. And to those who used to know me."
"Then who is the female driver I was told of?"
"How should I know? Do I look like I spend a lot of time with the other camionneurs -- sniffing around -- when I have my movies to go to..."
"*O sim*..." The woman stares at you, her mind elsewhere now, on other matters.
"Easy. It's the skinny man who thinks he's a poet -- never trust a poet..." She squints across the square. "Also, he's the only one I can see from here."

dialoguetext: There's something off about this woman. Tell her to show you the soles of her boots. Maybe she was at the hanging... somehow?
"I think we're done here, no?" He closes his notebook to stress it.
Nothing. Her smile just keeps widening; her hair is grey like lead.
Snap your fingers in front of her face.

The Republic of Mesque is a massive confederation on the isola of Mundi, the world's largest state by territory. It's a petrostate, a constitutional monarchy, and as of recently an outcast due to its tilt to the far right.
A *boiadeiro* (*boia* for short) is a cow herder from upstream Magritte, the great steppes of Northern Mesque. He is a rugged individualist and explorer.
A *boiadeiro* (*boia* for short) is a cow herder from upstream Magritte, the great steppes of Northern Mesque. People like Mañana, at the gates, have turned it into an ideology of sorts.
Bad Hand Hermenegildo's *bad* hand strangled three hundred people. What can I say -- some people just really like strangling people.
She says that as if something *narcotic* is the real reason.
"Wait -- you get high off driving a lorry?"
"Oh, it's so much more than *high* where I go, xerife. It's *low* -- I go to the bottom..." She closes her eyes in reverie.
Yeah, it's definitely some kick, some *terrible* kick in the dark. A sleep kick. Perhaps you can find out later...
Yeah, it's definitely some kick. Some *terrible* kick... the pale probably. This 'pale' sounds like it's the *shit*.
"Wait -- why is that, lieutenant?"
"Should you drive a lorry if you get like that?"
"Nothing. I just don't think she's connected to anything."
It's because of the pale. He doesn't want your frail mind caught up in it -- and this woman has spent time *in* the pale. A lot of time.
He doesn't want your frail mind caught up in something here. Something *unconnected* to the case. But connected to this woman tuning out like that.
He's worried. But not for her -- for you. Hmm. What is it about this woman, if she's not connected to anything?
"Okay -- let's change the subject."
"A pale dream, is what it is." She nods her head according to a rhythm known only to her -- staring at the photo in her hands.
"Oh, don't worry about me. I'm one of the best camionneurs around. I drive routes no one else will."
"What routes?"
"Lomonossov's Land. Udachnaya Zemlya. The Western Plain..." She nods and closes her eyes again, letting her mind submerge...
A terrible cold comes over her. Rattling her teeth, as she stares inward.
"The Trans-Katla Magistral. U41-A. As Estradas do Mirador. All the good ones. The deep trenches. Where the bluebirds fly." She opens her eyes again and shudders.
"Cool. Ride until you're dust, sister."
"Irmão..." she breathes out. "I already *am* dust."
She raises her boot, slowly -- with contempt -- and says. "I'm starting to think you should let me get back to Gabriel Buenguerro. You're no Gabriel..."
"Just before Gabriel it was the coronation of Franconegro -- now *there* was a real man..." There is no aberration in the pattern that you can see. She puts her foot down.
Moreover, the boots were size 37. Tiny. There are too many discrepancies in all this.
She's wearing sturdy worker's boots made of black leather. Buckles run across. The sole is also made of leather.
"Now the other one please."
"Please?" She raises her boot, slowly, with contempt. "I think you should let me get back to Gabriel Buenguerro. You're no Gabriel. Gabriel doesn't say please..."
"Wait, what do you mean it *was* the coronation of Franconegro?"
(Turn to Kim.) "She is not Odd Sole. These are not the boots that made the prints."
"These are not the boots I was looking for."
Another discrepancy, although not boot-related, is the coronation of His Innocence Franconegro. Which happened 500 years ago.
"It was," she shrugs. "And then it was no more. And I was no longer holding my father's hand. He was no longer descending the stairs in Raehl. The crowd had gone silent."
"Perhaps it was another *xerife* who came and woke me up, looking at my boots, asking questions? Or perhaps it was one of the others in this *carnaval*. I don't remember."
As she says *carnaval* she gestures to the empty square -- with the statue and the machines.
He takes a quick note. "I could have told you that from just looking at them. Her size is 37."
"The feet of a little girl," she smiles. "They fit well on the pedals."
"The feet of a little girl," she smiles. "They fit well on the pedals.
"The... Adversary?"
"Yes. There is a *protagonista*..." She gestures to the intersection. "And an *adversário*. I am on the side of the Adversary. There's no coming back from that haul."
The pale. Sounds like *the* drug to me.
I don't like the sound of any of that. Sounds like a horrible drug. The worst one of them all.
Those epithets are familiar somehow -- The Great Adversary, The Great Unrest.
Alright. Let's get you a pale-category licence and roll that doobie up!
"Fine. Let's change the subject."
"Good. I don't care about drugs. Little molecules. They're nothing." She glances wistfully at the photo.
"Ma'am, you're not responsible for what the client puts in your lorry as long as the seals are not opened. We officers know that." He gives you a stern look.
Lay off her.
That's correct. There is no visibility of any of the others.
"Like looking into the ocean at night. In the dark."
Yeah... it's not her. Believe me.
"Why are you scary to the people who used to know you?"
"Because they can no longer recognize the person I once was."
"You said *long* haul. That's..."
"The big ones. The tracts. There's no women and men there, it's all just..." She hums along, as if to a track on repeat...
"'In the middle of this town there's a ghostly motorway -- it takes all the people where they want to stay'..."
Something in her is pulling toward some unknown rest state. She twitches -- like a sleep kick.
In the background, a quiet song seeps from her cabin into the air. You don't hear any vocals.
"The routes you drive are *unusual*, aren't they."
"Some of them. Some of them are like home to me now." She nods. "I would say the routes I drive are *usual* to me."
"And what *is* that?" She sticks a filterless cigarette into a cigarette holder and reaches for the light.
"You're a paledriver. You transport goods through the pale."
"Nothing. No need to be direct."
"Some jamboree you turned out to be... You have about a third of the jawline of Gabriel Buenguerro, and none of the balls." She smiles.
"Great." The lieutenant concedes with a head shake. "He asked the Pines rep about the pale."
"You don't have to protect me from this. I'm a big boy."
"I can't operate in this world without knowing its basic terms."
"I'm a detective. I need to know things."
"No. I just remembered it myself." (Point to your head.) "With my head."
"Fine." He's not buying it. "Just try not to black out again. And don't *contemplate*. We don't have time for that."
"Fine, then." He sighs. "Just try not to black out again. And don't *contemplate*. We don't have time for that."
"Oh -- I'm contemplating, Kim. I'm drawing *existential conclusions* from this."
"Yeah, no. Just for detective work. That's all I needed it for. Now..."
"Everything is related to the pale. My condition. The case. Everything. It's all *entroponetic*."
It's death -- but for the Universe? Oh, we're contemplating the living *shit* out of this.
"That is *exactly* what I didn't want you to think..." He sighs and turns to the woman. "Ma'am, my partner wanted to know if you work in pale transport."
"*Exactly* what I didn't want you to do..." He sighs and turns to the woman. "Ma'am, my partner wanted to know if you work in pale transport."
"No offence, but *your partner*..." She lights the cigarette, a white and silver cloud of smoke disappears into her mouth.
"That is *exactly* what I didn't want you to do..." He sighs and turns to the woman. "Ma'am, my partner wanted to know if you work in pale transport."
"...seems like a bit of an idiot." She breathes out. The air tastes sweet.
"*Oh meu deus*, the Lawman solved the case..." She lights the cigarette. A white cloud of smoke disappears into her mouth.
"And here I was thinking you were an idiot." She breathes out and the air tastes sweet. "So, are you? An idiot, I mean."
'República', a filterless cigarette from Mesque.
"'República'." (Smell the air.) "That's not very healthy."
"I blacked out after a night of heavy drinking and lost all memory of the world."
"I blacked out -- from sheer heartbreak -- and lost all memory of the world."
"Neither is pale transportation." She shrugs. "Life is transitory."
"I'm not an idiot. I'm a detective of the RCM. Don't say I'm an idiot."
"You *are* an idiot. And you're keeping me here. Glued to this racket. Unless there was anything else..." She puts the cigarette out and stares at something in the distance.
"Like Gabriel Buenguerro in 'Pergunte à Poeira.'" She nods and smiles, unkindly. "You're the opposite of me, then. I remember everything -- even things I never knew."
"Like Gabriel Buenguerro in 'Segure-me, Paraíso'..." She nods and smiles, unkindly. "You're the opposite of me then. I remember everything -- even the things I never knew."
"Things you never knew?"

"The smell of liquor on Gabriel's lips after the shoot. In the motor park. The roses on the day of Franconegro's coronation. On the grand stairs of Raehl. The smoke from the fowling piece, when Dolores Dei was shot..."

"The look on her face -- like an orgasm. The wound in her chest. My hand in my father's hand..." She closes her eyes, her eyelids trembling. "Except I never had a father. And I never shot Her Innocence Dolores Dei."
"Over-radiation?"
"Heroic doses, *xerife*. Heroic."
"Isn't that dangerous?"
"Thought insertion? *Dithering*? The Graad-Katla Magistral?" She savours the lungful. "It's more than dangerous -- it's *sad*. But... at first I had to make a living. Now..."
"When you've seen it all go *away* like that, rolling off like the sea, and then come back to this..." She gestures at the square. The broken horse monument, the clanging of machines in the distance.
"What are we *doing* here? For thousands of years, Gabriel... It doesn't have to be like this. We can just give up. We can just become vapour."
"What does it look like? The pale?"
"I would rather have what I have than what you have."
"I would rather have what you have than what I have."
"You cannot see it but you know it's there. And it's big -- bigger than anything. Bigger than all the other things combined."
"I feel I already *have* what you have. In some way."
"What does it feel like?"
"How do you pass through it?"
"In the belly of an airship, behind steel windows -- so you don't look straight into it. It's not *advised* to look into it."
"Not on this lorry then?"
"No -- the same one. A *roller*. They all are nowadays. Special wheels for connecting to the floor of the hold." She points to the machines, clumped up like toys.
"One last thing. You said we can just become... vapour?"
Their wheels all small and round, multi-axle trailers.

"Nothing. Until it starts. When you're deep enough -- then, for me... it's like autumn. Dark grey and orange, the orange of streetlights and the colour of trees in the electric light. It smells like autumn too. It smells terrible."
"Yes."
No elaboration.
Nostalgia. Cooped up in the cabin, shaking... Terrible nostalgia. For yourself. For humans. It's too much to bear. She loves it.

"They say there is a point -- one that *I* have not crossed -- in the pale superdeep. If you stray too far off course on the U41-A, or in Lomonossov's Land... where every step you take is one step further from home, no matter the direction."

"It's a point you cannot come back from. Your mind becomes so radiant with the past -- there is a flip." She flicks the ash from her cigarette. "Instead of writing, it erases memory. Nearing some kind of..." She shakes her head. "Indescribable *finale*."
"Maybe you've been down the *Motorway South?*" She looks at her cigarette, it's almost out. She has swallowed it hungrily. Then at you...
"The Motorway South?"
"It's a story us longhaulsmen tell -- longhaulsmen, *xerife*, not *paledrivers* -- way beyond the established pale that's lit by radio frequencies. Where it goes silent."
"And dark. And the process begins. Erasure. Kilometre by kilometre. In any direction. The Motorway South is a road you cannot come back from."
"What is at the end of the Motorway South?"
"No one knows what's at the *end...*" She takes the cigarette out of the cigarette holder and extinguishes it. "I've only glimpsed the beginning."
"I've only felt it in the distance. When I was a child..." She goes silent, her eyes close and her hands shake. "A child. Rowing on the lake."
"Ma'am?"
"*Hosiannna...*" A sigh escapes her lips, then silence, as she stares within herself.
"Thank you. Good bye." [Leave.]
"'They say I've been away on a kind of holiday'..." She replies, silently.
"'It takes all the people where they want to stay.'"
'In the centre of this town there's a ghostly motorway', she sang.
"You've fried both your brains enough for today, detective..." He inspects her. No response.
"Let's get some air. This one's far gone..." He shakes his head silently as he turns to leave.
There is nothing more to do now. She's far away.

"Don't be stupid. The boiadeiro returns from the Western Plain a *changed* man. One night, as he and his beloved are out walking along the River Magritte, she pleads with him to give up his riding and settle down..."
So he doesn't think she's the lady driver?
C'mon, he thinks -- she's not the lady driver.
A correct appraisal, you're quite shabby.
"Yes -- go. Enough jamboree. I need to get back to Mesque..." Her voice trails off.
"So the boiadeiro strangles his beloved and throws her body in the Magritte. Then he rides off, because the Western Plain is calling to him."
"The *most* beautiful -- a true boiadeiro needs a whole horizon to himself. He can't be tied down by man or woman. His beloved was selfish. She didn't know what it meant to love a *boiadeiro*."
"When you've seen it all go *away* like that. Rolling off like the sea. And then come back to this..." She gestures at the square: the broken horse monument, the shadows of the machines in the night.
She is receding. In the clutches of some indescribable, scattered emotion. A child. Descending.
The woman looks at nothing, her eyes closed and her lips moving.
"Girl child," you hear her say. "Girl child. Girl child..."
This man's got a hold over her. Even fifty years later, you can feel it...
All of what -- the world? The present?
What if... to truly love a boiadeiro is to float lifeless downstream?
So he doesn't think she's the smuggler?
She clearly doesn't think she's a 'lady'. Don't repeat it.
You feel very cold suddenly. As if standing face to face with a terrifying adversary. Then the feeling dissipates and all you see is an ageing woman.
"Great." The lieutenant concedes with a head shake. "He asked the Pines rep about the pale -- and now he's talking to everyone about it..."
"I'm looking for Ruby, the *lady driver*. Know anything about her?"

dialoguetext: She cups her ear and leans forward. "Did you just call me a *lady*, xerife?"
If you want to know more about Ruby, this is a dead end. She's only heard the word 'lady' and latched onto it. You can push on if you're interested in *that*, though.
"Never mind. I have other questions."
"I'm terrifying to small children. And to those who used to know me."
"This is about turning *back* time, Kim."
"We're still on this ridiculous *side-task*, I see..." He sighs and turns to the woman. "Ma'am, my partner wanted to know if you work in pale transport."
"Hold on, you said it *was* possible to turn back time, through the pale..."
"*Xerife*, what you understand wouldn't fill a pamphlet..."
This is your chance. Ask her, is it really possible?
"You don't need to turn back time. The pale is already churning with it. As the tide of pale rises, so does the past. Someday both will cover the whole world. That's it. That's the story."
"You're saying the future will *be* the past..."
"You mean, we'll all be drowned in our own past..."
"You're saying, one day I'll be able to return to *love*..."
"And that's just fine with me. I don't mind becoming vapour. I *like* vapour..." She gathers a cloud of smoke in her mouth, then slowly exhales.

There is a name for this ideology: Entropolism. A faith in and desire to accelerate the spread of pale across the world, until humanity has reached what its adherents call the 'rest state' of humanity, the final reconciliation of past, present, and future in timeless spirit...
You don't like the sound of that, chief. All the *really* good stuff is *right here*, in the present...
"You've fried both your brains enough for today, detective..." He inspects her. No response.
"Now, I'd like to have a word with you about this *side task* of yours..."
This is all you're going to get out of her. There's nothing more for you here.
Yes, *yes*. This is what you've been searching for...
"It sounds... *wonderful*."
"Thought insertion? *Dithering*? The Graad-Katla Magistral?" She savours the lungful. "There's a kind of wonder there -- a *sad* wonder. But... at first I had to make a living. Now..."
But there *is* one more kingsman to confront.
"I feel like I'm getting *really* close."
"I feel like there's still a *long way* to go."
"You've been saying that for a while. And yet, we only seem to be getting *further* from our actual goal..."
"No. You see, we've already spent too much time on this nonsensical side-errand. There's no magical fascist who's going to unwind time for you..."
"Because the problem isn't time, it's *you*, detective..."
"If you're serious about this, really truly serious, then I suggest you take a long, hard look in the mirror and ask yourself what's *really* going on..."
"Now come on, let's leave this one to her reveries." He shakes his head silently as he turns to leave.
Who?
*YOU*.
It's time to face yourself, mano y mano. The next time you find yourself alone before a mirror. *That's* where this will end... The final showdown.
B-b-but what if you don't *like* what you find there? There'll be no going back from it...
Are you s-s-sure you want to do that? Remember what happened *last* time...
Why don't you ever listen to us. We tried to warn you that you wouldn't *like* what the mirror had to say...
The lieutenant is right. It's the only way forward. Face yourself, kingsman!
"Just a moment, detective. Before we go, I'd like a word with you about this *side task* of yours..."
Stop. There's nothing else she can do for you, but this isn't the end of the line. No, there's one more kingsman to confront.
"But Measurehead said she knows the secret to turning back time."
The lieutenant considers the slumped form for a moment. He sighs.
"I don't understand why you're so set on what seems like a... *personal side-task*, but if you must, then let's get it over with..."
It's time to face yourself, mano y mano. The next time you find yourself alone before a mirror. *That's* where this will end...
What are you doing? This woman might be your only chance to figure out how to reverse time... Grow a pair!
No-no-no... you'll never figure out how to turn back time if you're not honest with her. Explain what's going on with you.
Whatever it is about this woman, it's connected to *time* -- she knows the way back.
"Great." The lieutenant concedes with a head shake. "He's figured out the pale. And now he's talking to everyone about it..."
"Actually, I haven't figured anything out yet..."
"You haven't? Why are you bringing up *pale* then?"
"I blacked out -- from the love I felt for my Motherland -- and lost all memory of the world."
"Like Gabriel Buenguerro in 'O Céu Dourado'..." She nods and smiles, unkindly. "You're the opposite of me then. I remember everything -- even the things I never knew."
"What *is* it?"
"Beautiful... it's beautiful."
That's the most you can get out of her -- only shapes and sensations, no dictionary definitions or scientific explanations...
"If you wait long enough, it's going to be much more than just 'love'... It's going to be the entire history -- vapourised."
"Everything is good here!"
"There's something here for everyone!"
"I let the goods do the talking."
"Step right up, mister!"
"You're *guaranteed* to find something exciting!"
"Astonishing quality! Unbelievable prices!"
"Deals so good you just *can't* pass this up!"
"I'm practically giving goods away here."
"Welcome to Revachol!" the rotund man announces. He has a lit cigarette between his fingers.
"Welcome to Revachol!" announces the rotund man. The remark isn't addressed to you. It’s addressed to the lieutenant.
"C'mon, man, I just said 'Welcome to Revachol'... It's a lorry driver thing."
"I know exactly what you meant. You think my *kind* doesn't belong here. That I should *watch myself* and *behave*."
The man bites his lip and drops the near-finished cigarette lingering between his fingers. He reaches for a new one.
"What are you hauling?"
"Not much anymore. I'm here to pick up some cargo, but the dockworkers are on strike, so... it's a sit-and-wait-on-your-ass situation."
"What kind of cargo are you supposed to pick up?"
"Apples."
"Wait, how long has this been going on then?"
"The strike? They've been at it for a while. A month, two months maybe?" He gestures towards the lorries. "But *this* here is just the last week or so."
"Apples" is exactly the kind of thing you'd say if you had something to hide...
"Sounds like a cover story to me."
"Fair enough. I got some other questions."
"I'm here to pick up a load of fuckin' apples, man. Just regular, Kojko-picked apples."
"Fine." He shrugs.
"So, lately we Occidentals have experienced an unfortunate downturn: when members of the superior race cease to believe in their innate superiority, they stop competing for resources."

"The problem? The damn kipts are showing a real good game lately! Same with the mesquitos. And all the other intruder species out there, breeding like rabbits. They're on the precipice of cultural victory."
"Okay, sure, whatever. I'd really rather talk about something else."
"Go right ahead." The man scratches his heavyset stomach. "You may be a cop, but that won't help you avoid the calamity to come."
"You just look at people and make arbitrary judgements."
"As arbitrary as any judgement. That doesn't make it less of a fact. We all have to use *facts*. Once you accept it, you'll gain the clarity of understanding."
"Yeah, they're a big deal. My great-grandfather was a carter. Had a royal license and everything. We've tried to hold on to our privileges."
"And that's a privilege?"
"Yeah. I think I can get down with racism."

"Good. If we, the Evening People, pull together -- we can form a bulwark against these troubled times!" The man grins at you. "Root out the forces that seek to undermine the well-being of our people."
"Let me see the soles of your boots."

dialoguetext: "Hello. Who are you?"
"Oh, I'm just a simple camionneur, a father of three, and a Revachol patriot."
"We're done for now." [Leave.]
"Looking for something?" The lorry driver recognizes you.
Lieutenant Kitsuragi's stern expression remains unchanged -- but you sense he can't be happy about this turn of events.
"Yeah, I'm *not* down with this -- why don't you go fuck yourself?"
"Don't push your luck, runt." The man gives you a disgusted look, then turns his attention elsewhere, ignoring your presence.
"Got a smoke?"
His physique reeks of heavy motor oils. His breath smells of high-tar content cigarettes. Probably *Astra Whites*.
"That's... disarmingly direct."
"What's a camionneur?" (Pretend you missed that last part.)
"A lorry driver. Who drives a lorry. Or is sometimes stuck in traffic jams, guarding that lorry."
"Just the truth." The man shrugs. "I'm a truth-teller, above all else."
"No."
"It's my last one."
"You're smoking one right now."
He's got a smoke right there, in his fucking hand! Snatch that shit out of his fat fingers! You need it after listening to his garbage.
"Then I'm gonna need the one you're smoking."
"Can't have it."
"Can I get a drag of that then?"
"You hiding smokes from me?"
"Why would I do that? I am an honest man." He puts out his cigarette and flicks the tiny stub toward the street.
"Sorry, all done." He puts out his cigarette and flicks the tiny stub toward the street.
"Hand it over. I'm confiscating it as evidence."
"But I really need it."
"Evidence of what? I haven't done anything." He puts out his cigarette and flicks the tiny stub toward the street.
"Fuck, I oughtta..."
"Oughtta what, officer?" The man looks at you coolly, noxious effluence wafting in the air around him.
Say nothing.
"Shit."
"Sorry I couldn't be of any help." He gives you an ambivalently mocking half-nod.
"That's too bad. It's all done for." He puts out his cigarette and flicks the tiny stub toward the street.
"Nothing worthwhile here." [Leave.]
"Oh, so they grow apples in... Graad?"
"Yup, it's one of their main exports. They grow 'em down south Yekokataa. A beautiful place, got great scenic vistas."
In fact, Yekokataa is a desolate wasteland whose name literally translates to *Zone of Ecological Catastrophe*. It features no scenic vistas and supports virtually no plant or animal life.
"Yekokataa is not in the south and they definitely don't grow apples there."
"So. Can I see the apples?"
"Well, I think we all learned something here." (Smile at the lorryman.)
"Fuckin' A, Kim. I've got your back." (Give the lieutenant a punch on the shoulder.)
"You keep saying 'Kojkos'. What does that actually mean?"
"You know: Graadniks. Graadvolk. The degenerates from Graad."
"Okay, but why the word 'Kojko'?"

You sense slight embarrassment for the outburst. Or is it pride? Impossible to tell.

"He's your man, alright. One-hundred percent. He's a lorryman selling his employer's stuff -- broke the seals on his Humanox lorry. No doubt he's selling drugs too."

"Not just the unions. He has peones *everywhere*. Some say he even has them in the RCM." He gets closer to him. "Dirty fucking peones who'd do *anything* for him. Multi-ethnic drug addicts..."

Say nothing.

The lieutenant adopts a rodentine quality. Be cool, sire. He's getting *into* this.

"Oh... I like expeditions, and I like you. I can give you..." He counts in his head. "... 10 reál."

It's just like *bus*, or *seagull* -- a kid watching out of a window describing things going by. He doesn't like it too much, but what do you do.

"What, only a fiver? You can't even buy a pack of Royal Extras with that -- let's make this one *stick*, my man."
"Alright, this should help you get back on your feet." He takes a ten-note from a leather pouch.
He looks you straight in the eye. "I hear you, officer," he agrees. "What kind of a sum are we talking about here?"
"It's an investment in me, a highly experimental human being. My risk/reward ratio is insane."
"It's an investment in your customer base. Gotta prime the pump, man!"
"A guy told me I need money to live, otherwise it's game over -- and I don't want to die."
"Okay, officer," he finally says, "I can't leave a man in need like that. How much do you need?"
"I don't think you really understand how bribes work, detective..." He looks at you, then the vendor.
"Sounds like a fair deal all around." He takes a ten-note from a leather pouch.
"One million reál."

The air between you becomes a little awkward as it becomes clear you don't know the first thing about bribes.

"Ten reál."

"One million reál."

"Ah, yes. Lots of cops are." The street vendor nods, dead-serious.
"You said I was a cool cop, but it's not very cool to freeze to death on a cold park bench."
"I guess it can't be any riskier than speculating in exotic derivatives... how much are we talking about here?"
"Fair point," he agrees, "You can't have a successful business without a loyal customer base. How much is your loyalty worth?"
"Are you trying to ask for a *bribe*? If so, you're not doing a very good job..." He looks at the vendor.
A bold move! Let's see if it pays off.

It feels great.
"One million reál."

After all this mess -- the broken seals, lying to you? C'mon!

"So, Siileng -- what's *your* stance on drugs?"
"Unless *you're* into drugs, of course -- in which case, drugs are *excellent*." He kisses his fingers. "Tasty-tasty drugs."
"Drugs?" For a moment he's unsure how to respond. "I don't go in for that, officer. Drugs ruin lives."

"I'm super into drugs."

"That's very cool. I don't like drugs, either. I only said I do because I didn't want to sound *lame*." He smiles. "Peer pressure."
"That's cool. Especially after you already said you're into them. All the coolest detectives in the movies do drugs *and* are very conflicted about it. Still -- no drugs here." He smiles.
"That's *even* cooler -- you investigating narcotics crimes like that. But --" he points to the goods. "I am not a lorry driver, I'm just a street vendor. I don't know anything about that."
A blatant lie, sire. Yet he tells it with such conviction. We'd believe him -- if we didn't know better.
"That's *so* cool -- you investigating the local drug trade like some cool Narc. But --" he points to the goods. "I am not a lorry driver, I'm just a street vendor. I don't know anything about that."
"*Who* said that? It's the fat racist, right? I bet it's him. He has an agenda against me, because I'm an immigrant who works harder than he does. He's a hater."
"So you admit you're a lorry driver?"
"So you admit you're a lorry driver."
"No! I just said I work harder and he's an asshole. I'm..." He stops to think.
Realizing he can't get out of it. Smart man.
"Okay, maybe I'm a lorry driver too -- a little. But that's not the most important thing about me, that's my day job. This is my *dream*." He spreads his arms.
"So you *forgot* to tell me?"
"So you were *embarrassed* to tell me?"
"Stop squirming. What do you know about the drug operation at the harbour?"
"No. I just forgot. It's such a small part of my life. It's in the rear view mirror now. I'm climbing out of that hole -- with ingenuity."
"Exactly! It's such a small part of my life. It's in the rear view mirror now. I'm climbing out of that hole -- with ingenuity."
"Siileng, my source tells me *you're* the one transporting drugs for the Union."
"No. That's insane... It's the fat hater! He's been eyeing me for a week and he sent you here. Maybe *he's* the one, huh? Have you thought about that?"
"Nothing, I told you. I'm not a dumb guy -- I don't get involved with that crowd. "
"Crowd -- you know? The drug crowd."
"Wait, what crowd?"
"And what *crowd* is that?"
There's more here. He's *afraid* of this crowd, whoever they are. More than he is of the racist lorryman.
No. He wasn't talking about an abstract crowd. It was *that crowd*.
"Who are you afraid of, Siileng?"
"It wasn't *some drug crowd*. You know who they are. Tell me now!"
"You're wasting my time. Tell me who the *fuck* is transporting the drugs here!"
He doesn't want to talk about them... he's *afraid*.
"Okay. If you don't know then I'll tell your employer you've been selling his stuff."
"Look..." He looks around and lowers his voice. "There's bad people doing *bad* things here -- that's all I know. Please don't get me into this mess, I've spent fifteen years working my way up..."

"Shush, please..." He looks around, then lowers his voice. "There's *bad* people doing *bad* things here -- that's all I know. Please don't get me into this mess, I've spent *fifteen* years working my way up..."
"No use -- he's not telling us. He's too afraid. We need to take him to my station and ask him there. *After* we've called his boss."

"Okay, look..." He looks around and lowers his voice. "There's *bad* people here. Doing *bad* things. That's all I know. Please don't get into this mess. I've been Revachol for *fifteen* years, working my way up..."
Here we go. There's a *tiny bit* of truth on the table. Zoom in on it.
"If you don't want to get into this mess..." (Raise your voice) "You HAVE to give us a REASON to move on."
"We're buddies, Siileng. Help us out. No one will know it was you."
"It's a *she*, okay?" he whispers. "The other drivers call her the *lady driver*. You're better off staying away from her -- the way they talk about her..." He shakes his head. "She's no lady."
"Who are these 'other drivers' who talk?"
"Is the lady driver the old woman back there?" (Point to the Paledriver.) "Dazed out, *strange*?"
"Okay. We're cool now." (Conclude.)
"All of them, I don't know. I told you all I know. Are we cool now? I really want us to be cool now."
"All of them. Even the ones who've left. I don't hang out with them, I don't remember who has tattoos."
"Who *exactly* is talking about this lady-driver of yours? The racist? Or the other one, with the tattoos?" He points north.
"I don't know... maybe? If she is, I haven't gone near her. I don't get *involved*, I told you."
"All right!" He snaps back to his act. "Very cool. Let's cap this off with a *purchase*. A pair of funky sunglasses, detective. You deserve it! And *I* deserve it too, don't you think?"
He's *aching* to get back to his usual shtick. All this whispering is bad for business.
"She? Where is she? I haven't yet met a woman on the roundabout."
"There's one by the statue of that king." He points towards the roundabout. "I haven't gone near her. And I *won't* either."
"The third driver," he nods. "We haven't talked to her yet. Where exactly is she -- near the horseback monument?"

"Aye, officer." A woman in a rain coat stands on the quay, considering an overturned boat. A sword in a scabbard hangs from her hip.
"Be seeing you." [Leave.]
"Aye, the sea's gonna calm down soon. I can feel it. The wind is turning southeast." She nods. "What's on your mind, officer?"
"Sure is. *The Sun* I call her. Coated with a fresh layer of tar just yesterday. It'll take some time for it to dry, assuming the sunny days continue."
"Anything I can help you with?"
"And go where? The fish are plentiful here and we get enough orders to get by. It's not great, but it's something."
"Unfortunately, the factory sold this one with a three-year warranty instead of a story." She smiles at her own joke. "It's to intimidate folks, mostly."
"It's a regular mass-produced sword, like a shovel or an axe. Nothing fancy, just for intimidation."
"Sometimes I also walk the beach to see what the sea has given up. The sea is full of surprises."
"Wood. Pieces of glass. Every once in a while we see dead bodies -- human, animal, fish, other odd sea creatures. A mine washed ashore, once..."

"Don't have any," she replies with a shrug. "Those get cleaned out so fast even the local bums can only stand by and watch with watery mouths. Always by strangers too. Union folk don't stand this kind of stuff around here."
"Hold on... do you know how to use it?"
"Not really." She glances at the blade. "I know some basic moves and I know it sure as hell beats a knife, when you're in a tough spot."

"From time to time people need a lesson in respect. That's just the way it is. Back in the day I caught the eyes of many men and believe me," she adds, tittering, "men need a lesson in manners from time to time."
"Why don't more women arm themselves if it's so effective?"
"What makes you think we haven't?" She smiles. "Heh. The truth is that almost everyone in this life is scared and tired and stupid and too *dull* for that."
"Behold!" (Point to *The Expression* on your face.)
Her eyes meet yours and suddenly she starts laughing. It's hoarse. As if she hasn't laughed in a while.
"Sure." Her face straightens. "It looks as if you could face-down any horror in the world with that same unchanging grin. It's like a shield."
"Nice sword." (Point at the sabre on her hip.) "Does it come with a story?"
"What do you do around here?"
"That's my motor carriage in the sea by the way." (Point to the sunken vehicle.)
She needs to go on a date with *another* drunk. Badly.

"Gone."
"I've questions. The first is -- what's your name?" (Move on.)
"As always, I am... the Lawbringer."
"That depends. Where are we exactly?"
"You've graduated to *Lawbringer* now?"
"The name is Lilienne. People call me Net Picker." She gestures toward the fishnets. "I think I have time for questions. What are the other ones?"
"A fishing village. On the seashore." She looks around. "This place doesn't really have a name. It's sometimes called... *Illisible*."
"I'm good." [Leave.]
She whistles quietly, picking at the fishnet at her feet. The wind ruffles her hair.
"Are you now?" She smirks. "There are a lot of lawbringers around Martinaise, but not a lot of law."
"This place looks bad. Why don't you leave?"
"It *is* imposing." (Nod.)
"Why do you need intimidation tactics?"
"Isn't that what guns are for?"
"Guns are expensive... and fragile. I think." She shrugs. "Besides, I got kids. Can't have guns around them and sometimes a sharp blade is enough to keep folks at bay."
"Figures. Typical patriarchal nonsense, mascu-venomosity."
"So where are all the men now?" (Proceed.)
"Some went to patch their wounds, their lesson learned, others were more thick-headed..." She looks down. "And one of them I ended up marrying."
"Ugh... sure. Venomosity." She nods. "But boys will be boys and god knows we don't have many around. So far the sword has been enough to keep them in line."
"Where's your husband now?"
"Gone where?"
"To the waves." Her eyes stop in yours. "The sea took him. It was a long time ago."
"I'm a proper man. Believe me."
"That goes for men too, but they put on an act for us. Pretend like everything's good and living in shit doesn't bother them. Like anyone falls for that."
"Oh..." She shakes her head, smiling faintly. "Believe *me*, everyone here is a 'proper' man. Must be something about poverty that makes all the men *real*."
"Wait, why? If they're thick-headed..."
"Guess I enjoyed the way he bled." Her expression doesn't change. It's hard to say if it's a joke.

"Gone? Coward! I would never leave anyone."
"He disappeared? Sounds like a missing persons case."
"It absolutely does not," the lieutenant quietly interjects. "We are *not* going to look for him."
"No, no. There's nothing to find. He's dead. Lost to the waves."
"Uh..." She raises an eyebrow. "Good for you. He, however, was lost to the waves. It's been quite a while now."
"That's bad... What happened?"
"Oh..." Say no more. Wait for her to continue.
"He died? Was he... murdered?"
The lieutenant shakes his head again.
The harbour seawall endures the wash of the freezing waves. Many things wash up against it and onto the beaches of Revachol. Some inanimate, some just no longer alive... You shudder.
She refuses?! But your word is the *law*. *You* are LAW!
"Like I said, fish, mostly. Sail the waves, take care of the kids. Pick nets... right now I'm tarring a little skiff."
"What else?"
"Is that enough to make a living?"
"I sell the fish to people in the Delta to serve at their fancy restaurants. Authentic Insulindian cuisine."
"Interesting. What have you found?"
"I never thought the sea brought in anything particularly interesting."
"Alright, I think I get it. Let me ask you something else."
"Bottles. Drugs, also. Lost cargo in general." She looks at the beach. "But most of the time, it's just wood and glass."
"I need to know about those human bodies."
"Drugs? I need info on this. Major narc." (Point to yourself.)
"Well, you're barking under the wrong tree then, officer." She shakes her head. "I have no interest in floaters. Seen enough of them in my life already. A very unattractive bunch."
"A mine? The RCM could use a mine. Where is it?"

"Well, the RCM has to wait for another one, cause some army folks came by, took it in the middle of the bay and blew it up." She spits over the railing. "The blast was surprisingly timid for such a huge spiky thing."
You could use a hit right about now. Any hit really. Feel that itch in your hands, the stiffness of your neck? That strange *restlessness* in your bones?
"Walking on the beach. Sounds quite... romantic."
"Oh, very." She laughs. "Finding pieces of glass, bits of wood. Every once in a while we get dead bodies -- human, animal, fish, other sea creatures. A mine washed ashore, once..."
"What else?" She looks at the beach. "Bottles. Drugs, also. Lost cargo in general. But most of the time, it's just wood and glass. *Very* romantic."
"Oh..." she looks at the pointed direction. "That's good to know, I guess. Why is it in the sea?"

"People imagine picking up and finding *something better* is an easy solution. But how is that supposed to work, when all your time and energy goes to staying alive? You have almost nothing to set aside to actually fight your way out."
"Anywhere with better opportunities."
"You just gotta follow the work, that's where the money sleeps."
"Just, somewhere..." (Close your eyes.) "Away from all this sadness."
"Is that your boat?" (Point at the overturned boat.)

"Exactly." She tries to smile and reaches in her net. "I don't mean to complain about my sad pauper life. We do manage alright. We're tough people here."

"I don't mean to complain about my pauper life. We are warm and fed here and..." She smiles faintly and plucks some seaweed out of the net. "I don't know, there's just something about this shit hole."

She's making a joke. Her voice softens.

"Everyone does that, in a way. You don't have to get shot for that." She waves her hand dismissively.
"What happened to you anyway? We heard gunshots from the town. They were closer than usual."
"Officer, what happened? You're limping. Why are you limping? You look terrible."
"Officer Harry... you're wounded. Why are you wounded? You look terrible."
"Is this from the shooting in town?" She's not letting it go that easy. "We heard gunshots. Not that we don't hear gunshots all the time, but they were closer than usual."
"There was an exchange of fire on Rue de Saint-Ghislaine. It's nothing to be worried about, ma'am."
"Of course, ma'am. It's only for a day or two -- official police business."
"That won't be a problem. It's windstill -- and the tar just dried." She points to her skiff next to the jetty. "We've got two days of *relative* sunshine ahead."
"Can I borrow your boat?"
"What's on that island?"
"Thank you, I'll use your skiff to get there then."
"I need to get to that island." (Point to it.)
"I dodged the second shot. I can also get *not shot*."
"I also got shot in the chest." (Point to your chest.)
"You should see the other guys. They're all dead."
"I have a question for you." (Conclude.)
"Well, good for you." She smiles.
"Officer Harry, what happened? You're limping. Why are you limping? You look terrible."
"Officer, what happened? You're wounded. Why are you wounded? You look terrible."
"It's nothing."
"Doesn't look like nothing. Looks like you got banged up real good."
"That's nothing to brag about, officer."
"It's not serious. He'll be okay."
You feel the ligament move on your left shoulder. And a small, warm drip of blood. It's nothing.
"So you're a killer." She nods solemnly. "That's good, I guess. I guess... Better than being dead."
"Most cops are killers."
"I'm not a killer, I'm a cop."
Scoff in a masculine manner.
"Aye, I bet they are. The good ones at least."

She just looks at you, her tea-length skirt flapping in the wind.
"Of course. Can I help you with something?"
"I was a killer long before this happened."
"Aye." She nods solemnly. "Not a lot of RCM men who aren't killers."
"Aye." She nods solemnly. "I've always taken you for one, that's for sure. Not a lot of RCM men who aren't killers."
"I'm sad to hear that. Take care of that with ether, will you? Don't get too many RCM men around here. Be sad to lose the first one."
"If you promise to bring it back. And no scraping the hull -- I just got it nice and yellow. And *no* drinking on the boat." Her eyes narrow. "And no joyriding, either."
"Aye," she nods.
Nod along attentively.
"What if I wanna rock?"
"See, that makes me not want to lend you my skiff. On a boat, *rocking* leads to capsizing. That there is an absolutely one-hundred percent *rock-free* skiff, you got that?"
The crow's feet disappear from the corners of her eyes, as she smiles at you.

"Mhm, used to be some kind of fortification there before the war -- for the communards. An anti-aircraft gun, I think. Bombed to bits in the landing... I haven't been there myself -- always steered clear of it."
"Two days of sunshine? I just got a bacterial infection."
"Is there anything I should know about getting there?"
"Well -- most of it's sunken. Underwater. That means concrete under water -- cut your boat if you're not careful. Be sure to enter from the south side, water's deep there."
"Who *has* been there?"
"My husband used to drink there. Him and his drinking buddies. Always seemed like a bad place to drink to me. People died there during the landing, you know, my mother told me..."
She looks around. "The kids sometimes go there too, I know they do -- on rafts. I tell them not to but they bring back old bullet casings and such."
"Which kids?"
"The twins." She points to the two kids playing on the concrete yard. "God forbid they bring the girl along on some rickety barge."

"Nothing, just ruins. Used to be some kind of fortification there before the war, for the communards. An anti-aircraft gun, I think. Bombed to bits in the landing... I haven't been there myself -- always steered clear of it."

"You said you haven't been there *yourself* -- who has then? If not you?"
"The twins." She points to the two kids playing on the concrete yard. "God forbid they bring the girl along on a rickety barge."
"Which kids?"
"Hundreds. Maybe thousands even..." She looks around. "The kids sometimes go there too, I know they do. On barges. I tell them not to but they bring back old bullet casings and such."
"My husband used to drink there. Him and his drinking buddies. Always seemed like a bad place to drink to me. People died there during the landing, you know -- my mother told me..."
She nods. "Please be conservative with the fuel, will you? I just filled her up, but it's a small tank."
"Be careful out there. Sea's calm as death, but still... there are ruins underwater. You can scrape the paint... or worse."
"I don't want a funeral. I *hate* death."
"Holding a funeral doesn't mean you love death. Don't be childish. You're a police officer..."
"I don't think they have funerals for motor carriages."
"What an... odd thought. Maybe I should."
