"*You* made me do this. You did this to yourself."
"Phe... whht... fuuh..." The disoriented twelve year old is trying to get his bearings.
"*Taivaan tähden*, you killed Cuno!"
"Fucked your shoulder, fucked your knee, fucked your fat body up!" the one behind the fence hisses like a lit fuse ready to go off from delight.
You can almost hear the gears rattling -- a change in set decorations.
"I told you not to tempt such forces." The annoyance in his voice is directed at you, not the gremlins.
"Cuno knows to respect that violent shit. You should see Cuno's dad -- Cuno's dad doesn't give a shit about *anything*," he declares with pride.
Say nothing, try to hold it together.
Everything about her is saying *Wow -- what a man*. Her admiration is fuelled by camaraderie.
"Do you have any idea of the shit you just got yourself into, kid?" (Get up.)
"Okay, pig. Talk to Cuno. We're back in this shit." He brushes the dirt off his pants. "The fuck do you want?"
"Cuno can't believe this shit!" It's like he's now realized he has super-powers. "Can *no one* stop the Cuno?!"
"Cuno's just gonna beat the shit out of you again." He is clearly still in awe of himself right now.
Cunoesse is staring at Cuno with pride-filled eyes, almost forgetting your presence.
"Cuno beat the shit out of popo!" The kid is laughing so hard, tears are running down his freckled cheeks. "Beat your fucking knee off."
"Yeah, laugh it up. Let's just get back to it." (Get up.)
"Okay! Everybody calm down."
"You lost control," says the lieutenant, breaking his silence. "You need to get yourself together."
"No, officer -- you did this," says the lieutenant, breaking his silence. "Get yourself together."
"Officer, this is very far from normal police conduct," says the lieutenant, breaking his silence. "Get yourself together."
Cuno *feels* it; this was no light tap.
"Who's doing a *sick charade* now?"
"You are, officer," says the lieutenant, breaking his silence. "Get yourself together."
For heaven's sake, he thinks, this has gone too far. Don't make this any worse than it is -- just get back to questioning the kid.
The lieutenant doesn't appreciate your *sick charades* on his crime scene. His opinion of you has lessened.
For heaven's sake, he thinks, this has gone too far. Don't make it worse -- just get back to questioning the kid.
He gets it, you lost it. Just don't dig the hole any deeper.
It's safe to say he *did not* establish dominance over you.
If this act was about him trying to establish dominance over you, it's safe to say things didn't go as he'd planned.
The creature behind the fence has fallen ominously silent. Only her eyes are alive, jumping from actor to actor.
She understands: The battle for the control over Cuno is a battle of madness against madness. For the time being, her madness has proven less potent.
Interesting. This tug of war has probably happened between her and Cuno's violent father too.
"Ouch, my arm... and my fucking *knee*..."
"Yeah, I deserved this."
"Stop laughing!"
"Kim, help me up!"
"No."
The creature behind the fence makes it a point to laugh even harder.
"Someone call an ambulance, I think I really hurt myself!"
"Officer, you need to get up. This is turning into a farce."
"That's what you get if you fuck with the Cuno. You get fucked up."
It's a dry laugh. Mirthless. She's not even actually enjoying this. She only wants to hurt you.
"Cuno made you his fuck-gimp!" He bursts into a violent fit of laughter. Sounds like a flock of seagulls taking flight.
The lieutenant isn't laughing. At all.
"Pig, Cuno thought you had this. What happened? Cuno can do *anything* now." He's writhing with joy, like the power you gave him is too much to take.
Get a hold of yourself. At least the previous horror is over. At least they're no longer...
It's not as bad as it feels. You've maybe pulled a joint; the indignity makes it worse.
Try really, *really* hard to hold it together.
"Pig's tryin' not to cry. Cuno can't believe this shit!" It's like he's now realized he has super-powers. "Can *no one* stop the Cuno?!"
"Pig's biting down on his knuckles. Cuno can't believe this shit!" It's like he's now realized he has super-powers. "Can *no one* stop the Cuno?!"
Stay with me, the biting is having *some* kind of effect, the pain is receding...
"Yeah, you deserve this. Trying to show your dick to Cuno. Cuno was scared."
Oh god, do something quick, they're gonna start *that* again!
"Now how about we go and do something worth the public's time?"
He gets it. You lost. Now walk away with what remains of your dignity.
You lost. Now walk away with what remains of your dignity.
"Look, f*g..." Cuno whispers, even softer than before, vanishingly silent...
"Look, f*g..." Cuno whispers as you retreat, vanishingly silent...
"I know you wanted to hit me..." He lets it linger. "You got that 'I'm gonna fuck that Cuno up' look that Cuno's dad gets. The murder look... the rage look..."
"Yes, how do I get back to it? I wanna go back to that thought!"
"Yes, but I didn't act on it. It was just a fantasy."

"No!"
"It's good you said that -- here it is! Here we go... Cuno likes this..." He starts prancing around again, tongue lolling out of his mouth...
"Yes. No. I've changed my mind again."
Relax, he can't read your mind. He doesn't know you were thinking that.
There's a dead body, remember? That's what you were doing here. You're a cop on a case.
"Why don't we get back to the interview, Cuno."
"I know what you thought: 'I'm gonna fuck that Cuno up, I'm gonna shut that shit down...' You know what? You should've, because now..." He raises he's voice again.
For emphasis. A *ghost* is saying this. A shit-eating psychopathic ghost with an ace up his sleeve.
"You're NOTHING! You're a joke to Cuno. Cuno LAUGHS at you!" He spreads his arms, taking dominion over the yard. "KING CUNO!"
"Cuno turned you into his prison bitch! You're gonna be *in* this shit with Cuno..."
"No." The lieutenant almost rolls his eyes. "You're not. We can just leave..."
"Bitch, you're gonna be in this shit with Cuno *forever*!" The pipo-headed critter doesn't let him finish.
A pipo is a type of hat by the way.
"Whatever. I had some questions about the crime scene."
[Leave.]
"I can." His voice is so silent, it seems the words are echoing in your head, not coming from his lips. "Cuno can smell that violence shit. I know what you were thinking..."
"'I'm gonna fuck that Cuno up. I'm gonna shut his shit down...' You know what? You should have hit the Cuno, because NOW..." He raises his voice again.
"Nice pipo."
"You don't talk to me about my fucking pipo! You don't know where I come from. You're just Cuno's bottom bitch."
It's safe to say he has established dominance over you.
The whole charade was about establishing dominance over you. It's safe to say he has succeeded.
The whole charade was about establishing dominance over you. You backing up means he's succeeded.
Backing up was a bad idea, now he thinks he's established dominance over you.
"Okay, Cuno is kind to his bitch. Ask your questions, but remember." He taps at his temporal lobe. "This *changes* shit."
"*Click*, *click*, *click*, *click*" goes the little pipo-wearing asshole behind the fence.
Meaning, there's been a change in some kind of evil clockwork. There will be *consequences*.
"Oh no, you pussied out again. Shouldn't have done that, Cuno's gonna bitch you out now. Cuno's gonna *sub let* you..." He raises his voice again.
"Pass you around like Candy, fat boy! Pass your fat ass AROUND!" He spreads his arms, taking dominion over the yard. "KING CUNO!"
"Don't listen to the blind fuck, piggo, you're doing the right thing here, trying to get Cuno to like you again." He pauses to think.
"I've come to ask questions -- I still have a case to solve."
"Look, C, it's the fucking war-pig! Try not to knock yourself out, f****t!"
"Have you come to make your offering to Cuno?"
"Look, you're on my crime scene. I can't have uncooperative civilians here."
"Whoah-whoah!" The boy hovers in your face. "What's this psycho shit? You gonna pretend like nothing happened?"
A material offering is implied. He wants *stuff*. Only stuff can make it okay again.
"Cool what? What the fuck is wrong with you?"
"I think you broke his brain when you fucked him up, Cuno."
"You lost your shit in the booth, tried to beat a confession out of Cuno... and pissed yourself?"
"That's right, Cuno. You're right." The sycophantic pipo-wearing pup behind the fence agrees.
"What, do you think Cuno's fucking *eighty years old*? Tryin'a bring me bum juice... make the Cuno paranoid!"
"Why?"
"You don't like alcohol?"
"Okay then."
"Just because you get high off that shit doesn't mean Cuno has to fuck himself with that fermented," -- he points at the bottle -- "piss and shit mix."
"Tryin'a get a get a twelve year old hooked on the shit-shake..." He looks like he can't believe your depravity.
"Hmh..." the lieutenant mumbles optimistically. "Alcohol use *has* been declining in the under 16 bracket this past decade..."
This pleases him.
The lieutenant's opinion of you has *definitely* lowered.
"You don't need to. He doesn't know anything."
"Oh, Cuno knows. Cuno knows shit," he squints at you. "Expensive shit. Mysterious shit. *Killer* shit."
He does not know *killer* related shit, sire. It's a falseness. He *may* know mysterious shit, however... it's hard to tell.
"See? He could know something. So how about it, Cuno?" (Shake the pack of cigarettes at the boy.)
Historical revisionism has taken place.
The wide grin above his clenched jaw agrees. His heavy breathing, his dilated pupils, it all speaks of one thing -- this was a really good idea!
He *really* likes this. This motor lorry shit makes Cuno happy. You could say you interfaced with his good side.
"Check out this bizarre drug I found." (Show him the pyrholidon.)
"No, you don't." He stops you. "No one is *checking out* anything. Put that away."
"Not this *dreamer* shit again..." Cuno slaps his face. "Why do Cuno's bitches always try and bring Cuno that lame sha-la-la-la-bang shit? Cuno's not a fucking witch doctor!"
"No, I didn't..." The adolescent is momentarily disoriented. "It's fucking *Cuno*. Say it right, bitch, say it like it's said."
"It was only once..." The little rat isn't having it. "And you fucking asked me to nick it, *Kuuno*!"
Kuuno. That's an Oranjese name.
"Anyway." He mentally props himself back up. "Cuno doesn't do that radioactive shit. Makes Cuno's dick fall off. Cuno's got a huge dick."
A pretty *lame* oranjese name. Nowhere near *Cuno*... The thought crosses your mind and then it's gone. Perhaps something for later?
"Bitches slapping each other, fighting for Cuno's attention. Cuno likes this pole dancing shit -- but it's not good enough." He crosses his hands.
"What a fucking pooper..." Cuno points at his heart. "Bitch doesn't have the pump for it. Old bitch, pump's bust. Cuno has the pump for it. Cuno has a giant pump."
Don't ruin it for Cuno. Can't you see Cuno's pump can still take it? Can still pump the good.
What the *fuck* are you talking about? Those are barely words. Anyway... this didn't work.
"Whatever then."
[Leave.]
"Nothing, lieutenant. I don't want to get into this." [Leave.]
"This is probably too lame for you, Cuno, but maybe you know someone..." (Hold out the *Hjelmdallerman* book.)

"Cuno knows this four-eyed fuck, totally hooked on the book, can't get enough of this shit. Fucking sad really... Cuno could make mad money off him, exploit his disease."
"Who are you talking about, Cuno?"
"A guy Cuno knows!" He shouts at the fence. "Martin. From out of town. From Graad or some shit."
This boy of twelve does not know anyone from Graad, sire. We suspect the boy himself might be this mystery 'Martin'.
"You don't know anyone from Graad. You want it for yourself, don't you?"
"So you want the book?"
"Fine... Cuno's gonna take it off your fat ass. At least he's gonna make some paper off this shit..." He eagerly pockets the book. "Now, what do you want?"
"Fine... Cuno's gonna take it off your fat ass. At least he's gonna make some paper off this shit..." He eagerly pockets the book. "Now, what do you want?"

"Shove that shit in your fat ass and stop wasting Cuno's time if you ain't got anything to offer to the Cuno."
"Actually I wanna keep the book."
He's disappointed by your change of heart.
FUCK THAT. Confront him.
"Shitload, pig, what's your question?"
"You're testing Cuno's patience here."
"Get lost, f****t!"
"More on this later. Right now let's talk about something else."
"Don't tell the pig shit, Cuno!"
This is where you *quickly* ask him questions. Real cop-questions. Like a cop.
"Fucking idiot *mulkkupää* doesn't know any questions."
"I don't have questions."
(Whisper.)  "Kim, help me out here. What do we want to know?"
"If I were to want to waste my time -- which I do not -- I would ask them who he is, how he got there, and the *usual*."
"Pig's choking, he's totally choking!"
"Just a lone pig trying to sugar-talk some kids. That seems pretty fucking suspicious to Cuno."
"Do you know how it got up there?"
"Probably climbed? Cuno was busy *down the road* when that shit went down."
"Told you, pig bacon. Cuno doesn't do regional. Cuno's been to places you wouldn't dream of."
"You didn't really leave the city. Where were you?"
"You heard Cuno -- Cuno wasn't even in Martinaise. Cuno wasn't in Revachol." He puffs himself up. "Cuno wasn't *regional*."

dialoguetext: "So you didn't see it happening?"
"Where's the rest of his armour?"
"Have you seen anyone suspicious around?"
"Just a couple of pigs sniffing around in the dirt. That seems pretty fucking suspicious to Cuno."
"Yeah, you tell the *fägäri*, Cuno!"

The lieutenant is sitting on the edge of his bed, twenty kilometres from here, and cleaning his boots. An archetypal policeman like him would *definitely* come up with some questions to ask right now. Unlike you, standing here alone, unable to gather your thoughts.
"Do you know who he was?"
"Oh, okay. Where did you go then?"
The usual being "have you seen anything out of the ordinary" or "have you seen anything suspicious"?
Stop choking or everyone will see you're a fake! All this *thespianism* isn't doing you any good!
The kids are overwhelming you. Regain control of yourself and the situation.
"I don't know, some fucking..." He looks around, trying to come up with something.
"Mesque, or... or I don't know. Some other place... Night City! Cuno was in fucking Night City."
There is no Night City anywhere. That sounds like the name of a city in some pulp science fiction novel.
"That's a fictional city name. Night City doesn't exist."
"Where is Night City?"
"Why you gotta be riding Cuno's ass? You haven't been where Cuno's been. You haven't been in Cuno's head."
The city's too large for him to have left. But he wasn't *here* either... So where was he?
"You wanna know where Cuno was? You wanna know what Cuno's been fucking *up* to?"
"Don't tell him that Cuno, it's lame!"
"It's not fucking lame! Cuno's building Cuno's city -- Night City, Rage City, the City of Rage. That's it. And it's not lame!"
What the hell *is* it about then? A city of toys? No, with this kid, it's probably made of cigarette butts. Or maybe sand and melting snow?
This is a minor discovery. Don't let this Night City business clog up your mind. Proceed with your investigation. If it's really important, it will come up later.
"That's the name of Cuno's city, bitch! Get the fuck off Cuno's back. This shit ain't about that."
Looks like you're a *fägäri* now, whatever that means. The *suspicious* question doesn't really work in antagonistic situations.
"There are contusions all over his body. Did you do that?"
"Fuck are you talking about? What is this *con-tush-on* shit?" He grabs his head like it's suddenly hurting.
"He says you're *stupid*, Cuno! They want to make you stupid again!"
"A contusion is a bruise. I'm talking about the marks your stones left on the corpse."
"I hate words too."
"Oh, did Cuno make your shit-sniffing harder? Obstruction of shit-sniffing?" He lets go of his head, suddenly feeling better. "This is Cuno's Kingdom. Cuno fucking rules here."
He's thinking the kid has amassed quite the vocabulary of law-enforcement terms. But he's not going to stick his nose into this.
"Hmmm..." you hear the lieutenant hum.
"Me and my partner are wondering, where did you pick up so many police terms?"
Proceed with the questioning.
"Me and *my* partner are wondering..." The demonic hiss behind the fence gets louder. "Do you guys puff Peter?"
Cuno erupts into laughter, pointing his finger at you, then Kim, then back at you...
An unfortunate choice of words, the lieutenant from Precinct 57 thinks. He looks downwind at the rotting corpse. He could use a cigarette right about now.
An unfortunate choice of words, the lieutenant from Precinct 57 thinks. He looks at the harbour walls looming overhead. He could use a cigarette right about now.
Good. That's what the lieutenant from Precinct 57 would have done as well.
"Words are fucking shit, make you stupid!" He spits on the ground. "Cuno's got his own words now -- Cuno-words."
Has Cuno been to some kind of school? Probably a school for children with behavioural difficulties.
"Cuno, shouldn't you be at school or something?"
"I have behavioural difficulties too."
Better not to mention it.
"Watch out, Cuno, he's trying to relate to you!"
"That's the past, pig. Cuno's not *there* anymore. Cuno did his time." He nods solemnly. "Now ask about that pig corpse shit and don't go sniffing into Cuno's past!"
"Pigs come to take you back, Cuno!" the hat-wearing fiend shrieks. "Tryin'a dig up dirt on you!"
"Cuno doesn't give a shit about your handicap. Get a wheelchair or something. Cuno doesn't care."
It's tough to tell, but he actually does... a little. He tilts his head to the right, reassessing you in the light of your bad ass learning disability.
How is that better? At least get back to the corpse then.
"Cuno's fuck-gimp." He picks up a rock. "Cuno uses the fuck-gimp for target practice."
He's trying to hide the fact that he doesn't know.
"So you don't know anything."
"I meant who he *was*. Before he died?"
"Cuno knows all kinds of shit. Cuno's not a snitch, that's all." He shakes his head, clearly offended. "Tryin'a make the Cuno sing into the popophone..."
"Cuno knows what you meant. Cuno's not a snitch, that's all." He shakes his head, clearly offended. "Tryin'a make Cuno sing into the popophone..."
He could've just said he doesn't know.
"Cuno *knows* shit. Cuno's not a snitch, that's all." He shakes his head, clearly offended. "Tryin'a make Cuno sing into the popophone..."
"You could've just said you don't know."
"Okay."
"Yeah it's fucking okay!" He throws the rock. It misses. "Gotta have a gimp for rock practice..."
"Don't ask the pigs for permission, Cuno. Don't ask the pigs for shit!"
"Okay. About the dead body..."
"Yeah? Cuno didn't smoke him, if that's what you mean." He draws snot up his nose.
Thanks, Cuno. That's one name you can now cross off the list.
"Let's back up. This isn't going anywhere."
The buck-toothed gremlin lets go of his head. Looks like the attack has passed.
The pain of the word recedes, he's feeling better now. Further away from *education*.
"Cuno gives this info out on a need-to-know basis. And *you* don't need to know." He draws snot up his nose. "Cuno didn't smoke the gimp, if that's what you meant."
"Lame!"
It's impossible to deduce what it *is* about, at least for the moment. If it's important, it'll come up later. Focus on the case.
"Yes, that's what I'm saying. You're stupid."
Cuno lets go of his head. "Get the fuck out of here, calling Cuno stupid? Pigs come to Cuno for guidance, then say he's stupid? The fuck is up with that?"
"They're lost without you, Cuno! They need you. You're in control of this!"
"Why don't you figure your shit out yourself -- before you come to *Detective Cuno* for help?"
"Hmmm... maybe we should." The lieutenant raises an eyebrow.
Got told by a twelve-year old. Here's a tip for the future: If you wanna win an argument, wait for my sign. Don't just go barging in.
"Cuno's fuck-gimp's got one big thing wrong with him. He's a fucking mutant."
"Shoot that shit at Cuno."
"How come?"
"Okay, another question then."
"Cuno doesn't give a shit about the armour."
"A mutant?"
"Look at him!" He points to the body. "Fucking growth hormone shit. He's a giant. The armour's too big for *any man*."
Oh, come on. He's just pretending that he doesn't care because he's too small for the armour.
He drills his temples with his fingers in some strange, aggressive gesture. "Cuno doesn't give a shit about that freak armour. Cuno threw that shit away."
"You're just too small for the armour."
"What do you mean you *threw it away*?"
"You threw it in the sea?"
"Who do you mean, troubadour?"
"Get the fuck out of here, tryin'a fuck on me with that midget shit? Cuno's twelve! He's huge!" He squints at you.
"What are you... fucking eighty? When Cuno's eighty, Cuno can fit four of you in Cuno! Fuck outta here!"
"Trying to fuck on Cuno? Fuck outta here!"
"Cuno tried to get the helmet on. It was too big." He performs a kick-off on the imaginary helmet.
"Cuno kicked that shit in the sea. Rugby style. That shit means *nothing* to Cuno."
"Yeah, that shit means *nothing* to Cuno," he repeats. "Cuno doesn't give a shit about material shit. Cuno's a fucking monk!"
"You wanna fuck on someone 'bout that armour? Go fuck the moustached Union fuck -- the jolly troubadour shit at the gates."
"Yeah, Cock-in-Boots. You know that jolly Union cow fucker? Came around talking about cows or some shit. Came around pretendin' like he cares about cows."
Yes, you met him at the gates. The one with the boots and the jolly smile.
He means Mañana, the laid-back striker at the gates.

"So yeah, he's the one you wanna talk to. He's fucking crazy about that armour shit. Coming here, pretending like he likes cows, tryin'a catch a peep at Cuno's armour... Go to the gates -- ask him yourself."
"You mean Mañana?"
"Yeah, he's the one you wanna talk to. He's fucking crazy about that armour shit. Coming here, pretending like he likes cows, tryin'a catch a peep at Cuno's armour."
Curious, my liege. Why did Cuno feed you this information?
"And you're just telling me this out of the kindness of your heart, Cuno?"
Let it be.
"Yeah, Cuno's doing charity today. Cuno Day. Cuno feels *sorry* for you two loser-pigs. Cuno's doing pity now."
Yes, pray pardon, sire! Better to let it be. I did not mean to make you paranoid.
Still, seems suspicious... He may have it in for that guy. Or you may be paranoid. That is also a possibility, sire.
"Yeah, Cuno's doing charity today. Cuno Day. Cuno feels *sorry* for you, loser-pig. Cuno's doing pity now."
"The fuck about it?"
"Fucking Mesque, or I don't know. Some other place... Night City! Cuno was in fucking Night City."
"Do you remember how he looked?! Fucking growth hormone shit. He's a giant. The armour's too big for *any man*."
He drills his temples with his fingers in some strange, aggressive gesture. "Cuno doesn't give a shit about that freak armour. Cuno threw that shit away."
You have no idea what the *usual* is. Just ask whatever comes to mind.
End of conversation. Very strong. You should be this stoic.
Yes. This troubadour has it. You can *feel* it.
"Remember Night City, pig fuck? Cuno was in fucking Night City getting shit *done*."
"What the fuck, Cuno! Stop being so fucking lame!"
By killing in his territory, someone has *openly challenged* Cuno. It's in his best interest to put them in their place.
"Yes, I see it. The big tall one behind you."
"You mean the Doomed Commercial Area?"
"Fine, Cuno... *Don't* help me then." (Back off.)
"You gotta get in that shit." He points again. "In there *deep*."
"Whatever, don't fuck back at the Cuno." He makes a sudden discarding motion. "You gotta get *in* that shit. In there deep."
"I was in there already."
"Ah, I didn't check the basement when I was there..."
"And you didn't notice the fucking *ice bear* fridge?" The kid scoffs. "Pig, you need a new pair of eyes. This is fucking embarrassing."
"You didn't hear it from Cuno, pig." He looks at you seriously. "But don't forget where you heard it from."
"Cuno knows all kinds of shit. Cuno gets *around*."
"I've lost almost everything, Cuno. My memory, my money, even my name... I *can't* lose my job too! Please, PLEASE help me..."
"Listen to Cuno -- *always* check the basement." He nods solemnly and crosses his arms. "Cuno always checks basements. Deep style."
"There's a giant fridge down there. Fuck-gimp will fit, no problem." He nods confidently. "It looks like a white bear or some shit. Try not to piss yourself when you see it."
Don't pay attention to him. Just keep telling your sad story.
"All right. Cuno hears you. See that shit house over there?" He points to the collapsed building with the bookstore.
"The fuck are you doing right now?" He looks at you suspiciously. "The fuck is this shit?!"
"Cuno's clock's not doing shit." He looks at his wrist. "Cuno's got a fuckload of time."
"For the fuck-gimp? Good thing you asked The Cunmeister." He nods, trying to look older. "Cuno knows a fridge, perfect for freezing f****ts."
"Thanks, Cuno." (Conclude.)
"Kid, this is *serious*. My job is on the line. If I don't get this sorted, I might actually get fired..."
Cuno's a poor kid from a poor neighbourhood. Say your job is on the line. He'll sympathize.
"I thought you would! Where is it?"
"Really? I don't believe it."
"Where can I find this perfect fridge, then?"
"Uhm..." The lieutenant's eyes flash behind his glasses. "It's not *that* dramatic. We can just send the body to Processing..."
"Baconman's in a rush. But what's in it for the Cuno?" He crosses his arms. "What's the return on Cuno's investment?"
"Cuno's got everything Cuno needs. All civics and shit."
A dark flame smoulders in Cuno's eyes as he ponders your argument -- wordless. Like kings do.
Convince *the Cuno* to spill the beans.
"Kind sir, I'll repay you for this information one day. Right now the clock is ticking."
"A corpse-free yard. Don't you have civic pride?"
"Wasn't going to." He waves you off. "Cuno's not into bacon-charity."
"What do you mean *in there deep*?"
"Check the fucking basement, pig. Don't you know anything?" The kid rolls his eyes. "Always check the fucking basement. Recon style."
"Don't believe him, Cuno! He just wants to use your fridge!"
"You can't turn Cuno into your little popo-man! Cuno's his *own* man!"
"You can't buy Cuno, pig! Cuno's already got everything!"
He doesn't know what that means. Talking about *civics and shit* didn't make this any easier.
There's nothing on his wrist.
"Cuno owns you now, pig! You're Cuno's property!"
"Some arrogant shit thinks he can kill in the Cuno's kingdom, without asking the Cuno first? That sounds like lawlessness to me."

Just trust me. He'll sympathize if he realizes you could actually lose your job over this.
Don't fuck it up, you *need* a fridge.
A cold comes over you as you glance behind him -- at the crumbling colossus there, casting a shadow on you.

Coach Physical Instrument endorses these pants. They are tartan-ready.

You'd have to be blind not to notice the giant white letters "F-A-L-N" running down his trouser leg.

The lieutenant remains silent, but his expression couldn't say *I told you so* any louder.

The lieutenant takes a quick note in his notebook.
"Get the fuck out of here, pig! Cuno doesn't have a magic tree house!"
"Hold on, the gardener *used* to work there?"

"Yeah, that's what Cuno said. She couldn't handle the heat, so she took off. Cuno can take it." He fills his lungs with the rancid air. His eyes get a little watery. "Shit's *nothing* to Cuno."
"You mean the young woman by Whirling-in-Rags? That gardener?"
"The gardener? She's actually not a gardener. Turns out she's a union fixer."
"Look it up in the library. Cuno's not a fucking dictionary..." He shakes his head. "Fuckin' small-brain. Cuno means the gardener, alright?"
What was she doing in the greenhouse in March anyway? What kind of *gardening* is done in March?
Fish is sometimes used to fertilize the soil a few weeks before planting something. Maybe she was preparing  the garden beds?
"Look, Cuno doesn't explain shit -- Cuno just *says* shit." He looks you in the eye and nods, as if agreeing with himself.
Yeah, her.
I should ask her about that. (Accept the task.)
Not important right now. (Refuse task.)
Yes, it was probably fish. I'm not gonna waste more time asking about it. (Refuse task.)
"The fuck are you staring at with your mouth open? Ask Cuno a question or get the fuck out of here."
Yes, it seems suspicious. You don't like things being like that... suspicious.
"The fuck does this have to do with the Cuno? Cuno doesn't give a shit who she is."

You were expecting relaying this information to him to be more rewarding, right? Telling him you found out she isn't a gardener. You know what you should do, if you want to get rewarded? Drugs. Drugs are more rewarding than work.
Cuno is actually a *little* interested.
"That's just some shit roofing-gimps left behind. Lazy dinks."
He's hiding something.
"Are you hiding something?"
Shit 'some gimps' left behind. Sounds legitimate. Let's move on.
Of course, sire. Better not anger the Cuno with this silliness. We regret bringing it up. A thousand years of misfortune upon us for bringing it up!
"Pig... if Cuno was hiding something, it would be hidden," he says with exaggerated confidence.
But it is not hidden, is it, sire? You picked up on it. You should examine the pile of roofing material again.
Was there something here you were supposed to pick up on? As soon as it crosses your mind, the thought is gone...
There it is! That strange *feeling* again! As if... there was more than meets the eye about that pile of roofing material.
"You can't hide it, I see without vision.  With my inner eye."
"So you say, but I saw *past the veil*."
"Yes, yes... some shit gimps left behind. Were those gimps..." (Suddenly raise your eyes.) "...left-handed?"
"The fuck are you talking about? Cuno doesn't know what-handed gimps they were."
"Tryin'a get you to talk gimp, Cuno. Don't talk!"
Don't I have a single normal thing to say?
We are *way* beyond normal already. We are in the STAR CHAMBER.
"Inner eye?! Fuck are you talking about?!" He loses his cool for a moment and starts yelling. "Ask me a normal question, pig!"
"Kim, I think I'm *already* in the Star Chamber."
Better not to bother the lieutenant with my Star Chamber. He wouldn't understand.
"Are you having a seizure in Cuno's yard now?" He sounds agitated.
"Huh..." The lieutenant has his nose in his notebook. "I have no idea what you just said."
"They're trying to make you feel stupid, Cuno!"
He loses his cool for a moment and starts yelling. "The fucking wellll... ?! The fuck are you talking about?! Ask me a normal question, pig!"
You glance again at the roofing material in front of the shack -- yes, you should go back there.
"Yeah, Cuno sees where this is going. Cuno's got that fast-brain," he whispers excitedly. "You saying you pigs are after the mug fucker -- coz he's the clothes fucker..."
"Can't hear you, Cuno! Speak louder, Cuno!"
"That's exactly what I'm saying, Cuno. Someone has tampered with the crime scene, cleaned some of it up."
"Not just that. I also think the hypothethical *mug fucker* lives in that apartment there." (Point to Gary's apartment.)
The lieutenant turns to see where you are pointing. He looks interested.
"Shit, that's tense..." He thinks for a moment. "Someone's going to the beatdown-basement, huh? Mug-guy gonna get tied to the radiator." He nods in approval.
"Cuno doesn't know who put that shit in there. And if he did, he wouldn't squeal. But if you find out, maybe you can..."
"Stop turning into a pig, Cuno! They're trying to get you hooked on the snitching!" She lets out a hiss, even meaner than before. "Get away from my Cuno, f****ts!"
...tell the Cuno who it was? He's curious. He likes putting 2 and 2 together here.
"Yeah!" Cuno jumps back. "Get your bacon shit away! Cuno doesn't like to be seen with the popo. Get your shit done and out of Cuno's face!"
The kid may have something there. He's already come up with an interrogation technique too.
*Kipt* is a pejorative term used to describe people of South Semenese or Areopagite descent. It used to be a common first name among the Areopagites of Iilmaraa -- not so much anymore.

Or alcohol, if you don't want to do drugs. Alcohol is just as rewarding, but it isn't a drug. This has been going on for quite a while, hasn't it? You've been thinking about drugs and alcohol for a long time now. Juicy drugs, tasty alcohol...

Seems kinda boring now, going back to... What was this about? Some yard? Yards aren't interesting. Only drugs are interesting. Drugs and alcohol. You feel sad now, but what can you do. Life has to go on. With a heavy sigh, you say...
"Cuno doesn't know who lives there. And if he did, he wouldn't squeal. But if you find out, maybe you can..."
The boy shakes his head. "You need these pants. But you ain't gonna get these pants, pig!"
"That's what the f****t gets for trying to split us up, Cuno! NO FUCKING PANTS!"
It's not Cuno. It's Cunoesse.
He's on your crime scene, bossing you around. And he's been here for some time, too -- this is where he *hangs out*. You have to get more out of him. He could be useful.
"Hey Cuno -- think you can turn *the Cuno* down for a moment? Let's talk like normal people."
"Cuno, listen. I know this *boundary-pushing* thing is new to you, but it's old news for us grown-ups."
"Cuno, you must have seen all kinds of things throwing stones here. Wanna help the RCM bust a murderer?"
"Tryin'a fuck at the Cuno! Tryin'a fuck at me! Tryin'a fuck!" He spits fast. "Cuno only gets HIGHER! It's faster-faster-faster! Can't take the Cuno -- stay out of the reactor!"
"Get your snout out of Cuno's ass!" He waves you off. "Cuno knows how hard Cuno pushes it. Cuno pushes it hard-level..."
"You hear that, C? Porko wants to talk about how he can't hack this shit. Porko wants to move in with Cuno!"
"You should give up, popo. Or the Cunn will keep fucking it out of you."
"Cuno gonna FUCK YOU UP!" She pumps her bony fists in the air. "UP! UP! UP!"
"Take the pain, fucko! Take the bad!" The child is not grinning -- it looks more like a wolf bearing its teeth.
"Don't let him move in with us, Cuno."
(Act on it, try and separate them.) "Cuno! Psst..."
"What do you mean, she smoked someone?"
"You think she has anything to do with the dead man?"
"You said she's... insane?"
"What's that language she uses -- *napakymppi*, *fägäri*?"
"Is she your sister?"
What's going on? He's an ungovernable youth on your crime scene, throwing around incendiary language, trying to push your buttons.
"Cuno -- 'City of Rage'? 'Night City'? What's going on there? I'm intrigued."
"Nooooo..." The evil shit behind the fence hacks like she's coughing up a furball.
"I don't know what to do anymore... I'm just a busted old piece of meat. This case is all I have -- and you're not helping."
Like you don't have enough on your plate! You feel a sudden surge of self-pity coming on...
"You told him about it and now he knows you're lame!"
The prospect of the Cuno turning lame is physically painful for her.
"The city's not fucking lame, *you* are lame! Cuno's tired of defending Rage City from..." He waves his hands in the air. "Just fuck off, alright."
"And fuck you too," he adds, turning to you. "Putting Cuno on the spot like that. Cuno doesn't need to fucking *explain* his shit, Cuno's KING, he rules here -- fuck did you want?"
Explain himself? As if... explaining some kind of *work*? Some kind of avant-garde work way ahead of its time?
I'm intrigued.
No. I'm not interested. I don't wanna *art*.
You *must* get to the bottom of this, one of these days. Sadly, it's unlikely to happen today.
Stop denying it. You want art all over you. You want to smear yourself in art, been dying to ever since you got up...
"Fuck no!" He bursts out loud. Laughing. "What are you, fucking... mentally handicapped?"
"Cuno, they've almost made you a snitch now..."
"Ease off, C. Cuno always takes the bullet over the hammer." He nods, big-boy style, incredibly proud of himself.
He'd rather die than work with the justice system.
"Are you okay, Cuno?" She looks worried. The *Cunn* has her confused.
That went wrong. He took it as a compliment. Then he had a minor seizure.
Normal is not what we got here. You've got to work with what you have for now.
Smelling weakness. She loves it.
You have no idea what to say now. You're just going to have to try to change the subject...
Interesting. How?
All in all, Cuno respects madness. You cannot hope to outdo her on that front. You must win yourself a few minutes with him alone.
Cunoesse is by far the worst of the two. Cuno has no problem being near you, but the other hides behind the fence, afraid for her life, like she's *done* something. Something very bad.
Also, Cuno hasn't stopped talking to you. Even enjoys it from time to time. When you talk to the other one it's like talking to a cornered animal. She only hisses.
And then there's the fact that she's a girl. And appears to be a little younger, certainly smaller. And yet Cuno is afraid of her. What's up with *that*, Cuno?
She came up with that psychopathic scheme of screaming for help before. Cuno just wanted to talk to you about his name. Cunoesse was the one who wound him up and directed him.
"Fuck you whispering about?" he whispers back.
"If Cuno wants to whisper, he's gonna fucking whisper, okay?!" He turns back to you and hunkers down: "Let's *whisper*, pig!"
He's whispering too. He's going with it. But watch what happens...
"Fuck you *f****ts* whispering about?!"
She puts extra stress onto that word. Expecting it will make you uncomfortable.
This is it, you've got him. But be careful -- you can still fuck this up. Don't make Cuno look bad in this.
"Cuno, listen to me -- she's trying to *control* you. We gotta get you outta here."
"What's up with her? She's terrifying... Crazy scary."
"Phew, am I glad she's out of our hair. She's fucked up."
"Crazy?" he whispers tensely. "You don't know the half of it. She's not crazy, she's insane. Dangerous. She smoked a man. She's done people in, probably even pigs..."
"She's not fucked up!" He raises his voice, but then lowers it again. "Everyone's fucked up. Stop judging shit."
"Stop talking to him! Cuno, I'm fucking warning you! You're gonna get us into shit!"
She understands what you're trying to do.
"It's okay!" He straightens his back and turns to Cunoesse. "The pig's trying to pit us against each other. Not gonna let him do that."
"Yo, C?" He pops his head up. "Did Cuno not *tell* you?! Cuno told you -- CUNO TALKS TO WHOEVER HE WANTS."
"Talk, pig. Cuno's got it under control." He hunches down again.
You did it. They're separated. He's even turned his back to her so she can't read his lips.
Fuck, she can read lips? You should cup your mouth.
Wrong move. But he's whispering still. You haven't lost him, just don't mess up again, or you will. There are no guarantees here.
That's it. You let him off the line, that was a *bad*, manipulative thing to say. You should understand: I got you this far, I couldn't get you all the way.
Idiot! You bungled it up.
"Tried to fuck my Cuno!" A giggle, malicious and gleeful. She pulls herself up higher on the fence. "Tried to fuck my Cuno away! Me and Cuno are tight. We ride for life!"

"Fuck knows -- she says it's the *song of her people* or some shit."
"Crazy people? The fucking *näkkies*? I don't know..."
"What people?"

It's Suruese. The Suru are an indigenous ethnic minority in the social democratic powerhouse Vaasa, on the tundra and taiga covered isola of Katla. Far, far away from here -- as far as possible, really.
Sounds *boreal*, like something from the tundra- and taiga- covered Katla isola. Far, far away from here -- as far as possible, really.
Do they have red-haired people there?
"Cuno, could she be Suruese?"
This isn't important right now.
You mean evil little red-haired people like her? Yes, they do -- the Suruese have that ginger gene.

Revachol does have a small Suruese community. Or she climbed into a yakberry crate and was shipped over accidentally.

"It's none of our business. That's what a *näkk* is. Cuno keeps his nose to himself -- doesn't go poking around in *näkk* shit. Cuno's wise that way."
She regresses and pretends she's a mythological creature when she's under too much stress.

"Cuno... do you think it's possible that she's killed other children?"
"Really? Isn't she too small to overpower someone?
"You serious about this killing business?"
"What if she has, Cuno? That would explain things..."
He's meant everything he said before; but right now he not only means it -- he is sincere.
His little green eyes are fixed on yours.
"Are you getting this? You think I'm fucking telling you a joke here? How hard do you think it is to kill a fat-ass?" He pokes you in the gut. "Sweet talk 'em, then knife 'em."
"She's probably killed a pig too. I mean, I'm pretty sure she has."

Four-eighty-eight? The criminal code doesn't go higher than 190.
"Fuckin' yeah. Cuno knows you don't want to face this right now. This dark shit. Cuno faces this shit every day -- makes Cuno's skin crawl."
"C'mon. She hasn't killed police officers."
"Okay. How many cops has she killed then?"
A cop would be too large for her to overpower. But a determined child of her size can still kill the vulnerable. The elderly. The homeless. Or other... other children.
The creature peers at you both from over the fence. There is something searching in her eyes.
Fear.
Fear of the truth.
"I knew you pigs were too naive for this shit. Good thing Cuno's got her under control. Cuno keeps her calm." He feels eyes on the back of his head -- and stops.
There's something cold in the air. Like water lapping against cold stones. Or dripping. In a hallway nearby. Three years ago. There were shoes in the corner...
"Forget Cuno said that. Cuno was just shitting. Cuno was just running his mouth. Cuno's stupid like that." He feels eyes on the back of his head -- and stops.
Though her friend spoke too low for her to hear, Cunoesse is not smiling anymore.
Cuno falls silent. He does not look at you when he replies...
He usually looks you straight in the eye. A little something just crumbled there.
"Cuno, uh... that's.... that's what Cuno is starting to think. Yeah."
Don't move your head. Just from the corner of your eye -- look at her.
Look at her.
Look at Cuno.
The kid is just that now -- a kid.
"Yeah, she would've liked to fuck him up. But she didn't. Cuno wasn't around. And C was with Cuno."
"Look, Cuno's gonna put you at ease. We didn't do it."
"Cuno wasn't around. And C was with Cuno. Told you this already."
"Where were you?"
He speaks the truth, my liege.
"Fuck no, she's not my sister. She's just a stray who got in. Like a mad dog or some shit."
"Yeah, she's psycho." He leans in even closer. "None of that kiddy-psycho, cat-burning shit -- she does the real deal."

"Snuff radio shit... Believe me, pig, you don't wanna know."
"Let's leave it at that."
"Whoa..."
"Yeah." He watches it sink in.
"Yeah -- let's."
And he doesn't want to even think about it. This isn't just another boast.
"Stray?"
"Yeah, she was just there." He points at the apartment building behind the fence.
"She was in the hallway, dripping wet." Cuno flinches, then lowers his voice even more. "By the fucking shoe rack. In the dark."

"Cuno's got no fucking idea. Her hair was all wet. I think she pissed on the floor too. She was there for three days -- in the corner. Every time Cuno went out."
"Why was she dripping wet?"

What, if any, is the downside of *not* giving the drugs to Cuno?

None that you can see.

A small lump forming in his throat.
No. You *can* see it. This young man has junior officer material in him. In another life, where he trusts you.

In truth, Cuno doesn't really believe there's anything you can do to make up for this. The damage is irreparable.

"All right, now we're talking. Whooh that's heavy..." He waves the minuscule bottle around, then slips it into his coat pocket.

"I told you he can't be trusted! I told you, I told you..." the little rat repeats it six or seven times. "I told you he'd steal the shit!"

"This is about you and Cuno. You mismanaged this shit. Now everything is *fucked* between us. How are you gonna make this up to the Cuno, huh?"

His posture changes, the swaying rooster motion stops for a second. Then he gets it going again. Reorienting himself.

In his mind, his father isn't vulnerable the way other mortals are.

That room was so small. To be stuck in there with him... not an easy fight for a kid.

Sam Bo is an acronym for Samaran boxing. Graceful martial arts stuff. "Sam Bo style" implies stealth, cleverness, and cool. Just letting you know.

dialoguetext: Who is Kras Mazov?
Seems like a good guy judging by the moustache. By the way... doesn't he kind of look like *you*?

"He's known as the father of scientific communism, also known as Mazovianism. His theories about economic history greatly influenced -- some would even say *sparked* -- the Antecentennial Revolution."
Situated between a poster of a white star and a photo of revolutionaries posing with their guns... This can't be a coincidence. There can be only one explanation.
Kras Mazov is a *communard*.

Yes, Kras Mazov (nom de guerre), was an economist and theoretical historian. He was a leading figure on the Graad side of the Turn-of-the-Century Revolution, where he headed the Eleven Day Government. Mazov is considered the father of scientific communism (Mazovian thought or Mazovianism).
The lieutenant raises a brow.
"I hate deviants."
"Whoever lives here definitely shares your enthusiasm." He leans closer to inspect the photos of revolutionaries on the wall.
"I suspect that's exactly what they're trying to do." He leans closer to inspect the economics book on the table.
"He was definitely controversial. The tenant here seems to like him..." He leans closer to inspect the photos of revolutionaries on the wall.
"Thank you for sharing this wonderful opinion on human sexuality." He pretends to read the economics book open on the table.
Honestly, he does kind of look like you after all.
"Hold on a second... Is this why you broke in here? To find out whether you're Kras Mazov?"
"I have to consider and investigate all possibilities."
"No, it's purely coincidental."
"I'm not saying that I *am* Kras Mazov, I'm just saying that we look alike."
"Sure it is."
"Well, you both do seem to share an affinity for sideburns. But it seems like old Kras here didn't drink nearly as much as you."
"Except that Kras Mazov is dead. He's been dead for 50 years now."
"Just humour me for a moment... Don't you see the resemblance?"
"You're right, this is silly -- I'm no Kras Mazov."
The lieutenant doesn't even bother to reply to this.
"How do you know? The bust is probably just a romanticized depiction anyway."
"Maybe this bust shows him *before* he started drinking."
"Sure you are."
"Very well." The lieutenant leans closer to the sculpture. "Let's look for identifying features then..."
He puts a finger on a pale dot embellishing the bust's cheekbone. "Doesn't he have a birthmark right here? What about you?"
"I can't tell -- I can't see my face."
"I definitely don't have a birthmark on my left cheek."
"Then it's settled," says the lieutenant, straightening his back. "You're not Kras Mazov."
"Alright. But here's the big thing -- Kras Mazov looks Samaran, and you don't."
"No, it's not settled -- I might still be Kras Mazov. It's just a birthmark."
"You're right, I'm really not."
"No, he doesn't."
"I'm part Samaran myself."
The lieutenant closes his eyes. "Okay, you win. Be Kras Mazov then, I don't care..."
He opens his eyes again, tilting his head in a quiet wonder. "Why are you so hell-bent on proving that you're Kras Mazov anyway?"
"Yes, he does. Look at his eyes. Wasn't his mother a Samaran immigrant?"
"You're right, that's something we definitely don't have in common."
"Good, so you're not him."
"It's decided -- you're *not* the most famous philosopher of the modern period." The lieutenant nods, turning away to inspect the photo on the other wall.
"I might not look like him, but I know it in my heart -- Kras Mazov, that's me."
"Because I'm a communard."
"Because I believe a powerful nation-state is the only way to protect the working class from subhumans."
"Because *actually* he wanted stability and incremental progress -- and so do I."
"I'm not sure, it's just a feeling I have. But I trust my feelings."
"Alright, *Kras*," the lieutenant notes. "If you say so."
"Alright, *Kras*. You fought in the Revolution and everything," the lieutenant notes. "If you say so."
"Why does this tenant have a bust of Kras Mazov in their bedroom?"
"The white star... the photos on the wall... I think we have broken into the apartment of a young communard." He looks around, before mumbling to himself: "How fitting."
[Leave.]
"Father Mazov, the hero of the working class!" (Salute the statue.)
"Whoever lives here needs to learn how the economy *actually* works." (Stare at the bust.)
"Kras Mazov was a mass murderer. There's nothing *cool* about keeping his bust on your night stand." (Stare at the bust.)
"Kras Mazov was a filthy homo-sexual." (Stare at the bust.)
A warm feeling fills you as you look into Mazov's marble eyes. The hallway behind the door is empty; no one else heard your courageous salute.
The bust doesn't reply. The hallway behind the door is empty; no one heard your words.
"A communard lives in this room." (Look around.)
A *poor* communard, from the looks of it. The room is barely bigger than a closet.
"Yeah -- I have a problem. A problem with alcohol."
"You do -- but that's not the point. The point is, he doesn't look like you."
"Because he was totally a gangster and a bank robber who went for *all* the cash in the world. That's *me*."
"I think you have misunderstood who he was, but..." the lieutenant sighs. "If you say so."
"That's right." (Nod.) "Filthy."
"There aren't many communists around -- not after the Revolution. Some youths still keep the ideology going, it seems."
"Officers of the Revachol Citizens Militia." The man in business-casual removes his cuff links.
"Was there anything else?"
You shouldn't be seeing him in an intimate setting. For some reason you feel this man is your... *superior*.
His hands are clean and well-manicured. This is a man who knows the importance of appearances.

dialoguetext: "Can you tell me about your friend?"
"What's Kedra?"
"Someone's baby is bawling its eyes out."
"Kedra is a candidate member of EPIS. But, between you and me, their potential membership is a more... *contentious* issue."
"What's this EPIS thing you keep talking about?"
"How did you two even become friends?"

"How did any of us become friends? Bad things happening on the Insulindian isola. Oil platforms ablaze in the night. Civil wars lasting for years. Finally, the international community is forced to step in."
"You're describing how the Coalition occupied Revachol."
Except that *candidate* members never become *full* members, do they?
A busy bee? What an odd choice of words.

"EPIS is a very special program developed by the Moralintern to support certain Occidental nations. It began as a unified system of weights and measures, which proved to be a *wild* success. Nothing but kilograms and centimetres as far as the eye can see!"

"It was *such* a wild success that we expanded it into an economic union for the processing of steel -- another success. And between you and me... the Moralintern feels *emboldened* by this success. Emboldened to take EPIS to the next level."
"My friend comes and goes. I'm sure you'll see him around, he's a busy bee."
"What's on the next level?"
"I was asking about your friend."
"A supranational political alliance, the United States of Occident."
"Is it going to be like this place here?"
"You mean Revachol? No, it's going to have transparent democracy."
Waves crashing in the distance, the sound of sea below the window.
"Is Revachol going to be part of EPIS?"
"Listen," he says, raising his hand...
"What view? It's dark outside."
A baby is crying in the neighbouring apartment.
"What are you talking about? No one becomes friends that way."
"We're old friends, nothing's taboo between us. He comes and goes."
"Officer, you have to understand... I can't give you his personal information. I'm sure you have your own methods and databases, right? Please don't put me in this situation."
"Au contraire. It's how millions of people end up where they are, meeting the people they meet. It's how I came here, and my friend, too."
"Fine, but what's his real name?"

"One of the wonders of democracy is that everyone is allowed to have his own opinion." The man pats his pockets, looking for something. "And not just allowed, *encouraged* even. Have you ever tried debate?"
"He's a bright young man here to pursue his education. Education is the foundation of our future, especially the arts. It is a cornerstone of our civilization."

"Ah, my friend. My friend is a good young man. His family immigrated here from Kedra and life has not been easy for him. But he understands the importance of education. He has taken his future into his own hands and that's all that matters."
"Isn't it rude for your friend to leave you alone like this?"

"Martin Martinaise? That's not a name. Are you referring to my friend? But I told you, he's from Kedra -- definitely not just another Martin Martinaise or Raoul Revachol. Perhaps that's why he and I became friends..."
"What do you mean?"
"Your friend, Martin Martinaise."
"Debating. You should consider joining a debating society for adults. I hear they're *oodles* of fun. I used to have a flyer for one, but..."
"I'm just enjoying the view," the man smiles, nodding to the window.
"But now that I start to think of it, it was for an improv class anyway. It's this funny theatre thing, you know," he moves his fingers, "very *creative*, helps relieve stress."
"But the million reál view stays. You can't take that away." He knocks on the balcony door, his face mirrored in the darkened glass.
"No, *listen*," he says again, looking outside...
"What do you mean?"
"That it's never going to happen. They entered negotiations in '21 and it's been pending ever since."
"What? I'm not hearing anything."
"The Insulindian Bay."
"But that doesn't tell me anything about Kedra itself. Is it warm there? Cold? Something in-between?"
"I'm all ears, officer."
"You still haven't told me who he is."
"It's one day going to be a *candidate member* of EPIS, sure."
"I had something else in mind..."
"Didn't you say that candidate members never become real members?"
"Someone's baby is crying."
"No, no, candidate members *do* become members, why do we even have the whole system in place if they don't? It just takes time -- time and evaluation."
"Which arts?"
"I'm sure you'll see him around, he's very active."
"So all you can tell me about him is that he's here to study the arts?"
"He's a truly free spirit. He likes all the arts. Perhaps graphic design? Printmaking? Who knows? The world is open wide for a talented youth like him."
"But I told you, officer. He's a bright young man here to pursue his education. Education is the foundation of our future, especially the arts. It is a cornerstone of our civilization."
"Sorry, who?" The man throws a quick glance at his watch.
"Your friend, the smoker on the balcony. We were just talking about him."

"This place used to be a luxury accommodation, before the Revolution. Apartments, of course, were much bigger then -- a few walls have been added here and there, leaving some of the tenants without a private bathroom or a kitchen..."
"What about it?"
"I can hear the waves."
"He's deeply enmeshed in the study of the fine arts, yes."
"It's warm," he nods. "It's also known for its mandarin trees and dust storms from Supramundi."
"Kedra's an emerging market, but it still has a long way to go -- maybe that's why my friend's ménage decided to emigrate."
"Do you think *peace* is boring? What about *prosperity*?"
"Yes. As I said before, I'm a commissioner from Sur-la-Clef working for the Institute of Price Stabilité." He glances at his watch. "This is one of the main projects of the Moralintern."
"What's an official like you doing in Martinaise?"
"Okay, but what are you doing *here* in this apartment?"
"So you're some kind of bureaucrat?"
"What is this *international community*?"
"What's the Moralintern?"
"Are you a moralist?"

"Ah, well, I'm renovating it. It is an interesting project. The building used to be a twelve-story skyscraper before the cannons took the top four stories off. This of course happened when the Coalition forces landed here..."
"Oh, yes, the big bad Coalition crushed the Revolution. Tell me, if the revolution was succeeding, would it have been crushed so easily?"
"La communauté internationale is what Revacholians colloquially call *the Coalition*. In other words, the nations that stopped the disaster of the Revolution."
"Whatever you wish, officer."
"What is *ze price stabilité*?"
"It is ze most important thing."
"Enough business, let's talk about something else."

"The Coalition is only looking out for *ze price stabilité*." He raises an index finger. "Inflation is a killer, like a heart disease blocking the normal circulation of the economy -- It must be controlled..."
"And what *do* I call the Coalition?"
"Your employer, technically speaking. The governing authority of Revachol. The RCM is but one part of this provisional administration."
"Ah, yes, the unattainable ideal. Never settle for less! Good luck with that, my friend."
"It's usually the most boring one."
"That doesn't tell me anything."
"I agree. And we as an international community should strive to bring this prosperity to every kid on every isola."

"It's the central goal of any sound monetary policy. Maintaining ze price stabilité is essential to maintaining high levels of economic activity, which is essential for maintaining high levels of employment..."
"Basically it makes sure the price of bread doesn't change."
"Exactly. *I* don't find it boring, I find it *fulfilling*. Peace is what allows me to have my morning coffee, my afternoon golf, my sundown friends."
"*Précisément*! Too much inflation, bread becomes too expensive; too much deflation, it becomes too cheap for bakers to produce..."
"Below 2% of what?"
"But not *too* far below, no. Too below is also bad -- below, *but close to* 2%."
"You're not answering my questions at all."
It's not like you're going to gather any forces soon with all that drinking -- and he knows it.
"The Coalition believes in the importance of informing the public about the benefits of ze price stabilité. Transparency is one of our principles. Would you like an informational pamphlet?"
"No, I'm good."
"Are we really so bad for wanting compromise, peace, and prosperity -- on reasonable, achievable terms? Ask yourself that."
"It's the international organization for moralists. Hence 'Moralist International.' The Institute of Price Stability is just one of its many *mind babies* -- as is the Coalition."
"That's why the Institute of Price Stabilité works to keep inflation just below 2%..."
"How does this benefit us, exactly?"
"Okay, sure, give me a leaflet."
"But why?"
"Because moralists believe in a normal, stable world governed by democratic values."

"Oranje's economy is one of the most advanced in the world. It has successfully transitioned from heavy industry to advanced services, and generally acts as an engine for sustainable change in the international community."
"Okay, but outside of EPIS, what is Oranje?"

"As founding members they are *both* very EPIS. Oranje carries a lot of political weight, while Sur-la-Clef takes care of the business side of things -- Sur-la-Clef hosts the headquarters of the major EPIS institutions."
"Which one of them is more EPIS?"
"But they are working towards it! You're all doing very well here, relatively speaking." He gives you an approving nod.
"But of course!"
"Tell me about Oranje."
"Am *I* a moralist?"
The smile he gives you is straight off a campaign poster, the kind of smile focus group-tested to appeal to the most gullible swathe of the electorate.
"Moralism is all about compromise and achieving the achievable. It's pragmatic, realistic, and level-headed, an ideology for *doers*. Are you a doer, my friend? It looks to me like you are."
"Well, do you value freedom? Do you believe in a normal, stable world governed by democratic values?"
"It 'didn't work' because the Coalition crushed it violently."
"We just haven't tried *real* communism yet."
"But what is a normal, stable world?"
"The Occident is part of the normal world. Oranje, Sur-la-Clef..."
"No, prosperity sounds like a lot of fun."
"Martinaise doesn't seem very normal, or stable, to me."
"Martinaise? No, Martinaise is... something else."
"No, peace sounds pretty good."
"What about the rest of Revachol? Is it part of the normal world?"
"It's moving towards the right direction and that's all that matters. Progress is measured in centimetres, my friend."
"Revachol is generally... difficult. It's led by an interim government, which means it hasn't yet achieved *full* democracy..."
"And you're telling me *this* world here is working out well?"
"Sounds like you're a moralist indeed, my friend. Welcome."
"Yes, everything else is super extreme. It's like I'm living with a bunch of lunatics..."
"Tell me about Sur-la-Clef."
"Is this 'Option D' usually the most *reasonable* answer?"
"Your full autonomy is important, I agree. But it's an ongoing process. Nothing happens overnight."
"It's like every time I'm talking to people I'm choosing Option D, 'none of the above'... Is that moralism?"
"Now, enough of this delightful political interlude. Was there anything else you wanted to ask?"
"I don't think I'm a moralist. Moralism sounds incredibly boring. I want more action."
"Moralism is the ideology of foreign occupiers. Revachol must be governed by Revacholians!"
"Democracy is a meaningless sham as long as the working class is under the boot-heel of Capital."
"Ah, my friend, but the lesson of the Revolution is that communism does not work."
"A moment, officer."
"Thanks, I've got all I need." [Leave.]
"You have acquired the hat." He assesses the situation. "Keep it, officer, it looks good on you."
"You have acquired the robe." He assesses the situation. "Keep it, officer, it looks good on you."
"You have acquired the hat." The man assesses the situation. "Keep it, officer, it looks good on you."
"You have acquired the robe." The man assesses the situation. "Keep it, officer, it looks good on you."
"What's there to say? Sur-la-Clef is a modern, urbanized country that measures very high on the Human Development and Freedom Index. Mostly, though, it's known as the executive heart of *EPIS*..."

"Oranje is an *exemplary* nation who, as a core member of EPIS, contributes 28% of our annual budget. Next to Sur-la-Clef, Oranje is probably the most prominent member of the international community."
"Do you have everything you need from me? I'm afraid we won't have the chance to speak again once you leave."
"I'm not going anywhere, I just want to take a look around in this apartment." [Leave.]
"Thanks for the heads up, but my work here is done." [Leave.]
"Of course, I'm glad I could help."
"Hold on, why can't we talk later?"
"Sure, go ahead, it's a beautiful space." He glances at his watch. "Let me know if you have any further questions."

"It's against diplomatic best practices for an official in my position to be discussing murders with local militiamen." He pauses. "And I'm pressed for time. After you leave, I should be leaving as well."
"No, that's not his..." the lieutenant sighs. "Martin Martinaise is a *joke*, a generic nickname for someone from Martinaise."
"And my friend's not even your typical local -- definitely not just another Martin Martinaise or Raoul Revachol. Maybe that's why we're friends."
But that didn't tell you anything about Oranje.
"Can't you just... talk like a normal person?"
"I once heard from *here* that they are a reasonably sized superpower." (Tap your head.)

"That's one way to put it, yes. They certainly have the power to exert influence over others, but they only do it in the name of regional stability. After all, Oranje is a Moralintern nation, not some crazed Mesque petro-fascist state."
"About what?"
"About Oranje -- just tell me what it's like there."

"Oh, it's very urban and very well-organized. Their streets are clean, their horsecars run on time, the people are polite and efficient. Like I said, they are an example for less-emerged nations to follow."
"What makes Revachol Sur-la-Clef's 'darling'?"
"Because a great percentage of Revachol's culture hails from Sur-la-Clef -- its language, its people, its cuisine even, or at least in the downtown La Delta area."
Jamrock and other parts of the International Zone have been mercifully spared of Sur-la-Clef's love for meatballs and mashed potatoes.
The tone somehow suggests to you that you're starting to become a little sponsored by him as well.
Superior? But he's not in the command chain...
(Point at the bed.) "Before we go on, I absolutely *have* to inquire about this wonderful canopy."
(Show him the silk robe.) "Before we get to that, tell me where you got this *beautiful* silk robe from?"
(Show him the Samaran hat.) "We'll get to that. Right after you tell me the story behind the black Samaran hat."
No, first ask an innocuous personal question to get the interview off on the right foot.
Yes. Make it clear you're the one setting the terms here...
(Get down to business.) "Hello, Mr. Villedrouin. Let's get started."

dialoguetext: Yeah, *yeah*! Let's *fuck* with him! Who does he think he is, assisting *you*?
Hanging? What a drag. He seems like a *cultured* gentleman -- you should ask him about the finer things...
"Of course. Let me just say it has been an emotional week for me." He forms a little rooftop with his fingers. Cold air comes in from the balcony.
The lieutenant takes out his notebook and nods to you to proceed.
(Point to the silk robe.) "Before we get to that, tell me where you got this *beautiful* silk robe from?"
(Point to the Samaran hat.) "We'll get to that. Right after you tell me the story behind the black Samaran hat."
"That's really all I can tell you about it." He forms a little rooftop with his fingers. Cold air sweeps in from the balcony.

"I got it from the head of the Samaran delegation on my trip to Lo-Manthang. It's made from a *special* charcoal-coloured bamboo. It's an emblem of the formal normalization of our diplomatic relations."
"Oh, we got it from an atelier in the East Delta Commerce Centre. Personally I think it's a little culturally insensitive, but the material is great. Sadly the shop is now out of business..."
He's alluding to the decade-long war of independence while deftly brushing aside the *complex* causes behind the conflict.
Wait, there isn't actually an *Institute of Price Stabilité*, is there? Or maybe there is... God, it's impossible to understand whether someone from the Moralintern is joking or not.
"Moreover, it is a great sponsor of less-emerged countries. Revachol is only one of its many darlings whose progress it supports and cherishes."
"My name is Charles Villedrouin and I'm an official with the Coalition Government. I work for the Institute of Price Stabilité, on assignment from Sur-la-Clef."
"I heard you talking to my friend outside... Very good. Super. I am here to assist you in any way possible. Ask me about the hanging."

"Oh yes, my friend has a great eye for these things. He refuses to tell me where it came from -- it's a mystery. Hehehe." He smiles. "I believe they call this type of frame *industrial*. It's very comfy."
That didn't work at all.
What was *that*?! You were supposed to *fuck* with him, not compliment the décor!
"The economy impacts the entire *international community*, which is why it requires international oversight."
"You actually *witnessed* the lynching?"
"I'm sorry to say I did, officer." The man gives a solemn nod.
(Turn to the lieutenant.) "This is just the break we've been looking for!"
"Start from the beginning, if you don't mind."
"Is it because you did it, Mr. Villedrouin?"
"Officer, it's very difficult to describe what I saw that night. It was so surreal to me, like in a play."
He holds out his hands and blossoms his fingers, like a drama teacher setting the scene.
"Because I *did it*?" the man scoffs.
He's clearly not a man accustomed to being spoken to in that manner, let alone to being accused of *murder*.
"I was on the balcony when it happened, getting some fresh air. I remember that first they came in, carrying what looked like a body, and then I saw all the surrounding windows go dead one-by-one..."
"My apologies, I misspoke. I mean, what did you see?"
"Don't jerk my chain, paper-jockey. You did it, didn't you?"
The lieutenant is already scribbling down notes. "What do you mean, 'like in a play'?"
"Meaning it was terrifying?"
"Meaning it was entertaining?"
"No, no." The man shakes his head. "I mean it was so strange I could barely believe what was happening..."
"There is no meaning, sir. Please excuse my colleague. This case has... been a great strain on his nerves."
"What's the meaning of this?"
"What gets on my nerves is *murderers*. Why'd you kill him, man?"
"Kim's right. I'm sorry. I haven't been myself lately."
"I'm sorry. Let's start over. My nerves got the best of me there."
"It means the jig's up, creep. I am the law!"
"Well, I can certainly understand *that*." The man loosens his tie knot and appears to relax slightly. "That hanging was a surreal play. Everything since then has been too..."
"I won't stand for this." His left eye starts twitching -- as the last warning. "What's your name? I'll have your badge!"
"*I* don't even have my badge -- so spin on this!" (Give him the finger.)
"I'm in-between names right now."
"My name's Harry."
"Harrier Du Bois, and don't forget it."
"You can just call me *The Law*."
"I am Detective Raphaël Ambrosius Costeau, at your service."
"Around these parts I go by Tequila... Tequila Sunset."
"Very well, *Harry*. You're a disgrace to the RCM. Get out of my sight, this instant!" He points at the door.
"Who were 'they'? Can you describe them?"
"How many of them were there?"
"I couldn't see their faces well, and there were quite a few of them. But they were very loud and very... Martinaise..." He pauses, looking for the right wording.
"Let's just say that the labouring classes can get rather *expressive* with their profanities."
"What happened next?" (Proceed.)
"I couldn't tell you exactly. Less than ten. Maybe eight?"
The lieutenant sends you a sharp look at the mention of that number.
Sound familiar? That matches the prints you observed at the scene.
"Were any of them huge? Like 200 kilograms huge?"
"Did any of them look like drummers?"
"What happened next?"
"Sounds like the victim *was* unconscious. Or at least incapacitated. Well done, detective." He nods to you.
"Drummers? Why... no... but then, I don't know what a drummer is *supposed* to look like."
"That's a giant you're describing. No, they were all *quite* human, so far as I could tell."
"I went back inside."
"Were you able to see anything from inside?"
"Wait, so you didn't actually *see* the lynching happen?"
"Officer, the yard was pitch black. There was nothing to see. But I could still hear their voices. They were threatening to kill that poor man."
"Were they men, women?"
"What ethnicity were they?"
"What happened next?" (Proceed.)
"All men, I presume. But again, I couldn't see very clearly."
"I believe they were mostly white, though I believe I saw two Areopagites among them. And I am quite certain that one spoke with a Mesque accent."
"Those funny... Oh." He blinks. "Officer, that kind of language is unbecoming of an officer of the RCM..."
Yes, back inside. Keep yourself safe from the killing.
"Are you sure at least *one* of them wasn't a woman?"
"It's possible, officer, but I cannot say with certainty. It was very dark, you must remember."
"Hmmm. But we're fairly certain the lady driver was present..." The lieutenant flips through his notes.
That doesn't quite comport with what you know. Don't forget the lady driver!
"Well, that's the strangest part, officer. *Nothing* happened. It was oddly quiet for a public lynching."
"What do you mean 'nothing happened'? They lynched a guy!"
"You're right, that does seem strange."
"Why didn't you call the RCM?"
The man wipes his glasses. "You're right, of course. That is what one is supposed to do in such circumstances. I was simply in shock..."
"Eventually their shouts died down, and that was all. There were no gunshots, no celebratory shouts, no anything."
"About what time was all this happening, approximately?"
"Can you at least tell me when it happened?"
"All I can say is that it was late."
"No, I didn't see the corpse until the following day."
"My watch..." He looks at his watch, as though noticing it for the first time. "Yes, now I remember -- it was thirty minutes past midnight, give or take."
"You didn't check your watch?"
"So let me get this straight. You didn't actually witness the hanging itself, did you?"
"I'm afraid I don't have anything else to add."
"It seems this wasn't the 'break' you were hoping for..."
"I think we have everything we need," the lieutenant says, closing his notebook. "Thank you for talking to us, Mr. Villedrouin."
"Of course, anything I can do to assist the RCM."
"Well, that was a waste of time."
"Those are all my questions. Thanks for your time."
"I'm sorry I couldn't be of more assistance."
"Ah, that clears everything up."
"Which is essential for maintaining *ze social stabilité*..."
"Take your daily bread, *par example*. Too much inflation, bread becomes too expensive; too much deflation, it becomes too cheap for bakers to produce..."
"Okay, I think that's all I needed to know."
"This is *fascinating*, but I wanted to ask you something else."

He pats his pockets. "But, oh! I don't have my leaflets on me today. That's too bad. You can always call our information line. Making information available is part of the Moralintern's commitment to transparency."
"A sound monetary policy is *essential* for addressing *uncertainty*. Stability is the *raison d'être* of the Moralintern. It's the reason why I identify as a moralist."
"Not boring, my friend. *Responsible*."
"My friend, that is only because you have never known the *alternative*. And I pray you never do."
"Yeah, that shit sounds like a snooze-fest."
"That's nice of them."
"Oh, yes. Sur-la-Clef is *mega-benevolent* to its darlings."
What is it about this 'benevolence' that makes you break out in sweat and want to run for the hills?
*Darlings*? That can't be an official designation.
(Turn to Kim.) "Lieutenant, are *you* a moralist?"
"Hmm, me? I... uh..."
You've managed to catch the lieutenant off guard, but only for a moment. He quickly recomposes himself.
"I'm a lieutenant of the RCM, dedicated to maintaining law and order in Revachol."
"A very moralist answer," the man nods.
The lieutenant is practised in the art of putting on a show for one's superiors.
The lieutenant clears his throat. "Of course, the detective's personal views do not represent the views of the RCM."
The lieutenant clears his throat. "Of course, the detective's personal views do not represent the views of the RCM."
God, yes. Sweet standardisation. The backbone of rationality -- and commerce.
"Okay, but like, what does it stand for?"
"Why, it stands for progress and stability, like the Moralintern as a whole."
"Sure, fine. What's this next level you were talking about?"
"No, what do the *letters* stand for?"
"It's been such a wild, *extraordinary* success thus far. We are very excited to take it to the next level..."
"You don't even hear the words I'm saying, do you?"
"What are you doing in his apartment by yourself?"
"Enjoying the view? There's a dead body hanging in the tree!"
The lieutenant sighs. "A dead body we still need to get down, by the way."
A chill runs down your spine as you envision a half-dozen people in professional attire standing around a chair awkwardly pretending to be waiting for a motor-bus. It's neither funny nor creative.
"Yeah, I'm what they call a *master 'bater*." (Brush some invisible dirt off your shoulder.)
"Oh! How wonderful. I've heard it's *oodles* of fun. Not that I have time to take up new hobbies myself..."
There's a joke here, and you know what it is.
C'mon. It's so juvenile. Besides, there's no way this man is going to get it.
That's why it's good.
See? He didn't get it. Good job, jokemeister.
As though you weren't envious enough of the boy as-is.
"You're a disgrace to the RCM. Out with you, this instant!" He points at the door.
"You're doing me no service! Get out, this instant!" He points at the door.
"What kind of name is that? You're a disgrace. Get out, this instant!" He points at the door.
"You'll be in-between jobs soon! Get out, this instant!" He points at the door.
"You're a disgrace to the law! Get out, this instant!" He points at the door.
"Very well, *Mr. Du Bois*. You're a disgrace to the RCM. Get out, this instant!" He points at the door.
"Good god, detective. One more stunt like that and they'll have you institutionalized."
"Now let's go, before you get us into any *more* trouble."
"Remember that guy, Ace Ulsterberg?" the redheaded officer asks. He leans against the doorframe while his bald companion is hunched over an open filing drawer...
"Hmm, the novelty dicemaker also mentioned that she didn't hear any signs of a struggle."
That comports with the dicemaker's testimony as well.
"Of course, I'm sorry I couldn't be the 'break' you were looking for. Good luck with the investigation."
"I have nothing to say to you. Get out of my sight."
The lieutenant lets out a long, nasal sigh.
"The man who was lynched outside your window was from Oranje."

dialoguetext: "Oh? That's unusual. The Oranjese are not the kind of people you associate with heinous crimes. It's such an upstanding and responsible country..."
"Well certainly one cannot rely simply on generalizations -- that would go against our commitment to individual freedoms..."
"That's not how I would describe this guy."
"Yeah, that's all I wanted to say."
"And, of course, any loss of life is a tragedy." The man seems to observe a moment of silence. "So tell me, what have you learned about the victim?"
"After he was discharged from the military he joined a group of mercenaries."
"As a merc, he killed a lot of people on the Semenine Islands to advance Oranjese business interests."
"He liked to get high and brag about war crimes he'd committed."
"That's all. That's who he was."
"His name was Lely."
