dialoguetext: "Lely? That's an interesting name."
"Lely wasn't his real name. It was a *nom de guerre*."
"His name's not really important. What matters is that he was a mercenary."
"Ah, he was a soldier?"
"Aha, a *condottiere*," the man says, as though describing a character from a fantasy novel. "Yes, it's hard to believe they still exist."
"A mercenary."
The man shakes his head solemnly. "A great shame, yes. Colonialism is a dark spectre in Oranje's past..."
"Who's talking about the past? It's still going on!"
(Shake your head too.) "History is very complicated and rarely simple."
(Shrug.) "What's a bunch of dead kipts where there's fortune and glory?"
"...which is *why* the work of the Moralintern is so critical. It is our great bulwark against another century of bloodshed."
"Officer, please! The Moralintern is dedicated to fostering a more tolerant and pluralistic society. There's no room for racial slurs there."
"That is extremely unfortunate. Yes, it's regrettable that this practice has a history in certain Occidental nations, even highly advanced members of EPIS..."

"But rest assured: The Oranjese government has committed to producing a timetable that would lay out a path to transition to a professional army. Soon there'll be no need for mercenaries like this poor man."
"What kind of a timetable are we talking about here?"
"Oh, well that solves that, then."
The man nods. "See? That's the kind of progress that the Moralintern makes possible."
"Oh, it's hard to put an exact date on it. I believe the proposal for the timetable is due to be completed around '60 or '61."
"What? That's like a decade from now!"
"I guess that's better than nothing."
"Extremely distasteful behaviour. I cannot condone either drug use or needless boasting..."
"Suffice it to say, that is *not* how we do things in Sur-la-Clef."
"As I said, the loss of any life is terrible, no matter who the person may have been..."
"I do hope you're able to bring his killer or killers to justice. We must show that the rule of law still applies... even in Revachol."
"What if I told you there's a fugitive from the Moralintern in Martinaise?"
Hypothetically sssspeaking, you might add.
"...hypothetically speaking."
"Well, I would say that is very bad, indeed. Not super."
"What sort of a fugitive are we talking about here?"
"Pretty serious, like corporate espionage-type stuff."
"I think they may have broken into some places."
"I'm pretty sure I saw them littering."
"That is *extremely serious*!"
"This fugitive must be turned over to the ICP immediately. Have you apprehended them already?"
"Oh! Hahaha. A good joke. Very funny. Littering is of course a local offence that need not concern the Moralintern."
"Actually, I think it was way worse than that. Like, corporate espionage."
"Cool. I guess we'll handle it from here."
"Hmmm, that could be *quite* bad, depending on what sort of place you're talking about."
"What if I told you it was the international headquarters of a major corporation?"
"Probably like a Frittte or something."
He won't tell you how to do your job, but a good police officer knows when to listen to his partner.
"Very good. Now was there anything else you'd like to discuss?"
"Ah, well. Burglary is a serious violation of the right to property, but it is a *local* matter. Thus, the Moralintern need not get involved."
"Now, was there something else you wanted to discuss?"
Pin it on someone else.
"Her name is Klaasje and she's already in police custody."
"I meant that as a hypothetical. I don't actually know about any corporate espionage."
"It's Evrart Claire, the head of the Dockworkers' Union."
Now's your chance, ssssire. Which of your enemies would you most like to make trouble for?
What about that gremlin child from behind the Whirling-in-Ragssss?
"There's this ugly-ass kid who hangs out behind the Whirling-in-Rags. He's your guy."
"His name is Garte, and he's working at the Whirling-in-Rags disguised as a cafeteria manager."
"You'll find him hanging out by the roundabout. He's disguised as a really racist lorry driver."
"He'll tell you his name is Raphael, but his real name is Herve, so make sure you call him that."
"There are a bunch of speedfreaks lurking around the church. They confessed while high on drugs."
"Very good. What else then?"
"A bunch of *what*, detective?"
"Kipts. You know."
"Nothing, sorry."
"Yes, well. As I was saying: Colonialism has left a dark legacy in many places, one we must move past, but also never forget."
There seems to be plenty of room for proxy wars waged by multinational corporations, though.
That's because they're all a bunch of squares who like to sit around with their fingers up each other's assholes.
"Ah, that's right. You did say this was all just a *hypothetical* scenario..."
"Whew! For a moment there I was concerned that we had *quite* the situation on our hands..."
"What do you mean 'as a hypothetical'? I don't mean to imply anything, officer, but there's no chance you're *harbouring* a fugitive, is there?"
"A moment, if you don't mind, sir." The lieutenant pulls you aside.
"You do realize what you're doing, don't you?" He whispers to you, *sotto voce*.
"Yeah, I'm turning over a dangerous fugitive."
"Oh, shit, Klaasje could really get in real trouble if I tell him about her, huh?"
"*Very* real trouble..."
The lieutenant looks you straight in the eye, trying to gauge your seriousness.
"I won't tell you how to do your job. But remember, this is an RCM matter. Make sure you weigh your next words carefully."
When you turn back the man is looking at you expectantly.
"A what... a *child*?" He seems confused at first, then disappointed.
"As a common lorry driver, you say? Interesting. Are you sure?"
"Much as I'm inclined to believe you, I'm not sure my colleagues at the ICP will..."
"Evrart Claire? Surely you're mistaken."
"What do you mean? Have you *met* Evrart?"
"He's already planning to go to war with Wild Pines. It's definitely the kind of thing he'd do."
"Besides, in certain less-advanced nations the Moralintern may defer to local custom..."
"I'll make note of your claims in my report, but I'm sorry to say it's likely to end up in the back of a filing cabinet somewhere in Mirova, unread and forgotten."
"He may not look like an corporate spy, but that's what makes him so effective."
The lieutenant makes a strange sound that he quickly smothers.
Was that... did the lieutenant just *snort*?
"A cafeteria manager, you say? How strange. Normally fugitives don't take on such *public* roles."
"He's extremely clever like that. Careful, though, he'll also try to convince you that you owe him money."
"A drug-addled *spy-ring*! That sounds rather *strange*, don't you think?"
"Not nearly as strange as the anodic dance music they're into."
"Drugs make people do *crazy* things sometimes, like steal corporate secrets."
"I *have*. The only thing Evrart is a fugitive from is the *exercise machine*..."
"No, no, no. Evrart would have no need to dirty his hands in such a way..."
"He was a motherfucker and a killer."
"Officer, you shouldn't speak ill of the dead!"
"It's okay, he told me so."
"You're right. That was disrespectful of me."
"He... so you spoke with the victim *before* he died?"
"No, this was after he died."
"Yeah, it was a wild coincidence. Let's move on, though."
The man gives the lieutenant a nervous look.
The lieutenant raises his eyebrows as though he'd stopped paying attention.
Your partner's doing you a favour by pretending not to have heard your insane ramblings.
"I... see. Well, you must be a very thorough detective. So what else did you learn?"
The man seems slightly relieved, as though he's just narrowly survived a perilous bend in the road.
"He was a poor kid before the Oranjese government put him in a military academy."
The man nods. "It's the responsibility of any good welfare state to take care of its most unfortunate citizens."
"They turned him into a psychopathic killing machine!"
"Yeah, he should have been grateful for the help."
"They gave him a successful *career*." The man holds up a finger as though he's made a brilliant point.
"Every one of us has our role to play."
YES. Killing was his business and business was *good*.
Did he love it before they made him do it again and again and again?
"What else has your investigation uncovered?"
'Customs' like blatant, systematic corruption?
"That's a shame."
"That's totally fine."
"Yes, it rather is. As much as I'm a true believer in international institutions, there are times when even I grow frustrated with the bureaucracy..."
"You think it's 'fine' that Martinaise is a safe haven for international fugitives? You know, concern for the rule of law is one of the Moralintern's main criteria for admission into EPIS..."
"Well, no matter. I should thank you for bringing this to our attention. Your efforts have been noted."
"Now, was there anything else you wanted to discuss?"
"What proof do you have that this *child* is involved in corporate espionage?"
"He's a ginger. What else do you need to know?"
"His dad's a major drug kingpin in Martinaise."
"He's been stealing locusts from some cryptozoologists."
"He's been throwing rocks at a corpse."
"He used reactionary slurs on my crime scene."
"Selling drugs is certainly unfortunate, but what does that have to do with corporate espionage?"
"Stealing from misguided pseudo-scientists is unfortunate, but what does that have to do with corporate espionage?"
"Tsk-tsk. Racial slurs certainly have no place in a pluralistic society, but what does that have to do with corporate espionage?"
"Corpse desecration is morally repugnant, but what does that have to do with corporate espionage?"
"What do you mean by that, officer?"
"I'm saying it establishes a *pattern* of criminality. Do I need to get a cork board and some yarn here?"
"It's a slippery slope, man..." (Make a sliding gesture with your hand.) "Real slippery."
"Hmm, that does seem kinda *tenuous* now that you mention it."
"There's no way I can submit this report to the ICP -- they'd have my head examined!"
"*Extremely* tenuous..."
"I suggest you work on your *investigative skills* a bit more before you go around accusing children of crimes."
"Now that that's sorted out, was there anything else you wanted to discuss?"
"Ah, good to hear. Excellent. On behalf of the Moralintern, let me thank you for this service..."
"I'll be sure I make a note of your contributions in my report. Revachol is fortunate to have police officers like you."
"You hear that Kim? Revachol's lucky to have me."
The man nods. "You are a credit to the RCM. If more Revacholians were like you, they might be part of EPIS by now."
"I said 'For almighty Revachol' you deaf frog-eater."
"Just doing my job, sir."
"What the detective means is that he's proud to serve the RCM."
"For almighty Revachol."
"Ah, of course. Carry on then."
"What was that?"
Somehow the man thinks of this as a compliment rather than an expression of patronizing condescension.
"Nothing. Just doing my job."
The lieutenant gives you a sharp look. He's bailed you out, again, but he's none too pleased about it.
"Now that that's settled, was there anything else you'd like to discuss?"
You should have heeded your partner's warning. Now it's too late.
"I'm still looking for the fugitive. I'll report back if I learn anything more."
"I'm afraid I must *insist* that you tell me what you know. Or I'll be forced to make a *very* unfavourable report to my superiors at the Moralintern."
A bullet deftly dodged, ssssire.
"Honour demanded it."
'Customs' like complete disregard for the *Rule of Law*?

"Corporate espionage may technically be legal in *Revachol*, but elsewhere it's a very high-level offence. It violates a number of international agreements, in particular the First La Cherte Accord..."
"I understand that you're here to investigate a *murder*," the man says, his face grave, "but I must impress upon you the *seriousness* of this matter..."
"*Thousands* of corporate secrets may be at stake here. I shudder to think what damage that might do to the international markets..."
The man sighs. "I only pray that the ICP apprehends this fugitive before more corporate secrets are lost..."
"It's certainly serious, sir. But there's also the question of jurisdiction. The Wayfarer Act places certain *strictures* on what matters the RCM may involve itself in."
"You're right, of course. What use are protocols if you don't follow them?"
"Now, was there anything else you wished to discuss?"
"I suspect he doesn't know the half of it."
"Her name is Klaasje and she's at the Whirling-in-Rags."
"Right. That should be enough for the ICP. Very good. On behalf of the Moralintern, let me thank you for this service..."
"Now that that's settled, was there anything else you'd like to discuss?"
"Now that that's settled, was there anything else you'd like to discuss?"
"Aha," he says, his voice suddenly cool. "A *nationalist*, I see. In other circumstances I might be compelled to report you for *sedition*..."
"Well, no matter. You've done the Moralintern a great service regardless of your *personal* views..."
"Ah, very good, then." Your remark seems to have completely vanished from his mind.
What? Are you intimidated by this sissy *bureaucrat*? Mediocre!
He won't, though, because he's nothing but a sissy *bureaucrat*.
"For some reason he gives you a discount if you trash the cafeteria."
Well, that wasn't pretty, but you do seem to have taken the heat off Klaasje, for now.
"You're right, sir. I'll be sure to give the detective an overview of proper police procedure." The lieutenant darts a quick glance in your direction.
That was a wink. Your good cop/idiot cop routine seems to have done the trick.
If he knows so much about Oranje, maybe he also knows about Oranjese mercenaries?
Of course, you're turning over a dangerous LAWBREAKER.
You're dooming a young woman in her hour of desperation.
Stop! Before you do anything, consider the consequences.
What do you mean?
Have you thought about what this might mean for Klaasje?
Don't concern yourself with the feelings of a LAWBREAKER.
Oh, right. She could get in big trouble if I turn her over to the ICP.
What happens to her is no business of mine.
The man looks at you expectantly.
It's your call.
Turn her in now and you'll never get the chance to feel her sweet young flesh against yours.
The lieutenant does his level best to suppress a deep sigh.
That's it. She's done for. Au revoir, Klaasje.
"This is a great relief. The sanctity of corporate secrets is a cornerstone of the international order..."

"The guy who got canned for trying to arrest that diplomat?" the bald man asks. "Well, *technically* he got canned for being shit-faced on the job. But yeah, trying to arrest the ambassador from Gottwald *while* shit-faced was probably a contributing factor..."
The bald man squints at a file, then returns it to the cabinet. A new drawer opens with a grinding screech. He turns back to the redhead in the doorway. "What made you think of him now?"
"Don't know. He just kinda popped into my mind." "Ahem, excuse me, Chester," says a female officer who threads her way into the file room. "Where is old Ace now?" the bald officer asks.
Here the female officer chimes in: "I believe he's part of a certain bureaucrat's security detail." "No fucking way!" The redhead is dumbfounded. "How'd he pull that off?"
"Family connections, I'd imagine? His father-in-law works for the Office of Standards and Best Practices." With that, the woman exits, a grey file folder tucked under her arm.
"Sounds like the victim was unconscious. Or at least incapacitated. Interesting."
Consequences? I don't care about consequences!
Do you not care for anyone other than yourself? Have you thought about what this might mean for Klaasje?
He nods. "Anything else?"

dialoguetext: "Already?" He glances at his watch. "Well, I'm glad I could help."
"I'm trying to form a committee to assign *la responsabilité*."
"My friend, if it's *la responsabilité* you're after, I have good news for you: There's no need to form such a committee, because it already exists!"

"The Comité de Responsabilité de Revachol. It acts as a sort-of clearinghouse for Coalition activities. To put it simply, they are the ultimate arbiters of la responsabilité in this part of the world."
"I would offer to connect you with the committee myself, but alas, I am not actually *in* Martinaise."
Yes, this is just the sort of reasonable authority you're looking for!
What? Where is he, then?
You *knew* there was something strange about this one! He's an astral projection, a phantasm!
He's speaking figuratively. He means he's not in Martinaise in his *official* capacity.
"What are you talking about? I'm looking at you right now!"
"Isn't it? A triumph of both technical ingenuity and international cooperation. I, for one, feel much safer knowing it's up there, watching all of us."
"Of course, we are speaking informally, but *officially* I am still in La Delta, preparing for an upcoming conference on fuel oil derivatives..."
(Attempt to stick your hand through his astral form.)
"I got it. You're only here on *personal* business."
"So... where *are* you, then?"
"So what am I supposed to do?"
"Unauthorised circuit-bending is a very serious matter with grave security implications, but as of the moment there is no specific law *forbidding* it, in Revachol at least..."
"Précisément. *Officially* I am still in La Delta, preparing for an upcoming conference on fuel oil derivatives..."
"Why, *officially* I am still in La Delta, preparing for an upcoming conference on fuel oil derivatives. I'm only in Martinaise in an unofficial capacity..."
"Mais que faites-vous, officer?" Your hand bumps up against the man's solid if somewhat fleshy chest.
"That's why it would be extremely irregular, or potentially even *inappropriate* for me to intercede with the Committee concerning a district I'm not officially in."
"Unfortunately not, no, I don't have the pleasure. I am merely a representative of the Coalition Government, not very well-versed in technology..."
"Well, of course it *is* a heavily armed and armoured warship with a full complement. But I assure you its purpose in Revachol is to *keep* the peace, not disturb it."
"Yes, I was wondering the same thing."
You *will* figure it out. Something tells you the person you're looking for is already on this coast...
Don't let the paintjob fool you, it's a goddamn killing machine, and there's nothing you can do to stop it!
Perhaps your new friends in the tent might be able to help you?
"I don't think I've ever noticed it before."
This sounds like something that programmer you met in the church might help with...
"Oh, right. The *Archer*. I thought you said... something else."
Don't let the shiny lights fool you, it's a goddamn killing machine, and there's nothing you can do to stop it!
"Oh, good: 'Techno-tinkerers.' Just what this *side task* was missing..."
"Hmmm, perhaps your young friends in the *tent* might be of assistance?"
"You said you weren't really here. I had to make sure you weren't an astral projection."
"Nothing, just lost my balance a moment."
"Hmmm, sounds like something that programmer we met in the church might be able to help with..."
"But this is an urgent matter. I *need* to get in touch with the Committee."
"How am I supposed to contact the Committee then?"
"Are you saying I should just give up?"
No, it's more like a creature from the abyssopelagic zone, a great dark bioluminescent fish...
It's about four-and-a-half kilometres from your position, you estimate.
"Ah, well, I'm glad to hear that at least. It would really be *quite unusual* for you to have never noticed it before..."
"No, no, don't be silly. We're simply speaking in an informal capacity. *Officially* I am still in La Delta, preparing for an upcoming conference on fuel oil derivatives..."
"Perhaps your blood sugar is a bit low? As I was saying, *officially* speaking I am still in La Delta, preparing for an upcoming conference on fuel oil derivatives..."
Not just any fish, it moves like some ancient bottom-feeder gliding over the ocean floor in search of prey...
"Yes, you've made your *persistence* quite clear. Under normal circumstances I would have to insist you go through the regular channels."
The man frowns. "Well, under ordinary circumstances, the Committee contacts *you*."
"I don't mean to discourage you, of course, just to say that it won't be *easy* to reach the Committee."

"Interesting. In a sense, that's the very idea. The Coalition doesn't want the people of Revachol to feel that they are under a *military* occupation. That is why the Archer is always careful to maintain a constant, discreet distance."
No, no. You can't let them give you the runaround.
In other words, the committee only knows what it *wants* to know.
Not exactly a model of accessible and accountable governance...
"But if you have information of a vital interest, they might be willing to entertain an exception. In which case, I would advise you to contact them via Coalition Warship Archer."
It looks, to your eye, like some kind of long, metallic fish, suspended beneath a number of ceiling fans...

"That is part of the idea, of course. The Coalition doesn't want the people of Revachol to feel that they are under a *military* occupation. That is why the Archer is always careful to maintain a constant, discreet distance."
"I suppose there might be some way to *circuit-bend* your way onto those frequencies, but you'd have to be one of those *techno-tinkerers* to do it."
"Fascinating. I always thought it was more like a dragonfly. But isn't it interesting how humanity always finds inspiration in nature?"
"That, my friend, is your responsabilité. I cannot take it from you, nor can you delegate it to someone else..."
"Is that... legal?"
"Wait, what's Coalition Warship Archer?"
"So how does one go about contacting a Coalition warship?" (Proceed.)
"Officer? You mean to say you haven't noticed the giant Coalition aerostatic peacefully patrolling the skies over Revachol?"
"Huh. Can't believe I never noticed it before."
"This is quite the problem, very tricky. Of course, the Archer has orders to fire on any unidentified aerostatics that might approach it, so it might be safer to get in touch *from the ground*..."
"It looks like a killing machine."
"It looks like a fish."
"It's amazing. An inspiring symbol."
"Do you know any of these tinkerers?"

"But in that case, you would require a radio transmitter capable of broadcasting on Coalition frequencies. And that kind of technology naturally isn't typically available for non-Coalition use. Yes, it *is* a bit of a conundrum."
You look out the window toward the north. There, hanging some distance above the horison, you can just make out a strange silhouette...
You look out the window toward the north. There, amidst the low-hanging stars, you can just make out signs of motion...
You look out the window, but you can't see anything. But then, it's dark, and your eyes aren't the sharpest...
It's a set of position lights moving in unison, like a restless constellation...
You look around, but you don't see anything unusual. Then again, your eyes aren't the sharpest...
"Let me just say that I have *complete confidence* in the RCM. I'm sure you'll figure something out."
"Why do I need to go through Archer to speak to the Committee?"
"I find it a great comfort to know there are benevolent powers watching over all, in strict accordance with the Wayfarer Act and the Bristelmüne Conventions."
"You see, in addition to being an airborne artillery platform, Coalition Warship Archer is also the linchpin of the Coalition's surveillance and communications infrastructure in Revachol."
"And listening! It has the most objective vantage point in the entire city. Not to mention a vast array of radio, photographic, and meteorological monitoring instruments."

The Bristelmüne Conventions are a series of international agreements governing the treatment of military personnel and civilians in theatres of war as well as occupied territories. In practice, they are more talked about than observed.
"Hold on, it's *watching* us, too?"
"A *fugitive*?"

"I can't believe it, Cuno's dad isn't a loser! It *must* be someone else."

A pair of half-open bug eyes is staring back at you from the dark, empty and frozen. It's clear that the person behind them is not awake.

A groan rises from the man's throat, dry like a death rattle... He's trying to say something in his sleep.

The bear is trying to wake up!

dialoguetext: "Thanks, I'm off." [Leave.]

She mumbles some kind of a response, then hacks something into her handkerchief.

"De Ruyters are at the end of this hallway, right next to the communal bathroom."

"Tell me about the man who lives at the end of the hallway -- Uuno de Ruyter."

"They don't like me cleaning behind their door, think I'm listening in on their fights."

"What are you doing here?"
She sighs and looks around. "I need to get it ready for the next lease, but as you can see, the previous tenant completely trashed the place."
"Reprehensible. Who lived here?"
"It was some kind of a moribund old man, who used to be a business owner. You'd think they'd make rent..." She stops, hesitating.
"Do you want to see my ID as well? You can't *legally* ask for it, but why not? Want to see my residence permit, too?" She fumbles through her purse, fishing out a light paper-clad passport.
It feels flimsy in hand, with the words 'Revachol Zone of Control' written under a nondescript municipal logo. There's a picture of her with shorter hair inside, along with all her personal details.
"But -- that was months ago. Anyway. Was there anything you wanted, or is that it? I'm in a hurry."
"Oh, that's another huge mess. The former tenant owes us three months of rent, *three*! We closed the apartment and planned on auctioning off the valuables, but..."
"Of course," she replies with a smile, but her eyes remain glazed over -- she's been waiting for you to leave.
"Don't ask me what happened with the wall, I have no idea how we're going to find the time or resources to fix it."
"*Both* apartments are now unrentable. Both!" She's still shaking her head, manicured hands now crossed over the chest.
"And again, I have no idea how *stupid* mistakes like this can even happen, but Ron, when he came to close the door, didn't close the neighbouring door! And there's a hole in the wall!"
"A hole in the wall, can you believe it?" She spreads her hands. "And then the tenant ran off with his stuff. He's gone, the *money's* gone, just like that!" She snaps her fingers.
"So wait, what happened with the wall?" (Proceed.)
"It couldn't have been that much money. These apartments look pretty shabby."
"These apartments are perfectly fine! They have gorgeous architecture, a million reál view of the bay, good ventilation, neighbours, life, spark... And they are affordable."
"My money has also disappeared, I think."
"Well, it does *not* disappear from my hands, no, I don't let it."
"I'll tell you, Martinaise has a future -- in a few years it's going to blossom with artists and creatives and those radiocomputer wizards."
A sudden serious look crosses her face. This story didn't have a happy ending.
"Everything seems to be in order." (Hand back the passport.)
"Thank you." She slips the passport back in her purse. "Do you have any questions? I need to be back in midtown in an hour."
"What now?" She crosses her arms impatiently.
"Nice haircut." (Hand back the passport.)
"Sounds like they knew how to have a good time."
The *radiocomputer wizards* are invested with magical economic powers.
Boy there are a lot of different keys there. More than *twenty* at least...
Her voice is really cheerful despite her obviously *hating* you.
Be friendly.
"I fuck shit up too."
"Heh!" She smiles aggressively. "Sounds like you've spent too much time undercover in some rock band."
"Who lived here?"
It's not a compliment.
"I glimpsed a *foreclosed* apartment down the hallway."
So preppy! She's probably on some low grade performance enhancers. Like Preptide or Pericanine.
The sum must've been puny.
Oh, it irks her. The *incompetence*.
It's as if they're *real* wizards, able to resurrect dead real estate and breathe life into bank accounts.
"Isn't it a bit late to be working?"
"It *is*." She breathes in and out to the count of three -- it looks like some special stress release technique -- before she continues...
"Everyone says that real estate agents don't *do* anything, but here I am, in the middle of the night, cleaning up someone's 'crash pad'."
"So, the sooner we get this over with, the better." She means you -- time for the next question.
Come to think of it, she *does* look incredibly tired.
A phone book lies open on the table, covering a stack of utility bills. Right next to it, in plain sight, sits a small bottle of amphetamine, conveniently equipped with a straw.
"Lieutenant, I've located psychoactive substances on this table."
Take the speed from the table.
[Leave.]
"Good, confiscate it."
You pocket the bottle as if it were the most natural thing in the world.
Don't wait, celebrate! Blast that shit right here! Take inventory of it once this boring table shit is done!
You could slip the bottle right into your pocket -- the lieutenant wouldn't even notice...
Blast it before you face the beast, de Ruyter. You're going to need the encouragement.
Score! It's right there, baby. Today's your lucky day.
The minuscule amount of amphetamine doesn't interest the lieutenant in the slightest. He listens instead to something in the other room.
A former architect stands before a slice of window, a room plan in her hand. A cold wave has made the air in the building stand still and frozen, with temperatures falling down to -20°C.
Her face...
The plan...
Shiver. [Finish thought.]
...is red from the cold. She's breathing on her fingers clasping the plan. Traces of sadness are visible in her expression.
... faint pencil lines on paper depict the same place, but a missing eastern wall connects the room with the neighbouring apartment. Ideas for arranging the furniture have been jotted down.
It's clean and empty, with new tapestry embellishing the walls. A standard HB graphite pencil has fallen off a three-legged stool in the middle of the room.
Look around yourself...
She had an eye for beauty.
A shift in temperature. The air chills around you. Dust settles on the stony floor.
[Discard thought.]
Rub your sides for warmth.
What happened here?
You can't foreclose on an apartment with a hole in the wall.
[Discard thought.]
It will still be accessible through the apartment next to it. That one didn't have a door... Sadly, nothing of great value remains here.
Except the stuff in the fridge.
There's always a little something in the fridge.
This looks so sad...
Put your emotions aside. Try to focus on abstract, impersonal things.
But this reeks of sadness!
Indeed!
That isn't *just* a five-pointed star -- it's an inverted white pentagram cradled in a wreath of antlers. The iconography of communism, in other words.
Inspect the symbol closer.
[Discard thought.]
The star-and-antlers was developed in the sixth decade of the last century and quickly adopted by Mazov and the communards during the Revolution...
Why is the star upside down?
What's the deal with the antlers?
Why white?
To symbolize the toppling of the old order.
What does it evoke in me? [Finish thought.]
The wreath of antlers represents a natural crown. It was about building a society that could exist in accord with the natural world -- and at the same time above it.
Also, some social democrats were already using it.
Because white is the colour of peace.
Gone. Gone is the glory. Of hope, only the scribblings of impoverished students remain. In dirty hallways...
You are the Big Communism Builder now. It's you or no one.
You see noble aims but also mountains upon mountains of corpses. They should've taken a more *measured* approach. Also, you're really smart.
Smug superiority? Esthetic musings? The triumph of Capital is undeniable, but... maybe the guns were sort of cool? Revolutionaries had loads of guns.
Nothing at all yet. Right now it's just meaningless shapes on a wall.
The price of idealism unrestrained by humanism. Never again.
Communism is the ideology of gutless intellectuals and clueless university students. They don't care about the *real* wörking man.
In other words, it doesn't mean a thing to *trüe* Revacholians.
Whatever kid drew this graffito will get it one day. You just can't beat FREEDOM and hustle-jiggling all the time.
"Look out, Kim: There are communists around here."
Even today, half a century after, the star-and-antlers retains the ability to evoke hope, disappointment, and fear in equal measure.
"I'll keep my Armistice handy, detective."
He doesn't actually reach for his gun.
Oops, it's a fashion faux pas! [Discard the thought -- and the shoes!]

Mm, the luxury of fine things. Just look at those black monk straps! After spending an entire day hustling, who's to say that you *didn't* deserve a pair of ridiculously expensive shoes on your tired feet?
You're right, beautiful things do make people happy...
Beautiful things give you a *rush*. It's power -- crafting your style, draping your flesh in silk and leather, deciding how to present yourself to the world.
Remember, when they come to take it *away* from you -- you *worked* for those shoes. Whether you like it or not, wearing these shoes has made you more liberal -- *ultra*liberal.
Let's hope no one saw you wearing these outrageously expensive -- and ultraliberal! -- shoes.
They're either a gateway drug -- or a booster pack -- to get you *deeper* into free market ideology.

The pockets of these new jeans are perfect for sticking your hand into. Makes you look cool, calm, and collected. As your hand enters the pocket, your fingers brush against something... soft, yet crinkly.
Take the item out.
Hey! It's a chewing gum wrapper. It reminds you of the fruity juice of apricots. You should inspect it closer if you have time. Something about the wrapper's texture is familiar...

By the way, the raw materials were most likely exported from Siigay (the Apricot Suzerainty) and processed in Sur-La-Clef into the apricot-flavoured chewing gum loved by kids of today -- and yesterday. Hmm. Something about it *is* familiar... And not only to your fingers.
*Not* familiar in a good way, you might say. There's pain in there somewhere...
A crinkled chewing gum wrapper. The worn label reads: 'Tutti Frutti.' It smells faintly of apricots, with a barely noticeable twinge of cinnamon.
There it is again -- the scent of apricots, with a touch of cinnamon. Smells like the end of some distant summer. The surface of another planet, or some ancient temple.
Why do I even care about this?
I'll hang on to it, just in case.
Take a deep, *deep* breath.
[Put the wrapper away.]
Good question, There is no answer or secret phrase written on the inside of the wrapper. Yet you're drawn to it.
Drawn by regret. Stop, before you *hurt* yourself with the Tutti Frutti wrapper. Throw it away, please.
Bitter, citrus, sweet, it seems to grow stronger, like a glow, with every breath you take...
Feels so, so familiar.
Feels very, very familiar. Harry. Please. You were supposed to discard it.
Your heart working overtime, trying to keep up with the panicked synapses firing all over your brain. Moving litres of blood through you, panicking.
Cinnamon's not a fruit.
You feel compelled to point out that there's nothing fruity about cinnamon -- It's a spice derived from tree bark.
Can a used wrapper shrug? It seems like that's what the wrapper is doing, somehow. This is not about flowers, or bark? What *is* this about? Why are you looking at this wrapper?
End of summer...
Whatever petrochemical by-products they used to create this artificial flavour have bonded tightly to the wrapper. Or is that just your memory, filling in the gaps?
The sun sets into the sea, but the water does not boil. Instead it turns to liquid gold. For a moment, the world's store of precious metals seems to increase dramatically, and you are rich...
There is a movement next to you. The shuffle of a small coat. Warm, like the evening. But when you turn toward it there's nothing there...
Where did it go?
Wait, come back!
Why are you talking to a gum wrapper?
You neatly fold the wrapper into a square before you put it back into your pocket. Carefully. Lovingly even...
... until a blossom of skin and flower petals erupts behind your closed eyes. Made of toffee, cream, and distance. You just *had* to take a dive.
You carefully fold the wrapper into a square, before putting it back into your pocket. Lovingly even -- despite the strange feeling of regret.
Ancient temple?
Yes. From the height of antiquity. A long, long time ago. Millennia ago. On an island of time you can never return to.
"So, the death notification..." the lieutenant says as soon as you've left the apartment.
"I'm sorry, I know I fucked up."
"There's nothing to discuss, let's move on." [Leave.]
"Well, I'll call the station when we're done with the day and inform them about the identity of the deceased."
"You did well," the lieutenant says as soon as you've left the apartment. The balcony feels cool and quiet, with a stunning view over the sleeping district.
(Nod.) "What now?"
"Great, the case is closed then." [Leave.]
"I'll call the station when we're finished with the day and let them know the name of the deceased."
"Sure, I'll call the station when we're done with the day. Let's go."
"It's alright, don't worry about it." His eyes wander over the sleeping district.
"I could have done more."
"You did enough." He pauses, rubbing his hands together to generate some heat.
"I'll call the station when we're finished with the day and let them know the name of the deceased."
"But yes, that's on me. Let's get on with the murder investigation."
"It's alright, don't worry about it." His eyes wander over the streets.
"I'll call the station tomorrow and let them know the name of the deceased."
"That's it?"
"What about Billie and her kids?"
"That's it. We should get back to our case. There's nothing more we can do here."
"There's not much we can do for them anymore, I'm afraid."
"Right, lets try to get back to it then." [Leave.]
He looks at you. "And... officer -- I've seen worse. This wasn't the worst I've seen, okay? Now, let's go."
"Can't save the whole world, you know?"
Say nothing.
"I'll call the station tomorrow and let them know the name of the deceased."
"What about Billie and her kids?"
He nods. "Let's go."
"That's it?"
"They'll manage."
"Right, this is closed then." [Leave.]
"That's it. We should get back to our case now that our duty here is done."
"Anyway, I'll call the station when we're finished with the day and let them know the name of the deceased."
"Anyway, I'll call the station tomorrow and let them know the name of the deceased."
He's avoiding your gaze. This is the time to say how sorry you are about how things went.
"That did not go..."
"*Well*? No, it didn't."
Can't bring the dead back.
They have to. It's not your place to live their lives.
They have to. It's not your place to live their lives.
I really have, he thinks. She was strong. She made it easy for us.

You look south, over the crumbling balustrade. There -- 1.2 kilometres away -- a piece of broken stone cuts into the sky. A tomb. On it, a mural that used to say: tomorrow is just a whisper away. You cannot *really* see the Feld building from here, but somehow you feel like you should return to it.
Take the speed. Take that glorious stuff. You have it now. You've got it! TAKE IT!
Let's get fucked up.
No. Not right now, anyway. [Discard thought.]
Come on. Come on! A little! Just a little bit! Whaddya say, huh?
FUCKING RIGHT! PUT THAT BOTTLE IN YOUR HAND AND PARTY DOWN!
Maybe just a little...
I said I discard the thought! [Discard thought.]
Fuck you. You used to be cool. Why can't you just take the bottle and snort snort snort?
Just a little. Then a lot. Come on, party boy! Let's get FUCKED!
I am yours... So nearly...
That's great. Tell me what circle I've got to run into this time.
I will be there soon. Wherever it is!
You better be ready when I find you, weird voice! I'm going to hurt you!
Yes... Reunion...! Listen within the circles that capture the electrical world… If you can hear me then, we will be united…
So near... Listen within the circles that capture the electrical world… If you can hear me then, we will be united…
Please do not... Just listen within the circles that capture the electrical world… If you can hear me then, we will be united…
"I'm alright, you can leave now..."
"Please just leave..."
"Hello, detective."
"Make this quick, detective."
"Governmental issues take me all over Revachol as you can see."
"Someone is always watching."
"None of z'is is weird."
"In a *wider* sense z'is is actually my apartment. And yours."
"If we can ensure *stabilité*, progress will naturally follow."
"*Transparence* has always been our highest priority."
"All of z'is is perfectly normal. A bit mundane if anything."
"I don't z'ink conclusions should be rushed at z'is point."
"A *politicien* is never off z'e clock."
"Moderacy in everything -- even in moderacy."
"Everyone needs to share z'e *responsabilité*."
"If *stabilité* is ensured, progress will naturally follow."
You can hear animated voices coming from the other side of the grille.
As you approach the metal grille you can hear several voices having what appears to be an animated discussion.
This must be it. Beyond this door lies the beating heart of radical communism in Martinaise.

Somehow the night air softens the smell of trash and sea brine. As the breeze pulls through the canvas like a shuttle through a loom you catch a hint of something unexpected, something earthy, warm, and burnt...
The acrid smell of failure...
No, that's just slightly burnt coffee. A smell you would recognise anywhere.
"Just look at this pig, sniffing about after-hours..."
"Why didn't you say the secret door was *right behind you*?"
"Hey, it's past curfew! Get to bed, Cindy!"
(Ignore her.)
"Must have slipped my mind. You know how it goes." She gives you a lackadaisical shrug.
"Go ahead and arrest me, officer. I swear I'll go peacefully." You can feel her smirk through the dark.
The metal grille is cool to the touch.
You notice the lieutenant is looking uncustomarily anxious. His posture is rigid, his right hand hovers near the zipper of his jacket.
He wants so badly to draw his Armistice, but he also doesn't *want* to want to draw it.
"You okay, Kim?"
"Relax, they're only communists."
Say nothing.
"Oh, I'm fine. I was practically *born* to infiltrate underground communist cells..." He takes a quick look over his shoulder.
"Something's not right here. The equation doesn't quite balance..." He taps his foot and takes a deep breath.
"Well, detective. It seems we've located your underground cell..." He looks over the balcony, down toward the water.
"Which is just to say: We should be prepared for *any* eventuality."
The metal grille is cool to the touch. The long stretches of canvas billow like sails in the night breeze.
Try to listen.
"Hey, it's me again!" (Knock on the grille.)
Bang on the grille.
[Leave.]
The clang of metal reverberates all along the scaffolding. The voices coming from the other side fall silent.
You can make out at least two separate voices.
You hear the voices conferring once again.
A pair of frightened hares cowering in some dark crevice of their burrow.
The voices are male, you think. Beyond that, you can't tell...
"He came back?" There's a note of surprise in the voice. "Do you have the passphrase this time?"
"Who's there? Is that you, Maurice?"
"It's not Maurice, it's the police!"
"That's right. It is I... Maurice."
"Are you all communists? I'm looking for some communists."
"Ever hear of the Wayfarer Act, you Coalition pawn? Come back when you've got a warrant, or when you've woken up to your own class interests."
"That's exactly why I'm here! I'm trying to get organised. Can you help me?"
"Come crawling back already? Get out of here, traitor!"
"I'm not actually Maurice. I'm trying to get organised. Can you help me?"
"That's right!" Another voice jumps in. "Take your miniscule, bourgeois turnips and get lost!"
Face it, sire, your little subterfuge isn't leading anywhere.
"Who said communist? Did *we* say communist? Get out of here."
"Listen, I've already built like .0001% of communism but now I need to get organised. Can you help me?"
For a moment, silence.
A slight sensation of static electricity, as before a storm. A miniature conference is taking place inside, and you are the subject.
"What's the passphrase?"
"It's 'We await the silent mole empire'."
"It's 'The end times cometh'."
"It's 'Disco Supernova'."
"It's 'Blessed are the sausage grinders'."
"It's 'Remember Dobreva and Abadanaiz'."
"Can't I get a hint at least?"
"Look, I don't know your passphrase. Could you just let me in?"
"Not a chance. We can't afford to compromise our operation, not at this point. Come back when you know the passphrase."
"Look at that, the pig's trying to break in without the passphrase. Tsk, tsk." The girl shakes her head slowly.
"Let's go, detective. We'll get nowhere standing around in the rain." The lieutenant wipes back a wet lock of hair.
"Let's go, detective. We'll get nowhere standing around here in the dark." The moonlight reflects white in the lieutenant's glasses.
"Let's go, detective. We'll get nowhere standing around in the snow." The lieutenant brushes a few scales of snow off his jacket.
There's no response. You begin to wonder whether they've slipped out some back way...
No! They're still there. You can *feel* them back there.
"Alright. The key's taped to the back of the doorframe. Just make sure you put it back when you're done or we'll all be locked out..."
"And do watch the concrete. It just kind of... falls away... in places."
"*Charmant*. After you, detective."
"Have fun at your *underground meeting*, pig. Hope it's a *blast*."
"Are you locked out of your radiocomputer or something? No, it's not '1234'."
"No, it's not. We don't do ironic passphrases here."
"Not even close."
"He said something about moles. Perhaps he's just a night-wandering lunatic."
"Did he say something about sausages?" The voice appears completely confused by your response
"Perhaps he's drunk?" the other voice asks.
Two voices, both male. Approximately early 20s.
"... Careful with those now..."
"I have it. It's going to work, I can feel it..."
"Would you mind? We've got *group business* to take care of."
"That means go home, gendarme."
The two young men are either oblivious to or ignoring your entrance. Their attentions are fixed on whatever it is they're stacking in the middle of the floor...

dialoguetext: "The gendarme returns." The young man turns to you. "What do you need?"
"You're back." The young man turns to you.
His eyes are tracing an invisible line back and forth from your jacket to his companion.
What a coincidence! You two have the *same* jacket. What are the odds?
Based on the prevalence of white Saramirizian suits in Martinaise? Extremely low.
"Hey, Steban. Isn't that *your* jacket?"
"It certainly *looks* like my jacket, Ulixes. Where did you get that, gendarme?"
"I just found it... in a room."
"Must be a coincidence. I see these jackets all the time."
"This jacket is RCM property. It's been confiscated as part of an ongoing investigation."
[Leave.]
"'Confiscated'? Next he's probably going to say it was civil asset forfeiture..."
"Unlikely. That's real Saramirizian twill. Only old Saramirizian communists and drug smugglers wear those anymore..."
He is neither of those, of course. He is simply a poor student, putting on airs. Also, he doesn't have the shoulders to fill out such a jacket.
"See, Uli? It's just like Mazov wrote. How does it go again?"
Damn right. If he keeps mouthing off, you should take his pants too.
"'Those committed to the rights of property are those most apt to violate them'." His companion nods emphatically.
"I assumed it was Maurice who broke into my room, to play a trick on me. I didn't think I'd *actually* been raided by the RCM!"
Just a minute. Steban... Ulixes... *why* do those names ring the faintest of bells?
Probably because they're the real names of 'Nasteb' and 'Exilus', the authors of that so-called essay about TipTop Tournée you read...
You should get to the bottom of this, when you have the chance.
There is surprise in his voice, naturally, but is that a note of *excitement* you also detect?
"So, do you want your jacket *back*?"
"Listen, comrade, it's not what it looks like..."
"Why do you sound *excited* to be raided by the RCM?"
"Look, man, it doesn't even fit you, anyway."
"Absolutely not. You have to keep it..."
"You're right. It's *better*!"
"Oh, gendarme, because this is perfect..."
"You're right. It was a gift from my grandmother. But now you've *got* to keep it..."
He turns to his companion. "Can you imagine the look on Maurice's face when he finds out the RCM has been kicking my door down?"
"He'll shit himself! Positively."
"And now they've shown up *in force* to break up our meeting!" He rubs his hands together excitedly.
"And now they've sent one of their agents to *infiltrate* our meeting." He rubs his hands together excitedly.
The lieutenant sighs. "Something tells me these young men are not very experienced with law enforcement."
"Hold on, I'm not here to *infiltrate* your meeting. I want to *join* your meeting!"
"The RCM wants to join us?" A quizzical expression...
"My partner, of course, is acting in a strictly *personal capacity*, not as an official representative of the RCM."
"Interesting. Does that mean you've done the reading?"
One leader and one follower, the most ancient power dynamic.
There's a great deal of tension in this young man's shoulders, more than someone his age should bear...
Meanwhile, his companion inclines toward him, eager to catch every word that dribbles from his friend's mouth.
Just a moment -- could this be the former owner of a certain jacket you 'acquired' recently?
Don't let them see you *flustered*, ssssire. Play along...
"Before we move on, do you recognise this jacket?" (Show him the Saramirizian jacket.)
"You weren't exactly easy to find."
"What am I late *for* exactly?"
(Play along.) "My apologies, comrades. I had to be sure I wasn't being tailed... by our *class enemies*."
[Leave.]
"That's the whole point, of course. We can't just have *anybody* waltzing in here. Martinaise is crawling with reactionary infiltrators."
"There are RCM spies, for one. Just recently, someone even broke into my apartment, if you can believe it..."
"To say nothing of Gottwaldians and Econoclards."
The young man's companion reflexively snorts at the mention of Gottwaldians and Econoclards.
"Are you saying you *haven't* done the reading for tonight?"  The two young men look at one another.
Uh oh. No one said anything about *reading*. You'll just have to wing this one.
"Mmmm." The young man considers you a moment...
He's taking your measure. Like an ideological boxer stepping into the ring.
This must be the *theory combat* the boiadeiro warned you about! En garde!
"We all have to take precautions, especially during these delicate times. What matters is that you've made it, and that you've done the reading."
(Just wing it.) "The reading, yes. I've *definitely* done that."
"What is this *reading*? I thought this was a revolutionary group!"
"There must be some misunderstanding. No one mentioned any reading."
(Whisper.) "Kim, did *you* do the reading?"
"You have? Excellent. Let's hear your critique then."
"Yes, a revolutionary *reading* group. The most ideologically advanced materialist reading group in Martinaise. But it sounds like that's news to you..."
"Well, this is getting awkward. I'm not sure what you were expecting to find here then..."
"No, detective. The only reading I've been doing is right here..." The lieutenant holds up his little blue notebook.
There's profound consternation in his voice. You suspect it's about something bigger than your not having done the reading.
"Maybe he can explain himself."
He seems to be wagging the notebook at you, as though he suspects you may have forgotten why you're here.
"I have not had time to seek out pretentious communist book clubs, nor have I done their 'reading'."
"It doesn't sound like he's done the reading, Steban."
"Go ahead." The young man gives you a half-smile. His companion sniffs.
"I liked... the characters and the plot."
"I thought the themes were... *interesting*."
"There were... too many words."
"Characters? What characters are you talking about?"
"They always say that when they haven't done the reading."
"Too many... *words*?"
"Yes, but if the writer just cut a few I'm sure it would be fine."
"What *exactly* are you two doing here?"
"In the most general sense, I would say we're cultivating revolutionary consciousness."
"But more specifically, we're running a reading group, the most rigorous and theoretically advanced materialist reading group in Martinaise."
"Comrade Steban is a great discussion leader. One of the best at the university."
It's obvious they take this 'group' of theirs extremely seriously. Whatever you do, *don't* compare it to a common book club.
*YAWWWWN!* Can you imagine anything duller than a bunch of binoclards yanking each others' knobs?
"Is this where I can square off in *theory combat*?"
"Sounds like a place for intense intellectual engagement. Exactly my kind of jam."
"Sounds just like a regular book club."
"Sounds like a yank-fest for binos."
"We have been known to get into some *spirited* debates. But it's always in service of our larger intellectual and ideological project."
"That's our whole *thing*. The world is so shallow, all noise and repetition. We're interested in genuinely radical critique."
"It's really nothing like that." The young man scoffs. "A book club is a place for talking about the plot points of bourgeois social novels and sipping effervescent cocktails."

"It's nothing like that. A yank-fest is a decadent bourgeois phenomenon, a pastime for over-educated office workers who lack proper revolutionary outlets for their social dissatisfactions and repressed sexuality."
"Repressed sexualities are something of an *idée fixe* of his."
"But now we're getting hung up on the pathologies of capitalism. Let's move on."
"One of capitalism's more banal pathologies. But let's move on."
"That doesn't sound so bad," the lieutenant says. "In any case, it's healthier than certain *other* after-hours pursuits I've seen officers engage in." He gives you a pointed look.
Extremely different from discussing the aesthetic merits of avant-garde literature while quaffing a fine Mirovan red, eh, Art Cop?
"Precisely. We're not interested in senseless parroting. We like to read *critically*."
"Within the contours of Mazovian historical materialism, of course."
"I didn't realise they taught radical Mazovian theory in the universities."
“Kim, can we arrest these kids for truancy?”
"Okay, so what does your reading group actually *read*?"
"I think I get the idea. Let me ask about something else."
"We study all the foundational texts of Mazovian theory, of course. Just last week we finished the second volume of Puncher and Wattmann's 'Innocence of Capital'..."
"Truly extraordinary."
"And before that we spent six weeks on 'State and Plasm'..."
For some reason the word *plasm* catches in your ear like a piece of old wax.
Uh oh, you can feel your attention span rapidly deteriorating...
This is fine. You can handle a list. In fact, you find the tedium strangely soothing.
Force yourself to keep listening.
"We've also read Wertmüller's 'The Mega-Structure of History,' and before that, 'Reál and Reality'..."
Communist theorists love puns, in case that wasn't obvious.
"Abelard's 'Un Pays Infernal'..."
"The original Fizdale translation, not that watered-down revisionist garbage."
These two deserve the Order of Honour for Bullshitting. There's no way they've actually *read* all this stuff.
"Obviously." He snorts.
"But, of course, our *special emphasis* is on the theories of Ignus Nilsen and his followers, especially the infra-materialists."
One of Kras Mazov's closest associates, Ignus Nilsen was a leading political and military figure in the Antecentennial Revolution.
Why do you always leave out the good parts? Tell him how he got his *true name*, right now!

Oh, right. During the disastrous retreat from Graad to Samara, Nilsen personally ordered up to 12,000 prisoners of war impaled on sharpened spruce trees in the Samaran backcountry. Thereafter his opponents began referring to him as the 'Apocalyptic Shrike'.

Today, Nilsen's reputation has waned in most parts of the developed world, with the exception of the People's Republic of Samara (SRV), where he is recognized as a founding father. His political philosophy is a variant of Mazovianism called Nilsenist-Mazovianism.
"Comrade Nilsen, father of the SRV." (Raise your fist.)
"Ignus Nilsen? He's not so popular these days, is he?"
"Isn't he the guy who had all those prisoners impaled on spruce trees?"
The young man raises his fist in reply and gives you a curt nod.
"Only because certain moralists and their ideological lap dogs pretend to object to his more *maximalist* tactics... as though they've never committed any so-called 'war crimes'."
"This gendarme talks just like a moralist. They *love* getting on their high horses about so-called 'war crimes'."
The young man grimaces. It seems he's less than 100% comfortable with war crimes.

"He *also* happens to be the greatest communist theorist after Mazov himself. It was Nilsen who first postulated the existence of ideological plasm, which forms the basis of infra-materialist theory."
Those words again! You've got to find out what this infra-materialist stuff is all about.
'Plasm', huh? Sounds like a hell of a drug. You might wanna ask about it.
Whatever it is, one thing's perfectly clear: These young students have a much deeper understanding of communism than you do...
You could learn a thing or two from them, if you can convince them you're *one* of them.
Let your mind wander.
Your attention detaches. The voices of the young men fade away. It's a cool evening, you notice.
Listen for night sounds.
Look around the room.
Out beyond the dull chatter, you catch the sound of a distant seabird, and of course the sound of the large stretches of canvas that cover the missing sections of wall...
Your eye drifts over the detritus and mismatched furniture. It naturally gravitates toward the pieces of canvas that cover a missing stretch of wall...
A patch of ocean turned on its side...
A woman's skirt swelling in the breeze...
A wild beast tangled in a sheet...
That must be it. You imagine yourself in a small dinghy buoyed along gentle swells...
The thought is almost too much to bear. What you wouldn't give to glimpse the bare legs behind it...
Yes, an image to get the blood pumping. An unpredictable power, fighting to free itself...
Gradually, the pleasant sensation recedes. You turn your attention to the two young men, who appear just about finished.
Slowly, too slowly, the pain fades from your side. You turn your attention to the two young men, who appear just about finished.
You let the invigorating sensation course through you, then turn your attention to the two young men, who appear just about finished.
"And before that, there was Abelard's 'Un Pays Infernal'..."
"They’re not primary school delinquents, they’re university students. Attendance isn't compulsory. Besides, we’re not the skip squad."

The Counter-Truancy Task Force (or 'skip squad') is the division of the RCM that drives around in wagons looking for delinquent minors. It's generally considered a punitive assignment for under-performing officers.
"Ha! As though you can call that pablum *teaching*."
"One thing you learn quickly at university is that you're not going to find a real education in any lecture hall or discussion seminar."
"We're post-attendance, basically."
"Exactly. The only worthwhile part of the so-called École normale de Revachol is the library. That's where we've made our greatest critical strides."
"Did this reading group have anything to do with the lynching?"
"Lynching? No. We're not an *operational* cell."
"Okay, but what's your group's stance on the lynching?"
"Is your reading group affiliated with the Union somehow?"
"So what's your stance on crime in general?"
"*Are* there any operational communists in Martinaise?" (Proceed.)
"To be clear: Communism is not an official suspect in this investigation. Because it's not a *person*, you see."
"You're saying you think the mercenary was killed *by* communism itself?"
"Seems unlikely, from a strictly infra-materialist perspective..."
What are these levels they're talking about? This doesn't sound like any communism you've encountered before...
"Our stance? What, does he want to know if the SRV has established a party line on lynchings in Martinaise?" The two young men look at one another.

The SRV refers to the People's Republic of Samara. Established as a socialist utopia by survivors of the Revolution, it has since degenerated into a bureaucratic workers' state under the decades-long rule of President Sapormat 'Sport' Knezhinisky.
"Though historically speaking, the SRV *has supported* direct action against right-wing paramilitary squads, especially when they're doing the Indotribes' dirty work."
"Good point. So as a provisional matter, I can say we support it."
It's not that the boundary between sarcasm and sincerity is porous with these two, it's that they actually seem to *overlap*, as though one is meant to conceal the other.
Are they being sarcastic? You feel like you're caught in some elaborate joke labyrinth, but it's impossible to see your way through.
It's always that way. Beneath the crust of irony there's a molten sincerity that threatens to erupt forth... You may witness it yet.
One thing *is* perfectly clear: These young students have a much deeper understanding of communism than you do...
You could learn a thing or two from them, if you can convince them you're one of them.
"No, we're an independent organisation," he says proudly. "We acknowledge and respect the Union's efforts, but our interests are more theoretical than Mr. Claire's."
He speaks the truth.
"That's easy: Crime is simply the inevitable expression of the injustice and incoherence embedded within capitalism itself."
Delivered with the smug assurance of a schoolboy reciting a maxim he's committed to memory.
"It's a symptom, in other words. Not a cause." He waves his hand as though this is all there is to say on the subject of crime.
His companion can barely suppress a yawn.
"No, unfortunately. The communards were hunted down and killed nearly to a man. All that's left of them are bones and old rifles."
"Right. They all got shot in the head, just like the anarchists."
"Like this one." (Show him the Belle-Magrave rifle.)
"This little guy is still going." (Show him the figurine.)
"Well, that's too bad."
"The Insulindian Deluge wiped out an entire generation of communists. Afterward, they were all bulldozed into mass graves." The young man looks slightly queasy at the thought.
"Not exactly the second incarnation of Kras Mazov, is he?" The young man considers the figurine with a slight grimace.
His companion's eyes widen as you hold up the ancient weapon.
"It's a world-historical nightmare," the young man says gravely. "One from which we've yet to awaken."
He's practically itching to stick that thing in someone's face and pull the trigger.
"Yes, like that one. I wonder how many of these are still lying around in cellars or sealed up behind the masonry." He knits his brows together, and then looks up.
"Can I hold it?"
"Here." (Give him the rifle.)
"I'd prefer you didn't." (Put it away.)
"It's heavier than I was expecting." The rifle rests in his open palms. Its position reminds you of something...
"Of course. What would I even do with it?" He gives you a half-smile.
The attitude of a priest bearing one of the holy relics of his faith. Though it is long out-of-service, its power is evident to him.
He doesn't mean to show it, but the disappointment is plainly written across his face.
When he's finished, he returns the rifle to you with a nod of appreciation.
... though what, exactly, you can't say. He turns the rifle over again, admiring the glint of light off the oily barrel.
"What's it for?"
"I'm holding onto it for someone."
"It kills fascists."
"What do you mean? It's just a nice figurine."
"Ah, I see. That's certainly kind of you." He gives you a curious half-smile.
"Right. Sure he does." He gives you a sly half-smile.
"Right, of course it is." He gives you a sad half-smile.
His friend, though, seems oddly unmoved.
On the contrary, he appears to be *savouring* the thought of so many people shot in the head, regardless of their beliefs.
Mark it, there's something sinister in that one.
When will *you* wake up? And what will you see when you do?
"Where is the rest of the reading group?"
"What do you mean? This *is* the reading group..."
"Shouldn't a group have, like, more people in it?"
"So there's just two of you?"
"Two's all you need. Me and Kim are the same way." (Turn to Kim.)
"Kim and *I*..." the lieutenant mutters under his breath. He scribbles something in his notebook but adds nothing else.
"We're in something of a rebuilding phase."
"Some of our former comrades didn't have the *ideological fortitude* our work demands."
"Okay, but what happened to them?"
"What's so bad about the Gottwaldians?"
"Who are the Econoclards?"
"And what about the liberals? Are they liberals, too?"
"Did you say something about *turnips*?"
"I've heard enough. Let's talk about something else."

"Intellectual attrition is maybe the best way to describe it. Felix said he couldn't keep up with the reading on top of his classwork. And Zuzanna wanted to read texts *other than* Mazovian theory. Like novels, if you can believe it..."
Imagine, the audacity of wanting to read a novel in a reading group!

"We've tried recruiting new members, but unfortunately the *current intellectual climate* is pretty hostile to infra-materialist thought. These days, if you're on the left, the ascendent schools are the Gottwaldians and the Econoclards."
"Don't forget about Maurice and the turnips."
He sighs. "Right, then there was the whole 'turnip' debacle."
Whatever this turnip business is about, one thing *is* perfectly clear: These young students have a much deeper understanding of communism than you do...
You could learn a thing or two from them, if you can convince them you're one of them.
"They're the most depressing school of communism. They love writing long books with a patina of Mazovian theory to cover up their cheap psychologising."
"It's okay for Uli to say that because his dad is from Gottwald."
"What's so depressing about their theories?"
"What's so bad about psychologising?"
"The Gottwald School believe that intellectuals as a class are incapable of sparking revolutionary change, so all they can do is *critique* capitalism from inside itself."
"That sounds miserable."
"Sounds rewarding, actually."
"It *is* miserable. That's probably why they're always committing suicide."
"If it were, they wouldn't keep committing suicide."
"Do you think all the problems in the world can be reduced to repressed sexual urges?"
"Speaking from experience, definitely."
"Probably not."
"I can tell you're a man who has his urges, but I can also tell you're no Gottwaldian." He smirks.
"Well, there you have it. You're not a Gottwaldian, then."
"You see, the Gottwald School *look* like communists, they *talk* like communists, but scratch the patina and you'll see beneath that they're just depressed liberals who've read too many books."
"That's why they spend all their time smoking cigarettes and writing long works of criticism that make you want to commit suicide."
"For starters, they love talking about *beans*."
"*Beans*?"
"What's wrong with beans? I like beans."
"No beans for me. Can't stand the stuff."

"That's right. Econoclards are *obsessed* with beans. They love thinking about beans, they love counting beans, but most of all, they love building models to predict how many beans there'll be *in the future*."

"Oh, sure. But Econoclards are *obsessed* with beans. They love thinking about beans, they love counting beans, but most of all, they love building models to predict how many beans there'll be *in the future*."

"You're no Econoclard, then. They're *obsessed* with beans. They love thinking about beans, they love counting beans, but most of all, they love building models to predict how many beans there'll be *in the future*."

Nota bene: 'Econoclard' is an extra-pejorative form of the already pejorative name 'Mazovian Economists', a moderate school of Mazovianism, which advocates a gradual transition to communism through carefully managed economic modernisation rather than violent social revolution.
"They're by far the most bean-centric school of communism."
Ah yes, the much maligned bean counters, ensconced in their think-tanks and highrises, believing they can save the world through a series of incremental, assiduously technocratic reforms...
"I don't get it. Are the beans a *metaphor*?"
"But isn't it good to know how many beans there are?"
"What's wrong with making progress through moderate economic reforms?"

"If only! They've got all the beans accounted for in their asset sheets, their quarterly budgets, their future projections. But for some reason there are never enough beans to go around, so we've just got to cut our bean rations in half..."
"See? You're already falling for that scarcity logic. You start off *assuming* there aren't enough beans to go around, so naturally you want to cut the bean rations in half..."
"Oh, please. There's nothing 'moderate' about their love for counting beans. If I were a Gottwaldian, I would probably diagnose them with *Bohnenfixierung*..."
"You see, Econoclards claim to be communists, but in reality they're just liberals with hard-ons for spreadsheets."
"Of course not. The only people who actually call themselves liberals are mouth-foaming reactionaries."
"Basically indistinguishable from fascists. You'd need an x-ray machine to tell the difference."
Another sigh. “It's an unfortunate story. You see, our ex-comrade Maurice is something of an economist...”
“He’s studying macro- *and* micro-economics.”
"Wow, a *real* intellectual, it sounds like." The lieutenant arches his eyebrows.
“Right, so a few weeks ago we were discussing the extra-physical capabilities of the revolutionary state, and Maurice said... what were his exact words, Ulixes?"
"It was unbelievable. He said, 'Turnips don't care if they're grown by communists, moralists, or welkin. They grow just the same'."

dialoguetext: Just a minute. Steban... Ulixes... *why* do those names ring the faintest of bells?
Probably because they're the real names of 'Nasteb' and 'Exilus', the authors of that so-called essay about TipTop Tournée you read in *La Fumée*.
You should get to the bottom of this, when you have the chance.
"Basically, he was rejecting the whole foundation of infra-materialist theory."
What is this *infra-materialist* business they keep blathering about? You've never heard of anything like it.
"To be fair, the theory *is* pretty out there."
"Man, what an ignoramus." (Shake your head.)
"Remind me what infra-materialist theory says about turnips again?"
Just go along with it.
"We're extremely disappointed. Maurice used to be a good friend of ours."
"I'll grant you it can be overwhelming at first, but once you understand the basics, it's all quite intuitive..."
"Simply that *under suitably revolutionary conditions* crop yields naturally increase relative to non-revolutionary crops. Which Maurice somehow has the gall to deny."
"Zuzanna said that he has been hanging out with some non-communists lately."
"Providing you haven't been hanging out with non-communists, like Maurice."
"For us the question boiled down to: 'If you don't even accept the basic ideas of Nilsen and infra-materialist theory, why are you in the reading group?'"
"Right, and this Nilsen is...?"
"I totally understand."
"I don't understand at all."
"So you expelled Maurice from the reading group over an argument about turnips?"
"Nilsen. Ignus Nilsen."
"Of course you do. It's pretty basic stuff!"
"Exactly. What educated person could believe that turnips grow at the same rate under capitalism *and* communism?"
"Well, it wasn't so much that he was expelled..."
"It's a sad reflection on our educational institutions."
"He just quit coming. We haven't seen him around for weeks."
"What were you doing with those matchboxes just now?"
The young man frowns at the little pile of boxes on the floor.
"Nothing, just messing around until the meeting started."
They're watching those matchboxes awfully intently for two guys who are just 'messing around.'
It's almost as though they were trying to create the most unstable structure they could...
With predictable results.
"Do I *know* you two from somewhere?"
"*You've* read our article?" For the first time since you've met the young man, words seem to desert him...
"I don't think so."  The young man gives you a curious look. "Unless you've been hanging around the Cultural Studies faculty at the École Normale de Revachol..."
"That I did not expect." His companion is blushing now, a sheepish grin on his face.
The energy in the room has shifted ever so slightly in your favour. They're afraid they've somehow *embarrassed* themselves in front of you.
"Well, don't keep us on tenterhooks! What did you think of the essay?"
The delicate egos on these boys! Even though you're just some cop they're desperate for your approval.
Hey! You're not just 'some cop', you've got highly developed critical faculties! Now's your chance to show them off.
Time to meet these two on the intellectual battlefield. Why don't you show off those highly developed critical faculties of yours?
(Show them your edits.) "I actually had a few pieces of constructive criticism..."
"To be honest, it doesn't sound like you know anything about motor racing."
"It sounded like a recycled university essay, frankly."
"I liked the parts about death and dismemberment. That's what racing's all about."
"It was a good article. You should keep developing your ideas."
The young man takes the folded up magazine with some hesitation. As he reads over your annotations and emendations a look of deep concentration comes over his face...
"Well, I hope you'll let us know when *your* monograph is coming out..."
"Well, yes, that's the crux of our thesis. Ulixes is especially interested in capitalist violence."
"Well, of course that's just an *initial foray* into the subject. We're hoping to return to it for a more substantial treatment next term..."
"In any case, I'm glad our piece found its audience. That's always the hope with these things, you know."
"I bet he's never written a substantial essay himself. He's really got no right to critique. None at all."

He has the look of a man spread naked on the operating table. He can feel the cool metal of the scalpel, the bracing sting of the antiseptic, and yet his expression isn't wholly unpleasant. A part of him actually seems to *enjoy* the attention.
"What does it say, Steban? I can't see."
Well, there you did it. You stung them, and to what end?
"They're... good notes. A little brutal on questions of style, but he's not *wrong* about any of it..."
"Would it be alright if I kept this for a while? I'd just like some time to think about your comments." He turns to you.
"Sure, you hang onto it."
"No, that's my only copy."
"Thanks, I appreciate it."
"Sure, right. I got the main idea anyway."
"Really just violence in general. I find it *fascinating*."
Something about this one makes you want to avoid dark alleys at night...
"Perhaps he subscribes to 'La Fumée'."
That's sarcasm. He does not expect you to subscribe to radical communist periodicals.
Of course! They're the ones who produced that overwrought *critique* of TipTop Tournée.
"Aha, you two wrote the piece about motor carriage racing."
(Show them 'La Fumée'.) "Wait, *you* guys wrote for *this*?"
"Is the reading group accepting new members?"

dialoguetext: "We typically only accept new members once per semester. There's this whole *process*, with essays and presentations on assigned topics..." The young man turns to his companion.
"But given that we have some extra seating at the moment, I guess we could be convinced to expedite an application or two."
"Steban, you can't be serious... for a gendarme?"
"I am serious. As materialists we've got to adapt to conditions as they are. Besides, he'll still need to pass the *interview portion* of the entrance process..." He turns back to you.
"... assuming he's even still interested, that is."
Convince them you belong in the reading group.
What's there to be scared of? You've really been cracking the books these last few days. You can go toe-to-intellectual-toe with any reading group in Martinaise...
Take a deep breath. You've done some reading these past few days. But you also know there's more to life than what you find in books...
Remember: Where most people go wrong is in thinking they have to hide what they don't know...
You've spent a not inconsiderable amount of time arranging the works in your mental library by theme and period. All the ideas and references you'll need are ready-at-hand.
You've survived things these kids can't even imagine. They've got nothing on you.
Another thing, these young men have the most exquisitely tuned insecurity receptors you've ever witnessed.
Now, chin up. You've got this.
"This is just the group I've been looking for. When do we start?"
(Crack your knuckles.) "Alright, let's do this interview."
"Oh, you want to start *now*?" He looks to his companion, then back at you. "Sure, we can manage that..."
You've caught him off-balance. The momentum is already in your favour.
"Go ahead and take a seat. Since we haven't had time to prepare an exhaustive questionnaire, I think we can keep this interview more freeform."
"Why don't you tell us a bit about the books you're interested in, and we'll just see where the conversation goes."
"Like you guys, I really get into political and historical subjects."
