He sighs deeply. "I guess it's only  logical -- at some point one of them bullets had to end up in one of them heads..."
"Why don't you push me some more and find out, gimp."
"Let's see..." He chuckles. "Yeah. I guess I am, you big pussy."
"I would *never* tell on someone!"
"Let me state this very clearly, coppo." He clears his throat and declares: "Hello, officer! I'm Titus Hardie and these are my boys. Hardie boys. How may we assist you?"
"Well, snitches get stitches and you don't have any stitches, although by the looks of it you could probably use some." He sizes you up.
"This line of questioning is *over*," the woman interrupts. "You got the cause of death already. Hanging."

"Huh?!" A sip of beer makes the surprise go down easier.
"How does the *bullet* in his head factor into this?"
"If there's any *post-mortem* trauma, it's your problem. This will not turn into a cross-examination."
"If you hanged him, why was there a bullet in his head?"

"So what now?"

"Now there's a whole lot of work to do! For me *and* for you. I suppose there was a reason you came here, so let's get to it. What can I help my best friend and comrade with today?"
"Oooooookay!" He swings his fist through the air and shakes his head in agreeance. "Hell yes, it is."
"Now we let bygones be bygones because there's work to do. For me *and* for you. I suppose there was a reason you came here, so let's have it! What can I help my best friend and comrade with today?"
"That's *wild* how you got me to do all that stuff." (Proceed.)
"Thanks for letting me play a part, Evrart." (Proceed.)
"Let's drop the funny stuff. I'm trying to make contact with my revolutionary brethren."
He's got you there. You've got to be 10 or 12 metres up, at least.
"If you haven't spoken with my man Mañana yet, I'd suggest you start there. He's more in touch with what's happening at the ground level, so to speak..."
That's all you're going to get out of him, it appears.
"Sure thing, Harry. We're *all business* now. The answer is still 'no'. I'm a busy man, as you can see. I don't block off time on my schedule for 'underground' types..."
"I'm looking for a cell of underground communists. Can you help me?"
That's a non sequitur if you've ever heard one!
"Mr. Du Bois, really. Do I look like a man who has time for *underground* communists? I'm as aboveground as it gets!"
That note of contempt in his voice is sincere, sssire.
"Now, was there anything else you wished to discuss today?"
"You've already spoken with Mañana, as I understand. I'm afraid I don't have anything else for you on *this subject*..."
"Have you heard about the horseback monument being renovated?"
"Ah yes, I was informed." He clasps his hands together and rests them on his desk. "It seems to be a big undertaking. What are you hoping to achieve with it exactly?"
"How did you know I was behind it?"
"I want the people of this town to understand my net worth." (Show him the stock certificate.)
"Indeed." He turns back to you. "I'm glad to see you making headway with your endeavours, Mr. Du Bois. I look forward to seeing the end result. Is there anything else on your mind?"
"I'm giving the ordinary folk a hero they can believe in -- *me*."
"A vanity project? Or is this your way of inciting *rebellion*? Tut-tut, I thought you lawmen were supposed to keep the peace?"
"Mr. Du Bois, please, it is clearly the work of a great businessman. And I know *I* didn't order it."
"We are," the lieutenant says firmly as he meets Evrart's gaze. "And we will do our best to ensure that's what happens here."
"Interesting. This is a small fortune waiting to be claimed." He turns his large face back to you. "Always exciting to see promising businessmen rise up through the chaff."
It's business etiquette to take compliments even if they aren't sincere. Like this one.
"In any case, I'm glad to see you making headway with your endeavours. I look forward to seeing the end result. Is there anything else on your mind?"
"Oh right. Thanks. Glad you think that."
"Anyway, I'm glad to see you making such headway with your endeavours. I look forward to seeing the end result. Is there anything else on your mind?"
Remain quiet.
He grins slightly wider than usual, pleased to know that you follow the rules of business etiquette.
He narrows his eyes at you for a brief moment. 'Why didn't he follow the etiquette?', he seems to ask himself.
"I'm glad to see you making headway with your endeavours, Mr. Du Bois. I look forward to seeing the end result. Is there anything else on your mind?"
Who told him it was you?!
Smooth-talking? Is that what it takes to open that container? Don't you worry, Savvy has got this -- they *have* to let a VIP in.
"You wanted us to relay all this information to her..." the lieutenant cuts in.
"I mean, I don't personally mind, folks is just folks, you know -- and folks gotta eat..." He doesn't seem to be waiting for you to answer.
"What are you doing with the containers?"
"Do you work here?"
"Okay, I'm off." [Leave.]
"Bye bye now!" He returns to his work.
"I'm looking for the leader of the Dockworkers' Union."
"Where is everyone? The harbour is empty."
"Evrart, Evrart, Evrart, he looks after everyone. Huh... well, hey there!" He smiles. "How can I help you, mister?"
The look in his deep blue eyes is as sincere as you've ever seen. Kind of makes you feel like an asshole for no apparent reason.
"Container, container, used to be Wild Pines. Container, container now belongs to Evrart!" The tiny man is so engaged in his work he doesn't notice you.
"I see you are not a Union man, mister. Did you get lost? You're not one of them scabs, are you?" A shadow passes over his kind face.
"Oh, most of the guys are down at the gates, keeping the scabs from coming in..." He leans in with a confidential look...
"Oh I'm just making some covers for them containers here, yes I am, yes I am... So it's easier for the crane operators to spot them." He waves at the containers towering behind him.
"Yes-yes, everybody needs a job and this is mine. I'm Leonard, by the way, Leonard Bellec, but everyone calls me Leo." The little man raises his hand in a welcoming gesture.

"Oh, you want Mr. Evrart, then. He's an awfully nice fellow, he is. Him and his brother are both nice fellows -- they've lived their entire lives in this here neighbourhood." He coughs, then continues immediately...
"Guys like Mr. Evrart and Mr. Edgar -- his brother -- are real good guys, made Martinaise what it is today... Mr. Evrart and Mr. Edgar and I went to the same school, we did, when we were boys..."
"Easy now, Leo -- I just want to know where can I find this man."
"Tell me about this Edgar guy you keep mentioning?"
Do not interrupt Leonard.
"Mr. Edgar is Mr. Evrart's brother. He's looks a bit younger, he does, but a very smart fellow, very smart fellow indeed. He's away on some Union business... Not even in Revachol, they say..."

"All kinds of places he visits. Him and his brother both do when they're on a vacation. Right now it's Mr. Evrart's turn to look after the Union, but last year he spent a whole winter in South Safre." He chuckles.
"Let me stop you there, Leo, I had another question."
Don't interrupt Leo.
"Uh... sure, mister," he seems a bit surprised by your abruptness. "What is it?"
"Oh, Mr. Evrart is where he always is, in his office, of course." He points to the two joint containers on your right.
"... had an arithmetics teacher, Miss Bellows." Leo let's out a little chuckle. "Her real name was Miss Bellams, she was a real pretty lady, but when she got mad..." He starts laughing.

"All the boys liked her if you know what I mean, mister..." He winks at you. "We used to sneak in her yard in the dark and peek through the window. One time we saw Miss Bellows with a fellow. Yes we did, yes we did, mister." He looks for signs of disbelief in your eyes.
"Evrart, Leo, where can I find Evrart?" (Interrupt him.)
Don't say anything.
"No you fucking didn't!"
He keeps nodding and looking at you with a smile that's too sincere to be clever. Finally he seems to loose some internal struggle and adds: "Them was naked too, that's all I got to say about that."
"Very interesting, very interesting. Thank you for telling me the whole thing."
"Yes we did, we did, mister." He looks at you and shakes his head. "Indeed we did. Him was a big, big fellow, used to drive the *troyka* near our'ses school and everything."
Leo leans in and whispers: "Them was all naked too. That's all I got to say about that."
"I'm like Mr. Evrart's right-hand man, when Mr. Edgar is out of town -- and Mr. *Edgar's* right hand man when Mr. Evrart is away!" He chuckles.
"But I can't listen to the radio all the time. There's so much to do around here and I'm always busy keeping things running here. Yes I am, yes I am."
"Hold on, who's this Miss Beaufort you mentioned?"

"Oh, Lizzy? She is a real sharp tool. Mr. Evrart put her through some fancy school and everything, east of the river. Four years she was gone and when she came back she was all fancy and *law-yerly*."
He respects that word -- that's obvious.
"But she's a real nice girl, grew up in this here neighbourhood, knows everybody and gets along with everyone, real pillar of the community one day, I'm sure."
"Doctor Lemaitre said so, and she knows about such things. Been a doctor for almost fifty years, she has..." He sighs and falls silent, watching you meekly with his blue, blue eyes.
"Leo, you seem to know everyone around here, I want to ask about someone."
"Mr. Evrart doesn't really want me to talk to people about Union guys..." He thinks for a moment. "But who did you want to talk about?"
"Tell me about Measurehead."
"Tell me about the guy in the container."
"Tell me about Evrart."
"Tell me about Mañana."
"Tell me about René."
"...but Titus and his boys got into some drunken trouble and Evrart sent them on a nice vacation. For a week or so..." He stops -- but seems eager to tell you more.
"What trouble did Titus and his friends get into?"
"Got it. But there were other things I needed to discuss..."
"Like what, mister?" His wide smile is truly disarming.
"Oh... I'm not really supposed to talk about that. That's Union business." He smiles and leans closer.
"Him and his boys stirred something up in town. Probably drank too much and got into a fight or something... I heard Mr. Evrart telling them to take some time off..."

"I guess the boys got a bit too rowdy and had to let out some steam. I don't really know the details. That's just how boys are you know..." Another chuckle. "I haven't been in a fight since I was in middle-school..."

"I remember I was the runt of the class." He laughs merrily. "The bigger boys always used to pick on me. You see, I had a bit of a temper back in the day, flew off the handle like nobody's business..."

"But Mr. Evrart and his brother always came to help. Once they beat old Noel Becker so bad he needed stitches on his head..." He chuckles again. "Noel never started another fight with anyone after this."
"Mr. Evrart and Mr. Edgar are real nice guys, mister. You should go talk to Mr. Evrart -- I'm sure you'll be good friends. He's friends with everyone around here." The little guy starts coughing.
"He's a Union man through and through. Good guy." He falls silent, hesitating. "He's very calm... laid back. Doesn't do much. Talks to Evrart sometimes."

"Ohh, he's really something..." The little man starts laughing. "He doesn't talk much to me usually, but when he does... I don't really understand most of what he's saying..." He suddenly falls quiet. "Actually, I don't think he would like me running my mouth about him like that."
"Tell me about Titus."
"Who do you mean, mister?" He's rubbing his nape and looking at you with childlike innocence.
You do realize he might be just a figment of your imagination, right?
"Container, container, I'll turn you nice and red. Container, container, put the logos on..."
The lyrics to this container-song are being made up as he goes along.
"The fancy guy in a suit -- in that container over there." (Point to it.)
"I don't know anyone like this, mister -- maybe he's one of Mr. Evrart's fancy friends. He knows all kinds of fancy people, with suits and perdy carriages." Leo falls silent.
He really feels very uncomfortable discussing matters related to Evrart with you.

"Oh, Titus is a longshoreman through and through, he was born on a boat, they say." The little man rubs a patch on his elbow. "His veins are probably filled with saltwater I tell you, hehehe -- nice friendly sort old Titus is."
He's probably one of those rare specimens who are born when two drunk seamen stumble on top of each other on the deck amidst a storm so violent it flings whales around.
"Uh... I'd best not... I mean I could, but I don't think Mr. Evrart would like it very much, you better ask him yourself, mister." If anything the ever present smile on Leo's face gets even warmer.
"The night guard? Oh, he's a peculiar fellow," Leo looks at the guard booth on the wall. "He's the strong silent type you could say."

"We talk all the time, but I don't really know much about him... He plays pétanque with my old human studies teacher, Mr. Martin down at the plaza. I think he's the only fellow who actually knows old René."
"Actually I wanna talk about something else."
"Uh... sure, mister, what can Leo do for you?" The expression on his wrinkled face says *I really want to help you*.

"Oh hey, mister! I knew you'd be back to talk with old Leo here, yes I did, yes I did. It's like Lady Leriche said when she opened a bath house in the basement of my apartment building: *They can only get so far before they're aching to get back*. And lot of folks really did keep coming back..."
"Leo, Leo... in the future, can we keep this greeting shorter?"

"Oh hey, Mr. Harry!" The little fellow looks happy to see you. "It sure is nice of you to help out Mr. Evrart like you've been doing. He's so awfully busy most days -- he doesn't even eat the turnip porridge me missus sends him every day. She makes it with lots of butter and sliced sausage, she does... It's delicious."
"Yeah, I'm pretty sure this place would totally fall apart if you didn't shine the bossman's shoes, Leo."
"I think you're doing a great job around here, Leo."
"Oh, mister... I do a lot more than that. I really do most everything around here. Mr. Evrart said many times I'm irreplaceable." He's still smiling, but his voice trembles ever so slightly.
He really takes great pride in being in Evrart's good graces.
You see disdain in the lieutenant's dark eyes when they meet yours for a moment. He does not approve of you ridiculing this little man.
"Yes, this place really seems to run like clockwork. Keep it up, Leo." The lieutenant smiles at the little man.
"Well thanks a lot, coming from you it means a lot, really." You didn't think it was possible, but the smile becomes even wider.
The white rectangle on your clothes might not mean an awful lot in Martinaise, but the recognition from an authority figure made Leo's day.
"Sure. Let me ask you about something else?"
"Sure, mister, about what?"
"Hi!"
Do not interrupt the little man in his joyous activity. [Leave.]
"No, of course not!"
"Actually I am, yes."
"What's going on here?" (Look at the mountains of containers rising behind him.)
The containers in the yard are green in Wild Pines livery and the mountain rising behind Leo is all red in Union colours.
Everything is so pretty and red -- you and Leo look like brothers as you glance around with similar childlike wonder.
Keep the amazement to yourself.
"Wow, red is so much prettier than drab old green."
"What is underneath these red covers?"
"Oh I don't know, mister. They say it's some *chee-mikals*. Most of them have labels on them I think."
"Oh no trouble at all, mister, noooo trouble at all," the little guy affirms merrily.
"Leo, has anyone told you *why* you need to change the covers?"
"Thanks, Leo. You've been very helpful!" (Conclude.)
"No, not really." He shrugs and continues merrily: "Mr. Evrart doesn't tell me all the big things. Says I go and tell them to everyone."
"This looks like a massive redecorating operation, Kim."
"Yes. They're hiding it from the inside. All the red containers have the Débardeurs' Union logo on them."
"I hate to break this bonding moment, but the red containers mean they're replacing the company livery with the Union livery. Which means this strike isn't gonna stop any time soon."
"But what did they actually do?"
"Okay, Leo, let's hear about this fight you got into."
"Sometimes I feel some of the guys don't really get how much I bust my ass for them here, but you guys are all right."
For a fraction of a second there's sadness in his eyes.
He goes on: "If me missus and me was to have a child I'd be real happy if she turned out like her... But she can't have kids."
Patience. Deep down, you have the mental power to keep listening. Not many would -- but you do.
"Actually, Miss Beaufort is the right-hand man, but she's a lay-dee," a goodhearted chuckle again.

"A real pretty lady with a skin like those 'Doux & Sucre' candy bars my missus likes so much. Them are real nice to suckle on once the dinner is done and me and the missus sit down besides the radio."
"We're on a *strike* -- the whole union is! You don't have to work when you're on strike. Ha -- we haven't worked for two months now."
"Not everyone is down there of course," he chuckles, "Mr. Evrart is in his office, where he always is, and Jean-Luc is guarding the gate..." He pauses to think.
"Too rowdy? Leo, what kind of a fight did they get into? Did they kill a mercenary?"
Too late! Leo's mouth is still moving and words are spewing forth... words, words and look -- even more words -- this guy could go on till the end of days.
"Sure is mister, sure is!" Leo looks around merrily. "Really livens up the place. Yes it does, yes it does."
Law school? Could he be talking about the Union fixer, AKA the gardener.
"Just, some of the other guys don't look too kindly on the scabbing-kind, if you know what I mean, mister."
"Sure, mister, absolutely -- I'm always willing to help out nice fellows such as yourself." He smiles his disarming smile and looks you deep in the eye.
"I had some questions for you, if that's not too much trouble?"

"Oh hey, mister! I'm not gonna bother you with a long greeting just like we talked about before. I know you're probably a busy-busy man, being an important police officer and all, and personally I think the more people keeping the peace the better."
"What's in that container over there?" (Point to the container suspended from the crane arm.)
"No trouble at all, mister. No trouble at all. It's like that old saying goes -- *wisdom withers if not shared* -- and old Leo is always up for sharing."

"Mr. Harry! Boy, old Leo sure was right about you! I knew you was a Union man at heart when I first saw you." He takes a quick breath. "Right as I turned around and looked at you, I said to myself: 'Now that fellow is a union man right there. Through and through.' And I was right, yes I was, yes I was."
"I guess you just *know* people, Leo. It's like a special ability you got."
"Leo, I only tolerate the Union to as long as it furthers my own goals. Nothing more."
"Sure, sure, Leo... go easy now and answer some questions please."
"It's true, it's true." he nods. "I've had an eye for helpful people for as long as I remember. I like helpful people, and I like helping helpful people, so what do you need, mister?"
"Oh no, mister, you've already done so much for the Union. The Union is in your debt, for sure." He nods with a happy smile. "So how can I help you, mister?"
"Sure thing, mister. I'm always ready to help out a helpful person such as yourself. Folks have got to help each other out, right?"
The old man whistles and hums a jaunty tune to himself.
"What do you mean by 'taking this soup to the men'? Is it for striking?"
"Oh, absolutely, mister." He nods along. "What do you want to know?"
"Are you the Leo, who wrote the note to make more banners?"
"Yes, yes, I'm taking it to them. The borscht keeps them happy and in fighting spirits. Makes you all warm inside. They brew it in the Whirling-in-Rags."
"It's very-very good. Makes a man feel so warm and happy." He shakes his head with a wide smile. "I feel like I could take on Mr. Renaudin's boar-dogs every time the lunch is done."
"Thanks, Leo. Another question though?"
Power-borscht, huh? Never heard of a borscht that turns little guys into dogfighters. Alcohol, however...
There appear to be cisterns underneath the Union container covers.
"Really? Did they kill someone?"
"I have another question."
Keep it together, no need to show your wonder.
It's like some red infection was spreading outwards from the container yard's core.
This looks like a massive redecorating operation.
Yes, moving from inwards to outwards. By the looks of it soon everything will be in Union colours.
"So *no one* is working?"
"So *no one's* working?"
Don't go all *bad cop* on this simple friendly fellow.
"Sure, sure." The small man nods along. "How can I help you?"

"No, I don't think they killed anyone." The little guy shies away from you. "Let's better talk about something else. Titus and his boys do good work, I don't wanna get them in trouble over a little drinking..."
"Easy, Leo, let's keep this on the Hardies." He looks to you for assistance.
You're never getting anything useful out of him. It's good enough you found out Evrart has a brother called Edgar and he helped Leo.
"Who is this Miss Beaufort?" The lieutenant looks up at Leo.
"Who's Miss Beaufort?"
Stay on this *Miss Beaufort* topic.
So Evrart trained a lawyer named Miss Beaufort. Interesting.
"Okay so this is the Union fixer, the gardener?"
"Another question, Leo."
"Yes sure, I'm glad to answer." His benevolent eyes are looking into yours.
"I'm not sure what a fixer is, but she is a real nice girl. Smart as a whip too." The little guy smiles a disarming smile at you.
"Looks like it."
"Thank you... Heh! Almost forgot! Mr. Evrart is in that container over there." Leo points to his left. "I got distracted telling the story, but he's in there."

They lived on the same street their entire lives -- even dated the same girl on and off for as long I can remember." He chuckles again. "Strange fellows, but mister Martin was always real nice to me in school... I remember once..."
"Hold up, Gaston was your human studies teacher?"
"I have another person in mind."
"Suuuuure," he stretches the word. "Who did you have in mind?"
"Mr. Martin, yes." Leo nods. "Don't really remember much about him. I was just a boy back then."
"Left with the first autumn rains and didn't come back before the trees where green again." The little guy chuckles again.
"Oh that one..." He looks at the container. "That should be empty as far as I know. Lots of containers here have nothing in them. They're just waiting to be loaded up."
"Told you."
"Oh yes, yes," he replies excitedly. "I leave all kinds of notes for myself. That old head of mine ain't so good at keeping things in no more. I almost forgot about the borscht."
"What was that about the borscht?"
"Cool. Another question then."
"Of course, mister. I'm more than happy to be helpful."
"Oh yes, I've been taking special Whirling borscht to the men every day since the strike started." The little guy chuckles merrily.
"Hold up, who makes it at the Whirling?"
"Oh, the Whirling's cook. He makes it. Them is always talking with Mr. Mañana in that weird language and laughing together. He doesn't speak what we speak, he's from Graad."
"Looks like the borscht is spiked, I'm gonna look into it." (Accept task)
"Something is off about this borscht... I'm going to look into it." (Accept task.)
"That's it. I just wanted to know who wrote the note." (Refuse task.)
"Oh, I did, mister!" He chuckles again. "Yes I did, yes I did."
"Oh sure, mister... sure." The little guy nods. "You do that, yes sir."
He didn't actually understand what you meant and now he's just nodding along.
Look at him, it's not gonna be anything useful anyway. Don't fight it. Better to go with the flow.
Mr. Martin -- Gaston also taught History and Human Studies to the Claire brothers.
Telling the gardener you know her name might throw her off? Perhaps something to consider, later...
The accent is so thick it's impossible not to notice he's Ubi. From the vanishing peninsula of Ubi Sunt? (sic) on Mundi.
"You're Ubi, right?"
"Oh yes, born and raised in Iraesh, mister. Mum had to leave my dad after he got a bit violent, took us here to the New New World. I was about ten then, too old to lose my accent then..."

"People say us Ubis are up to all sorts of trouble with sheep and other animals and what not -- I just want you to know there was *never* any of that where I come from. No sir. Those are just nasty rumours."
"Thank you for clarifying that, sir."
He probably doesn't know anything anyway. Who in their right mind would tell *him*?
"Thank you, mister... Heh! Almost forgot! Mr. Evrart is usually in that container over there." Leo points to his left. "But he already left for the day. He never stays after 22."
"Thank you... Heh! Almost forgot! Mr. Evrart is usually in that container over there." Leo points to his left. "But he usually leaves around 22, so you gotta be quick if you wanna catch him."
"Oh, Mr. Evrart is usually in his office, of course." He points to the two joint containers on your right. "But he already left for the day. He always leaves around 22."
"Oh, Mr. Evrart is usually in his office, of course." He points to the two joint containers on your right. "But you gotta be quick if you wanna see him. He leaves around 22."
Okay, so Evrart has a brother Edgar. That's something -- but the rest of it is taking *too* long my friend...
South Safre? A lot of *bulk* chemical manufacturing going on there. A lot of cargo shipments being made too.
The trade must've been lucrative for the trip to be so long.
"Honestly. I don't know *what* he does for us, but it must be important because everybody likes him. Yes, they do. I think that's what he does, he makes everyone feel a little better."
Oil for the wheels. Much needed in stressful times like these.

"Once he said he's a *dragon* to this mob fellow who came picking a fight with some Union men. Heh, I think he really believed Jean-Luc *was* a dragon, because he ran right off. Another time he almost killed another guy, but... I shouldn't talk about that."
That's precisely what he is. Evrart's dragon.
Now he's talking about some drunk sawmill owner who... no, he already switched to a prized fishing rod he apparently owned at some point... You know what -- just cut in there with your questions.
"The night guard? He was a peculiar fellow. Headstrong and proud. We didn't really talk all that much." The little guy looks you in the eye. "He died recently. Somethink with his ticker..."
"You can find Jean-Luc down at the gates." He turns back to you. "He's the big, impressive one. You know: tattoos, muscles -- ethnic looking. Can't miss him. Great guy."
"But of course, all joking aside, I *am* going to help you." He picks up the handset of a radio-phone to his right -- then clicks a button.
"I can certainly see how having him up there might start affecting *some* real estate values." He licks his fat lips and smiles.
"Yeah, the belt thing!"
He gives you a quizzical look, then smiles pleasantly. "Don't take this question personally, but *why* would I get involved in this matter, Harry?"
"Also, I studied the footprints at the crime scene. Worker boots."
"Footprints left at the crime scene point to someone wearing a worker's boot. Possibly a dockworker."
"Mr. Claire. The man was hanged with a cargo belt. A steel reinforced cargo belt. It's safe to assume the Union had *something* to do with the murder."
"The belt the man was hanged with incriminates the Union. At least you could help us out a bit."

dialoguetext: "Besides, getting the body down would benefit all of us. It's a stain on the neighbourhood."
"You are a community leader, help your community out!"
"You seem to be the community leader -- do this for your community."
Say nothing.
"Jean-Luc, the cop who bested you in physical combat is here and he has a little dead-body-in-a-tree problem. Namely, he needs it to be taken down. Please extend him this courtesy."
"Jean-Luc, my boy. I'm sending a police officer down. He has a dead-body-in-a-tree problem he needs help with. Namely, he needs it to be taken *down*."
"Jean-Luc, my boy. I'm sending two police officers down. They have a dead-body-in-a-tree problem they need help with. Namely, they need it to be taken *down*."
"You might have noticed there's one hanging on a tree behind the hostel-cafeteria."
"Oh my..." He smiles pleasantly. "Don't take this question personally, but *why* would I get involved in this matter?"
"And, Jean... please take it easy with the race science. That's a *yes* to getting the body down, *no* to the race science." He hangs up and turns back to you.
"I don't know what that means, Harry. Shady brew? There are so many moving parts in my operation I can't keep track of them all..."
"You know what? Don't even tell me. Whatever it is -- do it. Surprise me!" He reconsiders. "Just one thing... if you can, make it even *shadier*."
"What?" The big man looks at you surprised.
"The brew! The shady, shady brew."
"Oh, how could I forget your little side-project! Well done, Harry. Well done! Don't even tell me what it was. But good job! I love it when workers take the initiative like this."
"What?" The big man looks at you, confused.
"The shady brew. You told me to make it even shadier. I didn't. It had alcohol in it. Now there's no alcohol."
"Did I? Well done then, Harry. I like not knowing about it and I'm sure you made the right call. I spend the whole day delegating tasks, and it's a great relief to see people taking initiative."
"I don't even want to know what all of that means -- brew, shady, alcohol, turned off. I'm gonna let the world *surprise* me."
"Don't even tell me what was going on. Alcoholic brew, stronger, stopped it, strike. I'm just gonna let you surprise me, Harry."
"I don't know what that means, Harry. But I love it!" He chuckles. "I love your initiative! Knowing you're out there keeping things running lets me focus on the big picture stuff."
He sincerely has no idea what you were talking about -- and he doesn't care either.
So do I. That's one tasty brew, you should drink some right now if you can!
"Let's hear it, Harry." He sinks deeper into his chair.
"Where did you get that folder?"
"Ah, this?" He closes the folder. "My friends in your organization gave it to me, Harry."
"It's Harry..." He glances at the folder. "Harry Du Bois."
"But of course, Harry." He nods. "Your precinct is the 41st and you live in Jamrock. You're a Jamrock boy. A long way from home, but that's okay."
"Family? Harry, you're *not* a family man. There's not one peep of family in here. Unless you *think* you're a family man? Do you strike yourself as a family man, Harry?"
"Of course, Harry, of course! Let's not linger on personal details and amnesia. You wanted something from me?"
"Let's talk of other matters for a moment."
"Let's get this straight... what is my full name?"
"What kind of a cop does it say I am ?"
"Do you know anything about my family? Do I have a wife or kids or...?"
"Do you know where I live?"
This translates into: "Ha-ha, you guys are so corrupt."
"Mr. Kitsuragi, would you mind?" His eyes never leave yours. "Me and Harry are talking about his lost identity right now."
It's just a brown folder. You can't make out what's written on it.
"Of course, let us dispatch with the formalities. You call me Evrart, I call you Harry!"
