dialoguetext: "Are you trying to tell me you've gotten hold of some of our documents?" The lieutenant inspects Evrart over his spectacles.
"It's true. My memory is a bit hazy."
"My god so it's true! I didn't want to believe it, but you *are* a fantastic science-fiction amnesiac cop, aren't you?" He shrugs with an amazed expression. "What are the odds of that?"
"Is that my name?"

"So good to hear that, Harry. Apparently my sources were wrong." He pats the brown folder in front of him. "However if you *did* have a spot of memory trouble I could help you out -- with my big fat folder."
"My memory is fine -- I'm just testing you."
"I assure you, there's nothing to be ashamed of, Harry. You're among friends and the good news is..." He taps on the folder in front of him.
"I'm sure you had some concerns you thought I might be able to address," he pauses to look down on a brown folder on his desk. "And you were probably right -- I can."
I guess word has already reached him. No matter, no harm done.
It might be a good idea to hide your *confusion*... I mean, see what his game is first.
Don't trust him. For all you know *Du Bois* might be his name. You need to confirm this.
Have another look at that folder.
Words flow like a river of honey from his lips.
"You *must* have questions, Harry. C'mon on now..." He makes a come-hither motion. "Don't be shy. Let's hear them."
Asking too many questions will make you look weak. You should maybe focus on the folder.
You feel like a *Du Bois*, but you don't feel like a *Harry*. Strange.
You don't feel like either one of these things -- you know what your name is. You have a sophisticated name. Like that of a count. Or a beautiful man.
You don't feel like any of these things -- you know what your name is. You have a sophisticated name. Like that of a count. Or a beautiful man.
"Wait, I thought *you* are Harry Du Bois."
"That's not my name, my name is Raphael Costeau."
"I am Tequila Sunset."
"I feel like a Du Bois, but not quite like a Harry. Something longer."
"I don't really like it."
"Okay, I like it. I can work with that."
"Don't be silly, Harry." He smiles broadly. "Harry Du Bois -- That's a real man's name. A Union man's."
"And *I* can work with you, Harry!" He raises his index finger. "Now, what else can I do for you?"
"Sure, okay. You're Harold. Harman. Haroldemus. But that's not what the record says. The record says 'Harry Du Bois'." He taps on the folder. "A real *man's* name. "
"Excellent! I know you RCM people like your call signs. Harry 'Tequila Sunset' Du Bois -- I can see that. But to me -- and the census bureau -- you will always be little Harry."
"Fine, Harry." He waves you off. "You can even be Harry Raphael Du Bois De Costeau -- or whatever you *choose* to be."
"No. I'm really, really not. *You* are, Harry."
The lieutenant covers his face and sighs audibly.
"Mr. Kitsuragi doesn't seem even slightly empathetic to your memory loss, Harry." He frowns at the lieutenant. "I, however, wish to help you any way I can."
He doesn't really seem to know any more about it.
"Whether you're a family man or not is unimportant right now, officer. We are here for a different reason. In fact, we should probably move on to the murder."
"You're right, I don't."
"I think I do. I'd be a wonderful father."
"Never mind the family."
"Family, Harry..." He glances lovingly at the framed photo in front of him. "... is the most important thing in the world."
"That's why I like you, Harry!" His fat finger is pointing at you. "A good man knows both his strengths and his weaknesses and you my friend... you are one of the *all time greats*."
"Well... yes." He looks around, uninterested. "I'm sure you're gonna make one little boy or a girl very happy and proud one day, Harry."
"I find that very suspicious. May I have a look?"
"I'm afraid this is meant for Union eyes only, Mr. Kitsuragi. I'm sure you understand." He turns back to you. "Please continue, Harry."
As you look at the folder, Evrart covers it with his hand and pets it. Is he trying to hide that it's not a real RCM folder? It certainly doesn't have the RCM stamp on it.
Evrart's large hands are covering the folder, but the look on his face says *I know everything about you, Harry*.
"That's not an RCM folder."
"Okay, Harry, you got me," he says, grinning. "This is from the Census Bureau, not the RCM. Those Census Bureau people are absolutely *corrupt*. You should do something about them."
"He got the name from the Census Bureau and everything else from your actions here in Martinaise."
He got the name from the Census Bureau and everything else from your behaviour here in Martinaise.
"Yes, yes, Mr. Kitsuragi, from the Census Bureau, like I said." He looks annoyed. "Now I'm actually a very busy man, so is there anything else I can do for you, Harry?"
"But I really got you good there for a moment, didn't I, Harry?" He laughs like he just pulled off a successful prank. "Now what can I do for you?"
"He knows everything about me."
"I've got nothing to hide."
"I'm sure it's not that bad," the lieutenant whispers. "At worst he has an old RCM folder, and I very much doubt even that."
"Harry..." he says gently. "I just know the things that matter to our friendship. And I want you to feel free to ask me about those things."
"Oh Harry..." He peeks into the folder -- as if it's hard to turn away from the mysteries inside. "Oh wow... this is really something."
"I'm sure it's not that bad," the lieutenant whispers. "At worst he has an old RCM folder, and I very much doubt even that."
"So how about it, Harry?" He leans back in the chair. "You need assistance, I presume."

"It says..." He looks in the folder. "Oh yes... very interesting. It says you're more like a mad prophet than a cop. Always rambling about the end of the world... I'm sure these stories are exaggerated."
"Well, Harry..."  He turns a couple of pages in the folder. "If I were to sum you up in one word, it would be *apologetic*."
"Oh Harry..." He opens the folder and leafs through its contents. "You are the most regular, traditional, by-the-book law official imaginable."
"Harry, you're not simply a cop, you're a star! A bright shining star in the drab law enforcement sky, outshining all other stars. You're a *super* star."
"Well, Harry..." He opens the folder and leafs through its contents. "It looks like you like to party -- hard. And you like disco music. I guess you're a disco-cop."
"Exaggerated?! Evrart, the time is now! We are looking at a *catastrophic global* loss of life."
"Very much exaggerated. I'm not a mad prophet. I'm just a cop."
"What? I'm not apologetic. I'm confident."
"I'm... sorry?"
"Hey, I'm not *that* ordinary!"
"I just want to do my job, that's all."
"No-no-no-no... NO. I'm definitely not a star."
"That's what I like about you, Evrart. You get me."
"I'm planning on changing a lot of things about myself."
"I *do* like me some disco."
"Of course, Harry." He nods along. "Sin, blood, death, catastrophic loss of life... all those things. And that's why you and I must be prepared, so let's talk about how we can help each other."
"I know that, Harry." He smiles broadly. "I *know* you. And rest assured, your secret is safe with me."
He's probably just making a guess based on your recent activity in Martinaise.
"Well you sure come off as very confident in all our interactions, Harry." He chuckles. "You're a real man's man."
"Yes." He inspects you over his giant bug-eyed glasses. "You seem to be. A lot of the time. But right now there's no reason to be. Let loose a little. Be *you*."
"Of course you're not, Harry," he exclaims. "You're my special boy! Big friend of the Union. This is *very* non-ordinary."
"As do we all, Harry." He nods, a sympathetic look in his eyes. "We're all just trying to do our best, aren't we? I'm gonna help you do yours."
"Nonsense, Harry." He shakes his head. "You lit up this container, when you walked in here. You're my golden boy."
"Of course I do, Harry." He smiles a sly smile. "And I'm gonna help you shine. I'm gonna put you on all the big stages. Your name in giant neon letters: 'HARRY DU BOIS.'"
"I'm going to stand 100% behind you through all these changes, Harry." He reaches his arms out. "You need to understand that all I want to do is to help you."
"Harry, sometimes I think we're so similar it frightens me!" He holds his giant head between his hands. "I too love... regular, normal music!"
"Hey, I'm not that regular, check out my tie."
"Now that is *funky*, Harry." He rubs his big hands together. "You are a colourful fellow, not a boring stiff like this deceitful folder here implies."
We are charming his pants off, *bratan*! Great job!
"I think the odds of that..." He looks at you. "Are very low."
"I have a big fat folder on you, Harry. I'm sure you have a lot of questions to ask -- maybe I can help you out?"
"No, no. Don't interrupt him." He looks the lieutenant with reproach. "Me and Harry are having a moment here. Go on, Harry."
The giant neon sign reading "HARRY DU BOIS" hanging from the Kvalsund crane can be seen all the way to Jamrock.
Don't just jump to the folder. That's not smart, shows you're on the edge. Do some probing first.
Somewhere in Mirova a beautiful woman sees the bright glow on the horizon and says to herself: "Oh my god, I shouldn't have left him..."
"Oh, I know everything about you, Harry." He taps on the folder in front of him. "I have a big fat folder on you. Very juicy stuff."
"And the word on the street is your memory is a bit... hazy." He looks at you questioningly. "If that's true, maybe I can help you out? Do you a little favour so to speak."
"My memory is fine. Don't worry about it."
"It's true. My memory *is* a bit hazy."
"So good to hear that, Harry. Apparently my sources were wrong." He pats the brown folder again.
"I assure you, there's nothing to be ashamed of, Harry. You're among friends and the good news is..." He taps on the folder again.
"However if you *would* have a spot of memory trouble -- well, let's just say a fat juicy folder could really fill in the blanks." He winks at you.
I guess word has already reached him. No matter, no harm done.
Words flow like a river of honey from his lips.
It might be a good idea to hide your *confusion*... I mean, see what his game is first.
"My big fat folder is ready to serve. I'm sure you have a lot of questions -- maybe my fat folder and I can help you out? Do you a little favour of sorts?"
It's just a brown folder. You can't make out what's written on it.
"Mr. Kitsuragi, would you mind?" His eyes never leave yours. "Harry has some questions he needs answers to."
That's what the hanged corpse called you -- Harry.
That means he doesn't *really* know anything about you.
A pity. The mystery of *you* will have to remain a mystery for the time being.
"So the Census Bureau says my name is Harry Du Bois?"
"Yes, that's what I said. Try to keep up, okay? Let's move on."
"Mr. Kitsuragi..." He leaves the rest of this sentence hanging in the air and lets his smug smile deliver the rest of the message.
"Don't you worry, I've got plenty on you too, my rigid friend."
"Of course, let us dispatch with the formalities, you call me Evrart, I call you Harry!"
"I see you have gotten hold of some of our old documents." The lieutenant turns to Evrart. "They should have been destroyed some time ago."
"So Harry, what can I help you with today?"
"To be honest, my memory is a bit hazy right now, yes."
"Is that my name?"
"Fine by me."
The huge block letters on the folder read "HARRIER DU BOIS". There's something in small writing just above that...
"I guess the stress of peace-keeping and order-maintaining can get even to the best of us." He scratches his earlobe.
"I'm sure you had some concerns you thought I might be able to address." He pauses to look at a brown folder on his desk. "And you were probably right."
For a fraction of a second the big man looks at you inquisitively. "Experiencing partial amnesia, are we, Harry?"
"Nah, my memory is fine -- I'm just testing you."
It might be a good idea to hide your confusion, see what his game is first.
"I'm very glad to hear it. Some of my associates here in Martinaise told me you had trouble remembering things -- I am relieved they were mistaken."
"Don't be too hard on yourself, officer. And if there's *anything* I can help you with, please don't hesitate to ask."
Do *not* trust him. For all you know, it might be *his* name by which he is addressing you. You need confirmation.
"Revachol Citizens Militia."
"Harry... " he says almost gently. "Honestly, I'm just relieved you didn't get a hernia. A man your age..."
"'A man my age'? What are you implying? I'm at the peak of my abilities."
"I too am surprised by the resilience and athleticism of this tool I've been provided with." (Tap your chest.)
"My body's gonna break down any moment now. Probably pushed it to the limit."
"Enough wackiness. Let's get back to business."
"Anyway, I assure you, I am a very well-informed man. Information reaches me before I even get the chance to request it."
"Rubbish, Harry, rubbish! I mean look at you!" He raises his hands towards you. "For your age you are obviously in peak physical condition. A real silverback!"
"Hmmm..." He inspects you over the rims of his glasses. "You did look like you were gonna collapse and die when I told you about your lost gun."
He chuckles. "Things *do* always turn real wacky when you and I are in the same room, don't they, Harry?"
Say nothing.
"Yes, yes, Harry. You are obviously in peak physical condition and I salute both your initiative and your physical prowess. Very impressive, Harry. *Very impressive*."
"Hmmm..." He inspects you over the rims of his glasses. "You did look like you were gonna collapse and die when I told you about your lost gun."
The big man peers at you over the rims of his glasses for a moment, then interlaces his fingers and rests his chin on his hands.
"Am I going to ask? Hell, Harry -- you *spin-kicked* my strongest man in the face. I saw it from my window!"
"I understand. I am a terrifying death machine."
"I don't even know how I was able to do that."
"You don't have a window."
"It was a figure of speech, Harry. Of course I don't have a window. I'm in a container."
"Don't worry, Harry." He leans in closer. "Between you and me, I'm not a huge fan of his race thing, but the Union did not get where we are today by frowning on eccentricity."
"Harry, I assure you, I am a very well-informed man. Usually I have all the necessary information *before* I need to request it."
"Honestly, I didn't want to bring it up, Harry -- I heard you have become Measurehead's race pupil...?"
Yes, but it's because his word usually sets things in motion.
"I really believe in the race mystery and I'm glad I was given this chance. I hope to one day be able to contribute."
"I'm not a *race pupil*, I just listened to some of the things he had to say."
"It was a tactic, I needed to get in somehow. It's not like I'm a racist now."
"Yeah, I'm a big racist. It's basically like that in my head all the time."
"Personally I'm not big on the whole race thing, but that's okay. It's alright to be a massive racist, Harry." He sinks deeper into his armchair.
"Let me assure you, I'm very glad you're comfortable sharing this with me. I run a big and quirky organisation. Everyone is welcome. Birds of all feathers."
"Of course, Harry, of course! You're not some kind of a fantastic racist now. And rest assured, no one's gonna hear about it." He winks at you.
"No one's gonna know what you did with race there, Harry. Your race-bonanza is safe with me. Word of how *racy* it got will never leave Martinaise."
You can see the map of Revachol in your head. Dozens of red arrows are pointing outwards from Martinaise. Moving all across the city.
"Unfortunately, I can confirm this. My partner has some decidedly outmoded views."
"Evrart, that's just giving orders."
"Let's talk about something else."
"But of course, Harry."
"Oh, you're so clever, Harry. And technically you're right. Now... what else can I do for you?"
"Would *you* ask a man like that how he got into *your* container yard?"
"Yes, yes, my best men are tracking it down. Some kids saw some other kids running away with it. Some folks said a paranoid schizophrenic might have it. Leads are being checked, Harry."
"What's that, Harry? You're getting a little pale. Is it the words *paranoid schizophrenic* and *lost gun* in one sentence? Don't worry, it's just a lead. It'll probably turn out to be nothing."
"Yes. Your lost gun." His face turns serious. "My best men are on it. They're turning every stone, searching every playground, asking kids, grandmas, everyone."
"Your gun *will* be found, Harry. Let me assure you of that." He winks at you. "It's just a matter of time and... *effort*."
The only way to find it seems to be working with him. He might even be holding your gun hostage...
"I will not be blackmailed with this gun business."
"I don't care about my gun. Keep it."
"Does this mean if I do things for you I will get my gun back?"
"Damn it, Harry, that's exactly what it means!"
"'I don't care about my gun...'" he repeats. "I love it, Harry! Wish I could be like that. But I can't. I have a responsibility to this community. I can't have a loaded gun in the streets."
"'I don't care about my gun'..." he repeats. "I love it, Harry! Wish I could be like that. But I can't. I have a responsibility to this community. I can't have a loaded gun out in the streets."
"Harry, Harry -- I was only trying to be tactful. A lost gun is a dangerous thing. I can't have it around in my neighbourhood."
His tone is suddenly very serious. "Kids could be playing gun-roulette with it as we speak. Teenage gangs could be arming themselves. Get a hold of yourself, Harry!"
"I assure you, we are working on locating the missing sidearm as well."
"Excellent, Mr. Kitsuragi. That's excellent news." He claps his hands together. "Looks like we have a friendly gun-finding competition on our hands."
"The officer is exaggerating," says the lieutenant, leaning forward. "Of course we care about the missing firearm, and we are *actively* looking for it as well."
"Of course," the lieutenant replies dryly. "I understand. We help you -- you help us."
He is not.
Hold on, could he really hold my gun hostage?
Who knows? Only one thing is certain: If you work with him, you're going to get it back, and working with him might be the only way to do it.
The lieutenant is concerned about the lost gun and feels that the fact you haven't prioritized looking for it is unfortunate, if inevitable, and doesn't put the RCM in a good light.
"Wait... the gun may have been bought from Roy's pawn shop. Have your men factored that in?"
"Yes, thank you for the *hot tip* regarding your lost gun, Harry. My men have indeed" -- he makes air quotes -- "*factored in that you pawned it*."
It did not come as a surprise to him. He might actually not be bullshitting.
It did not come as a surprise to him. He might actually not be bullshitting.
"Now please... let the professionals do their job. Kick back, Harry, relax! I have *great guys* on this. You focus on what's important – building our relationship for the good of Martinaise."
"The golden boy returns once more! Wonderful -- simply wonderful, Harry." He claps his hands together like a child who's just been offered cotton candy. "Of course, I already knew this."
Oh, *bratan*, you played the old man like a three-string banjo. He has no idea.
"It's done. I mailed the signatures you asked me to mail."
"My friend, the mail-man, confirms the letter is on its way. You've done a great thing today. You've given the children of Martinaise a real future. I feel I can finally trust you, Harry."
"You're in my inner circle. You too, Mr. Kitsuragi," he nods to the lieutenant, smiling broadly. "We can talk about anything: the strike, the murder, your lost gun -- *nothing* is off the table."

He leans forward and looks straight into your eyes with the warmest of smiles. "You're in my inner circle. We can talk about anything: the strike, the murder, your lost gun -- *nothing* is off the table."
See, forging that signature really paid off.
Well done, sire. By guile and deceit, you're in.
"What was the fine print on the document I mailed? What was the catch?"
"There was no fine print, Harry." He leans forward. "But I do hope all that construction noise and limited street access *encourages* some people to move. After a year of that ruckus, who wouldn't?"
"And when they do..." He holds out his index finger. "They will have a *good* place to go. I'm currently working on renovating the buildings near the roundabout into affordable *workers palaces*."
"The signatures I got -- I know you plan to force them out with the construction noise."
"So the village is doomed -- because I helped you."
"Harry..." He shakes his head. "By now you should know I would never do anything tricky like that. However, if the construction noise and limited street access makes *some* people consider moving..."

"Well, let's just say there'll be freshly renovated buildings near the roundabout where those poor people can finally enjoy a significant uptick in quality of life. I'm talking real affordable *workers palaces*."
"Did *you* order the hanged man killed?"
"Can I get my gun now?"

"You were there, you saw the place. A waste land -- there's nothing left. But mark my words, Harry." His slams his fist on the table, causing some of the coffee to spill. "We are going to *reset* it."
"So the village is doomed," the lieutenant says grimly.
"*Re-set*," he repeats. "I have big plans for Martinaise. And they do *not* include humans living in those pig sheds on the coast. That land will be used for municipal buildings and commerce."
"What do you mean?"

"Harry, imagine a Youth Centre-Supermarket-Church complex! Employing hundreds, no, thousands of people. The coast will be lit up with enterprise -- and *life*! All those ruins out there turned into *low-income housing*..."
"Youth-Supermarket-Church complex? Do you really expect me to believe that?"
"Low-income housing? If even part of this is true, then why not."
"And *life*..." (Nod.) "I knew you were a man of the people, Evrart."

"Yes, I do. I got the centre, I got room for a retail complex, and in four years I'll get the church too. The wheels are already turning, Harry. The wheels of progress. This post-war limbo -- I won't stand for it. There are kids practically playing with their own *faeces* out there... It cannot go on."

"I accept your salute, Harry," he nods. "*All* of it is true. I've got the centre, I've got room for a retail complex, and in four years I'll get the church too. The wheels are turning, Harry. The wheels of progress. This post-war limbo -- I won't stand for it. There are kids practically playing with their own *faeces* out there... It cannot go on."

"And I knew you're one too, Harry! Right when you rolled into town. I've got the centre, I've got room for a retail complex, and In four years I'll get the church too. The wheels are turning, Harry. The wheels of progress. This post-war limbo -- I won't stand for it. There are kids practically playing with their own *faeces* out there... It cannot go on."
But will there be giant statues of the Claire brothers towering above it all? Joyce knew he was up to something.
"Joyce was right when she said you were up to something..."
"Sounds like you got this. You can rely on my vote."

"Oh I do, Harry, I really do." He crosses his arms on his chest. "I'm gonna make the working man as rich as *Joyce Messier* with that vote of yours. That's my job. Just like yours is to keep the peace."
"Damn right I am, Harry!" The fist lands on the table again. "I'm gonna make the working man as rich as she is one day. That's my job. Just like yours is to keep the peace."

"Order it? You know my men didn't kill him. They told you -- it was a happy accident. You know how it is, no one takes the *initiative*. If I wanted him dead I would have had to do it myself. And I'm too fat for that."
"What do you gain from him being dead?"
"Okay, another question."
"I'm listening, Harry."
"Victory, Mr. Kitsuragi. I have *victory* to gain. We are going to start a war with the Wild Pines Group -- and win before they even realize there *is* a war."
"They're trained military people. Aren't you afraid for your men?"
"Have you ever heard what two Giant Seraise Hornets can do to an entire colony of bees? They destroy it."
"I have. It's a great story, Harry." He nods. "Did you also know how the bee colony kills the giant hornet? They swarm and blanket it entirely, until it suffers a *massive heat stroke* and dies."

"Harry, we outnumber them fifteen hundred to one. And that's just Martinaise. With all the unions in Revachol -- and with public opinion on our side -- we can hold off two men. Or fifteen men. Or even fifty men."
"How is this connected to the strike?"
"Harry, there is no strike, only war. Class war. Or, in business terms: a *dawn raid*. Or wait..." He pauses to rub his chin. "Is that when you still *pay* them something? Because we won't do that."

"We're not gonna give nothing. We're gonna *take* Terminal B away from them: the roads, the gates, the containers, that big crane... even the damn coffee maker. We're gonna take all of it for the people -- and *fuck* Wild Pines."
"Is that why you haven't let Joyce in here?"
"So that's why you haven't let Joyce in?"
"Yes. It's also why I let that midget Gaumont go. He's too nice. I can't put him through this. Plus, he knows how to get in here. That woman can't tell her tits from her asshole. She has no chance."
"How are you going to fund your new independent harbour?"
"Drugs are a no go for me. I'll *report* this."
"I have to admit: that's a well put-together plan. And far-removed from you."
"Interesting stuff. I just want to solve this murder, okay?"
"Makes sense to regulate the drug trade like this. Keeps it out of more dangerous hands."
"Yes, yes, of course, and while you're doing that, please go ahead and also tell the Wild Pines." He snickers. "I wanna hear them squeal from the indignity."
He smiles slyly. "It's also far-removed from my men and the people of Martinaise, who've put their trust in me."

"Anyway, let's not focus on the sensationalism of the drug trade. This hypothetical drug trade is all anyone ever seems to be interested in. It would only be a small part of the Harbour's turnover -- just like the harbour is but a small part of Martinaise."
"You know why you're such a good detective, Harry? You don't get *sidetracked*. You care about the people you're supposed to protect, not some systems that may or may not be unethical."
"Oh, Harry, you've misunderstood. I have no drugs in my hands." He raises both hands, palms open. "It's all far-removed from me like some half-remembered dream."
"Is Ruby helping you secure this fantastic share?"
"Harry, if I *was* supplying raw materials to drug manufacturers, I would need an army of Rubies."
The lieutenant nods slowly. "Understood."
Okay, so that's basically his system here.
"I'm gonna unite them all into one economic body. We're gonna incorporate this place to kingdom come. Everyone's gonna be in on the wealth. And *everyone's* gonna pull their weight."
"Well, I mean, if it has the word *incorporate* in it, then I like it. I'm a money-guy."
"That's very ambitious. I love what you're doing for the working man."
"I'm not feeling a whole lot of *Revachol* here. Not enough flags or kings."
"Honestly, it's not my place to judge or express an opinion."

"Yes, if you start thinking about it like *that*, the socialist municipal body sort of is like a corporation, isn't it? It uses corporate law -- we're incorporated. I like to think we're using the best parts of *all* the ideologies here, Harry."
"Thank you, Harry, thank you." He bows courteously in his chair. "You have no idea how much it means to me, because in many ways *you* are that working man. You have already done so much work."
"Harry, the future I have in store for Martinaise will have all the *macho* aesthetics you love so much. The crowns, the guns... I will even slip in a skull and bones for you, my friend."

"Harry, the length you're willing to go to keep your nose clean is *remarkable*." He stares at you lovingly. "You will always have a warm bed in Mr. Claire's household, my friend, and a special place in the future of Martinaise."
"That's it for now." (Conclude.)
"How many of you guys are there in the Union?"
"2,372," he replies like a whip. "Plus yours truly, of course."
"You can bother Leonard with that." He points to the door. "He loves to run his mouth on such matters. But I'm in Big-Time mode, Harry."
"Can I ask you about specific union members?"
"A few more questions about the harbour."
"I'm always happy to educate and entertain you, my friend." He takes a sip from his coffee. "So, what's on your mind?"
"Harry, I've got to be honest with you." He turns solemn. "Your gun was found two days ago. Withholding this information weighed heavily on me. But it had to be done."
"You bastard!"
"Fine, where is it?"
"Your gun is with an old woman," he says, absolutely unperturbed by your outburst. "I hear she's a character, so watch out."
"An old woman has it and, let me tell you, Harry, word on the street is she's a character. So watch out."
"How did this woman come to be in possession of the firearm?"
"How did this old woman get a hold of my gun?"
"Turns out she bought the gun from Roy, the local pawnbroker. And honestly, Harry..." He winks at you three times in quick succession. "I have *no idea* how your gun ended up in Roy's hands."

"Someone must have *stolen* it from you while you were sleeping." He smiles. It's really friendly. "Anyway, the neighbours of this old lady contacted my men because they trust me and the Débardeurs Union. Apparently she was waving it around at the entrance to her building."
"She was waving it around at people?"
"As I said she's a character. I didn't have time for details." He smiles. "It sounds like she's unstable, but don't worry. No one got hurt."
"Who *is* this old woman?"
"Unfortunately, I don't know any more. You're gonna have to go in blind, Harry. But she's an old lady -- how dangerous can she possibly be? Oh, and she calls herself the Pigs."
"I, for one, find it refreshing. Finally someone calls *themselves* a pig." A smile flickers in the corner of his mouth.
"Can you set up a meeting?" (Conclude.)

"I already have!" He holds out his index finger. "Tonight, starting 22.00. Near the old fish market on the coast -- the one on the boardwalk, a little past the fishing village. Be careful, Harry. I would never set you up for anything dangerous, but you *did* ask for this. Now..." He claps his hands. "Back to the fun stuff."
"That's it?" He raises his eyebrows. "But you haven't asked about your gun yet. We have so much more to talk about."
"Great, Harry, great! I think we have truly built a bridge between Martinaise and Jamrock today. We have united the RCM and the Débardeurs' Union..." Suddenly there's sadness in his tone.

"This..." He points to you, then himself. "... has been *so* great. I'm sorry we don't have more fun things to do together, but if you ever feel like bouncing something off me, my door is always open."
"Very nice, Harry. Is there anything else?"
He leans forward. "Harry, enough is enough! We're taking this district back. The war was fifty years ago, for god's sake. It's time to move on."
"Why *are* you so fat?"
"Glad you asked. I've got Type 2 diabetes because sugar and fat was all my mother had to give me and my brother Edgar when we were kids."
He wags his finger at you. "Good job too, as it made me ugly. And ugly people, Harry, are *much* better at politics."
"Why, a war, of course."
"And what do you have to gain from a war?"
"Yes, but what do you have to gain from a war?"
"Victory, Harry. I have *victory* to gain. We are going to start a war with the Wild Pines Group -- and win before they even realize there *is* a war."
"Why are you telling me your plans?"
"Because we're friends, Harry! Besides, it doesn't matter now. You can go tell her, if you want -- it won't change the course of events. We have a significant head start."

"The more they send, the worse it's going to look for them. They made a *huge* mistake hiring those guys. *No one* likes foreign mercenaries. The leftists hate them, the fascists hate them, even the moralists think they're *in bad taste*."
"Yeah, everyone hates them. Except ultraliberals maybe. Which happens to be me."
"You're not an ultraliberal, Harry. Get the fuck out of here. Don't be a retard." He smiles warmly.
"What?"
"Tits from her asshole -- it's a local saying."
Actually, no, it's not.
"I did not, Harry." He shakes his head energetically. "Although I am very, very glad he's dead."
"Who killed the hanged man?"
"No idea. Could have been his own mother for all I know. If you ever find the guy, give him a big fat kiss from Evrart Claire. Couldn't have done it without him."
He really doesn't know.
"How do you know it's a guy?"
A guy, huh?

"I don't. I told you it could have been his own mother... I'm pretty sure it wasn't anyone from the Union. Maybe it was the mob... or maybe he killed himself 'cause he was a closet socialist? Truth is, I simply don't know."
He really doesn't.
"We're way past *specific* Union members now. This is the Big Time." His eyes are shining. "We're talking about the future of Revachol here, Harry."
There's something different about him now. He's more vibrant. More alive in his 'Big-Time mode'.
Calls herself *the Pigs?* That sounds bad.
Clients would take a well-known multinational conglomerate over a local mobster any day.
"Everything?"
"You can't possibly hope to continue like you have. Clients will leave en masse."

"Oh, you mean what sort of *goods* are gonna be flowing through? How am I gonna replace all the contacts we'll lose once the poo-poo hits the fan? The clients who'll ditch us? Harry, we've thought of everything."

"We've been running back channel negotiations with all the major clients. I think the company will be *unpleasantly* surprised to see how many of them stay loyal to Martinaise. And to the new, competitive contracts we can offer."
"Sure, some will go, but mark my words: the company will be *unpleasantly* surprised to see how many of them stay loyal to Martinaise. And to the new, competitive contracts we can offer."

"With renewed zeal sparked by communal ownership, the men will be shipping those containers double time. You'll be surprised to see how fast things go without parasites latching on. We'll have our hands free to pursue bold, exotic new revenue streams."
That's drugs!
"By bold new revenues you mean the drug trade?"
"Drug trafficking."
"Drug trafficking? Don't be stupid, Mr. Kitsuragi. There are perfectly legal, 100% ethical chemical factories on the Samaran isola. You don't need to be *colonialist* about it."
"All they do is produce components to keep the pharmaceutical industry running. That's people's health we're talking about. Old grannies, little babes, people with disabilities..."
"Drug trade? Now you're being stupid, Harry. There are perfectly legal, 100% ethical chemical factories on the Samaran isola."

"The company thinks transporting these chemicals in bulk 'looks bad,'" he makes air quotes, "'has bad optics,' 'may be illegal in some countries.' The Débardeurs' Union, however... we're all about the large volume column."
"That's just the top of the iceberg, though, isn't it?"
"God, that sounds shady..."

"We're gonna transport the living daylights out of those materials, Harry." His slams his fist on the desk once more. "So your sick kid can get his *benafed* and your wacky uncle doesn't have to come off *risperizole*!"
*Benafed* is children's cold medicine, usually apricot flavoured, and *risperizole* is used to treat severe psychosis.
"And the kids on the street don't have to give up on speed and pyrholidon?"
"And the kids on the street can get speed and pyrholidon?"
"I'm an old-fashioned guy, Mr. Kitsuragi. I sometimes grab a beer with the boys, but I have no idea about the things you just mentioned." He smiles.
"I'm an old-fashioned guy, Harry. I sometimes grab a beer with the boys, but I have no idea about the things you just mentioned."
He's basically admitting to it.
Nothing in his features betrays any concern.
"It would still be illegal."
"So is there a trade or isn't there?"
Say nothing.
"Go on."

"Let's look at the big picture. Martinaise as a whole. There are little girls out there with dreams of making music. Young mothers who want to start businesses. Models who want to walk catwalks and steel welders who want to weld steel."
Let's keep focusing on the drug trade. He was almost admitting to it.
"Hold on, I don't want to look at the big picture. I want to look at the drug trade you almost admitted to."
"No, no, Harry. That's boring." He sighs. "Alright, it's gone! The hypothetical raw materials trade is off the table. It's such a small and insignificant slice of revenue, I'm cutting it."

"Boys..." He looks around the container. "Harry felt queasy about it. We're not doing it. Can we talk about my beautiful incorporated Martinaise and its many-sided business ventures now? This bold new vision of incorporated socialism I'm offering?"
Oh yeah, skull and bones! Skull and bones on the Revacholian flag. The Revacholian Death Squad. Oh yeah! The visual image has completely bedazzled you. You're 100% with Evrart now.
This must be the woman who bought the gun from Roy, the one he described as "terrifying."
"So the gun's still with the woman who bought it from Roy..."

"Yes, the same one -- I see you've done your research. The pawnshop made the gun easy to track..." He smiles and shakes his head in wonderment. "Crazy stuff, Harry. Selling your gun like that! Wild. Anyway..."
Is this the same woman who bought the gun from Roy?
"Is she the person who bought the gun from Roy?"
"Uhm, I think I needed money so I pawned my sidearm."
Stay silent.
"It was my fault. I pawned it off. I'm a terrible cop."
"Wild stuff, Harry. Absolutely *wild*. I'm not judging you. We all have our dark days. What matters is: Union men are gonna help you fix this." He smiles. "Anyway..."
"...the neighbours of this old woman contacted my men, because they trust me and the Débardeurs Union. Apparently she was waving it around at the entrance to her building."
Better not to gloat, sire. 'Tis *arrogance* that gives the play away. Be subtle.
Judging from how happy he is, it looks like you did it. He doesn't *appear* to suspect trickery.
You don't know his full plan. Perhaps he expected trickery? Perhaps the signatures weren't important? The point is: do not think you're ahead of him.
Hear that? You did it the honest way. You got the *real* signatures and now he's happy. Well done.
We would've preferred trickery, but the choice was yours, sire, as always. You are the liege. And you're *in*.
Finally -- answers. Ask away, son.
I don't know... your dirty forgery-fingers aren't sure if playing this one straight was the right thing to do.
Oops... yes, the noise would do the trick. It'll be terrible.
He proudly spreads his hands to demonstrate the size of the palaces. They're very large.
There is true indignation in his voice when he speaks about the state of things. And even a touch of pain.
The pain is true. He's seen the kids do worse than that.
"Wait, but -- will you erect a statue to yourself?"

"I'm not a *symbolist*, Harry. I'm a realist. My statue will be Martinaise rebuilt: five story building complexes, workers on welfare and landowners in Ozonne *hating* me. That will be my statue -- *and* yours. We're doing this together."
You would look nice as a statue...
And then there will be a giant statue of him, towering above it all?
You would look nice as a statue...

"I'm not a *symbolist*, Harry. I'm a realist. My statue will be Martinaise rebuilt: five story building complexes, kids off speed and landowners in Ozonne *hating* me. That will be my statue -- *and* yours. We're doing this together."
"Wait, but -- will you erect a statue to yourself?"

"Oh I do, Harry, I really do." He crosses his arms on his chest. "I'm gonna make the working man richer than *Joyce Messier* with that vote of yours. That's my job. Just like yours is to keep the peace."
"Damn right I'm up to something, Harry!" The fist lands on the table again. "I'm gonna make the working man as rich as *Joyce Messier*. That's my job. Just like yours is to keep the peace."
"Sounds like you got this. You can rely on my vote."
"I knew you were up to something."
A true flash of anger in him -- as he thinks of her.
A true flash of anger in him -- as he thinks of her.
That *is* true. People don't trust pretty people.
He crosses his hands, contently, thinking of the interior temperature of the wasp rising.
They cook it alive in its exoskeleton.
The word *fuck* rings like a gunshot from his mouth. He doesn't swear often.
He looks at the swordfish clock and nods: "It's already *happening*."
And they're all well motivated. At least the ones you've seen.
2,373 is a sizeable contingent for a labour organization in Revachol.
"Diggin' it, Evrart. I have to say -- I'm diggin' this part!"
Wow, a neurochemical, psychoactive labour uprising / hostile takeover.

"So am I. The company thinks transporting these chemicals in bulk 'looks bad,'" he makes air quotes, "'has bad optics,' 'may be illegal in some countries.' The Débardeurs' Union, however... we're all about the large volume column."
In bulk shipping, *large volume column* is a major buyer. A shark.
He smiles. "But if I *were* to supply ingredients for some sort of rainbow party, I would make sure the Union took a fantastic share -- and I'd keep that stuff far away from Martinaise."
Uhm... because you *pawned off* your gun?
You pawned it off for liquor.
You pawned it, so you wouldn't *shoot* yourself in the head.
"It's good I sold it. I would've shot myself with it."
Union boys are gonna help you *fix* it, he winks at you. Don't worry Harry.
Waving the gun around doesn't sound good. None of this does.
Waving the gun around. Doesn't sound good.
It sounds like a very disturbed and desperate individual.
We might be looking at someone with a medical history here. Watch out.
Unstable is good, actually. She will be easier to disarm... no wait, actually unstable is pretty bad.
There it is again -- *the pigs*, like Roy said. Not good at all.
It actually sounds extremely bad, but let's not give him the satisfaction.
She will be there. From 22.00 till 02.00.
"More fun stuff..." He looks at you. "Seems like we already have fun stuff to do."
Did he just deflate slightly? Was there something he wanted you to ask about? Maybe you should come back if you learn something relevant and ask again.
"Do you remember you said you'd fund your new independent harbour with bold, new exotic revenue streams?"
"I sure do, Harry." He smiles at you idly twirling his thumbs. "One of our many great conversations. Heck, one of my favourites! What about it?"
"By revenue -- did you mean *drug trade*?"
"Cool. I'm glad you remember. Let's talk about something else."
He nods. "Sure thing, champ. Lead the way!"
"What kinds of bold, new exotic revenue streams are we talking about?"
You should definitely come back here and ask again if you learn more about the Union's dealings. There's something he's not telling you.

"Haven't you seen the crates outside, Harry? There's all sorts of fun stuff inside them!" He pushes up his glasses as he laughs. "I mean, heck -- this one has you, me, and my novelty swordfish clock!"
"A fantastic change of heart, Harry!" He rubs his nose. "Go talk to Mañana down by the gates. He'll brief you and give you the key."
"Are you shitting me, Harry? Did you not really open the door and are now just telling me you did?" His lively eyes are mapping your face. "You're a wild one, Harry!"
"I'm very glad to hear that, Harry," he says with a smile. "One question: you didn't actually happen to stumble in and see what's inside the apartment, did you?"
"You said the lynching and the strike are related. How?"
"Tell me about Titus Hardie and his crew."

He nods gravely. "A security contractor. Can you imagine that? Workers standing in peaceful protest -- united in the spirit of fellowship! -- and they send hired killers to *mow* us down with machine gun fire."

"I'm talking *beasts*, hardened killers from proxy wars in Yeesut, Semenine, Saramiriza -- you name it, they've done it. Raping, killing, burning villages -- killing little children for the Señorita Pineapple company, Harry..."
"Go on."
"I think I've heard enough."
"Hold on, you have a village elephant?"
"No, you haven't, Harry." He waves at you with a jolly smile. "I haven't told you anything about the crime yet."
"No, Harry, the elephant is metaphorical and so is the village, but the mercs -- and their brutality -- are very real."
"Now, I haven't *personally* witnessed the brutalities out there. I have the luxury of staying in my container, you see -- if I need to go somewhere, they just move my container." He laughs.
"There's a militant wing inside the Union. A group of people whose duties don't involve manual labour, but peacekeeping in the neighbourhood. Making sure everything runs smoothly."
That sounds a bit like organized crime.
"They're like you guys," he nods to you and the lieutenant. "Idealistic people who want to make sure bad things don't happen. And if they already have... well, punishment must follow."

"One of them got downright suicidal. Getting drunk, violent, a little rapey..." He shakes his head. "Even their own negotiator couldn't control him. That's your boy, the one who likes *hanging out* and trees."

"Mhmh. One day Titus Hardie -- leader of this peacekeeping faction -- comes up to me and says: 'Boss, socialist-democratic fervour drove us to take it upon ourselves to kill this beast that was burdening the land.'"
"He probably worded it differently, but that was the idea. Sure sounded to me like they killed him." He chuckles. "I gave them two weeks paid leave and told them to lay low to avoid retaliation."
"Oh, they are simply fine young men -- all seven of them! Exemplary Union members. Always working to advance their position in the local socialist-democratic movement. Core members."
"Good talk. Let's conclude for now."
"By all means, Harry. What's on your mind?"
"Harry, they're almost all of them *great* guys, born leaders. Whatever happened, I'm sure they only had the best interests of Revachol in mind."
"Work with them -- hell, interview them! But don't fight them. They really are just like you -- men who like beer, women, and some *order* on the streets."
"So let me ask you this... Which one of Hardie's boys is your least favourite?"
"Oh, that would definitely be Fat Angus. His feet smell from a city-block away and he's always having noisy stomach troubles. Horrible, revolting guy."
"So let's say something happens to Fat Angus... let's say a citizen's arrest..."
"You would die, Harry," he says, grinning. "You would die and in the process start a bloody and completely unnecessary war between the Débardeurs' Union and the Citizens Militia."
"Angus, his ever-growling stomach, and his smelly feet are all part of the Union. You have as much right to *arrest* him as he has to arrest you... "
"Angus, his ever-growling stomach, and his smelly feet are all part of the Union. You have as much right to *arrest* him as I have to arrest your partner here." He points to the lieutenant.
"Actually less, because this is my home town, my territory and my backyard. You are a guest here, Harry. Please remember that."
"...actually less, because it's his home and his backyard. You are a guest here, Harry. Please remember that."
"Oh Harry..." He starts laughing. "This is getting real grim and there's no need for that. We are friends." He sits back and looks you in the eye with a wide smile.
"Most certainly, Harry." The big man nods merrily. "Nothing brightens my day like brainstorming these things with you."
"Oh, of course. That's your main thing here. That's *why* you're in Martinaise." He nods. "I know everything that goes on around here and I would *love* to discuss it with you."
"I mean, it's no secret that the lynching is connected to the strike -- so much to talk about! Honestly, it's been weighing on me so heavily. I understand -- you need to *interview* me..."
"I sense there's a *but*."
Say nothing.
"...but there's a *thing* that's been keeping me up at night. I *want* to talk about the hanging. I mean... if we could just calmly talk, exchange information, we could blow this thing wide open!"

"But I *can't* think straight with this thing weighing on me..." He slaps himself on the forehead. "You're a police officer, aren't you? I have a crazy idea. You guys are basically door-opening machines. Incredibly talented at opening doors."
"Kim, is that true? Are we door-opening machines?"
"I've opened a few doors in my life."
"You've heard wrong Evrart. We're not."
"Oh, you're being too modest, my friend." He chuckles. "But don't worry. This annoying thing I have is completely legal. I just need you to open a door."
"And I'm sure you're gonna open this one with flying colours, Harry." He chuckles. "This really is very simple and there's nothing shady about it."
"I'm not sure I understand." He looks to the Union boss. "If you're asking us to break down someone's door, it's not going to happen."
"Come now. I just need you to go open a *little* door for me -- and leave it unlocked. A simple thing. Absolutely nothing shady about it."
"Oh, no one's. It's just a weasel. A weasel lives there. Nothing for you to worry about."
"Whose door is it?"
"Damnit, fine, I'll look into it, we need to talk about that murder." (Accept the task.)
"I can't accept this thing." (Refuse the task -- for now.)
"Why don't you just open it yourself?"
"Harry, I'm a very busy man and, more importantly,  I don't have that extraordinary physique you do." He slams his fists together. "You look like you could run around all day!"
"You want to send someone a message that the police are working for you."
He wants to send a message: "Even the police are working for me."
"I repeat, I'm a very, *very* busy man, Mr. Kitsuragi, and therefore I must occasionally enlist... outside help." He turns back to you. "So what will it be, Harry?"

"You can get the key from Mañana -- he's down by the gates. Mañana's like a free agent in the Union. Special operations. Hardened socialist. A real free-thinker too. He'll tell you precisely where the door is." He smiles, obviously satisfied with how well he planned it all out. "One last thing, Harry."
"Of course, Harry, I understand. But if that's the case, I don't think we'll *ever* find your gun. Even worse -- we won't be able to speak like equals about the murder..."
"Perhaps this was just bad timing for you? Know that you can *always* come back to me. I really hope you do." He winks at you. "For your sake, my sake -- and for your gun's sake too."
"I bet you don't even know anything about the hanging."
"Harry, my dear friend." He sinks deeper into the chair. "I am what people call a *local big wig*. I know everything that goes on in Martinaise."
"Fantastic, my friend! Just let me know when it's done and we can take our friendship to the next level." He flicks his fingers.
"Sure. I understand. But if that's the case, I don't think we'll *ever* get to speak like equals. Beautiful friendship unrealized. I really hope you'll change your mind, Harry..."
"What do you mean by a 'weasel'?"
"Just go there, unlock the door and leave it open. It's been such a burden on me, Harry. I just want this to be over so I can discuss business with you." He puts his glasses back on.
"A loud blabbering weasel. When weasels feel no one is watching, they start acting *foolishly...*" He removes his glasses and rubs his nose.
The lieutenant sighs. "Yes -- we both understand what you meant."
And just like that, it's happening -- the roller coaster is moving. Too late to take it back now.
"Just open *one little door*. You don't need to go in or anything. I just want that weasel to come home and see the unlocked door. That's it. Anything else we should discuss?"
"Yes, let's blow it open."
"Yes. That sounds good," the lieutenant says with a slow nod. "Let's do that."
"Just open the door. You don't need to go in or anything. I just want that weasel to come home and see the unlocked door."
This may be the only way, he thinks. I won't hold it against you. In fact, we  probably *should* reconsider later.
"No, no, Evrart. I really did open the door."
"You're right, I was just testing you."
"Actually, I need to get back to you on this door thing."
"Of course, Harry!" He exclaims. "What are friends for if not for measuring the falsehood one can pass in the disguise of truth."
"Oh, Harry..." He shakes his head, smiling. "You don't need to get back to me. You need to open the door. Very simple, really."
Good, now take it a bit further. Take it home.
You didn't say it with nearly enough confidence.
"And not only did I open it, I went inside too. It was a real weasel's den, Evrart."
"I bet it was, Harry." He says with a grimace -- then the smile dissipates. "But seriously, what did you see in his apartment?"
A guy who has antagonized the Union in a Union-run town? Maybe it's political?
"I saw lot of anti-socialist, anti-union stuff. Pamphlets saying: *Get the unions in check*."
(Shake your head.) "Fascist insignia everywhere. Memorabilia calling for the *Return to the Golden Age*."
"Misogynist posters, racist literature and a signed petition to 'euthanise the invalids'."
"That's exactly what I thought, Harry!" He slams his fist on the table. "What a weasel... And for the record, I was only curious, not testing you."
"Thank you, Harry. You have shown me that the Débardeurs' Union and the Citizens Militia can indeed work together." He nods solemnly. "Now, let's cut down to brass tacks."
He was testing you. You succeeded.
"Be it far from me to ever question your integrity, Harry, but you must have opened the wrong door," he says with a wry smile. "Next time, please be certain you get the right one."
"You know, what, Harry?" He points both index fingers at you. "I got a feeling they're gonna show up in full force *tomorrow*."
He's trying to figure out if you're lying.
"I *may have* gone inside and seen a collection of racist mugs."
"I did go inside. Weasel had the flag of the Old Revachol on his wall."
"The deal wasn't for me to go inside, so I didn't."
"Exactly the kind of fascist memorabilia I was expecting." He shakes his head. "Weasel probably prays to it every night for the downfall of the Union."
"Just as I thought. Culturally antiquated mug collection. What a weasel..." He shakes his head. "*Pissing* on Evrart's Rainbow Coalition."
"You're right, Harry. You only had to unlock the door." He gives you a clever look. "Which you did, so we're all good here."
He *was* testing you. And you succeeded.

"Now let's get down to brass tacks. It's time for men like me and you to figure out who's killed who and why." He pretends to roll up his sleeves. "Real police work is gonna start happening now. I promise you, Harry, this is gonna be good."
"I really went in there. Whose place is it? I just need to know."
"There was a collection of colonial mugs there, and I found a similar mug in the trash with the hanged man's clothes."

dialoguetext: "Why?"
"What if it's connected to my case?"
"Okay, you're right. It's probably not important."
"Believe me, he's not a killer. He's a nobody. Just a basement-variety armchair fascist, who comes up with needlessly complex conspiracy theories."
What if one of those *complex* theories is right?
"Did one of his *complex* theories turn out to be true?"
"Racist mugs in the trash AND in the apartment?!" He grabs his head with both hands. "You guys are just light-years ahead of me."
"I have *so much* confidence in the ability of your organization. I'm relieved you're doing this and leaving me to do what *I* do best -- helping people. With the power of *politics*."
"Yes-yes... Do you think this 'weasel' is somehow connected to the murder?"
"Did one of his theories turn out to be true?"
"Do you think this weasel has something to do with my case?"
"Oh, no, no, no, no. I don't cross paths like that." He shakes his head, laughing. "All I want is for you to succeed in your investigation. I would never *complicate* things for you."
"But this weasel might have cleaned up after the killers."
"Believe me, Harry, he's a nobody. Just your basement-variety nobody... Can't imagine him being connected to a high-calibre case like this."

"But he *does* live nearby -- maybe it's a pedantic weasel? Fascists are known to be neat freaks... I feel like a real detective right now, Harry! Am I getting this right?" He imitates bashing something with an imaginary baton.
"Great technique. You'd make a great sergeant."
"There's more to police work than whacking an imaginary baton."
Say nothing.
"Of course, of course, Harry. I'm not a real police officer. *You* are!"
"Of course, Harry. Stoic silence. I like that. Very befitting a police officer." He bows slightly in his chair. "I'm not a real detective. You are."
"Oh, you're too kind, Harry! Way too kind." He chuckles. "I know I'm not a real police officer. *You* are!"
"Would he? I'm not so sure about it."
"What if it did? What if he took a whack in the dark? Started telling people the strike is funded by a protection racket that drove local shops out of business?"
"What if he planned to write a hack-piece to the local newspaper regarding these crazy theories he had developed. Just to stir up trouble. Wouldn't that be annoying?"
"I see."
"That'd be awful if I intervened in something like that."
"That's not a big deal. Certainly not big enough to do something insidious."
"That'd be cool. I live for shutting these journalist fucks down."
"Journalism, Harry -- I love it, you love it, and you know why? Because we've got nothing to hide. Let's keep it that way."
"Truly awful." He shakes his head. "It's great it didn't happen then. I personally love journalism. And I know you do too, Harry. That's because we've got nothing to hide, right?"
"Insidious? Would I ever ask you to do something insidious? Of course not!" He shakes his head. "I personally love journalism. And I know you do too. That's because we've got nothing to hide, right?"
"So funny, Harry. I, of course, love journalism. And I know secretly you do too. And you know why? Because we've got nothing to hide."
"Now please, let's get back to the good stuff, the police stuff, Harry! I just see myself as one of you guys. Think of me as a sergeant or something." He smiles broadly. "Let's *crack* this, Harry."
"See, Harry? Many questions become irrelevant once we ask ourselves *why* we're even asking them." He winks at you. "But I'm sure you have plenty more where that came from."
"Harry, this strike is the culmination of many *many*, mistakes made by the Wild Pines Group. They tried to shut the strike down by sending in armed mercenaries."
"Everything they did there, they brought over here. They want to turn Revachol into a Third World slum. Honestly, the only thing they didn't do, is kill the village elephant."
"Wait, they move the container?"
"Go on."
"Yes! I'm an old man, Harry. My legs aren't what they used to be. They lift my office with that big crane. It's actually very fun, you should try it."
"But enough about me and my fun container." His face turns serious. "The killers the company hired... I think there were three of them. All hardened commando-types."
"Harry," he says, ignoring the lieutenant, "what you need to realize is -- we dockworkers are not pushovers."
"We got grit, Harry -- this whole neighbourhood does. Push us hard enough and we push back -- and when we do..." He raises his finger. "We push to kill."
"Who exactly did the *pushing*?"
"Wait, the whole *neighbourhood* is in on it?"
"Potentially, Harry, potentially. We got arm wrestling champions, rowing club people, ex-coal miners -- tough guys, all ready to spring into action for their home base."
Again: that sounds like organized crime.
"So these *idealists* killed our victim?"
"Did they kill the hanged man?"
"Aren't you worried we might arrest them for this?"
"Are you not afraid that we're going to arrest them?"

"Oh, I'm not *at all* worried about that. These are not the kind of men who get arrested. They're Martinaise boys, tough and gritty. I'd like to see the man who takes them in." He chuckles. "Besides I sent my lawyergirl to look after them."
Despite his boastful tone, he's having doubts about something -- but what?
"I think you're sharing information with the police, because you don't think they *actually* did it."
"Okay. Another question."
"Certainly, Harry."
"That's very clever, Harry. Yes. They might have said it just to impress some girls or something." He rubs his chin. "But Titus has a bad temper, so the chances are 50-50."
He thinks it's closer to 60-40. 60 they didn't do it.
"Guess what? Not only was the hanging a cover-up -- it was orchestrated by a woman named Ruby."

dialoguetext: "I've talked to the boys and it turns out the hanging was a cover-up. They were helping a woman named Klaasje."
