dialoguetext: "Of course, they just blew smoke up my ass..." There's disappointment in his voice. "I guess they're not as tough as they say they are. Or there's more to this than meets the eye."
"You're disappointed."
"Do you know Ruby?"
"Do you know Klaasje?"
"No," he says looking at the swordfish-clock inattentively. "I don't remember hiring any Rubies to the Hardie boys."
"Oh, the chick Titus and the boys have been hanging around all winter?" He chuckles. "She has them wrapped around her finger. They're paying her rent, bringing her stuff..."
"Maybe that's connected too?" He seems excited by the possibility. "I'm not some genius judge of character. What happened here is up to you to figure out, Harry."
There's more to this.
He *remains* honestly disappointed they didn't kill him.
This woman may be running drugs for him. There's no way he doesn't know her.
"So this Ruby is *not* running a drug operation for you, Evrart?"
"All right."
"Indeed, my friend. All *is* right."
His smile is so wide it could blanket the universe.

"I'm gonna say *no*," he says decisively. "I would say I don't have a drug operation, and if I did, I wouldn't have some Ruby, whom I don't even know, running it. I'd hire cops or... my mom. I don't even know, Harry."

"I'm not a drug dealer." Suddenly he starts laughing. "For a moment it seemed like you were on the track, had a good theory there, but now it's getting *convoluted*. My suggestion is to keep it *simple*. Truth is always simple."
"You're disappointed. Why did you want them to have killed him?"
"There were other things I was wondering about."
"Why was I disappointed that they didn't start a war? I'm not a floozy, Harry." He flashes you a sly smile. "You don't just get to second base with Evrart like this. We're at first base, Harry."
"Of course there were." He nods.
"There was a bullet in the hanged man's head."
"So they shot him?" He sounds pleasantly surprised.
"He was shot in the head *before* he was hanged."
"Yes. Someone shot him in the head before they hanged him."
"How odd." The man shrugs. "I don't know what to say, Harry. They told me they hanged him. A hanged man is what I saw when I took a look into that yard..."
"What I *do* know is -- the case is in safe hands. If anyone can get to the bottom of this shot-and-hanged man, it's my favourite policeman -- Harry."
"How do you know the mercenaries were hired by the shipping company?"
"How do I know? Let me tell you about these people." He slams his fist on the desk. "That's their MO. It's what they do."

"Last winter some poor workers in Terminal E went on a little strike. The company sent in *Sediment* -- a security contractor. The strike was over the workers' right to wear protective footwear, Harry."

"These guys turn up and start beating people. Tell you what, Harry, I wouldn't be surprised if we got the same mercenary company -- after a little *rebranding*. And I'm sure as hell not surprised to see an army of scabs under my gates."
"So you think the security contractor organized the scabs?"
"So you believe the scabs were organized by the security contractor?"

"You said it, Harry! Hell --" the fist lands on the desk again -- "one of those guys looks big enough to take down that proverbial elephant! Boys like that don't just *happen* to show up during strikes."
"The name of the company is Krenel this time. It might have been Sediment before."
"Of course, you're always one step ahead of me, Harry. I'm no genius. I'm in this position because people *like* me."
"The remaining mercenaries are organizing a tribunal to take on the Hardies."

"Tribunal?" He appears aghast. "That sounds *serious* Harry. We Union men should be *shitting* ourselves..." He rubs his chin and smiles suddenly: "I wish you hadn't told me that. I'm gonna lose *sleep* over this. Let's change the subject."
He's clearly happy about the tribunal.
"Let's change the subject."
"By all means, Harry. What's on your mind?"
"You don't *seem* too worried about it."
"Okay. Yes."
"Oh, Harry, what do I *really* think about the tribunal? You're trying to climb to second base with old Evrart before you've even courted him properly."
He wants you to do more *things* for him before.
"You're right, you're right. My sleep isn't your concern -- tell me, Harry, what else can I help you with?"
"You mentioned a *lawyergirl*?"

"Oh, Liz is a bright one!" He grins broadly. "I paid for that law degree myself, thinking it'll probably turn her all fancy, but hell, Harry -- she came back a firebrand socialist! Sometimes she scares *me* with her zeal."
"Did you send her to spy on me disguised as a gardener?"

"I did that, didn't I?" He snickers. "She thinks of herself as a guerrilla fighter. These middle-class kids and the books they read are crazy, Harry. I think she would rather be an *insurgent* than a lawyer. I hope it's a phase."
"In the future, I could use your backing. Can you ask the Hardie boys to cooperate?"
"Old Theo used to run them, but things really *kicked into gear* when Titus took the reins and named the group after himself." He starts laughing. "Gotta love his initiative."
Separate one from the herd.
"Where can I find them? The Union booth in the Whirling was empty."
"Where can I find them?"
"What if I were to pin this on someone and just quietly..."
"But of course! It's the least I can do for my good friend, Harry. I'll do it right after we've concluded this talk."
"Also, Harry, here's five reál." He holds out a banknote.
"Wait, why are you giving it to me?"
Take it.
"I don't need it, I only wanted you to help me with the Hardie boys."
"I'm not giving you anything. I'm just holding out five reál."
"Oh, I wasn't offering it to you, just holding it out there." He pockets the bill. "But I am willing to share *information*. Was there anything else?"
"Good boy, a real team player." He rubs his hands together. "Now -- do you have any more questions?"
The lieutenant watches you pocket the bank note. He looks a little puzzled.

"*Was* it a good talk?" He leans back, suddenly worried. "I'm not sure we made much headway here. I was hoping we'd bust the case wide open, heck, I even wanted to tell you what I *really* want to achieve with the strike..."

"I don't know what happened, Harry. I wanted you to feel like Mr. Martinaise! And, of course -- I also wanted you to *find your gun*." Great sadness comes over him. "But... it's like I can't completely trust you. Yet."
"Yet?"
"Yes, Harry. It's like I can't *fully* trust you if you're not a man of the left," he says, slowly shaking his head. "I *want* to, but I just can't..."
"I am not a 'man of the left'. I'm a patriot of Revachol."
"You're right not to trust me. I take care of *me*. I'm a hustler. I grind. I'm a money engineer."
"What's that supposed to mean?! I'm more left than *you* are."
"This is another corrupt scheme, isn't it? I'm neither left nor right. I do what my *heart* tells me to do."
"Just between us, I don't care for those lefty dinks either." He immediately changes course. "It's all about *power* and here's how we're gonna get it -- I need you to be my kingsman, Harry."

"Perfect, Harry! That's perfect!" he claps his hands. "My version of the left is not against the companies. It's *with* the companies. Honestly, what I have in mind is a business proposal. A left-wing business proposal, but still..."

"You're saying it, but I don't believe you. You know how it is -- company snitches, *agent provocateurs* everywhere... I'm barricaded in this fortress of mine, and I need to get a message out. Will you help me?"

"What does your heart tell you about your lost gun, Harry? Does it tell you to forget about it? Or do you think it wants to be found?" He picks something from his teeth. "I think it's lonely and cold. I think it wants to be found and I have a proposal for you."
"It's time for men like me and you to figure out who's killed who and why." He nods. "Real police work is gonna start happening now. I promise you, Harry, this is gonna be good."
"You see, Harry, it only benefits me if you open the right door. If you open the wrong door, then it makes things harder for me, 'cause now you're scaring random people in my district."
"I don't want them to be scared. I want them to think, 'Wow, I feel so safe. I like Evrart.' I only want weasels to be scared."
The lieutenant shrugs.
He means: "Fuck it, let's open the door then."

"You need to get signatures from Isobel Sadie and Lilienne Carter. The cul-de-sac is right past the pawnshop and across the canal. I heard there was some trouble with the water lock, but it should be fixed now."
"Once you have the signatures, mail this to 13022 La Rocca, district of La Delta. Then we can talk." He runs his fingers through his thin hair.

"Once again I require nothing unethical or illegal of you. You just need to get two little signatures on this piece of paper." He pulls out an envelope. "And then mail it to my accountant in La Delta."
"What are the signatures for?"
"There's a nameless little street on the coast with some old houses around it. Most people have already signed. I just need *two* more signatures to get this mission off the ground, Harry."
"No, I'm not going to do this." (Reject the task.)
"Fine, if I happen to be there, I can ask them." (Accept the task.)
"You bring joy to my heart, Harry --  such a pleasure to be working with you. Here..." He hands you an open white envelope.

"Perfectly acceptable." He smiles. "No one's gonna force you into anything, but I don't know about that gun of yours... You see, I'm a vengeful man, Harry. Part of how I got where I am is that, well -- I can be quite nasty sometimes."

"I'm glad you asked, Harry -- the Union is going to build a modern youth centre in Martinaise!" He grins broadly. "It will be *righteous*. We're gonna get those teenagers off drugs -- and *on* roller skates!"

"They're just gonna have to deal with the construction noise for six months and then they'll be living like kings -- right next to a fancy new youth centre, designed by the best architects from Stella Maris."
"What will happen to the current occupants?"
That's not how you baton someone! The technique is way off. You strike with your whole body not just the baton...
"By now I'm *sure* you've figured out who the dead man was working for -- the bad guys. Wild Pines. Sent to scare us. Another *violent measure* of the top hats against us flat caps."
"What do you mean?"
"You mean our victim?"
"Our victim?"
"About my fun container?" He chuckles. "It's a hoot, Harry. Who knows, maybe you'll be in here the next time they move it. It will be very fun, I promise."
"What makes you think the Wild Pines negotiator can't control them?"
"How did he end up hanging from that tree?"
"By *negotiator* you mean Joyce?"
"Harry, what you need to realize is -- we dockworkers are not pushovers."
Maybe he doesn't believe the boys *really* had it in them. They're his boys after all.
He's thinking: *Damn, what a mess. Good thing this isn't gonna come back to me.*
"What more can you tell me? Who's second in command? Who's the most violent?"
"Interesting. Who's second in command?"
The lieutenant marks something in his notebook.
"What would this entail?"
"And what would this entail?"
"Kim, what do you think of this?"
"It depends. I don't think what we just got from Mr. Claire was very useful." He studies Evrart.

"As I said, it weighs on me heavily..." He bows his head in shame, then looks up and smiles: "But once we get *really* talking... well, I'm gonna hand you the keys to Martinaise! And maybe even help you figure out who's behind this killing."
"You mean the fishing village?"
"Where is this *place* exactly?"
"Yes, yes, the little cul-de-sac on the coast. Where all the men have drowned -- in either the sea or the bottle. A gloomy place, doesn't have that Union attitude."
"On the coast, Harry. Across the canal. There's a cul-de-sac there -- a little *village* they're calling it. A gloomy place. You'll find it. I trust your detective skills, Harry."
Is he absolutely sure the tenants won't be thrown out in the street?
"Are you 100% sure no one's going to end up homeless?"
"Sounds like everybody wins."
"Am I...?" The big man shakes his head in disbelief. "Harry, these people... Martinaise is the most important thing in my life. I would never let anything bad happen to them."
"The people win, Harry." He nods solemnly and repeats: "The people win."

"You need to get signatures from Isobel Sadie and Lilienne Carter. The cul-de-sac is right past the pawnshop and across the canal. I hear there is some trouble with the water lock, but they should fix it by Wednesday morning."
"Another question."
"Absolutely Harry, absolutely. Sock it to me."
He's saying as little as possible as vaguely as he can. Deliberately omitting things.

"We're gonna build a youth centre there. The value of their properties goes up and kids have a place to play in. I'm looking out for these people, not pulling the rug from under them, Harry. I'm looking out for all of Martinaise, not just the harbour."
He means it.
"But the good news is, the moment you change your mind and want to look into this matter -- just tell me, and we'll be buddies again." He smiles pleasantly.
The lieutenant's eyes meet yours and he shrugs.
Okay. Fine.
"Let's change the topic."
"By all means, Harry!" He nods excitedly. "What's on your mind?"
"No. You have to put your weight behind it if you wanna do real damage."
"Oh, Harry," he bursts out laughing. "Thanks for the tip. I'll leave doing the 'real damage' to you -- you are the real police officer after all, not me."
"Harry," the big man says with a tragic look on his face. "Had you asked me earlier, I could have used your help in dealing with a certain weasel. It would have really *solidified* our friendship."

"Sadly the moment has passed and the weasel's back in its den. Nothing to do about it now, so get this --" He points at you. "-- I'm just going to *give* you the information, because I like you, Harry."
There's probably more to that.
"Wait, who was the 'weasel'?"
"Yes, let's talk about the murder."
"The time has passed, Harry. Were you not listening, when I just said that? Pay attention please." He wiggles his chubby index finger at you. "Now, do you want to hear about the hanging or not?"

"Fantastic! Time for men like me and you to figure out who's killed who and why." His fist lands on the desk. "Real police work is gonna start happening now. I promise you, Harry, this is gonna be good."
"The weasel-thing sounds fun, wish I could have done that."

"Yes, that would have been the interesting way to do things. For both of us really. But you were too slow." His expression turns to compassion. "But do not despair over this minor hiccup, Harry. I *will* tell you about the murder."
"But enough about me and my container." His face turns serious. "The killers the company hired... I think there were three of them. All hardened commando-types."
"You fucked up. You waited too long, the weasel came back, and now you can't open the door I asked you to open..." The big man looks you straight in the eye.
"Evrart forgives, Harry." A wide smile crosses his face. "Don't cry, my boy. It's gonna be alright. I'm *still* gonna tell you about the murder. That's just the way I am. Benevolent."
"I thought I had more time..."
"I don't deserve that information, I didn't earn it..."
"Fucking weasel..."
There is no way to sway this man in any direction. He is un-suggestable and un-swayable. Just tell the truth.
"I did go inside. He had the glorious flag of *Revachol the Suzerain* on his wall."
"The *weasel* is no true patriot, Harry." He shakes his head. "He prays every night for the downfall of the Union -- and spits upon the name of the king."
Oddly, it seems to be true.

"But he *does* live nearby... maybe it's a pedantic weasel? Fascists are neat freaks, if you don't mind me saying so. I feel like a real detective right now, Harry! Am I getting this right?" He imitates bashing something with an imaginary baton.
With a police baton. Like a crook or someone.
That's all he's going to say on this subject.
He performs a motion, as if spraying bullets from a machine gun.
Those Señorita Pineapple people are scary motherfuckers, decimating your state if you don't give them your pineapples.
An entire neighbourhood of... killers.
If he's just boasting then it sure doesn't feel like that to you. He's not worried.
He places a lot of faith in that *lawyergirl*. Perhaps this is a tactical error? Anyway.
"How odd." The man shrugs. "I don't know what to say, lieutenant. They told me they hanged him. A hanged man is what I saw when I took a look into that yard..."
It's impossible to say if he's telling the truth, sire.
That does sound quite unlikely, yes. The big guy leading the scabs at the gates is *colossal*.
He's not scared of them. If anything, he *likes* them being here. Strange...
(Better not to mention it.)
"Oh..." He smiles -- it's another big grin. "And she also really likes *gardening* I hear. In March. Strange. Anyway, let's move on."
Don't give him the pleasure.
Better not to.
Or what -- he'll give you info? Fine, don't ask it then.
That's him *allowing* the police to ask his men questions.
He's betting on them being useless to you.
Needless to say, this is another *move*. Don't take it.
How many micro-bribes would this guy take?
A man of the left? So you have to be a social democrat?
He's been *hurt* too much in the past -- by men who aren't *social democrats*.
Kingsman? Yes! Please, let's be that.
But, he thinks, it's your call.
Rollerskating -- not drugs, Harry. You like this.
Water drips from the eaves. A woman looks at her freshly tarred skiff. There's a pair of cavalry boots under the fish in the box and the wind howls like a vicious spirit...
You're already pretty deep into this. What's a little more? No one can see you here in Martinaise...
You can now go and tell Titus about this. See what he has to say.
Wait, the girl by the Whirling, who was keeping an eye on you -- is he talking about her?
When you meet this *Titus*, tell him about this. See what he has to say.
Uncertainty belies his boasting. In the end, though, he believes it -- or at least, he *wants to believe*.
So he doesn't want to counter with a narrative that exonerates the Union. But why?
"I'm not," he says with a widest of smiles. "But I guess you need to talk to this Klaasje person now. What a job!"
"Ruby?" His belly rolls as he laughs to himself. "You come across some wild characters, Harry, let me tell you! Ruby, huh? I guess you need to discuss her too?"
An excellent opportunity presents itself, sire! You could win the trust of the arch-liar, pretend to play into his hand -- then, should you wish, bend his efforts towards your own!

Does this jiggling ooze think he's going to *use* you? He's got another thing coming. Play his game, son, with your eyes peeled. He's going to slip up, and when he does -- you're going to come out on top.
Keep it cool, baby boy. You can use this, groove with this. Play along, let him throw his weight around -- and when he throws it too much, and you've got him off guard, that's when your trip him up.

The stars aligned into a cosmic frown here. He has your fate decided. Bide your time, however, and let the stars continue their course -- and that frown shall turn into a smile. Only if you play along...
He thinks he can force you into his scheme. You can turn this around on him if you accept.
If you can stomach agreeing, you can turn this around on Evrart. And physically speaking -- you *can* stomach it.
Agreeing to take the contracts does not equate to you agreeing to actually help him...
Take the documents off him and you take his power.
Before you stands a cargo container. Just one of many in the yard.
"Lieutenant, I think there's something *special* about this container..."
Open the door.
Nothing more to do here for now. [Leave.]
You attempt to turn the handle, to no avail. The doors seem to be mechanically locked.
"You do? Because I don't."
"There are a million containers here. Why are you fixating on this one?"
"What, why not?"
"I don't know, Kim, it just *feels* special."
Persuade the door to open.

dialoguetext: (Inspect the container.) "Maybe there's contraband in there?"
The lieutenant considers this for a moment. "There may very well be, but we're not here to look for that."
"Hey there, sugar."
"It's a cargo container, detective. Just like all the others." He doesn't even look at it.
The container door appears unmoved by your attempt at flattery.
"You're a fine piece of engineering, do you know that?"
Why are you even trying to open a door with rhetoric?
"Yeah, why *am* I?"
"Why are you what?" The lieutenant looks startled.
"Anything at all."
Despite the dirt that surrounds and trails you, a beacon of light emerges from deep within you.
"Hello, is there anybody in there?"
"If there's someone in there, I'd like to talk to you."
From deep within the container, a voice: "Ahoy! Come on in!"
"Never mind."
The door stands silent.
"Nevermind, I have better things to do." [Leave.]
Knock on the door.
No reply.
The knock produces a hollow ring of metal. Doesn't sound like there's anything inside the container.
The lieutenant sighs. "Is this like your thing with that wall again?"
"No, it's totally different. I don't want to paint it. I'm just *drawn* to it."
"Maybe? I can't tell. I think we should investigate further."
A tough nut to crack, for sure. But the strongest containers often have the softest hearts.
"C'mon, don't shut me out. Let me in."
The door does not respond to your advances. Is it possible that it seems somehow *more* closed than before?
Why does this situation feel so familiar? Do you have a history of propositioning inanimate objects?
"I wonder what's in there."
"What's the matter, honey? You shy?"
The lieutenant nods. "Are you satisfied, detective?"
"Now is not the time to get philosophical, detective. You can do that after hours."
"Because getting physical wasn't an option!"
Have I been summoned?
No one needs you. Go away.
"Because what wasn't an option?" The lieutenant looks startled.
You've got to dance with the one that brought you, detective.
"Using my body over my wits."
Try again.
"Satisfied, detective?" A wry smile crosses the lieutenant's face.
The smile disappears. "You can't be serious."
Just like that, you hear a click. Then a rattle. Some mechanism unlocks itself inside the door.
The door seems to be locked. Conclusively.
You're back before the cargo container. Its draw has not lessened since you were last here. If anything, it seems to have grown slightly.
Who understands anything you do?
[Leave the container alone.]
"It's just another day, another cop and another container."
"It was hanging from the crane."
"You just picked one out, because you wanted to interact with a cargo container."
Aaaaand as it's always been -- it's impossible to open a container with rhetoric. Maybe you're losing your mind?
The mundaneness of the situation does not seem to affect the container in the slightest.
The door does not respond to your advances. Is it possible that it seems somehow *more* closed than before?
"You're right, it's probably nothing."
"Damn it, now you've got *me* curious... this is *not* what we came to the harbour for."

"So you'll do it?
"That sounds like a lot of work."
"Precisely, which is why I'm not going to do it. Why would I do that when I can just speculate on exotic financial derivatives from the comfort of this shipping container?"
The lieutenant's disappointment is palpable. It's like someone just shot his dog.
"Now, was there anything else I could help you with?"
"He should what?"
"Just a minute. The RCM has its difficulties, but generally speaking--"
"You know, that's *exactly* what I've heard. From what I understand, the RCM as currently constituted is essentially a lost cause..."
"Hmmmm, a tried-and-true strategy for increasing the perception of value without improving the underlying asset. Not bad. But still..."
"Uhhh... I'd pay some designers to come up with a new logo and tagline?"

"If I could interject: the RCM's problems are mainly *structural*. We're hamstrung by a lack of clear lines of authority, and our system of performance reviews strongly *disincentivizes* inter-precinct cooperation."

"I think the lieutenant's right. Your problems run much deeper than equipment or funding. The entire org structure of the RCM needs to be redefined. You need a unified chain of command, new metrics for measuring performance that reward real *police work*. Does that sound right?"
"Yes, yes! That's *precisely* what we need."
"The pleasure was mine. Unfortunately, I must be away soon. The next time we meet, I'll be expecting an update on my investment!"
"Farewell, friend, and may your peace of mind guide you to happiness."
"Why go so soon? I feel we've so much more to talk about. Ah, well. Until next time!"
Unbelievable. You manage to meet a man who's so rich light *literally bends around him* and all you can get out of him is three reál? What's wrong with you?
"It's perfectly alright. Based on your appearance I can tell I'm dealing with a civilized man..."
"Could you please stop asking people for money? It does not reflect well on the RCM and to be perfectly frank we can't afford to look worse than we already do."
"I don't see how it's appropriate for a representative of the law to ask a wealthy person for money. This shines a... bad light on the RCM, if you catch my meaning."
"Come now, there is not even a scent of corruption here. I am merely being polite... so let me check my pockets."
"The name's Raphaël Ambrosius Costeau. Most likely."
"Pleasure to meet you, Raphaël," he says warmly. "I am surprised -- in a positive manner, do understand -- about your exceedingly high-net-worth name."
"It's Harrier Du Bois, but I prefer to be called Tequila Sunset."
"Harrier Du Bois."
"Pleasure to meet you, Harrier Du Bois," he says warmly. "I must admit, the name suits you very well."
"Pleasure to meet you Harr... I mean, Tequila Sunset," he says warmly. "It is an odd name, to be sure. There's something... rather grim about it."
"It is not..." The lieutenant stops to rub his temples. "Never mind."
"You would not even believe," the lieutenant mutters to himself.
Ignore him.
"We have a *murder* to solve, and yet you go around bothering everyone about *money*, arguing that you think it's 'somehow related to the case.'"
"Cool. I don't even have any interesting replies."
"One would imagine living such a high-net-worth existence is overwhelmingly exciting, but yes, as you now see... it can sometimes just stun you with its boredom."
"It is, truly. It's almost entirely care free." He nods. "It really leaves you time to better yourself spiritually."
"Capital." He nods. "Makes one speechless, does it not? Blinds like the sun that rises from beyond the horizon after a gloomy winter."
"A million?!"
"You know, a regular youth centre, with basketball courts and stuff. To *really* develop their physical proficiency."
"You know, a regular youth centre, with basketball courts and stuff. To teach teamwork and other emotional skills."
The *blaasma gun* that shoots periwinkle blue high energy plasma! This is your chance...
"Let me tell you about an idea that combines bigger guns with the latest and greatest in technology progress."
"I'm listening."

"Imagine, a massive gun that uses a magnetic accelerator to accelerate highly energized hydrogen-based plasma to near light speed. At contact with anything it detonates with the *power of a dying star*, erasing it from existence in a flash of periwinkle blue!"
The shape stands in stunned silence.
"Not the blaasma gun again." The lieutenant takes off the glasses and rubs his eyes with his fingers. "It's not even *possible*."
"It is not possible. But what a dream..." He shakes his head. "Either way, even if I could do it, I certainly wouldn't give an incompetent and corrupt police force *WORLD-ENDING* weaponry."

"But I appreciate the *grandiosity* of your ideas. Thus you might understand -- the entire org structure of the RCM needs to be redefined. You need a unified chain of command, an end to petty spats between precincts, new metrics for measuring performance that reward real *police work*. Does that sound right?"
Squint.
Cover your eyes...
Actually -- at the level this guy is, it takes several generations to do that, but all right.
"Exactly!" He agrees. "A world of slavery and violence. Which brings us back to the essential truth of modernism..."
"Yeah, that last one. Ile-de-Casherbrume."
"Maybe I should? Sadly, I've never been there. I'm sure it's nice but in the end -- does it matter?"
That's not good -- for you.
A man this *chill* is at least a triple-digit billionaire.

In the very, very early days of colonizing this archipelago, the Kingdom of Suresne, a precursor of modern Sur-La-Clef, used to own the city of Revachol. An obscure detail in the bigger picture, but still -- worth dropping.
"Wow."
"Yes. I imagine that *does* look strange to you. My container."
Okay. Well. Maybe I was wrong. We've all learned something today.
Stop embarrassing yourself. Pop a magnesium and calm down.
Wouldn't say it's exactly *safe* now -- but financially secure individuals are known adrenaline junkies.
"Have you considered breaking into the local art market?"

dialoguetext: We've hit the big time! This is the man who's going to make you *rich*. Always rely on your friendly neighbourhood swindler.
You better explain that you aren't Savvy, by the way. Can't have you nicking this identity after working hard to gain such a prodigious rep.
"There it is. I knew it as soon as you did the Milton 32-8 knock. A fellow entrepreneur!"
"The art market? Intriguing. You've already convinced me to invest in you, so please, go on -- tell me what you're thinking."
"The art market? Intriguing. Well, as I said, I don't carry much money on my person. But do go on, what are you thinking?"
"Ah, a fellow entrepreneur. Tremendous! The art market? Intriguing. Sure, I'm keen. What are you thinking?"
"The art market, you say? Sure. 'Hit me with it', as they say. I'm keen to hear what you have in mind."
"The art market, you say? Possibly. As I said, I don't carry much money on my person, but do go on -- what are you thinking?"
"Well, you've already convinced me to invest in you, so please, go on -- tell me about this opportunity. I'm keen."
"Wait, the Milton 32-8 knock?"
"Yes, the special knock that helps us ultras identify each other. I almost forgot it myself."
"But I'm getting side-tracked. Tell me about your business proposal. I am all *ears*." His face seems to distort in the blinding light, pulling and twisting at his sides.

The Milton 32-8 knock was created through data sonification. It's based on the time series data of the world's most profitable bank during its prosperous years in the Thirties. The peak points were turned into the rhythm that makes up the knock.
"I've recently discovered a local painter with enormous potential." (Show him Cindy's *chef d'oeuvre*.)
"However, there are a few *complications*.... I don't have the cash on me right now to pay for art of this calibre. What I can instead offer are shares in Mauer-Koshlai Mercury Group."
Shares -- that's even *better*. You can do a lot with them if you play your cards right.
"What are these shares worth?"
"We have a deal." (Accept offer.)
"Thanks, but I need some time to think about it." (Decline for now.)

"I bought these shares many years ago for a steal. As predicted, Mauer-Koshlai Mercury's operating profit has increased year on year, and there's no signs of it slowing down. People *always* need mercury."
"Which means you could net yourself a considerable profit if you need some immediate liquidity. But if you don't mind waiting I expect the value of these shares to double within the next five years."
"I've been thinking about those shares you offered me."
"They could set you up for a *long time*. Mauer-Koshlai Mercury is just getting started. Mark my words."
"Not a problem. The offer stands for as long as I'm around these parts."
"Splendid." You hear the sound of expensive fabrics brushing against each other. When it stops, a roll of paper emerges from the radiance.
"What's that?"
(Take the scroll.) "Thanks."
"This is a stock certificate. Well, a photocopy of one. Nevertheless, it's solid proof that you own shares in Mauer-Koshlai Mercury Group."
The light around the individual in front of you changes somehow as you take the scroll. You can't figure out what's different -- you just know that it is.

After you hand over the artwork, the voice from the light says: "Another deal complete. Welcome to the big leagues! If you haven't already, I'd advise you to consider hiring a Personal Brand Strategist."
"What does a Personal Brand Strategist do?"
"Could you hook me up with one?"

"What *don't* they do?" The shiny magnate chuckles. "They practically do everything -- from spotting good investments and analysing design trends, to booking a lunchtime table at the prestigious L'Ambroisie."

"Unfortunately not. I only know the ones who work with multi-millionaires and beyond. But take a look around and I'm sure you'll find one. Personal Brand Strategists are attracted to money like *sharks* to blood. You'll find having net worth opens many new doors for you."

Personal Brand Strategist, huh? Not the kind of person you're likely to find around here. We'll have to ask anyone who seems like they might understand marketing, reputation management... someone who dreams big.
"Actually, Savvy *isn't* my name. Hope you'll excuse me. Let me introduce myself again..."

Oh, and we should see what this net worth can do. Might score a discount, or better yet, get you some free goods. That's the kind of thing that really makes you feel like a hotshot. Ask the local merchants about it if you get the chance.
"Now, was there anything else I could help you with?"
It's a secret handshake of the ultra rich, distributed though private-access yacht clubs and interisolary balls for the heirs and heiresses of the old money. Where you picked it up is a mystery.
"A painter, eh? I am always looking to expand into new asset classes. Who's the artist?"
"Grotbags. Actually, make that Granny Grotbags."
"Let's go with... Lucinda Schweinehack."
"Cindy the SKULL."
"I'd prefer to keep it a secret."
"A-ha. And the name of the piece?" He leans in to take a good look at the rectangular plastic board coated thick with emulsion.
"Morve sur toile."
"The Arduous Slaughter of the Eighth Pinniped."
"Gross Profit."
"Keith."
"Not even a pseudonym?" The light appears to vibrate with surprise.
"Wonderful things aren't they -- names? They can completely change your reading of a person. Or, in this case, a painting."
"Well, I think that settles it. You've found a buyer, my friend. A pleasure transacting with you." The light around him warms you like a friendly embrace.
"No, a complete mystery. You can call her Anonymous."
"And the name of the piece?" He leans in to take a good look at the rectangular plastic board coated thick with emulsion.
"Original. I don't think any of my friends have any pieces from anonymous artists. Or maybe only Luca, the son-in-law of the Comte de L'Ys."
"No, not even him. He might have some Moelles and de Vignys, the *authenticity* of which historians are debating, but I don't think that counts. Perfect."
The Aloïs-Lorblanchet family is known to have one of the biggest and most impressive private art collections in the world.
"What are 'shares' and what can I do with them?"
"What is Mauer-Koshlai Mercury Group?"
"They are the very *unit* of capital. You can buy them, sell them, even sit on them if you think it wise. Trust me when I say this -- becoming a shareholder means you're part of the *big leagues*."
"It's a Gottwaldian-Iilmaraan company that specialises in extracting mercury. It's seen massive growth lately due to the discovery of rödfärg mercury."

"Rehm's using it in their next model. I can't wait for mine to turn up! My predictions say its improved speed and azimuthal range should increase my trade efficiency by a whopping 46%. You really should order one if you don't want to be left behind."
This is the only question that matters. Fail to come up with an interesting hook and he's out.
There's no sign of a reaction for a good three seconds. Then...
"Keith? Just *Keith*?"
Yes, Keith. Stick with it.
What were you thinking -- *KEITH*??!! You're not starting a boy band here, you're naming a future masterpiece!
(Nod.) "Keith."
Say nothing.
"Keith," he repeats.
Even the lieutenant looks tense, waiting to see where this is going...
"Keith, I like it. One of my nephews is named Keith. We haven't spoken in years, since I declined to pay for his most recent trip to rehab. But perhaps this will help patch things up between us..."
Sweat pools up in your clavicles, a rancid smell of *fear*.
There's no sign of a reaction for a good three seconds. Then...
Nod confidently.
Say nothing.
Joyce might be able to help?
Evrart seems to know a thing or two...
Garte seems to have his life together.
No one comes to mind...
She *could*, but she represents the Wild Pines, which is the top of that particular game. No way she's stepping down from there. We need someone lower down.
That old communist?! The only thing he'll strategize is a plan to *redistribute* your hard-earned money to losers and moochers!
He's nothing more than a middle manager living a middle-class life -- your aspirations are *much* more ambitious than that.
We'll stumble upon someone, someone with the right amount of *can-do* attitude... I'll let you know when we do. Just keep your eyes open!
"So! What's next on the agenda?"

Here's an *avant-garde* proposal... What about Idiot Doom Spiral? He used to hustle and hang with the sales hawks and trend pushers of the marketing world. Let's ask him if he knows any Personal Brand Strategists.
Seems like a clever investment. Definitely worth thinking about if you care about your future.
Yes, but chances are you can't use them to buy anything *right now*. No cigarettes, no alcohol, no funky little colourful pills...
He's right, the combination of Rehm's solid engineering and the new rödfärg mercury valves is huge.
It looks almost ethereal -- is it even real?
A step forward for technology, yes -- but only for those who can afford it.
"Have you heard about it? At the moment, it's trading at more than 1.5x the price of gold. That's because it's an essential component in the next generation of radiocomputers..."
"That concludes *our part* of the transaction. Once you've turned over the asset, my people will get the legal ball rolling."
"It's actually just a mixing palette."
"It's an early entry in an emerging style known as Art-ishoo."
"The artist was struggling. *Really* struggling."
"Value is something you should *discover* for yourself. What do you see?"
"I see..." The light appears to concentrate...
"Staring at it long enough lets you immerse yourself in *karperie*."
"Just a mixing palette? But where does the value lie then?"
"That's what I wanted to ask you about. Tell me, what's their *story*? Did they *suffer*?"
"I'll be honest, all I see are splatters that lack any true intention."
Great work -- that might have done it.
"It lets you *immerse yourself* in a modern school of thought? Are you sure?"
Ten seconds -- borders dissipate. Twenty seconds -- loss of self. Thirty seconds -- everything dissimilates into raw unreality.
That's just one of the many dangers of getting too deep into karperie.
"Yes. Spend time with it and the whole world becomes defined by karperie."
"Actually, forget what I said. It doesn't really make sense."
Complete nonsense -- both 'karperie' and what you just said. Can't bathe in thoughts!
"Mhmh. Karperie is *dangerous*. It spreads like a virus, infecting entire universities."
"*Dangerous*? I like things that are dangerous. You could even say I'm one of these 'adrenaline-junkies'." The light emanating from him seems to intensify.
"Sounds like a hell of a trip. I really must experience it for myself." The light emanating from him seems to intensify.
"I appreciate you saving us from wasting time. Is there anything else I should know about the painting?"
"This is a cryptograph used by circuit benders to bring down banks."
"Before I invest, I need to know more about the work. How do I know this asset is going to appreciate with time?"
Remember, you're not just selling a painting, you're selling a *story*. Give the man a reason to throw down that paper.
"Emerging? That's a word with plenty of appeal. What is it that defines this style exactly?"
The obvious answer is to be illustrative. However, he would be much more interested in art that directly tackles social issues.
Just tell him the truth. Why does no one ever want to tell the truth?
Why are you letting this opportunity slip away? Give him a story, an experience, make him want to run away with this painting and marry it in secret.
Running your fingertips across the splatters reveals frequencies used by finance companies for long-distance communication.
That's not very *art*. Tell him it contains an invisible pigment used by corporate spies. Own the palette and you can unveil a whole world of concealed communications.
Now is the time to champion the power of the sinuses!
"I've found it's much better for my health just to throw money at those kinds of problems and hope they go away. That way I don't have to feel guilty about avoiding them."
Looks like he's about to throw some of his money our way...
"It's the organs. She hardly has anything left."
"Actually, I lied. She's from a working class background, but seems to be doing okay."
"Oh." He sounds disappointed. "Well, I'm sure her work represents some very interesting *internal* struggle. Probably with mental illness. Yes, that sounds right."
"Pray tell." The human shape within the light appears to lean even closer. Tiny dots flood your retina as the shipping container gets too bright.
"It's the groceries. The poor thing has to go to Frittte every day."
"*Mesque bangers*? No! Have I told you I've stopped reading the news? It's too negative, can't let it affect my mojo."
This guy clearly gets off on macabre stories. You've got just the one -- an absolute skullfuckery.
"An artist's value doubles if they come with a good backstory. I thought you were an experienced art dealer, you should know this."
Seems like he's not actually that interested in hearing the details. Too bad, you had a good story cooked up...
"What a sad, sad story. I should ask Rhéa to look into this, maybe the foundation can set up some scholarships for cases like these."
"It's something even worse. See, she got involved with Mesque bangers..."
"*Every day*?" The blinding light becomes almost melancholy. "But how does she find time to do any work?"
That's disgusting and thoroughly unethical. You should refuse to engage with this.
You still have an option to not go along with this senseless sensationalism.
It's the artist herself who becomes a commodity, not merely their work.
"Just a hollow husk..." The blinding light becomes almost melancholy.
At least she still has her heart intact, unlike some people here.
"Actually, she seemed to be doing more than okay. If anyone suffered then it's me."
"Wait, why does it matter?"
"Oh." He sounds disappointed. "Well, I'm sure her work represents some very interesting *internal* struggle. Probably with mental illness. Yes, that sounds right."
"You?" The light appears to blink, as if someone switched off the light source for a second. "But why should we care about *you*?!"

"Any details? I've heard some struggling families have to sell their organs to pay the rent. There is also the terrible misfortune of having to go get your own groceries when you're poor. Which one is it?"
"Her socio-economic conditions were meagre, but her spirit remained strong."
(Nod solemnly.) "Terribly."
"In any case, is there anything *else* you can tell me about this piece?"
"Please, if there's something I'm missing, I'd love to know what it is."
"It's art that tackles issues. Art plus issues -- Art-ishoo."
"I see -- very good. What kinds of issues are we talking about? I've really got into the housing crisis recently."
"Poor thing! In that case, buying this will help me fulfil my *noblesse oblige* for the month."
"I see. What is so special about it then?"
"Oh yeah, this is all about the housing crisis. The artist doesn't even have a home."
"Nah, it's just another fad. But there's something else special about this painting."
"Oh yes, I see it now. Very *graphic*, isn't it? Really delivers insight into what it's like being that... unruly."
"It's art that is produced by way of sneezing."
"But perhaps I judge too quickly. Is there an intelligent reasoning behind the method?"
"Hm. Seems unhygienic. Is that what's *in* these days?"
That's it, lap it up, buddy. That might have done it.
"It's a real spit-and-sawdust affair. See those splatters? That's *poor* people."
He only wants to hear about struggles he isn't familiar with.
His scintillating face-shape flashes with an expression that resembles disgust.
"On second thought, not the kinds of issues you'd be interested in."
"The artist enters a state of no-mindedness and lets the body take over."
"Splatter, disarray, chaos -- it's anti-design."
"But design is the very signature of humanity. Everything we do is design. Text columns, urban architecture, the precise shape of a stapler... what are we without any of that?"
Challenge him on this. Cause a scene.
Don't you dare! This isn't the time. Put your personal feelings aside -- you're a salesman!
"Design is nothing. Let it go. It's holding you back."
"Exactly. Don't you want to find out what *else* we could be?"
He swills it around in his brain. "So it's an éxtrasomatic painting. An effort carried out by physical instinct -- not the mind."
"Perhaps I *have* been neglecting the triumphs of anatomical perspicacity lately..." He sinks into thought.
"That's a shame. Is there anything else to this painting, or is that it?"
"Hmm, I do cling to it rather a lot. Perhaps that is one of my shortcomings -- I just haven't realised it before now."
Tell him it was used to mix together an invisible pigment. Own it and he opens up a whole world of concealed communications.
"This is a new type of design. You'll work it out if you spend more time with it."
So close to envisioning what's beyond. Just needs a little push over the edge...
"Hm. I hadn't thought about it that way before. You might have just opened up a new door in my mind."
"That prophet-for-hire did say I should identify weakness and remove it from my life..."
"It contains a unique invisible paint. You can use it to hide important messages."
"Certainly not in its material form. But there's more to it than that."
Yeah-yeah, you're doing a good deed here, really giving back to society. Just give us the money already.
Doors, windows, toilet seats -- open whatever it is you need, buddy. Just get on with making a purchase already!
Here's a prophecy for you, pal. Buying this painting will make your life better (and ours).
"That changes everything."
"Perfect! I've been looking for a way to communicate without the information being intercepted or stolen by rivals."
"Go on. I'm listening..."
"Perhaps I could be the one to 'discover' it? To share it with the wider world..."
That's not how discovery works, but let him think whatever he wants if it means he'll buy it.
"You're actually the first person to see this painting after the artist."
"You mean even *you* haven't looked at it?"
"Still, only two people have seen it thus far. That makes it pretty *exclusive* and therefore potentially valuable."
"Oh yeah. Duh!"
(Lie.) "I haven't so much as squinted at it. It's the exclusivity that gives it value."
Wow, he worked it out all by himself. Such a clever boy. But is he gonna pay up?
"I see, so by artificially constraining supply you're also stimulating demand. I have to say, it's a brilliant strategy..."
Great work. I think you've got him. Let's see what he says...
"And if I don't buy it now, more people will see it -- ergo its value will drop."
It's now or never!
What he wants to know is how exclusive it is. The more untouched it is, the better.
Bit of corporate espionage? He's straight in there. Great job.
Sounds like a winner. Good pitch.
He ate that right up. Pretty sure you've done it.
This transaction has changed the physical relationship between you. You are now more alike somehow.
There! The blinding light dimmed just long enough for you to see his true form! He looked like a regular middle-aged man!
Something's rattling within you. It feels like the first penny dropped into a piggy bank.
Lying will get you nowhere. You can't outrun the truth -- it will catch up to you one day.
The comfortably wealthy want their views challenged when making a purchase. Don't hold back.
He's so close to envisioning what's beyond. Just needs a little push over the edge...
"It turns the artistic process into the art itself."
"What an original idea! By drawing our focus away from the final piece we gain a new appreciation for the craft behind it. An art in its own right that is usually hidden from us."
These people will find a way to justify anything. Looks like you've reeled him.
You've reeled him right in. That's got to have done it.
The Weiss-Wiesemann coefficient for you and this individual has now dropped to .9989 repeating.
Looks like someone left his tarpaulin cloak hanging on the railing here.
Man down! A trooper has been left behind the enemy lines!
When the wind ruffles the cloak you can most definitely see a white rectangle on its back.
You could swear it's more of an instinct than anything else, but you *know* it's a cop's cloak.
"Look, lieutenant! (Point to the flapping cloak.) Someone left his cloak behind."
Ignore the cloak. [Leave.]
I guess it's probably nothing. [Leave.]
"Yes. It is probably yours. It does bear the RCM insignia after all. Now -- how to retrieve it?" He judges the drop.
"You could probably make the jump. You look like you've done some track and field in your day."
"You son of a gun, it's a cop's cloak!"
Indeed it is.
Considering the limited police presence in Martinaise -- you think we might take a leap of logic and say it's yours?
You son of a gun, it's my cloak!
The white rectangle, now clearly visible in the wind, seems to confirm your hypothesis. But who's the cop?
You are the cop. It's your cloak. Don't make things complicated.
Nailed it!
"A cop's cloak! It's a cop's cloak!!!"
Unaware of your existence the cloak continues its helpless flapping.
Go for the cloak -- jump over the ledge!
"What exactly are we doing up here?"
Look around.
"Do you really think this cloak is mine? Should I go for it? Jump?"
"Yeah, not right now." [Leave.]
[Leave.]
Holy wow, that's *high*! You'd have to be a total madman to jump. This is certain death!
As you leap in the air, a chilly breeze engulfs you, sharpening you senses.
Close your eyes, let your senses take in the world around you.
Ankles tingling from the tension, blood roaring in your ears -- you are ready for your rendezvous with the concrete pavement below.

Martinaise goes about its daily routine as you soar through the air. The loud voices of protesters mix with the engine sounds from the traffic jam; waves crash against the pier and dense, salty sea air fills your lungs.
Don't let go of the moment yet.

dialoguetext: The corpse is dominating the yard and the stench is nauseating, even so far from the epicentre. It brings tears to your eyes.
We'll take care of that body too. We'll take care of all of it!
As the concrete floor welcomes you, you realize it's been a while since you felt so alive, alert, capable. Must be the adrenaline.
The little backyard, Kingdom of Cuno, looks almost idyllic when it's not dominated by a decomposing human being.
"Flying f****t... winged pig... shit is airborne..." These are the only words the wind coming in from the Insulindian ocean carries to you.
And its de-facto ruler, Cuno the Gremlin King, is pointing at *you*, talking to his friend. What is he saying?
His words remain indiscernible. No matter -- it's time to start thinking about the landing.
Continue the voyage through the salty air.
"Hell yeah!" The lieutenant exclaims. "My climbing might not have been as disco as your jump, but can we still get an Ace's High?"
"FRANCONEGRO!!!"
"Not bad, not too bad at all."
"The cloak? I *do* think it's yours, yes. As to whether you should go for it..." He looks over the ledge, at the cold pavement below.
The cloak looks like a bag of goodies floating in the wind. Who knows what its pockets may hide?!
"I was under the assumption we could ask the leader of this Union to help us get this body down. This is why we're here, right?" He doesn't wait for you to answer.
"What are we doing? We're awfully close to breaking into the industrial harbour -- they're bound to have information for us. I thought that was our intention..."
You could have died there! Shit, shit, shit, shit... I'm failing you. This wasn't part of our deal!
I got you, I got you, *bratan*. Let me just adjust your breathing a little bit... There, isn't that better?
(Tug on your tie.) God, now I can't breathe at all... Stop doing this to me, necktie, you were supposed to be a *friend*!
"Hey, hey... what happened?" He sounds genuinely worried.
The tears just come. From nowhere. Like a sudden guerrilla attack from the bushes, they overwhelm you.
"Hey, hey... what's happening? You okay?" He sounds genuinely worried.
"I'm alright, Kim... I... I just..." (Keep tugging on your tie.) "I can't *breathe*."
"It's okay, you're just having a *little* panic attack. Try to breathe as slowly as you can, alright?" He shakes you gently by the shoulder.
"Thanks, I think it's working." (Let go of your tie.)
After a while your sobbing stops. Up here no one saw the little meltdown you just had and your heart actually feels lighter now. Time to proceed.
Tears run down your face. You're clutching your chest and mumbling incoherently. How much worse can it get?
Just let me fucking *breathe*, Horrific Necktie.
Feel the squeeze, baby!
Fine, be boring, breathe! -- Get high on some of that sweet-sweet O, baby!
Just let it all out, let it go, let it happen.
As you let go a tidal wave of tears breaks through the dam and washes away everything.

dialoguetext: The tarpaulin cloak swings alone for a while there in the wind. No one's coming for it anymore.
The drawer opens smoothly. Inside is a well-organized selection of brown folders.
It's probably on rails.
Close the drawer. [Leave.]
The drawer slides shut smoothly.
On second glance, someone has forgotten to properly close one of the drawers.
Ignore drawer for now. [Leave.]
"It's *unfortunate* for the Union to just leave their paperwork lying around like this..."
Open the drawer.
The file cabinet stands steady as ever and the unlocked drawer slides out to greet you.
...let's see what's inside, he thinks.
Browse through the folders.
Hundreds of documents containing logistical data. Two kinds of transactions stand out: materials coming into Revachol from the outside world -- from Mundi, Graad, and even Iilmaraa...
It's hard to make sense of this thicket of company names, dates, quantities, and percentages. You try to focus, but the lines are getting blurry...
Force yourself to go through the folders.
Look how blurry all the lines on these papers are -- how unwieldy your own willpower is to yourself. You're like an absurdist Samaran monk -- focusing through not focusing.

Whatever's hidden here is hidden well. Concentration isn't enough, only a trained accountant, with a background in logistics, would be able to *really* make sense of it. However there *is* a little hand-written note, stuck on the side of the drawer.
Hermeneutics was almost within your grasp, but now only vague letters float before your eyes. Less meaningful, but aesthetically more pleasing.
Could I actually focus through *not* focusing?
Leave the folders alone for now.
"If I let my eyes go completely out of focus, all shapes start melting into each other."
You are a police officer, not a spiritual healer. You can focus the normal way by turning your attention to something and not letting go.
"Is that what you're doing with those folders over there?"
"Yes."
"No, of course not."
"Let's just get back to work, lieutenant."
"Right." The lieutenant's expression stiffens. "This is probably not relevant to our case. After all, we are not investigating an accounting mystery."
"Good." He turns away from the file cabinet. "This is probably not relevant to our case anyway. After all, we are not investigating an accounting mystery."
"My thought exactly, officer." He turns away from the file cabinet. "Shall we?"
You're trying hard, but the data here is *unbelievably* dry. Something about containers...
...and the same materials being handed over to companies inside Revachol. Couron, Coal City, La Delta, and Jamrock are listed among the many districts where the imports are being sold.
The file cabinet stands steady as ever. Sliding out a drawer presents you the folders you already went through. On top of them is the handwritten note.
You already went through all of these.
Look at the note.
"Never mind the note." (Close the drawer.)
It appears to be a to-do list written in large, uneven capital letters:
The drawer slides shut smoothly.

REMEMBER, LEO!

* EVRART'S SHOES
* SPECIAL WHIRLING BORSCHT
* WATER EVRART'S PLANTS
* SWEEP OFFICE FLOOR
* MORE BANNERS
"Evrart Claire, probably -- the head of the Débardeurs' Union." He inspects the note. "One of his aides must have left it. Nothing incriminating here."
All items on the list have been crossed out and the note itself is crumpled.
"The leader of the Débardeurs' Union, Evrart Claire, has someone running errands for him." He points to the list. "Nothing incriminating here, though."
(Turn to the lieutenant.) "Look, Kim, a to-do note with a list of errands for *Evrart*."
Ignore the note.
The *special* borscht seems a bit odd in the list.
There it still is -- inviting you to...
Anything interesting? (Browse them.)
Doesn't look too incriminating -- but still feels like a *find*.
What is so special about this *borscht*? Code for drugs? Booze? Blood?
Read the note.
All items on the list have been crossed out and the note itself is crumpled.

REMEMBER, LEO!

* EVRART'S SHOES

All those empty wine bottles and cigarette butts on the ground... Someone *partied* really, really hard here.
Let's just move on. [Finish thought.]
Snow is quietly covering the numerous wine bottles and cigarette butts on the ground. Someone *partied* really, really hard here.
It's probably nothing. [Discard thought.]
Numerous empty wine bottles glisten in the rain. Someone *partied* really, really hard here.
"Did I do this?"
Wait, how hard?
Well, they went through six bottles of *Potent Pilsner*, three bottles of *Commodore Red*, and almost four packs of cigarettes -- it must have been pretty hard.
"Well..." The lieutenant looks at you, then the bottles. "Yes. I think we can say with relative confidence that it was you."
Look at it. Of course it was you. You *partied* here.
Yeah we did, *bratan*! And from the looks of it we had hell of a time. Hell of a time, *bratan*.
"This is really sad. I must have been miserable."
"Looks like I had a lot of fun."
"I'm still not completely convinced it was me."
"Yes," the lieutenant agrees. "This scene isn't exactly ripping with joy. Let's just move on." He turns to leave.
"It really *really* doesn't." The lieutenant turns to go. "Let's turn our attention elsewhere and move on."
Move away from this scene and you don't have to think about it anymore. Just walk away and it's *gone*!
"I am. But it doesn't matter right now. Let's just move on."
Well, I am. Who else could crush such quantities, *bratan*? This is wild. You are wild. We should do this again. But right now you should keep moving.
Yeah... a *lot* of fun. Better not think about it and just move on.
You said it, *bratan*! And this can happen again if we want to. And we want to. Only in a different place. Right now you gotta keep moving.
Yeah, it doesn't exactly look like someone really enjoyed themselves here. No point in dwelling on it now, better keep moving.
No, no, *bratan*, I'm sure it was a blast. When do you and I *not* have fun together? Don't answer that, just take that positive feeling and run along!
"I must have been on an advanced scouting mission in the harbour."
Yes. That's what this was. A reconnaissance mission. Wish you'd only remember the good intel you brought back...

"Oh *SO* advanced. Deep in the enemy territory -- getting fucked up right under everyone's nose -- high on life and adrenaline... and alcohol apparently." The tie tightens around your neck. "I'm very proud of you."
"Yes," the lieutenant marks dryly. "This looks pretty advanced alright. For now, let's just move on."
Wow... this jacket makes you feel *strong*. As if your blood is mixing with that of the venerable Filippian loyalists of old.
It's time to clean up the streets and restore the city to its former glory! Whether you like it or not, this jacket gives you serious nationalist cred.
Apologies, you're right! The need for a strong central government has always been clear to you. You're a true patriot of Revachol -- born to do it.
Mixing? Does my blood *need* mixing? Or is it good as it is?
Oops, I didn't mean to wear a nationalist jacket. [Discard the thought -- and the jacket.]
Yes. Let's hope no one saw you wearing that outrageously fascist jacket.

dialoguetext: [Leave.]
Take the uniform.
"If you must." The lieutenant looks around. "But please hurry -- we're pretty easy to spot up here."
Nothing incriminating catches your eye. The cabinets are clean and their sparse contents meticulously organized. Apart from the uniform, the only noteworthy item is a framed photograph on the table.
Looks like the inhabitant is rather pedantic when it comes to order.
Take the picture.
Leave the picture alone.
It's a black and white photo of a young couple out in a street fair. The man is young, dark-skinned, and dressed in a Royal Carabineer uniform. The girl is smiling playfully at the camera.
"Let's get going," the lieutenant says impatiently. "The entire neighbourhood can see us up here."
The photo remains neatly placed on the edge of the table.
"Why did you take that?" the lieutenant asks, glancing at the photo.
"I'm a cop. It's instinctual to collect evidence."
"*Something* about this man peaks my interest. I think this can be a side-thing."
"I'm making an artistic photo collage, Kim."
"Of course you are," he says matter-of-factly. "What murder investigation would be complete without an arbitrary photo collage."
"Fine." He nods. "But let's move. I don't want to be seen snooping around here."
"I suppose René is not going to be needing it anymore." He studies the uniform. "It's a bit too colourful for my taste, though."
"I don't know about stealing people's *very colourful* clothes like that..." He looks on disapprovingly.
"This is gonna take my shit to the next level."
"I'm done here."
"Fantastic. Try not to wear it with other similarly colourful clothes, okay?"
Looks like the inhabitant was rather pedantic when it came to order.
As you take the colourful uniform, a few cookie crumbs fall to the floor. The owner must have a sweet tooth.
The young man looks happy as well. He's about to smile, right after this moment frozen in time. You're sure of that.
Nothing incriminating catches your eye. The cabinets are clean and their sparse contents meticulously organized. There's a framed photograph on the table.
Nothing incriminating catches your eye. The cabinets are clean and their sparse contents meticulously organized. There's a framed photograph on the table.

It's a black and white photo of a young couple out in a street fair. The man -- René -- is dressed in a Royal Carabineer uniform. The girl is young and very pretty. She is smiling playfully at the camera.
René looks like he's about to smile. This photo must be tied to some good memories.
"I'm gonna ask him about it."
"You're *really* interested in that old soldier," he remarks, surprised. "Not sure I understand your fascination, but sure -- as long as it doesn't take up a whole lot of time."
"It's something to remember him by."
"You really took an interest in that old soldier." The lieutenant sounds surprised. "I guess there's no harm taking the picture. The dockworkers would probably throw it in the trash anyway."
"It's, uhm, needed for work and all that."
Take it. It's just there. Who cares? It's not like anyone's gonna need it.
Generally speaking, it would be *dishonourable* to take it. But then... it looks like a military uniform! And wearing that is very honourable. So, a conflict of honour. It's up to you.

dialoguetext: Listen... It's okay to take a few minutes to yourself. Sit down and have a breather.
You need to rest. Your body is aching. Getting in here has taken something out of you. Have a seat.
Have a seat. Rest.
The chair is not as austere as the rest of the booth. A thin grey pillow is attached to the seat, secured to the stiles by black ribbons.
Search for a little something-something to help you out.
Get up.
The drawers are empty save for old time sheets and receipts. One small box, however, does hold some cheap painkillers. They are slightly out of date.
Take the painkillers.
"Kim, would you mind if I helped myself to some meds?"
The lieutenant shrugs. "I'm not here to tell you what to do, detective."
You take the painkillers. They are yours now.
Breathe deep.
Stale air floods through your nostrils. Not a single mote of dust floats inside your lungs, though. The inside of the booth is immaculate.
Read the side-effects.

Oh boy, where to start. Elevated risk of dementia? Mini-strokes? Prophet's disease? Sudden death? Hair death? Erectile malfunction? Critical flatulence? Watery blood? Black mucous? Uncontrollable weeping? Increased sensitivity to l'Opéra? Inoperable joint disorder? Total spinal collapse?
Maybe this was a bad idea...
Don't think about that! Quick, think about something else!
The imagined dazzle of light overwhelms any list of potential side-effects. Any negative thoughts are drowned out by the fantastic blast of *disco*.
Disco. Mirror balls. Kick-ass moves. Boogie beat.
... oh my God, I went up to a woman and actually said *I want to have fuck with you* earlier. What the hell is wrong with me?
I hope I'm not fucking René over by taking his painkillers.
I don't see what the big deal is. This sounds pretty normal to me.
I am scared I will never be held or loved in this world again.
Your nihilistic humour renders the list of side-effects null and void. Just like everything else in this empty world.
I'm a cop. I have cop things to do. Murders to solve. People to help. Kim's counting on me.
The enormity of the case before you dwarfs the list of side-effects. You can't even see the side-effects anymore. They're nothing to you.
That's kind of sad, actually...
Moving along!
Yes. Moving along.
Get up.
You stand and exit the booth.
You stand and exit the booth.
It is harder and harder to reach you... I am not sure how well you'll hear me...
Please, I want to help you! Where must I go next?
Can't you just tell me where you are? Or what you are?
GET OUT OF MY HEAD!
Listen within the flower of home… I am lost... Please....
I am lost and unfound... Listen within the flower of home…
Forgive me... I only want reunion... I am struggling to know where... Listen within the flower of home… Please...
With a loud grind the crane shifts overhead, moving a massive metal container through the air...
A rusting control panel with several knobs. Two buttons, marked *Marche* and *Arrêt*, are faded with use. It seems to control the large crane above -- a container is attached to its hook block.
Press *Arrêt*.
Press *Marche*.
[Leave.]
The crane stands tall: proud, erect and *still*.
No screech of metal when you push the button this time. Only silence, as the crane remains in its state of dormancy.
The crane does not return to its original position. It does not move at all.
... and with a surprisingly quiet thunk, the crane places the container down.
A rusting control panel with several knobs. The words *Marche* and *Arrêt* are -- very, very slightly -- even more faded with use.
*Marche* -- On. *Arrêt* -- Off.
What's inside the container?
Understood. Let's get back to the panel.
Who can say? All you know is -- it's special.
If only you knew...
This crane was built with a purpose which has now been fulfilled -- to move *this* container.
The harbour sleeps as the strike rages in the distance. The crane can rest again, now that its purpose has been fulfilled.
Moving *this* container, of course. For this purpose it was built; for this purpose it has acted. And now it will rest.
Its purpose? What do you mean?
Understood. Let's get back to the panel.
The rusty control panel grows warm to the touch. Then grows cold. It is finished.
A faint smell of burning rubber reaches your nostrils. A short-circuit.
"I can't see how that was worth the ruckus..." He looks at the crate. "Except for seeing the crane in action. Which, I admit, was satisfying."
The machine swallows your coin and seems to be waiting for your next move.
[Leave.]
Let your muscle memory dial a random number.
"No."
"Maybe you called to extend your rental period? Do you need to extend your rental period?"
"Maybe, but I don't even know my *name*."
"What is this place?"
"Video Revachol is a 24 hour video rental. We rent eight and ten millimetre film for home use. This is Lemmy."
"Do you know me?"
"Why did I call you?" (Continue.)
...a crackle, someone picks up! They say: "Video Revachol, 24 hour video rental. We rent eight- and ten-millimetre film for home use. This is Lemmy, how may I help you?"
"My name is Harrier Du Bois. Do you have anything on my name?"
"No, I meant what is this place to *me*?"
"Sir, I don't know. It's a video rental. Maybe you rent videos here?"
"If you need any further assistance you can visit us on the corner of Voyager and Main." He sounds annoyed now. "I can't help you over the phone -- are we done?"
"Uh... it's not an easy watch." He reads: "'After the death of his daughter and subsequent divorce, Zsiemsk immigrant Igidius Wójcik tries to come to terms with the onset of dementia...'"
He concludes: "No wonder no one's been missing it. Still, it would be great if you could return it to us. We're on the corner of Voyager and Main."
*It*.
An imposing combination of a punch-clock and a payphone is looking down at you from the wall. A note on the side says: "Tokens unavailable due to strike. Use change."
The already familiar cold touch of plastic welcomes you as you pick up the handset.
Insert 10 cents.
Your fingers run over the dial pad. 005... that's the dialling code for Revachol -- 49-52... and a moment of hesitation before entering the final numbers: 993.
It's unclear whether you actually have muscle memory. Right now your finger is just drawing vaguely occult patterns in the air.
Useful patterns?
I might try this again later.
Undoubtedly, no.
Sure, why not. Muscle memory is a tricky thing.
Nothing tricky about that. You just *do*, *fail*, *repeat* until it works. All it takes is motivation and practice.
The voice of a youngster on the other end sounds as enthusiastic as that of a man walking towards the gallows.
"Let me fire up the machine..." Keys are being pressed in the background. "Du Bois... Du Bois..."
"What kind of a film is that?"
"Oh, okay. Thanks."
"If you can, return it to us on the corner of Voyager and Main."
He thinks you're pulling a prank on him.

On the corner of Voyager and Main a large neon sign hangs on the side of a building: "Video Revachol, 24h." It's raining and there is almost no traffic on the street. A woman's footprints in the mud lead away from the front door.
Suddenly you feel like you don't want to hear about video rentals anymore. You don't want to hear about *any of it*. It was all shit. It's over.
The call is terminated by the other party. You're left with the discomforting sound of the disconnect tone.
What was all shit?
"Kim, I feel sad about Video Revachol 24h."
"We're done." Hang up the phone. [Leave.]
"That's enough for you today," the lieutenant says quietly. "Let's conclude this call."
The payphone hangs mutely on the wall. There isn't much more to do here.
Calling...
Calling...
"Here we are! You haven't rented anything in five years, but you still have a copy of *Blue Ocean Hell* from November '46. Wooh, not a fun film, that one."
Quietly hang up the phone. [Leave.]

The same exact belts. Even the same writing...

Yes, this confirms Titus's story.
I knew it was a cargo lashing belt!
Indeed, it appears so. This is where the belt came from.
"More ammo on our belt for the remainder of the investigation. Good find, detective."
A common office radio, like any of those found in countless waiting rooms, lounges, and other semi-public spaces all over the world.
How do I get the transceiver out of this thing?
"What do you need with another transceiver? It's almost exactly like the one you took from that radiocomputer in the Doomed Commercial Area."
The lieutenant gives you a brief nod.
"You sound pathological, you know that? Now come on, let's stop wasting time."
"There's usually a little switch somewhere... Ah, yes, it's the one that says 'RELEASE'." The lieutenant points to the side of the radio.
"But Kim, I need to collect *all* the radio transceivers. For thoroughness' sake."
"Good point, no need to be greedy."
You have no need for this transceiver, because you already have one just like it.
Good point, no need to be greedy.
But what if I want *another* one, as a backup?
The radio appreciates your restraint. It buzzes contentedly.
The radio appears to disapprove of your acquisitiveness. Its buzz seems to drive you away.
It's quite easy. Simply flip the switch labeled 'RELEASE' to disengage the lock that holds the transceiver unit in place.
Flip the release switch.
The lock disengages with a nice click. You may now safely remove the transceiver unit.
Examine the transceiver.
[Leave.]
"How does this compare to your DynaWave, Kim?"
