dialoguetext: "Do you think we'll actually be able to reach the Coalition with this?"
"I wouldn't like to guess. Your performance so far doesn't exactly inspire confidence, but all sorts of things are possible..."
"*You* could reach the Coalition and have your talk about *la responsabilité*... *I* could grow 10 centimetres and become a flanker for the Stormers."
"Who's to say what's possible and what's not?"
"It doesn't, frankly. Don't get me wrong, this appears to be a *fine* transceiver for a general audience, but it's not something a serious radio-head would use." He shrugs.
"That's fine. I'm not interested in 'pissing competitions,' as you know."
"Well, I guess this will just have to do, then."
(Clench your fist.) "I'll show you yet, Kitsuragi."
"Of course not, detective. This is *strictly* business." The lieutenant smiles to himself.
"I suppose it will." The lieutenant smiles to himself.
"Show me what, detective?" The lieutenant seems immensely pleased by your irritation.
There's nothing obviously remarkable about it. It's about the size of a common pasta box, with knobs of molded plastic. What else is there to say?
If this transceiver were a person, it would be an accountant at a large logistics firm. Perfectly competent, but unexceptional.
"I prefer a transceiver with a little more *flash and style*."
"Reliable and unassuming. My kind of transceiver."
"Sorry for stealing you, transceiver, but there was no other way."
"There's something *ominous* about this radio transceiver. It's an ill omen."
(Tap it with your knuckles.) "Yeah, this'll do."
"I guess pure functionality is itself a kind of aesthetics."
"I'm sure the transceiver understands, detective. Now let's go."
"Hmm. I don't think the people who typically buy these machines are very concerned with questions of *style*."
"Yes, 'reliable and unassuming' are *definitely* words I'd use to describe you."
"I'm not sure where you're getting that. It's a perfectly fine transceiver and this is a perfectly ordinary office."
"I suppose it does have a certain 'no-nonsense' appeal, if you prefer that sort of thing."
"Very good. Let's get going then."
The transceiver appears glad to be of service.
The transceiver appears quite at peace with its appearance.
The transceiver appears to understand and forgive you.
The transceiver appears slightly bewildered by your comment.
The transceiver appears slightly hurt by your comment.
The transceiver appears to take this as a compliment.
With its transceiver gone, the radio has ceased its peristent buzzing. It is as silent as a headstone.
[Leave.]
"To be honest, I mostly just want to ride on Coalition Warship Archer."
"You've surprised me more than once during the course of our investigation, but I have to say it still seems like a *remote* scenario." He shrugs.
"But now you've got what you came for, so I suppose we'll have to see this business through."
"I certainly understand the impulse, but this is our job, detective. Our whole *raison d'être*. At some point, we'll need to return to it."
"I think I just need a break from our main case for a bit."
"To be perfectly frank, I have my reservations about this whole antenna scheme. But who knows? We may yet be surprised."
"I'm more interested in *why* you're so fixated on this idea in the first place."
"But here's the thing, detective. *We're* the proper channels. Doing our work, right here on the ground, is how we'll solve this case. There's no need to bring the Coalition into this."
"We can't assign *la responsabilité* if we don't go through the proper channels."
"Let me make a prediction, detective. You are not going to see the inside of a Coalition warship anytime soon."
There! In that container you moved. There's *something* rich in there. We've got to get inside.
But I already tried to convince it to open for me and failed.
What do you suggest?
Then it's time to show you how a *master* does it. No lock survives a round with Savvy. Get me up close.
Opening the door? C'mon, I shouldn't have to tell you that. Get me up close and I'll show you how it's done.
Psst, hear that?
Hear what?
I don't hear anything.
The ominous hum of a preposterously affluent individual... It seems to be coming from above us.
Hold up a minute... why should a preposterously affluent individual be hiding themselves in a container?
(Look up.)
I don't see anyone. Are you sure?
Yes, I'm sure. *Someone* here has assets stacked away in OFCs. Look up.
Wait, OFCs?
See that massive container there, held up by that humongous crane? That's it! We need to get that box of treasures down. Try using that control panel over there.
You hear dock water quietly lapping against seaweed-slimed concrete, but definitely no ominous hums.
OFCs or Offshore Financial Centres -- that's another word for tax havens. EPIS has adopted the OFFNET approach into their frameworks for addressing OFCs, but it's still a problem.
Let's slow down here. Why would we search for rich people in containers?
Wait, you mean tax havens?
Tax havens, OFCs, Sinks, Conduits, *heavens*... Get with the terms, hustler-boy. Now look up!
No problemo, boss-man. On my way to lower that crane... [Leave.]
*Slow down*? We don't have time to slow down -- it's *crunch time*! Get your ass moving and control that crane! We've got sales to make.
Great *work* ethic, friend. No one should be scared to get their hands dirty on the road to brilliant *success*.
Yes, but...
No 'buts', I want to see your *can-do* attitude shine this time. Get moving!
You mean the rain?
Everything gets so quiet when it snows.
No, not the rain -- the ominous hum of a *preposterously affluent individual*... It seems to be coming from above us.
No, not the snow -- the ominous hum of a *preposterously affluent individual*... It seems to be coming from above us.
Here we are. Whoever is in there definitely has money, so let's convince them to part with it for our *exclusive* piece of art.
All around you, rain falls on the great city of Revachol. Rain drips from the eaves and floods the gutters, washing the filth away.
What am I doing?
Shake the shivers off. [Discard thought.]
The spring thaw must be here. The snow is melting...
Looking up at the sky, cold water dripping from your hair.
What do I see?
Grey sky like great battleships, clouds colliding with one another. Rain falls down on the world.
How does it feel?
Your shirt sticks to your chest. The shoulders of your disco blazer grow heavy. The cold finds its way in under your skin. You shiver, and the city shivers with you.
You're not dressed for this weather. You should get an overcoat, or a patrol cloak.
What's in the north?
What's in the east?
What's in the south?
What is in the west?
There's a Frittte on the corner. A plastic coat is folded into a small triangle under the counter by the window. Beyond that, the strikebreakers have gathered.
The great gates of the industrial harbour are locked. A chill runs down your back. You shudder like an animal trying to shake water from its hide.
Clench your teeth to stop shuddering.
Shake your shoulders again.
You shudder, looking down at your feet. Dirty rainwater runs veins into the plaza snow.
What's below?

Behind the gates -- heaps of supply crates. Red and blue metal shipping containers slick with rain. The Greater Revachol Industrial Harbour is an artificial mountain range. Immense wealth resides within, and immeasurable poverty in its shadow.
And beyond that?
And before that?
You -- on the Martinaise plaza. A small dot looking up at the sky. Droplets form on your eyelashes.
La Drisienne, King Dris's Passenger Harbour. Cruise ships flanked by dock arms. Cranes watching over the mouth of the river distributary.
What is across the distributary?
Couron, the lower middle class. Distributary after distributary cuts the city blocks in half. Seven-story buildings trail off into the rain.
A silvery curtain of rain over the houses. The class divide.
What is beyond the Couron?
You have never been there. They don't need the law east of the river.
Sheets of rain over the water. A flight of stairs leading into the ocean. Wave after wave washing the coast of Martinaise, with its motorboats and gently swaying reeds.
Capeside apartments -- tower blocks crowd one another, 4.46 mm bullets still lodged in their war-torn stone walls.
Will you ever go there?
What's above?

A traffic jam. Rain thrumming on the roofs of motor vehicles. Inside, drivers watch water streaming down their windshields. The statue of a king shudders, he too is cold. The canal bridge has been raised.
What's on the other side?

The road ascends; a raised motorway loops above the ghetto. Beneath its concrete columns -- a sea of rooftops, woodwork, and tar stretches northward. Four-story buildings as far as the rain can fall. The snows melt in Jamrock.
"Motherfucker." [Finish thought.]
These spring thaw will not last. The winter will return to Revachol.
What is Jamrock?

Collapsed storm drains. Old sewage systems flooded with rainwater. Hidden weapon caches from the Revolution. Doors leading down to Le Royaume -- the catacombs to which, for three centuries, they delivered the blue-blooded dead.
The skyscrapers of La Delta, the financial district. Faint golden light seeps from the office windows.
Who are you, ghosts?
What is down the shore?
Run your fingers through your dampened hair.
Coal City, end of all lines.
And beyond that?

Urban coastline, rain dripping off eternite-covered roofs. Cinder blocks left over from half-finished construction. A defunct research and development building once seized by revolutionaries. An old wooden church stands on stilts above the water.
Your hair is an oily mess flecked with ash from neighbouring coal plants. Smoke stacks rise somewhere in the distance.
Will I?
Let go of the feeling.
No. You are just one of the hundreds of thousands who watch them rise across the bay from Martinaise every day.
Your hair sticks to your forehead, cold and wet.
Revachol is the capital of the world. Jamrock is the capital of Revachol. Droplets form on your eyelashes.
It's home.
And closer to here?
A yard. Rain falls onto the roof of a woodshed. Coal leaks into a puddle beneath a dead man's feet. He swings from a tree, bloated. Droplets of rain slip from his cold cheeks.
You realize you still have only one shoe. Nearby, on the balcony of the Whirling-in-Rags hostel-cafeteria, a single crocodile-skin shoe now fills with rainwater.
Two green snakeskin shoes stand at attention on the mosaic paving of the plaza.
You realize you have no shoes on. Your feet are red with cold.

dialoguetext: From the corner of his eye, the lieutenant gives your feet a worried glance. Rain drips from his glasses.
"It's cool. I'm in control."
"I should probably do something about this."
Say nothing.
The rain falls.
The lieutenant nods, then looks east.
The lieutenant nods, then looks east.

Look up.
Why am I not there?
What am I doing here?
Where do I live?
To be in Martinaise, where no one goes. At the run-off point of a long-forgotten canal, in the whitest part of town. In the shadow of the day the Revolution failed.

On a street there that flows like a muddy river in the snow, with fire traps rising on either side. A film rental opens its doors to the rain, an armoured motor carriage rushes past the corner where you used to walk together... Suddenly, the hair on your back rises.
YOU CANNOT RETURN.
Standing in the rain, looking north, where Jamrock Rock City stretches inland.
Where the hood, where the hood, where the hood at?
HAVE A BROTHER IN THE CUT. WHERE THE WOOD AT?
Shudder, look further...
In the rain-swept distance above the rooftops of Jamrock, a re-purposed silk mill stands perched above the motorway exit. Precinct 41 hunches in the rain.
Satellite-Officer Jean Vicquemare rushes down the Precinct stairs, umbrella in hand. It's unopened. He doesn't seem pleased about the spring rain.
On the bridge, Officers Torson and McLaine are standing guard. Torson wears jeans and a fishnet wifebeater. Satellite-Officer Vicquemare passes by, and the young man remarks to him...
"Where's your homo, homey?"
"What?"
"It's not like that. They're what you call *hetero-sexual life partners*. They have a battle-tested relationship. A 'bröderbund', if you will."
"Huh? Yeah." He opens his umbrella, but the wind immediately turns it inside out.
"Hetero -- sexual. Life -- partners."
"Funny apery." Vicquemare struggles with his umbrella, the ribs are protruding from its canopy. "Male-centric workplace humour. Have you seen him?"
"Is there something wrong?"
"No, nothing. It's just... Judit went to his place and found the Monday mail unopened. I think he's still *there*. You didn't, like, drink with him over the weekend did you?"
It's the only home you have now. But you can't go back. Not like this.
"That would be *irresponsible*."
"In Martinaise. He's in Martinaise."
"With that animal? Never again, man. What, is he still down there, in... you know, south of the interchange? The... what was it?"
Your vision blurs. You wipe your face with your hand. The rain stings your eyes, making you look up and blink.
Coalition aerostatics hang like apparitions under the cloud cover. Way up there -- where rain forms -- rotors flutter silently. Your sight clears.
"This rain will not let up any time soon. You should get a raincoat. There's a Frittte to the east. They sell them there."
The ruins of a half-sunken seafort crumble on an inlet. Beyond the Bay of Revachol, ghosts rise into the sky.
Hallways collapsed from the mortar hits of a war that was lost long ago. Clotheslines go to waste in the rain. Radios play.
Your shirt sticks to your chest. The shoulders of your jacket grow heavy. The cold finds its way under your skin. You shiver, and the city shivers with you.

dialoguetext: "Not much. I don't have a *fresh perspective* on it. Shall we go?"
They look pretty ancient...
Probably not. [Discard thought.]
Is it? Is there a ringing? (Listen more closely.)
There seems to be. An *extremely* high pitched ring. Ultrasonic. Lena said it was very high-pitched, right? It's like something *tickles* your ear.
Lena also said that it couldn't be heard by any other animal -- including humans. What you're hearing must just be a regular bird.
But you're not a regular animal. You're not even a regular cop. You see -- and hear! -- beyond the veil.

Honestly, your ear isn't hearing a whole lot. The distant hum of the industrial harbour. The traffic. But, admittedly -- there *is* a high pitched noise somewhere there too. But then, isn't there always...
Listen closely first.
There it is again! You are about to re-discover a long-lost species!
Keep listening.
It must be very close... maybe, just maybe it will come toward you...
Yeah, but how are you going to catch it?
Keep still! It might perch on your shoulder.
Hold very still and hope the bird comes to perch on your shoulder. (Proceed.)
Move your head toward the sound. (Proceed.)
Oh no! The sound -- it's moving away, somewhere over there -- go after it!
No... Too late. It's gone... There is no ringing anymore. Just the sound of the streets.
What are you doing? You're a police officer, not a pansy ornithologist. The only birds you should be looking for are healthy women of child-bearing age.
Keep your ears peeled, then. If the species really has migrated to Martinaise, you're sure to hear it again.
No, come back, please! (Listen more.)
Remember that asshole Roy who wanted you to take me off? He didn't like music, only sounds. What a loser. It's good you're not like him. You and disco will be together forever.
Don't be a weirdo like that Roy at the pawnshop who doesn't like music. You don't need *sounds* when you have beats.
That pawnbroker -- Roy -- was into natural sounds too. Maybe you could talk to him.
Was that -- could it be -- the Col Do Ma Ma Daqua?! No. It's probably just your *imagination* ringing in your ear...
"Wait, Kim, do *you* hear a high pitched noise?"
"No. I don't hear the Col Do Ma Ma Daqua -- and neither do you."
Of course he doesn't. He's DEAF.
Go then, leave! Leave like everything else! (Don't.)
So it does. It's gone. All that's left for you -- is the disco.
This "Poste L'Aventurier" mail collection box has been heavily vandalized with graffito. A closer inspection reveals two bullet holes in the front.
"Good mail delivery box." (Pat the box.)

The box seems happy.

"Eat shit, pig!", "FUCKED BY THE CUNN" and "Saint-G" with a crown have been scribbled on it. "Jennie is a WHORE" and "*Baise cette* mailbox!" also.

And then suddenly you see it: over all the other graffitos someone has -- using the tip of a very sharp knife -- cut the words: REVACHOL FOREVER.
The mail collection box has no faith in your psychopathic manipulations.

He does not actually think it's cool. If anything, the lieutenant feels sorry for the poor box -- he's leaning in to inspect the layers of graffito that deface it.

(Rub your toe.) "You think so? You think it was cool?"
Say nothing. [Leave.]
The lieutenant pats the box on the head, ever so slightly, before walking away.
"I don't. Let's go."
The lieutenant pats the box, ever so slightly.

He must see the box as the weaker of the two, and you as a bully -- something he doesn't stand for.
A faint sticker on the side reads: "RCM Emergencies Desk no 8-100-2", with a slogan: "Mankind, be vigilant!"

Drop the white envelope into the mailbox.

Your toe has suffered damage. It hurts!
Drop the white envelope into the mailbox.

The dented yellow mailbox greets you with it's graffito and bullet holes in the front.

"I knew we'd get to use this mailbox -- for something."
Other than developing a personal relationship? Looks like you were right.

Other than kicking? You were right!

"Cool. And what are you doing here?"

dialoguetext: "Hello again, officer. How are things?"
"Oh?" She cranes her neck. "Well, I didn't write it there. I'm just sitting here."
"Of course. Where to?"
"Where am I?"
"In Martinaise, sir. In the city of Revachol..." She looks around, thinking what else to say. "This intersection is called Roundabout North."
"What is in the East?"
"Thanks, that's all for now."
"No problem." She nods, brushing a fleck of soil off her cheek.
"The harbour gates. Some kind of commotion, I think? I don't follow the local politics." She shrugs. "A Frittte store too."
"What is in the South?"
"What is in the West?"
"Some shops and a bridge. The canal bridge leads to the coast, but it's broken, I think? Some kind of accident probably."
"What is up in the North?"
"There's the pier, the Capeside apartment buildings. Some more tenements... Not a lot, really."
"It's just water..." She looks at the water, squinting. "No, actually, I think they call it the Martinaise Inlet. There are some islands in the bay, but they're hard to reach."
"What is on the other side of the canal?"
"Just coast. There's a little fishing village there... and a fish market. But that got closed down ages ago."
"Do you know where I could find the representative for Wild Pines?"

dialoguetext: "Wild Pines? You mean the company woman?"
"Tell me, what exactly have you been doing in your greenhouse -- in *March*?"
"It was clear just an hour ago..."
"It felt like springtime just a few days ago..."
She realizes she's about to criticize your work -- or lack thereof.
There's discomfort. She stops mid sentence.
"Go on, it's okay."
"There's a corpse there, keeping you from doing your work."
"Yes." She looks relieved. "It smells pretty bad, so I have to take breaks."
"As you *probably* know, there's a corpse hanging from a tree there. It smells pretty bad. So I have to take breaks."
"But?"
"Well... as you *probably* know, there's a corpse hanging from a tree there. It smells pretty bad. So I have to take breaks."
"Don't worry, miss. We're here to clean it up -- you can get to work soon."
She's black.
"You're black."
*Should* I say that?
So what? I'm also black.
Uhm... are you sure? In the mirror it looked like you were pink, grey and more than a little reddish.
What if I told you there's a *mirror* on your bathroom wall, upstairs? You *may* want to take a look.
You *really* need to take a look at that mirror upstairs.
I don't know -- what's the problem? You're just *reacting to stimuli*.
"What do you mean?"
"So, what kind of music do you listen to nowadays?"
"Nothing."
"I don't know..." She looks around. "Whatever's on the radio?"
"We should probably proceed with our business in Martinaise." The lieutenant interrupts her, turning to you. "Unless you didn't have any more *official* questions?"
"We should proceed with our business in Martinaise." The lieutenant turns to you.
She doesn't like that *giant* boat. Nor does she like the woman on it.
"Yes. A representative of the harbour. She should have set up operations nearby."
"Oh, that must be the woman on the giant boat." She points northwest. "There's one docked on the pier. It arrived a couple of weeks ago. It's very hard to miss."
"Yes. That's the one."
"You don't like the boat?"
Let it go.
"I'm okay with it. Was there something else?"
She would probably prefer not to go into it. It wasn't easy to pick up on either...
Rows of stalls under a broad roof, where silvery fish were heaped on newspapers. Water, water everywhere -- pouring from the heavens, in the shadow of the old church.
"What kind of a fish market is this?"
"I don't know... the abandoned kind? It used to gather every spring, but there's nothing to do there now. Just drug addicts."
Shake it off, you seem to be under some kind of cold spell...
"Anything else?" The girl watches you rub your sides for warmth.
She hides it well, but behind the sweat and dirt there is something... else. In her rigid posture.
"There's more to you than that."
"Is there?"
The quickness of the reply certainly does not prove you wrong.
Nothing to see here. Just a regular law official reacting to every day stimuli. Nothing noteworthy here.
"Working on what?"
"I have a greenhouse in the yard there." She gestures over her shoulder. "I've been trying to get some work done..."
"It's there." She points north. "In the yard, right through the hole in the fence."
She's relieved someone has come for it -- finally.
"You sound surprised."
"I have some questions for you."
"We don't see a lot of police around here, that's all."
"Of course. What can I help you with?"
"Later." [Leave.]
"You're back."
"Do you listen to disco?"
She seems more perplexed than threatened.
"Okay."
"Uh... I'm gonna say no."
"Sure thing." She narrows her eyes.
"Okay."
"What do you mean?"
"I'm... disorientated. I don't know where I am."
"Just tell me where we are, okay?"
"We're in Martinaise, sir." She looks around. "This intersection is called... Roundabout North, I think."
"He knows where we are. He just wants directions." The lieutenant seems uncomfortable with the level of disorientation you are displaying.
"Yes. What are you doing here?"
"Maybe." (Nod.) "Pleased to meet you, Just A Gardener. I have another question."
Those gloves would really come in handy for the autopsy.
She's not okay with it. It's a display of power and she feels threatened by it. You don't know why.
You didn't say she wrote it, you asked what it was doing there.
"I didn't say you wrote it."
"Sir, it was *implied* in your question."
The timidness is gone for a second. Something else takes it's place. A readiness.
"Okay, well, I didn't," she leans back, shoulders relaxing.
She's probably not gonna do it.
Salts? Ammonium salts? Perhaps useful for later.
"Go easy on that stuff. It gave me a terrible headache."
"Sure -- I'm done with them." She takes a small capsule out of her breast pocket and hands it to you.
Absolutely gone.
"Can you tell me when you've taken him away then. Because I'm sort of waiting for *that*."
Yeah, keep her in the *loop*. It's strangely enjoyable to report back on the minute progress you've made. Even to strangers.
No! Do *not* keep this random civilian in any loops.
No! Do *not* report back to this random civilian about anything.
"It was sent to processing in the morgue."
"I'm glad to hear that." A quick smile. "Thank you, officer. Looks like I'll get mint in the ground by April."
You get a strange feeling, looking at that smile. It spoils the moment. It is disingenuous.
What's going on here?
Surely it was nothing, sire. Just paranoia.
I don't care, I just wanna enjoy the nice moment.
Of course, sire, of course.
"Well uh..." She points to her wheelbarrow, surprised at the question. "This might be the last snow we get. At least I hope so..."
"Snow has nutrients in it -- helps everything green up in the spring. At least that's what my grandma always told me." She smiles shyly.
Yes, think about the cute grandma, not the weird snow.
"The grandma is a bit too much."
"A bit much? What are you talking about? That's what my grandma told me, okay?"
She feels interrogated now. It's hard to say if she's lying.
"Relax, miss. This is not an interrogation. We are just checking some facts."
Squint your eyes and look at her intently.
Stop looking at her, look around! What do you see?
All you can see is the fact that her skin is a different colour from yours. That's literally all. You're gonna have to run with that.
"Okay then. Snow it is."
"Mhmh." She looks at her wheelbarrow, where the snow is slowly melting.
"What nutrients?"
"Nitrogen and sulphur mostly." She points to the sky. "And whatever factories and aerostatics exhale too I guess."
The traffic jam?
"You're black."
Why am I thinking this, I said I'm black as fuck.
Are you entirely sure you're black as *fuck*? You should really check out that mirror thing. For now, go with she's black. It's important to the case.
No, you don't. Just back up, cancel this.
Yeah, I'm not gonna say that.
Better to get off before it starts. Nothing left to gain here.
"Ask me a normal question or leave me alone."
An entrance to the yard?
The plaza?
That's right. And the canal, the bookstore, the harbour gates... This is a great vantage point -- for keeping an eye on *you*.
"Are you by any chance keeping an eye on us?"
Noted, but I'll keep it to myself.
"No, of course not! I don't understand what this is about..." She looks towards the yard and her expression clears.
"The kid did this, right? The red-haired rat? Can't say a sentence without *f****t* or *kipt*... He's always giving me trouble."
"I was talking to him, yes."
"That's not important right now."
"Maybe you shouldn't be. I mean... you do your job, but that kid is beyond help. And he certainly won't help *you*." She shakes her head.
"It is, because he sent you to harass me, didn't he? You shouldn't listen to him." She points to the defaced sign above her on the corner. "It was probably him, who wrote that."
"It is, because he sent you to harass me. He's playing you." She shakes her head. "He hates the police, okay? A lot of people do around here."
"You've been resting here for quite a *while*, haven't you?" The lieutenant intervenes, looking at her intently.
"Yes. I'm tired."
"I understand -- the RCM isn't welcome here and the locals want to keep an eye on us."
There's silence. The smallest of smiles.
"That's okay, miss -- do what you have to do." The lieutenant nods at you. "I think we're done here. Let's go."
Glad to have been of service. Now you know -- the locals are keeping tabs on you.
"Yes, I'm black, how many times are you gonna say that?"
"That was the last time, miss." He looks at you with a stern expression. "Our questioning here is concluded. Let's go."
He didn't think you were about to bust a case.
"What does that mean?" She doesn't flinch.
"Okay."
"So, what kind of music do you listen to nowadays?"
"We should proceed with our business in Martinaise." The lieutenant turns to you.
"Nothing."
"Okay."
"I don't know..." She looks around. "Whatever's on the radio I guess. What does this have to do with snow, or gardening in March?"
"We should probably proceed with our business in Martinaise." The lieutenant interrupts her, turning to you. "Unless you didn't have any more *official* questions?"
"Uh... I'm gonna say no."
"Do you listen to disco?"
She seems more perplexed than cornered.
"Sure thing." She narrows her eyes.
"If you don't have anything normal to say I had something I needed to think about."
"Nothing, this is just something my brain told me."
"Okay."
What are you waiting for, ask about the disco already. You need some fresh jams to get out of this rut.
Ask her about music -- it'll get the convo flowing, don't worry!
Her gloves -- you get the feeling that you need them. You have a dead body to deal with, after all.
Psst! Her gloves -- they'll help you with the autopsy.
No. I don't want to say that.
Okay. The stimuli end.
She has changed the subject and won't let you get back to this.
In the West is the miracle...
"Thank you." [Leave]
"It's so late and you're still here."
"I'm a night hawk, what can I say?" She flashes a smile.
Odd...
There's a little meanness in that smile.
She's still here, because you're still here.
"You don't have to stay up because of us."
"I like the city at night. Don't you?" She looks into the darkness and smiles again.
She's uncomfortable. Maybe you should drop this line of questioning.
"Evrart confirmed, he sent you to spy on us."
"Is that so?" Her face remains expressionless as she shrugs. "I don't know anything about that. Must be a misunderstanding."
She's a pro. Nothing short of coming face to face with the fatman himself would make her admit it right now.
The place looks the part. There's graffito everywhere and the traffic jam behind you is completely *unregulated*.
Even all the way over here, there's a drop of death in the spring air.
Pier? Buildings? Apartments? You should *explore*, maybe scale a wall?
She's very well composed. Back straight.
Really? *None.* Maybe just a *tiny* bit of annoyance.
"That's one brutal motor carriage," says the young man with 'PISSF****T' written on his back.
"If I were a real SKULL now, I'd jack it, paint it in palm tree livery, then bottom-light it neon-style!" His companion wears a simple yet elegant slogan: 'FUCK THE WORLD'.
"Ahem." He steps in. "While I appreciate the interest you take in my *brutal motor carriage*, I have to stop you right there. The RCM takes threats directed at its property seriously."
"Who are the *SKULLS*?"
"What's with the jackets?"
"Well, talking with you has definitely been something." [Leave.]
"You don't know? What kind of cop are you?"
"A snazzy shit-ripped SKULL-mobile like this would make a fine trophy. We could, like, hang fucking shrunken heads from the side mirrors! Cops' heads... Scary tribal shit."
"Yeah, tribal shit..." he agrees. "A cop-carriage like this would have proper SKULL value..."
"I, uhm, it's just theoretical work, copper. No basis in reality." He turns to his companion: "Man, if we were certified SKULLS right now..."
"No, I really don't."
"Of course I do, I'm just testing you boys."
"Why haven't I seen any SKULLS around Martinaise?"
Say nothing.
"Non-verbal?"
"The SKULLS are the most vicious gang of the Besmertnyé." His voice rings with excitement.
"If a SKULL spots you, he will pull out his dagger and stab you without saying a single word."
"The nastiest bunch of psychos ever! Jacking carriages and getting into high-speed chases."
"They usually occupy the Burnt-Out Quarter in Jamrock. Or you can find them loitering around their brightly-painted, bottom-lighted vehicles."
"Possessing an infinite amount of fuck-all swagger, infamous for their non-verbal *modus operandi*."
"Oh, I can't wait to become a SKULL. Bottom-lights are *wretched* aggressive."
"Well," the young man remarks in a voice filled with longing, eyes glazed over, "there's Cindy..."
The lieutenant's voice is as calm as usual -- a testament to the violence and death he's witnessed through the sight of his firearm.
"Yeah. Cindy the SKULL!" He lights up. "A true artist of the future, just like Arno van Eyck or Rietveldt."
"Your rhetoric is confusing. Are you a part of the SKULLS or not?"
"Who's van Eyck?"

dialoguetext: "Oh, man, yeah!" he exclaims, then stops himself, processing the rest of your question. "We're not fucking kids, man!"
"Old man, it doesn't matter. You'll be long gone before his greatness is recognized."
A young woman kneels on a sheet of ice as if looking for something lost ages ago. She bends until her right ear touches the frozen water. She listens to it crack, slowly.
"The Union does their share of policing in Martinaise, at least where gangs are concerned," the lieutenant replies instead. "That's why there isn't much organized crime around here."
"What about them?"
"Be wary of the abyss," his blond friend adds ominously and points to his temple.
"Enough about this *skullery* then." (Conclude.)
"We're not *franchised* SKULLS -- well, not yet. Once we get our name out there, we'll have a chance to join them."
"I see."
"And what makes you think that the organization would accept you?"
"Oh, you'll see for sure once we're in -- it's the last thing you'll ever see before the void consumes you."
"Because we can be just as psycho and vicious. You'll see."
"Uh..." He looks confused. "Well... yeah I mean, we're only saying *practice* things for now, so... We don't mean no harm to the SKULLS brand. Or to you."
"This is definitely something the SKULLS would say, but we're not trying to encroach on the SKULLS brand in any way. On the contrary, we're just here to market it."
"Hold on, why does a criminal gang need marketing?"
"We think of it more like two franchises merging, you know -- us two and the SKULLS. I really feel like we would add more to the table."
Ask for the jackets for yourself and the lieutenant.
"By the way, if you see Cindy, give her our regards," he adds, returning from whatever void he was just visiting.
(Turn to the blond youth.) "Why does your jacket have 'PISSF****T' written on it?"
(Turn to the dark-haired youth.) "Why do you have 'FUCK THE WORLD' written on your jacket?"
Is it a *coincidence* that here we have two bad-ass jackets and two bad-ass cops?
"Spice things up here in Martinaise, you know. Get the old machine of pain and suffering oiled up real good."
"Okay, I get what the SKULLS do, but what do you franchise in? Youth unemployment?"
"Doesn't it already have enough spice?"
"Whatever, man. Work is for pussies." The young man frowns, aggrieved. "You wouldn't get it anyway."
"So you're just *pretending* to be as nasty and vicious as the SKULLS?"
"Hey, we can be just as hard! Like pavement on top of pavement, or a brick on top of another brick."
"Do you know anything about the murder that took place here?" (Point to the yard.)
"Yeah, sure, we'll gladly tell you everything we know about it." He clears his throat. "It was a man."

"I can answer that. Many men keep searching for *the one*. For so-called true love, which is actually just obsession masquerading as kinship. The thrill of the chase, the hollowness that fills your chest cavity after catching it."
"So, you're saying I'm an old man?!"
"Yeah -- the skull symbolizes the embrace of death and nothingness, present in all of us, the vehicle of our future operations. Death and nothingness."
"They're called SKULLS because when you're shot dead in the middle of the street, the skull is the only part the stray dogs won't eat."
Just trust me and follow my lead.
"Kim, maybe you shouldn't scare them like that?"
"So, boys, wanna feed the dogs?"
"And do what? Walk away, knowing that there are two delusional hoodlums interested in joining a criminal group whose main areas of expertise are jacking cars and killing police officers?"
"Well..."
"Don't *well* me. This might be fine by you but it certainly isn't fine by me. We've got to try to nip this kind of behaviour in the bud."
The young men stare at the two of you in confusion.
"Or a grave on top of a grave."
"Also, he was hanged."
"Anything else?"
"Don't fuck around. I am the law."
"He was hanged from a tree."
"Well, first off, it's a statement and not *necessarily* something that characterizes me as a person, even though the statement has character. And I *do* like piss..."
The youth looks confused for a moment. "There can always be more. In the end it won't matter. 'Til then..."

"The word PISSF****T epitomizes the struggle taking place in the world, things being defined as they seem, not as they are. And -- I guess -- it's also about communal spirit, the future, and *truly* appreciating our differences."

"Also, you've got to admit, it catches the eye. And since the grand piper is slowly but steadily moving towards basing the economy on it -- attention -- it is imperative that the medium itself convey the message."
"What I mean by this is -- we are *all* Pissf****ts. And that the world is inherently meaningless."
"Actually -- forget about it."
"To catch a fish you need to hurl the lure many times, and even then it isn't certain that you'll get anything. If you blow up the lake, though..."
"...you get more fish in a shorter time. And, for time is of the essence and fleeting ever so quickly, one must think of a way to fuck the whole world -- and not get caught up in fucking some *one*."
I'm wondering if the poetics come with the jacket or are they derived from something else entirely?
"Hey, Kim..." (Lower your voice.)
"Yes?"
"Do you think it's a coincidence?"
"What do you think about their jackets?"
"What is?"
"Leather jackets adorned with immature writing? The 'ideology' they convey helps the boys justify poor choices in life and fashion." The lieutenant shrugs. "I'm not a fan."
"There are two of us and two of these jackets..."
"What are you implying?" The lieutenant looks confused.
"Why are you always so patronizing when cool *possibilities* cross our path?"
"Which one would *you* wear?"
"You know what I'm implying."
"I'm not sure I understand you, detective."
"Are you more of a 'PISSF****T' or a 'FUCK THE WORLD' kind of guy?"
"No, I don't. What are you implying?"
"We should get these jackets."
"Fine, if only to end this discussion: Theoretically, if I were a juvenile delinquent -- if I were to already be down that path -- I think 'PISSF****T' is the stronger of the two statements."
"For what?"
"What do people do with jackets? They wear them."
"The concept of getting dressed *is* familiar to me, but wearing jackets like these isn't appropriate for an RCM officer. Unless he's *deep* undercover," he adds.
"But in theory, Kim, if we were to confiscate these jackets, which one would *you* wear?"
No, no, no! Don't *ask* anything. Be subtle and scary. The boys dream about being SKULLS... use that!
These guys aren't scary, *you're* not scary -- I have nothing to work with here. It's either begging or bullying. Or both. Just ask them maybe?
"Gentlemen, I need your jackets."
"Boys, with *those* jackets, you're gonna be the SKULL-kings in no time!"
"What... no!" He quickly looks around. "SKULLS don't have kings," he pauses. "I think, and we're not even *in* yet..."
(Raise your voice.) "Not even prospects and already aspiring to be kings?"
"Uh... why?"
"Neither."
"C'mon Kim, it's just a mental exercise!"
(Point at your clothes.) "Look at the shit I'm wearing!"
"I need them for official police business."
"I'm not wearing that jacket."
"I don't think this case requires us to go undercover. Or raise hell...  In fact I don't think the jacket will be useful at all."
"Why not? You could really raise hell. Go undercover. Hard."
"I already *am* expressing my individuality."
"But don't you want to express your individuality?"
"Still. It's good to know that we have it, should the need arise."
"The need will not arise."

"Look at this cute shit!" The dark haired youth points at you -- then turns to his friend. "How can we become SKULLS if you go around fraternising with cops?! Let's get the fuck out of here before anyone sees us."
"Fuck, I'm sorry, man." He hangs his head in shame. "I just... don't like confrontations that's all."
"And what kind of business is that exactly?"
"Yeah, like you said, total shit. What about it?" There's a spark of sympathy in the youth's eyes.
"I'm wearing horrible clothes to catch horrible people. It's depressing."
The lieutenant looks down at his bomber jacket and shrugs, obviously content with *his* uniform.
"*Police* business."
The lieutenant notices your agitation and opens his mouth to speak, but then decides against it and merely shakes his head.
"That ride is fucking lightning!" the young man exclaims.
"Hey, Pissf****t, look who it is! Shrunken cop head material!"
"Why?"
"Probably because of how *non-verbal* their mode of operation is going to be," the lieutenant answers for the two rebels. "It's a threat."
"Yep." He nods enthusiastically. "Old as fuck."
"Which is not to say that the SKULLS are bitches and f****ts. On the contrary..."
"Who are you?"
"I can tell you who we're not, cop. We're *not* snitches, f****ts, or SKULLS."
"We don't have time for this. Let's go." [Leave.]
"Murder?"
"A man was hanged in the backyard of the Whirling-in-Rags."
"Never mind, this is useless."
"The palm tree livery should be, like, pastel green. Fucking tropic shit..." He gazes dreamily at Lieutenant Kitsuragi's motor carriage.
"I can see it, bright as day. Oh, if we were SKULLS right now..."
"The part of this presentation you wanna take home with you, cop-man, is: We're not part of the SKULLS. Yet."
"Hey, Pissf****t, look who it is! It's the bully. He ran out of people to be an asshole to."
Was it a good idea on the lieutenant's part to get into this? Don't even answer that, just leave. You can always come back later -- on your own terms.
The lieutenant sighs. "No, they really, really aren't. It's porno-tuning. Say no to the porno."
Apart from the Union themselves of course.
That much is true.
No reply. The blond rebel scratches his chin, deliberately not focusing his gaze on anything. He looks very uncomfortable.
"Yeah, but... fuck the police."
"When you put it that way..." (Turn to the two young men and tap a finger against your head.) "Dog food!"
The lieutenant sighs. "I... appreciate the effort."

"No. You don't get to say that." His voice is sharp as a blade. "Police officers put their lives on the line to protect the people of Revachol, while punks like these joke about joining a cop-killer clan."
A young woman kneels on wooden planks, still looking for something lost ages ago. She's nodding her head along to the signal coming in through her headphones.
"Hey, I'm *only* 42!"
"Holy shit, that's even older than I thought!" He bursts out laughing.
"You're fucking ancient, man."
"Mhm." He throws a longing glance at the Kineema.
"Are you sure a SKULL would say that?"
These kids have the vocabulary but might be missing a brain.
"Yeah, I mean... duh."
"These punks don't know anything. Let's just move along."
"That works, I feel more like a 'FUCK THE WORLD' kind of a guy."
"Seems about right," the lieutenant remarks. "Especially considering your... heroic exit attempts."
"No way! If anything, I'm the *PISSF****T* in this scenario."

It's perfect -- big, with a powerful cooling system. Now if you could just get the lieutenant to help you with the body...
It's perfect -- big, with a powerful cooling system. Now if you could just plug in the fridge and get the lieutenant to help you...
"Of course. I'll take the head, you take the feet..."
"Alright, time to freeze the body!"
"Hold on..." The lieutenant inspects the dark interior of the refrigerator. "There's no use if the fridge isn't working. Let's plug it in first and then return here to move the body."
"Of course. I'll take the head, you take the feet..."
Try to remove the dead man's boots again.

dialoguetext: This must be the giant ice bear fridge that Soona mentioned. Look inside.
"So what do you think of this fridge, Kim? It looks big enough for *two* corpses."
Hm, the fridge looks big enough for the corpse...
This must be the fridge you were told about. Look inside, see if it's big enough for the corpse.
"Beautiful," he says, wiping his hands in his handkerchief. "A dead body in an ice bear fridge -- this is some of the best police work I've ever done."
"Really? You think it's good work?"
"I'm not sure I believe you."
"No. Not really. Look at that! What have we done? We stuffed a *dead body in an ice bear fridge*. This story does not leave this room."
"Of course you don't. Look at that! What have we *done?* We stuffed a dead body in an ice bear fridge. This does *not* leave this room."
"I think this is a glorious achievement and people need to hear about it."
"As impressive as the fridge is, this is a *small* victory. Among numerous defeats."
"We did our best with the means at our disposal."
"Yeah, I'm not *proud* either, but we did find a fridge."
"This isn't police work, Kim. It's *art*. We're *artists* and this was our vision."
"At least we've stopped the body from decomposing further. Now you can conduct another inspection. Under controlled *circumstances*."
"If I were an artist, this would certainly *not* be my vision. I would be much, much more conservative in my work..."
"Did we, though?" He sighs. "Okay, maybe we *did*"
"At least we've stopped the body from decomposing further -- or will have, once you plug the fridge back in. Then you can conduct one more inspection."
"No. They do *not* -- they *need* to hear about our uneventful, boring, downright *conservative* murder investigation."
He means it. He doesn't want to be the Ice Bear Cop.
"Bag him. Take him away, Kim." (Let the lieutenant take the body away without further examination.)

dialoguetext: Shoot, Loonie Roonie!
Tell me something, dead man.
"Tell me, who are you, dead man?"
"Of course. A giant, ice bear shaped fridge..." He relaxes his hand, his face bathed in the harsh light of the open fridge door.
"Let's take a look inside."
... but the optics on this are awful, he thinks. We need to be as silent as we can.
Your visual confirms: you could fit *two* more bodies in the ice bear fridge.
The two of you? Easily.
You've *definitely* earned a drink after this. Perhaps even some *pagan rites*.
You have created an *ice bear sarcophagus*.
"Yes. We need to celebrate by performing pagan rites. Let's bring out the mead and set it on fire."
"Behold! We have created an *ice bear sarcophagus*."
He nods gravely. "Talk of the *ice bear sarcophagus* must *not* leave this room."
"I *knew* you would say that! I *knew* this would lead to drinking..." He shakes his head vigorously. "No. No more. This is *paganistic* enough -- and it does *not* leave this room."
Inside the icy realm of the ice bear fridge, the corpse stands slumped, waiting...
A friendly cartoon bear smiles back at you from a glossy cellophane wrapper. It looks nothing like the fridge -- or the decomposing body in it.
The paper still smells of vanilla and chocolate. Even under this stench you can feel it.
Shake from the sudden cold sensation.
The fridge buzzes with energy. The electricity bill on this thing must be *catastrophic*.
"The electricity bill must be *catastrophic*. On the other hand, it did help us with a certain corpse situation..."
He's right. His work would be much more formal.
... lucky us.
Indeed. Refrigerated meat is much better for coroner's work.
"Okay, Kim. Take him away." (The lieutenant takes the body away -- work alone for the rest of the day.)
The fridge sits empty before you, an overindulgent wardrobe now that the cooling systems aren't active.
You've acquired an interactable item. Investigate this item further by going to the INTERACT tab in your INVENTORY.
A few bricks have fallen off, revealing a compartment behind the wall. It's too dark to see in.
"Where are we?" (Look around the secret room.)
"Look, there's a hole in the wall." (Point at the hidden compartment.)
[Leave.]
So there's a hole in the wall.
Where am I?
"Seems like an old bunker from the Revolutionary period. Look at all those rifles..." He points up, at the rifles under the ceiling. "Must be an old weapons cache."
"There is, yes. And there also appears to be something *inside* the hole... Interesting. Do you want to take a look?"
"Okay, I do..." (Look inside.)
"No, you do the honours." (Back off.)
Your hand reaches deep into darkness and spider webs, rummaging around. You find rusty rifles, hidden away...
"Sure," he nods and steps closer. "Okay, here's some more rifles... None of these seem to be working. And oh..." His hand reaches in, rummaging in the dark...
There is. Inside it's nothing but gloomy blackness. Better not stick your hand inside!
Inside a secret room infested with rats, spiders, and woodlice.
Seems like an old weapons cache from the Revolutionary period.
"An old Belle-Magrave rifle -- that's *rare* to find in such good order. Seems to no longer be functional, but still -- rare. Here..."
"It's yours, officer." He hands you the gun. "You found this place."
Inspect the rifles.
Most of them are rusty and inoperable like the rest, but one catches your eye -- a bolt action model with a fine wood stock. In better cosmetic order than the others.
"Rifles, Kim!"
The lieutenant steps closer, curious: "Are these any good?"
"This one looks nice." (Take the rifle.)
"An old Belle-Magrave, from the Revolution," the lieutenant notes with approval. His eyes are gleaming. "Seems to no longer be functional, but still -- a beautiful thing, in its own way."
Stick your hand inside the hole.
Never mind.

Your hand reaches deep into darkness and spider webs, rummaging around. You find a number of rusty rifles, hidden away... Most of them are ugly and inoperable, but a single rifle catches your eye. It's a bolt-action with a fine wood stock.
An old Belle-Magrave rifle, Revolutionary-era. Prized for its reliability more than it's accuracy. The rest are probably Belle-Magraves too, just too damaged to be identified.
Take the rifle.
Leave it there.
A fit service weapon for a fit officer. Too bad it doesn't work -- it looks like it's been out of order for years.
History is best left where it lies. The rifle doesn't work anyway.
Wait, what, really? You're not going to look inside a secret compartment behind the wall? Okay, officer... *Okay*.
Take it! You're a police officer. Police officers carry guns.
An old Belle-Magrave rifle, Revolutionary-era. Prized for its reliability more than it's accuracy. The rest are probably Belle-Magraves too, just too damaged to be sure.
"What does this mean -- a rifle here?"
This should cheer you up.
"It means there are firearms -- albeit inoperable -- still lying around in Martinaise. It's an interesting coincidence, I would say. Might come in useful in the future."
He likes this find.

"It means there are firearms -- breechloaders -- still lying around in Martinaise. This would have been good in our case against Ruby for Titus. Too late for that now, but still -- might be useful down the road..."
"It means there are firearms -- breechloaders -- still lying around in Martinaise. This could prove useful in our case against Ruby for Titus. Men are easily swayed by the sight of a rifle."
What does this mean -- a rifle here?

It means there are firearms -- albeit inoperable -- still lying around Martinaise. This is an interesting coincidence. Could prove useful in some way. You don't know *how* yet, but it might be useful down the road…

It means there are firearms -- front loaders -- still lying around Martinaise. This would have been good in our case against Ruby for Titus. Too late for that now, but still -- might be useful down the road...
This is a good find. Really justifies coming down here and looking around.
It means there are firearms -- front loaders -- still lying around Martinaise. This could prove useful in our case against Ruby for Titus. Men are easily swayed by the sight of a rifle...
"Isn't that the same gun that fired the fatal bullet?"
"It's the same *type* of weapon, yes -- a breechloader. But it's not the same gun. This one's been out of order for *years...* I'm afraid our search for the real murder weapon must continue."
This is definitely the same make of gun as the one that fired the fatal bullet in the murder case. It's not the murder weapon itself, but still... you should have it, just in case.
"Could the murder weapon we're looking for be similar?"
"It's the same *type* of weapon, yes. A breechloader. An interesting coincidence that we should find something so similar. But I'm afraid our search for the real murder weapon must continue."
"Could the murder weapon we're looking for be similar?"
"For that we would have to take a closer look at the bullet you found, officer. I wouldn't read too much into this, yet -- what we have discovered here is an *inoperable antique*."
"Look, Kim, it's a trap. There are no collars on the barbell."
A barbell lies on the floor. The colour has worn off its weight plates.
There are no collars on the barbell. This is a safety hazard.
You manage to hoist it off the ground, but the barbell feels wobbly and dangerous, your hands slick with sweat. Turns out you're no beast, just an old man with bad form.

dialoguetext: "What kind of a bastard would just remove the collars? It should be a felony."
A warm wave of accomplishment washes over your head, as you drop the barbell to the floor. For a moment it feels like you're strong enough to succeed at anything you ever set your mind to.
Conjuring up an inhuman amount of strength, you raise the barbell up in the air. Your biceps tremble, but you're a savage. This is a children's game!
[Leave.]
Hey, but you're still in a ghost house... What if someone heard this? What if they know you're here?!
See, see! This place is cursed!
"It was never my favourite, either." The lieutenant is obviously handling you.
"At the station gym, I mean. I prefer running. It clears your head..." The lieutenant steps away from the barbell, letting your recover in peace.
"You're right, the weights may fall off. Better not touch it then."
It's 60 kg. Your triceps hum at the sight of these weights. Show the world what kind of beast it's dealing with. Lift them.
Lift the barbell.
Even your body has failed you. It's a miracle you didn't injure yourself.
Maybe it wasn't such a good idea to smash through that back door...
"It would be a violation of EPIS safety regulations if the gym was still operating. But it isn't. No one's supposed to come here anymore."
"Whatever, weightlifting is for the intellectually impaired anyway."
"Seems like I'm a little out of shape. Or maybe my palms were just slippery..."
Say nothing.
"Fuck you, you stupid barbell!"
"Wearing gloves would definitely make it easier," the lieutenant agrees.
"Proper weightlifting gloves would definitely afford a better grip," the lieutenant agrees.
"Weightlifting was never my favourite, either." The lieutenant is obviously *handling* you.
"Actually, I don't really care about safety hazards."
"No one does, until they get smashed under the barbell."
"Oh yeah."
"I'm a true champion!"
(Say nothing, revel in the feeling.)
"Good technique." The lieutenant nods with approval.
The barbell waits patiently on the floor, like a dog for its master.
Why does it feel so familiar?
Is this familiar because I'm a weightlifter?
No, it's not that... It's the stale smell of rubber, the squeaky sound of sneakers, your bruised knee against the mat. And a whistle... then the feeling is gone.
It's just a memory.
A memory from another life -- when you were young and fit.
A warm wave of accomplishment washes over your head, as you drop the barbell to the floor. For a moment it feels like you're strong enough to succeed at anything you ever set your mind to.
This old green chalkboard is covered in scribbles, sketches and schemes like some ancient cave mural.
Inspect the photos.
Inspect the schedule.
Inspect the notes.
Inspect the drawings.
[Leave.]
This is a monthly calendar from the year '50. Cryptic words like 'sprint', 'daily minime', and 'GPI' span the marker-drawn grid -- the grand scheme of production and money.
As time goes on, the numbers in the boxes grow rarer and rarer. The board becomes an empty snowfield in the final days... Only failure and regret dwell in this region.
Keep reading -- what happened?
A note in the bottom left corner of the chalkboard says: "SEE THE PROD. SCHEDULE FILAMENT FOR DETAILS."
Your eyes glide over four sections of the imposing green chalkboard...
The handwriting is only partly legible, but you can still make out three slogans: 'Call in, tune out!', 'WIRRÂL UNTETHERED', and 'Heat death of the Universe'...
Everyone is constantly teetering on the edge of the abyss. An abyss of *production*. These squares look orderly but beneath them is chaos, worry, pain...
It looks a bit like an academic calendar. Only much more *brutal*.
'Minime' stands for a 'mini-meeting'. It's part of a bigger framework for managing work called R.U.N. Station 41 tried to implement it a few years ago, but failed.
These lithe, pointy-eared creatures appear to be different types of *welkins*. You make out autumnal *candle-welkins* casting wax-based magic...
Your flashlight slides over an old green chalkboard covered in scribbles, sketches and schemes like some ancient cave mural.
One of the welkins -- towering among the rest -- appears to be different, however.
The photo collage depicts barren, icy landscapes wrapped in perpetual night. You see permafrost and glacial landforms, dead trees groaning under the snow.
Who are all those creatures? Fantasies of a tortured, feverish mind?
This looks like an *enormous improvement* on the classic Wirrâl setting. Much more *advanced*. Light years ahead.
You should adopt one of those welkins as your *persona*. No longer a mere man -- but a welkin...
The lieutenant can't help but comment: "An inordinate amount of time has gone into drawing these little welkin creatures..."
"Why would anyone spend so much time on this?"
"Who *are* these creatures? Who drew them? Are they *real*? I have so many questions..."
(Whisper) "One of them is a welkin supremacist."
"Some people really *like* building a world, I think. Even if it's just for a game."
"Mhm... political commentary. That one has a great beard too..." The lieutenant nods at the welkin's facial hair.
"This looks like *concept art* for a project. It's not really real."
...and for what? All gone.
If they put this much effort into making welkin cooler, imagine what they did with the dweorg and the humans?
Step back and look at something else.
Entire oceans have been frozen from shore to shore. There are pictures of settlements on dried up riverbeds, abandoned in a storm. Animal corpses in the dark, carcasses and bones.
A pinned postcard reads: 'The heat death scenario -- a desperate fight for geothermal energy engulfs the world as Wirrâl becomes untethered from its sun, drifting through the Universe.'
"Looks like they didn't make it." The lieutenant looks at the frigid ice field of nothingness.
Looks like they didn't make it.

dialoguetext: Some of the writing has faded with age, but you can still make out sections here and there; photos and drawings have been pinned to the board.
The huldur, the dweorg, the humans, and even headless men... all of them. Purged. Imagine a world filled *only* with welkin! Green welkin, dread welkin... and the high welkin to rule them all.
*Translucent welkins* with organs shining under their skin, and even aether welkins -- hailing from the vast emptiness of sidereal space.
Examine the welkin -- this is important.
It's Vaarahamira, a *high welkin* -- his face white and scarred like cracked marble. This is clearly a welkin supremacist. The note says: 'All non-welkin races will be purged.'
I don't care -- step back.
You see primitive oil rigs built into glaciers -- by *boreal dweorg* -- yurts under the snow, great mammoth-like beasts of burden...
Albeit dark and cold, this vision also feels cosy in its own way. Like eggnog, or morphine! A much needed respite from our own world.
So much pain. Back pain, neck pain, headaches, carpal tunnel, chest pain... no gym membership can make up for working in this manner.
The full text reads: 'Heat death of the Universe is the new black'. Another note says: 'The biggest advancement in role-playing systems since the Thirties'.

Outside, a cold wind wraps the building in its bosom. Snowflakes in the wind. An old woman passes what the locals call the Doomed Commercial Area. She tries hard not to look at the bookstore windows. It's *unwise*.
"Just look at those details. So much effort..."
"Well. This has been educational -- let's move on from the welkins."
This appears to be some kind of machine with a cube-shaped heart and a wired framework. The keyboard has a rectangular ON/OFF button; a piece of paper still hangs from the printer.
Look inside the compartment.
Read the printout.
[Leave.]
It's empty like a beehive without its brood. Some cables have been left dangling, disconnected...
It's blank. The lower edge of the paper has been torn off.
Press PRINT.
Behind the hatch sits a cube-like crisscross of filaments, smouldering in the dark like fireflies. Silver tape on the side says in a black marker: "THE OFF-SITE COPY".
Behind the hatch sits a cube-like crisscross of filaments, smouldering in the dark like fireflies. Silver tape on the side says in a black marker: "THE PRODUCTION SCHEDULE".
It sounds like something cracks, before the piece of paper starts filling up with pure black ink.
With a quiet determination the printer starts printing, a piece of paper unfolding like a hand-held fan. A black criss-cross of letters covers its surface.
Nothing happens.
The paper is soaked with ink, its monochrome darkness spanning from margin to margin... It's not possible to make out any information.
Tear off the printout and throw it away.
Fortress Accident employed 18 people, the bulk of the team composed of writers and concept artists. There were also radio programmers, sound engineers, a CEO, two marketing experts...
Wait, why did a *radio game* need so many artists?
It didn't.
It didn't need so many concept artists?

No, definitely not. A few more producers could have come handy though -- especially when dealing with writers, some of whom routinely skipped work because of 'mental health issues' and extremely unprofessional sleep schedules...
Right, what happened?
Turn on the machine.
[Step away.]
The machine lights up like some prehistoric animal stirring from its slumber, revealing virescent PLAY and PRINT keys on the keyboard. The hatch on the machine's central compartment is wide open.
But on the other hand, their obligations *were* piling up at an inhuman rate -- a rate that could only be amended by Pyrholidon.
This is where the machine's memory should go.
"This is where the memory should go," the lieutenant notes, observing the machine.
Insert THE OFF-SITE COPY.
Insert THE PRODUCTION SCHEDULE.
Remove THE OFF-SITE COPY.
Remove THE PRODUCTION SCHEDULE.
Like a smooth drawer, the filament slides into place. On the keyboard, the PLAY key starts blinking.
Have you stirred the ghost of the Doomed Commercial Area from its rest? Could this be its dismembered heart, beginning to flutter?
"Please repeat -- is this the production schedule?"
"Please repeat, is this the off-site copy?"
"That's all for now." (Press OFF/SILENT.)
The filaments you have would fit perfectly inside the compartment.
The filament you have would fit perfectly inside the compartment.
"Thank you and good bye," the old lady's voice disappears along with the static.
The speaker comes to life, static seeps through the machine's planar magnetic driver. An old lady greets you, her voice sounds a hundred years old...
The filament slides out of its glowing nest.
...and a single overburdened producer who developed a habit of popping Pyrholidon in the basement to escape his obligations.
Why did Fortress Accident have so many concept artists?
One of them even managed to steal some valuable company property before skipping town for good.
Look at the table of contents.
The first few pages give an overview of the capital and workforce, while the rest of it seems to be a production schedule.
It was impossible not to fail. The project was too large and no amount of money could satiate the ever-expanding ambitions of the development team.
Tiles on the cube are still smouldering, casting the framework in a soft glow. Virescent PLAY and PRINT keys shine on the keyboard.
It's a project report written by the lead producer Andrew 'Andy' Schott about 'Wirrâl Untethered', a radio game developed by studio Fortress Accident.
Examine the printout again.
A single speck of white shines out from the shade -- for some reason the printer decided to spare this one tiny dot of paper.
Tear off the printout.
It's just black upon black, nothing to see here.
"What happened? It's just covered in ink."
"Odd." The lieutenant runs his hand over the ink-soaked paper, staining his fingertips. "Something is obviously broken here."
A dusty radiocomputer sleeps on its wired frame, forgotten and unused. Its keyboard has a rectangular ON/OFF button; a piece of paper still hangs from the printer.
Press PLAY.
A bar of fabric right above the keyboard starts producing a soft hum. The sound of static seeps through the machine's planar magnetic driver.
Nothing happens.
Something's missing -- there's no tape in the player.
Oh, so they were done in by their own ambition.
No. Even then success remained within an ever-narrowing margin of possibility that, despite everything, never entirely disappeared...
The what?
That sounds bad.
At the eleventh hour, the lead designer, Zsiemsk-born Sulisław Zawisza, decided that what 'Wirrâl Untethered' needed was a secret mystical location at the extreme edge of the map...
That's pretty bad. So that's what did them in?
Well, yeah. That, and the catastrophic data loss.
The what now?

On the nature of the data loss, there's ominously little information in the production log. It comes at the very end, where things get fuzzy and dark, where tables and numbers seem to vanish into an eerie nothingness, before their Igaunijan investor pulled the plug...
And the anomaly caused all the data to get lost in the air?
When the project was returned, it was completely blank.
The team spent weeks on the phone with Lintel, the service provider, but despite their diagnostics they could never produce a satisfactory explanation or pay for the loss.
Wasn't there a copy of the game, a *backup*?
Mysteriously enough, it seems that the off-site copy happened to be *on-site* when the catastrophic data loss occurred...
S. Luukanen-Kilde, the lead programmer of Fortress Accident: "The off-site copy was on-site because there was no *off-site* anymore, not for me, not after eight months of crunch."

"Still haven't gotten an answer from Lintel about what happened. All I could get were the physical coordinates of the error on the East-Insulindian front on that day. Since the computation happened on-air, I reckoned it had to coincide with an actually existing location..."
How many heads were there?
So many. At last count there were approximately 10,000 heads for 10,000 headless men, all of which could be endlessly recombined.
"I have compared the coordinates to a map of Revachol West. Turns out it's only 800 metres from here. The address is Saint-Brune 1147. I am going there to look this thing in the eye..."
They couldn't.
That is, until they discovered the Valley of the Heads.

This place was to be the *Valley of the Heads* -- where the heads of all the *headless* constructs could be found. The player would have been able to choose a head for their headless party member, and each head would been voiced on-air by a professional actor.
What is clear is that one day an unidentified numeric anomaly occurred on the East-Insulindian Lintel front, just as the 'Wirrâl Untethered' project was being compiled that day.
It was the lead programmer's responsibility to oversee weekly maintenance of the off-site copy and, well, keep it off-site. An explanatory note from the lead programmer has been attached.
What does it say?
Because of the concept artists?
No, not the concept artists. It wasn't even the writers, with their panic attacks and three-hour lunches...
I could have bridged the gap.
No, you couldn't have.
Definitely not.
No, it was good. Too good.
What do you mean? I totally could have.
Not a chance.
Even then, success remained within an ever-narrowing margin of possibility that, despite everything, never entirely disappeared...
This is some insane shit. Who were these people?
The world had never seen their kind before and might never again.
How many combinations could you make out of that?
Do you really want to know? There seems to be a calculation here, but it may take a while...
Yeah, how bad could it be?
No, let's not go there.
Good call. It's more than the number of atoms in the observable universe.
Keep going.
Uh oh.
What have I done?
Keep going.
Please stop.
Just let the numbers wash over you.
Okay, so that's what did them in?
I didn't understand a word of that.
Something spooky happened with the machines and the game was lost.
What! They lost the whole game and wouldn't even pay for it?
Always read the terms of service.
The lieutenant taps his foot impatiently, his arms folded tight against his chest.
He's dying for a cigarette. Come to think of it, you are, too.
And let's face it, they didn't have any money left for a legal action.
What if you broke the radiocomputer? What if it's never going to stop?!
Something's broken. Machines aren't supposed to behave like this.

But *what* drugs exactly?

"Hm. Really?" She looks at the windowsill, where a dead fly is lying on its back, legs curled up in a bowtie. "Anyway..."
"And -- naturally -- all the most fashionable tastemakers refused to be seen in chitin from then on. The atelier went bankrupt before they could finish the collection."
"They got what they deserved -- making clothes out of beetle wings is a *terrible* idea!"
"At least it had some spark to it. Most young designers just combine lace with leather and call it original." She shifts in her simple workwear shirt.

"Maybe. Because the taxidermist who made that bear definitely wasn't. Doing his best, I mean."
"I killed the bear." (You unplugged it.)

"Megatherion," nods the dicemaker, "a mega wild beast."

"I don't do drugs."

"But why do you convene, what do you *do*?"
"What did he look like?"
"Was he alone?"
"What about Thursday night?"
"Besides *muscular*, did he have any other identifying traits?"
"Why was he staying at your place in the middle of night?"
"Thanks for the information."
"The *homo-sexual underground*?" The smoker sits up immediately, his eyes wide with amused surprise; a honeyed smile lingers on his lips.
"Yes, but he was speaking to someone on his earpiece."
This *sexual* thing seems interesting... Ask around, become involved.
"Oh, let me think..." He turns his eyes upward in recollection. "He had an accent. He sounded like one of those mercenaries."
"Yes, I want to hear more about this *homo-sexual underground* you're part of."
"What was he saying?"
"What are you, you two?"
What is it about the way he carries himself?
"Just reporting back whatever I was telling him."
Yes, this man is definitely one of the homos, I've seen them homos with my own eyes.
"You did?" A small smile adorns his face. "And how did you like him?"
"He sounded vaguely Oranjese." He closes his eyes. "No, not vaguely, scratch that. He sounded *definitely* Oranjese."
Could he be... a member of the *homo-sexual underground*?
"Are you... are you part of the *homo-sexual underground*?"
"What did you tell him?"
"I met your Sunday friend."
"Nothing. That I didn't see anything."
"Did you tell him about your friend?"
"I see you've found yourself a little something from my wardrobe." He scans you. "Not bad, not bad at all. What brings you here?"
"About this hat I'm wearing..."

dialoguetext: "Hi again, gendarme."
[Leave.]
"Bye-bye, gendarme."
"You can keep it, I don't mind. I can appreciate beauty when I see it."
It's the sports, he's a sports guy, all about that physical prowess and athletic skill... Nothing else here.
"Hmm?" he hums honeyed.
"Why yes I am, officer. Why, do you want to *investigate*?"
He's assuming a role to mock you -- or to entertain himself with your ignorance. Don't fall for it!
"No, I just wanted to know whether you were one of them."
"Well, I *am* one of them, one of this *sub-rosa pleasure group* congregating in cellars under the cover of night... Saturday night, sometimes even *Friday* night!"
"Let's just not talk about this anymore."
"Why not? Don't you want to hear about how we want to destroy the last vestiges of meaning, the last things people in Revachol have to hold on to, the meaning of man and woman?"

"Or the true symbols of security, mother and father and their everlasting marriage... *Everything* will be constantly shifting and moving under our rule, the future will belong to a *circus* of identities, just spinning around, surreal and unreal..."
"You won't even know who you are anymore."
"But I like knowing who I am."
"Does it have anything to do with disco?"
"Other questions, I had other questions, really!" (Try to back off.)
The smoker starts laughing and leans back against the counter: "Sure thing, officer, what do you want to know next?"
"Yes, we listen to a lot of disco. Some say we *engineered* disco to spread our vision of a vertiginous, ever-changing society, where all there is a razzle-dazzle of gold!"
"We are going to *change* the family unit with all this razzamatazz and finger-dancing," he wiggles his hands, "and with mysteries, of course, the mysteries are also of sexual nature, very esoteric."
"I do like disco, maybe I should get into it?"
"No, this is not me."
"You can't just get into it, you have to be born into it -- one is either already *in* the homo-sexual movement or forever excluded from it."
"What if I can't remember whether I'm in or not? What if I can't remember anything about my life -- aside from the fact that I like disco?"
"Okay, then I'm definitely not in."

"Beautiful!" The smoker crawls up to you like an animal preparing to jump. "Beautiful, that's exactly what we're looking for! Who knows, maybe you *were* homo-sexual in the past, maybe all of that has been *repressed*..." He circles his hands around you.
"I have to say that you do look like someone who might be part of *the underground*. You have that very distinctive 'I-can't-understand-what's-going-on-here' look."
"But do you also like the *razzle-dazzle* of gold? Do you like parties and discos and having fun under the vibrant lights of Saturday night?"

"Because instead of the traditional family unit we're going to have all this *razzamatazz*," he wiggles his hands, "and mysteries, of course, too -- mysteries of *sexual* nature, very esoteric. And disco music and drugs."
"That much fun should be illegal."
"You're here!"
"Hi-hi. So what brings you here?"
"Hello-hello. So what brings you here?"
"I am. So are you. What brings you here?"
"What are you doing here?"
"Ah... But for the better part of history it *has been* illegal."
"Okay..." (Blink.) "Okay, I have to think about it."
"Absolutely *wonderful*."
"But it isn't anymore?"
"Admiring the atmosphere..." He smiles. "What about you, officer?"
"I live here, my room is right upstairs."
"I'm here to drink myself into oblivion."
"This is where I'm going to go down in history: I'm going to sing karaoke."
"I'm here to kick some ass and solve the case I'm working on."
"Convenient," he nods. "But what are you doing *here*, talking to me?"
"Thanks. It's like carrying a piece of you with me at all times."
"I wasn't really planning on giving it back anyway."
"I took it to blend in. I'm undercover, you see?"
"Is it now?" He starts laughing. "Well, enjoy it."
"Blend in where?" He raises his brows. "A carneval?"
"You were right, he was magical. Magically bureaucratic."
"I didn't like him as much as I like you."
"I didn't. He's a government official. I don't trust governments."
"Aw, shoot." He bursts out laughing. "Why not?"
"I told you, he can be very useful. I guess that's the charm of powerful people."
"I don't want to talk about other people, I want to talk about you."
"Hmm?" He hums. "What about me, gendarme?"
"A visitor from the first world. He's not like you and me, gendarme." He smiles and his smile seems melancholic. "He can always return."
"Friends, I told you. Sunday friends. Friends who like to get together from time to time."
"He has keys. And he likes the view..." He waves gently with his cigarette-holding hand. "To the sea, I mean."
"How cunning." He raises his brows and you're not sure whether he's mocking you or not. "I like men who take what they want."
"Really?" He straightens up, curious. "Well, I look forward to that!" He raises a glass to you.
"What does it mean -- a Sunday friend?"
He sighs: "That he won't be there when times get tough, I guess."
"Is that even a friend?"
"It is -- on Sundays." He smiles.
"Return where?"
"To his opportunities in Occident, Sur-la-Clef. Still..." He breathes in and keeps his lungs filled for a moment, before letting it out. "His coming and going brings some life to the village."
"Or is it just money, I don't know..." He stares at the bar.
"His earpiece?"
"Yes, you know those tiny speaker-microphones that fancy security guards sometimes wear."
"And he believed you?"
"Why shouldn't he?"
"A bit too dramatic, don't you think?" He says it like it's an aesthetic question. "If you really must do it then I'd go with something else... some other substance."
"Well, here's to you!" He raises a glass, before taking a sip of his drink, froth grazing his mouth.

"But then again -- you're a cop, it definitely fits the genre." He looks at his hands folded on a table. "*I* fit the genre, we all do... moulded by fiction like we're characters in some bad novella."
"I don't know what I'm doing here. I just go wherever life takes me."
"Human psychology is definitely lazy, don't you think?"
"Hmm... maybe you should figure it out, detective."
"No." He studies you from across the table.
"This is gonna be, like, a twenty hour mind-project for me. Twenty hours at least."
"Do think about it, officer." He starts laughing and leans back against the counter.

A man like you can figure out his sexuality in a working day. It won't be twenty hours unless you want to enter the heightened realms of the *fantasme érotique* afterwards. Then it may be twenty hours *or more*! But that would be on your own time.
