dialoguetext: "Oh, a *committee*." He smiles. "How interesting..."
"There's only one problem: I don't think he wants to talk with *you*."
"And if I may ask, gendarme, what is this *committee* about?" He takes a measured drag of his cigarette.
There's only one way through this. You're going to have to apologise...
Fortunately, saying sorry is practically second-nature for you.
Never. You're no sorry cop. *He* should apologise to *you*.
"Maybe you could intercede on my behalf?"
"Then I guess I should apologise for that little *misunderstanding* in the apartments."
"You can tell him I'm prepared to accept his apology anytime."
"No." He exhales a grey trail of smoke. "I don't think I will. This is between the two of you, you see."
"Yes." He nods. "I think that would be prudent..."
A bemused expression. "Oh, I don't think *you* should be expecting an apology from *him*."
"In any case, I would *love* to help, but the thing is, I don't know *where* he is. We don't talk about everything, you see..." He gently taps the end of his cigarette with his forefinger.
"He might have mentioned something about making a tour of some historical sites up the coast... in an unofficial capacity, of course."
"Do you know when he'll be back?"
"I guess I'll have to look for him along the coast."
"How did he get over the water lock? I thought it was impassable?"
"Not a clue. I'm not his agenda keeper, you see."
"I guess you will." He tips his head ever so slightly toward you.
He shrugs. "He has his ways. I don't need to know every detail of his life."
Then you have nothing more to say here.
Don't be foolish. There's greater things at stake here than your pride.
"Okay, fine. *I'm* the one who should apologise."
"Then he and I have nothing more to discuss."
"Oh, he'll be *devastated* to hear that, I'm sure..." He smiles.
He doesn't care one way or another. For him, it's all one entertaining chamber play.
"What, you're going to blow a lead, just like that?" The lieutenant gives you an incredulous look.
"I'm not sure if you've noticed, but Martinaise isn't exactly crawling with Coalition representatives. You're going to have to look for someone else now."
What are you doing, Harry? You better hope there's someone else around who can help you get in touch with the Coalition...
"In any event, good luck with whatever it is you're up to."
He's all bemused skepticism. He doesn't *actually* care what you want with his friend.
"I'm not really sure, I'm just trying to reach a higher authority."
"It's about assigning la responsabilité."
"I'm really not at liberty to say."
"Sounds like a bore, frankly." He takes a drag of his cigarette. "All the fun stuff's down here..."
"God, of *course* it is. My friend is always trying to convince me I need a little more responsibility..."
"Oh, a big *secret* committee. I understand perfectly..." His mouth forms a half smile.
"As though I don't have enough going on already."
"Tell me the truth, do you know me from somewhere?"
"To what station do you think you would belong in this alternate and totally fictional reality?"
"Forty-first?"
"Fifty-seventh?"
"Sixty-nine."
"That's..." The man looks extremely surprised. "...exactly right! Down to a fraction."
"Really?"
"No need for the sarcasm."
"No, not really." He let's the silence drag out.
"I don't even know what to say to that..." he shakes his head. "What is your god damn station?"
He seems to be observing you through the reflective glass of his eye-wear. There's no reply. Perhaps repeat it?
"I think even in this *fictional* reality, the 57th would still be *my* station." The lieutenant makes a little nod towards the man with sunglasses.
"Good job, that was very close." He now speaks with the tone of a mother helping her kid take first steps. "Maybe try again?"
"My condolences," the man with sunglasses replies dryly.
"Sixty-nine."
Repeating it gets no reaction from the man with sunglasses. Suddenly the world is very quiet. Even the howling wind outside sounds a bit embarrassed.
"Never mind, this is stupid."
"Stupid is a gross understatement." You feel his eyes behind the shades mapping you out.
You *know* what it is. It's like the two of you know each other. Just ask him.
There's something that binds you to him. Some kind of an outfit maybe...? A uniform!
A firefighters uniform?
Exactomundo!
"Go ahead," he nods. "Have another guess."
"Okay, okay!" The man sounds genuinely excited. "That's plausible. That's entirely plausible. Now we're really getting somewhere..." He gives you a long, meaningful look and adds:
"...somewhere *good*."
"How about 41? How does 41st sound?" He shakes his head. "Never mind, I'm not going along with this..."
An animal control uniform?
A nurse's uniform?
I understand, the *uniform* is metaphorical -- I'm actually seeing the working class, right?
The police of animals, yes!
Yes. Nurses, why not...
Uh... I want to say... yes? I think.
"No, not really," he replies with the familiar fake enthusiasm. "Not really at all! Now *please* go sort this hanging out, alright?"
"Nothing *works* for me, that's the problem, buddy." He closes his eyes and rubs his forehead. "Whatever, I don't really care."
"Me solving the case of the hanged man?"
"Listen, don't make anything out of it, but do you work for Animal Control?"
"This is going to sound really weird, but are you by any chance... a male nurse?"
"Level with me here for a second... are you *working class*?"
"Well, I *am* interacting with the most dangerous animal of them all -- you -- I'd say yes. I'm animal control."
"You think I'm dangerous?"
"You're making fun of me."
"To yourself -- yes, extremely."
"Stop it, Jean..." she says quietly and turns to you. "No, he has never been a firefighter. No one here is a firefighter."
She sighs and looks at you with something akin to compassion in her eyes. "Can we help you with something?"
"Well that depends," the man with sunglasses says tilting his head. "Define *fire*."
"I'm going to ask you straight: are you or have you ever been a firefighter?"
"Oh you know me... always the joker -- just can't but see the bright side." He's doing a weird dance imitation with his elbows. "Guess I'm just pathologically a *glass is half-full* kind of guy."
"Fucking *politics* again... You know what I'm more interested in?"
"Yes."
"Weren't you depressed or something?"
"Whatever works for you."
"Seven years and going strong!" He nods enthusiastically. "The head doctors are now calling it a medical marvel... no, wait, anomaly was the word they used."
"No."
This guy is suffering from clinical depression. And it's been going on awhile.
"But as you're still staring at me like a calf stares at a freshly made gate... I assume there was something else."
"You solving the case you're on." He takes a quick breath. "I'm passionate about that. So maybe -- get to it?"
"Oh, you're still here," he says, opening his eyes. "Must have had something really important for me?"
"Oh, you've done a lot more with ether than just *look into it*." He leans back and mumbles: "This was stupid, I shouldn't have..."
"Oh, I wish I could, I wish I could..." he spreads his arms and shrugs. "Unfortunately I'm a neck and chin nurse. What you need is a head nurse. Sorry I couldn't help you out, buddy."
"Why yes..." His eyes peer over the sunglasses. "Yes, I am a male nurse -- how could you tell?"
"Uh... really?"
"I see into the ether... that's how I know things."
"Could you take a look at me? I've been through a lot lately."
"Oh, I definitely know you from *somewhere*."
"From where? From another life?"
"Yes. From another life. A different life. Maybe the life of a police officer belonging to the ranks of the..." He pauses.
That there is a form of severe sarcasm... and he's not actually a nurse.
"You can sometimes be a real asshole, you know that?" Surprisingly, the words don't seem to be directed at you.
I don't wanna ask that.
Then don't. No one's forcing you.
Of course, you don't have to. You can talk about anything you want.
He's not a male nurse. I'm not gonna ask that.
Of course, you don't have to. You can talk about anything you want.
That doesn't sound right. I don't wanna say it.
Of course, you don't have to. You can talk about anything you want.
I don't think he's a firefighter. I'm not gonna ask that.
Another life...
Okay, the man with the sunglasses and his *hypothetical Station 41*. Weird, right?
I guess it was kind of weird, yes.
No, this whole interaction was perfectly normal.
Frankly I'm way past caring or wondering. [Discard thought.]
I know! Super weird.
There's something we're missing here... something you can't put our finger on. You know what -- just ask him. I know it sounds crazy (and you'll probably get laughed at). But still...
I was thinking the same thing. I should just ask him if we're from the same station.
It's impossible. I don't want to waste my time.
Yes. Just cross it off the list. It's probably not true though.
Of course. Yes. It's preposterous.
"*How* can a bar be out of vermouth?"
"Can't do it with class? Don't do it at all."
"Could I get a refill here, please?"
"Don't even get me started on beauty..."
"I'm practically a shrink minus the diploma."
"Yes, yes, I'm very attractive. Great, thank you."
"Okay, *you* tell me this doesn't taste like shit..."
"*Obviously* I'm gonna quit some day."
Pick up the handset.

dialoguetext: It didn't give you *any* fun for that money. Nothing. Your hand is turning blue now... blood drips to the ground.
Calling...
End of tone. Someone picks up.
"Pierre? Is that you, Pierre?" The voice is female and sounds about a hundred years old.
She does not answer. All you hear is hiss.
"I might be? What's Pierre like?"
"Yes, it's me -- Pierre."
"No, this is not Pierre."
"So nice of you to find the time to call me! It gets so lonely. Even the animals have died."
"There was someone there before. I heard someone. Who's there with you?"
"Do you have any news about Pierre?"
"Who is Pierre?"
"He's my sister's grandson. He used to visit me as a lad... Fine young man..."
"You're not a revolutionary, Harry... You're drunk."
"Yes, Pierre is dead."
"No, I have nothing."

"But who are you then? A salesman of some sort? Modern goods are rubbish. And I can't afford them anyhow. It's a shame what you did to our country..." The woman moans and the phone lines howl in unison with her.
Dora. The name feels like a *gift*. A gift that was meant for you -- to make it possible to live.
"I'm not a salesman, I was just calling a random number and you somehow ran with it."
"This is because we are bred to be leaders. I can hear the common or mixed background from your voice."
Calling...
"I just so wanted it to be Pierre... Have a pleasant evening, prankster."
Calling...
Disconnect tone.
"Is someone *there*?"
"Yes, I'm a salesman. What exactly did we do to your country?"
"You ruined it and you sold it to foreigners. You don't own anything if everything is for sale."
Calling...
"Give it a thought. Goodbye."
Calling...
"I don't know who I am... But who are you?"
"I was a baroness."
"Dora." She's still confused. "Who is this? The connection is bad..."
Pause. There is silence on the other end.
"You won't get me and you won't get my money!"
There's more?
"Sure you do. No one has anything nowadays."
Calling...
"You're either a salesman or a statistician of some kind. I am not interested in cooperating."
Calling...
"No, I'm a police officer."
And calling -- for who knows how long. But no one answers. You need to insert more money to call again.
"To hell with the police! To hell with you..."
"What a pity... I'm afraid I won't be coming to the funeral. I.... there... chrysanthemum..."
Don't react.
"That's... not good."
"It gets lonely even when you're with people."
You dial the number again -- as you've done many times. You remember it well now: 001 -- 41 -- 44 -- 47 -- 11 -- 17 -- 361 -- 451 -- 67 -- 451 -- 451.
"What kind of pets did you have?"
Don't react. Whatever you do, don't react to that last thing.

Yes. 451 -- 67 -- 451 -- you are going deeper now, into some unknown place. Far away from this island of matter and its telecommunication networks....

11 -- 17 -- 361 -- your fingers keep moving like a spider, every time the ring rotates back with a little ring of metal, like a bell tolling.

"No, but I got a feeling Al Kickurass is gonna make an appearance if you ever call this number again. Have a good one, asshole!"

"What are you, like five?" A woman's voice shouts something in the background and when Girard speaks again his voice is hushed...

Just let it ring.

Calling...

"I'm sorry it was a stupid joke, I shouldn't have called, it's stupid -- I'm so sorry."
"Pick it up!"

Why?

"I'm Mazov. Kraz Mazov."

Finish it.

It looks like she does not want to pick it up, Harry. Stop scaring her.

"I can't *tell* you who I am. I have a secret plan to win mankind three thousand years of peace on this planet. I have to be ominously vague..." (Proceed.)
"Doesn't matter, put her on, I don't like waiting."
"I am an ultra-high-net-worth individual. I understand how reality works. I have *seen* into it. My mind is clear." (Proceed.)

"I am the last faithful kingsman. I will free the city of Revachol. I will turn back the sea. I will reverse time." (Proceed.)
The sounds are muffled. You can make out two people: a man and a woman called *Bian*. They are talking to each other in agitated voices. There's a shuffle of feet, children maybe?
Calling...
More shouting. You're pretty sure you hear a man saying *fuck* several times. Then the crackle in the phone line gets violently loud, like the surf breaking.
You hear a faint *thuck*. You could swear you're hearing furniture falling over.
Calling...
"Stop it! I was just kidding, I'm not sleeping with your wife!"
Calling...
"Wait Girard! Let's just keep talking, buddy!"
"Get away from her, I'm a cop!"
Calling...
A sigh. She heard you, but she does not hang up. And neither do you. You can't.
Calling...
"I'm not going to stop. I'm going to keep fucking your wife, Girard."
"Harry, please..." A sad voice answers, dressed in distortion.
You can't make out a single word, just vague voices. One more, a child, has joined. Something breaks -- or falls over? Footsteps approaching!
"Who is this?"
"Mhm," she hums, her voice warm from sleep.
"What the hell are you doing?" The lieutenant has been keeping a distance, but steps closer now.
Now walk away. Forget about this. Walk away and do police work. *BURY* this in yourself and move on.
"What? I'm just having a bit of fun, what's the big deal?"
The headset lands in the cradle with a clank.
"You're right, Kim -- it went wrong. Horribly wrong. I shouldn't have done this..." (Hang up.)
Strange. This is not how you started before.
Let it call!
Something hits the phone with a loud crack of plastic and microphone hiss -- after that you are left with the disconnect tone.
Hang up.
What in the name of god did you just do?
That's it. You're caught in a trap. It'll take quite a while for the shit-circus to end now.
"What the hell are you doing?" The lieutenant has been keeping a distance, but steps closer now.
No. Let it call. I *must*.
"You're right, Kim -- this went wrong, I shouldn't have done this..."
"I was just having a bit of fun, what's the big deal?"
451 -- you have dialled god knows how many numbers. The headset has been waiting silently to relay a signal -- surely nothing can come of this, you think. But it does. A connection.
Before it's too late, please.
"I don't understand what I did wrong."
"I'm a revolutionary servant of humanity. I will free mankind and abolish the classes. I will raise the dead." (Proceed.)
"Big deal?!" Not a muscle moves in the lieutenant's face.
"You're right, you shouldn't have."
"Let's just go, I've had enough of this phone booth."
sequence: PlayAnimation(Tequila Sunset, PhoneboothHangup); PlayAnimation(Phone Booth, PhoneboothHangup);

dialoguetext: "You were making *prank calls*." Not a muscle moves in the lieutenant's face.
Put it down.
"Stop calling me, man!" Someone picks up. The voice on the other end is slightly hysterical.
Still calling...
Calling...
"Who is this?"
Calling...
Calling...
Calling...
Calling...
Calling...
"I want to die."
*Still* calling...
In the middle of it -- a familiar ring. Small. Distorted.
"Uh... who is this?"
You dial the number again -- twenty six pulls of the rotary dial. The machine eats the coin and a terrifying ocean of distance rustles in your ear...
"Yes, but a slight change of plans -- I want this delivered to the Whirling-in-Rags in Martinaise."
"We could all be a bit kinder to each other, don't you think? Consider your debt paid, my friend."
"You seem to be in some sort of trouble. Maybe I can help you, I'm a police officer."
"You're not a kingsman, Harry... You're drunk."
"My *debt?* I don't fucking owe you, it's..." The young man realises something. "Who is... ah never mind, I don't have time for this..."
"Hello." She sounds sleepy.
sequence: PlayAnimation(Tequila Sunset, PhoneboothCallDora)@2; PlayAnimation(Phone Booth, PhoneboothCallDora)@2;

dialoguetext: The phone gets hanged up fast as lightning, all you hear is a little shuffle of nylon as the hand moves on the other end.
"Tethys, I uh..." The young man realises something. "Hey, you're not Tethys! Screw you and don't ever call here again, you're fucking with some *serious* people!"
There's a moment of silence before the voice speaks again, more calmly: "You got the wrong number, don't call here again."
"You're not a high-net-worth individual, Harry... You're drunk."
Amid the howling in the wire you make out a woman's voice with a thick Samaran accent: "Girard... Girard, this is a joke. Someone is making a joke..."
"You're not ominous, Harry... You're drunk."
You just do. And you know it is going to hurt.
The handset starts slipping from your sweaty palm... your breathing is heavy.
"Are we about *done* with this now?" The lieutenant has taken a few steps back.
You close your eyes and put your index finger on the rotary dial, then pull down on the number, then move one up and repeat the motion, twice...
You close your eyes and feel your finger move on the rotary dial. You start with 005, as before...
Still calling...
Followed by seven digits at random. The last one makes the silence turn into a ring. It's calling...
And calling -- for two minutes now. You're out of luck. No one's home there either. But the payphone still has your ten cents in there...
Yeah, *bratan*. We've had all the fun there was to have here. And it wasn't much.
Time keeps passing. In the distance, seagulls squawk -- no one is home at this number. But the coin... it's still in there... you find yourself thinking:
What were you trying to achieve by closing your eyes? Did you want your muscle memory to take over and call somewhere? Where?
41 -- 44 -- 47 --  it's too late now, the movement is almost mechanical.
Home?
Pitiful and terrifying. You feel your pulse rise with each ring...
His own *heart*.
It's *really* time to stop this now.
Wait -- what did I just do?
Calling...

An ultra-long-distance call. Your ear fills with a crackle, the wash of a strange ocean full of white noise. A little bird starts ringing in there, not like the local calling tone before. No, a small ring in a cage of distortion, far away, a distant network of phones...
Keep dialling...
41 -- 44 -- 47 -- the rotary dial feels cold from the sea air.
Again you close your eyes -- and again your fingers move on the rotary dial. Ten metallic rings as the dial returns to zero after each number.
005 is Revachol ZoC -- 001 is Graad, on the Graadian isola, where the telephone was invented. The next two digits you dial are the area code for the city of Mirova...
You dialled 001. This is not the area code of Revachol. It is another destination -- on another isola. Some far-off nation state.
Stop!
Long windows... how do I know that?
You only have two, maybe three things left to say before the change runs out.
Ringing by the bedside of a dark but capacious apartment with long windows... you know this to be true.
It didn't give you *any* fun for that money. Your hand is turning blue now... blood drips to the ground.
"Officer -- that's enough. Let's return to work..."
Your hand is swelling up.
Fuck it, it doesn't hurt.
It didn't give you *any* fun for that money.
Calling...
Who cares. Run. Go. Don't think about this. Do police work, it's all there is.
"That's enough now, officer..." The lieutenant stands at a distance.
"Khm..." A single *khm* lets you know the lieutenant is ready to move now.
The headset lands in the cradle with a clank. There it sits -- still warm from your hand. You have no idea what just happened.
Put 10 cents in and dial the long phone number again.
sequence: PlayAnimation(Tequila Sunset, PhoneboothDial); PlayAnimation(Phone Booth, PhoneboothDial);

dialoguetext: "No-no..." She's waking up now. "It's *you*, isn't it? It's you..."
You pick up the handset. There's a tone -- the machine is operable.
sequence: PlayAnimation(Tequila Sunset, PhoneboothGrab); PlayAnimation(Phone Booth, PhoneboothGrab); HideActualHeld();

dialoguetext: Hang up.
There's still some unused change in there -- the machine waits for a number to be dialled.
sequence: PlayAnimation(Tequila Sunset, PhoneboothGrab); PlayAnimation(Phone Booth, PhoneboothGrab); HideActualHeld();

dialoguetext: A metal payphone under a yellow plastic dome. There's a bitter, caustic taste on the tip of your tongue as you look at the handset.
sequence: PlayAnimation(Tequila Sunset, PhoneboothGrab); PlayAnimation(Phone Booth, PhoneboothGrab); HideActualHeld();

dialoguetext: Calling still...
You can't. Some strange force is keeping the headset glued to your hand, your ear listening to the ring in the speaker...
Life is garbage.
The cold metal is hard and hurts your knuckles. You look at them turning purple.
The cold metal is hard and your knuckles bleed a little...
Takes your mind away from that voice, for one second at least...
Phone hanging up.
Disconnect tone.
Punch it again, the pain is good.
The cold metal is hard and your knuckles bleed.
Hello, Girard. Technically speaking, you're electricity.
That's right. You *can*. Whatever you're doing here, you can just stop it and go on with your life.
"You want more money now, huh?! YOU WANT FUCKING MONEY?!!!?" (Punch the phone again.)
sequence: PlayAnimation(Tequila Sunset, PhoneboothHangup); PlayAnimation(Phone Booth, PhoneboothHangup); PlayAnimation(Tequila Sunset, GenericPunch)@2; PlayAnimation(Tequila Sunset, PhoneboothGrab)@6.25; PlayAnimation(Phone Booth, PhoneboothGrab)@6.25;

"I don't know who I am. I am an amnesiac." (Proceed.)

dialoguetext: What *you* are is a *surprise*, get his wife on the phone...
Say you're not Pierre... that seems like a better idea. (You don't know why.)
The lieutenant is too far away to hear your yelp. The sea wind blows...
"You're not an amnesiac, Harry... You're drunk."
The lieutenant shrugs apathetically, then walks a little distance away to concentrate on his notes. Looks like he'd rather not get into it again.
Calling in the night....
This has lowered his opinion of you -- but only a little.
He accepts your apology.
Then the ocean breaks. Out of the depths, a woman's voice emerges. Small. The dearest thing you've ever heard.
Calling...
Calling...
"I'll get you your money, alright? I just need 'til tonight. Let me work."
Calling...
The saddest sound in the world.
He does not seem to be overly thankful of your kindness as he hangs up.
Disconnect tone.
Calling...
The area code for Revachol Zone of Control.
Put 10 cents in and dial a random number: 005-11-11-313.
sequence: PlayAnimation(Tequila Sunset, PhoneboothDial); PlayAnimation(Phone Booth, PhoneboothDial);

dialoguetext: Calling...
Hang it up.
"I'm tired..." A man answers, fast this time. His voice is hoarse from cigarettes. You hear typing in the background.
Sounds like he hasn't talked to anyone in quite a while.
Calling still...
"What are you tired of?"
"I'm tired too."
"Is there anything I can do to help you? I'm with the police."
Let it call more.
"Writing. I hate writing so much... But I have to get back to it."
You do not hear the customary disconnect tone, just silence in the handset -- the machine is still waiting for you to dial a number.
The man disappears with a sigh.
"If I could go just one month without writing. No, two months... I could regenerate my brain. Fucking liberalism..."
"There is nothing."
Lucky you. The call went too fast for the payphone to register. You can still make a new one without paying.
Seems like it did not have time to swallow the coin. This sometimes happens.
Both pitiful and terrifying. You feel your pulse rising with each ring...
Still...
He doesn't have a home. Not anymore.
He doesn't have a home. His home is under a boat.
"Is that you?"
And fight.
"Harry? How do you know my name?"
"I'm not drunk."
"Okay I'm drunk, what does it matter? I'm still *me*!"
"I'm gonna get even drunker." (Take a big sip.)
"I'm not drunk -- I'm *high*."
"Harry? Who's Harry?"
"Harry? Who's Harry -- are you sleeping with him? Is *Harry* there?!"
"Harry? Who's Harry -- are you sleeping with him? I'm also Harry!"
"Because it's me... Look, I don't understand what you're saying or why you're calling me. You seem drunk."
"I don't understand what you're saying."
"I'm not drunk or high, I'm just... hurt... why does it hurt to talk to you?"
"Oh god..." There's silence, it's heavy as tin. The white noise howls.
"Do you know what time it is? It's so late here..." Sounds like she's looking for a clock on the night stand.
"Hey."
"Ooo... are you there?"
Say nothing.
"It's four o'clock, Harry! I need to wake up in two hours."
"Do you want to party?"
"I want to talk about me. Who am I? You sound like you know me."
"Where are you? You sound like you're in another world."
"You're in Mirova, right?"
"No, I want to go to sleep..."
"What do you want to talk about? That we haven't talked about already..."
"I'm in Mirova. Sleeping."
"Yes, I'm in Mirova. Sleeping."
Catastrophic damage.
"The Academy? That sounds better than my job. I'm happy."
"Pfft, Academy... my job is *real*."
I don't know... I don't understand what's happening.
You need to stop, Harry. You'll die.
You need to stop. Harry. You're killing yourself.
"Where?"
No response, only a sigh. The connection crackles, like burning paper.
"To work."
"The Academy. Where I work."
"Where are you going in two hours?"
Say nothing.
What are you doing to yourself right now?
"My job is sad and terrible. It has dead bodies in it."
I'm making a funny prank call.
Fun? You need to stop. Harry. You're killing yourself.
"Oh no... please stop. Please let's just hang up..."
"My heart hurts. I'm gonna have a heart attack."
This is bad, you feel your right hand on the handset cramping up with pain...
No. We're not gonna do this. Your hand is *not* going to cramp up, not now.
(Hang up.)
Your hand isn't moving. The headset hisses in your ear with *evil* sadness.
Disconnect tone -- the machine ran out of money.
sequence: PlayAnimation(Tequila Sunset, PhoneboothHangupDora); PlayAnimation(Phone Booth, PhoneboothHangupDora);

dialoguetext: "Is someone there with you?"
"Yes."
"I am the law. I'm a detective. I'm doing a case. There's a hanged man."
Right now. I'm gonna give you *one* chance.
Push the headset in the cradle with all the strength you have!
She does not answer anymore.
"I'm gonna solve it."
"It doesn't matter. This case doesn't matter."
"None of it matters -- not anymore."
"Can you help me solve it? I need to solve it. They won't take me back if I don't."
"Harry..."
She sighs. "Look, I don't understand what you're saying, or why you're calling me. You seem drunk."
Smash the headset into the cradle.
No. I can't. I need the pain.
The cord dangles in the wind like a sickening worm.
sequence: PlayAnimation(Tequila Sunset, PhoneboothHangupDora); PlayAnimation(Phone Booth, PhoneboothHangupDora);

dialoguetext: Static sings inside the phone glued to your ear. Ancient, sticky...
Run. To the church. Home. Anywhere but here. Anything but calling her again.
Twenty-two million people live in Mirova, the capital city of Graad. It is the capital of the world after Revachol was destroyed.
That's right. Walk away.
It's over.

It's easier, this time, drifting off. Your head has found a comfortable indent in the pillow. Your legs and your torso feel like lead weights sinking to the bottom of the sea, until they're suddenly light...
This respite -- you've earned it, brother. Bask in the darkness. Let it swallow you up and swivel you around while you forget everything you've managed to remember...
Thank you, darkness. Thank you.
You're welcome, Harry-boy. You earned it.
(Fall into a deep, uninterrupted sleep.)
After centuries of darkness, the alarm rings -- but what's this? You *actually* feel rested. There's no time to cuddle with your pillow, however, or as much as shiver from the cold. The world awaits.
[Open your eyes.]
Is this the last dream?
No. This is the one before that. We'll just keep cycling it for you, if you don't mind. As long as we can. Spin it like black yarn.
Enjoy it while it lasts.
Go.
But I've been bad. I haven't earned this.
No, you haven't. You've just *been*.
I've heard this song before.
Sing along -- in silent communion.
This is greatest hits material. Black tape spinning and spinning and spinning... You finally tired yourself. Cornered the flicker of your mind and extinguished it.
For now -- a little while -- you can...
How many days have I been in Martinaise already...
There are no days here. There are no weeks. Just black tape spinning. On repeat. Until the end.
Blackness, blackness, blackness. The ultimate disco. The ruins of your life behind you, still smouldering. Ashes rise. But you're not looking.
(Sleep. Without words or images.)
When the pictograms and the hieroglyphs of the world return, they seem silent somehow. The alarm rings quietly too. You're ready.
Ready -- but something is coming. It always is.
Oh god...

It's your disgusting *body*. Even through your sleep, you feel a vague discomfort suffusing it. Your belly and your sides are unpleasantly tender. You wish you could curl up into a foetal ball of safety, but you cannot -- because of the PAIN.
Every cell in your body is moaning in agony, asking,  "What did we ever do to you?"
These are my just desserts. I will endure this pain with *dignity*.
That pain in your right side is your enlarged liver, by the way. As for your kidneys... you've really been compounding the damage lately.
No, please... Where is that blessed nothingness? That sweet oblivion?
I'm an artist and liver damage is my art.
I'm sorry, cells! It's all me! It's my fault!
This body's worthless anyway... no one does anything nice to it.
*Now* you're finally thinking about something other than yourself. Let's see how far that'll get you.
And why might *that* be the case? What love alights on such a bloated corpse-to-be?
There's no dignity here... only reflections of your body mass. Flashes of the day. You keep coming back to yourself in the mirror -- but why? To admire all your *accomplishments*?
You had your chance, Harry-boy, and you missed it. Started thrashing around, acting all brave -- now the Dark Centre has vanished. You'll never get back to it.
I think I... need medical attention.
Oh yes. *They'll* check you out, give you some pills, make it all okay. The wonder-makers.

What do you think you're doing right now? Coming to some greater awareness? Look at all these lights! Blinking in and out of existence -- *thoughts*! You're just *pretending* that you're asleep, even to yourself. While the world goes on without you...
Just get me out of here then. Back to the other place.
...But it never seems to let *you* go, does it? Time to rise and wipe that shining sweat off as best you can. Gather your bearings. Rock and roll.
That pain in your right side is your enlarged liver, by the way. As for your kidneys... you've really been compounding the damage lately. And, trust me, you don't want me to do the maths.
It's all the system's fault. The system failed me.
Yes, your body is a system, and and it's failing you because you're failing it.
You're just stuck here. In the half-world. Could try looking at other people. *Really* looking. But why would you want to start doing that?
I will! I'm looking at people all the time. I like them.
Human beings will *always* betray you.
How many promises have *you* kept lately, Sir Harry? To the great, see-through world, the tenderness?
Sure, you do. They're all so friendly, aren't they?
Put on your prettiest face for the masses!
Let it! Let it!
I thought I was on the express to The Silence!
Hey, what is this? I was on the express to Zero-Holm!
Wait, wasn't this the express to Fuck-All-Borough?

dialoguetext: Now, you've gone off the rails, baby, now you're stuck sitting here by the tracks, admiring the wreck around you. You just can't help it: looking at yourself, the sum total of your *accomplishments*...
But this suffering -- it must have *some* kind of meaning... A story that will come out of it. Perhaps even a story that you will write yourself?
[Open your eyes.]
Here we are again, my broken bird. The waves are coming... carrying you away... but you can't go. No -- you have to stay. Always half-aware of yourself.
You're not *cooperating* brother-man.
Why?
And there's a lot of it. Ever present in your organs. It's like every one of them has their own *nasty* song to sing.
Oh yeah, baby. Frame your suffering as a masterpiece. Only one problem -- no one's watching. It's boring, buddy, boring as death.
Don't be stupid Harry, it's not happening. They don't make new *kidneys* and *livers* in hospital. All you've got to do is pray to god it passes -- while you *stare* at the flickering darkness.
Some of them are. Some of them are nice. Others are scared.
Oh, baby boy. You're already *in* the other place. There's no nourishment for you tonight. Maybe tomorrow?
Maybe if you... you know... like... TOOK A LOT OF DRUGS? Before you go to sleep. That'd do the trick...
At least they're *interesting*. Each one has a process just like yours, running in the space between their ears, full of secrets.
Thou art honourable and just, sire. 'Tis the snakes who are vile! Hissing in the grass...
Women. It's the women. Look out for the women. They're *oathbreakers*...
Maybe if you cracked the damn thing, then you'd feel satisfied and tired. Holding the picture puzzle in your hands... complete!
Maybe if you weren't so hard on yourself...
People are beautiful. Statuesque. Parodies and tragedies of themselves. A great democracy of creatures...
Come now. Humans have earned your trust. And you theirs...

Thoughts, baby. A million little lights in the dark. You're one fine instrument, brother -- all those faces and all those names, all that laughter and screaming and scheming around... Every corner and every street...
Recorded in you. Forever. On ferrotape.
On and on it goes, for untold hours. At the disco where you first asked her to dance. Rising -- rising! -- above the dark curvature. The great wingspan of sleep, studded with stars.
Spinning on empty.
Spinning in eternity.
Spinning, spinning... tell me, am I dreaming?
No. You're spinning tapes at the discotheque. The great, unceasing disco of the mind. The flash! The bang! The endless *learning* experience.
Behold, there are *millions* of them down there. The first time. The last time. The smoke in her mouth, the potted flowers, the faces: turning, changing.
*What* is it?
It's the *world*, Harry-boy. And you're *made* of it. Every day you're out there you make more of yourself from it. I'm afraid you can't be *unmade* now.
The rain, the snow... I don't want to. It's beautiful.
You can never forget this shit.
The colours. The voices.
The endless visions. Erase them.
Beautiful? It's *stuck* on loop... whirling, spitting out words and images.
It's not possible anymore. It's *stuck* on loop... Whirling, spitting out words and images.
All *stuck* on loop... Whirling, spitting out words and images.

You're the son of the World again. Harrister -- a ceaseless agent picking up litter and old newspapers, collecting your little bubble gum wrappers and idiotic picture post cards. Meaningless, meaningless keepsakes.
Reading your awful letters and *recalling* things, aren't you? The endless names of the world... An address book, you are. The map of a city.
That's right. I *am* an agent of the world.
But what if I want to be the agent of nothing?
You'll go insane if you keep going like this. One more day and you'll be in the loonie bin. I just know you will. And for what, brother-man?
It's too late. You're not *made* of nothing anymore, you're something now, Harry. I tried to drown you in the black water but you re-emerged. Kicking and screaming. Running. And for what?

Solving your little crossword puzzles? Doing your tasks, crossing names off your lists? Trying to become some sort of world-detector... It won't make it *okay*. It won't put smoke back in her mouth...
Beep-beep-beep! The alarm is ringing, Harry. The disco circus goes on and on! You barely slept three hours last night.
You can do it. It's nothing. Do it for the city. Go.
Do it for the wind.
Do it for the picture puzzle. Put it all together. Solve the world. One conversation at a time.
[Open your eyes.]
Feel the pillow under your cheek.
Why?
Coz only love can break your heart...

dialoguetext: I can't give up. I have to keep going, for Revachol... [Pursue thought.]
I'm building communism for all. This time we won't fail... [Pursue thought.]
I'm just looking out for my economic self-interest... [Pursue thought.]
We're making progress. Measured, steady progress... [Pursue thought.]
There he goes again. He's a real political animal, our Harry. He still doesn't see that it's the world that's changing *him*...
For the working class.
For the greater good.
For the money, baby.
For Revachol. Always and only Revachol.
Forget politics. I'll never sleep if I keep on like this.
Are you sure? You could be closing the door on a brilliant and *special* future for yourself.
You're right. It's time to get political.
Yes, I'm sure. I am very boring and *apolitical* and sleepy. [Ignore thought.]
He's got no idea what he's in for.
I knew you couldn't resist. So now you're gonna change the world, but how?
Did you hear that? He's renouncing politics. He's *strictly business* now.
Just another thoughtless vessel ploughing the grey seas of the everyday.
Like a deftly cast fishing net, sleep pulls you out of the world and into its dark shore. The rough mesh chafes, then, tightening around you, it digs into your brain.
How've things been going for you out there? Helped anyone lately? Saved anyone lately? *Murdered* anyone lately?
Because, you know, you *are* a murderer. A disco music listening psycho-killer who offs poor people -- and then *forgets* about it.
[Open your eyes.]
Great. This is gonna be really chill.
Dark shore, my ass. I know what this is.
Yeah-yeah, just let me sleep...
This bastard isn't even listening to you!
I don't care. That doesn't scare me.
Shut up, I just want to sleep.
Hear that? You were *naive* to think he's afraid of his bloodied hands, soul brother. Oh no, I see inside his amygdala and his hippocampus. The thing he's *really* scared of...
Okay, so I'm a murderer and that's *bad*.
...is much, *much* worse than that.
Hear that? He doesn't even flinch. Ice-man doesn't care about killing people. That's *nothing* to him. Black water under the bridge. The thing he's *really* scared of...
Hear that? Ice-man wants to sleep, he doesn't care about killing people. That's *nothing* to him. Black water under the bridge. The thing he's *really* scared of...

We're trying to help you. All these processes -- these tortures, voices and tremors -- are all just *distractions*. Flares and countermeasures. To keep you from the *last dream*. The worst of them all.
Her face forms in summertime...
The last dream will be total annihilation. Cinders peeling off the fuselage. We won't be there to help you anymore, Harry. We will be dormant. You will be naked and alone.
Oh, but you *will*. You're already *going* there. Slipping. How long can we keep you from the precipice? *One* more dream? Two max, baby. Then it's...
Doesn't sound like it will be okay.
Why are you doing this? I just want to sleep. I can almost see the dark.
What is it?
Don't tell him, sister. It's too bad.
The... last dream?
And the air will smell of apricots...
I don't *want to* anymore. I don't want to think either one of those things.
...in hell and ancient sadness, brother. Ten thousand years later -- in front of the video rental. There is a warm breath on your face again. Everything is *okay* again.
Your eyelids flutter open for a moment. When you close them again, you sense the light of the room around you -- you're back. In two seconds the alarm will ring.
Everything is *so* okay.
Of hell and ancient sadness, brother. Ten thousand years later -- in front of the video rental. There is a warm breath on your face again. Everything is *okay* again.
I can't wait. I can't wait...
They're right. This is their function. To keep you from *it*.
The last thought in your head before waking is: you need to go to the church...
The last thought in your head before waking is: maybe you shouldn't have seen that stained glass window? In the church....

"Fuck it, let's go." The man points down the street. "Trant left his motor carriage behind the gates. It's a 20 minute drive to Jamrock."

Let's test. This is the last hub.
"Here are many options before leaving."
Let's test. This is the last hub.
"Good bye, then." (End alone.)
"Good bye, Harry. And -- I know it won't happen, but..." He looks at you, heart steeled and eyes cold.
"*If* you make it -- if you've been sober for 10 months -- tell us. I'll work with you again. But not like this. Never like this again. This is over."
Even now -- you're his colleague.

A grey rain falls on Martinaise. The city soaks in it, cold and dripping. Waves hit the concrete breakers. The homeless huddle by the fires behind the fences. There, among the shacks, is your home. Stay. Have a drink. Forever.
Despite all the thinking you've been doing, only 0.0001% of communism has been built. It's too great a task to undertake alone. You're going to have to *get organised*.
Does this mean I need to clean up my hostel room?
Judging from the state of my ledger, I don't think that’s possible.
I'm ready, let's get to it.
Your level of personal upkeep is irrelevant. All that matters is your commitment to *building the World Republic*.
You must seek out your revolutionary brothers and sisters. Find out how much communism they've built. Then, together, maybe you'll be able to build as much as 0.0002% of communism.
But it won't be *easy*. Decades of persecution by Coalition authorities have driven the remaining communists of Martinaise *underground*.
They live underground? These communists aren't men, they're *mole people*!
I don't know if I want to go searching for mole people.
But *I'm* part of the Coalition authorities! Have I been persecuting communists this whole time?
Will they help me fire up Mazov's Socialist Sausage Grinder?
How am I supposed to find them if they're hiding? (Proceed.)
They're not 'mole people', they're your comrades in the *eternal class struggle*. It's your task to find and join them.
Possibly? If you have been, it's only because you're a *double-agent*, acting in furtherance of your *long-term objectives*.
Just between us, you may want to lay off this 'grind up the bourgeoisie' stuff. It's a bit off-putting, even to fellow communists.
Let your *nose* guide you, detective.
My *nose*?
You must mean my *knows*, as in my huge and highly functioning brain.
Yes, fortunately communists are known to have a very *distinct* smell.
No, we meant your nose, as in that swollen muck-detector in the centre of your face. It just happens to be *perfectly* calibrated for sensing communists.
We really have no idea what they're talking about. There's no linkage between ideology and olfaction.
What does communism smell like?
Okay, I'm ready. Let's get organised.
This sounds unfathomably stupid. I want no part of it.
That's the spirit, comrade!
First, you'll have to locate the remaining communists in Martinaise. When you get near to someone with revolutionary potential your nose will give you the signal to *establish contact*.
Failure.
It's not *stupid*, it's the greatest endeavour in the history of human civilisation!
Well, if you say so. Guess I've got to get organised, then.
No, going around sniffing communists is definitely stupid. Forget about it. [Refuse task.]
Good luck explaining that to the Tribunal of Revolutionary Retribution.
There's so much failure in my life already -- I don't know if I can take any more.
Okay, but what does *failure* smell like?
That's why you're perfect for the job. No one's got a better nose for failure than you, detective.

It's a smell you know all too well. Simultaneously repulsive and yet darkly appealing. Musty with a sharp tang, but also a remnant of lost sweetness. Like a rotting mango that's been swaddled in a coat from your grandfather's attic...
What you're smelling is your own body odour, of course. Nothing a shower and change of clothes couldn't fix.
People sometimes complain there are no real communists left in Martinaise, but you can smell their presence. They're out there, waiting for you to join them!

Incidentally, during the waning days of the Antecentennial Revolution, a number of Revacholian communards constructed elaborate hideouts in abandoned root cellars, hollowed-out tree trunks, and even residential sewage tanks. This latter phenomenon gave rise to the early anti-communist slogan, 'The Future's Bright When You Flush Out the White!'
Again, no, it won't. Any olfactory response you perceive will be strictly psychosomatic.
Judging from the bust of Kras Mazov and other revolutionary paraphernalia you discovered, it seems that the Capeside Apartments may be a hotbed of communist activity.
You could also just look for more tangible evidence of communist activity. Images of Kras Mazov and white antlers are usually a dead giveaway.
You should begin by interrogating those lawless malcontents at the Dockworkers' Union. They're an obvious place to start.
Hang on, what will I do once I establish contact with my fellow communists?
(Roll up your sleeves.) Alright, let's get to it. [Accept task.]
On second thought, I have better things to do. [Refuse task.]

You'll discuss the monumental, world-historical task that lies before you. You'll engage in rigorous and spirited debates about Mazovian theory and practice. But mostly you'll probably complain about other communists.
Isn't that last part kind of counter-productive?
Not at all. Complaining about other communists is one of the most important parts of being a communist.
Here we go! 'Wake, brave worker! 'Tis no time for bed/ Fight till there's no slaves below, and no masters o'erhead.'
The condition of your paperwork is irrelevant. All that matters is your commitment to *building the World Republic*.
Have you engaged the shit compressor? This task won't permit any looseness on your part, mentally or physically...
Uh oh. Organisation hasn't exactly been your strong suit, historically speaking...
Have you *seen* my shit recently? I've really gotten it together.
It's good that your *personal* business is in order, but we're talking about political matters of world-historical import here.
Regardless, what's past is past. You need to look forward, to the work of building communism for all.
Listen to this. Do you really think you're the kind of person an underground communist cell would entrust with a mission that requires such discretion?
Maybe?
Hmm, probably not.
Rise and shine, comrade. It's time to get to work.
What's going on?
Not really my thing. [Discard thought.]
Good, you're up. Listen, there's something that's been bothering you for a few days now.
What is it?
It's a suspicion, or a feeling, really, that things are not quite *in hand* around here...
An earth-shattering deduction from your psyche. What will those guys come up with next?
Every day things seem to spin more and more wildly out of control. The centre isn't holding. And despite your efforts to *moderate* and *contain* these energies, things only seem to be getting worse.
Let's get right to it: What needs to be done?
Wait, I thought things were going pretty well?
Oh, sure. You've been making progress on your case, interviewing people, *solving side tasks*...
But who's focusing on *the big questions*?
You've got to find out who bears *la responsabilité*.
I assumed the most qualified and highly credentialed people were taking care of that stuff.
This really doesn't sound like my job.
What am I supposed to do?
But have you ever seen them? How do you know they're even there? More importantly, how do you know they aren't waiting for *your participation*?
Open your eyes. Stop getting distracted by details. It's time you started focussing on what really matters.
What exactly *is* la responsabilité?
I thought I *was* assigning responsibility, for the murder?
Alright, give it to me. *I'll* accept responsibility. (Proceed.)
The most awesome, terrible thing...
It is human nature to crave la responsabilité and to deny it. That's why it must be distributed across many different organisations, agencies, offices, and portfolios.
In other words, it must be diffused across the entire bureaucracy, so that no one can ever truly say *who is responsible for what*.
Harry, Harry. You're thinking about this too narrowly.
La responsabilité isn't concerned with trivial questions like *who killed who*. It's about the real issues: the human welfare index, the price of staple goods, the transition to real democracy...
Whoa, whoa, *whoa*. This isn't some kind of *dictatorship*. You can't simply seize la responsabilité for yourself. It must be given by a legitimate authority...
Like a committee.
You don't need no stinkin' committee. You're the Law.
But I'm the Law. Can't I just do it myself?
Do we really have time for all this?
And who should sit on this committee?
Sounds like too much responsibility for me. I don't want it.
Come on. You know in your lungs that true authority flows from institutions, not individuals. That's the single principle that separates civilisation from barbarism.
Technicalities.
If you want your work to be *accepted*, you'll have to go through the appropriate process.
There is always time to follow best practices. Once someone's decided to *cut corners* for the sake of expediency, who knows what else they're capable of?
Fun stuff, that's what they're capable of.
Only the most even-keeled minds in Martinaise.
Your half-brother, the lieutenant, is a natural place to start.
The one you seem so set on driving away, the lieutenant, is a natural place to start.
Together, you'll be able to discover who has la responsabilité in Revachol. And if necessary, you'll have the *wisdom and expertise* to assign it among yourselves.
And what happens once we've assigned responsibility?
I'm prepared to take on this awesome burden. [Accept task.]
You know what, this sounds like a drag. [Refuse task.]
Most likely your findings will be collected in a report, which will be carefully reviewed by your superiors.
Good luck. Your report is eagerly anticipated.
Once they've reviewed it, those same superiors will produce a set of recommendations to be taken up at the next meeting of the *standing committee*.
Rest assured, no matter what happens it will be done through the proper channels.
Don't run away from it now, Harry. You know it's the *right thing to do*.
This is a grave abdication of la responsabilité. A note will be appended to your personnel file.
(Sigh.) You're right. Who's going to sit on this committee?
No way. I've got too much on my plate as it is. [Opt out.]
Please, you're thinking about this too narrowly.
MASS EXECUTIONS.
A little self-dealing?
Swift, decisive action.
Not my problem. [Discard thought.]
Hey, money-mouth. Eendracht. The impeccable hustler-provider of the seventh generation. It's showtime with Savvy!
Are we finally going to solve the lynching?
Do I know you?
Eendracht? The hustler-provider? The *seventh* generation?!
Not today, thanks. [Discard thought.]
Oh, so now it's Savvy? What's up, buddy?
What's up? I'm worried about what's *down*, broke boy. I'm talking about your severe lack of money.
You will. I'm here to make your life better. They call me the Man-About-Town. Gilded Heart-Throb. Master of Money.
What? No, screw that shit-show. You're at the centre of this one. Come on down, contestant, you're about to make some *money*.
Yeah, swindle-father. Papa-preneur. Look, this is serious. No time for distractions. It's time to make *money*. Lots of it.
Money?!
I know all about money.
That's right! It's time to stop muttering about your 'economic self-interest' and actually do something about it. Yeah, I heard you back there. What the hell was that?!
No, you don't! You just keep muttering about your 'economic self-interest' and not doing anything about it. Yeah, I heard you back there. What the hell was that?!
Superstar talk. Don't try to keep up with me and my vast dreams.
What do you expect? I'm an ultraliberal. I speak ultraliberal-ese.
I'm just tired of being a low-net-worth-individual. It must be *the curse*.
You said before that playing the market could get me *rich*.
Superstar talk? Good one, hustler, gotta keep the dream alive. But it's not really showing up in your net worth yet, is it? And it's what -- day two, three, four?
Good, good, gotta spread the gospel. But talk alone doesn't bring in the cash. It's time for step two.

Did Ilona Wihuri-Vilakone blame ghosts? How about Admiral Gustav Lestock? Samir Loisir grew up in the coal mines of Gurdi eating dirt, and he still managed to make FIFTY-FIVE BILLION REÁL in his lifetime. So stop with the excuses.
Oh, it can. But first you need to *enter* the market. Right now you're as good as Samir Loisir eating dirt in Gurdi's immense network of mines.
It's day four if we're counting days since the *event*.
Listen, if you really want to make it in the big leagues, you need to *re-conceptualize* your entire portfolio. Collecting tare and moaning about taxes is not going to cut it.
Fifty-five billion reál is a gross overestimation and we're pretty sure eating dirt is going to send any kid to a hospital, even Samir Loisir.

Samir Loisir was a Gurdi businessman who made his first millions selling kilograms of the ultra-rare mineral phasium to luxury jeweller Zachaël et Cie. He made the rest of his many millions through wise investments and the invention of pleochroic lights.
Does this giant check that Evrart gave me help?
Mañana flicked me a coin.
I assume begging rich ladies on boats is not the correct answer.
I could sell Kim's motorcar, like I sold his spinners?
I could pitch another project to this Mega Rich Light-Bending Guy in the container?
Really, that's it? That's all I have to say? Why aren't *you guys* helping me out?
Alright, I give up -- I have no idea how to make millions.
Not unless you have thousands of them stuffed away in secret.
*One* coin. The first of many. Imagine so many coins you're going to need to hire someone to help you manage all your wealth.
It should be the other way around. Old mitred money showing up at your doorstep, begging for a slice of cake.
And then what? Join the ranks of blue-collar criminals?
We're getting somewhere. But what project? And what's the ROI?

Those guys? They're all financially illiterate. Only Savvy here knows how to *dazzle* and *embezzle* money out of investors' pockets with the acrobatic prowess of a four-time gold medallist in the Samaran Gymnastic Summer Games.
Of course you don't. You've never even been *close* to a sum with more than three zeros. Let's face it, you've been on a years-long losing streak...
The ancient Samaran tribes used carved rhodochrosite to represent their wealth. The bigger the boulder, the more money they had. In case you needed to know.
Money is only one form of capital, *human relations* are another. You're focusing on the wrong things.
You could force a coin *inside* you? Any hole will do. Not many more definitive tests of a man's mettle than the fortune yawn.

But Savvy's got your back. Savvy's going to book you a charter flight with eighty birds of prey on board, to a land where the streets are paved with krugerrands and fixed-income securities. You'll try again, but this time with *money*. You'll win her back.
Are you in?
Wait, win *whom* back?
I've hustled, I've *grinded*. Show me the millions. (Opt in.)
Something about this doesn't sit right...
The spirit of ultraliberalism. Your charm, your spin, your winning hand.

Attaboy, welcome to the final grind! Here we operate with money on a *much* higher level than the ordinary citizen, we feed it back into the machine. Stop saving, start spending -- become a *patron*...
Stop grumbling, it's time to move. Are you in or are you out?
Let's start by getting you into the lucrative art market to diversify your assets and increase your ROI. Speaking of which, know any artists?
Actually I'm good on the money front. [Opt out.]
Suit yourself and your middle-class ways -- Savvy doesn't need you, Savvy's got his own *entourage*.
Perfect, all you have to do is *pretend* to have taste. This will be your weapon when swindling artists for their overpriced 'work'.
Interesting. Are we speaking of visual art or something more *conceptual*?

Somewhere in La Delta, numbers flip and whirl on the giant split-flap boards of the stock exchange, marking gains the size of Kemi SR's entire economy. Radiocomputers hum below to the tune of gambling.
Hold on, I thought we'd be getting into the stock market?
Wait, so we're looking for a painting?
Good thing I've been preparing for this with my Actual Art Degree.
Artists, artists... I'm an artist myself.
Cindy seems the type.
What about the speedfreaks' anodic dance music?

dialoguetext: Cuno? Cuno is an artist.
No one comes to mind.

Do you see any stock markets in Martinaise? No? That's because for those living in the outskirts, the market is *nothing*. Just ghost numbers flicking through time. A spectral sport they're not invited to play.
Stop thinking of it that way. It's not a 'painting', it's a 'highly collectible and irreproducible asset'. So, know any local artists with assets to sell?
Don't be silly, the art market isn't about art, it's about gate-keeping, speculative bidding, and showboating.
Once we've brought in the millions you can be a tree log for all I care, but first we've got to work on increasing your net worth.
You're right. She has the poise of a struggling artist. Very *tangible*. You can *feel* the poverty on her. Plus, she has paint.
Music is a pet project, not a viable business scheme. Let's return to it once you've set up your estate.
He's also twelve. We don't want to attract the attention of tax collectors by dabbling in unnecessary child-labour.

By all accounts this place should be *swarming* with artist-types. It's just a matter of time until you meet one. Look for squats and cheap rentals, we might even chance upon a *political artivist* here.
Go and support them like the state never could. Everyone must know that you're a big fucking shark around here!
Go and support her like the state never could. Everyone must know that you're a big fucking shark around here!
What is this, the turn of the century? The world's moved beyond paintings. You want something *experimental* -- intramuscular puppetry, hyperrealistic vapour-porn, meditation opera...
Don't listen to this fool. It's not about the artists, it's about the *buyers*. You can't hang 'vapour-porn' in the foyer of your chalet.
It is but a symptom of the rapacious catastrophe that will devour us all.
I was asleep.
It's pathetic -- I know. Sorry you have to hang around with me. I'll do better.
That child's a common delinquent, not an artist. He probably can't even hold a paint brush.
He does have potential... defying authority, thinking outside the box...
Brilliant, catastrophes are *prime time* for money-makers. But you're not really reaping any benefits yet, are you? No shorting, no shameless speculation...
Exactly. Not making money when you're asleep, are you? If you wanna be rich you better work until your fingers bleed. You can sleep when you die.
No, don't you ever be sorry. You think the Salzneben Report's Top 500 has 'sorry' in their vocabulary? Think again. That's a loser's mindset.
Take heed of these wise words. *You're* in charge. 'Sorry' is a beggar's plea reserved for those beneath you.
(Your pecs dance.) No more sleep it is. A frazzled ride through eternity without pause. Hissing pistons pushed to the extreme.
Just take my money and leave me alone!
Alright, then. Show me the millions. (Opt in.)
No, you need something *real*, something you can hold on to with all your claws and teeth.
You need to become a MILLIONAIRE. Now, how do you become a MILLIONAIRE?
You were right, bröther. (There's a sudden tightness in your lower intestine.)
What? What's going on?
Back there, in your sleep. All the weak-willed delinquents, dilly-dalliers, foreign moneylenders, insane anarchists, and yes -- the wöömen -- they've run this place to ruin.
What's going on with my gut, did I not *eat* enough?
I *do* feel like everything's gone to shit...
No, bröther, forget about your gut, we've got much more pressing matters to focus on. It’s time to *turn back time*. (A solemn gurgle emanates from the depths of your stomach.)
It has, bröther, but we are going to turn back time! (A solemn gurgle emanates from your stomach.)
I will send you back to the time when the sun had not yet vanished, when it was still setting into the sea. The time of the Suzerain, the time when love was still possible.
Even if it was possible, what would it accomplish?
I'm not sure if I'm *feeling it*.
Think of all the possibilities... I want this.
I like it just fine right here, right now. [Discard thought.]
But just imagine... to go back with the knowledge and the experience you now have and do it all over. Do it *richtig* this time?
To go back with the knowledge and the experience you have now and do it all over? Do it *richtig* this time?
Protect the Suzerainty, clean up the city, revive disco music, and get her back? You could save Revachol. You could be the *man*, bröther.
Her?
Wait, get who back?
No one, don't ask about her.
Okay, how do we do this?
Yeah... I think I'm gonna let this one slide.
You fool!
Second chances are not about questions, they are about actions. Are you ready to start taking action, bröther?
Ultramarathon here meant Revachol. Our streets and all that. It's all there is. Just move on and answer the question.
There must be others like you. Men, who long for the days when words like 'loyalty' and 'love' meant something.
Love is shit, loyalty is meaningless.
People whose yearning for the past is so great they barely live in the present. Those are the men you need to find. Those are the guys who'd know.
You want to give up on redemption? *Revanche?* On Revachol?! I had you for a kingsman, bröther.
A chill runs down your spine when you hear the name of your light -- Revachol...
Well, if it's for Revachol... (Continue.)
You had me wrong. [Opt out.]
Wait, one of them could easily be a woman.
Wait, couldn't one of them be a girl?
So how do I find these men?
Think. Maybe you've already met someone like that?
Don't be ridiculous. They are all men, trust me.
No one misses the good old days like René.

"You must be Morell, the cryptozoologist?"

"Lena sent me. She's been really worried about you and is waiting for you to get back."

His self-conscious enthusiasm renders his movements ungainly. He looks like your understanding of a scientist.
"I hope you haven't been littering here. This is unspoiled wilderness."
"Well..." He points at the cage of mesh and wiring on the ground. "They may not *look* impressive, but Lena designed them quite cleverly, so I'm sure they'll do the trick."

"Yes?"
"I didn't expect you to take such an interest in our work here, officer." He looks at you with obvious surprise.
"So it *was* just a child..." He purses his lips, crestfallen.
"*Completely* empty?" The cryptozoologist's eyes grow wide.

"At least, that's the intention. The net isn't a perfect solution, but we didn't want to use anything that might damage the specimen's delicate exoskeleton."
"Cryptozoology and detective work are very similar."
"We're looking for someone hiding on this very coast. Looking for *another* thing may lead us to her."
"Chaos is my method. I am its scion."
"Yes, indeed! Both require a great deal of research, attention to detail, and, above all, *persistence*."
"Sometimes it's helpful to take a break and return to one's *primary pursuit* with fresh eyes." He nods.
"Well..." He doesn't know what to say. "Be that as it may, I'd really appreciate the help!"

His companion sighs. "Another trip to the reeds..."

He takes the dangers and discomforts that come with his work for granted, but just imagine the unforgiving desert heat he's endured, the wetlands filled with venomous reptiles he has crossed...
I'm the most rugged of men. That sounds like my kind of fun.
I don't know how he does it. I *already* want a bath.

Be careful where you tread in the reeds. Some less conscientious researchers may have left their traps out there -- armed, hidden.

The man surveys the cold coast. "I have a feeling the only people foolish enough to spend their time skulking among the reeds are these poor fools... and us. But fine. It's not like we're drowning in leads."
"Is it?" he doesn't look too convinced but the small shrug indicates -- why not?
"Even relative to examining a week-old corpse, I'm not sure mucking about in the reeds qualifies as *fun*... but have it your way, detective..."

He seems reluctant to talk about himself, but he'll open up -- if you prod a little.
"Why not just be a zoologist? Real animals are puzzling too."

"I have to resist the thought." He shakes his head vigorously. "Such an extraordinary creature is doubtlessly *highly resilient*. After all, it's generally thought to be capable of parthenogenesis."
He means asexual reproduction. The females of the species don't need to mate to produce viable eggs. This makes it easier for a species with a small population to survive.
"Par...the...no...genesis?"
"Yes. The females don't need males to reproduce. Makes it easier for a species to survive in adverse conditions."
"Females reproducing without males!? A travesty. A crime against passion *and* common sense."
"The male is a deficient life form. The world would be better off if women didn't need men to reproduce."
"That's pretty clever!"
"Nature does not concern herself with ethical propositions. As a scientist, my interest is *strictly dispassionate*."
"*Real*..." He scoffs at the concept. "I know you think one is a respectable profession while the other is superstition, everyone does!"
"Cryptozoology does seem like a lot of wishful thinking."
"My methods are the same as those of other scientists, I simply draw upon a wider variety of evidence, and I have more hope that something truly surprising might happen."
"And has anything 'truly surprising' ever happened to you?"
"Life's surprises are mostly miserable."
"Agreed. Yet there is always a chance, albeit a small one, of a truly *good* surprise. One simply needs to look at the history of science -- serendipities abound!"
"I have yet to *catch* a cryptid, if that's what you're getting at, but I have come close."
"So you're living your childhood dream out here."
"It's not child's play just because I have to traipse through the mud every so often." His eyes narrow.
It's probably this way of thinking that got you where you are.
It could be worse. So much worse.
"Everything from forgotten regional lore to newspaper accounts like the one that brought us here to look for the phasmid. I keep a very open mind."
He's interested in things that people believe that scientists don't.

"Yes, the Insulindian phasmid is a *very* clever insect -- that's why it's so damn difficult to catch! But as a scientist, I try my best to remain dispassionate."
"What makes you think the phasmid is here in Martinaise?"
"It's the first credible sighting in several decades. Admittedly, it's an unusual location for this species, but with all the sewage run-off upstream, it probably doesn't matter much anymore."
"There was a credible sighting here recently. A pair of teenagers described a creature that matched the Insulindian phasmid to an *uncanny* degree, *despite* not knowing what it was themselves."
"Who's there? Oh, the police. Hello, officers."
"Who's there? Oh, the police. Hello, officer."

"*And*, I suspect it may also have developed other *specialized techniques* to protect itself from predators... or scientists, in our present case."
"Very little, I'm sorry to say. No one's ever captured a specimen, so all our information is based on first- and third-hand accounts."

"Lena seems pretty eager for you to return."
