"Why are you so interested in this stick bug? It doesn't seem to be as colourful as some of the other cryptids I've heard about."
"Typical rookie assumption." He flashes you a sideways smile. "Insects are much more sophisticated creatures than those unversed in zoology give them credit for."

"Even simply catching a glimpse of the Insulindian phasmid would be the apex of my -- of *any* -- cryptozoologist's career. But to study it and its defences, find out how it's stayed hidden so long..." He shakes his head.
The traps do seem to be deftly and thoughtfully constructed. It's clear the cryptozoologist's wife knows what she's doing.
Won't *let Lena down*? Sounds like the cryptozoologist's wife shares a *special connection* to the phasmid somehow...
"Suffice to say, it's long been our dream to find proof of the Insulindian phasmid *together*. I can't abandon course now." Another cough, into his fist this time.
"Maybe you could go back to the Whirling, warm up, come back to check the traps *later*?"
"You should just give up on this bug hunt."
"No, no, no. The traps need to be monitored on a regular schedule. What would we do if the phasmid were to *starve* while we were sipping tea at the hostel?"
"*Give up*? After we've come so far? Not a chance!"
You're dealing with a subject near and dear to their hearts. It might behove you to tread *lightly*.
"Wait, Morell..." the old woman raises a hand. "He may have a point. We have an obligation to rule out other hypotheses..."
"You're right, dear." His face relaxes. "It's a fair point. But what other explanation could there be?" He turns to you.
But whose?
"Maybe it was a *different* cryptid who took the bugs?"
"Okay. I've been thinking and I'm just not sure that it was the *phasmid* that took the locusts."
"A *different* cryptid?" The cryptozoologist furrows his heavy brow.
"Really, officer, we can take it from here." The cryptozoologist furrows his heavy brow.
"Oh, sweetie. Maybe you should stick to human detective work?"
"Yes, sweetie, we've already taken too much of your time."
"Oh, you've been such a dear to us. Please, let us know whatever you turn up. I have a feeling we're getting *so* close!"
"Delinquents -- my favourite." It doesn't sound like it's really his favourite.
There's no mystery here. You've seen the Locust City and its spiralling mud towers. All that's left is to confront the city father himself...
"I'm pretty sure it was Cuno who took the locusts. He's built a whole city for them in his shack."
"What the devil is a Cuno? And why would he be making a *city of bugs*?"
The ageing cryptozoologist breaks into a hideous coughing fit.
He has a 38 degree fever. His resilience has given way.
She looks at him with tender concern. "Darling, I told you to take it easy. You're getting sick. Maybe it's time to go home?"
"You're right, you're right..." He breathes carefully, not to start coughing again. "We can come back next season... when it's warmer..."
"It's not worth risking your health. You should call it a day and go home." (Refuse.)
"I'd offer to help, but I have my own things to do." (Refuse.)
"Damnit, maybe I can still restock the trap for you?" (Accept.)
"He's right, dear Morell. Come now, we've waited so long, what's one more season?"
Self-deceit, sire.
"You're right, dear. We'll get our shot yet, I'm sure of it..."
The slouch in his shoulders tells you otherwise. He doesn't know how many more field expeditions he has left in him...
"Of course, sweetie. We couldn't ask you to do more than you already have. Come now, Morell, we've waited so long, what's one more season?"
"You *can*?" The lieutenant makes a show of suppressing a sigh. "Fine. It's better than having these people get pneumonia on the coast, but after *this*..."
"What Morell means is, we're grateful for your help." She nods to her husband.
"Really, it's too much, officer..." He starts coughing again.

"Here's a fresh batch of locusts. They should slide right down the funnel. And thank you again. We will definitely mention you, should this lead to a discovery. I'm not talking co-discovery, of course, but..."
"This place is *much* better for field work in the summer, believe me."
"What sorts of *specialized techniques* is the phasmid using to hide itself?"
"It's my hypothesis that it has evolved certain electro-chemical defences that allow it to interfere with animal perception -- impeding pattern recognition, confusing the visual cortex."
Yes, it makes perfect sense. You're beginning to suspect there's something *para-natural* about this phasmid.
"How big is this phasmid?"
"I'm expecting it to be quite giant. One known species of phasmid, called the *megaphasmodea zhouensis*, is about the size of a grown man's forearm. So..." He leaves the conclusion up to you.
"Lena said there has been a sighting of it, here in Martinaise."
"Yes, the most *recent* sighting was by a couple of teenagers along the coast here. That's what brought us to Martinaise specifically."
There's nothing *dispassionate* about the way he talks about the insect.
His spirit may be willing, but his body might be too old to endure the rigours of the coast.
He wants to see this tale through as much as *you*. Otherwise he'd have stopped this already. But he *cannot* let it drag out after this.
"Why are you so interested in this stick bug? Aren't there more sensational animals out there?"
"Khm..." The lieutenant interjects. "Just out of curiosity -- if there's no proof of its existence, how do you know it's real?"
"Got it. Parthonosis."
"Parthe-no-genesis. Meaning the females don't need males to reproduce. Makes it easier for a species to survive in adverse conditions."
"Lena designed the traps?"
"Yes," he says with some pride.
"Yes. What?"
Inside the traps, a number of locusts crawl and tumble over one another in a tiny, chittering swarm.
A meat-eating stick insect? Does it pretend to be the reeds as part of it's ambush behaviour? This seems unlikely.
"A carnivorous stick insect? Seems unlikely."
"Thank you for your opinion. We have also included plant material in the traps -- to satiate your *scepticism*."
Not a big fan of scepticism, this one.
"By *wöman* you mean my wife, I assume. I will return to her -- but I can't leave before we've finished with these traps."
"My wife understands that just as well as anyone." He looks south -- where Lena would be.
"I didn't know the phasmid was so important to Lena."
"Okay. I understand. I don't give up on things either."
"Good. A good quality to have -- both for a police officer *and* an experimental zoologist."
"Of course it's important to her, she's *seen* it. A verified sighting, on record, one of only four this century and it's hers."
"Really? She's *sighted* the phasmid? She didn't tell me that."
"Really? She's *sighted* the phasmid?"
"Yes. That's... how we first came to know one another, in fact. But that's *her* story to tell, not mine." He coughs, then continues...
He's dead set on this.
...would be *glory* itself.
"I'm *all in* with this cryptid shit. I'm hooked."
"That it will." The man cracks an unwieldy smile. "That it *absolutely* will. I hope you brought your good boots."
"Caught the bug, I see." He cracks an unwieldy smile. "It's easier to get caught up in the *search* than you'd imagine."
"My partner was joking," he says, unsure of himself. "We're on a search of our own. It wouldn't hurt to check the reeds while we're at it... I assume that's what we'll be doing?"
"Oh yes, officer. Very much so. The traps are all in the reeds -- that is where we expect the phasmid to prowl."
"There are four in total. One is to the south, on this little peninsula -- by the boat houses there." He points south. "It's very near."
"You should check at least one of those before returning to *this* one, since I just set it. This one's more of a *technicality*, but still... better safe and stupid than sorry."
"Another we set in Land's End, to the northeast. It's behind a small sand dune there, on your way to the old radio tower. After the church."
"The third is set near the canal, where you crossed. By a concrete slab. A big thicket of reeds going up the slope, and among them..." He gestures to the trap in front of him.
If you think it's important -- you *have* been right before.

"It *is* precious. A single dose cost me 50 reál to develop. Not that I expect *you* to understand self-financing one's own research." He looks at the lieutenant with disdain, then puts the spray back in his pocket.
He douses you with the odd-smelling spray and then gives you a satisfied nod.
"Lay it on me."
"Lay it on me -- thick." (Present your arm pit.)
"I don't want this, thank you very much."
He douses you with the odd-smelling spray -- a double helping as you present your other arm pit -- and then gives you a satisfied nod.
"Your choice." He puts the spray back in his pocket. "As I said, the chances of you encountering the phasmid are next to zero."
But you... you *feel* you should have it on you. Something bad might happen.
"I don't. It's a profession, just like any other."
"Honestly -- being a cryptozoologist trumps most of the garbage I've seen people do."
"Hmh," a hum and a nod. "My methods do not differ from other scientists, I simply draw upon a wider variety of evidence, and I have more hope that something truly surprising might happen."
"Indeed. My methods do not differ from other scientists, I simply draw upon a wider variety of evidence, and I have more hope that something truly surprising might happen."
"Have you ever discovered a cryptid?"
"No. Very few cryptids are ever discovered -- and not for a lack of trying. To stay hidden is a cryptid's primary quality. It's even in the *name* cryptid."
"So how many cryptids have been found?"
"Of the list of cryptids kept by the Cryptozoological Society of Chemnie, which is four thousand and eighty two items long, about two thousand have been confirmed as hoaxes."
"Two are categorized as 'confirmed discoveries'. The rest are in differing stages of discovery, refutation, and data collection."
"Only *two* have proven to be real?"
"Yes -- the Shautauquan forest pygmy who turned out to be an extinct species of primate; and a cave salamander from Yugo-Graad, who is... honestly quite unremarkable. It's in a zoo somewhere..."
"We cryptozoologists are brutally honest with ourselves, more so even than the public. Most cryptids are hoaxes or they are never found. That does not mean we should stop searching."
"Two out of four thousand is not even *one* percent!"
(Nod approvingly.) "Then the Insulindian phasmid will be the *third*."
"I don't even know what to say. That's a small number of discoveries."
"In fact -- it is 0.05%. Ever more magnificent, should our search contribute to making that number 0.075%!"
He has clearly done his math on this. There is no surprising him -- or swaying his opinion.

"Do you know what the success rate in pharmacological research is? 0.000003% of bio-reactive agents have reproducibly beneficial effects. Yet science persists in the search for medicine. *As* we persist in our search for new species."

"Indeed." He does not smile, just looks you in the eye. It's a forceful gaze. "If our expedition is successful, every paper in the world will report on it. From Revachol to Doushantou -- it will be a zoological miracle."
The hair on your arms stands up... electricity. Sounds like reeds hissing.
The lieutenant takes a short note in his notebook, then gestures for you to proceed.
He tries to play it cool -- remain professorial -- but inside, this man is itching for some news on those *traps*.
"Good, okay..." He breaks his calm. "*And?*"
"And one of them was *empty*."
"Nothing. Nothing. Maybe I didn't check them after all..."
"Sweetie, you'll give Morell a heart attack. This is no laughing matter for us..."
"I'm fine, Lena..." He coughs. "And I definitely won't have a heart attack. Rather a cough fit..."
Surprise -- tempered with fear and trepidation. He doesn't know what to think yet. Maybe you're joking?
"No but really -- I *did* check all the traps."
"Yes-yes -- *and*?"
"Yes. That's *exactly* what it is. What a deft hunter, this phasmid!"
"Of course -- be *sarcastic*." He misinterprets your words. "Unless you have an *alternative* hypothesis you'd like to venture, mine stands, okay?"

"Actually, no..." His tone changes. "Excuse me for getting emotional, this is a big deal for us. You've helped us *twice* now -- and brought some great news, too. My gratitude, *and* the gratitude of the Société Cryptozoologique de Revachol, is yours."
"Pardon me. This is... a big deal for us. You've helped us *twice* now -- and brought great news too. My gratitude, *and* the gratitude of the Société Cryptozoologique de Revachol, is yours."
Heartfelt gratitude -- but does it feel like closure? What *really* happened?
"Thank you for the vote of no-confidence, Gary. And *officer*, I appreciate your concern, but please leave this to the *experts*. Unless you have an *alternative* hypothesis you'd like to venture..."
"Really, Gary?" The woman's voice is a little shaky suddenly. "We're *getting* somewhere here. I'd love to play 'Suzerainty', but..."

"Lena, I'm sorry, but you're not *getting* anywhere, it was some kids. I know the little mutants around here -- leave anything out in the open and they'll steal it. Even if it's bugs." He looks at his tea.
"Morell, it's been fun, really. But I need a bath and I have deliveries to handle. When this tea is done, I gotta run."
"No-no. No need to apologize, Gary. You've been more than helpful. We'll have to take a rain check on that game of 'Suzerainty' today though -- we're gonna follow this through."
He keeps the language unemotional but it's in there -- disappointment.
The first man to break formation is always a blow to leadership. This is bigger than he lets on.
"We've come too far to quit. I'm gonna restock the trap. Lets *do* this." (Accept enthusiastically.)
"We're getting *really* carried away with this, aren't we?" He makes a show of suppressing a sigh. "Fine, it's better than having these people get pneumonia on the coast. But after this..."
"Man, I'm really feeling this is costing me time on my main investigation..."
"Of course, sweetie, you've helped us so much already. Everyone would understand if you..."
Wow! Co-discovery? You'd be famous. You'd show them all. This *does* tingle the pleasure centre...
This would *show* them all. We need to get you on that list of discoverers, no question about that.
A *ghost insect*, he said? These people are looking for a ghost.
"Ghost insect... so you're ghost hunters."
"No -- that is precisely what we're *not*. We are zoological specialists, looking for an extant species of phasmid."
Seems puny, to be honest.
"This arouses no special feelings in me."
"And it shouldn't. Nature does not concern herself with ethical propositions. As a scientist, my interest is *strictly dispassionate*."
More than some. He admires this about her.
Hmm... I could go for some trap-setting.
"I've changed my mind. Spray me with lots of pheromone." (Present your arm pit)
"It's truly not that special. What is *cryptozoology* anyway? A derogative. I just like puzzles, like any scientist."
Hmmm... interesting. Something for later. This close call.
"C'mon. You're doing this for yourself, not her."
"I'm doing this for *science*. And so is she."
Some kind of foul play might be afoot. Theft?
"Thank you, it's an honour," he says with a straight face, then turns to you. "We should probably return to our *main* investigation here. This has been refreshing, but..."
...helping cryptozoologists isn't really a priority for our organization, is it? The lieutenant looks out the window, impatiently.
Dammit lieutenant, have you no intellectual curiosity?
After this is your last chance to talk to Gary.
There won't be a next season. Not for this. Find the phasmid or admit defeat, people.
That's just something people tell themselves when they fail.
Is that a pang of sadness, lieutenant?
"Thank you dear." She bows to the lieutenant -- then turns to you. "And you, detective Fox..." A sad smile. "You've been great company to an old lady and her stubborn husband."
"You're right, Lena. The RCM is worth their salt -- more so than they say on the radio."
"See you around, wheels."
"Good bye, Lena."
"I live to serve." (Tip an imaginary police hat.)
Just nod.
"Good bye." She smiles and they leave -- two old cryptozoologists and one gas-powered wheelchair.
"You too -- Morell? Let's roll?" She smiles and they leave -- two old cryptozoologists and one gas-powered wheelchair.
"And you, detective." She turns to you with a sad smile. "You've been great company to an old lady and her stubborn husband. Thank you, truly."
More cardio? Let's *do* this.
"Thank you for telling us, sweetie." She turns to smile gently up at her husband. "This is good news, right? It means we can try *again*."
"Thank you for telling us, sweetie." She turns to smile gently up at her husband. "This is good news, right? It means we can try *again*."
She acts chipper, but something's changed in her tone. A hidden worry.
Something is secretly gnawing at her confidence. It's not this Cuno kid, or the missing locusts, it's something else.
"Ack! Of course. Thank you for passing along the message. That damned water lock is broken, and we can't go all the way around the 8/81..."
"Ack, so that's what this is." He ignores your jab. "Lena sent you. Can't say I blame her -- we've been here for days. That damned water lock is broken, and we can't go under the 8/81..."
"But I cannot describe how these defences work -- much less how they evolved -- without studying a live specimen."
Your nerve endings tell you there is no such thing as a *positive* surprise.
If it's more cryptid-related business you want to discuss, you'll have time for that later too.
But what if the information is vital -- on *the hunt*...
"The empty trap was the one at your campsite. Maybe this factors into it somehow?"
"Right from the camp site..." The old woman's face lights up. "It just means the Insulindian phasmid is even more clever than we thought!"
"I definitely left that one stocked. Hmm..."
"I found the locusts in a nearby shack. Some kid's built a city of them."
"What the devil is a Cuno? And why would he be making a *city of bugs*?"
"What the devil... Why would kids be making a *city of bugs*?"
A shadow of worry passes over the woman's face. "Oh, my dear Morell. You've been an old man for too long. Kids love to torment insects, almost as much as they love to torment old folks..."
"I'll talk to the kids, ask them to stop. It's probably the two kids in the yard near the shack."
"Oh, you've been such a dear to us. Please, let us know. If the kids can stop hampering us... I have a feeling we're getting *so* close!"
"Did *you* know Gary was hiding the armour?"
"Have you noticed anything *off* about your friend Gary?"

dialoguetext: "Hell no, I had no idea. And I'm still cross with him to be honest. It's not like him. He's got his quirks, but dishonesty -- or disloyalty -- are not one of them."
"Thanks," the man mutters in the distance. He doesn't dare say more.
He's still glad his friend stood up for him.
"I don't know what got into him, officer... Thank you for letting him off easy. He won't forget it; we'll make sure he won't."
"Huh? No. No, of course not. Why?"
"Are you sure?"
"Well..." He lowers his voice. "He's been a little unenthusiastic about the trip. More so than usual. But that's understandable. He just wants to get home and warm up."
He doesn't want to say it, but this *is* unusual. Gary's been to the jungle with him -- to places *way* more challenging than the coast. Why so eager to go home?
She's *seen* it?
Needless to say, you *must* ask her about the mysterious phasmid.
Uhm...
Don't mess around, take the pheromone, it'll make you sexier.
What about his eager-to-leave friend Gary there? Talk to him too, perhaps.
A sigh. She doesn't think you'll need it.
"Okay, it's 1113 Tabernacle Road. Jamrock, but..."
"Wait, can I have your address? In case there's news."
"Hello! I'm Gary. How do you do, officer?"
"Always a pleasure to see an officer of the law!"
"I mean…" He turns toward Kim. "Officers."
"Yes, officer?"
"Thank you for your cooperation." [Leave.]
"Are you a cryptozoologist too?"
Why's he shifting around like that? Analyze Gary's composure.
"What's that strange sound?"
"No-no... I help Morell with research sometimes and I've learned some things along the way. But I don't usually go in for picnics like this on my own."
"I'm into cryptids. Do you have a favourite?"
"What do you do, then? If not cryptozoology?"
"Fascinating. Let's talk about something else."
"Oh, yes! The Burning Rhino. Morell doubts he's real, but I don't much care -- because I won't be the one looking for him out in Safre Serai."
"What's a Burning Rhino?"
"Yellow Man!" He turns toward Kim. "I mean... officer."
"Oh, this and that." He grins.
"You were *surprised* to see my colleague, Lieutenant Kitsuragi."
"Not many Seolites here, or anywhere, other than Seol. I meant no offence, truly."
"Do you have a problem with Seolites?"
"Because they're not really human, right?"
"Yes. What *are* they doing in that Seol of theirs? Scheming?"
"A rhinoceros that looks ordinary during the day, but burns brightly by night. Well, at least the males do."
"How do they burn?"
"Why only the males?"
"They have special ducts just above their shoulder blades that secrete a combustible fluid. When the rhino is just beginning to light itself, it looks as though it has wings of fire."
But how is this combustible fluid lit?
"The rhino starts running very fast to build heat, then stops, raises its head -- and sparks fly from its neck, setting its back ablaze."
"How does the lighting of this... fluid actually work?"
"This seems unlikely."
"I want to be just like that rhino, running through the night with guns blazing!"
"Perhaps we should have more such *decisive action* in Revachol. You know -- this city used to be flaming rhino once, a long time ago..." he says and then pauses, thoughtfully.
"We don't really do that around here."
"Yeah, well -- Revachol used to be flaming rhino once, a long time ago..." he says and then pauses, thoughtfully. "That seems unlikely too, doesn't it?"
"The flames are not just for decoration. They are an integral part of the beast's mating behaviour."
"How so?"
"During the Burning Rhino's mating season, herds of male rhinos, all aflame, encircle herds of female rhinos, forming a fiery ring as they begin to copulate, loudly."
The lieutenant sighs without looking up from his notes.
"Local peasants call it the Passion Ring. They fear the rhinos. As, perhaps, they should. Anyway..."
"Sounds intriguing."
"Sounds shady."
"As long you're making ends meet and advancing your career objectives."
"Sometimes."
"That's not an answer."
"I just didn't want to bore you with unnecessary detail, officer."
"Officer, I would never. I just didn't want to bore you with unnecessary detail."
"I'm doing all I can in this economy, officer."
The lieutenant looks up at you, sighs, and goes back to his notes.
The lieutenant looks up at you, almost sadly.
"No, no problem at all." He flashes an impenetrable smile at the lieutenant.
"You said you'd tell me about Seolites, when Kim isn't here. He isn't here."
"That's not what I was implying at all..." He eyes the lieutenant nervously. "But, of course, you're just kidding, officer."
"The lieutenant is a native of Revachol."
"Oh, yes, of course he is. I was just speaking about his... connections." He flashes an impenetrable smile. "Let's change the subject, okay?"
"Yes, officer. I'm very glad we're getting a chance to speak about it candidly, man to man."
His smile, meant to convey total openness, is that of an experienced salesman.
"I'm listening."
"Get on with it, then."
"I'm not sure I like where this is heading, but I'm willing to hear you out."
"Well, the Seolites -- they're a very smart people. Smart and secretive. Most think they have isolated themselves on their landmass because they disdain to mingle with the rest of us..."
"I'm not saying that *you* think that too. You seem like an incisive man, officer. You must be, being a detective."
"Yes, sir, I'm a regular Dick Mullen. But better, because I'm *real*."
"I don't know how good of a detective I am, really..."
"Right, sure. You were saying?"
"I sense that you might be trying to flatter me."
His eyes widen momentarily. "Right, of course you are. Well, as I was saying..."
"Those who are best at their job are almost always the most humble. But, as I was saying..."
"Thank you, sir. It's not often that the RCM receives the recognition that it deserves."
"It's a shame, too. What would we all do without law enforcement. But, as I was saying..."
"Even as Seol remains closed off from the world, Seolite agents have been slowly advancing through the echelons of power on the other isolae."
"Perhaps I was presumptuous to suggest I knew anything about you, as we've only just met. My apologies. But, as I was saying..."
"They come as apparently well-meaning immigrants. Sometimes students -- they learn our *violin* and *cello*. But more often tech workers in cybernetics and similar advanced industries."
Seol is known for being technologically advanced, although it is not entirely known how far they have progressed.
"That seems harmless enough."
"It sounds like their presence could contribute to economic growth and prosperity."
"It seems dangerous that immigrants would go into fields that affect information technology."
"And you think there's a problem with this?"
"Yes, but consider: Seol is famous, or shall I say, *infamous*, for its spy tech. Don't you find it... convenient?"
Seol is indeed famous for its advanced microtechnology, and for exporting it to foreign governments. Kijion Eendracht, the owner of Eendracht Airworks, is Seolite...
"Consider, though: Seol is famous, or shall I say, infamous, for its spy tech. Don't you find it... convenient?"
"Precisely. Seol is famous, or shall I say, infamous, for its spy tech. Don't you find it... convenient?"
"But Seol makes their technology available for others."
"I find it alarming."
"It's only logical. Seol is known for its advanced technology and exports whatever is most profitable."
"Yes, it's the perfect way to create a false sense of security. They sell us fancy technology and then send in their experts, who pretend *not* to be experts..."
"They play their violin and cello -- oh, we like your music! -- or work in unrelated fields, like, say, law enforcement, where they have access to a *lot* of sensitive data..."
"...and use their superior technology to blackmail, mislead, and manipulate, turning high-ranking people in government and corporations into Seolite agents."
"Yes. They sell us fancy technology and then send in their experts, who pretend not to be experts..."
"I'm not sure I like what you're implying, but go on."
"Well, you see... They sell us fancy technology and then send in their experts, who pretend not to be experts..."
Could it be that someone is listening in on *this* conversation? Are there bugs in the reeds -- not only insects, but tiny Seolite bugs -- or maybe even some of the bugs *are bugged themselves*...
"I work as a special courier. You know, urgent deliveries, overnight deliveries, deliveries to out-of-the-way locations."
"So you deliver things. What kinds of things?"
"Oh, I don't know the contents, officer. Part of my job is discretion."
He's trying too hard to seem untroubled by your question. The rigidity in his posture gives him away.
"Do you deliver guns?"
"Do you deliver drugs?"
"No, no, that's far too dangerous. Besides, dealing drugs isn't for people like me and you, officer."
"No, nothing like that. I leave that to companies with hundreds of years of tradition in arms manufacturing. No need for an amateur like me cutting in."
"Oh, I guess that's okay then." (Conclude.)
He smiles broadly.
"Come on, man. You're not under suspicion yet, but you will be if you keep evading questions."
He sighs. "Okay, fine, you got me. I'm a special *topping pie* delivery courier."
"What?"
"You heard me. I deliver topping pies. It's temporary. I'm looking for another job. Not many jobs for good men out there these days."
"They're wheat-free. And vegan. And... *huge*." He pauses.
"Sure. If you want, I could get you one for free if we ever meet in the city, officer. Wheat free. Just ask me later."
"Do you deliver letters to the secret mistresses of corporate and government officials?"
"What do I look like, a pansy? Besides, that kind of cavorting goes against the community values that would strengthen our city."
"You said you deliver *special* topping pies. What makes these topping pies special?"
He's thinking of a way to gain some advantage from his embarrassing situation.
It makes sense that a technologically advanced nation that produces a lot of *microtechnology* would have foreign governments as customers. That in itself doesn't prove anything.
"We must put an end to this. What can I do?"
"I don't buy this theory."
"I don't know how I feel about the Seolites knowing everything about me..."
"Gary, I feel like you bring out the racist in me."

"I like to pronounce it the *hard* way. The old way. The Vespertine way." He nods solemnly.
Garbage. You're a *true* patriot and you know how it's said. The Suresne way. The *fine* way. With an elegant shhh...
He winks at you, trying to relay some hidden message. Inviting you to mispronounce it too perhaps? It's odd.
It's a secret rite. A very fringe-nationalist handshake, probably.
The *stupid* way?
This is a considerable expense to him. One month's wage, most likely.
It's, in a way, admirable how quickly he composes himself after such a blow. This man digs authority. Even when it's bullying him.
The sound you heard was not the sound of something easily abandoned.
"Gary, do you know how to turn back time?"
