dialoguetext: I got this, I got this... My age -- I think I'm...
Yes?
I'm old. A wizened sage who has seen it all across *three hundred years*.
I'm in my early thirties. A rough thirty. I *lived it up*.
Oh my god. I have no idea. Probably middle aged, but... but...
You're a rough rider, but not in your early thirties. Do you want to know *the truth*?
Bring it on. I am not afraid of the truth.
I don't want to think about this anymore.
To the Laboratorium!
Okay. Seek not the truth. Cower in barbarism, you 58-year-old man-child.
Yeah, but probably not though. Do you want to know *the truth*?
Do you want to know the truth?

A warm column of air rises around you, encircling the building you stand on. You feel its twisting shape, bits of paper and birds -- on the *thermal*. Along with several million litres of water. All rising up into the great Insulindian sky.
Nothing happens -- there is a mass of droplets above the planetary body, colourless, merging into one another...
The sky is more black than grey; you hear the distant murmur of motor-connections somewhere south of here. That is all.
"So, officer..." the young woman says with a sigh.
"So, officer, what were we talking about -- in the final hours of this twilight world?"
"Silence, officer. Wouldn't have thought you the silent type... What were we talking about?"
"So, officer. Sad silence -- a lamentation? What were we talking about?"
"So, superstar law official -- what were we talking about?"
Continuously nothing. The sky slowly slides above you. The young woman exhales, the scent of menthol tobacco. Sounds like a sigh.
The sky is low and cold. You hear the distant murmur of motor-connections somewhere south of here. That is all.
From the vapour, a great cumulus is formed. A cloud castle one thousand metres high. A flock of seagulls screams, hitch-hiking on the thermal. They too are part of the procession, the honour watch.
Shudder.
Because it's warm -- from the gathering spring; from the oceanic current flowing into the bay; the people on the streets; and the machines that hum in the harbour. Heavy fuel oils too.
"The Return of *what* exactly?"
Everyone is a guest on this isola. A guest of the air and the water, and the humidity between. You are as well, surely.
"Miss. What are you waiting for?"
"I'm waiting for the miracle to happen. It'll take one to get me out of the mess I'm in."
Revert your eyes to the rooftop and shudder.
Is she safe here?
As safe as you keep her.

Her thought trails off. The wind picks up again. Above her, a great cumulus cloud rises -- ready to fall down as precipitation. April will come, then May; a month, maybe two from now... you shudder. The feeling dissipates. The thought ends.
"Of the king? Of the nation? Of communism? Return on investment?" She tilts her head. "I don't know exactly. It's meant to be vague, as promises generally are."
"What is the Return?"
"Don't you know, sir? I thought you were from around here. You look like *Mr. Revachol*."

"The Return, well... It's part urban myth -- part political science. It's a fool's hope, sir, and it's also all I've got. They say there will be an *event*. That it will happen somewhere here..." She looks around, then at the sky.
For whom?
For her. The guest. Waiting.
What is she waiting for?
For Gloria. Soon these clouds will all fall down as rain. Spring will come. Two more months. Maybe less. It's time.
"You mean here -- in Martinaise?" She takes a drag, slow and long...
Nod.
"Never mind. Tell me something else."
"Sure."
"And what would that miracle be?"
"And what miracle would that be?"

"The Return, of course." She smiles. "Now, I know I'm not from *around* here -- I would only be hitch-hiking. The Return is a big hit in the industrial espionage circles. A lot of desperate, seedy types there. All screwed in this unipolar world."
"Humour me."
"Oh, you don't know? I drank so much I can't remember my entire life. Turns out that can happen to a human being."
"You know I'm a bit spotty -- about a great many *things*. Like being a cop for example."
"As I said -- there's talk. In the competitive intelligence crowd. A lot of people, like me, who need... a new colour on the map. It's all blue, you see. And that blue doesn't like us."
"*Le Retour...*" the lieutenant says. His forehead furrowed, he puts his notes down.
"How soon will it happen?"
"Is this why you said you would like to surrender in a *free* Revachol?"
"Thank you -- one last question. Do you *really* think it will happen?" (Conclude.)
"Some political event? How do you know of this?"
"Yeah..." She looks at the sky, then at you. "I guess it is."
So she thinks -- at least partly -- that this Return will feature a self-governing Revachol. She has already placed her bets.
"Soon. But it's been *soon* for almost half a century now, so don't hold your breath."
It's an empty vessel, an amphora waiting to be filled. Something always *returns* from the past -- it's how the future happens. And when it does, many guesses turn out to have been right.
"You came all this way because of a rumour?"
"No, I came all this way on a false passport and some money. To hide, mostly. In the most volatile part of the Reál Belt, where it's easiest to disappear."
"Where the walls are still porous and you can slip through. This is just... something to get me through the night you know. A little *espérance*."
Still, the story influenced her choice of where to run. It must have some hidden layers...
"No need to worry, lieutenant." She turns to the lieutenant. "I'm sure the streets will not erupt in seditious violence just yet."
"These streets?" He looks over the railing. "I'm not so sure, miss."
"I do." She lights another one.
"In Revachol. Revachol West. They say it will happen soon -- and that it will change everything."
"But at the same time, I mean -- things can't go on like this forever. Something will give. It always does."
"So do I."
"I don't."
"I agree, detective." The lieutenant looks to the sea. "Something is coming -- *trouble*. It will be a hard spring. I don't know what exactly, but..." He shakes his head.
"Something is happening. In this city." She nods -- a puff of smoke. "I can feel it. When I'm out here at night..."
"Don't be so sure." The lieutenant looks to the sea. "Something is coming -- *trouble*. It will be a hard spring. I don't know what it is, exactly, but..." He shakes his head.
"Something is happening -- in this city. I can feel it. When I'm out here at night..."
"Something is happening in this city." She nods -- a puff of smoke. "I can feel it. When I'm out here at night."
Why does it rise?

"The Return, well... It's part urban myth -- part political science. It's a fool's hope, sir, and it's also all I've got." She smiles. "They say there will be an *event*. That it will happen somewhere here..."
As you look back you think: So love did *do him in* after all.
I was right...
[Discard thought.]
No. Communism killed him, remember? Love made it possible. You know this much.
It *killed* him... (Look at Klaasje.)
What is communism in this?
You do not know. A wind of needles. Airships flutter in the stratosphere.
How do I... know all this then?
Who knows?... It's getting cold out. You should go.
Or was it communism that killed him and love that did him in...
If it weren't for her he would not have been there. The shot would not have connected with his soft palate...
(Turn to Klaasje.) "Looks like love did him in after all."

dialoguetext: "Yeah..." she finally breaks the silence. "I'd like to think he didn't *love* me. Or that it was chemically-induced and not real."
"Why?"

dialoguetext: The IIR or interisolary reál is the global reserve currency. Whatever part of the world you're in right now, it's safe to assume he means you owe him some money.
"I don't owe you shit."
"What's *real*?"
"Oh, excuse me. You owe me 130 *reál*." He pronounces the 'r' with a mock aristocratic accent.
"By *real* do you mean some form of street cred?"
"Oh, I understand, you mean I owe you money."
"*Reál* sounds like some fancy skin care product... but why would I owe you one hundred and thirty of them?"
"You're under arrest."
Did I just hear my tie speak to me *twice*?
No one is saying that. No one is saying the tie can talk -- that would be ludicrous. It's just that... you should arrest him. It would be *wiser*. He wants to take your money.
I'm not comfortable with this. (Try to somehow tuck the tie away.)
Great advice, I'm considering it. (Give the tie an affirmative tug.)
No way, I have duties. I'm a cop, I'm not talking to a tie. (Take the tie off.)
"Oh!" He puffs with indignation. "You don't owe me *shit*? Well, officer, you're right -- you *don't* owe me shit, you owe me MONEY."
He turns to you, calmly. "We do not need to assert ourselves here. We only need instructions from him. This is the proprietor, remember?"
"No! He called me a f****t!"
"Sounded like extortion to me."
"Alright, calm down. What is this about?"
"But, you see, he didn't."
A man in his late twenties stands behind the counter, inspecting a stuffed seabird. As you approach, he gives you a sideways glance, then looks down again.
That was disdain in his eyes. Even now he's purposefully ignoring you.
That was disdain in his eyes. Even now he is purposefully ignoring you. Looks like he's not a fan.
Look at the stuffed bird.
"Are you the bartender?"
[Leave.]
"Something tells me you don't like me."
"What's wrong? Don't you like The Officer?"
"I sense you're not a fan of mine."
"Oh no," he says without looking up. "You're a hero. A real hero cop."
"So not only am I a cop, but I'm also a hero?"
Could the massive property damage upstairs have anything to do with this?
"Wait, did you just say I was a *cop*?"
"Yes, you are! A real decorated hero."
"What did I do?"
"You're being sarcastic."
"What did you *not* do? First you took the body down, then you solved the murder, then you *didn't* trash my hostel room. Maybe you even negotiated the strike..."
"I'm guessing I didn't do any of those things?"
"Oh my god, I did all those things?"
"I do not appreciate your tone. This is no way to talk to an officer."
"No -- you see -- actually you didn't. You haven't done anything even remotely useful since you got here."
"You're right, you didn't. And it's only taken you *three days* not to."
"Oh, it's not?!" He raises his shoulders like he's about to say something more, but then gets a hold of himself.
"What have I been doing all that time? Have you seen me around?"
"No, I haven't *seen you around*. I'm not always here." He looks down again and keeps plucking at the bird.
He has no respect for you personally, but this man sees himself as a law-abiding citizen -- and you a representative of that law. He tries to avoid outright conflict.
"What have I been doing then? Have you seen me around?"
"No, I'm not the *bartender*. I'm the cafeteria manager."
"What kind of question is that?"
"Am I? Or did you ride in, take the body down, solve the murder, and *not* trash my hostel room?"
The man plucks at the seabird, frowning.
"I didn't know I was a cop. Are you sure?"
"That makes sense. Ever since I got up, I've felt something in me..." (Look at your hands and feel it flowing through your veins.) "Now I know it's *The Law*."
"I can't be a police officer... This is insane."
"Nothing. I just wanted to hear you say it."
"I don't know. Am I?" He looks at you, taking stock of your cop-ness and finding it lacking.

"Never mind? *Gloaming*? What is this? Is *this* what you get when you call the police now?" He points at you. "*This* guy? Lieutenant, we've been waiting for a week here!"
"What is this, a joke to you? Is *this* what you get when you call the police now? *This* guy?" He turns to the lieutenant. "We've been waiting for a week here!"

"This stuff gets on my nerves. I am a feminist."

"I give credit where credit is due and that was a crazy move -- crazy *effective*. Petroleum bomb, never seen anything like that... I was there until it struck him, crawled inside then. Bullets started flying. Anyway..." He clears his throat.

"I wish you a quick recovery. Also!" He raises his finger. "You and your partner are staying here free now. This establishment supports cops. The stay is free -- the drinks are not," he adds. "Just felt I needed to specify that."

"I hope at least your partner is recovering quickly. Also!" He raises his finger. "You're staying here for free now. That's right, this establishment supports cops. The stay is free -- the drinks are not," he adds. "Just felt I needed to specify that."

"I give credit where credit is due and that -- was crazy. To throw a petroleum bomb at him and then *miss*. Maybe not super effective, but very *crazy*. I was watching until that, then crawled inside. Bullets started flying. Anyway..." He clears his throat.
He really wants you to realize that he was also on the balcony looking by. In the *danger* zone, so to say.
"I'm glad she got out of here before all that. Bullets flying and stuff... people inside were quite terrified you know. I had to take action and step outside too..."
"Exactly --" He looks at you. "But all in due time. Crypto-business is not a priority right now."
"Anyway, I can't help you there. A lot of women come and go here."
"Yeah, you're right."
"No. I meant it, like, in a good way."
"Sure. Anyway, I can't help you there. A lot of women come and go here."
"Yeah, Cuno doesn't know what the fuck this is about, but you should chill down, pig. You'll get this Lena fuck. On false charges." He nods confidently.
You'll see her again one day. You know it. Things went like they did for a reason.
He's almost completely forgotten what this began with.
"Okay, so I have to mention -- when it happened, *you* were right out there. On the balcony."
"By the way -- where were you when it happened?"
"Yeah, I was, yeah." He nods. Trying to remain aloof. "That's because I'm a *bad ass*."
"If you say it as two different words like that, it sounds like there's something wrong with your ass."
"Yeah, I guess you are a bad ass."
Just nod -- *stoically*.
"Yeah, well..." He scoffs. "Fuck you too then. You have any more questions, or stylistic pronunciation advice?"
"Yeah, I don't know..." He feels the need to explain himself. "Clients were panicking. And also, I guess I sort of found out that I don't give a shit if I die."
He means it. It's not just boasting. It's something he discovered about himself, stepping onto that balcony.
He nods back at you -- even more stoically.
Just two bad ass men nodding, stoically.
Make that three. Cuno is nodding too, hands crossed.

dialoguetext: "Where was *I*? How do you think I know the crazy shit you pulled off out there? I was *there* -- out on the balcony, protecting my establishment."
That's actually true. You remember him, from the corner of your eye, right behind you on the Whirling balcony...
"So yeah." He looks around, aloof. "I guess I'm what you call a bad ass."
"Did you see the HUGE graffito outside?"
"Did you see the HUGE BURNING graffito outside?"
"Yes. Very *responsible*."
"C'mon, you've gotta admit -- it was pretty cool."
"I guess you're right, it was pretty irresponsible of me."
"Yes, well..." He sighs. "At least nothing bad happened -- yet."
He's so exhausted following recent events, he doesn't even have the energy to really get on your case.
"Looked pretty hot to me..." He stops, realizing that this is also a compliment. "At least nothing bad actually happened," he adds with a sigh.
"No, I *completely* failed to notice that. It's only in front of the entrance to the establishment I manage. Though, maybe," he continues reluctantly, "it's still better than just the blood."
"Do you think it's connected to The Return?"
He rolls his eyes. "The Return of what? Some commie bullshit? The Return of the king? I don't concern myself with paranoid political rumours. I have a *real* place to run."
"Now what the hell did you want? I assume you *wanted* something to come back here..."
No. I don't want to get angry.
WHAT THE FUCK? He's *laughing* at you trying to not get angry right now -- GET ANGRY.

"This is about your room being locked, isn't it? It's about the electronic lock?" He cuts right through it, with his smarmy know-it-all attitude. "Unpaid bills are no laughing matter to me, sir. I *assure* you."
"Fuck you, I have a *vast* soul and she will always come back to it."
"Yeah, I sucked up there. I'm sorry."
"You don't *understand* my performance. Those high notes? I purposefully shredded them to convey a strained, worn out sadness."
"Good for you. I'm not letting *anyone* up there again -- ever. Now what did you want?"
What was that? Who's the *she*? And why do you feel so *bad' suddenly...
"Forget about that, I had something."
"How can I forget about it?" He stops the slow clap. "It was *unforgettable*..."
You feel bad suddenly. You see the delicate loops of the handwriting, in your mind's eye.
"Good. It's good you're sorry. I'm not letting *anyone* up there anymore. Now what did you want?"
"I get it. You were *purposefully* shit. So original. I'm not letting *anyone* up there again -- ever. Now what did you want?"
"Yeah. The Church is actually my *life*."
"Told you I'd rock that shit."
"Yeah. The Church is actually my *love*. Things are really *bad* with it."
"Don't worry. The fire will go out -- soon."
"Mhm. *Before* it reaches the Whirling, hopefully..." He sighs, more tired than angry.
"The end has begun."
"Sure. I don't know. Maybe. Maybe *the end* has begun? Fuck it." He sighs, more tired than angry.
He turns to the man. "Thank you anyway."
"So I talked to Sylvie." (Wink.)
"God..." He does not look too pleased.
Oh -- but he *should* be. Lay it on him!
"Turns out she's a whore who likes to ride the cock carousel."
But... I don't want to *lay* that on him.
Don't I have anything else? Like a *BACK* button for example?
Life doesn't have a *BACK* button. Now get off your ass and speak the truth about Sylvie the Whore.
Of course you do. This was your plan all along. *This* is how you *fix* it for them -- by answering the *woman question*.
Uhm... I don't like this. There doesn't seem to be another way.
"Wonderful."
It is! It's wonder-full!
"What?" He squints at you, worried. "What does that mean -- *cock carousel*?"
"She rides the cock carousel until she's too old to ride it. Then she settles down with a *provider*."
(Just drill the inside of your mouth with your tongue.)
"No time for lectures. The point is: you're losing at her nasty mind games. Sylvie's a total *psycho*."
"Huh?"
Yeah. This feels right. It feels *wise*. Good setup. Now speak the real shit.
He realizes something. "Does it mean you talked to her? What else did she say about me?"
"God... does it mean you talked to her? What else did she say about me?"
What *else* do you need?
"Yeah, she said that she likes the cock carousel very much. So fun!" (Depict a carousel of cocks going merrily around.)
He looks at you spinning your arms, then leans on the corner and sighs. His head drops between the shoulders, heavy and defeated.
"I should have known -- it was her way of telling me to piss off. I should stuff it up my ass." He stops and stares at the counter.
*Or* you broke the bird. It can also be that. I think Sylvie even...
YES! The bird is connected to this. It's a symbol of hope and she broke it.
"Or... you know. *Maybe* I broke it?"
"Yeah, man. Signals. Mixed signals. This is classic cock carousel behaviour."
"Broken bird. Feathers." (Nod knowingly.) "This is all part of the mind-fuck on the cock-carousel."
"No. It was her." His voice is cold now. "She's off to ride that carousel you told me about. Heh..." A mirthless laugh. "Cock carousel -- I understand now."
He takes a bottle of wine off the shelf and pours himself a glass. "They ride the cock carousel until the clock runs out. Here. Have the rest." He corks the bottle and hands it to you.
"Now, let me have a drink and think about this shit for a moment -- on my own." He stares into the blood red liquid in the cup.
"Heh..." A mirthless laugh. "Cock carousel -- I think I understand now. It's what they ride. Until, like, 39."
"The bird?"
"Yes, the bird. I found it lying on the floor with a broken wing the morning she left."
"I just break things. It's the way I am."
And there we have it. Isn't that beautiful? Another situation fixed by Doctor Love.
"Yeah... I do have a lot of cafeterias to manage. And a lot of employees there. I can't make this part of my work practice, it was... unprofessional of me."
"Anyway -- thank you for clearing it up. Now, if there isn't anything else..." He does not seem to be overjoyed about his new-found professionalism.
"I assure you, it was him."
...or can you give him a moment? Somehow you realize this is not going to net you any *professional discounts*. Already he's reverting back to defensive.
"What -- the interior-decorating kind?" He inspects the bird, somewhat suspiciously -- then mellows. "You know -- I'm sorry. This is actually a nice bird. A competent piece of taxidermy."
"I can fix it to the plaque and have a... new bird in the establishment I guess?" He hesitates. "So, I don't know... thank you? I'm gonna go with *thank you*."
"I feel good about our work here today." The lieutenant nods. "It's all about the little things -- like bringing people random stuffed animals."
It's.... not actually about that. But he liked it.
People just don't know how to accept gifts, especially taxidermy. He likes it. He likes the bird. It solves his broken bird problem.
"It was actually me who broke the great skua. I wanted to apologize by bringing you this ruffed grouse."
"Cool. Okay." He inspects the bird. "I was really hoping *not* to think about the cock carousel any longer, because it made me feel like *shit* -- but this *is* a competent piece of taxidermy."

"I should have known Sylvie wouldn't *accidentally* break things here..." He inspects the bird, somewhat suspiciously -- then mellows. "Okay. This is actually a nice bird. A competent piece of taxidermy."
"Okay..." He inspects the bird, somewhat suspiciously -- then mellows. "Okay. Well. This is actually a nice bird. A competent piece of taxidermy."
He tries not to look at you -- it's dangerous to *acknowledge* the karaoke man.
"It's for the..." He begins confidently, but then stumbles on his own words. "It's for no one. It's a prop. I'm not letting anyone use it after the Great Karaoke Catastrophe of '44."
"What happened in '44?"
"A lot of people got killed because some asshole wanted to sing karaoke."
"I'm having it uninstalled," he mumbles to himself.
"Oh, that's so sad to hear," he says with a barely disguised grin. "I'd *totally* let you sing karaoke, if you only had a tape -- *and* you'd paid your bills."
"I have the tape now. You *have* to let me sing karaoke." (Give him the tape)
"Fine. Okay. The kitchen is closed until 13:00 because the cook is working. You can snoop around after that -- if you must."
"Fucker?" He shakes his head. "Lay off the swear words, they don't make you *cool*. This isn't kindergarten."
"Okay then, never mind."
"Yes. What else?"
"It wouldn't hurt to get a little life in here. Other than the hellish karaoke machine. That one's always *causing trouble*."
Yeah, those numbers he's adding up must be making good sense to him right now.
"Garte, what if I told I got into the back room? Behind the blue door in the kitchen."
It takes a lot of willpower not to ask. Obviously he's been wanting to know what's behind the door...
"Aren't you gonna ask me what's back there?"
"Okay -- what *is* back there?"
"Pinball machines. A pinball workshop."
"Skeletons. A mausoleum of the dead."
"Nothing. The black gaping maw at the end of Time."
He shakes his head. "There is no gaping maw. If you don't want to tell me you don't have to. It's okay."
"Yes. Ha ha. What's *actually* behind there?"
"Hah! I knew it. I've always wondered where those machines by the door came from -- *and* they told me there was some kind of pinball thing here too..."
"I knew it." He repeats. "Were there any back there? In working order I mean?"
*But please do still tell me!*
Sounds like he cares about the place. He's not going to be overjoyed to hear that it's part of the Doomed Commercial Area.
He should still know. You have to be *forewarned* about these things.
So he knows of the Doomed Commercial Area. *And* its address. He's thought about this.
There is an acrimonious note. It's clear he's doing the real work around here.
"For 14 years, man -- that's how long I've worked here. I've kept this place up through hail and through sleet. Fuck me, if some Doom Ghost..." he steadies his voice.
You're guessing there aren't *that* many others.
"And who named it Whirling-in-Rags?"
"Well, it sure as hell wasn't the real estate company."
"You did?"
"It was you?"
"You look surprised? What? It's a great name, I know. Cafeteria managers come up with great names too. It's from a song."
"A song?"
"*Hail Holy Queen* by The Etenniers. 'Hail holy queen of the sea,'" he quotes. "'You're whirling in rags -- you're vast and you're sad."
"Good pick," the lieutenant nods.
Good pick.
"Well -- too bad it's all doomed then." (Conclude.)
"Luck has got nothing to do with it." He looks to where the hidden room is. "I need to think about where I'm gonna place those pinballs -- I have a feeling they're gonna help."
Against the Doom, it's implied.
"So if you didn't have anything else to tell me -- about my establishment -- can we, you know, wrap it up?"
"Wait -- so you *know* of the curse!"
"Everyone *knows* of it."
"Klaasje. In Room #3. She nicked the phone line."
"Why?" He stops himself. "No. Fuck it. I don't wanna know. I don't want to know why these degenerates do what they do. I thought we had *one* good guest in the building..."
"Yeah, I bet you didn't want it to be her."
"Well, anyway, mystery solved. I don't like loose ends."
"You have Lena. Lena is a good customer."
He really doesn't like it being Klaasje.
"What's that supposed to mean? Fuck you, buddy -- she's not my taste. Good thing she pays for her stuff on time, I'll forward her the bill and be done with it."
"Now was there anything else? I have, like, four thousand coasters to stack and then I need to wash dishes because it turns out I have to do that too now."
Hmm... wow. She really isn't his taste. Her spell hasn't spread here.
"Yeah, neither do I. Thank you for telling me I guess. Good thing she pays for her stuff on time -- I'll forward her the bill and be done with it."
Hmm... sounds like she has money tucked away somewhere. Enough to be a stable paying guest.
"Yeah, well -- she's not a guest, is she?"
"What?" the woman chimes in. "Did someone mention my name?"
"We were just paying you a compliment. And finding out a *degenerate* from room 3 nicked the phone line. Everything is okay here!" he yells, then turns to you.
"Good thing that guest pays for her stuff on time -- I'll forward her the bill and be done with it. Was there anything else?"
"Anyway, I'll forward that woman her bill and be done with it... Now, was there anything else?"
"Sir, he was only asking a question. It's his job -- and mine. See that it's covered."
"Yes. I absolutely will." He calms his breathing. "Sorry. It's been a bit of a day -- and now a hole in the wall."
"In your defence -- neither do I."
Damn you fat Evrart, your novelty check is useless!
"Like what? I was really enjoying talking about the *money* you owe me..."
Draconian measures...
I *really* didn't want to resort to this, the man is thinking.
"Why? Do you want to play? Because I might be up for a game..."
"Didn't check. Pinball isn't relevant to the investigation."
"No, I was... just wondering." He appears to be making a calculation in his head. "If you found pinball machines there..."
"I was... just wondering." He appears to be making a calculation in his head. "If you found pinball machines there..."
He was *wondering* about something business-related. About how much money he could make off one.
He's really, really holding himself back here.
"Oh? Okay. Well." He controls his excitement well. "I did hear you make noise back there. So -- good for you."
Seeing the disappointment in your face, he relents. "Oh, fine, hero-cop. Lena left a forwarding address. 1113 Tabernacle Road, in Jamrock. If you see them again... do give them my best."
"But we weren't done looking for the phasmid..."
"Especially when you're so busy doing *nothing* to stop psychopaths. How could you just stand there? Still, you did risk your life..."

"'Defended' may be putting it a bit generously, though. I had a great view of you doing *nothing* to stop those psychopaths. Then I crawled inside. Bullets started flying. Anyway..." He clears his throat.
"About my bill for tonight..."

dialoguetext: "This again?" He stares at the novelty cheque. "You just won't let it go, will you? Real funny."
"You must be kidding, right?" He stares at the large novelty cheque, baffled. "Yeah, good one, officer. Real funny."
"But this establishment only takes cash. Now, do you have that cash, Mr. Novelty Cheque Man?"
"I found the victim's clothes in the trash container out back."
"You can cash it in at the local Frittte, near the harbour gates -- though it might not be enough to cover it..."
Literary demotion! That's the worst...
"Oh, lieutenant -- we're *done* here."
"Frittte. Near the gates." The lieutenant sounds tired. "They'll exchange it."
How could ANYONE forget, asshole?!
"Maybe I have a vendetta against it?"
We were sort of hoping there would be a gun, an expensive jewel, or at least a *sword* in it for you -- if you deliver the message. Oh well...
"Garte, I found a new bird... dammit, I FORGOT to take it with me!"

dialoguetext: "I have no idea what you're talking about."
It's a long *healthy* trek back to the village.
Back to the village -- then back here -- then back to the coast *again*... That must be 3 kilometres in total. Okay...
This was mostly about the fucking *cardio*. Massive cardio here. You'll live 'til 90! *Or* you'll get a heart attack from running.
*Or* you broke the bird. That's why you brought the replacement. Out of guilt...
"Okay, *fuck* me then! Just FUCK me!"
"Stop yelling."
This is the look of a man who's *defeated*. He knows he's out of excuses.
"By the way, I'm going to sing karaoke here."

dialoguetext: "Absolutely out of the question."
You wait and see, cafeteria manager!
Absolutely *in* the question! First we find a *sad* banger, then we sing this place to SHIT.
Your body is ready, sire.
"Garte, I saw another *thing* at the Whirling..."
"What?"
By the way -- you should come back to this *thing*-based questionnaire if you see anything interesting in the Whirling later!
Hmm... you feel like you should come back to this *thing*-based questionnaire if you see anything interesting in the Whirling later.
"So, just to be clear -- you don't know how to open it?"
"Nope. No idea -- don't *want* to either."
What a shame. To fix such a good peephole.
"I feel a capitalist plot coming up."
"Capitalist *plot*." He rolls his eyes. "The pinball we have in the corner now is broken -- I want to diversify the entertainment options."
Damn! Your feet thought we got away!
"Maybe I *am* a cook?"
"You're not. You're a menace..." He gets a hold of himself. "Fine, okay, the kitchen is closed until 13:00 because the *real* cook is working. You can snoop around after that -- if you must."
"... and, come to think of it, Frittte's probably closed at this hour. They're open from seven to eleven."
Correct him!
Flattery is the way.
"Yeah. We've heard you have, like, a *huge* fridge. Colossal. Practically a mausoleum."
"You've heard wrong. And you're *not* putting a dead body into my fridge."
Damn, I thought the size thing would work...
That bird ain't no symbol of hope. It's a menace and a traitor!
"Didn't check. Pinball is stupid."
The lieutenant nods in agreeance.
Take it easy on him. Deep down he really hates being the guy who has to remind you.
You know, there *might* be other places to sleep on this coast... you'll find one eventually.
It's safe to say this is about your karaoke performance.
It really took courage. Don't pick at him.
He's not too offended. The experience has changed something in him.
"I don't think I have *any* money." (Proceed.)

Time stops advancing after 02.00 in the morning. If you haven't paid for your room by then, it's game over. Don't leave finding money to the last minute, however -- it's harder to make cash after nightfall, when the shops are closed and the streets empty.
"He's right," the lieutenant whispers, "you *really* have to sort out your money problems, starting tomorrow. I can't help you again."
He's right. You can't depend on Kim helping you out again.
How many times do I have to tell you about the trash bin idea?! Let's get climbing already! Into trash bins!
You could try climbing into that trash bin in the yard, hobocop style...
You could try climbing into that trash bin in the yard, hobocop style... after you've gotten open the lid.
"Come on, man. It's late. Do I really have to pay you *again*?"
"Wait, really?"
"That's more like it, Garte! One free room, please!"
"Do you *have* money tonight?"
"Yes, I do."
"No."
"That's not any of your business, Garte."
"Uh... Yes. I do." (Lie.)
"Uh... no. I don't." (Lie.)
"Then you really don't need a free room, do you?" He shakes his head -- and stops as a strange, new, cruel light rekindles in his features.
"Too bad," he mutters. He shakes his head -- and stops as a strange, new, cruel light rekindles in his features.

He blinks, as one might at a burning motor-carriage. "It is though. Right now, it literally *is* my business..."  He shakes his head -- and stops as a strange, new, cruel light rekindles in his features.
"As a matter of fact, you already have the key to your new room -- the trash container, remember? You said you'd give the key back and didn't..."
"Here. A new room key." He places a key on the counter in front of him. "It's the key to the trash container outside."
The lieutenant is painfully silent.
"I embrace my fate, Garte. This is the night of the Hobocop." (Take the key.)
THE TIME IS NOW! HOBOCOP LIFE, HERE WE COME.
A new dimension of reality will open. A portal is this bed of waste. Sleep there and awaken *elsewhere.*
"I'll try my luck. Thanks, Garte." (Take the key.)
"I'll see if I can figure something out." (Leave the key for now.)
He is very still as he watches you pocket the key.
"Right. Well, there you are. Now, was there anything else you wanted?"
He is not proud. But he'll deal with that later.
"Are you serious?"
"Really."
"Perfectly serious." The corners of his lips turn into the slightest smile. "You don't *have to* pay me anything."
The breath catches in his chest. The light in his eyes snuffs out all at once. After a moment, he speaks.
"Really really?"
"Uh-huh."
"You're fucking with me, aren't you?"
"Not at all, officer." The corners of his lips turn into the slightest smile. "It's true. You don't *have to* pay me anything."
"You can sleep in the trash container outside. I know you don't need a key, since you *tore it open*."
I helped you once. It was your responsibility to help yourself this time. I am sorry.
This was your responsibility. I cannot help you now. I am sorry.
"Oh, sorry, I think you misunderstand. Let me explain." The corners of his lips turn into the slightest smile. "I didn't say *I'd give you a free room*. I just said you don't have to pay me."
"But I *need* a fucking room!"
His eyes flash with fury. "You want a free place to sleep? Fine."
"Okay. I don't want to talk about this right now."
He rolls his eyes. "Anything else you need?"
"You don't *have to* give me any money at all. If you *want a room*, yes, you'll need to pay me -- but you don't *have to* just give me money. Giving me money for a room is *your choice.*"
"So, uh... you sure you can't swing me a free bed?"
"This isn't a choice. I have nowhere else to go..."
What does that mean?
It is not clear. All that is known is: Sleep in the trash and there is *no coming back.*
"Wait, I still don't understand. Do I get a free room or not?"
"No. You can choose to give me 20 reál for a room or you can choose not to. I don't care what you decide."
THIS ISN'T A FUCKING JOKE.
"You already have the key to your new room. I gave it to you earlier -- to unlock the trash container, remember?"
"I'll see what I can do."
"Fuck you, Garte. Seriously, fuck you."
He looks you in the eye. There is silence in the space between you.
"You do that. If you can pay another 20 reál, I'll give you the room again. If not, the garbage is yours. Free of charge."
"I embrace my fate, Garte. This is the night of the Hobocop.
"Fine. Fine! Here's 20 reál for the night."
"That wasn't so hard, was it? The room is yours for the night. Don't forget you'll need *another* 20 reál tomorrow."
"Fine. Fine! Twenty reál for the night."
"That wasn't so hard, was it? The room is yours for the night. Don't forget you'll need *another* 20 reál tomorrow."
"Keep your key, Garte. Keep it in your ass." (Leave the key for now.)
"Right. Well, there you are. Now, was there anything else you wanted?"
He is not proud. But he'll deal with that later.
He takes a breath, and says hurriedly, "I don't make the rules. Pay 20 reál or sleep in the trash container. It's not up to me."

"You do that. If you can pay another 20 reál, I'll give you the room again. If not, the key and the garbage will be waiting. Free of charge."
He takes the key from the counter and puts it back under the counter. "Now, is there anything you wanted?"

From the comfort of his own bed.

dialoguetext: "All yours." He hands it to you quickly. "Anything else?"
"You've already unlocked your new room. The trash container outside is ready and waiting."
"No. I know you just broke it open. You don't need the key and I'm not giving it to you."
"Got the 20 reál?"
"Fine. 20 reál for the night."
He sighs so much he seems to deflate. He slams the key before you. "The room is yours for the night. Don't forget you'll need *another* 20 reál tomorrow."
"But you know what? You're in luck. Because you don't have to ever pay me again."
Here comes a layup, sire! Fall not for it!
"Wait, you want me to sleep in the *trash outside*?"
"I don't care what you do. Sleep in the trash or pay for a room -- I don't care anymore."
"I don't care what you do. Sleep in the trash or pay for a room -- I don't care anymore."
"Wait, you want me to sleep in the *trash outside*?"
"Well... Least I got a place to sleep tonight. Thank you, Garte."
He stares at the key before him on the counter, then up at you.
"Thank you..." He stares at the key before him on the counter, then up at you.
"And... I'm sorry about the other night. I'm sorry I told you to sleep in the trash. That was wrong of me."
Wordlessly, he places it back under the desk.
He looks pale. Nauseous. He's guilty. But not enough to apologize...
"Apology accepted."
"Fuck you, Garte."
"Do you feel bad enough to give me back my 20 reál?"
He smiles. It's a moment before he puts the key back under the counter. "Anything else I can do for you, then?"
He smiles ashamedly through the rebuke. He feels the sting for a moment before returning the key under the desk. "I understand. Is there anything else you want?"
That meant a lot to him. Felt good, didn't it?
Okay. This is a good chance to start fresh. Just forgive him -- see how it goes.
NO, FUCK HIM. HE TREATED YOU LIKE GODDAMN HUMAN WASTE.
FUCK SORRY. FUCK HIM. HE TREATED YOU LIKE GODDAMN HUMAN WASTE.
See? That meant a lot to him. Felt good, didn't it?
"You're a traitor to the Revolution, and should be first against the wall."
He shakes his head as he returns the key under the desk. "No. I don't feel bad enough to give you a refund. Now, is there anything else you want?"
"I can pay it off with my net worth if that's cool?"
"No, of course it's not *cool*." He shoots you a look of disbelief. "What am I supposed to do with your *net worth*? I need cash, moron."
"But I paid for the work on that monument out there. Does that mean nothing to you?"
"That was *you*? Of course it was. The man behind every new misery in my life." He looks you right in the eyes. "But let's get back to the topic of the money you owe me."
"Hey, has a package been delivered for me?"
His brow furrows in confusion. "You're expecting a package? To arrive for you here?"
"Yeah, Speedfreaks FM said they might send me something."
"I guess it hasn't come then?"
"No, it hasn't. I'll let you know if anything arrives for you. Anything else?"
"Speedfreaks FM? I -- no, you don't have any packages waiting for you here. Anything else?"
"What about now, is my package here yet?"
"No, your package isn't here yet," he says with undisguised disdain. "I told you I'd let you know."
"I know you said you'd let me know about the package, but -- what about now?"
"I'm not dignifying that with a response."
"Did a package from Speedfreaks FM come for me?"
His eyes go wide with recognition. "Oh my god, the package -- I forgot, yes, yes it did arrive, when you were..." He stops, unsure how to continue.

He searches underneath the counter. After a moment, he produces a pair of neon sneakers, packaged in a plastic bag. A postage label directs it to the Whirling-in-Rags, to the 'Wildest Cop in Revachol'.
"They actually did it..." The lieutenant stares in amazement at the package.
"The fuck?" pipes the boy. "Pig's selling out for Speedfreaks FM now?"
"Thanks, Garte." (Take the shoes.)
"What? Oh -- yes! Something did come addressed to the 'Wildest Cop in Revachol'. One moment..."
"Thanks, Garte." (Take the shoes.)
He nods. "Happy to help, officer."
He nods. "Happy to help, officer."
Too late. You just did.
"But you just did. Right there."
"Fair enough."
The man actually remains silent this time. He looks at you expectantly.
"Package?"
"I wish Kim could have been here. He really liked these guys."
His face moves between a sympathetic smile and a sincere frown. Unsure what to do, he covers his mouth with his hand and pretends to cough.
After a moment, he speaks. "Maybe you could send the shoes to him? In the hospital. Maybe it'd cheer him up. Do you know where he is?"
"Yeah. Totally. I totally know. Of course."
"I... I don't know what hospital he's in. I don't know where Kim is."
"Sounds good. Send it to Kim."
The lieutenant lies in recovery. Where he does so, however, is unknown.
"Right..." He looks pained on your behalf. "I'll tell you what. I'll find out if you like, and can send them on to him. What do you think?"
He looks pained on your behalf.
Your liessss, sire! He seesss through them with a dissscerning eye of truth!
"Right... I'll tell you what. I'll find out if you like, and can send them on to him. What do you think?"
"Happy to help, officer. Anything else I can help you with?" He puts the package back under the counter.
"Jealous, Kim?"
"It's not something I'd wear on the job." He smiles slightly.
"You can have them if you want, Kim."
"Good. Because it's finders keepers, sucker."
A thought flickers in his eyes, and is then extinguished. He shakes his head. "Keep them, detective. You earned it."
"Fair enough. Now if we're finished discussing this, can we return to solving the murder?" He struggles to keep his smile.
"Sounds good!" (Take the shoes.)
"Thank you." (Take the shoes.)
"Anything else I can do for you, officers?" The man smiles at you both.
"I'm sorry, Kim. You can have them if you want."
He refuses to reply. Only his breathing quickens with badly-concealed irritation.
"You sure? Seriously, you can have them if you want."
"I am sure," he says, smiling at the plastic-wrapped shoes in their neon glory.
[Discard thought.]
By the way, where *is* home? The address is coming up blank and this place sure isn't it...
As I said, I don't think I have one.
I really don't remember.
But you've been at this hostel-cafeteria for only three nights. Where were you before? You had to be somewhere.
I don't know... near? South maybe.
Far away?
Up on Marvel Hill.
Why did you say that?
These are just synapses firing. It doesn't mean anything.
The name must have some meaning for me.
In time or space?
Both.
In time.
You don't really know, do you?
"Lieutenant Kitsuragi, do you know a place called Marvel Hill?"
"No..." He thinks for a moment. "But isn't that an expression, not a place?"
"An expression?"
"A saying. Up on Marvel Hill -- a great, high place. One that is impossible to climb back to."
The old thesaurus comes up empty. Maybe you should ask the lieutenant.
I don't. Does this mean I'm homeless?
I have only a vague, blackened image.
In space.
Could I trace the way back somehow? To the exact street, the exact number on a building...
I'll live in a dumpster, I don't care. Fuck everything. Hobocop.
That doesn't sound like somewhere you can stay if you run out of money.
A vague, blackened image doesn't sound like somewhere you can stay if you run out of money.
I have no idea.
"South maybe" doesn't sound like somewhere you can stay if you run out of money.
You can try. Run some addresses in your head when you get the time. Maybe a street or an apartment will appear.
Entertain the thought when you get the time. Maybe being a hobo *and* a cop has its advantages?
Do I even have one?

You don't really know, do you?

Something produced by the random firing of synapses doesn't sound like a place you can stay if you run out of money.
I don't. Does this mean I'm homeless?
You did it. You fucked up now. No money, no way to pay Garte. There's only one option left...
What is it?
Go... to the trash container...
A simple little cadence. He seems to be making it up as he goes.
"That's your machine behind you?"
"This rockin' beauty?" He points at the lorry with his thumb. "Sure is, like a rash you can't get rid of. You interested in heavy duty cargo machinery?"
"What's going on here?"
"It's the Jam, my man." He motions toward the sprawl of lorries with a sweeping gesture.
"Man, you look sad. What's going on with you?"
"Man, nothing's troubling me. Just the usual lorryman tropes and hopes: the road and the rhymes. This jam ain't helping either..." He looks around.
He's a poet. Hit him with your best verse.
Wait, there's something *here*. Stored away in some dusty corner. It starts like...
Your *best* verse? You don't even have a *bad* verse in here. Just tumbleweed and liquor stains... wait, no! What are you DOING?!
"A mirror’s temperature is always zero. It is ice in the veins. Its camera is an x-ray."
"Dang," he grunts, unable to suppress his reaction. "That's some *great* shit. You came up with that yourself?"
A motor lorry, also called a *camion* on Caillou and neighbouring islands. This one looks roughed up enough to be some sort of a FALN rust-bucket, maybe the A-6?
"I'm just a vessel for the muse."
"I think that may be an actual poet. And I've learned it by heart."
Or did you learn it in school? More importantly: who can prove if you did? Go with it -- you *deserve* some acclaim.
"I think the words are mine, yes."
"Right. But really -- no bullshit. That's great stuff. I sorta wanna know if it's yours..."
"Fuckin' A! Seems I got you all wrong. Cops aren't much known for their artistic sensibilities these days."
"What's the Jam?"
"It's a traffic jam for the ages. Harbour gates up the street are shut tight. No explanation given. Workers on strike. Scabs agitatin'. An all-around clusterfuck."
"All of who?"

"Us lorry drivers. Camionneurs. A few still hang around here waiting for this mess to end. Most have scurried off somewhere. To get drunk, or high. Or laid." He smiles awkwardly. "Not that I blame 'em, really."
"Tell me more about this... *strike*."
"Not you?"

"Not my thing. Chasin' transient pleasures is a drag these days. I prefer the examined life now -- thinkin', reflectin', observin'." He glances down the road toward the horizon, a glint of... something in his eyes.
He tries his best to look nonchalant, but there's a rigidity in him, as if trying to conceal something warm and deep beneath a cool exterior.
"What's the Union demanding?"
"Some pretty wild stuff, I hear. Like a giant new power-crane and half the company? I forget *what* exactly. Good on them, I guess..."
"So how long have you been here?"
"Feels like forever, like I was born on this here roundabout and this was all I ever knew. Just me and the metal and the tyres, the oil and the fumes of mazut..."
"Yeah, imagine -- it's been a whole week already." He snickers.
"Got any smokes on you?"
"Nope. Don't smoke." He nods toward the big lorry behind him...
"Some of the other drivers do, though. There's still a few around, waiting for the Jam to disperse. Or waiting for the sweet release of death."
"You *lying* to me? Being all stingy with the smokes?"
"Hello again, my man." He greets you. "What's on your mind?"
"I don't... really know."
"Just messin' with you. It's cool, you're an okay guy, for a cop."
"It's good to meet a fellow poet -- someone with an appreciation for *real text*. The others here, see, they don't really *get* it."
"It makes it all easier to bare. If the words are *pretty*."
"Hey, man. Cops are human too."
What gall he had to admonish you earlier for your prejudice, yet here he is, saying cops are usually dull-minded. Are you going to let him get away with being a hypocrite?
"I get ya. When they really *click* it makes the world seem manageable. Good to be on the same page." He gives you a thumbs up.
"Yeah. I guess I owe you an apology for thinking otherwise. And again -- *great* shit." He gives you a thumbs up.
You've found some common ground with this man. Even impressed him. The next time you look in the *mirror*, though. Remember those words...
"Meanwhile, we're all stuck here in long haul limbo for days upon days upon days..." He glances south, down the road. "Upon days."
"No matter. Great verse is like that sometimes -- ephemeral. You might not look it, but seems you have some literary chops. Maybe there's hope for me yet!"
"That's... a strange compliment."
"No matter, it's a fine stanza. You're not so bad after all, for a cop."
"For a cop?"
"They're more often into fists than rhymes, see. Let alone *honesty in verse*."
"Any organization gets all kind of folk. I'm sure we try our best."
"Well. You've given *me* some hope, I guess!" He gives you a thumbs up.
The lieutenant looks at you in silence, a curious look in his eyes, nodding slightly.
"He ain't one of us drivers -- I know that. All accounted for. Otherwise, I haven't really asked about that. Been wastin' time right here. Keepin' busy."
"Busy -- with what?"
"Analysin' the fundamental structural and psychological conditions of being stranded in the midst of a sea of motor lorries and their sad, despondent chauffeurs."
"And your conclusion?"
"A sense of surprise there ain't more bodies hanging from more trees."
"Man, relax. I quit, been clean for some time. There are some commitments you have to honour." He looks at you with compassion in his eyes.
You really need them smokes. Need 'em! Gotta get some. You sure he's not lying to you? You can't trust a lorryman.
"Never mind." [Leave.]
Mazut is an antiquated term for heavy fuel oils -- this man has a barely suppressed performative streak. Or he just likes unusual words. Or both!
"I am the law."
"You sure are, my man." He nods emphatically.
"Yes, people get that you are *the law*. You really don't have to keep saying it."
"I'm good for now, good talk." [Leave.]
The man taps his fingers rhythmically against his arm.
"Extravagantly phrased -- but I can roll with it."
"I don't quite understand what you just said."

In a small office behind the Old Military Hospital, hunched under the green glow of his desk light, officer Hans Blau browses through a test print. Of his futurist magazine. It's called "The Futurist". The typeface on the header is too small...
"I'm doing what little I can to do right by people."
"Guess I'll ask around then."
"No joke, man. Fuck the police."
The air from the east is thick with the smell of crude oils, heavy metals and other by-products of the modern era. You can almost *taste* it.
A flinch jolts his frame. The question has touched a nerve.
"Man." He sighs. "I don't know what to say. Not much anyone can do... there's no helping an absence, you know?"
"Not me, man, no way. I don't need any trouble. Shit's bad enough anyway. This jam's got folks up in arms and I'm afraid it's headed toward a conflagration."
"I'm a cop, I can fix anything."
"I miss my family. They're all I have, my wife... a second kid on the way... waiting all the way in Deora. And here I am, stuck in this shit, so far from home."
"You could also check the kiosque down the street. Frittte." He points towards the harbour. "With three t-s. Revachol is weird..."
"Care to spare some change for a working stiff?"

dialoguetext: "Hey, Tommy -- spill the beans. What's troubling you?"
"Huh?" Sudden financial duties snap him out of his daze. "Oh. No, I ain't got any money. They don't want to pay for unfinished work."
"'They' who?"
"The bosses, man."
"Could you say it again, only a little less plodding?"
"I dig your style, man."
"Whoa." He leans in, his eyes bright with attention. "What else?"
"It is a chalice held out to you in silent communion."
"It's like... whatever's going on over at the docks. Workers got a blockade set up. Making demands. No way in or out."
"What do you think the company wants?"
"They want to keep that money flowing in, my man." He makes a 'ka-ching' sound.
"Maybe *I* should go on strike..."
"Maybe you should. Cops don't get paid much and the hours are long. Plus, you can get shot. Why not?"
"Anything else I should know?" (Conclude.)
"Anything else?" He thinks. "Yeah, this ain't really my area of expertise. I just do my job and get paid. I have things to do and places to be. All of us do."
"The RCM is a self-managing organization that operates on donations. We promote our own leaders. It would be like striking against your own... mother."
"I don't know my mother -- but I'd go on strike against her too. For my rights."
"Okay." The lieutenant's face betrays little reaction. "But do continue. You were asking about the strike."
"I've heard talk there's a company rep in town too. Like... a strike negotiator type. They'd know what's up. Precise demands and so on."
"What are you hauling anyway?"
"You seem like a man who knows about *drugs*."
"Who do you think could be conducting the drug trade then?"
"I heard that one of the drivers is a woman, but I haven't seen her around. Do you know this *lady driver*?"

dialoguetext: "Do you finance those 'other addictions' with drug trafficking?"
What do you see in his eyes?
"Don't be a stranger." He gives a salute with two fingers.
"Everyone understands you're *the law*. That's why you have that insignia on your arm. So you don't have to keep saying it."
"Gotta guard the stuff -- bosses don't look kindly on missing cargo. And it gives me time to work on my rhymes."
"Hmm. I guess you've got a point there."
"Still here, stuck in this damn jam, my man." The man greets you with a smile. "What's up?"
"Oh, high-grade narcotics. Illegal fire-arms. Stuff like that."
"Okay. And what are you *actually* hauling?"
"Can't even get a few jokes past you, my man." He grins. "I've got another haul of FALN cargo. Mostly sporting goods. Tracksuits and that kinda thing."
"They usually get shipped to Graad and the Occident. Though we've been making headway in the Iilmaraan market lately."
"So, nothing illegal then?"
"Could I get one of those FALN tracksuits you're hauling?"
"Not unless they've illegalized sports equipment while I was on the road."
"We're pals and all, but I can't just freely hand out the merchandise. The bosses won't be happy."
"Yeah, these lorries are pretty neat."
"Neat -- for carrying large quantities of cargo a long distance. These FALN tracksuits need to find their way to the kids way out in Uamrao and L'Iramburde somehow..."
"Right. I had another question." (Conclude.)
In his eyes? A half-familiar longing.  Flecks of brown and gold.
Ease into it, don't go too far. This seems like a personal matter...
Behind the laugh, however, a touch of sorrow.
That all the beans you got, Tommy? Damn. It really is hard to *talk* man to man...
It's hard to say. His gaze wanders southwest -- down the street that goes beyond the horizon...
"What's it like to miss someone?"
"What's it *like*? Good. And bad. An ache that brings you joy." He smiles warmly. "I think of them a lot. I dream up these silly scenarios, in great detail. Of living with them... it comforts me."
"But... thanks for this. It's nice to talk to someone. And I know it wasn't easy to ask." He smiles. "I hope you find your way through your own troubles."
"I feel for you, my friend. It's good to miss someone. I like it. Knowing there's something *more* than what I have with me here."
"No, Tommy. These are my rhymes. Listen!" (Continue.) "'She *fucked* me 'til I bled.'"
"I don't want to talk about that..." He shifts around, suddenly uncomfortable, then looks away.
"Ah, man, me and narcotics go way back." He folds his hands behind his head and leans back. "Had some good times surfin' the psychic waves of my own consciousness, you know?"
"But..." he pauses, letting the memory dissipate. "Those days are behind me. There are other addictions in my life now. Why the inquiry, my man?"
"Hey man, that's serious criminal talk. Are you trying to pull some sort of an... entrapment thing on me?"
"What? No, of course not."
"Entrapment? What's that?"
"Entrapment is where a law officer gets a person to commit a criminal offence they otherwise wouldn't commit. Often through some trickery or fraud."
"Yes, it's like... trying to trick a person into doing something criminal that they'd never do."
"Wait, then why are you still hanging around?"

Entrapment is a practice whereby an officer of the law induces a person to commit a criminal offence that the person would have otherwise been unlikely to commit. Usually through some trickery, persuasion or fraud.
He rubs his jaw. "Then what's your deal here?"
"So, you do realize entrapment doesn't work if you announce you're going to do it in advance?"
"Umm... if you say so, officer." He gives you a cautious thumbs up.
The lieutenant closes his eyes and lets slip a loud, long sigh.
"Why, do you know something? What is it?"
"I don't mean to pry, but I need your help -- looks like she may be involved in drug trafficking."
"Okay, let's change the subject then."

The road continues for miles, flowing together with other roads, turning into causeways or bridges, ending suddenly in dead ends -- or ramping up or down highways. It forms a criss-cross pattern across the land...
Where does it lead?
Shake off the daze.
You may ignore the labyrinthine pathways, but you will never be freed from them -- they are carved into your soul.
"What's in the southwest?"
Above the Jamrock Quarter, in the form of a raised motorway, and then the never-ending sprawl of Faubourg. High above buildings new and old, the air filled with the rumble of motor engines.
Further...
What's beyond the border?
You cannot see. It's out of the city. Up ahead, the mist blocks all sight. A gale blows across your cheeks... it is cold. Before you stands a tall lorry driver with sad eyes.
To the Old-Old South, to the farthest outskirts of Revachol. Through the chequered fields of farmland, upstream to the River Esperance, past Monte-Martin... The border approaches.
Blink rapidly.
The road disappears, it is but a mirage... before you stands a tall lorry driver with sad eyes.
"Excuse me?" He emerges from the reverie.
"Hell, I get longing. I've felt something similar since I woke up."
"Really, you can tell me."
"Deora?"

"Deora-of-the-Seven-Seas. It's on the other end of Le Caillou, pretty much -- on another island, called Laurentide, off mainland. We've got a little place there. I can almost hear my kid laugh, when it snows..."
There's a pause and a sigh. Then he turns his eyes to you. "What about you, cop-man? You missing someone?"
He chuckles. "There are things even a cop can't fix, my man. There's no helping an absence, you know?"
"I miss my gun. I lost it."
"You lost your gun? Oh man, that's bad news. Especially here, in Martinaise. I hope you find it soon before things turn foul."
"I'm *fine* man, I don't miss *anyone*."
"No. I feel *hunted*."
"Hunted? By what?"
"By a shadowy figure known only to me as the ex-something."
"Ex-wife? No. It's a sinister presence that hunts me across all planes of existence."
"An ex-wife?"
"First -- what *is* marriage?"
"Maybe it is. We're doing our best to keep ours together. I *hope* it's not, but you never know..." A pause. "Thanks for the dark words, I guess. I'll make sure they don't come true."
"Yeah - no. It's more like a sound. A black reverb, that slipped into this reality along with me."
"No, it's the great white ghost that eats the world."
"It's definitely going to happen to your marriage too."
"Don't worry. I'm certain nothing bad is ever going to happen to your marriage."
"Yeah... In marriage you never know if you're doing the right thing. I *hope* we're doing our best to keep ours together, but -- anything can happen. Look, man..."
"Man, who even knows? It's like a legal contract, but also a bond between spirits... Every one is different, that's all I can say."
"Cool." [Leave.]
"*Limbo*, huh? So that's where I am."
"I am a gander and a hunter and a gatherer, feel like a traveller..." The man mutters to himself, accenting the beats as he goes.
Keep listening.
"From another... planet," he finishes and turns to you: "Hey there."
"Yeah, yeah -- exactly."
"Everyone's a critic, man." He waves you off. "It's okay. I've been here a whole week already."
"Make way for the master poet!" He greets you with a nod.
"Stuck in the rain in a traffic jam, man. What's on your mind?"
"Now it's turning into a... kind of a..." He searches for the right expression. "Snow limbo, man. What's on your mind?"
"Back already?" He grins at you.
"Welcome back!" He gives you a knowing nod. "The days ain't going by any faster, believe me."
"My man, you're alive!" He assesses the situation. "Almost... kind of... sort of alive."
"I'm still looking around. Loose threads to tie up."
"Yeah, the case seems kind of done. Gonna check on a few last things."
"Man, what a day... I missed out on most of the action, but I heard it was quite the encounter." He nods thoughtfully. "Had a strong sense of *finality* to it."
"Good luck with that, my man. Ain't easy being you, but hey, you're still breathin', right?"
"Yeah..." He makes a half-hearted salute.
"So, tell me... what do you need?"
"By the way, you're not angry with me anymore?"
"Oh look..." As you approach he instinctively averts his eyes. "It's the cop who turned me into a bad person."
"Alive and limping."
"Fuck it," he shrugs. "I'm a bad guy now. There's things more important than holding a grudge. It's okay -- you've been through enough."
"I... uh... saw you poking around in lady driver's lorry. She in trouble?"
"No trouble. She's going to be fine."
"Oh man, that's like... a load off my mind. All that stress was messing up my rhymes."
"There's going to be an investigation."
"What's the plan with those rhymes anyway?"
"Tommy L'Homme was taken." He shrugs in a what-can-you-do manner. "My real name is Jerry Lefitte -- Tommy's way better."
"Why Tommy Le Homme?"
"Oh, you know..." The thought lightens him up. "Tommy Le Homme's gonna be a musician. *Sprechgesang*, but with beats. I've got lot of free time on the road to hone my craft."
"Yeah, maybe I should just keep my head down... and work on my rhymes while I can."
"No need for you to do anything, don't worry. The police are looking into it."
"The last thing we need is more civilians involved."
"I really don't know. "
"Damn, I always warned her to watch herself... man, nothing to do now, I guess."

dialoguetext: An *idea* lights up in your head...
No. It's too far fetched.
"This is an air-gapped system." The lieutenant inspects the indicator. "*Off-air,* I think they call it. That won't work."
"Are you sure?"
"Okay."
"No, I'm not, but it would not be very good military technology if programmer ladies could control it remotely. Also, it's ancient. Incompatible."
"We're better off looking for a mechanical solution -- if we need one at all."
"INSULAR..." The lieutenant leans in to inspect the cursive writing. "This is an *off-air* radiocomputer, I believe. Used for military communications."
It's an air-gapped system. An *off-air* military model. Its circuits are nearly impossible to *bend*, i.e. it cannot be remote controlled.
You're right. You're not a *circuit bender*. You don't know about these things.

Wait, actually, this would not be very good military technology if *programmer ladies* could control it remotely... It's probably not connected to the front. Or just plain broken. Nice idea, though...
[Leave.]
This device was used to control the electronics in the room. It could open doors, control lights, function as a radiocomputer...
The boat engine!
"Or we could get some from the boat engine?"
"Failing that we could... go back to the mainland and get some from..."
Nod in agreement.
"But, officer," he looks you in the eye, "then we would have to *swim* back to the mainland. Let's just look around, okay."
The console looks on as you talk, mute and unpowered. Its dials are covered in dust.
"My Kineema?" He shakes his head. "I don't want to do that. Let's just look around."
The old button is stuck.
With the door open, the dial switch has locked into place -- a security measure of some sort.
The dial slides under the dusty glass, dark and silent despite the power being on. You make out defunct stations on the UKV frequency. The words "FELD INSULAR" are written on the band.
The glass is dusty, it's hard to make out the writing on the band. Nothing has changed about it.
Automatic boot.
"I think yes. Let's see..." He points to the emergency dial switch. "That one. The emergency open..."
"After you." The lieutenant gestures at the opening.
"Before -- outside. When we were walking across the sand, I felt someone watching me."
"What's there?" (Point to the door.)
"Let's go." [Leave.]
"So did I. Not back there, but... I've felt it since we came here."
"I don't know."
"I'm scared."
"Don't be. I have a gun." He takes out his sidearm, checks the barrel, then holsters it again.
A sudden wave of anxiety makes your skin crawl.
Pollen drifts in the light shaft.
"I don't have a gun."

dialoguetext: "Then it's extra good that mine is not."
"I know. It was not easy to acquire."
Harry, this reminds you -- you're out of bullets.
A sudden anxious fear makes your skin crawl.
Pollen drifts in the light shaft.
The blast door opens with a series of clicks. A shaft of light appears, then widens, as the light shines in.
The door comes screeching to a halt. Behind it you see a hole in the concrete wall, where light shines in.
No, it's more than that. There's something there, waiting.
No, it's more than that. There's something there, waiting.
"What if we get into another fight?"
"Don't worry. I have a gun." He takes out his sidearm, checks the barrel, then holsters it again.
"Old hardware." He points to the wires running into the machine. "From the big power-box upstairs. Circuit-bender shit. Military-grade."
"Try fucking with that one. It's red." He points to the emergency dial switch. It is large and alarmingly red.
"Cuno isn't a machine-meister." He stares at the dials. "'Urgence -- Ouvert!', 'Allumer', 'Radiodiffusé'.... Yeah, why the fuck not?"
"The fuck is this...." He stares at the dials: "'Urgence -- Ouvert!', 'Allumer', 'Radiodiffusé'. Maybe, like, press the buttons or something."
"Fuckin' right!" Cuno points to the opening.
"Whoa... Told you. Military mega grade. Also, like, four hundred years old, I think? A thousand?"
"Who the fuck is Soona?" he grunts. "Never mind. It won't work. This is fucking... military mega-grade shit, you know? It's also, like, four hundred years old."
The door comes screeching to a halt. Behind it you see a hole in the concrete wall, where light shines in.
Pollen drifts in the light shaft.
A sudden wave of anxiety makes your skin crawl.
No, it's more than that. There's something there, waiting.
"Let's go." [Leave.]
"There was something I needed to do with this console first..."
"Why? The door is open -- we can just fuck on now."
"What's there?"
"Before -- outside. When we were walking across the sand, I felt someone watching me."
"Cuno doesn't know, but Cuno wants to know."
"Cuno knows. This place is spooky as fuck."
"Fucking great. Spooky island shit is gonna shit on us and we can't even *shoot* it."
"Don't worry, I've got a gun. No bullets, but I have a gun."
