dialoguetext: "Are you?" He squints at you -- squints into your soul. "*Are you?*"
"Don't worry kid. I'm a good guy with a gun."
"Fucking great news, cop. Scare away whatever shit out there's gonna spook on us with an *empty fucking gun*."
"Wait, what about this fuel I found from my MC?" (Show him the canister.)
"There's barely anything left. That won't work."
What about the fuel you found in the MC? The red government-marked fuel...
"Wait, what about this fuel I found from my MC?" (Show him the canister.)
(Peek into the canister.)
Nah, it won't work. The canister feels light.
Yeah, okay. There's barely anything left in there. You have to find a larger supply.
"It's sweet you got government fuel -- way sweet -- but there ain't shit left in there. You need, like, a full load. Let's check outside when you're done with this."
Of course. Anything else you want with this console?
The console stands by, mutely. 'Urgence -- Ouvert!' reads a dial key. 'Allumer,' reads another. The frequency band says: 'Radiodiffusé.'
Nothing happens.
"Aw shit, it's on..." He grins. "Turn: Emergency -- Open!"
It's on! Automatic boot. Now, just turn the key...
Turn: 'Emergency -- Open!'
A thin wisp of smoke rises from a charred black firepit... the wind picks up, then dies down again.

This book is written by an angry humanitarian sciences doctor from the La Cherte University in Sur-La-Clef, a Dr. Benoit Mejean. He does not like Sur-La-Clef, La Cherte -- or in fact even the University he teaches in -- but what he likes even less is...
Read it.
Capitalism.
Can't stand the shadow of it. This book promises to *really* get into everything that's wrong with capitalism -- to do so once and for all in an *exhaustive* and *final* manner.
Why would I want to?

Critical theorists the world over agree: once *everyone* knows *every last shortcoming* of capitalism, capitalism will end. You are but one of billions, and there are over seven billion things wrong with capitalism, but one has to start somewhere. And Benoit Mejean, PhD, wants to start with...
It's capitalism, isn't it?
Nope. [Put the book away.]
Will this book turn me into a commie?
Sure. The more communist books you read the more communist your brain becomes. That's how communism works.
Yes, it will make you a little more communist. Not a lot. It won't *unmake* whatever else you are but you will also become a tad bit more communist, yes.
It will. The more communist books you read the more communist your brain becomes. That's how communism works.
No it won't. I'm impervious to critical theory.
I don't think I want that.
Good. Here -- almost in the end, limping and bleeding -- is a good time to get into some communism.
Then don't read it. The more communist books you read the more communist your brain becomes. That's how communism works.
Then you've found the right book. The more communist books you read the more communist your brain becomes. That's how communism works.
You.
You feel an ominous tingling in your fingertips as they browse the pages...
You start reading it, but it's hard to really understand anything. It's all some sort of garbled word-wankery. After a while you give up and put the book down.
A strange feeling... looking at the water. Maybe you should just wander off into the sea? Leave it all and walk in...
Why?
But it's cold...
[Shake your head.]
Yes -- cold and still. But love is warm, like the inside of her mouth.
Perhaps there's someone there? Under the water. Waiting for you.
Where it has always been.
In front of the video rental on the corner. At the crossing...
Baby, you know it's going to hurt.
In the still mirror of the bay you see Martinaise, reflected. Tall edifices of ruins reach into the water, like shimmering towers. And the shacks too. Pine trees and motor lorries, upside down...
Yes, please...
No-no-no-no...
Oh *fuck* yes. Go there in your head. It's been days since you've thought about her. A week...
Yes, yes, yes, yes.
A bottle in my hand?
With a bottle in your hand.
Always.
Raise your sight.
Islets and posts like stepping stones lead into the water in front of you. Go. Step in... it's been too long.
Smelling of Tutti Frutti and betrayal.
No-no, we're not starting with that. Not now. Not this time. This thought is over.
An old man wearing tracksuit trousers leans on the frame stock of his rifle. He gathers a big ball of spit in his mouth...
...then spits it out into the extinguished fire before him. He raises his black eyes, hooded by creased eyelids, to meet yours.
He's practically tearing up from spite. Hatred got the best of him a long time ago. This man hates everything.
"Nice gun you got there."
"Sir, I need you to put down that gun so we can talk further. I'm with the police." (Proceed.)
"It's not nice, it's a piece of shit." He shrugs. "But it gets the job done."
"Is that a Belle-Magrave?"
"What make of rifle is that, exactly?"
"It's a Triangong 4-46."
"A Samaran rifle... How did you get hold of one?"
Southeast Samaran-made. Exotic. Must be defunct too. No modern rifle manufacturer of that name springs to mind.
"A Samaran-made rifle."
"It was sent to us by our brothers in the Hsin-Yao Commune. Military aid." He pats the rifle.
"How did you get hold of it?"
"You're a glorified night-watchman." He looks you in the eye. "This is a service rifle. I can only lay it down before an enemy commander of corresponding rank."
Unclouded by cataracts -- his eyesight is sharp.
The lieutenant pulls his pistol from the holster.
He scoffs. The corner of his black eye twitches. He does not reply to the command.
His elbows rest on the frame stock, calmly for now, but he may still get it in his hands. Looks like he knows the weapon...
Yell at him, now! LOUD!
"Put the weapon down, NOW!"
"Kim?" (Turn to the lieutenant.)
"I *am* an enemy commander of rank -- put it down."
"Okay, but keep the gun down while we talk."
"No." The lieutenant aims his pistol square at the man's head and says:
The words "I *am* an enemy commander" sound cold as iron from your lungs. The old man still hugs his gun...
It's a good line, but your voice slips on *commander*, producing a little squeak. Sounds like you're afraid.
"And what rank would that be, dog?"
"A big time operator of the pederast army. How about I keep it, huh? Hand it over to a real killer. A *briscade*."
"Lieutenant."
"A big wheel of the 4th Regiment of the pederast army." He sighs. "To hell with it. It's a walking stick anyway...."
"It's out of bullets." The old man lays the rifle down, carelessly -- then stares at it, just lying there.
The lieutenant aims his pistol square at the man's forehead.
"Put it down *now*, sir."
"It's out of bullets." The old man lays the rifle down, carelessly, then looks at it lying there.
"Lieutenant-Yefreitor."
"Lieutenant Double-Yefreitor."
You don't see a magazine in the well.
There does not seem to be a magazine in the well...  the rifle's side is clearly visible.
"You don't even have a magazine."
"You're right. It's a good thing I got one in the chamber."
"I'm not from the homo army."
"What's a *briscade*?"
"Just put the gun down, okay? I don't know how else to convince you."
"Did I offend your moralist sensibilities? You beat people to death with a baton, you fucking dog!" The old man spits.
"Clearly not *you*. What do you want from me anyway?"
"You've retained your eyesight."
"My eyesight?" He clears his throat. "Yes. Helps me see all the shit."
Oh, wait. Yes.
"You *fasces* are pathetic when you're alone..." He snorts. "To hell with it. It's a walking stick anyway..."
"Who are you?"
"That's it for now, old man. Stay put." [Leave.]
The old man leans on the frame stock of his rifle, looking up at you.
"I ain't going anywhere."
Pick up the gun lying in the sand.
His gaze follows your motions. The rifle feels surprisingly light in your hand, frame stocked and patched in places with tape and wire.
"I ain't going anywhere."
It has stayed true to him. He can still make it sing.
"Military aid," he pats the rifle, "from our brothers in the Hsin-Yao Commune."
"Your weapon has stayed true to you. Mine has stayed true to me too." (Put your hand on your belt.)
"Yes, I bet you've killed a lot of people with it..." His eyes narrow. "...you fascist *fuck*."
"Have you come to make me one of them?" His grip on the rifle tightens.
"We have *come* to ask you questions, nothing more." The lieutenant puts his hand on his holster.
"I'm with the police. You can keep the gun, but keep it down. Not *one* move." (Proceed.)
His right eye twitches -- with what? Fear? Rage?
Another spitball lands in the ashes. That's all the answer he gives.
"If you do not comply, we will take you in. Do you understand?"
The danger levels here are hard to read. One moment he's a fire, the next -- a fire gone out.
"Sorry for disturbing you. Good bye."
"Fucking clowns..." He squeezes his eyelids shut and shakes his head slowly.
That was not the right move. You should have pushed on.
"Fucking clown..." He squeezes his eyelids shut and shakes his head slowly.
"Yeah-yeah, one move and you'll kill me. Put me against the wall..." He sighs. "To hell with it, it's a walking stick anyway."
"It's out of bullets." He lays the rifle down, slowly. Then just looks at it lying there.
Like an amputated limb in the sand.
"The Hsin-Yao Commune?"
"You heard me. It's good now. Like chalk wiped from the board." His gaze turns inwards.
He's right. Almost no one remembers there was a third metastasis of the World Revolution, in the Safre Empire, extinguished in '06.
"It's not wiped from the board. *I* remember it."
Let it vanish.
It's almost as if they were never there. Only the rifle remains, cradled by the old man.
"They wouldn't like hearing their name in your mouth. A damn dog..."
The time will come to win his trust, comrade. It is not now. You need to take care of the gun first.
"Or you're gonna blow my brains out before you question me?" There's a moment's silence. "To hell with it. It's a walking stick anyway."
Look at him raise his bushy brows. That's a lie. He's empty.
"I'm looking at another windbag who's got a problem with homo-sexuality."
It's war time slang for an experienced soldier of high rank. From the days of the Revolution in Revachol.
"No one cares, droite." He shakes his head.
"I shoulda known they'd send the fucking clowns for me..." You hear him mumble to the blackened logs.
You were right.
He stares on, his wrinkled mouth moving without a sound -- a strange sadness, like a song.
Let it be.
"The future teaches you to be alone."
"What did you say?"
"The present..."
Let him say it.
"The present to be afraid and cold." The old man pulls back the hood of his plastic cape and looks up into the sky. It's blue grey, the same colour as the sea.
The old man pulls back the hood of his plastic cape and looks up into the sky.
"Those words: 'the future teaches you...'"
"*Real music, real proletkult*." He nods. "That's La Revacholière, not your rock-and-roll misanthropy. *Chanson de soldat* of the black-and-whites."
"My name..." He looks across the water, then back at you: "...is Iosef Lilianovich Dros, Political Commissar of the 114th Anti-Aircraft Division of the 4th Army of the Commune of Revachol."
Marching song...
"What is La Revacholière?"
"Understood."
"You don't understand *anything*." The old man squints at you -- you see two black beads, gleaming.
"It is the anthem of the World Revolution." His eyes remain fixed on the sky. "One of three."
"I know La Revacholière. It's the marching song of the World Revolution."
"There you go." His eyes remain fixed on the sky as he sighs and adds: "One of three."
"In Graad they sang 'Brave Children, Favourites of History' and in Hsin-Yao it was..." He struggles to remember, then gives up. "...some Samaran shit, I guess."
In Hsin-Yao they sang "Boy with a Scythe / Golden Sun."
"First, it wasn't *some Samaran shit*. It was 'Boy with a Scythe'..."
"La Revacholière... I've heard that name, somewhere else. In a dream."
"I fucking know what they sang!" he hisses. "I watched those little fuckers die in my arms -- little ones came to help us. Got cut to shreds..."
"You don't fucking tell me what they sang..." He closes his eyes and exhales to calm himself.
His nostrils are still flaring with rage. He brings himself back under his own stewardship, slowly.
"No, that's not it. I've talked to her."
"Everyone has. They named a fucking perfume after it."
"Yes. Must've been that."
"A fucking perfume..." he sighs.
"Talked to *her*?" He raises his bushy brow and looks down from the sky -- straight into your bloodshot eye.
"Yes. I get these... cold spells."
"Yes. In the church." (Point southwest.)
"Nothing. We have serious things to talk about."
"It's the *drugs* you're all on. Druggies, winos, and whores..." He closes his eyes in disgust.
There was something there -- when he said *talked to her*? He was curious...
"God's shithouse." He chortles. "Should've taken it down like they did in Graad; dismantled it for firewood."
All around you, the air slowly circulates the islet, carrying little swallows and black-beaked seagulls in its slow drift. They all -- every one of them, every bird, mammal, and crustacean...
What?
Rub your sides.
Keep their distance.
The cold dissipates. The old man watches you, carefully.
"I've seen kids lose their minds and start *talking* to the city. Asking it to *protect* them, when the shelling gets bad. Calling it La Revacholière..."
"Doubt it, dog..."
"Thank you for clearing that up." (Conclude.)
"Heh". The old man squints and looks you straight in the eye -- two black beads, moist from the sea air.
"When I said I've talked to *her* -- you were curious."
No, he was just confused. Let it go...
Don't be so sure...
"I'm not a shit-licking boujee dog. I'm a half-dead police officer who's just doing his job."
"The job of a boujee dog."
Forget about that for a moment. You need to address that remark first.
You need to address that remark.
Still warm from his parched hands. Not the metal. The metal is ice cold. This weapon has been modified several times.
Inspect it closer.
"It's as he said: it's a Triangong. Made in Hsin-Yao."
Stow the gun. (Conclude.)
The rifle's in a shabby state, like a crutch that's seen too much travel. Hieroglyphs are embossed into the forearm made of walnut.
They say: 'Triangong 4.46. Hsin-Yao Commune. For Safre -- and for all mankind.'
I know Seraise?
Look at the butt of the gun.
This is Vulgate Seraise. You can barely intuit the words. *Know* is stretching it.
(Whisper.) "Kim, I know Seraise."
"What does it say?" he asks doubtfully.
"For Safre -- and for all mankind."
"That's what the little guys told us." The old man says silently. "Every day at 4 o'clock in the morning, they'd go on and on about their Safre, their mankind, and Mazov..."
"Those men were commandos. They weren't shit on a stick, like us. They were small and..." He doesn't say more. The thought dissipates on his lips.
"For Safre -- and for all mankind?"
On the butt you see Vespertine writing, burnt into the wood: Triangong 4.46 mm, made in Hsin-Yao.
"No one said it has to be a Belle-Magrave..." The lieutenant does not take his eyes off the old man. "We were just guessing."
"This uses jacketed ammunition. 4.46."
"The right type and the right calibre," the lieutenant nods -- glancing at the gun.
The old man keeps following your motions with his gaze. His right arm twitches suddenly...
"This is a Triangong, made in Hsin-Yao."
"Worn. Personalized even. Looks like this weapon has seen a lot of use. Hasn't it, sir?"
"It doesn't matter if it was made in Shantih-Shantih. All it has to do is use jacketed ammunition. And it does."
From ballistics, it could easily have been a Triangong too.
"Jacketed -- military-grade ammunition. Stable in flight, good for hitting something that's very, very far away..." He says -- mostly to the old man.
No response from the old man. The plastic cape around his shoulders rustles in a small bout of wind.
He's liking this.
As he speaks, he stresses every word. He's liking this.
"The rifle has been patched and modified several times."
"I wonder how old it is."
The old man does not answer. He just stares in front of him.
The old man blinks slowly. A strange jitter comes over him, he pushes his right leg down and does not reply.
"Hmhm." The old man smacks his lips.
"Things keep falling apart if you don't tend to them."
Some kind of involuntary response? Something is slightly off with his motorics...
"I am a deserter, a partisan, and a prisoner of war. This is my termless surrender." His eyes turn to the reeds again, dead and dull.
There, behind them, across the Delta -- the INSURCOM building. Coalition Government Insulindian Mission Control.
"The Commune of Revachol..." The lieutenant forgets to close his mouth. "Do you mean the ICM? You're a holdover from the..."
"From the Insulindian Citizens Militia -- the Army of the Revolution. I was recruited in Jamrock in '07, trained in the Ecole de Contrôle Aérien and consigned to emergency defence duties in '08."

"I left my unit on the eve of the Landing. When I returned here on May 14th the Commune had fallen. Still armed -- and *ideologically trained* -- I wrote a criticism of myself. And resumed partisan duties."
"You've been on this island for 43 years?"
"How long have you been on this island?"
"No." He looks into the fire -- a wisp of smoke rises from somewhere between the charred logs. "I've been on other islands too."

"I was on Résurrection until they turned it into a *spa* in '18. Then I was on E48, a nameless sound, until the sea washed over it. Then I came back here. That was..." He thinks. "Twenty-two years ago."
Embers going out.
"How does it go -- the song?"
"How did it go..." He looks at his gun in your hand and shakes his head slowly.
"How did it go..." He looks at his gun on the ground and shakes his head slowly.
"Something about shooting *rabbits,* I don't know... I can't remember. It doesn't matter. It's gone now."
He waves erratically -- with his hand, annoyed that he can't remember. A little tremor passes through him.
It was dear to him. He resents forgetting it.
'So if I can shoot rabbits then I can shoot fascists too' -- those are the next lines.
"I have trouble remembering things too."
"So if I can shoot rabbits, then I can shoot fascists too."
"What are you talking about?" He squints and looks you straight in the eye -- two black beads, moist from the sea air.
He squints and looks you straight in the eye -- two black beads, moist from the sea air.
"You're a holdover from, the ICM, the Insulindian Citizens Militia?"
"You're a holdover from the Army of the Commune of Revachol?"
"Yes. Recruited from Jamrock in '07, trained in the Ecole de Contrôle Aérien; consigned to emergency defence duties in '08."
"Yes, I am from the Insulindian Citizens Militia. Recruited from Jamrock in '07, trained in the Ecole de Contrôle Aérien; consigned to emergency defence duties in '08."
"Forty-three years... No." He looks into the fire -- a wisp of smoke rises from somewhere between the charred logs. "I've been on other islands too."
"You said this is your *termless surrender*."
"So you're a communist soldier? From the communist army?"
"I did," he breathes out with a wheeze. "And you opened it -- how?"
"Did you close the blast door?"
"Reactionary rock-and-roll music." He gestures north. "Playing on the water."
"I fuelled the generator. Then used the console."
"How did you know I was coming?"
"I should've burned that console down..." He shakes his head.
"The boat engine." He gestures north. "On the water..."
"It was not rock-and-roll. It was Sad FM!"
"It was not reactionary. It was cool."
Say nothing.
"Told you we shouldn't play Sad FM."
"The fascists were right about rock-and-roll. It *is* degenerate... Hip-gyrating mental illness music."
"But you didn't say that, Kim."
"I did."
We have entered a world where he said you shouldn't. It is the only world.
"Sad FM, huh? I always hated that station. Phlegmatic, counter-revolutionary dirges... Sadness is a mental illness, a weapon of the bourgeoisie."
"Real music. It's La Revacholière, you shit-licking boujee dog. *Chanson de soldat* of the black-and-whites."
"The job of a shit-licker."
"I'm not a misanthrope, I'm a half-dead police officer who's just doing his job."
"How have you survived all this time?"
"You said you deserted your unit?"
"Again -- you've been hiding here for *43 years*?"
"Forty-three years and 10 months."
"I was just sixteen years old, fifteen when I volunteered. I had a lapse of faith..." He clears his throat. "And of courage too."
"That's insane."
"That's steadfast."
"That's the length of my entire life."
"I don't even know what that is."
"It's not how a human being should live, but I had to..." He grimaces, clearly in pain. "...I couldn't just forget. I couldn't just forget what I saw."
"Always waiting. Always...."
"What have you been doing during all this time?"
"Hiding, fishing, waiting..." He looks across the water.
"For what?"
"For her to return."
"It's too long. It's not how a human being should live..." He grimaces, clearly in pain. "But I couldn't just forget what I saw."
"It's inhuman. It's sick. It's not how a human being should live, but I had to..." He grimaces, clearly in pain. "I couldn't just forget. I couldn't just forget what I saw."
He just *couldn't*...
"You couldn't give up."
He nods.
"What have you been doing all this time?"
"Her, who?"
"Girl Child Revolution."

Where night falls... Hydrogen streetlamps burn on Rue de Saint-Ghislaine, golden light casting black shadows. Further inland, in Jamrock, the street grid appears black -- unlit avenue after unlit avenue. Altocumulus clouds form above Precinct 41.

dialoguetext: (Now we are done.) "Iosef Lilianovich Dros, you are under arrest for the murder of the colonel."
The old man stares at the reeds. His face shows no emotion -- only a faint tremor passes over his features, like a leaf in the wind.
"Cities can't talk. It's bourgeois idealism... I don't wanna talk about this shit anymore."
This looked very much like the murder weapon. It can be used against him -- later.
This looked very much like the murder weapon. It can be used against him to get a confession -- in time...

"Good, *Cuno*. Be that." He nods toward Martinaise. "I saw the *traitors* of this city turn the lights back on. More and more each year. Ruins, glittering in the dark, like a fucking merry-go-round..."
i wanna see phasmid with kim
i wanna see phasmid with cuno
"Well, guess what? I *am* an enemy commander."
"I want to ask again about the people you don't like."
A shudder of disgust passes his right side. His left side remains motionless.
He is not afraid of such displays. This was the wrong move...
The present...
He doesn't recognize it.
But he can now.
He would answer, but something happened. It's like his tape cut off suddenly...
"My pig asked you a question. Quit spazzin' out and tell him about the..." The kid doesn't get to finish the sentence.
The *position*? Sounds like a hiding place...
The creature stands on long stilt-like legs, antennae hanging from its head like a woman's hair -- white and curled at the tips. It is no more than five steps away from you.
The segmented antennae move with apprehension, searching for something... you.
Take long, deep breaths. Slow down your pulse. Don't move yet, and when you do -- be light as a feather.
(Whisper.) "This is the Insulindian phasmid."
Approach carefully.
The hiss is different from the strings you heard before. It says something *else*, in a lower pitch...
Listen carefully...
Sssss-hsssss-tik-ssssss-hssss-tik...
You smell...
Tik-tik-tik... hisss... tik-tik-tik... hisss....
Be afraid. You smell wrong.
"It is," the lieutenant whispers behind you. You hear the familiar ring of his jacket unzipping -- slowly. Painstakingly so...
You glance over your shoulder. The lieutenant holds a piece of milled aluminium. He begins to pull it open, extremely carefully -- it's the camera!
You glance over your shoulder. The lieutenant holds a piece of milled aluminium. He begins to pull it open, extremely carefully...
No! The flash will scare the creature off! Warn him NOW!
No! The flash will scare the creature. Warn him NOW!
Looks like camera! Yes!
"Kim..." (Whisper.) "The flash is loud. It won't like that."
(Whisper) "Are you sure you won't scare it off?"
(Point to it.) "What is that?"
"My camera."
No! The sound of the flash will scare the creature off. Warn him NOW!
"We *need* a photo -- no one will believe us." He continues to pull the lens open...
"We need a photo -- or no one will believe us." He continues to pull the lens open...
From the corner of your eye, you see a sudden cascade of motion ripple through the insect's limbs. A series of ultrasonic clicks fills your ear...
I am not palatable. Do not eat me. I am afraid.
"Okay, take the picture."
"Stop. Let me approach it first."
With the sound of metal sliding against metal, the lieutenant reveals the lens. The glass glints in his hand as he begins to slide in an ampoule...
"I won't be one of those fools who didn't take a picture..." He has stopped fiddling with the camera, but does not put it down.
He's letting his pride get in the way.
(Whisper) "Who cares what they *think* Kim."
(Whisper) "I have the pheromone, I can approach it."
He comes to, abruptly. "Understood. Of course," he says with a nod.
"Just listen to me!"
"I don't think the pheromone will do anything." His whisper turns to a sceptical hiss -- but he has stopped now.
"Shh... okay." The lieutenant puts his finger to his lips and nods.
The spindly mechanism turns itself back to you, its antennae taking their measure of the air, slowly...
(Say something to the insect, quietly, like...)
Retreat slowly. [Leave.]
The creature tilts its tiny head to the side and appears to look at you. It is incredibly light, like the slightest gust of wind should blow it away, but it doesn't...
Its insect mind is impenetrable to your reasoning.
(Whisper.) "What is that?"
"Hey."
"Don't be afraid..."
"You exist..."
A sudden chirrup fills the air -- the walking stick moves its whole body, limbs working independently of each other, like the parts of a masterfully constructed machine.

Nothing changes in the cyclical, praying motion of the creature's limbs. They are porcelain white on the inside, and reed-coloured on the out -- beige, light brown and striped. You are unsure if it is scared or not.
There is a sadness in there -- or is it in you, from the dream... It's still with you, the pitiful *hey* you told her, even now...
It moves just an inch closer to you. Or does it only *feel* like it does?
Something in its body language has changed, just slightly...
No one hears you whisper. Behind you, the straggler sits despondently by the fire, oblivious to his surroundings.
You see the insect turn to him, its mandible antennae reaching out. Its motions are quick, sudden.
"We can't just leave it standing there. We have to do *something*, detective. It could be..." He thinks. "It could be connected somehow even..."
The ghost insect watches you disengage, continuing its hypnotizing motion. It's unclear whether it even registers that you're going...
You've never seen him get this excited. His voice is almost trembling.
He not as much as glances at the gigantic insect to his right -- nor does it look at him. Its antennae take their measure of the air, slowly... searching for something -- *you*.
"I have absolutely no idea..." The lieutenant whispers back. You hear the familiar ring of his jacket unzipping -- slowly. Painstakingly so...

Meanwhile, in the antechamber of the Station 57 lazareth, a neatly packed pair of cargo pants and an orange bomber jacket sit in a locker. Nested on the jacket -- a small block of milled aluminium, tucked away in a leather case.
An instant camera -- the Trigat Sunshine Mini. A moan of discomfort sounds from the lazareth, as he turns onto his side...
A camera -- an instant colour camera the lieutenant keeps tucked away in his coat pocket. A moan of discomfort sounds from the lazareth, as he turns onto his side...
Back on an island 28 kilometres away, the gigantic insect moves its antennae, taking its measure of the air, slowly... it's searching for something -- *you*.
Slowly, with your breath held, you take two small steps toward the phasmid. The creature lets out a series of ultrasonic clicks that swarm around your head like swallows...
You barely get to take one step -- the invertebrate reacts with uncanny speed, skating away across the water. It's gone, like a skipping stone, leaving nothing but rings on the sea's calm mirror...
The tracheal system on the creature's abdomen expands in front of you, to take in and expel air -- it's *smelling* you.
Like laughter. A sort of happiness.

...hissing and clicking, it extends its mandible-like antennae to greet you. You're right below it now, looking up at the colossal chitin of its white limbs. The head of the creature is crowned by reeds and its eyes are like small droplets of water.
Sweat drips from your brow, soaking your chest... you reek of it, your chemicals.
Raise your hand slowly.
(Whisper) "Okay Kim, take the picture."
"Hello. I don't know who I am."
Disengage slowly. [Leave.]
The insect stops its stridulation, seeming to observe you. Below its crown of reeds, little pin-prick eyes detect motion, glittering. The world stands still around you.
No reply. A total, ancient silence comes from its mouth, along with what appears to be some kind of foam... The stridulations of its limbs continue all around you.
Praying to you.
Tell me -- what are you doing?
Stand on your tiptoes and look more closely...
Back off.
You were right. Little bubbles form on the mouthparts of the creature -- on its segmented lower lip. It looks to be foaming, slowly. The foam is white, then yellowish...
The faintest smell, like you've never felt before. Like burnt roses.
(Whisper.) "Kim, it's foaming."
"Why are you're foaming?"
Let your heels drop back onto solid ground.
"Careful. It may be poisonous." The lieutenant watches you apprehensively.
The foam slowly turns a darker shade, like burnt caramel -- as the insect moves its mouthparts, masticating. The little bubbles begin to burst, one by one...
Letting out that same smell, like summer burning.
Apricot blossoms. White blossoms erupting. A sensation, like cold hands on your face.

Silence. Click. The foam slowly turns a darker tone, like burnt caramel -- as the insect moves its mouthparts, masticating on nothing in particular. Then the little bubbles begin to burst, one by one...

The invertebrate stops, raising its scythe-like arms and tilting its tiny head, formed from the fused plates around its mouth. For a second, the effigy is frozen, then it nudges back into motion with a click.
Raise the other hand too.
As you do, the invertebrate comes to life, its limbs moving independent of each other. As if each has a mind of its own. They are white like stalks of porcelain, knitting above you.
(Whisper.) "That's right. Pray."
"Don't pray to me. I'm nothing."
Put your hands down instead.
Suddenly there is silence.
(Look behind you.) "It's smelling me..."
"Maybe it *is* real, the pheromone..." The lieutenant's mouth is agape.
Put your hand down.
The invertebrate comes back to life, stridulating. Sets of complex eyes follow you, moving in tandem, on either side of the insect's small head.
No. Stop. Be afraid.
Unwittingly the insect continues its stridulations. As it moves, tuft-like structures still pretending to be plants rustle along on its joints.
The reed-creature does not stop its stridulations -- it towers above you, parting the reeds it emerged from. Tuft like structures still rustle on its joints.
About now he is ready to believe in anything.
(Look up.) "You're smelling me..."

dialoguetext: The insect's head is crowned with reed-like scales, the shape of seed heads. They rustle as the air moves. The ventricles at its abdomen continue to expanding, like lunglets...
Breathing you in -- your sour, greasy semiochemicals on the breeze...
Perhaps it is preparing to *eat* its god?
Sets of complex eyes follow you --droplets of dew on either side of the head.
"Okay..." With a slow ring of metal, the lieutenant slides the lens open and raises it to eye level.
There is no change in the insects motion while its being aimed by the camera. It remains fixated on you.
"In three," the lieutenant whispers, his voice is tense. "If it moves, you jump back, I'll shoot. Here we go. Three, two, one..."

The shrill flash of the camera cuts the air like the blade of a sword. The phasmid freezes in its bright light -- head turned toward the lieutenant. Hypnotized by the flash, it stands frozen before you.
The sweat on your arms feels cold as ice. As if you're frozen as well, in the shadow of this giant statue of chitinous marble.
(Yell.) "No!"
"Where did it go?" (Look north.) Can *you* see it?"
"How did it *do* that? Glide?"
"Did you get it, did you get the picture?"
"It appears the insect can walk on water. Like a water strider, you know. It's almost as fast..." He stops, short of breath. "Uncanny..."
"No." He shakes his head. "It's gone for now, detective."
"I don't think..." He tries to explain, patting slightly: "I don't think it had *anything* to do with the ox-spray. It was just scared."
It's blending into the tufts of reeds in the distance! Moving from islet to islet...
And you, a detective of the RCM, standing there with your mouth agape -- alone and dumbfounded.
"I shouldn't have taken a bath, the pheromone washed off!"
There is uncertainty in his phrasing.
It *definitely* had something to do with the ox-spray! It was repelled by you, as if it was scared.
Your voice echoes on the water.
"It *did* have something to do with the ox-spray!"
"Okay, but..." He shakes his head in disbelief. "I'm not an entomologist, okay? Neither was the para-scientist. Who knows? The only thing I'm sure of is..."
He shakes his head. In silence -- an expression on his face that you've never seen there before.
"I don't understand... I *had* the pheromone...."
"Tell me you got the picture..."
"I think it went into the reeds there, on that islet..." (Point North.)
"Looks like it doesn't like to stay out in the open for long." The lieutenant squints where you're pointing.
"You didn't get the picture?"
"No..." He shows you the white slip of photo paper. There's a rainbow of colour -- blue, white, yellow, and brown like a child's painting.
Even a wildlife photographer couldn't make out a familiar form, let alone a gigantic stick insect.
However hard you squint you can't make out anything recognizable, let alone a stick insect.
"What now?" (Continue.)
There's a flicker of a smile on his lips, like he can't believe what he's saying: "We *saw* it -- it was real."
"I should have taken the pheromone from Morell!"
Say nothing, swallow it.
"It's just a blur," he says, looking at the slip of paper in his hand.
"What now..." the old man behind you repeats suddenly. He's put his hand into the ash -- it's dirty and black.
In some kind of strange, semi-catatonic state.
"Our suspect's not looking so good. We should check him over -- also..." He points to the reeds.
"What in the name of *god* was that?"
"Damn, we should have helped the cryptozoologists."

dialoguetext: "Helped them?" He falls silent for a moment. "I don't see what more we could have done?"
"We could have learned something about the phasmid's behaviour. Searched for it with them."
"We should have been more thorough Kim. We should have..."
"You're right."
"I'm not. We should have... it's my fault too." He looks across the water. The slip of photo paper still drying in his hand, hanging despondently for a second.
"I know. We *should* have... It's my fault too." He looks across the water. The slip of photo paper still drying in his hand, just hanging there for a second.
It's too late now.
He subdues the feeling. Dusts himself off and moves on. So should you. There will be other chances.
"A stick insect of some sort. Pretending to be the reeds..." He shakes his head. "Has it been there the whole time?"
You never had a chance. There was something off the moment you approached it. It was scared of you. Of humans.
Reed-like tufts stick out of its joints. As the insect moves its forearms it produces a faint hiss -- like a reel-to-reel machine spinning after the tape breaks.
The segmented antennae move with apprehension, searching for something that's not there...
"Where? Where did it go?" The lieutenant has the camera in one hand -- and a slip of white paper in the other, developing.
"I tried," he explains. "But it was moving too fast. And I didn't get the ampoule in right. And..." He gathers himself. "Dammit. I believe my eyes. It *was* there."
"Damn it! Damn it! I didn't get it right..." [Leave in rage.]
Neither have you. But you know who would -- a cryptozoologist!
A cryptozoologist? Oh god, there was one...
"The cryptozoologist! There was one in the bar. Maybe she knew something?"
"The paraplegic? She could have, yes..." He seems unsure.
"The paraplegic? *Or* the other one on the coast? They could have, yes..." He seems unsure.
We missed it, he thinks. We damn missed a spot. We should have... then the lieutenant collects himself.
"I never thought the damn *cryptozoology* would factor into this... Well, we know it's here now. We *will* find it again."
"Okay, yes, you're probably right."
"Am I?" He shakes his head. "I don't know. I'm not an entomologist! Neither was the para-scientist. The only thing I'm sure of is..."
"It looks like it has some kind of nest there... Maybe there's proof in there."
"It was *definitely* that. He didn't like me. I didn't get to take a single step."
"*Like* you?" He shakes his head in disbelief. "I'm not an entomologist, okay -- neither was the para-scientist. Who knows, maybe you're right. The only thing I'm sure of is..."
Like a little boy... for a moment he's unable to keep it together when he looks at the slip.
"The ampoule will produce a loud hiss." He turns to you and whispers: "You're right. It could scare it away. I need a better moment, when it's not looking."
Something cracks in the lieutenant. He's letting his pride get in the way.
You see the insect turn to him, its mandible antennae reaching out. Its motions are quick, sudden.
(Yell.) "No!"
"What are you talking about, *pheromone*?" The strange state the old man is in ends, momentarily. Something in the word animates him...
"God, I shouldn't have taken a bath! The pheromone washed off!"
You know who would know -- a cryptozoologist!
Your voice echoes alone on the water. Not so much as a scoff from the old man.
"I don't understand... I *had* the pheromone...."
"Dammit. What now?" (Continue.)
"I should have taken the pheromone!"

"I should have helped the cryptozoologists. It's too late now..."

dialoguetext: It's not use telling him...
"The cryptozoologist... there was one in the bar. I bet she knew something..."
"What was what?" The straggler looks around. "It's just the reeds, playing tricks on you, droite..."
A cryptozoologist? Oh god, there was one...
Subdue the regret. Dust yourself off, proceed. You'll get it in the next life, where you don't make mistakes. Do what you can with this one, while you're alive.
Looks like you're right. He's extending his hand into the dust now, for some odd reason. Smearing his finger in it, confused like a child...
"No one will believe me... no one will believe this was real."
Wordless, he's staring at the ash. Not responding to your yelling.
...and then he is back to staring at the dust.
Like a junkie...
"I don't..." He's extending his hand into the dust now, for some odd reason. Smearing his finger in it, like a confused child...
"He must be *really* out of it, yelling like that. Well, at least he's *alive*...." Officer Minot in the blue uniform frowns: "Jean, maybe something *happened*? He's in distress..."
Three-hundred metres inland special consultant Trant Heidelstam cups his ear. Satellite-Officer Vicquemare nods to him on the jetty: "I heard it."
"He must be *really* out of it, yelling like that. Well, at least he's *alive*...." Officer Minot in the blue uniform frowns: "Jean, maybe something *happened*? He's in distress..."
Three-hundred metres inland, on the jetty, special consultant Trant Heidelstam cups his ear. Satellite-Officer Vicquemare nods to him: "I heard it."
"Crypto-what?" Some odd connotation catches the old man's ear.
Crypto-*fascist* probably.
The lieutenant had a *camera*. A camera, he could have taken a picture. Now they'll all think you're mad...

"I got it..." You hear the lieutenant whisper, as the creature's shape develops onto photo paper in his hand: a polychrome ghost of white streaks against the reeds and the sky. And you, as a shadow before it.
Immortalized.
For all time.
*Slowly* reach out and touch the creature's whisker.
Carefully pet its scythe-like forearm.
"We got it..." (Back off.)

The antennae hang from a great height. With your hand shaking you barely touch the tip of the left whisker. On contact the chitin curls into a spiral, like the tip of a poison ivy. Its touch on your fingertip feels cold, ticklish...
"Be careful, detective... It's moving."
It is surprisingly delicate -- the curly end of the whisker, like a young bine. It's even a bit wet.
The sensation is electrifying, resounding through your body.
Look at your finger.
It tastes like... sugar. Very faint. The arthropod towers above you, tufts of reeds pointing from limb and head alike.
Odourless, mostly comprised of water.
Lick your finger.
You were right, it glistens with some kind of moisture. The creature in front of you stays frozen...
The limb before you is incredibly light, like eggshell. It's much lighter than a reed. You feel a soft push could tip the creature over, its hollow exoskeleton collapsing...
Here, within the smooth white inner part of its limb you sense... something very intimate. Thoughts.
Warning!
Run your hand up the slender limb, higher...
Pull your hand away.
A small shudder passes the creature's arm. High above you its black pearl-eyes still glisten, mesmerized by the light passing its nervous system.
There is some kind of countdown happening, as it slowly processes the overwhelming brightness of the signal. The invertebrate is regaining control...
The stimulus overloaded it. It's passing, like an extended moment, or a gall stone.
"Lieutenant, it's thinking with its *limbs*."
It's your secret alone.
"The nervous system could be spread out like that..." He whispers behind you. "Over the extremities, like a cuttlefish."
Or a *ryacintha*, an Occidental leaf insect with its brain stored in four leaf-like extensions. Or a mimicry octopus with its intelligent tentacles...
Another shudder passes through the forearm under your palm -- feels like blood pumping through a brain. It's coming to, you withdraw your hand slowly.
A sudden shiver passes the limb. Looks like the creature is awakening, wave by wave from its stupor.
Some sort of countdown process is happening. That's all you have time to think...

Another shudder pulses through the creatures limbs. It jolts back to life, like a record continuing were it left off -- in a swaying, praying motion. Even the small black pearls of its eyes do not stray from you...

A shudder pulses through the creatures limbs. It jolts back to life, like a record continuing were it left off -- in a swaying, praying motion. Even the small black pearls of its eyes do not stray from you...
They are filled with adoration and curiosity. The adoration of some wheel,  or dominion spinning around its parent deity. And the curiosity of a common wasp, tasting sugar in a fizzy drink.
"It's good, it's good," the lieutenant whispers, holding it up. "Don't worry. We got it."
For a moment there, he was afraid you didn't *get it*, but he's calmer now, looking at it.

The arthropod towers above you -- just like in the picture -- oblivious to your chattering. The ventricles on its abdomen slowly expanding, vestigial wings like barely visible gossamer hanging from the inside of its slender joints.
It's about to move, you can sense it!
Don't say it! Are you sure? This may be the only chance you get to touch it...
(I'm sure.) "We got it, Kim..." (Keep backing.)
No, wait...
The arthropod towers above you, frozen in place. A twitch passes one of its hind legs, as you...
Wipe it off.
Feels like nothing. The arthropod in front of you stays frozen...
I want there to be more.
I want to know your mind.
There is no mind to speak of. And if there is, it's beyond your imagination -- too simple to be compatible with yours. Segmented mouthparts foam, it tilts its head.
It is impossible to see inside. There is only chitin, pretending to be reeds -- or polished, like stalks of marble. The occasional series of clicks, undecipherable to the human ear.

What more is there in any of us? You think, as the sight of the insect fades and pain shoots up your right foot and into your abdomen, darkening your view... when it returns the insect twitches, feeling the blood on you...

The sight of the insect pulses with pain, as a streak of fire tries to shoot up your leg. You swallow it. Unmoved. Not now. There's blood dripping... warm.  The creature must feel it too, it twitches.
Mute, the insect foams from its mouthparts, tilting the plates of its fused together head. From left to right, without reason.
I exist.
I exist too.
Tell me what it's like for you.
Now I will tell you what it's like for me. For me it is a series of half-lit images. A kind of darkness, being intruded upon. Transient. Dim. Moist.
Nothing. Its simple eyes give off no flicker of light, no one is home. The twitches of its limbs are insect-like, unknowable, perhaps without substance even.
I want to see inside you.
It's spread too thin among its limbs, performing incomprehensible operations on the world; and you -- looking at it, mouth slightly open... You cannot even imagine what it thinks.
In its marrow -- a combination of complex biomolecules. Hormones, amino acids, lipids.
Another flash of pain. Again you swallow it, but this time, some of it does not stay down. You think you taste it in your mouth. So does the insect, twitching suddenly...
Suddenly -- another flash of pain. Worse than the one before. The taste of blood in your mouth. The insect tastes it too, twitching suddenly...
As you back off the phasmid also takes a step back into the reeds. Something tells you -- the next time you engage and disengage it will probably flee.
Something stirs in the insect as you begin to back off. It seems to also takes a step back... Something tells you -- the next time you engage and disengage it will probably flee.
As you're turning away, the phasmid mirrors your movements, stepping on the water -- the long limbs carry its feather weight without breaking its surface.
Fire, burning.
It's *wunderbar*.
I'm ill.
Not even the birds know that. Not even the water lilies.
Where does this come from? All this? Around us? The world?
Is this a dream? What is happening?
No. You are awake. I am real. Light is forming me. This is real.
Shifting around in the reeds around it, in the muddy water... you notice some of its hind legs apparently standing on the water from time to time. It's *that* light...
And... is that a glimmer in the water, below it? Like plastic? Could it be hoarding something?
"Kim... there's something there."
Not now...
"A nest?" The whisper is anxious. "Don't do anything now. Later, when it's gone maybe..."
Of course, no time. The insect towers above you, parting the reeds it emerged from.
Shapes of plants and animals. And *internal* sensations. A swarm of sounds, tiny vibrations on the inside of my forearms -- all speak of complexities totally beyond my understanding.
What is your illness?
My body aches. I'm bleeding.
I'm ill in my head. I'm insane. That's how it is for me.
In my heart. For me it's sadness -- input after input.
If I tell you, what will happen?
Then I will tell you what it's like for me.
For me it is not like that. I have states, not emotions. For example, I experience excitement at unexpected sugar rewards, but that is not important.
I am not. There isn't even a central nervous system in my head. Only mouthparts for eating wetland plants.
I smelled it, as soon as you stepped on the island -- strawberries. Fresh burst of red strawberries. Ripe turning riper. Soon you will be rotten.
Now I will tell you how it is for me. For me it is a series of half-lit images. A kind of darkness, being intruded upon. Transient. Dim. Moist.
Fire? Where?
Inside.
In the city, all around. It's going *down*.
On the horizon. Pale fire. This thing we're both sensing is coming to an end.
That is your problem. Nothing ever ends for me. There is only room for two, maybe three pictures in my mind.
I am oblivious to the city. It is only on my margins. A ball I sometimes spin. A toy, Or the cylinder of a discarded trash bin.
I do not have fire inside me. In me there is not even blood, but lymph -- like sap from a wine palm.
Yes, holy is the lord of hosts. And all the Earth is filled with his glory.
I am at the end of a narrow funnel. Weightless. So light it only feels like *something* to be me. In truth -- perhaps I'm nothing? I certainly do not have a soul. And if I did, it would never ache.
You're the type of animal I would like to be.
I'm glad to be me -- an incredibly sensitive instrument.
The fuck is happening to me right now?
I don't know. You're just a shadow for me. Far away, faintly transmitting, but for a curious smell.
Are you sure?
A small leg. That's horrible.
That's cool.
Yes. The leg tried to move around independently, making it hard to walk.
Intruded upon -- by what?
For me it is a series of half-lit images. A kind of darkness, being intruded upon. Transient. Dim. Moist.
So what if the next picture doesn't come? This creature is not the photographer, just the camera.
You don't have a foot there now!
Yes, thankfully someone ate it. The next time I moulted I grew an antenna again!
Okay. I don't want to hear more about that.
This would explain its antenna being smaller.
*This* is the explanation I came up with?
Got it. Solved it.
No -- it's what the three metres tall stick insect came up with.
Officially, it was the three metres tall stick insect who solved it.

"Then, I think I'm having a vision. About the final fate of mankind."

This is my masterpiece.
It was very disorienting at first, but I'm keeping my shit together.

Few of us can begin to imagine the horror of you -- with all of creation reflected in your forebrain. It must be like the highest of hells, a kaleidoscope of fire and writhing glass. Eternal damnation.
It's hell. I change my mind. I want to be you.
Even when you're sleeping... And when you wake, you carry it around on your neck. With eyes open that cannot help but swallow more behind the mirror. I feel great, mute empathy for you.

The leg tried to move around independently, making it hard to walk.

Then all we can do is beat our fists against it? Day after day. With no answer.

I am an unknown species of the order Phantasmodea -- endemic to the Insulindian isola. For the last three hundred and fifty years I have hidden in plain sight, masquerading as the reeds. Moulding, cloning myself, unfolding at night to play with trash bins and buoys.

I can't.

In honour of your will, lieutenant-yefreitor. That you kept from falling apart, in the face of sheer terror. Day after day. Second by second.
In honour of your shit, lieutenant-yefreitor. Which you kept *together* in the face of total, unrelenting terror. Day after day. Second by second.

The killer.
Also that.
No one believed I exist -- almost no one. Until you came, detective. Dripping of blood that smells like strawberries. Across the calm sea, the first in a thousand years.

Wait, so...
Too sensitive of a matter.

Very slowly -- and only because he won't go away. It is meant to keep them from noticing me, to interfere with the pictures in their heads. But he has looked at me too long. And I'm destroying him.

I don't have that kind of power.
...how?

I will.

The arthropod follows you with its antennae. As you back off, the cracks and hisses of the tape that's come to its end grow more distant...
"It's gone..." The lieutenant looks north, with his hand raised to his brow.
...and something under it! In the place it stood, bobbing there, among the reeds. A collection of items.

Nothing but you, a detective of the RCM, standing there with your mouth agape.

Everything your eyes touch goes back there -- behind the nerve mirror. What if you blink? Are we still here? (Please don't blink). What if you misplace us all one day -- or just forget?
Instead of air, you exhale thoughts. There are no trees that eat thoughts.
So it is already happening. Soon, one of you will close your eyes -- and open them to see that none of this ever existed.
But I *want* to blink and undo 12 billion years of matter expansion.

dialoguetext: Don't leave any loose ends. Get him on everything.
You've almost got him. Just a last little push...
Tie up every loose end, now. There's no other chance.
Leave no stone unturned! Get him on what matters most!
He heard you. He just wants to hear you say it... you're in!
Damn, he saw you. He's watched it happen.
"And so they did."
He nods. "From nothing to this in a day..." A crooked little smile. "This is *good*, we just need a confession first, and then *maybe* a solid motive later."
"Do you think he did it?"
There is palpable excitement in his tone. He likes him for this -- *a lot*. But there's something more too...
"How do you think the questioning is going?"
"What can I put on him -- to get him to fess up?"
"I'm trying to get him to confess..."
"Yes, good going -- that should be our *first* priority."
"Good." He nods. "We're doing very good. He *wants* to confess -- I can see that. We just need to pile it on, a little more -- the more we have on him, the closer he is..."
"He's a communard. The victim was a mercenary. We should get him talking politics again. You could even tell him we already *have* a motive."
"Okay, let's do this." (Conclude.)
"Remember," the lieutenant whispers. "He wants to tell us -- but he doesn't want to *help* us. It needs to look like we already have everything."

"Ballistics. Let him cook here for a minute or two -- we can have another look around the island for a sniper's nest." He looks to the small tower on the coast. "I think we should check out the post."
It doesn't have to hold in court. Just establish a line of sight and he'll do the rest himself.
"Also, the gun." He smiles very politely. "We should pick it up and discuss it in front of him. Make a show of it."
Yes, sire! Make a production of this examination!
"Well, I can think of one thing. The gun." He smiles very politely. "We should pick it up, and discuss it in front of him. Make a show of it."
He thinks the deserter has more than just this case in him. Forty-four years here...
"You think he has more? Than this case?"
Pat him on the back. [Leave.]
"Oh yes..." He nods. "And -- he hasn't spoken to anybody in a long time. If we get him open, who knows what will pour out..."
You hear that? He thinks you're *this* close...
"I'm slapping myself to get ideas!"
"I can see that, yes. I'm not judging."
"What am I missing? What haven't I done?"

"Ballistics. Let him cook here for a minute or two -- we can have another look at the set-up he had there, with the mattress." He nods southeast to the tower. "Ballistics always impresses these military types."
"Remember," the lieutenant whispers. "He wants to tell us -- but he doesn't want to *help* us. It needs to look like we already have everything."
"We just need to get him back to the mainland." A crooked little smile. "We actually did it..."
"We really did, didn't we?"
"Let's get him back before we congratulate ourselves."
He smiles. "You should be proud. Come on -- let's wrap this up."
"Three weeks ago, when the rich hag came in on her galley. Her honour guard came in tow."
"By that you mean Joyce Messier, the Wild Pines rep?"
"And by that you mean the representative of the harbour company?"
Joyce... he means Joyce.
"Wrinkled up whore," he nods.
That must be the representative of the Harbour company, who came in on her boat.
"Khm..." (Cough.) "Moving on -- the victim arrives some time after her..."
"They moved into a deserted apartment above the roundabout." He nods toward the city. "Radio equipment out for all to see -- reactionary radio playing. Sloppy and drunk."
"I've seen their kind during the Landing. Those Occidental and Mesque falangues weren't conscripts -- boys, like us. They were wights. All they know is to destroy and hurt."
"Wights?"
"Them fucking..." He looks at the charred wood. "I didn't like that."

"That's all it takes for the bullet to reach his head." He squints. "Now that I think of it, I wasn't aiming for his mouth. I wanted his brains to spill out on her... but..." he shrugs, "you can't have everything."
"So you were jealous?"
"Jealousy is a reactionary concept. I didn't *like* the reaver enjoying himself -- drugged out, soothed in the arms of a young woman. I wanted him to die so he could not enjoy life anymore."
"And I wanted her to see his head explode," he nods. "That too. She should know better than to hold a child murderer between her thighs. I knew he'd be there for one more second, *writhing*..."
For him to stop reacting to stimuli, to be broken off from the world. Cordoned into darkness.
"Okay then."
*Splat*, a bloody spitball lands on the firewood.
And now he longs to see her covered in blood.
Her body sweating from the drugs, slick from cerebral haemorrhage.
This man has seen past her, like you did.
He wants to see her covered in blood.
To punish her.
"You wanted to punish her, so you killed him."
"Did you have feelings for that woman?"
"How long had you been watching her?"
"So in conclusion, it wasn't about him. It was about *her*." (Conclude.)
"Her..." He repeats, staring at the ashes -- then the reeds. There's a twitch in the corner of his eye.

"Since she came to Martinaise. I saw her sneaking in the reeds early in the morning, behind the Feld building. It was dark, still winter. She didn't have her skimpy outfit on then, just a spot in the night, moving..."
"Hiding something in the water. She had a fag after she'd done it. I was up in the ruins there -- she couldn't see me, but I could see her. Smoking... she was nervous, but not scared."
"Past the Feld building, on the coast? What was she doing there?"
"What was she doing there?"
And beautiful.
"And beautiful."
"What do you think she hid there?"
"That too," he nods.
"How could you see what she looked like? You said it was dark."
"The sun came up, her hair was like cobwebs. She smoked more fags and snorted a line of whatever shit she was on. Right there..." he shakes his head. "She needed it just to move."
"Her passport. And tickets to Villiers." He coughs. "And from there to Casherbrume."
"This is the hidden buoy she told us about... You looked into it?"
"Some kind of hidden container on the coast? You looked into it?
"After she was gone." He nods.
"Did you keep what was in it? When we found the submersible it was empty."
"No. Why would I do that? I didn't need tickets to Villiers... I put them back. If I wanted to extort someone I'd do better."
"Are you sure? I checked the submersible. There was nothing there."
"Where was this submersible, looks like the investigation missed it?"
"You saw her name on the passport. But before, when I said her name is *Klaasje* -- you didn't seem to recognize it."
"Why would I need that trash?" He looks to the reeds, confused. "I'm not going to Villiers..."
There it is again. The strange neurological state he's sometimes in.
A strange confusion comes over him from time to time. Some kind of aberration of the nervous system?
"Yes. After she'd gone. It was a submersible. Well made, actually..."
"Sloppy, we should have gotten her to tell us about this..." the lieutenant mutters to himself. "Did you take the documents?"
"No. I put them back. Why would I take them, I'm not going to Falne..." He seems confused, momentarily. "Or... I mean..."
"In the water, behind the camp site there," he waves erratically toward the coast. "I don't remember precisely. It was in the winter. It was cold out..."
"It didn't say *Klaasje* in there..." He shakes his head.
"What did it say her name was -- in the passport?"
"It was something else..." He stutters. "I don't remember. It was dark that morning. I only remember her face on the photo."
"Did you keep the materials? When I found the submersible it was empty."
"The sun came up and her hair was like cobwebs. She smoked more fags and snorted a line of whatever *shit* she was on. Right there..." he shakes his head. "She needed it just to move."
"Moving on -- did you continue watching her after this?" (Proceed.)
"I did." He almost smiles. "She had a face like an archipelago, with those birthmarks. And a body, hard and lean and bruised all over -- black and yellow. I could see she's taken a beating."
"Did you take the documents?"
He's setting it up for you...
In the Free State of Semenine. Hidden away at the edge of the Earth, near the pale.
How does he know those minute details about her body?
A little inconsistency -- he was surprised to hear her name Klaasje, before. Would he not have seen it on the documents?
"You could tell she was a *spook* from the documents?"
"I could see who she was, too," he nods. "A spook. On the run. Revachol's the cloaca of capital now. All the bagmen and arms dealers end up here. To do drugs and have sex like animals."
"First -- you could tell she was a *spook* from the documents?"
"She practically breastfed that man. You wouldn't believe the things she let him do to her..." He shakes his head and stares at the ashes.

He must have... climbed to the roof maybe?
"Oh yes," he smacks his lips. "Cutting those drugs of hers into little lines with a knife, masturbating..."
"The bruises on her body -- any chance you've seen them through a *hole in a wall?*"
"Like that too, yes," he nods. "Bending like a bow against the glass..."
"Ever see her through a window, on a roof?"
"You've been through the secret route behind the Whirling-in-Rags." (Move on.)
"I've been through *all* of Martinaise -- every nook and cranny."
"And that too."
"Yes, that too." He shakes his head, almost in awe. "The things they did in that little room. What she'd *do* to feel good..." He explains: "Funny, the way light works..."
"She had different colour hair on the photo, and glasses. *Forged*. Some sordid, bourgeois affair. I've heard about this kind of thing on the radio..."
"And the bruises -- you could see her bruises through the scope of a rifle?"
"You can't see that through a scope. It's just a blur there..." He shakes his silver-grey head.
"I've seen her like that, yes," he nods. "Cutting those drugs of hers into little lines with a knife, masturbating..."
"Mhm," he smacks his lips. "Bending like a bow against the glass..."

"You turn it on inside and it gets so dark out you can't see a man looking in. I learned that in the Twenties when they were still hunting me. I've seen people do *some* shit, but..." He keeps shaking his head.
"You've been through the secret route behind the Whirling-in-Rags." (Move on.)
Everything in him fills with impossible longing, all at once.
You hear the familiar scribble of the lieutenant's pen. A quick glance at you...
One more loose end down. We're doing this, detective.
"One more thing -- the flowers, Mr. Dros. The dried flowers that were on the roof."
"What about them?"
"Did you make that hole?"
"You made that hole?"
"With a clip point knife."

... then at the man. "How did you get in there? The hidden pinball workshop?"

"I can just walk in the hostel now, after a good wash. They all think I'm an antisocial, a vagrant. Closing hour is a good time. The kitchen's empty then."
"You had to open the steel door in the kitchen? How?"

"I got that open a long time ago. Some bourgeois game-merchant lived there -- I don't know... fifteen years ago? He left spare keys all over and I took one. Then I saw her turn the light on one night in my scope..." He points toward the Whirling-in-Rags.
And he found use for it -- a spare key, like the one hanging behind the Union box window.

He must knows his way around a creaky floorboard and a rusty hinge on a door...

On her.

"That fucking whore..." He waves his hand, with sudden anger. Something comes over him...

Say nothing.

Neither does he. He lowers his head, like a sunflower on a withered stalk.

The coals of his eyes glisten suddenly, like stones dripping with water. Is he crying?

"There have been others?"

"I don't understand..." He shakes his head.
"Maybe..." He lowers his head and just stares at the logs. "I told you, I have holes in my brain now. I wouldn't just sit here waiting for you..."
"Maybe..." He lowers his head and just stares at the logs. "I have these... holes in my brain now. I wouldn't just sit here waiting for you..."
"I just got this feeling. From what you said. Do you agree?"

"Woman..." he smiles suddenly.
And inexplicably. It doesn't go with his pained voice.

"I hate women too, you know."

"No one gives a *shit* what you think," the old man spits in the ash. "You and your cronies kill ten working class men a day. I've heard the statistics on Channel 8."
He nods. "Made a little love-nest up there. Sweaty linen and bottles they would use for god knows what... I saw other men there too, but I can't be sure. Even a woman once."
"True, there is something bourgeois about women..." He nods. "The weak are more vulnerable to exploitation by capital, unless they rise up in arms, which the likes of her..." He shakes his head.
You stare at them too. In your mind, Her Innocence Dei still turns to leave, airport bag in hand, silks flowing in her wake...
The dream...
This has got nothing to do with that. (Try to forget it.)
It's no good, Harry. Her voice rings in the evening air. It smells of burning buildings...
See you tomorrow, Harry. Her voice rings in the evening air, burning...
"That kind of thing is fine by the Party so it's fine by me, but it goes to show you..." He just shakes his head.
"A red haired woman? Ruby..."
"*Twisted* by psychopharmaceuticals, alcohol, and the class interests of the bourgeoisie. They all are -- women nowadays..." He raises his eyes from the ashes.
"The world is insane..." He raises his gaze. Something glimmers in there. Then it's gone.
Say nothing.
The old man raises his gaze. Something glimmers in the corner of his black eye...
A bitter taste on his tongue.
"A red haired woman? Ruby..."
Let it be.
"That kind of thing is fine by the Party so it's fine by me. But it goes to show you..." He just shakes his head.
Safe and sound, sire. Surely you have not misplaced the witness.
"She got away. I don't know where she is."
"I arrested her." (Lie.)
"I arrested her."
"I am not at liberty to say."
"She got away, but she led me here first. She figured out someone was watching her from the seafort."
"Gone..." He looks to the city and nods: "I knew it. She kept staring into the scope this last week. At the island, like she knew...." He sighs.
"Good for her..." He looks to the city and nods: "That girl kept staring into the scope, you know -- in the end. This last week, kept staring at the island..."
"Locked up with your masters, like I'll be... maybe we'll meet?" He looks to the city. "She kept staring into the scope, you know -- in the end. Like she *knew*."
"I know she's gone." He looks to the city. "Locked up, or on the run.... She kept staring into the scope, you know. In the end, this last week. At the fort. Like she *knew*."
"You saw through her? So did I."
"Why did you?"
"I was there one night and she was crying. Like a child, in the corner of her room -- on the floor. I'd never seen her do that before."
"You're delusional. There's nothing to *see* in the soul of the bourgeois woman. It's the same as the surface -- sick hedonism and desperation."
The lieutenant nods at you, in acknowledgement.
"Where is she?" The old man looks at you. "I haven't seen her there for days."
"Her..." He repeats, staring at the ashes -- then at the reeds. There's a twitch in the corner of his eye.
You hear a low frequency hiss, barely beneath the audible spectrum. Then it's gone.
You hear a low frequency hiss, barely. Beneath the audible spectrum. Then it's gone.
That's it. Motive. We have it.
"It was about bitches." The boy nods grimly.
There -- motive, detective. We have it.
"At night, crying or smoking on the roof. Like she knew I was here..." He says to no one in particular: "It doesn't matter."
"Staring at the island, the fort, like she knew I was here..." He adds, to no one in particular: "It doesn't matter."
Look east...
Shake it off.
Inside, in a cell, a young woman is withdrawing from amphetamines, barbiturates and alcohol. Shivering, she fades from your mind's eye...

There, on a dilapidated jetty in a nameless village, two police officers and one special consultant look across a narrow strip of sea. The ruins of a seafort stick out of the water, built by Filippe II, re-appropriated by the Commune, then lost in the Landing...
"He's there, doing... *what* exactly I don't know," Satellite-Officer Vicquemare points at the ruins. "Behind that anti-aircraft-something. That's why we can't see him."

Special consultant  Heidelstam is optimistic: "We'll see the boat when he comes. Let's go get a coffee until then. I know this interesting little place, where..." His voice trails off as the three walk down the jetty.
"We could get more..." the lieutenant uses the opportunity to tell you -- in a lowered voice. "We've got him talking..."
"She'd look -- at night, crying or smoking on the roof -- staring right into me..." He adds, to no one in particular: "It doesn't matter."
"Like she *knew* I was here..." He adds, to no one in particular: "It doesn't matter."

Across the harbour, on the South bank of the River Esperance, white snow falls on a two story box of duraluminum. Precinct 57, near the gates to Terminal H.

...and knows it's over. They've come for her. Outside it's springtime, the river  flows blue and green into the Bay of Martinaise.

Smaller. Distant. Hidden. Not like the great chandelier she sees sparkle in the dusk below her. Streets, towers, tenements and cold water; and across the water -- a dark strip of ruins barely visible, if she didn't squint her eyes...
