Look north...

Midtown, across the bay of Revachol. Cold rain falls on forty-story towers. Above them -- Lausanne Central Aerodrome; a cocoon suspended in the grey sky by a web of suspension wiring, encircled by hybrid aircraft.
Shake it off.

Midtown, across the bay of Revachol. Snow falls on forty-story towers. Above them -- Lausanne Central Aerodrome; a cocoon suspended in the snowy sky by a web of suspension wiring, encircled by hybrid aircraft.

Midtown, across the bay of Revachol. The oceanic wind washes forty-story towers. Above them -- Lausanne Central Aerodrome; a cocoon suspended in the sky by a web of suspension wiring, encircled by hybrid aircraft.
Good bye, Martinaise.

Across the water, on a dilapidated jetty in a nameless village -- made of grey cinder block houses with eternite roofs -- two police officers and one special consultant look across a narrow strip of sea.
As the men go, Patrol Officer Minot looks back over her shoulder -- at the crumbling fortification in the rain, like a rotten tooth rising out of the water...
As the men go, Patrol Officer Minot looks back over her shoulder -- at the crumbling fortification in the snowfall, like a rotten tooth rising out of the water...
As the men go, Patrol Officer Minot looks back over her shoulder -- at the crumbling fortification, like a rotten tooth rising out of the water...
Good luck, Harry, she thinks. You need something *good* for this...
The old man falls silent. Staring at your feet, the burnt logs.
You could get more out of him... He likes talking.
*Enough*. Take him in. Bend his arms behind his back and end this.
Who knows what he's seen and done over the years?
"Barely alive. They like to kill while they're on their drugs. After the landing, in the burning years I would take shots at them, *end* them. The worst ones. If I had a bullet to spare."
"I could see they've returned now. To show their real face -- the face they don't dare show their bourgeois voters back on Mundi, with their families and polyester clothes..."
"Rich hag?"
"Wrinkled up whore," he nods.
"What is it with these *whores* and *pederasts*... aren't you a communist?"
"Whore. Good strong word. I use it often myself."
"Yes," he nods enthusiastically. "Old-fashioned."
"Lax sexual morals are a bourgeois ploy," he gargles a spit ball. "As to pederasty, the Party legalized it in '04. My Party, not your liberal masters." He spits it out on the dying coals.
"So don't you sermonize me, you racist shithole." He adds. "It's still bourgeois when the bourgeois does it. Fiddling with their sexual organs..."
Some strange glandular process takes place in him at the thought. Like yeast rising...
An anger too, in addition to loneliness.
"Khm," the lieutenant coughs.
The old man has fallen silent, staring at your feet. The burnt logs in the fire are moist from the sea air.
"She had different colour hair on the photo -- and glasses. *Forged*. Some sort of sordid, bourgeois affair. I've heard about this kind of thing on the radio..."
Joyce... he means Joyce again.
"This is the so-called soucriant again, right? Joyce?"
"You mean the Wild Pines representative again, right?"
"Did you keep the documents in it?"
"Did you keep the materials?"
"Yeah." Cuno nods knowingly. "The lightning gets shit going. Speedfreaks fuckin' in the bushes..."
"You climbed, right? You *climbed* behind her window, like the CRAB-MAN?"
"You've been through some secret route shit, huh? *Inside* the Whirling-in-Rags, creepin' around?"
"I've been through *all* of Martinaise -- every nook and cranny."
"Yeah, but that one too, right? Secret Whirling shit?"
"We can totally get more out of him..." the kid whispers. "He's squeelin'..."
"Got it."
"Herding the strikebreakers like that -- I kept an eye on them." He stares inland, then back at you.
One little thing -- what was her *name*, on the passport. Just curious...
Those two took the cake.
Thank god, the lieutenant is picking it up...
Thank god, the kid is picking it up...
"I don't really know. I was there one night and she was crying, like a child -- in the corner of her room, on the floor. Like she does sometimes...."
"Why then?"
Seems like the answer was yes.
"Let's talk about something else for now."
He draws shallow breaths.
He draws shallow breaths.
"Let's talk about something else for now."
The calibre of bullet he used does not do that kind of damage.
While he stands here and rots.
He knew she knows. She was looking at the island, figuring it out -- day by day, cigarette by cigarette...
"More specifically?"
"A tragicomedy..." He shakes to life. "Druggies, prostitutes and rentiers."
Animated? By what?
Perhaps. But his seems more than that. The inner turmoil takes unexpected turns, as if forced on him in a way...
Is it some kind of substance damage? Like he's addicted to something -- not only the painkillers he's clearly on.
For a sixty-year-old man with stomach trouble -- who's spent his entire life alone on an uninhabited island -- he seems surprisingly fit.
That's it? (Squint at him.)
He's clearly a drug user of the painkillers sort, prone to erratic hand gestures -- and malnourished. But that's it. The moment passes and you say...
Aside from the rare erratic hand gesture, smacking his lips and despondently staring into the fire, you can only see that he is old.
He's prone to erratic hand gestures -- and clearly malnourished. But that's it. You can see no more by looking at his slouched frame. The moment passes and you say...

What strikes you about this gaunt man is not the stomach pain, or the cough, or the malnutrition. It's precisely what you could *not* see before. For a man who's spent 44 years hidden in the urban wild...
What strikes you about this gaunt man is not the stomach pain, or the cough, or the malnutrition. For a man who's spent 44 years hidden in the urban wild...
Indeed. He speaks fluidly, his movements are rapid, if erratic. His voice, despite the cough, is there. It is capable of expressing complicated ideas. Above all, he seems *animated*.
He is surprisingly okay.

It's a mystery. This animation comes at a cost too: erratic hand gestures, thought processes cut off like threads, as he just stares at the logs or the reeds. He also suffers mood swings, bubbling to the surface, unconstrained by his nervous system.
Dementia?
You've seen demented people before. This feels similar, yet different. When his thoughts move they are lucid, keen even -- not senile.
And also flashes of lust, simmering in there. Not too common in people his age.
Great leaps of emotion: from anger to grief, despair...
"Mr. Dros, are you on some kind of a psychoactive substance?"
Wouldn't a foul temper be a by-product of his life?
The lust. Wouldn't his *glands* have... stopped by now?
There is definitely something hormonal there. Whatever the condition he's suffering, there is a sexual element to it.
"No!" he snaps out of staring through you. "I won't be stuffed full of shit like the rest of this city."
In summary, you sense some underlying neurological disorder.
"How about pyrholidon?"
"You said you take painkillers..." The lieutenant follows your lead.
"I take them to cope with pain. The people of this city use painkillers, because they have *pain*. Untreated illnesses, not enough money for a greedy doctor."
It's not a downer. Rather an upper, judging by his snaps.
"I don't know what that is..." He shakes his head.
He is indeed very lucid at times..
Are you sure about him being lucid? Maybe he's just affected by an extreme case of *socialism*.
"Are you on amphetamines?"
"Like some kind of decadent rock star?" He doesn't dignify it with more of an answer.
"Mr. Dros, are you okay? How is your memory?" (Finish the examination.)
Didn't he say...
"You said you take painkillers..."
No matter.
"No I'm not *okay*..." He waves his hand, chasing something that's not there. "I shit blood and I'm surrounded by insane people..."
There it is again -- erratic hand motions. Bouts of rage. And the stomach thing too of course...
Could it be a symptom of overdosing on something? Something even you have not tried? Keep your eyes peeled.
"Imbeciles..." The old man in the dirty tracksuit trousers stares at you, panting from hatred. A gust of wind blows in from the sea, bending the reeds behind him...
"Yeah, wait. We have more serious things to discuss."
The familiar *put put put* of hatred.
"Specifically, the whole city is a charnel house, stripped clean and draped in neon. But Martinaise..." he shakes his head in grave disgust, "Martinaise is the worst."
"Yes, the fly larva in his container. He let some nihilistic advertising yuppies erect a statue of Filippe III -- a syphilitic murderer -- on the town square. To spit on the working class."

"Not since the serfs of ancient Perikarnassis has History produced a more *inert* social class than the Martinaise proletariat. The rest of Revachol at least *pretends* to rebuild, these people still live in ruins..."
"Anything more?"
Let him finish, do not interrupt.
"The worst of them is the blood-drenched *soucriant* on her yacht, licking her lips. The old whore's gone now, her gun toting porcelain men are dead -- so, actually, no..."
"That all?"
Nod.

"The *worst* is that old cock parading around in his uniform, throwing balls all day. It's not enough that the racists and liberals are dancing on our graves! The old loyalist ghouls still parade the ruins too."
Detest pushes the cobwebs out of his eyes, pushes the melancholy aside. He relishes it.

"In tents, like animals..." He points to the church. "Like those boom-boom-morons on the ice. A pity they didn't drown in that tent of theirs." He keeps shaking his head with sorrow for the sight he missed.

"Every morning he's there. While the parasites he fought to protect are off in Ozonne, or Croyant-Morain, or some other island they've built their palaces on. Feeding on drugs and having sex with their own children."

"That's all the rich *really* want -- sex with their own children. Throughout history -- even the royal bloodline of the Suzerain! --  it's all just an excuse for them to have sordid sex. At least that old cunt Frissel is now dead..."
Just nod.
"We did good when we pushed him under that horse car. If only... in the Thirties, those *disco whores*..." What follows is ominous mumbling. You cannot make out a single word.
The disco whores are too much; hatred shuts down his brain's language centre, leaving only a nonsensical sputter.
"Disco... whores?"
"Hmmm... and the racist on the gates, pumped full of steroids?"
"There was something about the statue on the roundabout -- and syphilis?"
"You mentioned the Union is social-democratic -- and Mr. Claire a farce of a social-democrat."
"The *boom-boom-boom morons* on the ice..."
"The blood-drenched soucriant on her boat -- what is a soucriant?"
"By the 'cock parading in his colourful uniform,' you mean *René*?"

dialoguetext: "I'm glad we talked about this. Now..."
"Glad? It's all gone..." He stares into the dust at his feet. Grey and dirty spring grass all around.
"Mhm. Now -- I have some questions about this..."
"We did good when we pushed him under the horse car. Until, in the Thirties, those disco whores..." He breathes in, his breath heavy with hatred, you cannot make out a single word.
A strange little engine seems to fire up in him again. It straightens his back.
"How come?"

"Because of the *racists*. Everyone is a racist in Martinaise, it's their favourite thing to do in the whole world -- listening to race-themed radio shows. In the ruins, in their lorries." He points inland.
"Pumped full of steroids and Radio Revachol '92. Race this, race that... It's all sanctioned by that social democratic Union and the farce of a social democrat who runs it..."
"Mr. Claire?"
"Parody of a social democrat?"
"Whores..." is all he says. Even that word has to be pushed through his teeth with great force. The rage seethes too hard.
"Yes -- *steroids*. A racist on steroids."
"No," he answers for you. "The rich man's looking at real estate and fiddling his kids. Wading through the corpses..."
"You're right. I too am a level headed moral person, unaffected by Measurehead."
"I for one *do* have an opinion on Measurehead that people need to hear. And it's not positive."
"Did you notice that he is not..." (Point toward the general area of your face.)
"You mean Measurehead, right? What is your opinion on him?"
"Got it."
"What is my *opinion*? You think the rich man has an opinion on this idiocy? Is the rich man on the radio, telling you his opinion?"
"Steroids and radio shows..." His voice trails off into a despondent sputter. "Probably that Revachol 98AM that's *irradiating* the lumpen, it's the worst..."
"I find it strange that you keep bringing this up. You moralist types are eternally fascinated with these race topics. Helping the ruling class conduct their swindle."
"Old? An alcoholic?" With each word he squints a bit more. "Fascist?"
"Yes."
"No. I meant..." (Keep pointing to your face.) "Generally reddish and pink, like me."
"You're obsessed with your own features," he shakes his head, "because it's all you have left. The rich man took everything from you. Except your bottle."
"And he left you here -- gesturing at your swollen face. The rich man rules over you and over the world. And he laughs at your fidgeting." He stares into the dead embers.
"Not everyone is." He nods. "Most people are *young* and that. The rich man took everything from you, lumpenproletariat. Except your bottle..."
"The rich man doesn't care about *complexion*. He rules the world. And he laughs at your moral soliloquies." He stares into the dead embers.
"Then why was he *there*?"
"Scratching away at the race question... You Moralintern monkeys keep the conversation going on Channel 4, helping the rich man conduct his swindle with this inanity."
Ha, yes, but he was *there*. Why was he *there* if you can't have an opinion?!
"You think the rich man cares about your little race games? He rules the whole world. And he laughs at your moral soliloquies." He stares into the dead embers.
"You moralist types are all cryptofascists, eternally fascinated with lurid race topics. Helping the ruling class conduct their swindle, keeping the inane conversation going on Channel 4."
"And your race garbage. You can keep that too, keep the conversation going for the rich man, on Channel 4, eroding working class solidarity." He stares into the dead embers.
Now wait a moment. Let's get serious here.
"Let's get serious for a moment. This is the *real world* -- and in the real world it *means* something if your skin is a certain colour and you say things."
Yeah no. Enough of that, this isn't going anywhere.
"By the way, I have internalized his *weltanschauung*."

"I've seen the *real world*. In '06. The flags unfolding. Young people marching, being kind to each other. They dreamt of a million years in the stars. This here..." He looks down at the ashes. "Is pale in waiting."
"Oh, I'm sure you have *all* internalized your fair share of *racism* at the RCM. You don't have to tell me. It shows. Can't stop talking about some kind of head-measuring man..."
The lieutenant gives you a nod. Go on, he seems to say.
Keep talking about the head-measuring man. Politics yields information from this man, gets him spilling facts.
"The end." He nods. "The pale will swallow all of this. The water, the sky, the city. Soon. There is nothing to be serious about." He shakes his head. "We're all gone."
"Got it."
"Pale in waiting?"
"They're morons, duped by bourgeois culture. What *more* is there to say? I've seen their kind -- pop up, like worms after the rain." He makes an erratic gesture of annoyance.
"Your beloved *Joyce Messier*. A soucriant. A blood sucker. Women like her *feed* on the life energy of young working class men. And they *let* her."
"A soucriant, a blood-sucker, the rich whore on her boat."
"Oh, you mean Joyce."
"Oh, you mean the company representative."
"Women like her *feed* on the life energy of young working class men." He nods. "And they *let* her...."
"Your beloved *representative of the harbour company* is a soucriant. I saw her. Women like her *feed* on the life energy of young working class men. And they *let* her."
He *could* be referring to Joyce in her youth. They must have listened to disco when they came here... but it's hard to say.
Or maybe it's just his body and mind giving up on him, at last...
"Syphilis is a disease Filippe III contracted in a whore house," he fires quickly. "The statue is an abomination."

"The bacteria entered his brain and made him squander trillions on sparkling wine, *cocainum*, and monuments of himself. His son Filippe IV the Insane contracted syphilis in the womb..." he breathes in with a wheeze of hatred.
"Abomination?"
"Good. Now that that's settled..."
"Mhm," he sputters attentively.
"And he *still* went on to govern Revachol for twenty five years! We lost 2 million lives toppling that mode of government -- and those grotesque statues too, hundreds of them..."
"But it's still there."
"What a keen remark!" He sputters. "Yes it is, isn't it?! It's still there. Do you know *why*?"
That is technically possible, although Filippe III was not actually syphilitic, he was just mad.
"Because you forgot to take it down?"
"Because cynical advertising yuppies erected a *deconstructed* version of it."
"I don't know."
"Because the king is holy and his statues are indestructible."
Say: "Because the king is holy and his statues are indestructible." (But mean it ironically.)

"Forgot?!" he spreads his arms. "The Party had each of the 141 Filippian monuments detonated with plastic explosives. We were *pedantic* about carrying out the order. No..." He points toward the city.
"Some advertising cockroaches used their accumulated capital to erect a new, ironic version of it." He shakes his head in disgust: "Art is a bourgeois establishment. It's an affront to humanity."
Wait, the bullet hole in Filippe's heart! The statue had been shot -- that was him!
It had to be, he's already proven capable of taking a far more complicated shot from here.
The bullet hole in Filippe's heart... he'd been shot in the heart. By him?
"Actually, it was not de-constructed so much as *captured in the moment of the explosion*."
"It was you. You shot the statue -- there was a bullet hole in his heart..."
"That's it for the statue then. Tell me, Mr. Dros..."
Forget about that! Something much more noteworthy goes off in your brain! Could it not have been that...
"What are you talking about?" The ancient communard cocks his head.
"It's not a monument to Filippe III anymore -- it's a monument to the monument of Filippe III exploding."
"What is this madness?" A dim light comes on in his eyes...
"It's not madness. It's a monument to what you did. To your program of de-statuing Revachol."
"So you're saying it's... a *communist* monument now?"
"Yes, and furthermore -- the design bureau people are probably left wing too. They often are."
"The king was a congenitally deformed adulterer. The Party had his monuments detonated with plastic explosives. That one was *especially* destructible..." He points toward the city.

"That's right. Some *advertising* cockroaches erected a cynical, *deconstruction* of it. We tore it down with honest working class plastic explosives -- and there it is again..." He shakes his head in disgust.

"Until some *advertising* cockroaches used their accumulated capital to erect a new, ironic version of it." He shakes his head in disgust: "Art is a bourgeois establishment. It's an affront to humanity."
"Art is a bourgeois establishment. It's an affront to humanity. Every gallery should be bulldozed and the artists should all be given 30 years of hard labour in Yekokataa."

"No, cynical *design* cockroaches like you erected a new, ironic version of it. We tore it down with honest working class plastic explosives -- but there it is again, grinning..." He shakes his head in disgust.

"I do. Some *advertising* cockroaches used their accumulated capital to erect a new, ironic version of it. We tore it down with honest working class plastic explosives -- but there it is again, grinning..." He shakes his head in disgust.
Wait! It suddenly strikes you... perhaps it was not as it seemed?
"Never mind."
"Delusional art bourgeois..." He waves you off.
The lieutenant, too, has cocked his head and is looking at you with a strange expression.
"Yes."
Not only.
"I don't know. Maybe it's too far fetched."
"We did always have the prettiest posters... Maybe you're right." His eyes fill with understanding. "That *is* how dialectics work. But understand this -- art is *still* a bourgeois institution."
"Maybe you're right..." His dark eyes fill with the sudden understanding. "That *is* how dialectics work. But understand this -- art is *still* a bourgeois institution."
He coughs, then adds, in a gravelly voice. "And they should all still be sent to Yekokataa."
"Of course it is. Delusional bourgeois musings. Everything is some kind of *subversion* on the way to the bank." He waves you off. "All artists -- on a train to Yekokataa."
"Of course. Straight to Yekokataa."
"I don't know about that. Could we not?"
"You know, you don't sound like a liberast anymore. Maybe I was wrong..." He measures you with his black eyes. "Maybe I will be escorted to prison by another Mazovian communist -- as I should."
"Yes, well..." the ancient communard sizes you both up, not sure what to think of it.
"Typical far left treachery, repressing your own people."

"It is *commonplace* to relocate the workforce according to the needs of the land. All nations do it. It's called settlement." He shakes his head and mumbles: "Browbeating from the bourgeois art-fascist..."
"Straight to Yekokataa for this old revisionist." He gives you a little nod. "At last -- atonement for my sins: revisionism, reactionary ideation, desertion..."
"As you ought to. *Communism* style."
"You're wrong. I'm no communard. I'm a cop."
"For a middle-class cop you're damn good at getting information out of an old revisionist deserter. Go ahead," he gives you an acknowledging little nod.
He still refuses to believe you subscribe to Mazovian socio-economics, but entertaining the thought has given him some measure of solace.
Camaraderie even. For a second there he feels less alone -- but then the second passes.

"Don't be squeamish. It is *commonplace* to relocate the workforce as the need arises. All nations do it. It's called settlement." He shakes his head and mumbles: "Some kind of bourgeois art-fascist..."
"Mhm," the lieutenant hums. "Straight to the open pit mine. Or cleaning up radiation in Severnaya Zemlja."

Don't think this helmet would have helped me anyway. (Look down at your wound.)
Can't do anything about it now.
And maybe scared the enemy combatants...
That's a good attitude to take. I like it. Keep it up, and keep the helmet handy.
Exactly. But no use crying over spilt milk. Keep up the pace. Only forward.
[Leave.]
O glorious Falnier! You wear the full set like a true-born hero. The *ULTIMATE PERFORMANCE* of FALN flows in you.
You are the most *Ultra* of men. Peak performance!
Go on! The fucking sunset awaits, FALN rider!
I feel... so *dynamic*.
I look so *futuristic*.
You are Next Century personified, the synthetic man!
It's like I can do anything. *ANYTHING*!
You are literally untouchable. A god among mere men.
"Fuckin'... May bells everywhere."
"Empty... Gotta look elsewhere, piggo."
"Got the fucking fuel, yeah."
There's a rain-soaked mattress on a concrete slab, only half-covered by the crumbling roof. At the head of it -- double embrasures -- firing slits, like two eyes in the wall.
"B triple prime..." The lieutenant lowers his voice, stepping closer with his hand on his gun. "This looks like a good place to shoot from."
Look through the hole in the concrete.
Inspect the mattress.
The springs screech as you lean on the mattress and crane your neck to look out...
Trepidation. A tingling feeling in your stomach...
A single-person mattress. Modern, civilian use. Brand name: Marjorie. There's a fuel stain on the cover, along with cigarette burns.
Pick one out of the can.
Back off.
A small piece of Martinaise coastline opens up in the square in front of you -- like a tiny landscape painting, one kilometre across the water. The ruins look familiar.
The red chimney and collapsed rear wall of the four-story tenement in front of the Whirling-in-Rags -- Rue de Saint Ghislaine 10.
A towering skyscraper, its top floors shaved off by artillery fire -- Capeside Apartments: Rue de Saint Ghislaine 33A and 33B.
On the left...
On the right...
And between the two...
The box-shaped silhouette of the Whirling-in-Rags. Its sloped roof. A tiny fleck of light catches your eye on the rooftop -- sunlight reflecting off the upstairs window of Klaasje's room.
"Motherfucker."
"There it is."
"I can't be 100% certain, but..."
"What? Do you have line of sight to the window?"
"Do you have line of sight to the window?"
"Kim, with a pair of binoculars, I would be able to see *inside* the room."
Whenever you wanted. Like your own little dollhouse...
"A pair of binoculars? Or a scope of a *rifle*?" He points to the makeshift bed. "You'd be prone, lying on the mattress, barrel resting on the embrasure..."
"Yes -- there's an opening between 33A and 10. I can see to the roof."
More than that.
Cheek against the cheek rest, hand on the hair trigger. On a calm day like this...
"Kim, I could make it -- I could make the shot."
I don't want to boast...
"Good." He pats you on the back, three small pats in a row. "I think we have it, detective. The origin of the shot. This is the *sniper's nest*."
"*Why* didn't we come here before?"
"That embrasure... What can you see through it?"
This is B triple prime -- on the island... A nest.
And an empty can of beans on the ground next to it -- filled to the brim with cigarette butts.
The silhouette of a tobacco picker adorns the paper filter. The brand: Tioumoutiri.

Contemporary Revacholians prefer Drouin (a local blend from the southern islands) or Astra, the legendary cigarette from Graad. Tioumoutiri is favoured by older men for its paper filter tips, sweet smell, and added tar.
"Tioumoutiri. Like the ones we found at Land's End, remember?"
"I saw the same brand of cigarettes extinguished in Land's End." (Point west.)
"Someone's been smoking Tioumoutiri cigarettes. Not a lot of that around."
"I may have been wrong -- when I said it was unimportant." He stares into the can for a second. "This means the same person could have visited both locations."
"Could be a coincidence. Or -- the same person has visited Land's End and..." He looks around, "...here."
"I didn't see any signs of smoking inside, though. If people live there, they keep it tidy -- this here may also be a smoking spot."
"Someone's been smoking Tioumoutiri cigarettes."
[Turn away.]
"No, wait." He points to the embrasure. "This is important, I have a feeling... What can you see?"
"A good place to hide. Cosy. Relatively safe from the rain..." He pokes the mattress.
A good place to hide. Relatively safe from the snow and the rain...
"This looks like a good place to aim from..." The lieutenant looks around. He steps closer with his hand on his gun.
He nods. "The smoker's a clean person. I didn't see any signs of smoking inside. Keeps it tidy -- prefers to come out here to smoke."
"What does that mean? Do you have line of sight to the window?"
"I think we have it. The origin of the shot -- this is the *sniper's nest*." He pats you on the back, three small pats in a row.
What are you talking about -- "Can't be certain?" It's certain.
"I can see it," he nods. "Through the scope of a rifle. The shooter would be prone, lying on the mattress, barrel resting on the embrasure."
"Why? We don't go everywhere in a thousand metre radius of the crime scene. That's not procedure."
"Better late than never."
"Finally."
"Boo-yah. Master cop work."
He nods. "Nothing pointed here -- many leads pointed elsewhere."
"Six people are dead. We could have prevented it."
"Don't beat yourself up, officer. We did not put guns in their hands, or get them drunk." He looks north, over the fortification, then adds:
"It's only *moderately* effective cop work until we have the weapon. It will not be, how do you say it..." He looks north, over the fortification. "*Boo-yah*, until we have that..."
"You're right."
He looks north, over the fortification. Then at the mattress.
"We will make up for it. Here. I feel it."
The lieutenant pauses. Regret comes over him.
He's conflicted for a second. There's guilt there, it takes him a moment to rationalize it away.
I could take the shot.
This is where the shot came from...
Cheek against the cheek rest, hand on the hair trigger. On a calm day like this...
...but not with 100% certainty.
The wind blows suddenly. The clear surface of the water shudders. Yes. This is it.
Is the shooter still here?

dialoguetext: The wind picks up slowly. The clear surface of the water shudders. Yes. This is it.
In the North, something moves. Leaving circles on the water. Long stalks in the shallows...
"Where?" He looks behind his back.
"In Martinaise."
"On this island."
"Right *here*." (Point at the mattress.)
"You think so?" he whispers, pointing to the mattress. "We would *see* them if they were here."
Perhaps it's a...
"No, officer. It's not an *invisible* shooter. But..." He lowers his voice even further. "This island, on the other hand..."
"But." He lowers his voice again. "This island on the other hand..."
"I have always assumed it's someone local." He nods.
He does not answer, just nods. With his back hunched, he looks around once more and says...
"We should move. Now."
"Or *she*." He almost whispers. "We should move."
"You think he's here?"
No answer comes. Not even a whisper on the water.
YES.
"Anything?"
"Someone been hidin' here like a bitch," he whispers. "Maybe  jerkin' off too?"
A rain-soaked mattress on a concrete slab. In front of it -- double embrasures -- firing slits like two eyes in the wall.
"Where?" Cuno looks around the small compartment-sized room.
"Motherfucker."
"There it is."
"I can't be 100% certain, but..."
"Motherfucker?" He sounds excited. "You seein' the window or not?"
"There what is, the window?"
"You see the window or not?"
What are you talking about -- "Can't be certain?"
More than that.
"Cuno fucking knew it. This a sniper's nest, right? Fuckin' assassin action... Cuno *barely* understands what's happening -- but he likes the shit out of it."
"In Martinaise."
"On this island."
"Right *here*."
"Yeah, detective Cuno thinks it's some local asshole too. These people are rats..."
"Right fucking on." He stops. A shudder.
"You see someone here?" He points to the mattress. "Fuckin' invisible shooter? Spooky shit..."
"No, but what about..." He points to the embrasure. "What's out there?"
No. You feel there's something important here.  The embrasure. Look again...
"Let's get a move on. We're out in the open here..."
"Yes -- there's an opening between 33A and 10. I can see to the roof."
"Cuno, with a pair of binoculars, I would be able to see *inside* the room."
"Someone's been smoking here."
"An old man's brand of cigarettes...."
"Our shooter's a heavy smoker."
"Tioumoutiri. Like the ones we found at Land's End, remember?"
"Yes. This guy gets around."
"Noted." The lieutenant stares into the can for a second.
Say nothing, drop the cigarette back into the can.
The same rare brand... from Land's End, before. Interesting.
"Yes. It all adds up." He stares into the can for a second.
Affirmative.
"Why not? We have the weapon and ballistics. As you say it's..." He looks north, over the fortification. "Pretty *boo-yah*."
Then again... his face twitches.
He feels... uncomfortable suddenly.
He feels... uncomfortable suddenly.
Inspect the wall.
Touch the concrete first.
Quite old, and grimy from years without cleaning by anything other than the rain.
Got you. [Leave.]
There's a firing slit in the wall in front of you. Like a little window...
"In our defence -- nothing pointed here. Many, many leads pointed elsewhere."
"Stop, this is the police!" (Get between them.)
(Whisper.) "Let's walk away for now."
"No," the lieutenant says firmly. "We have to step in. This is not going to end well if we don't..."
"Get lost, comedian. You cops had your chance. Now it's fucking time for some justice." He licks his lips, waving his gun at the crowd. Losing his balance for a moment, he staggers backward.
"Listen! They didn't do it!"
"You're all drunk, look at yourselves!"
Stand there quietly; hope nothing bad happens.
"Fuck, there's a third one... How did we miss something like this?" The lieutenant points to the helmeted figure.
Shoot Kortenaer.

dialoguetext: "The Wild Pines rep does not approve of this!"
With a crash of shattering glass and a terrible roar the fire draws in oxygen -- the bomb hits the mercenary in the chest,  swallowing him in flames as he staggers backward.
No. It's off. *Way* off. I told you.
"...*PIGFUCK!*" The voice from beneath the helmet interrupts your thoughts. You only make out the last word.
There is a hole in his cheek. Blood gushes out as he stumbles backward, eyes filled with rage and disbelief -- gurgling, muttering something unintelligible...
"Go ahead. Give it another try." The man doesn't even move. He’s smiling.
"They teach you to shoot the chest in copland? Stupid fuck..." The man shrugs and turns to his left and says: "Kill him."
IT'S A *FIASCO*, BRATAN!
'I only ever wanted you to have fun, Harry!' it calls out to you. One last time.
To your right, the killer raises his rifle and takes aim at you. His moves are steady, but the long barrel of the rifle sways slowly...
Dodge the shot.
You leap left. A swarm of angry lead passes mere millimetres from your side, tearing fabric off your coat. Feels like the lightest of tucks.
The shot rings and you stumble. Something violently tugs at your shoulder, pushing you backwards with incredible force.
A plume of smoke and fire erupts from the gun and your hand goes numb from the explosion...
A small explosion expels the bullet from the chamber. With a puff of smoke it hits the man square in the chest -- producing a soft clicking sound in the armour.
A low shot rings. You feel a tapping, like rain on your chest plate. Heavy drops of rain. Then the sound of dice rolling, as the cuirass distributes the shot evenly from plate to plate.
"God, please..." the lieutenant says quietly, without trembling. He aims, face pale...
Blood gushes from the helmet's eye-sockets as Ruud staggers back, disoriented. The sounds coming from his helmet are not human.
Then -- two shots ring at once. One from the lieutenant's pistol and the other from De Paule's. It's aimed at the lieutenant, but it misses. You hear a scream behind you...
Glen -- dying in a puddle of blood behind you. His mangled torso has two gunshot wounds, blood gushes out of them like red geysers.
You see two cold eyes looking at you -- through all the smoke and the panic. And a pistol, raised, aiming at your chest, point blank. Then the man squeezes the trigger...
Evade the shot.
You can't. There is no time. Something inside your pelvis explodes. Your entire lower body is on fire and your legs can't support you... you fall down like a rag doll.
The Hardie boys are screaming, fighting, dying. Someone jumps over you -- nearby gunfire shatters glass.
"You're bleeding out!" Nothing. Darkness, blurring lights of pain. Out of it, a silhouette emerges -- crouching over you. A familiar voice, filled with urgency and fear.

But you can't. It's so hard. Your eyelids grow heavy and the sounds ever more distant. And a cold comes over you. The lieutenant, too, is somewhere far away. Almost gone... when suddenly! You sense something behind him...
A slender white shadow, towering. Someone stands there -- raising her pistol at him. The lieutenant does not see it. He's pushing down on your wound with both hands...
No!!! Kim...
"No," you scream: "BEHIND YOU!" from your bloody lips. Your eyes are full of fear.
"There... behind..." You hear your bloody lips mumble, but he does not understand. He does not look into your eyes and see the fear there. He does not trust you.
Like a pillow, he falls on you. Cold nylon and blood slumped on you, as the lights go out. All the lights. The last thing you hear is the sound of his spectacles landing on the pavement next to you.
This is death. One more door, baby. One more door.
Good, I want to die.
No. Let me back into the fight.
It's *STILL* not over, he's hurting now. Deep inside, the minuscule matter which you are composed of persists. The ride never ends. It just gets harder.
"Think you can hang our brother and then just fucking *talk* your way out of it?" His eyes flash.
Throw the gun at him: "Die!"
The weapon bounces off his shoulder. He turns to his left and says: "Kill him."
Look through the smoke rising from the barrel.
Look at Kortenaer.
The smoke drifts west with the wind. You hear the plaza erupt in violence, slow, like a waterfall in reverse.
His lips -- moving, swollen with fear -- are trying to say: 'Shoot him, shoot him!', but he can't.
Blink -- think!
You stare down the barrel of the gun. You see Ruud's mask behind it -- his eye in the slit of the helmet. Like a camera lens focusing on you.
Is there anything -- *anything* -- we could use to protect this frail body? That gun will tear us to pieces.
Kim! Where is Kim?!
From the corner of your eye you see the lieutenant raise his pistol -- and aim it at Ruud.
The pain flows over your entire body like an awful shock. A grim knowing rises from within -- half of your body must be gone.
Joy! I am alive!!!
The man tilts his head, trying to see through the clearing smoke -- for the *next* shot.
OH GOD! WATCH OUT!
Who screamed?
You see two crazed eyes stare at you -- through the burning meat and the flames. With his face boiling off the man raises his pistol at you. Then he squeezes the trigger...
You see two crazed eyes stare at you -- through all the smoke and the panic. With blood gushing from his face the man raises his pistol at you. Then he squeezes the trigger...
Look him in the eye.
Here it comes. Death.
The pain is too immense to scream. It pushes the air out of your lungs. Everything goes dark, a distant blur as you recede into it...
Listen... *through* the darkness and the pain.
(Try to open your eyes.) What do I see?
Touch your lower body...
The Hardie boys are yelling. Someone is running, jumping over you. In the background you hear gunfire shatter glass -- and then a man in pain. A familiar sound.
It's Titus. With a splat like meat, you hear bullets rip into him. His voice, still giving orders, grows fainter... A gurgle...
Nothing. A persisting darkness. Dancing lights of pain. Distant shadows cast by them, like a hellish play...
"No one wants to *do* anything with me... no one wants to party with me."
"Of course... I get gunned down and die. Sorry fuck..."
"Gunned down in the line of duty... it's okay."
"The wolf is at the door, Kim. He will eat the sun."
A shadow, towering. Someone stands there -- raising his pistol at him. The lieutenant does not see it. He's pushing down on your wound with both hands...
Just let the darkness take you.
It's not all dark yet. As you're leaving, *he* is in there too, with you. You can *feel* the figure move. And then a distant gunshot. Velvety smooth. Muffled.
Wait!!! I didn't even know your name!
What's wrong with me?
Good bye, necktie!
Your heart is broken, *bratushka*. And it cannot be mended. Believe me, I've tried.
This guy? Well -- his face has *cracked open* into a scream of terror. It looks like he's performing some sort of a shamanistic dance... that requires you to be on fire?!
What's going on with *that* guy?
What's going to happen now?
I'm sorry. (Conclude.)
*What's going to happen now?* Everyone's going to die, what do you think is going to happen?
Wait! Uh... what's the story between us?!
You were a sad drunk who bought an ugly tie -- who gives a shit! Everyone is going to die because our plan failed. I have *no idea* how you're gonna get out of this. No idea.
"What's the matter, loincloth? Got your mouth full of dick?" He croaks. "Think I'm gonna spare you?! My brother is dead..."
Shit, this is it. Tell him anything, tell him you have more information!
"Kill me and you'll never find out who killed your colonel. I've been withholding information."
"Go ahead then. Kill me then. I *want* to die."
"Me and Kim are gonna fucking murder you!"
"Ruud..." The man looks to his left. "Kill him."
WATCH OUT! To your left, de Paule is about to take a shot too -- at Kim!
What parts of me are... missing?
"Where is Klaasje? She can explain this."
Kim -- did he hit the rifleman?!
So... it's not going to hit?
"Put your damn gun down." Titus remains calm. "People are gonna get hurt. We need to talk this through, alright?"
"You're all drunk, come to your senses!" She sounds very sure of herself. "You won't gun down seven people in the middle of the street. This isn't a frontier town or a jungle outpost."
"This is a misunderstanding. Nothing irreversible has happened yet. You can just return to your unit and forget all about this."
"The kipt is merciful. Willing to spare us if we just forget about our murdered and humiliated commander." Her tone is frighteningly emotionless. "I think we should just kill everyone, Korty."
*Kipt* is a pejorative term used to describe people of Semenese descent.
"Easy, Lizzie..." His voice is almost gentle. "Let me handle it. I know guys like this. I'm sure we can come to a peaceful agreement. Ain't that right, fellas?"
"He's dangerous..."
"Kim, what's going on here?"
The lieutenant is genuinely worried for his life. You should consult him before getting in there.
"Easy now... No one needs to die here today..."
"No one is going to kill anyone. Let's just put the guns down and talk like civilized human beings."
With a wordless gurgle, the killer loads his long rifle...
"I can see you're drunk."
Say nothing, cross your arms.
"Oh, people are gonna die today. We're not leaving it like this. These *tribals* hung him up for everyone to see..."
"Oh yeah, welcome to the fucking party." He looks around. "You're probably gonna get killed too, I don't give a shit if you're cops."
"You..." Kortenaer turns his bloodshot eyes to you.
The leader gives a small nod to the helmeted man. Suddenly the blue medicinal spirit in your hand seems to have a pulsating glow. It feels enticing somehow...
The leader gives a small nod to the helmeted man. Suddenly the grip of your side-arm feels comforting and warm in your hand. Feels like it's saying: Do it!
The leader gives a small nod to the helmeted man. You feel your fists contract, as you stand there, between these men -- all carrying real weapons.
The leader gives a small nod to the helmeted man. Suddenly your fingers holding the grip of a gun, that has just taken a life, tingle... Go for it, it seems to say.
You really, really should have a gun in your hand by now -- or *something* dangerous. This feels *scary*.
Shoot him in the mouth. Shoot him before he shoots you.
'I feel it in my fingers... I feel it in my toes...'
Am I going to stay like this forever?
No. You're going to be mowed down by gunfire from the two remaining mercs, so no. Not forever.
Who broke my heart?
You both did, *bratan* -- deep down you know it was the both of you.
May he find peace in death.
He got what was coming for him.
It's good to see you still have capacity for compassion my friend. Deep down you are a good man.
Eventually we all do, Harry.
This is it. I'm gonna hit the ground and burn away now. Most of the people in this yard are gonna die -- if not all. Probably you too. It's a COMPLETE DISASTER.
Wow you threw it far -- great throw. Too bad the goal was to throw it a very *short* distance and now everyone will die.
Thanks, coach!
Don't thank *me*, you did this!
"Uh, what?" The lieutenant quickly glances at you.
An Ister AR-FA7, built for taking out light armoured vehicles. It will devastate you.
He's trying to find a straight line of sight before the rifleman can take you out.
Absolute destruction.
He's drunk. Drunk fighters over-correct. Move right -- he aims further right. Get him to overshoot!
A full suit of armour can't be too agile. You can shift direction faster than he can.
Just dodge the first shot -- and the second will be easier. Drunks are quick to anger -- and make mistakes.
I cannot be killed. I have become *immortal*.
(Shout.) "Stop shooting at me!"
He's aiming for the eye-slot in Ruud's helmet. An extremely difficult shot...
He has to. The rifleman will fire at you again.
The helmet looks like the face of an ancient god of war, crying blood.
Let it happen.
"STOP!!!"
He's not gonna make it.
Feels slick and warm with blood. The pain is too strong to know what has happened there. Even clutching to your consciousness takes everything you got.
Most of what's down there.
Oh god...
I don't care. Fuck me.
You can also feel bone where the bullet went in. Something very sharp, like broken teeth under your fingers.
... it's all gone. Open your eyes now. You have to see what's happening!
Liquid parts mostly, and you're quickly running out of them. There is a major artery on the inside of the thigh...
No. No. It's just a fear. Even if... who cares. No one wants you anyway.
See you on the other side... The necktie disintegrates into molten heat, its last remaining embers letting out a pop and crack that sounds like:
"It's so dark... I can't see anything."

dialoguetext: "Live fast... die *old*." (Wince from pain)
"Kim, I lied. About not remembering who I am. I made it up... I remember everything."
"Stay with me!" You feel burning hot tears streaming from your eyes.
"I'm a fucking failure and the love of my life left me."
"Stay with me!" The lieutenant pushes down on your wound, hard. "You hear me?! Stay awake! Look at me!"
"Everyone knows I made it up. I'm just a drunk. A stupid dead drunk."
"Yes! Keep talking!" The lieutenant pushes down on your wound, hard. "Stay awake! Look at me!"
It's not all dark yet. As you're leaving, she is in there too with you. You can *feel* the slender figure move, like a snake. And then a distant gunshot. Velvety smooth. Muffled.
"NO," you say, and hand out your firearm to him. Your hand trembles and your eyes are full of fear.
He just shakes his head, still crouched over you. You hear a distant gunshot. Velvety smooth -- a red circle has appeared on the lieutenant's jacket. It's growing fast.
"Shoot... dead." You hear your bloody lips mumble. You try to give him your gun, so he'd understand. But he does not. He does not look into your eyes and see the fear there.
Do nothing.
He turns to his left and says: "Kill him."
This time feels different. You aim higher -- as if pulled by a magnet. Your hand goes numb from the explosion and a plume of smoke erupts from the gun...
Another soft explosion, like a firecracker goes off in your hand. Another soft *click* from the gleaming white cuirass.
"There's a white shadow that smells like apricots, it's... always there."

dialoguetext: "Peaceful..." It sounds like the armoured figure is weeping.
"Fuck, she was right... That must be the *third* mercenary..."
"... nest in your abdominal cavity, like a little wild mouse..." The masked man's words are barely intelligible, but you can hear them.
This third one -- he is the most dangerous of them all. Heavily armed.
"Ssshhhhh...." The lieutenant raises his left hand.
"I'm all out of shits to give, loincloth." There's a feverish gleam in his eyes. "Welcome to the fucking reckoning."
"SHUT UP!!! You're not gonna talk yourself out of this, loincloth-shit fuck!"
Say nothing.
"If this turns into a firefight, we should take him out first." He nods.
This is the scab leader. His chest rises and falls under the ceramic breastplate. His fingers reach for the butt of his sidearm.
This is the mercenary at the gates! His chest rises and falls under the ceramic breastplate. His fingers reach for the butt of his sidearm.
There's something very wrong with him.
"We're out of time. This is..."
"... the mercenary tribunal." The lieutenant nods.
"What do we do?"
"My plan is not to get killed." He puts his hand on his holster. "But we have to intervene."
I think he's calmed down a bit...
No, he didn't -- he's about to open fire.
No, he's calming down. I can talk to him.
So which one is it, who's right?
He is, he's about to snap!
He is. I was wrong.
Oh yes he is, he's about to snap and shoot someone right now.
You can't think that way now, this is serious.
"...*PIGFUCK!*" is the only word you can make out.
"...*PIGFUCK!*" is the only word you can make out. It doesn't sound calm.
"One wrong move and I'm taking you out."
"We're gonna tear right through you, I don't give a shit if you're cops."
To your left you hear the lieutenant cock his gun.
"You're probably gonna get killed too... I think I'm gonna kill you. I didn't think I had it in me to kill a cop..."
To your left, you hear the lieutenant cock his gun.
She doesn't seem to understand the severity of the situation.
(Whisper.) "The big one is the mercenary at the gates! The scab leader."
(Whisper.) "The big one is the damn *scab leader*."
You throw the bomb and it's way off.
Scream IMMEDIATELY! He's gonna die.
All right! END GAME. Light me on fire and throw me in his face!
Wait. It's a good thing you have an anthropomorphic petrol bomb. It really is. But you have to soften him up first. Present an argument!
If you waste time people will die.
No. We can do this. Drag it out a little. Get under his skin.
Even if it comes to a fight it's a good idea to get under his skin first.
I don't know about this getting under his skin. What if he gets under *yours*? I'm barely keeping your hand from trembling here...
I'm barely keeping you together here. If you talk to him, he will rattle *you*, not the other way around.
Yes, yes! Just throw the bomb at him. I'm barely keep you together here -- no time to talk. He will only rattle you.
Whatever you do -- stop wasting your time *thinking* about it.
No, please. Peace -- it has worked this far. Start with the first idea you have, move down from that...
No. We can do this. Drag it out a bit. Get under his skin.

"I'll be okay... I'll be..." She puts her bloody hand on her heart and starts shaking.
"Guys, I, uh..." The little guy breaks formation. "I'd just get in the way. I don't even have a gun."
"She'll be gone soon too. Company bitch is gone, Lely's gone. Fuck are we still doing in this shithole?" He looks around, tired suddenly -- sad even.
"The company bitch is gone. Lely's gone. Fuck are we still doing in this shithole?" He looks around, tired suddenly -- sad even.
"Hold your ground.“ Titus turns to his men as the other one runs to the yard. "Any more of you run I'll shoot you myself. We're *doing* this -- together."
They're *afraid*. All of them. Trembling reeds in the wind. They'll run, scatter, soon. One by one.
No. The rest will stay. They will hold their ground. Even if it means dying here -- with you.
They're huddled close, in a formation. Steel. The rest will stay. Even if it means dying here -- with him.
"She's gone, you stupid fuck." He points to the sea. "Sailed off five minutes ago. She doesn't give a shit about you silos. You're *alone*."
"We're working together. She knew you're out of control. She told me."
As you look to the bay you see a small green sail on the horizon -- by the crumbling seafort -- growing smaller...
"She's gone, you stupid fuck." He points to the sea. "Sailed off -- five minutes ago. She doesn't give a shit about you silos..."
He isn't just boasting. He really doesn't care. Back out of this *now* or it'll get bad.
Ignore her. She's not the main threat yet.
"I don't care. It's not okay to kill civilians and local law enforcement officers."
"You were called *Downwell* once. What happened?"
"This tribunal is against the law. The international law."
The large man laughs. "Look around you, livestock... we're about to butcher the lot of you! Where is your *international law*?"
"If I fuck and kill you, hang you to that street light..." He points to it. "... by your shit-pipes -- then that's called a *necessary display of force*."
"No one's going to give a shit about dead loincloths." He snorts. "That's reality."
"What always happens when you get good at your job. That name meant night raids, fucking extra-judicial funkytime... burned villages. Shit that sounds bad on the radio."
"The same thing happened when we were called whatever-the-fuck it was. Probably won't be called *Krenel* for much longer either..." He looks around.
"Not after this shit."
"Just a question -- who's in charge of your unit after the death of your colonel?"
"I am a Krenel major with over 15 years of live-combat experience. When my colonel gets hanged by clay-monkeys I lead the platoon on a *retaliation strike*."
"So you are the highest ranking of the three of you?"
"Hold on, what's the highest rank in Krenel?"
"As the leader of this group -- reconsider your actions. This does not need to end in bloodshed."
"King Reaper," he says without irony.
"Nah... I just have the biggest gun." He raps on his armoured barrel-like chest.
"You're right. But you see..." he pauses and smiles. "I *want* it to end in bloodshed."
C'mon head, give me an argument!
"Krenel does not give you the right to conduct a tribunal!"
All right, here we go -- this is an *illegal tribunal*. Their employer would never *sanction* this. Who's the *commanding officer*? Take your pick!
International-something?! International law!
"Pops..." he says looking at your saggy sideburns -- they seem to calm him down for a second. "You have no idea about the rights Krenel extends to us."
Really? None of this looks like it's going to do anything but piss him off.
I have some *trivia* too! Get him *interested* in facts!
The woman has grown silent. She draws shallow breaths.
Okay -- it's not much. But he's thinking about something *else*. And his hand is off the gun. This did *something*...
"Okay. What rights are those then?"
Gulp and say nothing.
So you just *stand* there!? This is bad, very bad, DO OR SAY SOMETHING NOW!
"There will be ramifications -- but there don't need to be. Let's go inside and discuss what our investigation has uncovered. We have important..."
"We're not fucking coming anywhere, seolite!"
Say something. Get off this trail. Thank god it's only *ineffectual* thus far.
Now fire! Fuck them up! DO IT! The muscles on your back tense up...
It's a *miracle* no one got shot this time. Stop attempting to use your *head*. It won't work!
Don't say it.
DON'T SAY IT? But now you've stood there scratching your ass for 1.5 seconds, you think this *helps* things?
Technically, the other man has the biggest gun, but... we're beyond that now.
You only have time for *one* argument, choose wisely...
Easy, now... Tell them these men didn't do it. There's a peaceful way out!
Easy, now! Easy. Just tell them these men didn't do it. There's a peaceful way out...
I should talk to him about the hanged man.
Dangerous! Ask about him first. You don't want personal facts about his dead friend coming out of your mouth -- *he* has to start it.
Of course! Nothing bad will happen. Talk about his dead friend! He seems stable enough to take it.
"I knew you weren't a god damn scab leader!"
"Who are you?"
"Sergeant Major Raul Kortenaer -- reporting in to burn this fucking mud hut to the ground!" He points at the Whirling-in-Rags...
"Yeah, I don't fucking *act* so well. Lely had a hard-on for making faces for you natives. Fucking food-aid shit..." He wipes his mouth. "That shit is done now. Trigger time."
As he moves, the interlocking pieces of his armour click, softly.
...click, click, click! The realization comes to you, like a picture puzzle coming together: His name is Raul Kortenaer -- the dead man's name is Ellis Kortenaer. He's *brothers* with the deceased!
No -- probably foster brothers! Ellis was put into a foster home, remember...
Korty -- Kortenaer. Major Raul *Korty* Kortenaer. Friends with Lely. Raul and Lely.
"Kortenaer -- I know that name."
"His parents left him in a fucking leaf compactor."
"Listen, your Lely -- everyone says good things about him. He was a talker."
(Conclude.) "Your colonel did not deserve to go out like that. I promise -- I *will* find his killer."
He sways from left to right, inspecting you.
"Raul and Ellis Kortenaer..." Look him in the eye. "I'm sorry about your brother, Raul."
"He wasn't my fucking brother! We just grew up on the same farm and got beat into place by the same sick fuck..."
"And then went to the same military academy. And the same unit. And the same war..."
"You were foster brothers. I know that."
"Same fucking mudhut town too..." he looks around, then wipes his face with his armoured glove.
Beaten by a foster parent, or someone on the farm?
"Who... Lely?"
"Yes. When he was small... just an infant."
"Fuck do you mean *talker*?"
"We've heard testimony. People say he was charismatic. A nice guy to be around."
"Yeah, he liked to chat up the natives. Share leaflets, squeeze a bit of kipt ass here and there. Great fucking idea that turned out to be..." He points toward the yard.

"If Lely was here, he would spare the lot of you. Maybe shoot one for show. But me..." He points to himself. "I'm not a big fan of public affairs, clay-monkey. I'll gun every one of you down for what you did."
"Ready to open fire, major. At your command."
"You don't *know* shit. Lance Corporal, why don't you.." He turns to the radio officer on this right...
You lost him. Quick!
Don't let him finish the sentence!
"We researched him. We contacted the ICP and looked at his birth records. That was in there. And other things..."
"They fucking put Lely in a leaf compactor and now these cunts finished the job..." He waves at the gang huddled by the doors.
"It's a mind-fuck, Korty. He wasn't put it a leaf compactor. They're making it up to fuck with us." She glances at him. "Major, permission to..."
There's real anguish in his voice. A drunken sadness suddenly engulfs him. Memories...
...open fire -- we can't have that. Interfere, now!
"Banaital, '41... that really happened didn't it?"
"He had blue eyes didn't he -- your colonel."
"Baby blue, yeah... Like someone fucked up and put a baby's eyes on a grown man." He smiles, pulling his face in a strange way.
"Our colonel did what he had to do. It was either one cunt, or a hundred of them. Ruud here..." He points to him.
"... in your shit-pipes, right..." Indecipherable mumbling.
"He likes to fire mortars at random coordinates. Wipe out mud-huts like that. When he gets *bored*. Lely knew how to command."
"He was a good commander. I can see you miss him."
"Oh yeah, he would have commanded this fuck-hell way better than I did. But that didn't happen, because Hayseed Bill and Kipty the Kipt here..." he points to Titus and Eugene.
"...fucking murdered him. Had him stink the village up for two weeks after. And you fucks did nothing." He points at you.
"Listen, man. We told you we..."
"Told us WHAT?!" He staggers forward. "What did you say? Who said that? Tattoo-fuck -- you'll die FIRST."
"It was creepy, but bitches... bitches like that shit, I guess. Or... I don't know what bitches like. I just know how to mow down *cloths*."
"They... they didn't..." The woman holds on to her side, teeth rattling.
"Find his killer?! Cop, his killer stands right there!" He waves at the men behind you. "Shitting his pants -- and *you're* standing in the way protecting them."
"Find his killer?! Cop, his killers stand right there!" He waves at the men behind you. "Shitting their pants -- and *you're* standing in the way protecting them."
...and then he bellows: "For killing, maiming and humiliating our commanding officer -- you're all sentenced to death by lead!"
"Shush..." He squints at her. "Blood's all gone out now. Not long to go till the rattle starts. One down, girl -- seven to go..."
"I know what this tactic is, Silo Sam." He stares at you, eyes pink from the alcohol -- fingers tapping the pistol. "You're gonna die for them. Right here. Today."
"Told us WHAT?!" He staggers forward. "What did you say? Tattoo-fuck, you'll die NEXT. Right when the she-kipt's out..."
This did nothing. You think you were on to something?! You *just* wasted time... please, act.
Big talk, but that leaf compactor won't leave his mind any time soon. It's a small thing -- but it got him off centre...
Big talk, but you got him to admit he's a bad leader. It's a small thing -- but it got him off centre...
He doesn't seem stable at all....
"I feel like I got to know your dead friend. During our investigation."
Ever better! It will further destabilize him -- costing time and maybe even lives!
"You don't fucking TALK TO ME about my brother, loincloth!" He squeezes the words out from between clamped lips, his hand on the pistol...
Uhm... this might be a *very* bad moment to come up with this, but he's *Korty* right?
Okay, yes. Immediate failure. Things are worse now. He's observing your every motion carefully...
Yes, go on. I don't want to do anything but say that thing down there.
The man he's mourning was called Ellis *Kortenaer*. Korty could be short for Kortenaer? Could they be brothers? Ask him that. What could go wrong. It's a discovery!
"Hey... I don't mean to pry but the hanged man -- was he your brother?"
Yes. This will be good. It will calm him down and won't cost any lives. Lives that could have been otherwise spared.
And if not -- lives aren't *that* important anyway (including yours). There are billions of them, being lived.
"You don't fucking TALK TO ME about my brother, loincloth!" He squeezes the words out from between clamped lips, his hand on the pistol...
Okay, yes. Immediate failure. Things are worse now. He's observing your every motion carefully...
Okay. Good.
Yes. This will be good. It will calm him down and won't cost any more lives. Lives that could be spared.
This one isn't used to being suited this long. She's uncomfortable; will open fire just to hurry things along.
"Klaasje -- the woman upstairs? Where is she?"
"She left!" The manager calls down from the balcony.
Unarmed, hunched, but keeping it together.
"What do you mean she *left*?"
"Garte, what the hell are you *doing* here?"
"She LEFT! Her room's cleaned out -- right before these assholes showed up!"
"What am I doing?! My fucking establishment is UNDER FIRE!" He points to the armoured figures. "You know how much windows *cost?*"
"HEY, BUSHMEN!!!" The veins on the man's neck expand as he yells. "Your little CUNT isn't gonna help you out of this one!"
"We should have arrested her..." The lieutenant whispers, his eyes still on the armed mercenaries.
You can *feel* how upset he is with himself. Just for a second. Then the fear takes over and he's back in the moment.
She's gone. Forget about it now. Concentrate on this.
"Who the fuck is that?"
For god's sake, tell 'em the Hardies didn't *do* it, present a case!
"Basteeerds! We have a RIGHT TO WORK!" the man yells towards the harbour gates. His voice is the loudest of the lot -- and oddly screechy for a man his size.
"What's going on here?"
"Beats me. They mumble nonsense about *board rooms* and *workers' rights*. While we --" he raises his fist and starts shouting again, "-- HAVE THE RIGHT TO WORK!"
"Have fun." He snorts. "Union shits are on full strike. Don't think they're going to let you through the gates. You trying to meet their fat boss?"
"I'm interviewing people about a murder that took place here. Behind the hostel-cafeteria there."
"It would be better -- for the neighbourhood -- if you went home. At least for now. If you can't get in anyway."
"Wait. They might go home eventually. Or get drunk. Leave the access panel unguarded. Or the company sends someone to reason with them..."
"Unexpected situation. But we hold the pressure on, until someone makes a mistake. Then it's our time, we strike." The man rubs his jaw -- a lightly bearded square wedge.
"We're all workers. Right? Workers stick together. Came from the Eminent Domain, in Jamrock. Background's in odd-jobs -- heavy lifting, cargo hauling, bouncer work. I know the drill."
"A bouncer? Where? I frequent a lot of bars, maybe it's one I know."
"Worked at... *Territorial*. Ring a bell?"
"Yeah, I think I've been there."
"Not right now, but I might have been there. I don't really remember things well."
"Never heard of it. Are you lying?"
"I'm just going to leave now." [Leave.]

A monstrous shadow, high above the firetraps of the Domain -- the 8/81 motorway running over this district of Jamrock. Concrete pillars rise up from the midst of the dilapidated wooden houses. On the horizon, barely visible, the hazy machinery of the harbour...

Every once in a while, it is like you can see glimpses of another guy under the guise of this *fighter for jobs*. He seems a more brutal, cunning and suspicious person. Just a hunch. Or... you just might be paranoid!
"Good. We're fighting for a cause here." He chants at the gates: "RIGHT TO WORK! RIGHT TO WORK!"
"Hold up and stay frosty, everyone! Cops are here." The broad-shouldered alpha male turns to you. He's a full head taller than everybody else here.
Boots -- black in colour, crafted of hardened leather, if you had to guess. They look sturdy and stable, useful in rugged environments.
"Why should I?"
"I am the law."
"What do the strikers want?"
"What is a *strike*?"
"What exactly is your goal here?"

"RIGHT TO WORK!" He again shakes his large fist, then turns back to you. "It's shameful, cops doing nothing. You should bring backup, open the gates for us. Blockading gainful employment for workers is a *crime*."
"We have families to feed, you piece of shit!" He points his finger at the man sitting on the railing.
"So do we, scab!" the loitering man hollers in return.
His manner of speaking is wooden, the tone of voice bland and uninspired. Almost as if compiling replies from a set of learned phrases.
"Okay, I gotta ask. Where exactly are you from?"
"Honest men and women. With rights -- to work. To be useful. Not toys for corporate interests." The man runs a hand through his steadily graying military haircut.
"Who are all these strikebreakers?" (Look around.)
The mention of a killing sends a barely noticeable shiver of tenseness through him. Interesting...
"We came here to help the harbour run smoothly in time of crisis. If Union fucks don't want work, they ought let in those *WHO DO WANT WORK*."
"Everyone understands you're *the law*. That's why you have that insignia on your arm. So you don't have to keep saying it."
"When a bunch of ungrateful, lazy cockroaches can't get their act together. Decide to block honest work for other people." He shifts uncomfortably in his worker's overalls.
There's something odd in the way he carries himself. His set of clothing looks vaguely mismatched. The different pieces of the attire seem ill-fitting.
"Yes, people get that you are *the law*. You really don't have to keep saying it."
"Looks like too much trouble for my taste." [Leave.]
"We're here to fight for a cause. Stripes usually have problems with people who have *causes*."
"What kind of a cause are we talking about?"
"Rights of people. Rights of workers. To have gainful employment. To make a salary and feed their families."
"RIGHT TO WORK! RIGHT TO WORK!" the ostensible leader of the strikebreakers chants furiously. "SHAME ON YOU!"
"I don't *think* I've chosen any sides yet."
"Yes."
"No."
"Hah! Couldn't handle us. A cause gives the workers strength. Gives them power." He bellows at the gates: "We have -- A RIGHT TO WORK!"
"Might be time. Don't let the fat bastards tread on you. Cops tend to side with the higher-ups, but you're essentially still *workers*."
"This is an official matter, not to be discussed with outsiders."
"I don't know..."
"This really isn't my area of expertise."
He nods. "You go, take the bastards down a peg or two. Squeeze them a little. Show them the rule of law." He bellows at the gates: "LET US WORK!"
"I know nothing about a murder." His reply is snappy and terse.
"Wouldn't put it past these harbour bugs. They'd do *anything* to stay alive."
"What's it to you?" Deep-set suspicion drips from every syllable.
"Curiosity. Going to figure out this strike mess."
"Routine. Part of the investigation."
"Am I a suspect?" His eyes narrow. "Done no crimes. I only fight for the rights of people."
"Big mess. Caused by Union greed." He shoots you a wary, distrustful look. "But I only fight for the rights of people."
"Already got that. I'm interested in *your* background."
"Uh huh. Was a long time ago." The man is quickly losing interest in talking with you.
"Hey *tough guy*, I had more questions."
"I thought you looked real familiar for a second there."
"No, don't think we've met before." His eyes narrow with mistrust. "I came to help out *the people*."
"Sweet, I know bars. Been thrown out from several. Maybe that's why you seem familiar."
"I wasn't done asking questions."
He looks annoyed. "Things are busy enough. You going to waste less of my time?"
"Maybe."
"We'll see."
The hulking man oozes stark scepticism.

As he does, he stomps his foot on the pavement and... stop everything! Look at that sweet pair of boots on his feet! They would absolutely complement your *soul*, would let your style fly even higher!
Imagine what you could do with boots like this. Not be a little fuckin' weakling baby, for starters. There are boots for mewling and there are boots for smashing shit.
If only I had boots like this, I could stomp many things. Got a problem, punk? Eat my boot.
Get your daily infusion of vitamin PB -- for Police Brutality. Makes you feel like a boss. The man in charge.
It's just a pair of boots. Who cares?
Never thought you so spineless. Where's your wrecking ball spirit, your brutal mojo?
"Those are some sweet boots. Can I have them?"
I don't really care what either of you think. I'm a cool-ass bitch, baby. You can't *fake* stardom.
I stand corrected.
I don't think the boots really fit *my style*. They look militant and uncomfortable.
Geez, live a little. At least give things a try. It's just boots. A set of sweet, stylish boots.
Damn, you're right. Super sweet. Where can I get in on this bad-ass boot fashion?
Ask the man. Ask around. The doors of good taste are open to you. Be in vogue.
"Establishment hasn't had its fill, is that right? First they obstruct our work, then they come for our shoes."
"No."
"Come on, why not?"
"I mean, where did you get them? I would like a pair of my own."
"Oh, okay, whatever. Too much of a hassle."
"Around." He shifts his gaze away. "Eminent Domain. Previous... workplace."
"I'm hardly the establishment."
"Okay okay, I got it. None of this *rob the poor* stuff."
"That's what they always say, before stabbing you in the back. You want boots? Go find your own."
"Well shit. I'll have to check around then. Maybe there's a boot store around."
"You do that."
"Absolutely nothing?"
"Why so tense?"
"Excuse me, I had further inquiries."
The man has turned his attention elsewhere, he shakes his fist slowly -- while observing you from the corner of his eye.
"I don't really drink. But work *has* taken me to some. Which one was it?"
"And you are unable to breach the entrance?"
"Wait -- *Head-Measurer*?"
"Have you considered storming in? Like, all of you?"
"Huge Semenese guy standing up there on the overhead passage. Won't let anyone by. The access panel is right behind him."
"Why don't *you* go arrest them instead? I'm sure they've done plenty of criminal shit, they have *that look*."
"I need you to be my champion against Jean-Luc up there."

dialoguetext: "No." He slowly shakes his head. "I'm not a fighter -- I'm a WORKER!"
"You're not from The Domain."
"Yeah?" The man grunts. "What makes you say that?"
"I don't know what makes me say that."
"It's a... gut feeling."
The beefy man snorts and spits on the ground. "Yeah. I don't know either." He turns his attention back to the harbour gates.
"Your gut's got too much alcohol in it. Getting delirious." The bulky man guffaws and turns away from you, focusing again on the harbour gates.
Shudder and breathe on your hands.
Don't. No need. Focus on something else.
Ignore the discrepancy.
Ill-fitting... what does that mean?
His shirt is far too small and an unpleasantly tight fit. While the overalls, held up by a belt, seem to fit a man with much *more* corpulence.
Fine. It was probably nothing.
Life in the Domain is even worse off than in Martinaise. The cold air is stiff from the fumes of motor carriages and lorries roaring overhead.
Sweet boots? I require details.
Don't care. I already have boots of my own, thank you.
Prissy milksop. Get back to me when you've grown a backbone!
The burly man has a set of not-very-sweet-nor-impressive boots protruding out from under the baggy, hanging folds. They are of little interest to you.
"And I don't mean the scrawny Mesque punk either." He points at the dockworker idling on the staircase. "I mean Head-Measurer -- or whatever he is."

"Main gate's locked -- would take *heavy ordnance* to bust it open. Could try to get in through the secretary's office." He points up the stairs. "Door's locked. The guard's blocking the way to the access panel."
"How bad could one guy be? You seem capable."
"Bad." The man glares at you. "Standing on a narrow bridge, he's got a strategically advantageous position. And he's trained."
"You here to fuck with us? Beat the honest worker down?"
"I don't trust cops, but... I can see you understand the --" He raises his voice and chants: "RIGHT TO WORK! RIGHT TO WORK!"
"Sure, why not?"
"Why don't you just *talk* to them?"
"Like civilized folk, you mean?" The man rubs his chin. "These native fucks don't understand *civilized*."
"Okay, I wanted to discuss something else."
The physically impressive man-tower has turned his attention back to the gates. He ignores your presence.
"Uh. I'll be going now." [Leave.]
"Besides, we're not that different." He leans closer. "It helps if people see us talking -- cops and strikebreakers together. Shows authorities are on our side. Builds confidence."
"RIGHT TO WORK!!" the man chants, then turns to you. "Back again, eh? Here to show the militia's support for our cause?"
"RIGHT TO WORK!" He seems to have returned to his previous routine, as if he'd never seen the photo of the tattoo.
"Went native on the chief, huh?" He nods in approval. "Those ballerina antics were reckless. Should have just punched him in the throat again."
"Nice aggression with the native." He nods in approval. "Don't let the chief fool you next time. You don't need to be that up in his face -- leave yourself space to move."
"Regardless, I have some questions for you." (Proceed.)
"Maybe you should ask *them* the questions, like why we're not allowed to make a living here?" He bellows to the gates: "SHAME ON YOU!"
He pauses, then abruptly changes the subject: "Let's talk about our right to work."
He abruptly changes the subject: "Let's talk about our right to work."
"I want to get into the harbour too."
"What are you talking about? I'm not tense."
Yes, he's tense.
And dangerous. Somewhere below it all...
He nods. "You go take the bastards down a peg or two. Squeeze them a little. Show them the rule of law." He bellows at the gates: "LET US WORK!"
"We're not picking a side in this just yet, sir."
"Why not? I see *numerous* reasons not to pick a side in this local matter."
"Pity." He turns around and bellows at the gates: "LET US WORK!"
When the man moves around, you perceive some *serious abs* underneath his tight-fitting shirt. This man is in *shape*.
"You wearing new clothes?"
He ignores your question, choosing instead to turn to the emaciated workers -- raising both fists in the air. The clothes are obviously not his.
Silence is the answer. There's something off here but he won't say what.
"We were promised work." He points to the gates. "We'd be in there -- WORKING -- if the bastards hadn't shut the gates."
"I don't know how the Union has a trained killer up there, but that one's no joke. And my men are tired. And hungry. They're WORKERS, not fighters."
"So what are you going to do now?"
"No. They will give up eventually. Or get drunk. Leave the button unguarded. Then we charge." The man rubs his jaw -- a perfect, lightly bearded square wedge.
Odd out of place colonial reference there, Mr. Scab Leader...
"I work hard." His voice booms ever louder: "And I would work *even harder* -- if the fuckers would LET US WORK!"
"How come you're built like a brick shit-house, but the other scabs are so scrawny?"
I don't want to ask that.
Yes. Of course.
"I have a question." The lieutenant looks him in the eye. "Why do all these men follow your leadership?"
Now that *is* interesting.
"You think they follow because I'm big and loud? No, they follow the rules of the market. The rules of the economy. Because they were --" he starts bellowing, "-- GIVEN A JOB TO DO."
You've been talking to him for quite a while now -- something is off with this guy. Ask him where he's from.
"Makes sense, I guess. Never mind, not gonna pry."
Below -- broken-down, battered people mill on the dusty streets with no purpose. Yet amongst them there is no sight of this man. *Nowhere*.
"So anyway, cop. That's where I'm from. It would be *stupid* to doubt that."
Pretty okay, as far as lies go.
He squints at you --  a little spark of violence gutters in his eyes. Then he blinks and turns to his men. "We're done here. I have a strike to break."
He's stopping this to control himself. You were on to something.
"No one there knows you."
The beefy man snorts and spits on the ground. "They know me -- that's bullshit." He turns his attention back to the harbour gates.
"Are you a mercenary hired by Wild Pines?"
"FREE FLOW OF COMMERCE!" The man yells and wipes his face. Sweat is dripping down his brow.
"Hell no. I'm just an honest scab. I won't have talk like that around here, you understand?"
"'Hell no, I'm just an honest scab?' That didn't sound too convincing."
His neck muscles tense up, the veins on his neck bulge. Be careful -- he's holding it *deep* in but there are things in there you don't want to meet.
It just has to be said -- that was not a convincing line.
Don't talk to him any longer. Just leave, please.
"Okay." (Back off.)
Say very quietly: "Is there a *tribunal* being convened by any chance?"
"Fucking loincloth..." He stares you down mutely for a second.
The man's breathing steadies but his eyes are still narrow. Slowly he's trying to get his 'Right to Work' dance back on...
Loincloth? Now, you see, that's not really what a scab would say is it? Better not to press the issue further, sire. He seems... tense.
"Fucking bug..." He breathes out slowly -- his giant chest deflating and his mouth slightly open.
You hear a tiny rattle, a small radio, cracking somewhere -- an earpiece?
"How about you fuck off now, huh?"
A punch is not imminent, but it's being cocked. Hard.

It's hard to do that, when you want to beat a man into a pulp instead.
