dialoguetext: Banaital is one of the inhabited islands of the Semenese archipelago, near the pale. Covered in  jungle. It was the anchor point for the Semenese nationalists -- in the proxy war held on the islanders' territory.
"Our colonel is *deep* in the bush here. Deep in the fucking bush, in Banaital, '41... Monsoon season. He's on a reconnaissance mission."
Suddenly the laughter stops. "Drowned in a creek a week later. Spirits my ass."

"He's spent a month behind enemy lines scouting kipt villages. Nothing but fucking bugs and snakes for fun. Men are getting restless... there's talk of switching *employers*..." He licks his lips, as if drunk suddenly.
Don't interrupt him. (Hear it.)
With some strange emotion. This is about to get really graphic. Last moment to back off.

"Our boy -- he's only a captain then -- but he knows how these men think. If they don't see action soon..." His voice gets strangely quiet. A long, long way from *right to work*. His gaze pierces the paper.
There's a word on the tip of your tongue. Colourless, odourless. It's...
"What's the matter, militiaman... no stomach for it?" He looks at the photo in your hand and smiles. "This man was worth a thousand loincloths. We're done talking here."
"Actually, no." (Take the photo back.) "You knew him right?"
The story must have stirred up some conflicting emotions. The man looks tired for a second...

"She was quite the entertainment. For the week she lasted. Expired in the hands of Sarge Mason -- the kinda guy who'd make Chief there," he nods towards the man on the gates, "shit his pants and cry like a bitch."
"God..." He suddenly bursts out laughing. "Mason couldn't let go. Cut the tits off her cold body and fuckin' ate them. Said primitive spirits were watching over him now..."
"Don't think so," he grunts, barely glancing at it.
Suddenly this feels like a really, *really* bad idea.
"Of course. Yes. Forget about it. Let's discuss something else." (Cancel task.)
Another grunt. He's turned his attention to the gates and seems tense.
"Actually..." The lieutenant turns to you. "I think we should maybe even *get going* now?"
He clearly does not think poking the hornet's nest is a wise plan anymore.
Silence. He takes the photo. Grey eyes dart  back and forth on the glossy surface -- his face is unmoving.
After a while, he cranes his head side-to-side and sighs: "Fucking loincloths really did him in."
Wordless, he takes the photo and looks at it. Grey eyes dart back and forth on the glossy surface -- his face is unmoving.
Hard as a stone. But beneath it...
You see dead flesh -- in colourful rivers of Polychrome -- melting skin and hair.
"Can you tell me what the tattoo means?"
"What it *means*...." He points to one tiny star in the web of lines, away from the man's heart, almost on his stomach.
"Yeah."
"Uhm... loin-cloths?"
He's clenching his teeth. There is silent pressure behind them.
In what must have been Semenine.
"I can tell you what this one means. Only one." He squints at it. It's so small. "You wanna hear what happened here?"
"Yes."
"Actually, no." (Take the photo back.)
"At dawn he comes upon two kipts, breeding in the bushes by the river. Or maybe they weren't breeding -- maybe they were just making eyes at each other. I like to think they were breeding..."
"Okay. This isn't useful." (Take the photo back.) "You knew him right?"
Say nothing.
"Good choice." He nods.
He clearly does not think poking the hornet's nest is a wise plan anymore.
The lieutenant turns to you. "I think we should maybe even *get going* now?"
There is absolutely no need to push this any further.
"Evil."
"What *is* evil?"
"You can have that." (Conclude.)
"Nah, you've earned it." He turns toward the gate, slowly, and yells: "All right now! FREE COMMERCE! KEEP THE GOODS FLOWING!"
"You bet it was."
"It's just... nature. This guy," he points at the picture, "he used to say evil is when nature and spirit meet in the wrong place."
"You're not really a *scab leader*, are you?"
"Fucking mask is getting sweaty. I want take my mask off, but..." He shrugs.
"Can I have it back?" (Conclude.)
"Go ahead." He turns toward the gate, slowly, and yells: "All right now. FREE COMMERCE! KEEP THE GOODS FLOWING!"
On the photo in your hands -- the dead man's skin is studded with stars. Tens, hundreds of them, littering his dead skin.
"You were there?"
"No. I was somewhere else. That's just a *guess*. As to what this one little star on his belly might mean. I'm just a bouncer."
"We shot the boy, he was useless, but the girl... she was nice. A little fat you know. But not too old."
"No -- I was in the Domain. In Jamrock. Being a bouncer."
He's under orders. And orders -- are orders.
I'm going to interpret that as a *yes*. There's a tribunal. And it won't be long until it's ready.
"They were on the body of the man who was hanged behind the cafeteria there." (Give him the photo.)
"It was on your colonel." (Give him the photo.)
"We're investigating a murder. These tattoos were on the victim's body." (Give him the photo.)
"Don't think so," he grunts.
He seems to be following his orders well enough for now -- but beneath it all there is a boiling rage. And a dangerous carelessness.
Do not be fooled by the programming. There is a precarious balance inside him, keeping him in check. But it's shaky as hell. And he's tired of it all...
"Yeah, I saw your ballerina moves up there." The man spits out a yellow clot. "In a real fight these acrobatics will get you killed faster than a bullet."
"You caught him off guard -- that only happens once. Now he's alert, standing on a narrow bridge and *my* men are tired and hungry..."
"Wait, you can't get by Measurehead? But *I* got by Measurehead. I kicked him in the face."
Something stirs in your stomach.
Not bad advice, actually. This might do the trick..
"You don't have any tips on how to punch a guy out, do you? Say, a really big race-theorist guarding a button?"

dialoguetext: He smirks. "Not before you get in there and get your ass whooped. Learn by failure, I always say."
He might have some advice, but you gotta at least *try* to fight Measurehead first. Return if you fail.
"What about it? You're 'right to work'?"
Wrong. You did the right thing with Measurehead. The ballerina antics won you the fight.
"Scab?" asks a man with jolly eyes, tilting his head.
"What exactly *is* a scab?"
"A kind of a worm, content with mere survival. They come, they want to do *our job* for shittier pay, screwing over both themselves and us. Everybody loses."
"Personally, I'd rather beg than scab. If the gentlemen shouting on the street came *begging*, maybe they'd have gotten something."
(Nod.) "Have you tried talking to them?"
"We've explained the matters, but they don't listen." He shakes his head. "This lot would be reasonable and go home if the big guy wasn't riling them up all the time."
"I'm not a scab. I'm a cop." (Proceed.)
"Ah, I was just messing with you." His smile deepens his wrinkles even more. "No one's ever seen a cop scab."
"Oh. Good, good! What matters do you want to discuss with Evrart?"
"I need to get past the gates and speak with your boss."

dialoguetext: "Sure, I've had the necessary free time." He spreads his arms wide, using the reach to show how much time he has. "Fortunately, there's always time."
The look in his brown eyes conjures up an understanding: for him, having command of his time is the most important thing.
It all comes together now, the way he speaks about scabs, his general attitude. He's a follower of a 500-year-old Franconigerian boiadeiro code -- itself an appropriation of Vespertine cool...
"He might have information about a killing that took place behind the hostel."
"Body still hangin' in the tree?" He rubs his chin as if pondering his core beliefs. "Aye, that's a rough pickle... can't help you with that, sorry."
"There's been talk of suspicious activity at the harbour."
"Why are you striking?"
"We're negotiating our share."
"Your... share?"
"Wait, so not wages or pensions or..."
"How large a *share* would you like?"
"This stuff -- they already covered."
"Aye." He seems pleased with himself.
"All of it. However, right now we want all the harbour workers to be on the company's board, so they could take part in *the decision-making process*."
"Shouldn't you be grateful then? It's a lot more than most people here have."
"Never grateful. Were we ever grateful, we'd have nothing. You fight for every piece."
"Are you a... communist?"
"No," he pauses to think for a moment. "I don't think I'm a communist. Seeing something of value and saying *I want it all to myself* is a much older and simpler notion. No science to it at all..."
"Even a weak child can think it. The only things holding someone back are *I can't* and *I shouldn't*."
"But don't you think the owners have a right to the harbour? Didn't they organize it into existence?"
"You see, the owners already benefit greatly from the harbour. No one can doubt that. They get so much."
*The board* is where the stockholders send their representatives. Often those representatives don't even represent the stockholders' interests. It's not actually like some council-based democracy.
"You seem to have the wrong idea here. The board of a major company is not *council democracy*."
"Quite a shitty board, I must say. Means someone's gotta reform it. I, for one, want to face the *fat ones'*, when decisions are made."
"Got the picture. Let me ask you something else."
"But the stuff you do aligns admirably well with the World Republic, why not call yourself a communist?"
"I have nothing against communists, they are honourable boiadeiros." He takes a swig from his flask. "And they have good analysis."
"But my own code serves me well. If my code starts failing -- a code can fail a man as well as a man can fail a code -- then I will have to submit to a new one. Which may well be communism."
"I guess I understand..."
"I am not sure I understand."
"It sounds like you're a communist who thinks he isn't doing enough to call himself one."
"See, I am primarily a lazy person." He looks very amused, as if thinking about some private joke or mystery.
"The bossman, Evrart, what can you tell me about him?"
"Hey, if the rich folk screw over poor folk, with little concern for their merits or futures, why shouldn't poor folk screw over rich folk from time to time?"
"I think it's best you make up your own mind, now that you've met him." He shrugs. "In my eyes, he is a capable organizer and a decent businessman."
"By Heavens, why would he not be corrupt? We live in a harsh and disordered world, see. And in this world..."
"He is *reasonably* lavish, sure. That's his prerogative. It's not like you want a saintly demeanour on a corrupt motherfucker. That would be a manipulative illusion."
"What does bossing the Union entail anyway?"
"I guess you kinda get to be the village chief. He oversees the harbour, makes deals with the owners or other relevant parties. Watches out for his own."
"Wait... I don't even know your name. Who are you?"
"Call me Mañana. I'm just a humble harbour-worker... for the past six, seven years."
"Call Me Mañana.. What kind of a name is that?"
"It means *call me tomorrow*."
"So, not a given name, I take it?"
"I'd say a real name is what most people call you." He realizes something.
"So it's a... nom de guerre?"
"A nom de guerre would be more like *Guerra Mañana*." He chuckles. Then realizes something.
"Hold on, have you had any other names?"
"Now that we're getting so well acquainted -- what's your name?"
"It's... umm... Harry."
"I hear you and it's... uh, pleasure meeting you, *Harry*." He nods. "But do keep an eye out for an alternative, alright?"
"Honesty. I *lost* it while drinking."
"Wow! This is major! You're like... a man born anew!" His eyes light up. "Okay, so if you can't find it, maybe make up a new one?"
"I may take that into consideration."
"It's been said I call myself *Tequila Sunset*."
The man is deeply moved. You see his eyes turn teary with appreciation. He is extremely happy for you.
He reaches his hand out to you and shouts: "Boiadeiro!"
Shake his hand.
Leave him hanging.
"Well, boiadeiro --" He pauses to think a moment on the situation. "I guess I don't really have a claim to your hand or anything."
You receive a good, strong handshake in return.
"What's a... *boiadeiro*?"
Mañana sounds like a mesque word, but he doesn't actually look much like a mesque.
"Mañana? You don't look like a Mesque..."
"I'm not. I'm *Vacholiero*. Not all Mesques have the Mesque look, either, you know. Things in the real world are a bit more... fluid. Stuff ain't always what it appears to be."
It feels like there's an entire history behind the word... but it doesn't really matter. You got it. You know what it *means*.
He takes a swig from his flask, then offers you some.
"Oh yeah!" (Take a swig.)
"Thanks, I'll pass. I'd just go wild."
"And then we might go wild together, which sounds fun. But I guess I have a strike to watch."
"Keeps you warm on a day like this. Or any day, for that matter."
"What kind of a cool guy exactly? It's not *just* a cool guy, is it?"
"Like me and you. Exactly so." He takes a swig from his flask, then offers you some.
Have a moment of silence.
"Does this mean you can let me through the gate?"
"The Measurehead thing didn't go well for me. Could you help me with that somehow?"

dialoguetext: "Sorry. Busy surveying the situation." He takes a swig from his flask. "I'm sure you'll figure something out. You guys have all sorts of gadgets these days."
"Olá, wandering man." He looks at you with soft and hazy eyes. "How can I help you?"
"It sounds scary, I don't want to."
No doubt he's communist enough to call himself such. But he won't.
He knows who he is. Firmly grounded -- has no need to reinforce or elaborate his political identity to himself or others.
"Hold on, where did they all come from?"
"Beats me. Somewhere in the ground, I think."
"You don't seem to like them much."
"Gotta be bloody stupid or freakin' evil to scab. Or, I guess... scared, maybe. But scared of what, of who?" He looks at the mass, squinting his eyes as if trying to ascertain what they're scared of.
Not a given name, for certain. It's a taken name -- the kind for artists, or criminals, or revolutionaries and the sort. An alias. A *nom de guerre*.
"Suit yourself. Yet one can't live nameless; names are important things. Vessels of the soul."
"Okay, I have a name for myself, it's..."
Your mind can only conjure up Hunk Handy, Fucke Waldéz, Bosco... you might want to decide to keep quiet about these.
"Uhhhh.... I actually don't have a name."
"It can take time to come up with a good one, for sure."
The encroaching doom is golden red. It is inside you, but also outside, on the horizon, by the water's edge. Innermost but yet to happen -- things make sense from that angle...
"I can't do it. I'm sorry."
You're *Tequila Sunset*. You have been Tequila Sunset for a long time now.
"The name's... Tequila Sunset."
No. I don't *want* to be Tequila Sunset.
"Name-invention feels too dangerous."
"Yeah," he nods. "A name's the kind of shit that can kill a man. Mañana's a good name in that regard."
"What's your deal with names, anyhow? Is it a spiritual thing or a philosophical one or...?"
"More a poetic thing. Any attempt to formulate a grand unified theory about it ends in the stupidest shit imaginable. Doesn't make it less true, though." He nods sagely.
"That means I can't *tell* you about it. I can only *show* you. You may understand in time... or not. But it might be easy enough."
"Sounds stupid, is what I think."
"Yes, friend. The world is certainly stupid enough to have stupid features." He grins.
The man sits on the railing, his hands reaching far and wide, yet it feels as if he could effortlessly go even wider, if need be. An endless torrent of time.
"Nice talk. Gotta get moving." [Leave.]
"Can't live in this world without names, see. Important things, they are. Vessels of the soul."
"I can't disclose any details of an on-going case."
"The fat ones, always leeching on the honest man."
"And you're the ones to reform, thus reaping your own benefits?"
"At least you got the benefits, that's something."
"It's not enough. Not enough to get ahead. More about keepin' us in our place."
"So, anything else you wanted to discuss, boiadeiro?"
Nod knowingly.
Yeah! Let's get this party started, it's your chance to shine, boy!
What's there not to want? It's got range, meaning, layers, colours, associations, the whole works!
"The name's done! It's Raphaël Ambrosius Costeau."
"Are you *quite* sure?"
"Of course! It's such a *cool* name. Solemn, classy, historical... almost regal."
"Well, better than the other names I can come up with at least."
"Hold on, man. Keep it slow and steady, don't succumb to fate. It can take time to come up with a really good one..."
"You can't tell a Raphaël what to do."
"Fine, perhaps I'll try again... later."
"There's no rush to find yourself."
"If you say so." He shrugs and looks about at the surroundings.
"Yeah... okay, I'm totally Tequila Sunset."
"I don't operate in that capacity. I'm not a *granter of passage*." He takes a swig and points up the stairs with his flask. "The passage grants itself."
"Aye -- walk right past Measurehead and go in."

Surely a step in the right direction -- feel that smooth texture, savour that flavour. How it flows down your gullet, like a warm caress. *That's* the sunset. By the time you arrived in this world it was already late.
"I have no interest in drinking while on duty."
"A man walking on the edge of a razor, eh? Leaves more for me!" He laughs and takes another sip from the flask.
The idea of alcoholic swill sloshing around in your bloodstream feels fairly unappealing.
"Any idea who killed the hanged man?"
"The mercenary, aye?" He shrugs. "Who could have killed him, that's indeed the question. Why even do such a thing?" He shakes his head solemnly.
What's the matter with this wimp? Is he obstructing *justice*?!
"The merc was hanged with a very specific type of a cargo belt. One often used in heavy transport areas, for example, harbours."
"The harbour is a prime area of suspicion. In your opinion -- are the dockworkers involved in the killing?"
"Stop being a wimp, you need to help me out right *now*!"
"Let's change the topic."
"No need to get aggressive." He takes a swig from his flask. "I'm really not the one to ask."
"What a thought!" He scoffs, looking shocked. "Why would noble workers resort to such a thing. Unless they were *pushed*, of course."
"Your dead guy -- was an enemy combatant."

(Take a close look at the card.) "Guess not."

"Yes."
"Good thing too. I've known Johannes for a few years now, be *sinister* if he turned into a completely different person overnight."
He leans in to inspect the card. "How did you get his shift card anyway?"
"Does not seem plausible, now that I think of it."
"I found it on the ground. At the Whirling-in-Rags."
"Highly unlikely. I've known John for several years now. Also, you *told* me you're a cop, remember? How did you get his shift card?"
"Sure, I have no real need for it."
"No, I'm afraid. The card's evidence in an on-going investigation."
"Thank you plenty. I'll make sure John gets his card back."
"Oh, is my friend in some sort of trouble? Who knew..."
"Yes, and you also *told* me you're a cop. But now that this is settled..." He leans in to inspect the card. "How did you get his shift card?"
"Suspicious activity? How very troublesome... yet, take a look around. Strikers, protests, scabs -- isn't it all so very suspicious?" He smiles widely.
"So mysterious. So intriguing." The man gives out a jolly chortle. "Either way, the road in front of you is wide and open."
"Plenty to go around. Don't get greedy and try to swipe mine, though." He smiles merrily. "You've got your own."
"All right then." (Conclude.)
"Well met, Mañana. That's a sweet-ass name."
"A name worthy of the man who holds it, friend. Names are important."

The man whispers a jaunty tune. A coastal breeze ruffles his hair.
Why is that?

It might come in handy to present ideas as a part of reality -- the only reality that exists -- instead of some abstract *true form*. On the other hand, he's not lying when performing this sleight of hand. He's a self-interested moderate.
I don't want to talk about these interesting things. It's not my business.

Because?

"Past Measurehead?"
"Yeah, the two-and-a-half-metre tall Semenese supremacist there." He points to the bridge above the gates. "Walk right past him..."
"Uh. Gotcha. I think I have some questions for you first."
"Hmm, for some reason it doesn't seem like it's going to be that easy..."
"Don't worry, I'm sure it's not *completely* impossible. For example, you could best Measurehead in a physical confrontation."
"Or you could convert to his Semenese supremacist world view. Or, hmm," he strokes his moustache, "maybe it actually *is* completely impossible."
"Has anyone here ever bested him in a physical confrontation?"
"Has any of the scabs tried converting to his world view?"
"Got it. Another thing..."
"Jean-Luc himself would say the philosophy has proven... *overly heroic* for the scabs to convert to. Not enough intuition."
"Not yet, no." He fixes his eyes on you, evaluating your prowess. "He's... incredibly strong."
Nothing a couple of solid hooks from Dexter and Sinister won't fix.
"No-no, I said *scab*."
"Yeah, I'm a scab -- poor and downtrodden." (Wave your fist.) "Right to work!"
"Oh, sorry, friend. Didn't mean to throw it like that... it's a thing we harbour folk do. Comes naturally."
"Appreciated."
Say nothing, pocket the coin.
"Appreciated."
Say nothing, pocket the coin.

Say nothing, pick up and pocket coin.
Leave the coin where it landed.

"Yes," he nods solemnly. "The city has a way of pairing souls. John's been out drinking himself blind..."
"He should be more careful, that Johannes. Can I have the card?"
"Oh, John's been out drinking himself blind again? He should watch his step, that John. Can I have the card?"
"You're quite the righteous man." He smiles appreciatively. "Honour allows us to keep a respectful distance from each other. So, what do you need?"
You feel like you earned a significant amount of honour points today.

"... then press the button to unlock the door..."

He rubs the back of his head. "Was not meant as... provocation or ridicule."
"Right, always glad to help out! We're on the same branch, you and I. Not like these slithering scabs."
"Man of honour." He raises his eyebrow. "I respect that. We were talking about scabs, yeah?"
"Always glad to help out the RCM. Shame I can't do more -- things are meagre at the moment, due to..." He nods toward the protesters.
"You know -- the winter's fat is slowly running out and all. Still better than scabbing, though."
"Right, always glad to help out the RCM! We're on the same branch, you and I. Humans, I mean, not slithering scabs."
"The Union has problems getting by?"
"I'm always glad to help out when possible -- not like these slithering scabs." He looks at them in disbelief.
"Nothing to worry about, really. The jam's a bit of a mess, cargo can't get in or out. The rationing is a bit stricter, is all. Supplies should last the strike, though."
"Every little bit helps, you know."
"Gotta spend money to make money."
"Aye, you lost me there, honcho. But it's okay as long as you're not a sorry-ass scab." He looks at them in disbelief.
"Aye, now here's the thing... at any time, some other capitalist could take the place over with the blink of an eye, without even owning any of the buildings."

"He's probably in his container at the harbour, so head right on in there." He re-adjusts the beret on his head.

"You shouldn't take what's not yours."
That's a strange way to go about it.

"Then how can anything ever be 'mine'? But that's okay -- we don't have to agree. The prairie is wide enough for all of us."
What is this, news of the world? Talk about *personal stuff*. Get to know him.
Maybe I am a boiadeiro?
No.

"At least some people are willing to make the necessary sacrifices in order to reach higher, and to better the world."
"Is it the dulcet tone of ultraliberalism I hear?"
"Sure thing." A gust of wind blows through his hair.
"Hold up, what does that mean?"
"He was an agent of the opposition, attempting to undermine our honourable efforts."
"Fair enough. Seems interesting."
"Words guide our life, we commune with each thing through its word. Every word is also a name, is it not?" He smiles.
It doesn't sound that cool. Sounds antiquated, obsolete, *passé*. It's not *disco*.
That of a noble peasant or a travelling herdsman. True to yourself, independent in your actions, loyal to your friends.
What if...
No.
But...
Maybe...
I could...

Walk away. [Leave.]

"It was nothing."

"So..." He stares at you with his hazy eyes. "How'd you like our harbour?"
Big guy -- he means the leader of the scabs.

dialoguetext: "I guess getting past the man ain't that simple after all…" He pauses to think. "So, what now?"
"Who or what is a flying desperado?"

"He said it belonged to a weasel."
"I don't know, some whistleblower's I think?"
"Oh, say no more. I got you." He taps the side of his nose with a little wink.
"They're sort of like you. Preserve the rule of law and all that. Except it's Evrart's law." He takes a swig from his flask. "But, really, they're just like you."
"Los Ardies?" He smiles. "They're an independent militant group. A bit too high-strung, but it comes with the responsibility."
Is he actually comparing you -- an officer of the law -- to some neighbourhood vigilantes?!
Come on. He's just trying to keep the peace.
"There is only one law, friend -- and that's me!"
Let it go.
"Why not? Must be nice being something else for a change. The rest of us are just folks."
The boiadeiro stares at you with respect -- then gestures towards the trickles of blood adorning your clothes.
"Yeah, I got shot. No big deal."
"It really hurts, Mañana. Pain -- that's what your strike brought upon us."
"Danger comes with the boiadeiro lifestyle, right?
He shrugs. "There are types of danger. The one I'm usually concerned with is lung cancer, or getting mauled by wildlife. Not... bullets."
"Yet you live?" He nods approvingly. "It calls back to an older era, where this was commonplace. You have a true boiadeiro heart."
He shrugs. "Any political movement goes through a period of strife. Shame you got mixed up in it, though."
"What's going to happen next?"
"Time will tell..." He shrugs. "I'll tell the bossman you dropped by. I'm sure he'll be glad."
"Okay, I think might be Harry." (Conclude.)

"A strong, solid name telling of dedication and honour." He gives a small salute. "Well met, Harrier."
"Right. So where is everyone?"
"It calls back to an older era, where this was commonplace, though. You have a true boiadeiro heart."
"Yet it calls back to an older era, where this was commonplace. You have a true boiadeiro heart."

"You can't help me get inside?"

"Heh." He smiles. "The little *boia* did good on his promise."
"Hey, you're the man in boots at the gates -- Cuno said you know about the armour."

dialoguetext: "His promise?"
"To get me into trouble. To *sic the pigs* on me -- pardon the choice of words. Not mine."
"What happened?"
"What happened?"
"I was asked to look into that armour situation. Official Union probe, you know -- track it down, see who took it."
"Serves me right for doing menial footwork. I dropped that probe right then and there -- and it *still* got me into trouble," he smiles. "One bad move is all it takes."
"So Cuno used us to, what? Scare you?"
"Did you?"
"Did you?"
"At first I thought -- why not, maybe the pieces can feed the strike? Buy us a few more days under the sun, you know."
"So I went to this boy. He said he'll make me his *prison bitch*. He's got *eyes everywhere*, the cops in his pocket and he's the king of Jamrock."
"It's a minor nuisance. It's all good." He contemplates taking a swig from his flask.
He thinks -- not yet. Better to get this business out of the way. Sweeter then.
"The probe into the armour -- what did you learn?"
"I learned that people don't want to talk to a drunk Union man about some armour."
"Not much. Technical stuff mostly. That was the interesting part."
"What else?"
"Okay. Anything else?"
"I did some research into this *armadura*. Let's say I have friends at the library," he explains with a wry smile. "I didn't get into the material science, just how it comes off."
"What sort of technical stuff?"
"In parts. Four in total. The helmet was the first to go, the kid says he tore it off and kicked it into the sea. I believe him. The boots were still on the guy last I saw. Too hard to remove."
"So -- as I count -- there are two parts missing: the gauntlets and the cuirass. This is where I left off. Too much hassle. More like a job for some *milicia*."
"Thank you for the cooperation, sir."
"How then?"
"How *does* it come off?"
It's implied he finds it unlikely that you will succeed in this.
"No problem." He finally takes a swig from the flask. "If you see that kid, thank him from Call Me Mañana. Thank him for showing me the *way*."
He is sincerely grateful he is not tracking down pieces of armour right now.
"I'm ambitious. I'm going to find *all of it*. All the pieces."
"I'm going to find *one* piece of it. One is enough."

dialoguetext: "Actually, I may have better things to do too."
"Nice." The moustached man nods in approval. "From what I learned it was a very heavy, boring set of armour."
"I agree, officer. Let's focus on the hanging and later some junior officers can take care of the rest."
"Nice and balanced," the lieutenant nods. "Some junior officers can take care of the rest."
"All of it?" The lieutenant raises his brow. "There are junior officers out there, eager to prove themselves. I would leave *some* for them, but okay. Let's find *all of it*."
"Smart choice," the moustached man agrees. "It's only that *one* spot you need armoured too -- the one the bullet hits."
"A Mesquese epic then, all across Martinaise." He glances south, where the canal runs: "I hope it will be a real *bonanza* for you."
"What's the strike about anyway?"
"You know... serious business." He smiles. "I'm sure the big boss would be glad to tell you. You'll have to ask him first."
"Right! You talked to the boss, eye-to-eye -- like men of the plain. If you have any more questions, I'm set to talk."
"Serious business, as I'm sure you now realize. The boss would have been glad to tell you. Alas, you cannot get to him anymore."
"What will *you* be doing now?"
"I'll be okay here, doing lookout." He surveys the red flags, draped from the harbour gates. "Quite the sight, aren't they? Getting to like that red, I am..."
"Don't worry about me. I live to alleviate the worries of our brothers. See if any other insane killers turn up. Then I'll run. And live."
"I'm sure you'll do good."
"Try not to get shot, eh?"
"You know it, friend." He smooths his moustache with his hand.
"I'm sure I'll be luckier than you, friend." His grin is as wide as a desert.
"I was hoping you could tell me."
"I got *that* key right here. And let me tell you, it's mighty good of you to help us out during the strike -- working class solidarity, as they say."
"I heard something about a weasel and it didn't sound like a local *polar* weasel, if you know what I mean." (Wink.)
"I saw an opportunity and I took it. I'm a hustlegrinder."
"I'm not really doing this for political reasons."
"I'm not opening this door for myself. I'm opening it for all working men."
"Polar weasel? Oh... I know what you mean. I'm pretty sure he's actually Occidental though. So you're gonna be commitin' fratricide, my racist friend."

"What you're looking for is a basement door behind the greenhouse -- that's behind the Whirling-in-Rags -- that's all I know. Our organisation is what you call *compartmentalized*. Means we keep out of each other's business."
"Okay, but where did you get the key from?"
"Where did you get the key from?"
"Hehe, I'm not so sure about the hustle-grind, but..." He waves at you. "You know, it doesn't matter. It's a good thing you're doing. Thanks."
"Oh so the none-of-the-above type, are you? I get it, I get it. I like to keep my distance too." He nods. "But it doesn't matter. It's a good thing you're doing. Thanks."
"I knew this man was a commie." He smiles, tilting his head. "And it's a good thing you're doing too. Thanks."
"The janitor gave it to me. Nice fella. We talked about life and things that really, *truly* matter." His gaze wanders off into the distance.
He shakes his head. "I'm more of a philosophical dockworker. I like to talk about the big picture stuff. Who I am. Who you are. What we are fighting for..." The man takes a big sip from his flask.
He's a chatty guy. *Wants* to talk about the strike. Return once you've met the Union boss, and are on a better footing with the organization.
"That weasel I visited. Turns out he has one hell of a colonial mug collection."
"Yeah..." He nods, rubbing his chin. "The janitor who gave me the key to his apartment said the guy's a bit of an asshole."
"Yes, his mug-collection certainly represented... *antiquated* social values."
"A man with such a funny mug collection can't be that bad."
"All I'm saying is he had lots of mugs."
"Like I said before, I don't know much about this weasel, but the bossman said he's a real piece of work." He touches his beret. "Thanks for helping out, friend."
"None of this mess we're in. This jivin' and jugglin'... What's it for?" He doesn't wait for your answer. "To feed our children I guess."
He means he's not gonna tell you, 'cause he doesn't know. But he will shoot his mouth off with you now that you're working for Evrart.
Who *he* is and what they're fighting for? This is interesting.

He can't know that. Maybe you're just younger on the photo.

Something changes in his disposition. A merciful smile in the corner of his eye.
He's not lying -- about not doing it himself.
"I've come to Martinaise investigating a murder."
"Murder, huh? That sounds like a lot of hard work. You'd never see me investigating a murder."
"It's actually very fun and easy."
"You're right. It's almost impossible. I'm 91% sure I'll never get it solved."
(Whisper) "I have no idea what I'm *doing*."

He didn't do it. It's the truth.
Should we? He's *nice*. I don't like *nice*.
"I don't believe you. Poste L'Aventurier said the same thing. They tried to get me to be their postman. So fun, so easy, they said. It's just walking." He shakes his head at the memory.
"It wasn't. I'm doing much better here at the harbour. Being an honest Union man with *a lot* of free time on his hands."
"Probably not." He nods. "I wouldn't even know where to start with that. Much better here at the harbour -- for an honest Union man like me."
He whispers back: "That's okay. I have no idea what I'm doing either. I don't even know what day it is..." He thinks and then decides: "Don't tell me. It's a *better* day that way."

He's a chatty guy. *Wants* to talk about the strike too. Just can't break the command structure and tell you now.

"I almost had a heart attack..."
"I'm really sorry, friend. Frittte's nearby, get some *nosaphed*." He points to the boutique just right of him. "Good stuff. Helps against heart attacks too."
"Why not? I need to get through the gate to the harbour. You need to let me in!"
Unless...

"All right, I may have *some* advice for you on how to deal with Jean-Luc there -- out of solidarity to the RCM. It's low on technology, however."
Hmm... maybe that *would* work? We'll have to see.

You've been in there, he means -- talked to the boss man too probably...
"Labour utopia." (Nod approvingly.)

He means -- a more violent faction could easily take care of such a thing.

"Thank you -- this has been of *limited* use."

"Got it."
"I'm more of a philosophical dockworker, see -- I like to talk about the big picture stuff. Who I am. Who you are. What we are fighting for..." The man takes a big sip from his flask.
"However much you feed the wolf..."
"... the wolf always wants more. I like wolves."
"Cool. I don't have anything to add to that."
"A *none-of-the-above* kind of man? No harm in being that."
"You mean corruption?"
"By that you mean corruption?"
"... the old man is corrupt for our *benefit* and we know it. Appreciate it, even. He is, personally, not too lavish."
"That desk seemed lavish to me."
"You're right. He's very ascetic."
"Okay, he's *reasonably* lavish, sure. That's his prerogative. It's not like you want a saintly demeanour on a corrupt motherfucker. That would be a manipulative illusion."
"Besides, there are no non-corrupt systems in the world anyway. And *moralism* is the most corrupt of them all."
This man has political theory -- and it has not failed him today.
Not you, you would like to say... But then there's that weasel door.
This was great. You feel mentally reinvigorated.
Be honest with him.
"I've tried that. They don't like what I came up with."
"Too bad. Can't live in this world without a good name, friend. Important things, they are. Vessels of the soul."
"I've already got some armour. I'm pretty happy without struggling to find more."

Now's your chance! Remember, communists are notoriously skittish, so it's best to *insinuate* your way in...
Hold on: This isn't a man who goes in for subterfuge. He prefers someone who'll look him in the eye and say exactly what's on his mind.

It was a foolish approach to begin with.
"I'm looking for some people who know how to really grind a sausage, if you know what I mean."
"It involves our mutual friend, Kras." (Put your hands next to your head and curl your fingers like deer antlers.)
"I'm investigating a peculiar smell, one with revolutionary implications."
"I'm looking for a secret cabal of *mole people*."
"I believe there's a cell of radical communists operating in Martinaise. Can you help me find them?"
"What I'm trying to say is: I'm looking for communists. You know any?"
"Hrmmm. Have you tried a butcher shop?" He looks at you with perfect equanimity.
"Don't think I've ever met a Kras, personally. Then again, I've never been to Graad." He narrows one eye at you.
"Could be coming from one of the jammed lorries? Cargo's been sitting out for a while." He sniffs the air and looks toward the roundabout.
"Hrmm... you might have to look elsewhere for help with that." He scratches his chin.
"Now that *is* an important subject, but also a sensitive one. Still, good of you to just come straight out with it. No beating about the bush..." He smooths the twin bars of his moustache.

"Oh, he certainly likes to take his time with things, especially when politics are at issue."

"I'm not 'hunting' communists, I'm trying to get organised by them."

"Honestly, I had a weird dream and now I need to get to the bottom of it."
"Oh, I see..." He gives you an exaggerated wink.
"A fellow plains-roamer, in search of greater understanding. A classic story..." He nods approvingly.
"Chasing a dream, huh? I have to respect that, boia..." He gives you a small salute.
"I wish I could help. Unfortunately, I don't know many communistas."
"Maybe, maybe not." He shrugs. "Either way, I'm not institutional. A man's got to blaze his own trail, in my book..."
"Some are, some aren't." He shrugs. "It's a big institution, room for all kinds: communistas, Semenese supremacists, even an anti-institutional boiadeiro..."
"Didn't realize you could smell communism." He frowns. "But then, I've never studied the subject..."
"I know you said you're not really a communist, but aren't you actually a communist?"
"I thought you Union guys were all communists?"
"Are you sure? You smell just like a communist."
Blazing his own trail, being his own man... not exactly your typical communist spiel.
There is warmth in his voice when he talks about the Union. Whatever his personal politics, this is his home.
You can smell all sorts of things... fear, disgust, desire. Not communism, though.
Okay, so maybe he's not exactly a communist, but there's definitely some communistic residue about him.
Alright, so if he isn't personally a communist, he's definitely hanging out with them.
Maybe it's not taught in any of your so-called universities, but there's definitely something going on here...
He snaps his fingers. "Ah, but you know, I did meet a genuine *ideólogo* a few months ago. Perhaps he is your guy?"
"What's an *ideólogo*?"
"Did he say his name was 'Steban,' by chance?"
"How did you meet him?"
"Okay, how do I find this guy?" (Proceed.)
"I couldn't tell you. Once I declined his offer, we finished our cigarettes and he disappeared back into the night. Just before he melted into the shadows he turned to me and said..."
"*Remember Dobreva and Abadanaiz*..."

Wow, this one's a deep cut. Julia Dobreva and Jean Abadanaiz, popularly known as the 'Revolutionary Lovers', served as Dual Commissars of Revolution on the Insulindian front during the Antecentennial Revolution. Their forbidden love, as well as their disappearance during the final collapse of the Revacholian commune only contributed to their mystique...
Their remains were discovered on a beach in Ozonne in '35. Subsequent forensic analysis suggested suicide by poison.
"... and then he was gone."
"Who are Dobreva and Abadanaiz?"
"'The Revolutionary Lovers.'"
"What do you think it means?" (Conclude.)
"I don't know. Guess not everyone remembers." A tight, half-smile crosses his face.
"So they were lovers, eh? Makes sense, he seemed like a romantic, in his way."
"He's not the only one, it seems." The lieutenant doesn't even look up from his notebook.
"*Ahem*..." The lieutenant clears his throat.

"Been wondering about that myself." He scratches his chin. "Some communista inside-talk, could be. Not meant for the wider public. They love that kind of thing. You'd have to ask someone who knows this ideólogo personally..."
"Not to interfere in your personal errand, but it might have something to do with that *passphrase* Cindy mentioned earlier."
Of course, such "inside-talk" might also serve as a handy passphrase...
"I have to say, though: It sounds like you've found yourself a proper hunt."
"That's really dumb. You should feel embarrassed even suggesting that."
"Wait, what was that about again?"
"Oh, right. Good thinking, Kim."
"I was totally about to say that."
"She said that you would need some kind of *passphrase* to gain access to this so-called *mega secret* meeting." He snaps the elastic band around his notebook.
The lieutenant nods.
"Of course you were, detective. Apologies for interrupting." The lieutenant smiles to himself.
"You're right. How foolish of me. Won't happen again, detective."
"Just in time, the faithful partner arrives with the key that turns the lock. You two make a good pair..."
No, you weren't. Otherwise you *would have* said it. In truth, it was quite beyond your associative powers.
"Sound like you two may have been riding together too long. The strain of the open range, and so on..."
"I salute you, boias, and wish you good fortune on this grand ideological quest." He tips his hat ever so slightly.
"I have to say, though: It sounds like you've found yourself a proper hunt."
"Is that so?" He raises an eyebrow. "Well, in that case, I salute you, boia, and wish you good fortune on this grand ideological quest."
"That's alright. I think you may have just given me the last piece of the puzzle."
"You know, a guy with a theory. Someone who likes to pit his theory against other theories in deadly theory-combat."
"Didn't say anything about his name. Wasn't the sort of encounter where names matter."
"It was late one night as I was leaving the harbour. He was waiting on the corner in a bright white jacket, classic Saramirizian style..."
"He asked me for a light. We shared cigarettes. Then he asked if I ever thought about 'getting into some of the extra-physical branches of communism'."
See? All this political chit-chat is just an excuse to rip tar with strangers. Let's say we just skip right to the good part, then?
"Hang on. What does that mean, *the extra-physical branches of communism*?"
"What did you tell him?"
(Nod.) "An extremely cool way to establish contact. Wish I'd thought of that."
"The same thing I always tell people who try to press some claim on me: I said, 'Every boiadeiro rides alone'."
"No idea. I took it to mean he was asking me to join some sort of underground cell..."
"A very old-school organising technique, the sort of thing communistas used to do before the Revolution."
He shrugs. "It was alright. A little like something out of a Vespertine spy novel, but I must respect the effort."
"It was late one night as I was leaving the harbour. He was waiting on the corner in a classic Saramirizian jacket, a lot like the one you've got there..."
"IT IS MY TASK TO KEEP THE DEGENERATE DRUNKS FROM ENTERING THE HARBOUR."
"ARE YOU ADMIRING MY MORPHOPHYSIOLOGY?" A ripple of muscle passes underneath his skin. He lets you look.
"STOP IT. YOU ARE EMBARRASSING YOURSELF IN FRONT OF THIS WOMAN, AND YOUR PAEDOMORPHIC FRIEND."
Say nothing, size him up first.
"YOUR BODY BETRAYS YOUR DEGENERACY."
"Yeah, Measurehead, his body totally betrays his degeneracy," the young woman at the giant's side agrees.
"We don't have time to get into this now." [Leave.]
"YOUR RACE DESCENT HAS ONLY *WORSENED* SINCE I LAST SAW YOU -- YOU HAVE REALLY LET YOURSELF GO."
Things are not as bad as they look. Sure, you have high blood pressure from metabolizing heroic quantities of ethanol. But you are robustly built. You will survive.
You hear your heart pumping, fast and irregular. Your joints ache and you feel old... but still alive, somehow.
Merely standing up makes you sweat profusely. Your breathing is erratic. Your own heartbeat in your ears grows frantic and you feel your blood pressure rise.
"I CAN SEE YOU WERE ONCE AN ATHLETE. THEN DETERIORATED IN YOUR TWENTIES. IT IS TYPICAL OF YOUR HAPLOGROUP. LET'S BLAME THE FAILED EDUCATION SYSTEM AND LENIENCY TOWARD DEGENERATES IN YOUR HOMELAND."
Don't say anything, size him up first.
"Come on, I just need you to move about twenty centimetres back."
Push him out of the way.
"THAT IS RIGHT." He doesn't even flinch. "YOU SHOULD LEAVE THE STAGE OF HISTORY WITH DIGNITY -- BY INVITING THE OTHER RACES TO A *GREAT WORLD WAR*."
Subscribe to his advanced race theory.
Knock him out.
"Evrart told you to help us get the body down from the tree."

dialoguetext: "BUT." He leans in and intones: "WHILE I AM GONE SOMEONE MUST STAND GUARD ON THE BRIDGE. THAT SOMEONE NEEDS TO BE *YOU*."
She turns to you. "So, you guys are like cops or something?"
"Yeah, we're the Law around here."
"You hear that?" The lieutenant looks toward the yard. "That sound. He's *breaking* something."
"Apparently so."
The man turns to look behind him -- at the behemoth appearing around the corner, approaching him, walking past him...
"Yes, I am an unbelievably corrupt cop. I am corrupt every opportunity I get."
"Look at you, RCM rent-a-cops!" A loud voice booms in from below: "Guarding that bridge like Evrart's lapdogs, is this where it's at now? The RCM is for sale?"
"THE CORPSE HAS BEEN REMOVED FROM THE TREE." He brushes wooden flakes off his hands: "STAND DOWN AND CONGRATULATE YOURSELF. YOU HAVE SIDED WITH RACE VICTORY TODAY."
"I'll work with whoever I want."
"Cool. I like men with guns and power." The woman twirls her hair. "I'm Katya by the way..."
The man is still knocked out. He breathes slowly and steadily.
It'll take a few moments for him to recover.
"DO NOT PRESUME THIS HAS DRASTICALLY ALTERED OUR RACE DYNAMIC."
"TRUE. I SAID NOTHING ABOUT OUR PERSONAL DYNAMIC -- THAT HAS ALTERED." He adds: "A LITTLE."
[Leave.]
"Please, stop doing this. You're making us look bad."
Go ahead, don't be shy. Just ask for race secrets.
Ask what kind of races are there first. Classification is core to this stuff.
"I knocked you out like a god of martial arts."
"It was just something I had to do."
Just like that, instinct took over -- a solid strike straight into his throat, into the cartilage! You could swear you felt the soft palate break...
How did this happen? Your little fist is in his giant hand and he's squeezing it. It hurts...
"YOU MUST BE OUT OF YOUR MIND, DEGENERATE DRUNK." The pressure on your hand becomes unbearable. "SAY IT: *I AM A DEGENERATE ALCOHOLIC*."
Don't say it. You're not a degenerate alcoholic, you're a cop and a hero.
"I... am... a... a degenerate al... alcoholic."
"F... d... dfuck you!"
"I'm a... cop."
"Help!"
"GOOD." He releases your hand. "NOW LEAVE, BEFORE YOU HUMILIATE YOUR HOMO-EROTIC ORGANISATION ANY FURTHER."
Your fist cracks in his hand like a ripe apple. Pain shoots up into your brain as he's twisting it more and more:
Your hand cracks and twists in his grasp but your body is too numb with adrenaline to feel it...
Your hand twists in his grip and the pain blinds you. Still you press the words out of your swollen mouth...
"No. I... won't fucking say anything."
"I... am... the law."
"I am invincible. It doesn't hurt..."
"There's nothing you can do to me... that *treacherous whores* haven't done to me already."
He can't hurt you. What more can he do that you haven't gone through already?
"RABID ANIMAL, YOU SHOULD BE PUT DOWN." He releases your poor hand from his grasp. "I WILL NOT BE THE ONE WHO GETS YOUR STINK ON ME."
All you hear is a small gurgling sound as a trickle of blood appears on the man's lip.
Now's the time for a SPIN KICK! He expects the one-two, not the one-three-sixty!
He's open, rip into him. Right hook. Escalate it, get *intimate* with him... bring the hurt closer!
No, don't be a fucking ballerina, rip into him, right hook! Get *intimate* with him... bring the hurt closer!
(Rip into him with a right hook.)
(Back up and perform a 360° flying spin-kick.)
Oh god, wrong move! Your head is in his hands, like a pair of forceps crushing you and you can feel every joule...
"SAY IT: 'I AM A DEGENERATE DRUNK.'"
Take the pain, god damn it, at least take that!
"YOU ARE A POOR PLAYER OF PHYSICAL CHESS." He lets go of your head. You slump to the ground.
(Try to somehow wiggle yourself loose from his grasp.)
"Assault of a police officer! Help!"
"I.... am a degener... degener... degenerate drunk!"
"Never."
The compression is unbearable. This is causing some serious damage to whatever precious, gelatinous thing is inside there... your sight turns red.
Even under the increased force on your skull there is no pain... just the sound of your own blood gushing in there, feeding your mind with oxygen.

The man lands with a dull thump, like a broken down puppet of muscles and sinew. For a moment he still tries to keep his head up, dazed eyes looking at you with unimaginable surprise.... To your left is *The Button.*
"Welcome to Revachol!!"
As you slam your fist on the button the man collapses entirely, his head rolling to the side...
(Just press the button.)
"Disco inferno!" (Press the button.)
"The end has begun -- I am the lion-headed cavalry." (Press the button.)
"I'm so sorry, I didn't want to do this." (Press the button.)
"No one is the new Measurehead -- let's go. Before he gets up..." The lieutenant makes haste toward the door.
"I... I... I am a violent drunk..."
It has happened *again*! The titan has your fist locked in his hand and he's twisting it...
"GOOD." He releases your small hand. "NOW GO. BEFORE YOU ENTER CARDIAC ARREST."
Try again, punch his lights out with a right hook!
Not again... take the pain, god damn it, at least take that!
That would mean you're openly showing the people that you're taking the Union's side.
"Wait, that showing everyone that I'm taking orders from the Union."
"YES. THAT IS PRECISELY WHAT IT MEANS, HOMONCULUS. THIS IS NOT GOING TO HAPPEN ANY OTHER WAY."
"Okay then." (Wait here while Measurehead goes.)
"No, I'm not going to do that." (Back off.)
"FINE. GOOD-BYE. RETURN TO YOUR DEGENERACY."
The woman looks toward the yard. "Jean-Luc must be really tearing it up over there. I wish I could see it..."
"I also wish I could see it."
"I don't. I've seen enough of that dead body already."
Your body does *not* betray your degeneracy, that's a lie. You're in great shape.
"My body does *not* betray my degeneracy!"
"What do you mean, my body betrays my degeneracy?"
"My body is unimportant."
"IT MUST BE FRIGHTENING TO STAND IN THE SHADOW OF THIS *RACIAL PINNACLE*. BE CALM, HAM SANDWICH. YOU ARE NOT IN DANGER, BECAUSE YOU ARE NOT A THREAT TO ME."
"THAT IS PRECISELY THE NEGLIGENCE THAT HAS LED YOU TO SUCCUMB TO *AL GUL*." His face contorts in disgust, as if he were smelling a dead rat.
Puff out your chest, still say nothing.
"WHAT IS THIS *ANDROGYNOUS* DISPLAY OF SEXUAL MATURITY?" He looks down at you, taking stock of your physique.
"THIS DISPLAY OF WEAKNESS MAY APPEAL TO OLDER WOMEN, WITH A STRONGER MATERNAL INSTINCT -- BUT IT IS A LIABILITY, HERE ON *BATTLEFIELD MARTINAISE*."
"Jean-Luc, his body is betraying his degeneracy pretty hard..." She holds her nose. "Maybe you can ask him to leave?"
"Wait, uhm... *Al Gul*?"
"You're right, I'm an alcoholic. Now, I need to enter the harbour."
"You're right. I'm a servant of Al Gul, but I still need to enter the harbour."
"YOUR BODY CONTINUES TO BETRAY YOUR DEGENERACY."
"YES -- *AL GUL*.
"YOU HAVE SUCCUMBED TO *AL GUL*." His face contorts in disgust -- as if he were smelling a dead rat.
"YOU REEK OF IT. AN INVISIBLE SWORD OF *AL GUL* EMERGES FROM YOUR THROAT. YOU CANNOT SEE IT, BUT OTHERS CAN. IT IS MAKING THE WOMAN IN MY COMPANY SICK."
"THIS IS A FABRICATION THE AL-CHEMISTS OF YEESUT AND BASHIR AND THEIR GOLEM, AL GUL, HAVE FED YOUR PEOPLE. GO ON BELIEVING IN IT, *RACE LOSER*."
"But what *is* Al Gul?"
"CORRECT, MY SMALL-SKULLED SERVANT." He nods approvingly.
He means *alcohol*.
"AL GUL IS AN ANCIENT IILMARAAN POISON, A PARASITIC FUNGUS THAT HAS COLONIZED YOUR RACE. IT IS A TRICK THE DESERT PYGMEES PLAYED ON YOU -- FOR HUMILIATING THEM AND STRIPPING THEM OF THEIR LAND."
Intentionally fermented drinks have existed for ten thousand years...
"The Iilmaraan people did not invent alcohol. It's existed since the neolithic."
"You mean alcohol?"
"This explains everything."
"I don't think that's how history works."
"That's probably right, yes."
"WHY DON'T YOU HAVE ANOTHER DRINK? YOUR FEATURES ARE NOT YET CONGENITALLY DEFORMED ENOUGH."
"Oh yeah, Measurehead..." The babe looks at him with eyes full of admiration that transcends the merely sexual.
This is going well for Measurehead.
"GOOD, THERE IS A *FRITTTE* NEARBY. CONGRATULATE YOURSELF WITH ANOTHER DRINK. YOUR FEATURES ARE NOT YET CONGENITALLY DEFORMED ENOUGH."
"CORRECT, MY SMALL-SKULLED SERVANT." He nods approvingly.
"NO, YOU DON'T, YOU NEED TO GET ANOTHER DRINK; OCCIDENTAL HAPLOGROUP B4 IS DONE GIVING ORDERS AROUND HERE. THE INFLUENCE OF THE *HAM SANDWICH RACE* IS WANING."
"YOUR MOUTH MOVES, BUT THE ONE WHO SPEAKS IS AL GUL. YOU ARE BUT A VESSEL FOR THE GHOUL NOW. VERY LITTLE OF YOUR SELF REMAINS."
"Understood."
"I DOUBT IT, MY MICROCEPHALIC RACE SERVANT."
(Smell your breath.) "Kim, is it really so bad?"
"It's not good."
It's like a rat crawled into your stomach, got drunk and drowned.
"Enough. I need you to open the door to the harbour."
"This has nothing to do with why I'm here."
"YOUR LIFE AND THE LIFE OF YOUR RACE REVOLVE AROUND *AL GUL*. IT HAS EVERYTHING TO DO WITH WHY YOU'RE HERE."
"SERVITUDE TO AL GUL DOES NOT EXPLAIN *EVERYTHING*. THERE ARE OTHER REASONS FOR YOUR RACE DESCENT."
"YOU GAVE THE WORLD *EUGENICS*, ELECTRICITY, AND POWERFUL WEAPONS OF WAR LIKE MISSILES AND AEROSTATIC AIRCRAFT. YOU MADE GREAT GAINS IN METALLURGY, RACE THEORY, AND STATECRAFT."
"NO." He cranes his head. "I HAVE HEARD ABOUT IT. ON THE RADIO."
"So, you *did* come from the islands?"
"So... you did *not* come from the islands?"

"I AM A DESCENDANT. THE NARROW STREETS OF ULUNBUIR ARE WITH ME IN MY GENETIC DREAMS, I SEE YOUNG SEMENESE WOMEN WALK INTO THE GREY MASS ON *ILE DU FANTÔME*, WAITING ON IMMACULATE CONCEPTION FROM THE PALE."
"So you were born and raised on the islands, before you moved to Revachol?"
"It is, baby, yeah. You know it!"

"YOU DOMINATED LESSER CULTURES -- LIKE THE DEFORMED HIMEANS AND THE INEXPLICABLY POTATO-OBSESSED KOJKOS -- BUT NOW YOUR ASCENT TO THE GENETIC SUMMIT HAS HALTED. YOU ARE OBSESSED WITH SADNESS AND WITH FRIVOLOUS POP CULTURE."
"BRING YOUR TROOPS TO THE SEMENINE ISLANDS AND TO BOOGIE STREET AND WE WILL PULVERIZE YOU. WHEN YOU ARE GONE WE WILL BUILD A MUSEUM FOR YOU."
"THE WALLS WILL BE LINED WITH BOTTLES OF *AL GUL* -- YOUR BELOVED BEVERAGE. INSIDE WE WILL STORE THE ODES TO HOMO-SEXUALITY YOU CALL ART AND YOUR MICROCEPHALIC SKULLS."
"I don't have a problem with Al Gul. I just drink a little on the weekends."
Show him the ham still got it!
Does this remind you of someone? The guy down there...
"That fat racist over there... (Point to the racist lorryman.) You're just him after pumping some iron."
"Actually, I think the ham sandwich race still has it in them."
"I am the police and I need you to comply -- now!" (Take a step closer.)
"The race stuff is unimportant here -- I just need you to help me do my job, please."

"LOOK AT MY CRANIOLOGY. I AM THE PINNACLE OF MY HAPLOGROUP. THE PINK BLOB IS A BAD EXAMPLE EVEN OF YOURS. IT SADDENS ME..." He pauses in melancholy reflection. "YOU WERE ONCE A NOBLE AND POWERFUL RACE."
"WILLINGLY CALLING YOURSELF A HAM SANDWICH. HOW FAR THE OCCIDENTAL HAPLOGROUP HAS FALLEN..." He pauses in melancholy reflection. "YOU WERE ONCE A NOBLE AND POWERFUL RACE."
"JERKING MOTIONS. SIGNS OF A LATE-STAGE NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDER. HOW FAR THE OCCIDENTAL HAPLOGROUP HAS FALLEN..." He pauses in melancholy reflection. "YOU WERE ONCE A NOBLE AND POWERFUL RACE."
"BEGGING FOR HELP. ATTEMPTING TO PASS FEAR FOR COOPERATION. HOW FAR THE OCCIDENTAL HAPLOGROUP HAS FALLEN..." He pauses in melancholy reflection. "YOU WERE ONCE A NOBLE AND POWERFUL RACE."
"OCCIDENTAL HAPLOGROUP B4 IS DONE GIVING ORDERS AROUND HERE. THE INFLUENCE OF THE *HAM SANDWICH RACE* IS WANING."
"First, let me make this clear: I'm not a drunk. I'm a cop. I just have a drink every now and then, everyone does."
"THE ETHANOL FUNGUS IS DEEP WITHIN YOUR NERVOUS SYSTEM, PULLING THE STRINGS. YOU ARE MERELY ITS *PUPA* NOW. I SEE NO HOPE FOR YOU OR YOUR KIND."
There is a button right behind him, just out of reach... it must be the one that opens the door to the harbour.
This man is not budging. Let's hope his superiors inside are more cooperative.
"You're right about all this. Now I just need you to let me go into the harbour."
"The situation is serious. Your people have probably killed a man. I need to talk to your boss."
"This is going nowhere." [Leave.]
"LAST WE SAW, YOUR RACE WAS BEING SUPERSEDED BY THE SEMENESE."
"YOU WILL BE SUPERSEDED -- ISN'T THAT RIGHT, BABE?"
"ENOUGH WITH THIS BEGGING. YOU SHOULD LEAVE THE STAGE OF HISTORY WITH DIGNITY -- BY INVITING THE OTHER RACES TO A *GREAT WORLD WAR*."
No, there's a peaceful solution. You could *internalize* Measurehead's race theory. He would take you as one of his own.
There may be a peaceful solution to this. You could *internalize* Measurehead's race theory. He would take you as one of his own.
Right. Good idea.
Wouldn't that mean I have to become a Semenese supremacist myself?
But I already subscribe to one race theory, won't they conflict each other?
The *down with racism* thing? That's basic race theory. This is way above that. *Way*.
Well, not as such. What you do with a mastery of advanced race theory is up to you. You could reject the findings, sure -- or accept them and become an *advanced* racist.
The *best* idea.
I like the punching idea more.
Do it! Now!
"You serve the Union, don't you? Aren't they... white?"
There must be *some* friction there. He's keeping it well hidden, however...
"You keep telling yourself that."
"I'm sorry, of course. I understand now. Deeper."
"ALSO -- TO SERVE IS NOBLE, IT TAKES DISCIPLINE. YOUR PETULANT INDIVIDUALISM HAS ONLY CONTRIBUTED TO YOUR *RACE FAILURE*. IT IS LAX AND MORONIC."
"JAM. INDIVIDUALISM. YOU HAVE GOTTEN THESE IDEAS FROM DEGENERATE YOUTH CULTURE, HAVE YOU NOT? YOU HAVE PICKED THEM UP FROM ROCK AND ROLL SONGS?"
"MR. CLAIRE IS A MAN OF VISION AND MEANS. HE HAS THE WILL TO CONFRONT POLYCULTURAL CAPITAL -- SOMETHING *YOUR* RACE NAIVISTIC COMMUNISTS NEVER DID."
"MR. CLAIRE IS A MAN OF VISION AND MEANS. HE HAS THE WILL TO CONFRONT INTERNATIONAL CAPITAL, WHICH IS SOMETHING YOUR RACE NAIVISTIC COMMUNISTS NEVER DID."
"Communism is pretty cool."
"Individualism is my jam."
"Enough of this."

"IDIOTIC COMMUNISM IS THE SINGLE GREATEST CONTRIBUTOR TO YOUR RACE DESCENT. EVERYWHERE AROUND YOU, THE FRUITS OF ITS FAILURE TO CHALLENGE THE WORLD ORDER: INDIVIDUALISM, ROCK AND ROLL MUSIC, SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED DISEASES..."

"ABOVE ALL -- RAMPANT MULTINATIONAL FINANCE STILL REIGNING LARGE. TELL ME, WHERE HAVE YOU GOTTEN YOUR LOVE OF PATHETIC COMMUNISM FROM?" He leans closer. "DEGENERATE YOUTH CULTURE? ROCK AND ROLL MUSIC?"
"I'm no communist."
He looks toward the harbour, motionless. The tattoos on his face like a web of stone.

"OF COURSE YOU ARE, REVACHOLIAN MAN. THE FAILURE OF COMMUNISM TO CHALLENGE THE WORLD ORDER IS THE CORE OF YOUR RACE FATE. ALL AROUND YOU, THE FRUITS OF ITS DEFEAT: INDIVIDUALISM, ROCK AND ROLL MUSIC, SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED DISEASE..."
"What are those tattoos of yours supposed to mean?"
"RACISTS ARE GENERALLY NOT VERY GOOD EXAMPLES OF THEIR RACE." He gestures toward the lorryman down the street...
"I AM NOT LIKE THEM. I AM CRANIOMETRIC PERFECTION. I HAVE TAKEN THE TROUBLE TO PERMANENTLY DRAW A PHRENOLOGIC GRID ON MY SKULL AND FEATURES. THIS SHOULD DISPEL ANY DOUBT."
"DON'T BE VULGAR. WHITE OR NOT HAS GOT LITTLE TO DO WITH THIS. THE *RACE ENIGMA* RUNS MUCH DEEPER THAN THAT." He turns his eyes towards the harbour, seemingly bored with you.
"Welcome to Revachol!" you hear him yell at a red-head woman visiting the Frittte nearby.
He must think red-heads are immigrants.
"I have gotten it from disco, actually."
"It's true, I am a rock and roll star and a rebel."
"Youth culture does not affect my thinking."
"OFFSHOOTS OF THE SEMENESE PEOPLE INVENTED DISCO WHILE HAVING SEX UNDER THE INFLUENCE OF COCAINE. IT IS A SHAME UPON MY RACE -- BUT WHAT IS DONE IS DONE."
"I AM NOT SURPRISED YOU ENJOY IT SO MUCH. THIS HAS HAPPENED TO MANY OF THE SIDE-PRODUCTS OF THE INEVITABLE CULTURAL VICTORY OF THE SEMENESE RACE."

The drawings are precise and look true to their pseudoscientific ambitions. One thing however -- it is not *entirely* free of throwbacks in the phylogenetic tree. His large jaw, for example, could be a trait indicative of criminalism. Also his ear lobes could be smaller.
"SO IT WAS. YOU BESTED ME IN RACE COMBAT TO REACH MY SUPERIOR, THEN HAD HIM GIVE ME AN ORDER. I SALUTE YOUR CUNNING, ENEMY. I WILL GO AND REMOVE THE BODY FROM THE TREE -- WITH MY BARE HANDS."

"SO IT WAS. YOU SURMOUNTED THE HARBOUR WALL IN A DISPLAY OF ATHLETIC PROWESS TO REACH MY SUPERIOR -- THEN HAD HIM GIVE ME AN ORDER. I SALUTE YOUR CUNNING AND I WILL REMOVE THE BODY FROM THE TREE -- WITH MY BARE HANDS."
"You're so noble, Measurehead."
There's a but.
"Lieutenant, what if we don't want to do that?"
"This is the uncomfortable result of not taking it down ourselves. I can live with the compromise."
"LISTEN TO YOUR LITTLE FRIEND. HE IS WISE IN HIS CHILDLIKE WAY. HIS MYSTERIOUS RACE MAY YET PROVE FIERCE COMPETITION TO MY HEROIC HAPLOGROUP."
"BABE, SEE THAT THEY STAY HERE THE WHOLE TIME."
The woman's gaze follows Measurehead as he leaves...
"We're just trying to keep things from going to shit."
"Have you ever thought that maybe things *should* go to shit?" The woman twirls her hair. "I'm Katya by the way..."
"That's none of your business."
"And who are you?" The lieutenant fires back. "What is your business here? Why are your clothes four sizes too small for you?"
"Spoken by a mercenary -- pretending to be a worker."
"There has been no side-choosing. We did what we had to do to keep order."
"Thank you for your cooperation, Measurehead."
"FAREWELL, HAM SANDWICH. YOU ARE A UNION MAN FROM NOW ON."
He nods slowly. "AND WHAT YOU HAD TO DO -- WAS TO BECOME A UNION MAN FOR ALL TO SEE."
"ROCK AND ROLL IS MORIBUND, ONLY KOJKOS LISTEN TO IT ANYMORE. THERE IS NO LIFE LEFT IN IT, MY PEOPLE ABANDONED IT LONG AGO. IT LEADS ONLY TO NEUROGENERATIVE HERPES AND HEROIN OVERDOSES."
"OF COURSE IT DOES. YOU ARE A DEGENERATE INDIVIDUALIST AND A ROCK AND ROLL REBEL. A PAWN OF INTERNATIONAL FINANCE, JUST LIKE THE REST OF YOUR HAM-COLOURED RACE."
"I said I'm *not* a communist. I don't know who I am but that's one thing I know."
"STOP EXPLAINING YOURSELF, NO ONE CARES ABOUT YOUR BELIEFS. THE CONVERSATION HAS MOVED ON. TELL ME WHAT DEGENERATE SUB-CULTURE HAS MADE YOU DRESS IN THIS SHAMEFUL WAY?"
"Okay, I'll ask -- who are the *Semenese*?"
"I don't really know who the Semenese are. I've recently experienced head trauma."
"Wonderful. I need to enter the harbour now -- on police business."
"Wonderful. We're done with this line of inquiry."
Measurehead stoically looks to the distance -- in silence.

"Hello?"

"Hang on, how *do* you know who I am and what I do?"
"How do I get to the other side of these gates?"
"Are you some kind of a sex pervert?"
"No. And even if I were, I'm not engaged in anything factually illegal. No crime here."
"Who do you think you are, being disdainful and judgemental about a person's private, idiosyncratic, voyeuristic-erotic preferences anyway? Fuckshit. Goddamn pigs."
"Geez, sorry. I was just being curious?"
"I make it my responsibility to judge and police the intimate behaviours of complete strangers."
"Bi-curious or plain curious?"
"Believe me, we know. We've got our eyes on you. Can't keep it to yourself, can you? Always creepin' into the lives of others, trying to dominate their actions, even their conversations."
"What? I don't understand."
"Umm... bi?"
"Uhh... plain, maybe?"
"Figures. What else is new! Certainly not a surprise when it comes to you nit-wit coppo-goons."
"Yeah, I bet you are."
"That's a bit boring, don't you think?"
"Err... okay, I guess."
"Can you stop being such a jerk?"
"Fuck you, man, come say that to my face."
"Hum. Well, this went... nowhere. Zero fun and excitement here. I'm getting real bored, how about we change the subject?"
"If you say so... I haven't really thought about it?"
"Ha ha ha ha!" A loud, derisive laugh echoes wildly through the gates.
"Whatever. Jerk."
"I'm going to get over there and find you, mark my words!"
"Ha ha. Okay, good luck! I'm getting bored now... change the subject, why don't we?"
"Fair point. Sorry, I haven't been... doing well these past days."
"You're apologizing to me after *I* called you a bunch of shitty things? Goddamn, now who's the weird one?"
"Maybe you're like a... masochist. Into humiliation and stuff."
"Nah... I'm just a sorry sack of a man, a positively shitty cop."
"Maybe I am? Never thought of that."
"Ha... live and learn, lawman. Get out there and blossom into a flower! Go figure things out! Meanwhile, I'm getting bored... how about we change the subject?"
"Do what, look?"
"Yes!"
"From your perspective... I'm a Mysterious Pair of Eyes, boo!!"
"Know what? Fine... no point in getting riled up by some clown trying to be abusive."
"Ha ha. Okay, you've got me *cornered* there, good sir officer. Anyway, this is really boring... change the subject, why don't we?"
"I don't know if that's completely accurate..."

"*We* who?"
"That's not funny."

"Ha ha. It was funny enough to me."
"Good use of sarcasm there, man." You hear a faint clapping sound, brimming with caricature.
"None of your business. Ooh, so spoo-ooky!"
"The gate is broken as shit. Someone absolutely destroyed the access panel in the control tower above."
"Why would anyone do that?"
"Probably a docker, aiming to block these loud-ass scab fucks from getting in. The guys get panicky sometimes..."
"To keep the strikebreakers out?"
"Most likely, Mr. *Amazing Investigator*. Aren't you a sharp-ass pencil! Maybe someone should write a novel about you."
"Are you making fun of me?"
"Of course! Amazing! If a little girl says so, it absolutely should happen!"
"Yeah, someone should."
"Step right up, folks! Read all about the Incredible Adventures of Flop the Wonder-Cop! Able to solve the *most dastardly* of plots and ploys. Ha ha ha."
"Whatever, it's not really my thing anyway."
"Oh no, certainly not! Who would ever dare such a thing."
"Not a learned type? Sure is a shocker!" The eyes gleam brightly in the darkness of the void.
"I'm a cop, it sure is my business!"

"You've got something against honest workers?"
"Just look at the guy, come on."
There's something twitching in the back of your mind... a connection hidden between the numbly aching folds of your brain.
"Honest, my ass. Just look at the guy, geez!"
"I dunno..."
"I'll have to... think about it."
"I mean... maybe, somehow?"
"Look at you, Super-Constable on his way to solve a suspicious case! Seems like that's going to take a long fucking while, ha ha."
"No, I meant... don't scare people like that."
"Never mind, doesn't matter." (Calm yourself.)
"We are the eyes, we cannot be closed... if one pair shuts, another takes its place, ha ha!" The eyes grow wide and ominous.
The mysterious pair of eyes attentively follow your every move.
The eerie pair of blue eyes is still here, gazing out from the dark void between the gates.
"Boo! The eyes of Martinaise are upon you, piggy!"

"Fine, if you won't take this seriously, I'm going to ask about something else."
"Try not to hurt yourself, old man, ha ha." The pair of eyes beams impishly at you.
"Why should I beware?"
"I'm not scared of you."
"Go think-man, go. Find some clues, put two and two together. That's how the magic happens, ha ha."
"I don't really believe you."
"Is it now, is it *really*?"
"You know what you've done, don't start denying it now."
"Yes."

"Well, maybe?"
"Look at you, little authoritarian. Bet it also makes you feel good and strong to discriminate against any disenfranchised people that get in your way. Makes you feel all *manly*."
"I sincerely doubt it. You're supposed to help people and handle actual crime. Not walk around like an oppressive tyrant, passing punishments however you feel."
"It's easy and comfortable to side with the ignorant, the arrogant, the condescending, isn't it? Hide away in the soft, secure existence of perceived superiority, a vapid fantasy of your mind."
"Well, we know what you're up to. We observe your every move. Take care and watch your back." The eyes suddenly disappear from sight, only emptiness remains, floating in the lacuna between the gates.

"I haven't done anything!"

"O-ho! I wonder what *harrowing mystery* lies behind this feat of self-destruction."
"An intriguing mystery! I wonder what *terrible secrets* lie behind this dark and ominous veil, ha ha."
"Your life sounds like an immeasurable clusterfuck. Something's gone *really wrong*."

"There's no way you could *fit* inside all those nooks and gaps."
"Prove it, creep."

"We've had our eye on you for some time now. And I can tell you straight... goddamn, you're one *boring fuckin' cop*!"

"Huh..." The lieutenant thoughtfully rubs his chin as he turns to move. "So there is something we agree on after all. Didn't see it coming. But let's move, I'm getting cold."

I don't need a word-for-word retelling, but we're partners -- say *something*. An adjective will do.

"Good good, that's very good." The smile persists as he turns to leave. "I almost feel bad that we need to focus on our investigation now. But we do. Let's go."
His remorse is insincere. That gent's relieved to beest able to moveth on my liege.
"Can't you for just once roll with it, lieutenant?"
"I don't think I should talk to him any more."
"Oh, of course. I didn't realize that." He looks at the lorries down on the street and turns...

That makes absolutely no sense, but I really don't want to get into it with you.

I hope he means it and at least some kind of an early defence system in his psyche is working.
"I hate to repeat myself, but was that not what happened back when you became his race pupil?" He flashes you a disarming smile.

Was it a mistake leaving him alone with that guy?
"But... why?" He looks completely perplexed for a moment, but quickly gathers himself. "Actually, do me a favour and please don't tell me. Let's just quickly go and that'll be it."
"No, but I learned that no matter how though you are, someone's always tougher."

Just nod.

The lieutenant doesn't break eye contact. He slowly nods too, then pats you on the arm...

"Let's go now," says the lieutenant and turns to move. "It's getting cold and it's too late to put him in a foster home."

Yeah, there is definitely something wrong with it.
What? What's wrong?
Where to even begin? There's the bloatedness, then the swollenness... It's like there's an upholstery of alcohol underneath your skin.
I'm scared. I want to stop doing this.

It's not. It's swollen and snail-like, wriggling between your fingers.
Don't be scared. It's only your face. It's not like anyone is going to *see* it.

Bet you are. Your nose feels like a small balloon in the middle of your face. It hurts when you honk it, and it doesn't appear to be a particularly tiny nose either. Not with all the drinks it's *absorbed* for you.
Wipe the mirror now.
Behold!
Dear lord help me, what is this?!

I'm not making it, the face is making it itself.

You *can't*, can you? It's like it's not even voluntary anymore. You have worn that grin into your face and now it won't come *off*...

God, I don't know -- it's indescribable.

I'm insinuating that I'm vaguely sympathetic. I think I'm sort of pulling it off too -- in a *sad has-been* kind of way. There is some charm to it.

Superstardom.
You are correct.

I promise. (Lie.)
I'm outta here. [Leave.]

Abort! You clearly have not thought this through. You won't like what you will see there -- and you will never *un-become* it.

Really -- all recollection of the person you are, the people in your life and even the world you're in has drowned in a sea of blood alcohol. This was no mere night of drinking, it was a deluge. Of world-ending proportions.

Getting clever appears to make *The Expression* even worse. Now it's mixed with smugness.

It's too late. Like an image on film, *The Expression* belongs to your primary motor cortex. It would take a minor neurological miracle for you to cease producing it.
Like the rest of you, it comes from a bad place somewhere in the past. That's all you know for now.

It belongs in The New -- the third decade of the current century. Enough time had passed from the failure of Revolution that, for a fleeting moment, free market economy seemed like the ultimate, uncontested way of life for our species.
Things were good. It was *smooth sailing*. People made gold-and-champagne-tinted interiors and façades to suit the times, calling this *The New Style*. But, more importantly -- disco happened.
For Revachol -- your city -- that meant only one thing: Guillaume Le Million!
If it doesn't rhyme, you're not pronouncing it right.

Out of the dazzling swirl of disco music, in an open air *boîte de nuit* somewhere in Revachol West, Guillaume's blond mane appeared on the screen. He sang some bullshit. Then he made *The Expression*.
So I adopted it? Why?
I feel the need to add a clicking sound when I make it: *Click-click*.
How long ago was The New?
Everyone loved it. Maybe you thought some of the stardust would rub off on you? Maybe it did? Either way, it's all gone now. Only the grimace remains.
The click is used to spur on a horse. It also features heavily in Guillaume Le Million's regional mega-hit "Don't Worry (Your Pretty Little Head)".
Sometimes you like to add finger pistols to the mix, because unlike Guillaume le Million you are a police officer. It's your nifty little way to say: I'm armed and dangerous.
Anything else? Like who am I? Why did I drink myself into oblivion?

There is a vast ocean of time between right now and *The Expression* looking good on you -- or anyone. Two decades, if the calendar is to be trusted. Humanity has run aground in that time, it's a different world now. The Expression is a relic.

Some twenty odd years. There is a vast ocean of time between right now and *The Expression* looking good on you -- or anyone. Humanity has run aground in that time, it's a different world now. The Expression is a relic.
I guess that's it then. (Conclude.)
You have some understanding of the recent history of disco. The rest is darkness.

Oh my god, you're right! It's like it's not even voluntary anymore. You have worn that grin into your face and now it won't come *off*...

The faucet is quite terribly mangled, but you just might be able to twist its parts into place.

It's like something snaps in you -- a nerve ending, a thought, a sadness. Your face in the mirror is suddenly clean of the leer that had distorted it for god knows how long.

Oh yes, they're all *wiped out*. Your bushels of grain, your salted meats, your hogsheads brimming with bitter ale. All gone. Your fields have been put to the torch, your great-hall is a ravaged husk. You are bereft.
