But I was trying so hard! I was making progress!
It wasn't enough. You simply don't have what it *takes*...
Oh no...
What was *that*? Did you just *flinch* before your own reflection?
I did not.
It was just a reflex!
Yes, you did. There's no use denying it...
Goddamnit...
Hold on, my cocksmanship is on par with...!
What's that? Can't hear yourself over the moans of your wömen in the hands of foreigners who play them like instruments. Be careful, or they'll wear you like a sock, Harry-boy.
Can't hear you over the moans of your wömen. They writhe in pleasure as the foreigners are playing them like instruments. Be careful, or they'll wear you like a sock, Harry.
*Never*. May this serve as a constant reminder of your sacred, un-put-downable burthen.
Will I ever be able to make another face again?
That's one way of saying that the nerve damage is *quite* severe. The only way you'll be able to change your face now is with your fingers...
You step back from the mirror. A loose board creaks.
In a rundown shack on the far coast, a middle-aged man pounds his fist and looses an animal cry as he stares into a sliver of clouded glass...
A cold damp seeps in through the gaps between the wall planks. There is no one to bear witness to your vow...
From above the Bay of Revachol, a cold wind gathers in response. The people of the fishing village pull their coats and blankets tight about themselves...
Fine... The three of you, all together, ride an aerostatic into the sunset. The question remains: Will you sacrifice love to keep Revachol safe?
It's time you knew the truth, bröther.
I am ready.
This is a horrible allegory for... whatever is on the other end.
Love... time... Revachol...
Maybe it will make you temptation-proof, so something good will come out of this at least?
This is the face worn by the first law-bringers, the noble tyrants. Today you join their number...
You are a terror even to yourself!
Wait, can Kim be in the aerostatic too?
Pull the imaginary lever.
It's all shit.
(Bow down.) Yes. My heart forever beats for Revachol, I am all she has left. The constant kingsman.
Face it, bröther. No one's got the *willpower* to build her up again. They won't do what has to be done.
*Ahem*. It's a *lot* like the face on that rather unfortunate muscle-man t-shirt you just so happen to be wearing...
*Ahem*. It's a *lot* like the face a certain muscle-man is making on that t-shirt you insist on carrying around...
*Ahem*. It's *very* similar to the face Hjelmdallermann is always making on the cover of those books...
It can't be.
All of it?
An involuntary twitch runs through your hand, almost like reflex.

We keep it buried like a horrible secret. We feed it through the cracks in the floorboards out of a sickening sense of nostalgia. Just enough to keep it alive. And yet it still comes to us in moments of weakness, unbidden, a source of shame and panic...
Wait, why do I need to do that?
The bloated whores, schizophrenic anarchists and deformed moneylenders tremble, trying to shield their eyes, as he -- *Le gendarme en diamant* -- walks by!
A day will come when you need to take a shotgun to that cellar, shoot whatever is down there in the head, and walk away, never looking back.
No-no, not the voice! Make it stop...
You haven't yet banished all weakness, but you will. We know you will...

Remember: Kingsmen are not born, they are made. And the only thing that can unmake us is that which drove us to rise above in the first place. We keep that thing locked in the deepest cellars of our mind. So deep we forget what it is.
You'll plough your way toward the frigid lands of Katla and Vaasa, smashing every ice sheet in your path. Nothing, *nothing* can stop an icebreaker...

While the world burns, the two of you, together again, ride an aerostatic into the sunset. Maybe it will work this time? Spare Revachol and you'll never hear from her again. Will you sacrifice a second chance at love to keep Revachol safe?
It can, and it *is*. Just a mountain of shit, every bit of it.
It was time to banish that ridiculous *Expression* from your face -- and replace it with a perfect reflection of your unyielding resolve, your noble suffering.
It was time to banish that pitiful, *sad* look from your face -- and replace it with a perfect reflection of your unyielding resolve, your noble suffering.
How dare you speak of Revachol that way...
You're wrong. There's still a way to turn back time. To make things *richtig*.
He sets down the paper and quickly scribbles the date and time in his notebook, along with a note: 'HDB possible relapse? Check in first thing.'
You step back from the mirror. A bead of water drips from the pipe beneath the washbasin.
I will never forsake my vöws. (Conclude.)
Now shout from the top of your lungs: YOU ARE THE NOBLE SUFFERER.
Even love?
*All* of it.
Does this thing *unmake* you, or does it heal you?
Yes... you truly are. (Tightness -- in gaseous form -- leaves your body.) She's lucky to have you, watching her sleep.
What happens to me then?
I don't think I can do that.
You're a hard motherfucker... (Tightness -- in gaseous form -- leaves your body.) If we didn't know better, we'd say you *enjoyed* consigning your city to the flames.
Wait, what happened to my face?
What's going on? I thought I *succeeded*!
Face it, bröther. No one's got the *willpower* to set things right. They won't do what it takes.

Meanwhile, his colleague is filling in the last clues of his nightly crossword when he hears what seems to be some kind of animalistic howling from the adjoining room. He directs his eyes toward the door of their shared bathroom...
Especially love, bröther. Face it, no one's willing to make the sacrifices that are necessary, not in this day and age.
Look deep inside yourself. You know it's true, because it *hurts*.
Nine million souls flicker out of existence. Sixteen if you include the greater metropolitan area.

You will be free to love Revachol like no one has ever loved her. You will be her champion, and she will be *faithful* to you. If you can just make this last sacrifice, you will *finally* know happiness.
He sighs and returns to his crossword. He is a police officer, not a baby-sitter.
In a mould-covered bathroom inside a trashed hostel near the edge of Martinaise, a middle-aged man grips the sides of a cold sink in white-knuckled fury...
(Rack the imaginary shotgun.) Whatever it takes. For *Revachol*.
I may as well give up then...
So ask yourself, when the time comes, can you shoot the past in the head, walk away, and never look back on its rotting remains?
I won't give up. I *can't* give up.
Now open your eyes and witness the (small) wonder! The HMS Modest Kingsman has left the docks. You are neither the greatest nor the strongest icebreaker on the seas, but you are what you are.
Now open your eyes and witness the wonder! The HMS Last Kingsman has left the docks. The world will tremble as you smash all the ice in the world.
That voice... so warm and sweet...
Your heart can belong to Revachol or it can belong to darkness. As long as it's torn between them it's broken and useless.
Despite doubt, fear, sentimentality and weakness, you plough ever forward, like an icebreaker, tearing through the frigid North Sea.
*Nothing* -- not pain, fatigue, hunger, fear or desire -- will ever deviate you from the path. Like an icebreaker you crush all opposition, ploughing forward *no matter what it takes*.
You're tired, afraid, sad, hungry and in pain. But most of all: confused. Yet *still*, like a tiny icebreaker -- the tiniest boat in the fleet -- you plough ever forward...
It takes a true kingsman to summon the *will* to face reality in all its darkness. To stare straight into the abyss and do *what must be done*.
Bröther. You *have* succeeded...
Who said anything about giving up?
You used to believe you came from a large family with many half-brothers and sisters, but where are they now? However you shout, they can't hear you...
Enough. The Franconigerian Court of Honour has held your naked soul up against the Sevenfold Sun Miracle and looked right through it. Close your eyes and *know*, this is who you are:
I will bear any burthen.
There's a lever in front of you. Pull it, and atomic fire blankets your beloved Revachol. Millions die in an instant. But you are spared. You, and the voice in the payphone.
How do I know I'm a true kingsman?
You hear a jingle! Keys are clinking in the pocket of your flare-cut pants.
Fish them out.
The "Whirling-in-Rags" is a hostel-cafeteria on the urban coast, frequented by dockworkers.
It says "Whirling-in-Rags" on the aluminium keyring. There is a single key on the ring, the number #1 is etched on it. It should open the door.
This person also *forced* the drinks on you.
Congratulations, you smashed the window with your own shoe. Now you only have one. If you're lucky you can still find the other on the balcony outside. The door to it should be outside your room.
Wait, what am I doing?
What did this then?
Maybe it wasn't me?
You mean someone else took your shoe off and smashed the window with it?
The shards face outward. Whatever broke this window came from the inside.
A fine web of scarring covers the back of your right hand, but none of it is recent.
More likely a projectile than a held object. There are no fragments on the floor from pulling a tool back in after impact.
It is too large for a bullet yet too small for a piece of furniture. You're looking for something heavy and larger than your fist.
The single green shoe you found fits the hole almost as well as your foot. It would have also been heavy enough, if thrown with force.
Assess the size of the impact.
Like the green shoe that's on the hat rack in the corner, which -- coincidentally -- is missing its friend.
Something you've done before.
Did I break it with my own hands? (Look at them.)
The window stands broken in its frame. Cold wind blows in.
Look out.
[Leave.]
Assess the damage.
What do you mean *assess the damage*? How would you do that? What are you even trying to do?
I don't need it. I don't need *anyone*.
I should go and get that shoe.
The window agrees. Its cracked smile is cold and sparkly.
A cool wind gushes in. Your toes curl up from the cold.
The morning light hurts your eyes. It's hazy, but you see the ocean and some war-torn buildings...
The shoe you found out on the balcony fits the hole almost as well as your foot. It would have also been heavy enough, if thrown with force.
Congratulations, you smashed the window with your own shoe.
This person also *forced* the drinks on you.
You mean someone else took your shoe off and smashed the window with it?
Maybe it wasn't me?
I'm sure I had a good reason for it. Maybe I was trying to hit someone?
What a stupid thing to do.
And maybe, just maybe, you succeeded. We'll never know.
Or maybe you were trying to smash your own reflection in the windowpane?
Pretty much. But, hey, at least you found your shoe.
Not that it will keep you warm at night. Brrr.
Congratulations, you smashed the window with your own shoe. Now you only have one. If you're lucky, you can still find the other on the balcony outside. The door to it should be outside your room.
The shoe you found out on the balcony fits the hole almost as well as your foot. It's similar to the green shoe that's on the hat rack in the corner, which -- coincidentally -- is missing its friend.
Congratulations, you smashed the window with your own shoe.
Play the tape.
You push 'Commencer' and the tape starts spinning. Violent static and machine sounds fill the air....
"...this isn't Revachol," a man's voice says. "This is a fucking village, I can almost see the elephants." Another loud screech. Some kind of machinery.
"The harbour." The lieutenant takes out his notebook. "That's the sound of a Kvalsund crane."
More static. "When this shit is done I'm gonna tear that place up, Soldier of the Apocalypse style -- kill shit, dogs and chickens too..."
"I'll fucking do them all in, rape that disco cunt on the counter. You know, the dancer whore upstairs. Do it Co Hoi-style."
"What was that at the very end? Silence?"
"Who's this *Korty*?"
"Okay then. What now?" (Remove the tape.)
"End of recording."
"Korty could be short for 'Kortenaer'. One of the other mercenaries, the one he was talking to. The third one must be relaying the signal."
"One of the other mercenaries I think. The one he was talking to. A friend of his?"
"What's Co Hoi?"
"A village on the Samaran isola, in South Safre. Graad committed war crimes there -- the kind of thing he talks about."
"You think he was there?
"Who knows? Maybe the tattoos would have an answer. Or maybe Co Hoi is just merc talk for atrocity. Slaughter."
"No. The tattoos did not say so. They said he served on Semenine. I think Co Hoi is merc talk for atrocity."
A symbol of *Soldier of the Apocalypse*-style conduct in a civil environment.
"I agree. He also sounded inebriated."
"But he *did* say he's going to do it. You can't edit words into someone's mouth."
"Still..." The lieutenant looks at the tape. You are familiar with this look now -- it's his *look of suspicion*.
"Indeed, but..." The lieutenant looks at the tape. You are familiar with this look now -- it's his *look of suspicion*.
The South Safre conflict is an ongoing proxy war between Graad and Safre. It has been hot for 12 years with the atrocities piling on. Mostly committed by the Graad.
"I think we've got a few more questions for Klaasje, don't you?" He looks around. "This seems to contradict her testimony. At least to some degree."
The Kvalsund crane in the harbour. Its screaming is distinctly apocalyptic.
He's right.
"What do you think?"
"It seemed authentic enough. Probably recorded off their shortwave, then *edited* to seem more incriminating. He sounded like he was on patrol around the harbour walls."

Somewhere between the GRIH and Le Cycle, the good lieutenant steps out of his Kineema. A brisk, chill wind greets him. You get the feeling he should have been here for this. Listen again when he's here.
"Never did get that taste out of my mouth..." A click -- then silence. The rest of the tape is empty.
"Gonna rent a room, Korty, a real nice one..." This part is unintelligible. "I don't give a shit, I'm fucking done. I'm done mentally."
You stare at the Great Doorgunner Megamix. If only you had a boombox, you would be able to play Titus' tape.
The tape feels ominous... Upon it, the dead speak. Respect the tape!
The porta-reel is just what you needed -- the reels attach to the apparatus with a satisfying click. The tape is routed behind the magnetic reader.
Don't play the tape. [Put porta-reel away.]
The lieutenant is out there somewhere. Doing something. You get the feeling he should have been here for this. Listen again when he's here.
"I think he sounded all right. Just letting off some steam."
"Yes," he says incredulously. "It was just *locker room talk*." The lieutenant looks at the tape. You are familiar with this look now -- it's his *look of suspicion*.
The lieutenant presses the button marked 'Arrêter' on your porta-reel; the tape stops spinning.
There's more going on here than we know.
Bad news.
The porta-reel is just what you needed -- the reels attach to the apparatus with a satisfying click. The tape is routed behind the magnetic reader.
Take out the tape.
As you take out the tape, the boombox tunes itself back to the cheery radio again, spewing out beats like it's a Friday night.
The contrast feels chilly -- inappropriate even.
Play the tape.

Not so fast. Somewhere between the GRIH and Le Cycle, the good lieutenant steps out of his Kineema. A brisk, chill wind greets him. You get the feeling he should be here for this. Listen when he's here.
Not so fast. The lieutenant is out there somewhere. Doing something. You get the feeling he should be here for this. Listen when he's here.
This is not the cleanest bathtub in the world, but it's cleaner than you are right now.
Ah, that soap scum smell. It smells like life. At least compared to you.
Run yourself a bath.
I want to live forever with the corpse smell. Memento mori and stuff. [Leave.]
The bathtub slowly fills with water. The water beckons.
Undress, close your eyes, and submerge.
The water is only lukewarm, but still comforting, like amniotic fluid. A few beer cans are bobbing up and down along your flanks like sad duckies.
Take the beer cans out.
Leave the beer cans in.
Now you are alone with your thoughts in the tub. But it's easier than being alone with your thoughts outside the tub.
The cans continue to bob, as do your thoughts, aimlessly splashing up against the sides of the tub.
Linger in the tub a little.
Get out. (Conclude.)
The water line recedes as you stand. You are cold now. Your clothes stick to your still moist skin.
Your fingers grow pale and are covered with tiny whorls as the water cools.
What are you doing? You're not some fat fish in a fucking aquarium. Time to get moving.
You feel nice and lonely. And so, so tired.
They're not even really thoughts. Just assorted sensations, none of them acute enough to focus on.
Imagine something.
You see the corpse. You can still smell the cadaver on you. It's going to take more than one bath to get rid of that stench.
Hold it right there! Keep your head above water, or you'll lose all those pheromones Morell sprayed on you.
I don't care. I just want to be engulfed.
Keep your head above water, just in case.
The water doesn't feel particularly clean. A few beer cans are bobbing up and down along your flanks like sad duckies. You pause to think before letting your head go under.
The lukewarm water is comforting, like amniotic fluid.
Then -- houses along a narrow street. A video rental. Darkness on the planet's curvature.
The compact tape player is still and silent. Seems it has completely broken down now.
There is no fixing this one.
"This would have been *very* helpful with the 'Megamix'." He stares at the tape player. "But it isn't anymore."
"Yeah... any ideas?"
"It's not *my* fault."
"Fuck off, Kim."
"My Kineema only comes with a radio," he ponders. "We should try to find a new tape player. There's a pawnshop near the water lock, south of here. Maybe they have a spare."
"My Kineema only comes with a radio," he ponders. "Let's try to find a new tape player. Perhaps we should talk to Roy at the pawnshop -- he has stuff."
What should I do now, Stereo 8 Player?
The broken tape player doesn't have the ability to respond. But Kim would.
Great. What now?
Well shit.
Best find a new player. A boombox, funky style? Maybe the guy at the pawnshop can help out?
"Of course," he notes. "We should try to find a new tape player. Perhaps we can talk to Roy at the pawnshop south of here -- he had stuff."
"Of course," he notes. "Anyway, we should try to find a new tape player. There's a pawnshop near the water lock, south of here. Maybe they have a spare."
The lieutenant doesn't even flinch. "Anyway, let's try to find a new tape player. There's a pawnshop near the water lock, maybe they have a spare."
The lieutenant doesn't even flinch. "Anyway, let's try to find a new tape player. Perhaps we should talk to Roy at the pawnshop."
The machine was made in Revachol by a company called Lemercier -- their logo depicts the triple-towered Delta skyline. It was supposedly built to last.
I guess the only thing to do is to find a new player. Might be one waiting for you out there somewhere.
Fuck is that going to achieve? Being a smart-ass... making your nostrils flare.
"You're looking at the destruction?"
"I did it -- my way."
"This is where *the magic* happens."
The man is finding it hard not to trip on the tape -- and not to send any of the bottles rolling across the floor...
...where unidentifiable sludge makes it hard for him to breathe. Smells of vomit in here.
"It's not as bad as I thought. There are no elephant corpses. Should we go maybe?"
He takes a step toward the door. Like he'd like to leave.
Say nothing. Nod stoically.
He nods.
"I can see that. The potted plant under the table is a Seraise Fern. They have those in South Safre too. All things considered..." He looks around, as if to check.
"I can see that." He takes a step toward the door. It looks like he'd like to leave now. The atmosphere is oppressive.
"I'm sorry for... this."
"I have no idea what that means." He looks toward the exit, longingly.
"No, I meant disco... never mind."
"I know what you meant." He looks toward the exit, longingly.
"Got my own little Co Hoi here."
"Wonderful," he nods, then looks toward the exit, longingly.
"No problem, officer." He takes a step toward the door. Like he'd like to leave.
"And by that you mean crimes against humanity?"
"Yes."
"Yes. Disco doorgunning villagers."
"No. I am something *much more*."
"I can see that." He takes a step toward the door. "You're the RCM's own Soldier of the Apocalypse, aren't you?"
Kim also tries *not* to look at the pile of tape viscera on the carpet. Or the weird suitcase on the hat rack. Or the potted plant dying in the corner. But it's all just too morbid to ignore.
"Of course." He nods, then looks longingly toward the exit.
"Well, crimes against myself anyway."
"I have no idea what that means." He looks toward the exit, longingly.
"I defied bourgeoisie morality in here. Defied it *hard*."
"This is an expression of *me*. My individualism."
"Oh, this?" (Point to your face.)
"What happened to you?" the lieutenant asks as he leans in, eyes mapping your frozen face.
"What do you mean, lieutenant?"
"I am Icebreaker."
"No, you are not. What you are is an officer of the Revachol Citizens Militia conducting a murder investigation."
"This is what I am now, Kim. What I was always meant to be."
"I plough my way towards the frigid lands of Katla and Vaasa, smashing every ice sheet in my path..."
"No, but you see, you *don't*," the lieutenant explains patiently, although his voice is very tired suddenly. "You're not a firewalker, you're not an icebreaker."
"No, but you see, you don't," the lieutenant explains patiently, although his voice is suddenly very tired. "You're not an icebreaker or a firewalker, or even Tequila Sunset."
"Nothing, *nothing* can stop the Icebreaker..."
"Are you fucking insane?!" the lieutenant snaps at you. "Don't answer that! And STOP doing it! Let's go."
"No, but you see, you don't," the lieutenant explains patiently, although his voice is suddenly very tired. "You're not an icebreaker or a firewalker, or even Raphaël Ambrosius Costeau."
"No, but you see, you don't," the lieutenant explains patiently, his voice suddenly tired. "You don't plough anything, you help me solve this case, please remember."
"No, but you see, you don't," the lieutenant explains patiently, but his voice is very tired. "Your name is Harrier Du Bois, not 'Icebreaker'."
"No, but you see, you don't," the lieutenant explains patiently, but his voice is very tired. "You're not an icebreaker, Harry. Please stop."
"No, but you see, you don't," the lieutenant explains patiently, but his voice is very tired. "You are not Tequila Sunset and you are not an icebreaker. Stop, please!"
"No, but you see, you don't," the lieutenant explains patiently, but his voice is very tired. "You're not Raphaël Ambrosius Costeau and you're not an icebreaker!"
"I'm sorry, Kim, I don't know what came over me."
"It's okay," he says quietly. "We're both under a lot of stress right now. Let's just try to not let it get to us and remember what we came here to do."
"It is a powerful metaphor, lieutenant. For my resolve."
"Okay, that's all right." He looks visibly relieved. "As long as you understand it is a metaphor and don't build a persona around it."
"They say you can hear the ice crack from a..."
"I understand. It's not gonna become a thing."
"I understand *nothing*."
"Oh, good." The lieutenant's posture relaxes. "Thank you! And sorry I asked about it. It's none of my business. Let's just get back to work."
"You look... different. Constipated somehow?"
Suddenly the whole Icebreaker concept seems... just lame.
It's like he re-conditioned your brain.
The lieutenant's command instantly lets all the wind out of your sails, like he overrode your mind or flicked some secret master-switch.
"Yes, your face." He nods, looking worried. "Looks like you're having a stroke. Can you even move it?"
Better keep the lieutenant in the dark about the whole 'Icebreaker' thing. He's not gonna get it.
"There's nothing more to talk about, only to *endure*." [Leave.]
That's a negative, lieutenant.
"And what is that? A walking mask?"
"A noble sufferer."
"Absolutely." (Lift the corners of your mouth with index fingers.) "See?"
"I don't need to 'move it', this is my final form."
"He Who Stares Straight into the Eclipse."
"He Who Withstands All Temptation."
"The last kingsman."
"I'm fine, don't worry about it."
"So now you want to go blind as well?" He shakes his head. "How about we become Those Who Solve Murder Cases instead and get back to work?"
"Including drinking?"
"Excluding drinking."
"Including drinking."
"Excluding drinking. And drugs."
"No, you are not. What you are is an RCM lieutenant conducting a murder investigation."
"You don't look fine and I'm *very* worried about it." He crosses his arms on his chest.
"I just don't understand, officer." The lieutenant just stands there, looking perplexed. "Please, help me understand."
Should I contact his station's lazareth? Behind his back?
"I don't think *you* are supposed to call yourself that." A fleeting smile crosses his lips. "But I appreciate the honesty. Now let's get back to work."
Neither was an actual question.
The lieutenant is *not* loving the new look.
"The last kingsman..." he repeats pensively, inspecting your face. "That's fitting, I suppose. Almost as if you *did* manage to turn back time. If only for yourself."
"Alright, detective," he reaches out and pats you on the arm. It feels strangely encouraging. "Let's get going, we've got a killer to catch."
Face of a millipede trapped in amber...
But somehow it doesn't scare him, like it scared you. Doesn't make him quiver with cold. Poor guy...
"What temptations is *He* withstanding then?" asks the lieutenant with a puzzled look.
"You know what? I don't even want to know. Let it be one of your *internal* side-cases. I just want to get back to work."
"Hm." The lieutenant seems almost impressed. "Admitting a problem is the first step forward. Perhaps now we can finally get some work done."
"Shall we?" He looks ready to go.
So I'm guessing this is bad.
Well, this feels familiar.
Very. *Very* bad. *This is the end* bad.
I'm sure it's just heartburn. Oh god...
No. It's many years of combined self-neglect and self-abuse.
Don't go grabbing at your chest and screaming bloody murder. Keep your cool. Remember -- looking good always makes you feel better.
We've been here before. You've got this.
Fucking shit, I'm scared. What do I do? Who do I call?
Nope, sorry, you don't. Not this time.
Don't think this is a sign of anything other than your heart failing.
The end of the world is here.
Yeah, screaming isn't happening on account of extreme shortness of breath. You're just making it worse. Oh god, it's painful...
Get it together, boy. You've gotta hold on, no matter how bad...
All you feel is pain and weakness. You have to surrender now. We all do, it gets *so* dark. You don't even see her face, like you always thought you would. You only see pain and fear.
Try to remain conscious.
You feel something in your chest. An unnatural pressure. It's spreading to your left arm, your jaw...
Let it all go.
There's no shame in surrendering now. We all do, it gets *so* dark. You don't even see her face, like you always thought you would. You only see pain and fear.
"Help.. someone..."
"I wish I was fucking dead. Fuck you, fuck you."
Nothing you can say would make you feel any better now...
"I'm done. No one even likes cops."
Despair creeps into you, getting fat on your weakness. Whatever noble intentions you once had as a police officer -- it's eating them all up now.
There's something else in there. There has to be. But -- it's like reaching your hand into muddy water, fishing around, and coming up with nothing...
"Yes, it can be difficult to be on the receiving end of so much distrust and outright hatred," he says with a sad half-smile.
You're still coming up with sentences. That's a step up from total annihilation, right?
"I'm seriously running out of shits to give, Kim. Fuck you."
Yeah, I'm pretty sure you're shit out of luck *fishing around* right now. You're drowning.
"Fuck me? I understand this is by no means an easy investigation, but..."
"I've wasted my life protecting humans. They don't deserve it."
"I don't dispute that you have been charged with protecting the people of a particularly... challenging district. But poverty does not make one a loser -- poverty is just... poverty."
He watches your meltdown stoically from behind the lenses of his glasses.
"Too late for that. So whatcha gonna do now? Skewer yourself?"
"Cuno don't give a shit about your shits."
"That you are a loser, Cuno doesn't doubt, but why go around whining about it?"
"Cuno knew the pig was a f****t."
"I wish I was fucking dead. Fuck you, fuck you Cuno."
"I'm done. No one even likes cops."
"I'm seriously running out of shits to give, Cuno. I'm quitting."
"I've wasted my life protecting humans. They don't deserve it."
Fuck Martinaise, fuck Revachol. And fuck me. I'm done.
I'm done. No one even likes cops.
"I've wasted my life protecting humans. They don't deserve it."
